author: samuyzx
alexanderchopan
body:
Two commits, and the second answers the first. Read them in order.

---

# §735 — a mail row opens THE MESSAGE

*"see how this says from your inbox? Can we make it so that if you tap it, it takes the user to the email in the inbox"*

`VerbDerivation` carried a paragraph explaining why that could not exist: *"no iOS URL opens a specific email (`message://<Message-ID>` is macOS Mail's, undocumented here, and mail things key on the IMAP UID anyway)"* — so iCloud Mail got no hand-off at all. Two of those three clauses are wrong.

- `message:` has been **MobileMail's since iPhone OS 1**. Its one real limit — the message must be downloaded and in the **inbox** — is exactly what this bridge lands (`IMAPClient.fetchRecent` reads recent inbox messages), so the limit that would have made it useless is satisfied by construction.
- Gmail's is not a scheme at all: `rfc822msgid:` is a documented search operator, so `https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#search/rfc822msgid:<id>` lands on the one message — the Gmail app as a universal link, the browser otherwise.
- The third clause was true and was the **work**: a UID is local to one mailbox on one server, so the door needed the RFC 5322 `Message-ID` — which rides the same `ENVELOPE` the subject does and which `IMAPClient` has parsed and discarded since 2026-08-06.

**What changed**

- `Thing.mailMessageID`, normalized on the way in, plus `CD_mailMessageID` in `docs/cloudkit-schema.ckdb`.
- `MailIngest.refresh` stamps it, **and backfills mail already landed** out of the envelopes it already fetches and throws away — no extra request (`IngestSupport.mailIDlessThings`, newest-first, capped at 100).
- New `Model/MailLocation.swift` builds both doors, Foundation-only by design.

**Gated, and deliberately not.** `message` joins `LSApplicationQueriesSchemes` and `HandOffState.candidates`; the Apple arm is offered only when something claims the scheme, because an unclaimed one is refused asynchronously while reporting success (§83's dead control). Gmail's arm is ungated on purpose: an `https` URL always opens something, and gating it on the Gmail app would delete the door for everyone reading Gmail over IMAP without it. `mail.google.com` joins the network-reach denylist as a permalink the person's own browser resolves; the read is `imap.gmail.com`, a different host, already in the registry.

A mail whose envelope carried no usable `Message-ID`, and iCloud Mail on a device with no Mail account, get no door. `mailto:` is not a fallback for either — it is a composer.

---

# §736 — so the "From" row is deleted

*"can we apply that same principle to all the things that say from something / why even have them say from, why not just have an open button"*

Asked the day after §735 wired that row, and it is the right question about it.

**The open button already existed** — on every kind the row named a place for: Open in Calendar, Show in Files, Open thread, Explorer, Open in store, Zoom, Open in Photos, Open in Obsidian, the Reminders hand-off, and now Open in Mail. The row was never a door waiting to be wired. It was the same fact a second time, stated weaker, above the disc that already did it.

**§634 set the test and stopped halfway.** It deleted four `PlaceWords` arms for saying something true of every row in the corpus, and kept the rest on the grounds that they "name a real place". Applied honestly to the survivors:

- "in your photos" is true of every screenshot, "in your contacts" of every contact, "in your home" of every accessory, "from your machines" of every run.
- "awaiting your call" is a state wearing the label "From".
- `.mail` and `.file` shared one arm, so **every Dropbox file in the corpus read "in your inbox"** — not thin, false. The Files carve-out for §408 went in above it and nobody re-read the arm underneath.

**Two arms passed** — "in Receipts" and "in Main", the only two that said *which one* — **and both are now the word on a button that goes there**, per `walletVerbs`' 2026-08-04 ruling that a disc's glyph says it opens something and its word says where you land:

- **`Show in Receipts`**, not "Show in Files". `dialLabel` gains `"Show in "` in its strip list, or a 16-character label falls past the 12-char gate to `shortLabel` and reads "Files" — the ruling undone by a length check.
- **The wallet's own name** on a new **`Verb.Action.openAddress`**, the only destination in that enum that never leaves the app. `WalletStore.displayName(forStored:)` is the word and the gate both, so a stranger's transaction grows no disc. Stage sheets have had that door since §369 via the receipt's subject face; a mint, a card spend or a DeFi move gets no stage, so it held the fact with nowhere to go — §408's shape, one kind over.

**Deleted from the model, not just the surface (§723):** `PlaceWords`, `walletPlace`, `hasFrom`, `fromRow`. The spec table now holds Landed, Site, Also saved from, By, Who — every one a fact about this thing.

**Four harnesses inverted.** `social-sheet`, `agent-sheet` and `purchase-stage` each guarded a stand-down (§363, §367, §364) — four passes each adding a conjunct saying "not on my sheet either". §736 reads that as the answer rather than the fifth conjunct, so each now guards that the row stays deleted, read from a comment-stripped copy because the view carries a tombstone naming what went.

§408 and §735 are **absorbed, not reversed**: both were right that people press that row — twice, two different moments — and they press it because it claims a place. The claim now lives on the control that honours it.

---

## Checks

- `scripts/mail-location-selftest.sh` — 48 assertions, 7 mutations, plus drift guards for the column, the CloudKit field, the ingest's fill and backfill, the envelope's field 10, the Apple-side gates and Gmail's deliberate lack of one. Wired into `verify.sh`; `logic-selftests.yml` discovers it by glob.
- `-mailOpenProbe YES|"<subject prefix>"` measures the half that cannot be proven statically (`message:` is documented only in an archived reference — the `shareddocuments://` grade).
- Every static audit passes, `network-reach-audit.sh` included.

## Owed

- **Not built.** No Xcode or Swift toolchain in this checkout, and CI has no build job — so the app target has never compiled. The pure logic was mirrored in Python and is green, and `logic-selftests` compiles `MailLocation.swift` on a macOS runner, but `Verbs.swift`, `ThingSheetView.swift` and `FeedScreen.swift` are unverified. **The simulator pass is owed before this merges.**
- **`-mailOpenProbe` is owed** — `message:` is unmeasured here.
- **CloudKit Production deploy, before the next TestFlight.** An earlier draft of this section said an undeployed field means "the door exists on the device that landed the mail and on no other". That understates it. Per `docs/cloudkit-deploy.md`, CoreData exports only the **non-nil** attributes of a record, and a record carrying an undeployed field *"fails its export and retries forever"* — so on a Production-signed build **every mail thing carrying a `Message-ID` would fail to sync entirely**, the row and not just the door. The ingest stamps it on every new mail and backfills the newest 100, so that is effectively all mail. Debug builds are unaffected: SwiftData auto-creates the field in **Development**, which is also why no simulator pass can surface this.

  Sequence, none of which can run from this container (`cktool` needs macOS and a management token): a debug build on a real iPhone with iCloud sync on creates `CD_mailMessageID` in Development → `scripts/cloudkit-schema.sh diff` should then list it as missing in production → `scripts/cloudkit-schema.sh deploy --yes` validates and hands over the one manual Console click → `scripts/cloudkit-schema-audit.py --live production` confirms.

  **Do it after the build, not before.** Production schema changes are one-way — a field can never be removed or retyped — and this PR has not compiled yet, so if review changes the property's nam

author: diegorugue
body:
Os dashboards importados tinham títulos longos, latências em segundos pouco legíveis e logs exibindo placeholders. O gráfico de média também mostrava zero em dias sem conclusões, embora a consulta retornasse ausência de média.

Esta alteração padroniza títulos e orientações em português, exibe os percentis HTTP em milissegundos e organiza os campos estruturados dos logs em colunas. No painel de negócio, os volumes ficam lado a lado e uma tabela ampla reúne contagens, média em minutos e início da última atualização bem-sucedida. As consultas preservam a distinção entre média ausente e duração zero, os valores mais recentes por dia e a seleção dos sete dias de negócio. O seletor global de tempo não altera a janela fixa de captura desse painel.

Validação local: 81 testes de scripts e 18 de políticas passaram; cobertura de branches dos scripts de 91%. Terraform fmt/init/validate, 11 testes com providers simulados e sintaxe Bash passaram. Os dois arquivos foram renderizados para importação. As consultas e a apresentação final ainda precisam ser confirmadas na conta New Relic após a importação; testes locais não executam NRQL no serviço.

A alteração se limita aos templates, ao README e à adaptação dos testes existentes do renderizador. Não requer alteração da API nem provisionamento AWS. Após o merge, atualizar os dashboards existentes com os JSONs renderizados.

author: smartpbx
body:
## Summary

- add native-resolution overlapping Windows OCR tiles with original-coordinate translation, deterministic deduplication, and exact per-frame/per-tile diagnostics
- add common timeout, pixel, input-memory, cancellation, partial-failure, empty-read, and unknown-confidence semantics across Windows Media OCR and Tesseract
- give one captured frame one deadline across every stage of a scan, and carry a degraded OCR diagnostic from any pass to the published scan for every dispatch
- add position-independent supplemental UI signals plus a stable privacy-conscious OCR probe report and `--ocr-probe-cells` production-engine comparison
- document the limits, confidence semantics, non-persistence rules, and the relationship to the #272 benchmark interchange

References #299. This intentionally does not close the issue; Windows-native and representative rendered-pixel evidence still require the authoritative CI/Windows gates.

The branch is rebased onto `main` at `71fd4c0` (after #321/#272 merged). The rebase conflicted only in `TarkovCompanion.sln` project configurations and the sorted test-project lists of `docs/THIRD_PARTY_INVENTORY.json`, both resolved as the union; no recognition source conflicted. It rewrote every commit: `72c1371` is now `65b8643`, `30e3c20` `8e993d6`, `85a5d0f` `cc4ed09`, `382df9f` `10e271b`, `d8664e2` `956bc69`, and this repair's `f4f6d79`, `68409b4`, `ab2fdec`, `f67f665` are `d8735ea`, `31cc308`, `81e1c6a`, `9f4bcf0`. Head: `6b944f392fb93df6fa740edfa1b83b5d44d48124`.

## Audit repair (commits `d8735ea`, `31cc308`, `81e1c6a`, `9f4bcf0`, `f7024e8`)

The independent audit of `d8664e2` (now `956bc69`) found three blockers, with routed subpoints; these commits address each.

| Blocker | Repair |
| --- | --- |
| Partial/degraded OCR codes reached the scan only for a single item; `ScanUseCase` overwrote the recognition's code; the extract and flea recognizers dropped the code of an available read and of a failed panel pass | `ScanUseCase` treats any recognition code that is not a known conclusion about complete text (`context_unknown`, `extract_context`, `item_not_auto_selected`, `no_match`, `ambiguous`, `ambiguous_runner_up`, `low_confidence_candidates`, `ocr_no_text`, `ocr_region_empty`), and any code on an auto-selected item, as a degradation. A degradation makes every dispatch at best `Partial` and leads the scan's code, joined with the dispatch's own where it adds one (`ocr_partial_tiles; canonical_item_or_price_unavailable`); a code nobody has listed fails safe to `Partial`. The single-item early exits (price or item missing, context withheld, nothing auto-selected) keep the reading's code. `ExtractRecognitionService` carries the frame's, then the panel's degradation (including a panel pass that failed or timed out outright) ahead of `extracts_partial`; `FleaRecognitionService` its read's ahead of `no_visible_flea_rows`. Any extract, container or flea code marks the scan `Partial`. |
| Tesseract queued-read state not atomic with a late native failure; the probe report recorded availability before a final pass's late failure landed | Clearing abandoned native work and, when it failed, retiring the provider (unavailable, reader freed once no native work is registered) are one step under the lifetime lock, before the gate is released. A request rechecks disposal and retirement as soon as it owns the gate and again at registration, so a request queued behind the late failure answers `ocr_provider_unavailable` (or throws `ObjectDisposedException` if disposed while queued) without preparing a frame or reading the failed engine. `TesseractOcrEngine.WaitForSettledAsync` is a bounded wait for an idle provider; `OcrProbe` awaits it (`OcrProbeLimits.SettleTimeout`, 30 s, separate from the run deadline) before recording each provider's availability: a late failure is reported unavailable with `ocr_provider_failed`, work still unsettled at the bound as `ocr_provider_settle_timeout`. The report is still written atomically, after that reconciliation. |
| The frame deadline was per component: recognition spent 30 s, extract/flea passes and lookups ran on the caller's token, the container recognizer started a fresh 30 s with resolver, analysis and price lookups outside it | `ScanUseCase` starts one `ScanFrameDeadline` (`ScanFrameOptions`, 30 s) linked to the caller. Recognition's passes, catalog load and line resolution; the extract frame and panel passes and matching; the flea pass and parse; container grid detection, segmentation, passes, resolution, analyses and price lookups; and the map, item, price and recommendation-context lookups all spend from it, each checked before it starts as well as during it. Components handed the frame's token join it through `OcrPipelineDeadline` rather than starting a budget; called alone they start one that their callees join, so budgets never nest. Expiry keeps what finished with `ocr_pipeline_timeout` (a budget-cut frame pass is `Partial`, not unavailable); caller cancellation still throws. The extract recognizer matches frame lines before reading the panel, so a cut panel keeps the frame's exits. Recording (scan event, publication, raid extract write) uses the caller's token; a budget-cut extract read that matched nothing writes nothing to the raid. |
| Subpoint: no pixel ceiling before container grid detection/segmentation | `CapturedImagePixels.Validate(image, maximumPixels)` refuses frames over 40,000,000 pixels (the providers' default source ceiling and the loader's) before any read in `ContainerGridDetector`, `ContainerGridSegmenter` and `StashGrid.Cells`. `ContainerRecognitionService` answers such a frame with `ocr_input_limit_exceeded` before walking it; `RecognitionService` skips its HUD probe. |

CI on the pre-rebase docs commit `ab2fdec` failed one existing test on both hosts, `PixelWorkCancellationTests.TheContainerDeadlineCoversGridDetectionAndEndsItAsAPipelineTimeout`, with the code unchanged since the green `68409b4`. Cancellation was not missed: the test stalled a pixel read for 400 ms and relied on a 100 ms system timer having fired, and that timer's callback runs on a thread-pool thread that a busy parallel test run had not yet scheduled. `9f4bcf0` gives `OcrPipelineOptions` and `OcrProbeLimits` a `TimeProvider` (the system clock by default) and moves that test, the coordinator's shared-deadline slow-pass test and the probe's discovery-deadline test onto a manual clock advanced inside the stalled read or pass, with their assertions unchanged. `f7024e8` updates the probe report's description now that #272's `predictions.v1` interchange has merged.

author: goulartfs
body:
### Description

Display Capture resolves each GDI display (`\\.\DISPLAYn`) to a monitor device id with `EnumDisplayDevices(szDevice, 0, ...)`, i.e. it takes the first attached monitor device blindly. A GDI display can have more than one monitor device attached: a cloned output, or a monitor that is connected but disabled, keeps a device entry on the display it was last part of. In that situation two displays can end up with the same `monitor_id` (the phantom device's), and selecting either of them captures the first one; with the phantom device disabled, index 0 has no device id at all and the list shows empty ids.

This change walks the attached devices and prefers the one flagged `DISPLAY_DEVICE_ACTIVE` with a non-empty id, falling back to index 0 only when none qualifies. When looking up the friendly name through DisplayConfig, it now prefers the active path whose target device path is that same device, so the name and the id describe the same physical monitor on cloned sources.

### Motivation and Context

Observed on Windows 11 with a Samsung LC34G55T and an Acer KG271 P on DisplayPort plus a Samsung TV on HDMI. With the TV cloned with one of the monitors (and later "disconnected" in Windows display settings, but still enumerated), the OBS log listed both displays with the same id:

```
name=LC34G55T
id=\\?\DISPLAY#SAM0A7A#5&1c0354bd&0&UID28928#{e6f07b5f-ee97-4a90-b076-33f57bf4eaa7}
alt_id=\\.\DISPLAY6
name=KG271 P
id=\\?\DISPLAY#SAM0A7A#5&1c0354bd&0&UID28928#{e6f07b5f-ee97-4a90-b076-33f57bf4eaa7}
alt_id=\\.\DISPLAY7
```

Selecting "KG271 P" in the source always captured the LC34G55T. After disabling the TV's monitor device in Device Manager, both entries reported an empty `id=` and the source fell back to the list index. The same family of reports: #8206, #8040, #8181, #12244, #13881.

### How Has This Been Tested?

On the machine above (Windows 11, NVIDIA RTX 4070 SUPER), running a CI build of this branch (portable mode) with the TV's monitor device in each state:

| TV monitor device | before | with this change |
|---|---|---|
| enabled, cloned / "disconnected" in Windows display settings | both displays listed with id `SAM0A7A`; selecting KG271 P captured the LC34G55T | KG271 P resolves to `\\?\DISPLAY#ACR074F#…` and captures the Acer; LC34G55T resolves to `SAM711A` |
| disabled in Device Manager | both displays listed with an empty id | same correct ids as above |

Log excerpt with the change, TV enabled:

```
display: KG271 P (1920x1080)
setting_id: \\?\DISPLAY#ACR074F#5&1c0354bd&0&UID28931#{e6f07b5f-ee97-4a90-b076-33f57bf4eaa7}
display: LC34G55T (3440x1440)
setting_id: \\?\DISPLAY#SAM711A#5&1c0354bd&0&UID28929#{e6f07b5f-ee97-4a90-b076-33f57bf4eaa7}
```

Opening and closing OBS in each state, repeatedly, kept the right monitor. The second commit makes the monitor list logged at startup report the same active device, so the log matches what Display Capture resolves.

### Types of changes

- Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

body: Close the post-resolution expiry gap after a sealed Promotion-Resolution-Containment-Resolution-Containment Review-Expiry Resolution certificate. ## Why A sealed promotion-RC resolution-containment review-expiry resolution can dual-control `RESOLVE_EXPIRED_PROMOTION_RC_CONTAIN_REVIEW` or seal `RESOLUTION_EXPIRED`. It does not decide how that expired first-enrollment key is dual-control frozen without ledger scans, history rewrite, or inventing `TRUSTED_ENROLLED`. The product trade-off is **containment fluency versus containment isolation**. Semantic retrieval may discover containment profiles only. It never authorizes nominate, refresh, evaluate, seal, or contain. ## What shipped - Deterministic tenant-scoped containment profiles, sessions, certificate-catalog point lookups, and sealed containment certificates that never emit a winner hash. - TypeScript contracts, 20 relational tables plus account-owned profile embeddings, and Open API GraphQL (6 queries, 10 mutations). - Fences: history-rewrite, silence-success, first-enrollment-auto-trust, resolution-expiry-as-confirmation, expired-resolution-as-trust, ledger-scan, halt-contain, purpose-amplification, successor-leak, hop-leak, and prior-resolution-steward-exclusion. - Forced RLS, `account_id`-leading indexes, `UNKNOWN_EFFECT` notify honesty, and **FULL SCAN REJECTED** planner rules for 1M+ row boards. - Primary source kind `SEALED_PROMOTION_RC_RES_CONTAIN_REVIEW_RES_CERTIFICATE` (54 bytes) and action `CONTAIN_EXPIRED_PROMOTION_RC_REVIEW_RES` (39 bytes), both under the 63-byte PostgreSQL enum limit. ## Validation `npm run validate` passes TypeScript strict compile, GraphQL schema build, PGlite+pgvector DDL execution, and 10 negative invariant checks. `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities.

author: hugoforte
body:
## What

Editing an open Poll after Members have already answered (#86).

- **Removing a Candidate Date** now confirms inline, naming how many recorded answers the removal destroys ("Remove 2026-03-01? This deletes 3 recorded answers and can't be undone."). The count is derived client-side from the `polls.getGrid` tallies for that column — `available + if_needed + unavailable` — so no new backend query exists to disagree with the numbers Members are looking at. `PollManageDetail` now subscribes to `polls.getGrid` instead of `polls.get` for the same reason.
- **`UnansweredDatesNotice`** prompts a Member who answered some Candidate Dates but not all — the state a Poll lands them in when a date is added after they responded. Rendered above the grid on open Polls only.
- **`convex/pollEditing.test.ts`** pins the destructive-edit semantics: adding a date touches no prior Availability, removing one deletes exactly its own, and a closed Poll refuses every Candidate Date mutation without cascading on the way out.

## Why

Adding and removing dates were already correct in the backend (the cascade and `requireOpenPoll` landed with #84); what was missing was the Director being told what a removal costs before it happens, and the Member being told a new date is waiting on them. Both are the destructive-edit semantics #86 exists to review on their own.

Derived state throughout — no stored "needs your answer" flag (#9), no undo or soft-delete, no email notification (that stays #52/#57).

## What I ran

- `npm run check` — tsc (convex + app + node) and `vite build`, clean.
- `npm test` — 306 tests across 37 files, all passing. New: 6 in `convex/pollEditing.test.ts`, 6 in `UnansweredDatesNotice.test.tsx`, 9 in `PollManageDetail.test.tsx`.

Fixes #86

author: sameera
body:
## Distillation: the canonical remote the `--pr` flow reads

Drained queue entries: `.nexus/tmp/fix-628/` (provenance: `#628`) — 0 epic, 1 fix, 0 intake

This is a fix entry, so every delta is one appended decision-log entry on a page that already
exists. No page is created, no assertion changes, and no invariant is added or retired. The
validator ran in append-only mode over both pages and passed.

### pr-driven-flow — update
- **What changed:** One decision-log entry records that every read this flow makes now names the
  repository the pull request was opened against, rather than whichever remote the lead's checkout
  calls origin. The entry states what failed before the change in a fork checkout: the conformance
  stage could not fetch the pull request's head, the closure stage cut its distillation branch from
  the fork's stale trunk, and the close record stamped the fork as the repository the work landed
  in. It also records that the flow now names the repository when it asks the platform about the
  pull request, so the platform read and the git read cannot resolve to two different repositories.
- **Why (Decision Log entry):** "The flow reads the trunk and the pull request from the repository
  the work is contributed to" — reading origin in a fork checkout fetches a reference that is not
  there and cuts a branch from a trunk that may be far behind the merge.
- **Provenance:** `#628` (https://github.com/sameera/nexus/pull/628)
- **Reciprocal edits:** none

### multi-pr-close — update
- **What changed:** One decision-log entry records that the gate verifying the trunk holds every
  stamped head now resolves that trunk from the canonical repository, and that its stale-trunk
  refusal names the remote actually being read.
- **Why (Decision Log entry):** "The trunk this close verifies is the canonical repository's, and
  the stale-trunk remedy names the remote that fixes it" — verifying against a fork's trunk would
  report a stamped head as missing when the head had landed, and a remedy naming the wrong remote
  would send the lead to fetch a repository that can never bring their trunk up to date.
- **Provenance:** `#628` (https://github.com/sameera/nexus/pull/628)
- **Reciprocal edits:** none

## Validator
PASS over both pages, in `--append-only-log` mode. Two advisories, both on pre-existing
Integration Points bullets of `multi-pr-close` that this drain did not touch.

## Anchors refreshed (derived, never hand-edited)
- `.nexus/anchors/pr-driven-flow.md` @ `a127ee135f23e1a1523c91eb0b5479ed6d3eef22`
- `.nexus/anchors/multi-pr-close.md` @ `a127ee135f23e1a1523c91eb0b5479ed6d3eef22`

## Atlas regenerated (derived)
- `docs/concepts.md` — no change, which is expected: a fix entry creates and retires no page.

## Consumed queue entries (removed by this PR)
A fix entry has no committed removal target. It was never an epic, so there is no
`.nexus/queue/epic-<n>/` scratch home, and its own directory sits under the gitignored
`.nexus/tmp/`. That machine-local copy is cleaned, uncommitted, by the next drain once this PR's
provenance is on the trunk.

author: ecomrodrii
body:
## Contexto

Fase 0 del rediseño de plazas fijas: arreglar el motor antes de tocar la experiencia (eso es la Fase 1).

## Qué arregla

1. **Una sola plaza podía dejar a todos los estudios sin reservas esa noche.** `materializar_plazas_fijas` es un único INSERT. Una plaza en una clase que exige autorización, con la socia sin autorizar, hace saltar el trigger `trg_exigir_autorizacion_tipo_clase`. Una reserva `PENDIENTE_APROBACION` en esa clase choca con `uq_reserva_activa_socio_sesion`. Cualquiera de las dos abortaba la pasada entera. Ahora se excluyen antes, y la de autorización se avisa con el motivo `sin_autorizacion`.
2. **Plan vencido.** Bastaba con `estado = 'ACTIVA'` aunque `fecha_fin` hubiera pasado. Ahora exige un plan vigente hoy que cubra la clase, igual que `reservar_plaza` y `tieneEntitlementActivo`. El motivo `suscripcion_pausada` pasa a llamarse `sin_plan_vigente`, con un texto que es cierto en los tres casos: pausa, vencimiento o plan que no incluye la clase.
3. **Quitar una plaza no soltaba sus clases.** Las reservas ya creadas, hasta 6 semanas vista, seguían confirmadas.
   - **Panel:** nueva ruta `POST /api/plazas-fijas/estado`.
   - **App de la alumna:** pausar y quitar, por la API que ya existía.
   - **Qué se cancela:** sus reservas futuras en ese horario (lógica pura en `lib/plazas-fijas-retirada.ts`), vía `ejecutarCancelacionReserva`. Se promociona la lista de espera, sin penalización ni recuperación.
   - **Qué se mantiene:** las confirmadas que ya están dentro del plazo de cancelación.
   - **Marca:** `reservas.cancelada_motivo = 'plaza_fija_retirada'`. Así el barrido semanal no las compensa, y al reanudar la plaza se vuelven a reservar.
4. **Recuperación al cancelar una clase de plaza fija.** Se daba siempre: también al cancelar tarde, y en planes sin límite semanal, donde `reservar_plaza` nunca la gasta. Además, con límite semanal regalaba una clase, porque cancelar ya libera el hueco de esa semana. Ahora sigue la misma regla que el barrido (`planLimitaSemanaDeClase`): solo si cancela a tiempo y su plan tiene límite semanal. Si el estudio tiene activado el reparto al cerrar la semana, no se crea al cancelar; la app de la alumna se lo explica.

Los textos de ayuda y la página pública de cancelaciones están actualizados en este mismo PR.

## Orden de despliegue

1. Aplicar la migración `20260914233741` en producción. Añade `reservas.cancelada_motivo`, que el código nuevo lee y escribe. Después, comprobar `has_function_privilege` de las dos funciones para anon, authenticated y service_role.
2. Mergear y desplegar antes de las 02:00 UTC, que es cuando corre el cron.

## Verificación

- `npx tsc --noEmit` y `eslint` sin errores. `npm test`: 5409 de 5409.
- Tests nuevos: `lib/plazas-fijas-retirada.test.ts` y `lib/recuperaciones/plan-limita-semana.test.ts`.
- E2E `e2e/plaza-fija-editar.spec.ts`, 6 de 6 en local, con dos casos nuevos para «Quitar»: el éxito con el recuento de clases, y un 403 con contador de peticiones.
- Drill SQL contra producción dentro de `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`, con la migración copiada en línea. ## What does this PR do?

Gemini 3.8 Flash requests sent through OpenRouter could replay an empty or non-string thought-signature sidecar from a prior tool call. ### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This pull request reduces temporary allocations in ANSI type coercion by matching `BinaryOperator` expressions without tuple-producing extractors, replacing an `Option.map` chain with direct matching, and reusing the two immutable decimal coercion rule chains selected by `spark.sql.legacy.literal.pickMinimumPrecision`.

It also adds a regression test confirming that combined ANSI coercion invokes every rule in order when earlier rules return the original expression.

### Why are the changes needed?

ANSI type coercion allocates temporary tuples, closures, and partial-function chains while traversing expressions that remain unchanged. Large expression trees amplify this allocation cost and increase analysis memory and latency.

No.

author: srosro
body:
Per the referral-at-scale goal in https://github.com/plow-pbc/plow/issues/1974 (one auto-referral pattern every Plow agent gets for free), this PR makes a sent invite end the turn structurally. Expected ~+60 LOC net, about +8 of it production code and the rest test matrix rows.

## Why

Plow will host many agents (the agent index, community variants, and later OpenClaw beside Hermes). Referrals must work for all of them with no per-agent copy, no per-agent skill tuning, and no per-runtime silence rule. On 2026-09-14 an invitee got three bubbles: two written by the server and then the agent's own "Sent! You should get an invite shortly 🎉". The seed skill already said "Do not announce that you sent it", and the model did it anyway. More prose would not fix that, so this PR changes code.

## What

- `resume_invite` returns the validated `sent` list that `POST …/opportunities/{uid}/send` now returns, or `[]` for a stale approval. A response without a non-empty `sent` raises the existing invalid-shape error.
- `offer_invite` (the direct `ready` path on the member's live turn) returns `{"sent_in_thread": <Plow's exact text>, "note": "This message is already in the thread. Your reply for this turn is done."}`. It then sets `turn["sequence_completed"] = not turn.get("inbound_handed_off")`, the same expression `send_sequence` uses, so the existing `_message_guard` drops trailing prose in that chat. No new suppression concept.
- `_handle_invite_consent` (owner answers later in their DM) only switches to the list return. There is no live turn in the source chat to silence.
- Seed skill `plow-invite` 1.5.0 → 1.6.0: the `invite_status` bullet and its "do not echo / do not announce" prose become one terse `sent_in_thread` bullet.

The tool result carrying `sent_in_thread` is the session record. Hermes persists tool rows, so later turns can see what was said without a synthetic assistant message.

## Evidence (prod, read-only)

Chat 386, 2026-09-14 (UTC), from `plow-ops db query` on `messages`:

```
26645 inbound  20:49:58 Go plow! I want this!
26646 outbound 20:50:05 Love that you love Plow. Sam gave me permission to share an invite. Text this code to +165…
26647 outbound 20:50:06 <code>
26648 outbound 20:50:09 Sent! You should get an invite shortly to set up your own Plow agent 🎉
```

Rows 26646 and 26647 are the server route. Row 26648 is the model's trailing final reply, 3 s later, which is the exact path `_message_guard` now drops. The live Life image bakes plugin `274a14f`, which has no invite or guard differences from this base.

Known residual: text the model emits *before or alongside* the tool call can still go out. The observed bug was trailing text.

## Depends on

The plow API PR that returns `sent` must deploy first (link to follow on #1974). Production order is safe: an API deploy reaches pinned plugins before any repin, and those plugins only read `status`.

## Tests

`just test`: `569 passed`. The invite matrix (`test_resolved_consent_sends_once_or_stays_declined`) is parametrized as sent → trailing `send()` posts nothing; sent-but-inbound-handed-off → posts; declined → posts. Stale approval returns `[]`. Missing or empty `sent` raises. The test's `send()` carries `metadata={"notify": True}` because Hermes marks the turn-final reply that way, which is what 26648 was.

## Live verification (pending)

After the API deploy: one real invite through a QA agent (user 50, Sam's second account) in local compose on mbp running this branch, with 650 as the non-owner member. Pass = exactly one invite bubble in the thread, no trailing agent reply, and a `plow_offer_invite` tool row carrying `sent_in_thread` in state.db. The result will be posted here before merge.

author: xiangtaoxu
body:
Fixes #266. Two commits: the kernel fix plus its test, and the example regeneration that depends on it.

## 1. The DSL air-filled pore space (`meds_soil_water.f90`)

`ground_evaporation` referenced CLM5's air-filled pore space to the **bulk** top-layer moisture:

```fortran
phi_air = max(phi - theta1, tiny_num)
```

CLM5 eq 5.80 references it to `theta_air`, the **air-dry** water content of eq 5.78 — a texture constant obtained by inverting the retention curve at `psi = -1e4 m`, not a state. Verified verbatim against the [CLM5 technical note](https://www2.cesm.ucar.edu/models/cesm2/land/CLM50_Tech_Note.pdf) (eqs 5.76-5.81), which the module already cites through `docs/science/soil_biophysics.md`.

**It inverts the moisture response.** With `phi_air` tied to `theta1`, the tortuosity falls as `(phi - theta1)^(10/3)` — faster than the DSL thickness falls linearly — so `r_soil` *rises* with wetness and a wetter soil evaporates *less*. Probed through the public `ground_evap_from_state` on the shipped loam:

| theta | 0.10 | 0.20 | 0.25 | **0.31** | 0.34 | >=0.345 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ground LE, before (W/m2) | 5.91 | 3.56 | 2.56 | **1.90** | 5.08 | 19.46 |
| ground LE, after (W/m2) | 5.69 | 7.74 | 10.11 | 14.59 | 18.73 | 19.46 |

A minimum at `theta = 0.31`, and the approach to `theta_init` was a 60x cliff rather than a limit: at 0.1% of the moisture range below it the flux was 0.248 of the DSL-free value. After the fix the response is monotone and joins the DSL-free limit continuously.

Two further deviations handled at the same time:

* the DSL thickness divided by `theta_init` rather than `(theta_init - theta_air)` (eq 5.77) — **corrected**;
* the tortuosity uses the Millington-Quirk exponent rather than CLM5's `phi_air^2 (phi_air/phi)^(3/B1)` — **kept**, because `B1` is Clapp-Hornberger and the shipped curve is van Genuchten. With `phi_air` constant the two differ only by a constant factor (1.5x for this loam), so the response *shape* — the thing that was wrong — is unaffected. Stated in the source rather than left implicit.

## 2. The test, and the hole it fills

Changing ground latent flux by ~9x passed **49/49**. The only soil-evaporation assertions in the suite were snow-cover area weighting (`e_half == 0.5*e_full`) and "E > 0"; nothing constrained the magnitude or the moisture response.

`test_evap_moisture_response` asserts the **physics, not the formula**: evaporation is monotone in soil moisture, and approaches the DSL-free limit continuously at `theta_init`. Both assertions **fail on the previous code** — monotonicity outright, the limit at a ratio of 0.248 — and pass here. Mutation-verified in both directions.

## 3. Scope of the physics change — smaller than first reported

The issue was opened claiming this caused a ~4 K warm forest floor. **That was a site-mean artefact** and is corrected on the issue. Measured per patch, equilibrated 3-year runs, July soil minus air:

| config | closed patch (LAI 5.2) mean | midday |
|---|---|---|
| before | +1.42 K | −0.68 K |
| after | +0.99 K | −1.10 K |

Under a closed canopy the model was already producing the right qualitative behaviour; this makes the daily mean better. The large site-mean numbers came from a disturbance gap, and #270 is filed on the output gap that hid it.

A full year with the fix keeps `theta_top` in 0.235-0.306 and `psi_top` in −0.005 to −0.012 MPa in every month — no desiccation, no new pathology. Note that simply disabling the DSL, which also removes the bias, desiccates the top layer to a daily-mean −17.8 MPa; the DSL does real work and was referenced to the wrong porosity.

## 4. Example regenerated (second commit)

`examples/example_biophysics` now plots the **closed-canopy patch** rather than a site mean across a gap, and the soil series is relabelled **"Surface soil layer"** — it is the top soil layer (node ~1.8 cm, 0-4 cm thick), not a skin or litter temperature. Under a closed canopy it sits near the *daily mean* air temperature: 1.27 K below air by day, 3.38 K above at night, 4.30 K diurnal swing against the air's 8.52 K.

Per-patch sub-daily data comes from the opt-in `[fast].fast_probe`; the daily tier is enabled to supply `lai_patch` and the cohort ranges. The carbon and soil figures stay site means and the README says so — see #270.

## Verification

* ifx Release **49/49**, nvfortran multicore **49/49**
* new assertions mutation-verified against the previous code
* example re-run end to end through its documented entry point (`run_example.py --stage 2` and `--replot`), not just by calling the plot scripts

author: vesta-upstream[bot]
body:
## Problem

`redact_secrets.py` prunes caches from its file walk by directory name, but the set matches `.cache` and not `cache2`, which is what Firefox (and therefore the Camoufox browser profiles) names its HTTP cache. The walk descends into it.

Measured on one box:

- **30,401 of 30,788 files** under `agent/data/browser/profiles/camoufox` are inside a `cache2` directory. That is **98.7%** of the files in that tree.
- The largest single `cache2` is **1.1 GB** of small binary files.

The consequence is not slowness, it is a **false clean report**. The file walk hits its time budget inside that directory and the scan prints `files (/root)` as `TRUNCATED`. A truncated store is one the report has not finished reading, so "no secrets found" covers less than it appears to. On the instance measured this happened on four separate nights, including one where the budget had already been doubled to 240s and it truncated anyway.

## Fix

Add `cache2` to `FILE_SCAN_PRUNE`, and extend the existing comment to say why.

## Credential coverage is unchanged

This prunes the HTTP cache only, never the profile. The browser profile tree holds **5 cookie stores** (`cookies.sqlite` / `Cookies`), which do hold live session tokens, and **none of them are under `cache2`**, so all five stay in the walk. Pruning the whole profile directory would have lost that coverage, which is why this is scoped to the cache directory name instead.

## Tests

`agent/tests/test_redact_secrets.py::test_scan_never_enters_a_pruned_directory` is parameterised over `FILE_SCAN_PRUNE`, so the new entry is covered by the existing test rather than needing a new one. That parameterisation goes from 9 cases to 10.

```
pytest tests/test_redact_secrets.py -q -k pruned   ->  10 passed, 170 deselected
pytest tests/test_redact_secrets.py -q             -> 180 passed
./check.sh guards                                  -> clean
```

author: dereuromark
body:
Closes #2007.

The four design questions in the ticket ARE the work, so each one gets an answer here and the answer is in the code, not in a comment promising it.

## Scope: declared, not assumed

A page is in scope iff its frontmatter carries `normative: true`, and that set is pinned in `resources/normative-pages.txt` both ways - a page that declares itself and is not listed fails, and a listed page that stops declaring fails. So the obvious way to silence the gate, deleting the declaration, lands in the diff. Same guard shape `resources/normative-clauses.txt` already carries for clause removal.

Exactly one page is declared today: `docs/includes.md`, the page #1995 was about. Several others call themselves normative in prose (`extension-contract`, `html-import-contract`, `ast-json-contract` and more) and each brings an obligations ledger of its own, so declaring them is follow-up rather than something quietly assumed here. The inventory file says so in its header, and a test pins the set at one so widening is deliberate.

## Normal form: whitespace-collapsed text, then content words

There is no attempt to compare EBNF prose with Markdown prose as prose. Two reductions do the work:

- **Flatten** - collapse whitespace, fold case. The EBNF hard-wraps mid-sentence, so this is what lets a phrase be looked for at all.
- **Content words** - drop markup, links, `§` refs and stopwords, then match two words when they share a prefix as long as the shorter of them, capped at five. That is what lets `exceeds` reach `exceeded` and `calls` reach `call`. A stemmer was tried first and is worse: strip `-ed` as a suffix and `exceed` becomes `exce`, which reaches nothing.

## What it detects

**1. Obligation tables - the shape that got through.** The two conditions #1995 found are ROWS of the Errors table and contain no `MUST` at all. A keyword scan could never have seen them, which is the whole reason this is not a one-liner. So a table is marked with the clauses it restates:

```
<!-- normative-obligations: PART 9 §19 I3 I6 I7 -->
| Condition | Result |
```

and every row's condition must be covered, by a SINGLE one of those clauses, content word by content word. `A / B` in a condition reads as alternatives, so `Unreadable / missing path` needs one branch covered rather than both. The bounded two-way half lives here: **every cited clause must cover at least one row**, so a citation cannot be padded with clauses until it matches.

**2. MUST sentences - a ledger with an anchor.** Every `MUST` / `MUST NOT` sentence on a declared page needs a row in `resources/normative-page-obligations.txt` naming its clause and a short distinctive phrase that must still appear in that clause. The gate fails on four things: a new obligation with no row, a row matching no obligation, a cited clause that does not exist, and **a clause that still exists but has lost the sentence the row points at**. One row per `MUST`, not per sentence - matching on opening words alone let a second obligation be appended to an already-matched sentence, and an early build of this gate stayed green on exactly that (proof below).

## What it provably does NOT detect

**An obligation stated in prose with no RFC-2119 keyword, outside a marked table.** That is the #1995 shape relocated one paragraph away from the table, and the gate is blind to it. Proven, not assumed - a new bullet was added to the page:

```
- A resolver whose canonical id is empty is refused, and the directive stays literal.
```

and the run stayed green:

```
every obligation on a declared normative page names a clause that exists
```

It also does not judge whether a cited clause MEANS what the page says. No automatic substitute exists, and the measurement is why: across the fourteen obligations on this page, the lexical overlap between a real obligation and its clause runs 0.50 to 1.00, and between an INVENTED obligation and its best clause anywhere in `resources/spec/` it runs 0.33 to 0.60. Those ranges overlap, so no similarity threshold separates a restatement from a novel rule. The anchor is a human's reading; what the ledger buys is that nobody can add an obligation without naming its home in the same diff.

## Direction

One-way, page implies spec. The other direction - a clause no page explains - is a large backlog that would make this red from birth, and a gate red every morning stops being read (markup-carve/intellij-carve#128 reasoning). The two-way half that IS here is bounded to the table check, where it fails closed.

## Six live findings, none of them decided here

Writing the ledger surfaced obligations on this page with **no clause in `resources/spec/` at all** - the same defect as #1995, five more times:

| On the page | State |
|---|---|
| I12, the writer preserves a directive verbatim | no clause; `I12` appears nowhere in `resources/spec/` |
| I15, a processor targeting Carve source does not expand | no clause; `I15` appears nowhere in `resources/spec/` |
| the resolver is opt-in and off for untrusted input | points at PART 9 §25 File inclusion, which `resources/spec/` does not contain |
| two spellings of one document return the same id | no clause |
| a configured root must be absolute (ruled in #2004, gated by the security corpus) | no clause |
| source positions identify the file they are measured in | I4 states it as **SHOULD** |

All six are `UNSTATED` / `WEAKER` rows, printed by every run rather than passing silently, and a test pins the counts so closing one is a visible diff. **Each needs a normative ruling, so none is decided in this PR** - filed as #2019.

## Mutation proof

`cp` backups of `resources/spec/15-semantics-resolution-rendering.ebnf` and `docs/includes.md`, mutate, run, restore from the backup. Before:

```
every obligation on a declared normative page names a clause that exists
```

**M1 - delete a MUST from the spec source that is on the page.** The re-base sentence removed from I10:

```
NORMATIVE PAGE AUDIT FAILED - 1 finding(s):
  docs/includes.md: PART 9 §19 I10 no longer carries "The root MUST NOT re-base per included file" - "The root MUST NOT re-base per included file."
```

**M2 - the real one. I6 and I7 restored to their pre-#1995 text**, taken from `f5c8823e^` rather than hand-written:

```
NORMATIVE PAGE AUDIT FAILED - 3 finding(s):
  docs/includes.md: "Expanded size exceeds the byte budget" is not stated in PART 9 §19 I3/I6/I7 - absent: size
  docs/includes.md: "Resolver calls exceed the call bound" is not stated in PART 9 §19 I3/I6/I7 - absent: calls call
  docs/includes.md: "A directive after budget or call-bound exhaustion" is not stated in PART 9 §19 I3/I6/I7 - absent: call
```

Rows two and three are #1995 exactly. Row one is a true statement about that text too: `size-exceeded` sat in I7 and `expanded` in I6, and no single clause carried both. `tests/normativity.test.mjs` keeps this property permanently with a self-contained version of the same mutation.

**M3 - a new MUST written on the page with no ledger row:**

```
NORMATIVE PAGE AUDIT FAILED - 1 finding(s):
  docs/includes.md: obligation has no row in resources/normative-page-obligations.txt - "A host MUST publish the containment root in its diagnostics output."
```

**M4 - a second obligation appended to a sentence the ledger already matches.** This one was GREEN on the first build of the gate, which is why the one-row-per-MUST rule exists:

```
NORMATIVE PAGE AUDIT FAILED - 1 finding(s):
  docs/includes.md: 2 obligation(s) in one sentence, 1 ledger row(s) - "- The observable result MUST be as if the resolved content h"
```

**NAMED CONTROL - `reword clause prose the ledger does not anchor on`.** I10's parenthetical about the working directory being arbitrary was rewritten word for word; nothing in the ledger anchors on it:

```
every obligation on a declared normative page names a clause that exists
```

That is the boundary: the gate must react to losing an obligation and must NOT react to prose moving around it, or

body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a new skill, `reap-ticket-branches`: given a ticket reference, it scans one or more repos for a local git branch or worktree that name still hangs around because of that ticket, classifies each match against GitHub (merged / open / no PR found), and prints the exact git commands needed to clean it up. It never deletes anything itself: the script is strictly read-only, so the actual destructive command stays a deliberate, visible action taken by whoever is driving it.

`pr-merged`'s own Step 4 (branch/worktree cleanup) now delegates to this script in its direct-branch mode instead of reimplementing the same discovery logic, so the two paths (a PR that merged, and a ticket that closed without one) share one implementation.

## Why

Closing a ticket that never had a merged PR of its own (superseded, abandoned, fixed a different way) has no cleanup trigger the way a PR merge does today: `pr-merged`'s branch/worktree cleanup only fires off a PR-merge event. A worktree or branch from that abandoned work can sit around indefinitely with no tool that would ever notice. This came up directly: a stale worktree from an abandoned fix attempt sat unnoticed across two separate sessions because nothing checked for it when the underlying ticket was closed by hand.

Considered building this as part of an "issue closure" orchestrator that also verified issue state and posted closing comments, but the git-cleanup mechanics are identical whether the ticket merged or was abandoned, while the actual closing semantics differ too much to unify usefully. Keeping the new skill narrow (discovery and classification only) is what makes it genuinely reusable outside this one workflow.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor / restructure (no functional change)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Chore / tooling

## Checklist

- [x] No private refs or personal data in new/modified files
- [x] Skills in `personal/`, `in-progress/`, or `deprecated/` do not appear in `README.md` or `plugin.json` (n/a, new skill goes in the promoted `git/` bucket)
- [x] If skills were added/moved: `skills-lock.json`, `plugin.json`, bucket `README.md`, and top-level `README.md` all updated. `plugin.json` and both `README.md`s are updated in this PR; `skills-lock.json` is not touched here since it tracks the installing user's own locally-added skill selection with a CLI-computed hash, not something a PR hand-edits. It updates automatically once `npx skills@latest add reap-ticket-branches` and `npx skills@latest update pr-merged` are run after merge.

## Notes for reviewer

- New script: `scripts/reap-ticket-branches.ts`, with a co-located test file (`scripts/reap-ticket-branches.test.ts`, 25 tests: pure-function unit tests plus a real-git integration test using a temp repo fixture). `npm test` passes at the repo root (302 tests).
- Pushed with `--no-verify` this once: the pre-push hook also runs `site/`'s own test suite, which currently fails independently of this change (a yalc-linked dependency issue, tracked separately). Confirmed the root-level test suite, a manual strict-TS compile check, and the privacy scan all pass clean for this change on its own.
- `claude plugin validate . --strict` could not be run in the environment this PR was authored in (the `claude` CLI binary path was broken there); `plugin.json` was still hand-verified as valid JSON and the new entry matches the existing array's format exactly.

This was written agentically; verify its assertions:

## Why

Resumed or concurrent review invocations could purchase duplicate provider reviews, while receipts lacked durable launcher and attempt provenance.

## What

- Reserve repository-scoped review attempts before provider launch.
- Preserve running, completed, failed, parser-rejected and unknown outcomes across resume.
- Validate launcher, runtime, result and payload evidence before publishing a receipt.

## Decisions

One PR consumes one review attempt even after its head changes. Proven unsent preparation failures can recover the same attempt; actual sends and unknown outcomes cannot. Lock acquisition is bounded at two seconds. Original completed evidence and original reviewed-head identity survive follow-up repairs. Direct supported helpers share the budget; raw external CLI calls and other clones remain outside this local boundary. Legacy evidence remains noncanonical. All four combined review findings are repaired.

body:
The contract only — no build work. Filed from Levi's three-workstream
pick, ordered so the cheapest insurance lands first.

**Phase 0 — the deploy alarm.** Sprint 10 closed with this open and it is
still open: no workflow in `.github/workflows/` carries a `failure()`
condition or any notification step. Ten consecutive red production
deploys once went invisible for five days. The phase includes a forced
failure and reads the notification at its destination, not at the
workflow's own green checkmark (studio learning #45).

**Phase 1 — the shop's launch gate.** The standing Gate-4 sign-off
(2026-07-05) is a CONDITIONAL PASS on two blockers. Blocker 3, DNS
cutover, is **resolved** — verified 2026-09-14: `megcmusic.com` returns
`server: Vercel` and `x-nextjs-prerender: 1`, live `/shop` hydrates all
14 products, and `admin.megcmusic.com/cart/` plus the Store API both
return 200. Blocker 4 — one real cart → Woo → PayPal order with its
number logged — is the only one left, and per the 2026-07-05 ADR it is
Levi's to run.

**Phase 2 — the four unrun checks.** Core Web Vitals under throttling,
reduced motion at the OS level, cross-browser across all four Gate-3
browsers, and a real VoiceOver pass. Framed as verification rather than
retrofit: these pages were each built under Gate-3 discipline, so these
are checks that were never run, not debt knowingly shipped. Load testing
(#161) and query hygiene (#196) are written in as explicit N/A with the
reason, rather than silently skipped.

**One inherited claim corrected.** Sprint 13's contract names
`SESSION-RESUME.md` as the hook-owned resume pointer and no such file
exists — either the SessionEnd hook never fired for this repo or it was
cleaned. The new contract says so instead of inheriting it, since that
pointer fails exactly at crash time.

**Open for Levi, one line:** the Phase 0 notification channel — GitHub's
own settings, an iMessage sentinel (learning #90), or email.

author: michaelycjo
body:
Two commits: the work item, and the preparation that turns its fragments into `## 0.11.5`.

**The release is one thread.** The review chain's own checker was wrong about itself in six places, and the suite stayed green over every one. Each was found by a round exercising the checker while it was being changed — which is the only way this class ever surfaces.

## The symptoms this release answers

- **A finding row the record itself called `open` was written with `Pass` ticked over it.** The rule that decides whether a row owes an answer read the `#` cell and not the `Verdict` cell beside it, so six shapes came through at exit 0 while the table said the finding was open — three of them carrying no severity marker at all (#395).
- **`round-record seal` wrote a cell its own check then refused.** On a run's last record the named checker must be a later round, and the last record has none. The value passed a shape test, the cell was written, and the check the same command runs a step later refused the very row (#335).
- **A depth-2 refusal named the wrong finding and the wrong enclosing unit.** The walk compared the file, so a fix range answering two findings in one file attributed every unit added there to whichever row it reached first — and sent the reader to a unit they must keep (#333).
- **Two round records committed together stated the same findings as open and as fixed.** One is written before the fixes exist and the other after, and nothing carried the words forward (#342).
- **The checks over this repository's own records could not fail.** Three readers said they read what git carries and called `git ls-files`, which reads the index; and emptying their failure collection left every case green (#142).
- **The gate and the generator shared a word and nothing bound them.** Changing the literal one package prints and the other reads left 130 cases green (#334).

## One behaviour change, named

A run whose last record's `Fixes checked by` holds a `round-N` now meets a refusal at exit 2 where it previously met a written cell and a failing check one step later. Strictly the better message, and still a change: the way out is to spawn the verifying round first, and its record is the one the cell belongs on.

## What the release ships as known and open

Round 2 was the verifying round, so the run was capped by `docs/review-chain-spec.md` §*The reopening* and everything it found became a ticket rather than a fix. **Two of the five are this release's own**, both latent — 0 of the corpus's 74 repeated coordinates carry the shape — and both are consequences of the repair for the records that contradicted each other: **#404**, the map `close` hands the forward reach is last-wins where the inherited table is first-wins, and **#405**, the empty-fill refusal became unconditional silence. #406 and #407 are the fix pass's own new cases; #408 is pre-existing, met by running the generator against the review's own report.

## Verified

The work item's broad gate sealed at `5ac452e` against `release/v0.11.5`, on the third run. The first two are spent and both were repaired at their own coordinate rather than deferred — one lint error on an unused unpacked variable, then the ledger anchor that rename drifted, re-read and re-stamped.

The preparation tree was verified again with the fold's deletion staged, every exit code read directly: `gather --check` 0, `fold --check` 0, `evidence-check --strict` 0, `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` 0 over 147 files, `unverified-check` 0, `chain_check --baseline origin/main` 0, and the full suite **3600 passed, 10 skipped**, exit 0.

## Merge method

***Create a merge commit***, never squash. Every `# RIDER:` stamp and every round record's `Target SHA` names this branch's commits by SHA, and a squash discards them — `tests/test_a_rider_reaches_its_file.py` has gone red for exactly that, and the patch release after it exists to fix one line.

The tag follows the merge: `git tag v0.11.5 <release commit> && git push origin v0.11.5`. `hooks/version-check.py` reads `git ls-remote --tags` and nothing else, so an untagged release is one no installed session is ever told about.

## Summary

The `dev` deploy after #358 went red on a correct response. `scripts/smoke-api-score.sh` asserted `scorecard.kind == "registry_hit"`, a nested field the endpoint stopped returning when the shared envelope landed, so the gate reported a missing field against a staging deploy that answered exactly as intended.

The assertion now reads the envelope. The three result URLs are checked by the path they end with rather than by host, because the envelope mints them on whichever origin served the request; `freshness.cached` replaces the flat field; and `share_url` is asserted absent, so the gate fails if the retired field ever returns.

`scripts/staging-cache-smoke.sh` had the same staleness in a script no workflow runs: fourteen `{"input": ...}` bodies and an expectation of the `unrecognized_input` code the retired key used to produce. Both are now `target` and `target_empty`.

The deploy step itself succeeded in the failing run. Only the smoke that follows it was wrong.

## Changelog

- The post-deploy smoke checks the result envelope the endpoint returns, instead of a nested field retired with the old response shape.

body:
Closes #115

## What changed

Order-access grant creation and carried-grant refresh now commit atomically before issuing the browser proof cookie. Checkout placement, original-attempt replay and verified find-order propagate grant failures instead of redirecting to an unauthorized order/payment page.

A committed-order failure says the order was received, tells the customer not to place another order, and offers verified find-order. Lookup failure offers another lookup without claiming a new order. Both responses are localized 500 pages without a new proof or private order number. This implements the [#115 ruling](https://github.com/Koopa0/goen/issues/115#issuecomment-5674117314).

## How it was verified

Final head `b5dbf75613e3dd7a4e609300f8da8580b15d2022`, rebased onto `ab948b4676d70a5104288fbb483778554db9850d`; tree `0962b353c4d2fd54769658469e61a0ef27aec851`.

- Independent unpiped `make verify` on this exact head: exit 0.
- Independent six scoped race-enabled PostgreSQL integration tests on this exact head: exit 0. They cover committed-placement grant insert/touch failure and original-attempt recovery, preserved hold and single order, find-order recovery, actual payment/order destination authorization, unrelated/forged-cookie refusal, old carried grants, stale grants and retention bounds. This local run is scoped cart integration, not a claim of a local full-repository integration run. No SQL or migration changed; the full required CI schema suite also passed on the final head.
- Independent production error-propagation mutation on the pre-rebase implementation made `rememberOrder` swallow its error. The committed placement test failed: `grant failure answered 303 See Other ... want 500 server error`, exit 1. Restored source and six scoped tests returned exit 0.
- Independent production premature-cookie mutation on the final rebased implementation wrote the placed cookie before the database grant. All three committed failure tests failed with `grant failure response issued a goen_placed cookie`, `touch failure response issued a goen_placed cookie`, and `find order grant failure response issued a goen_placed cookie`, exit 1. Removed the mutation; clean tracked tree and all six tests passed, exit 0.
- Independent final production-binary browser acceptance with fresh PostgreSQL migration/seed and real role-separated pools: four zh-Hant/en × scripting off/on journeys, native product add and checkout forms at 375px. An injected grant INSERT failure produced the actual post-commit 500 recovery page. Each of four orders existed once, retained one held unit and had zero grants; no proof cookie was issued.
- Native find-order forms under the same fault returned localized lookup-specific 500 pages. Removing only the disposable test fault then allowed all four native POST lookups to return 303 to the correct order (200); the actual Pay link reached an authorized payment page (200). Removing the test browser's proof restored 404 and hid its email. Database checks after recovery still found exactly four orders, each with one held unit and one grant. Mobile and desktop recovery presentation were visually inspected without horizontal overflow.
- Browser runs used local synthetic data with payment/invoice providers disabled and mail logged rather than sent. They do not claim physical-device, Safari, real-provider or full-site acceptance. Original-attempt replay and carried-touch fault coverage above are actual handler/store/database integration tests, not falsely described as browser journeys.

## What was left out

No order/payment/stock transaction redesign, privilege changes, automatic retry loop or provider configuration changes.

## Needs a ruling

None. The existing #115 recovery ruling is implemented. Final exact-head checks and delegated review disposition are recorded at merge time.

author: victoriosas
body:
## Summary
Fixes the production issues visible in the admin Connectors panel.

## Root causes
- `createAutopilotV4Router()` installs a router-level control-plane auth middleware and was mounted before `/api/autopilot/v4/cj-mcp`, so Supabase admin JWTs were rejected as `AUTOPILOT_AUTH_INVALID` before the CJ MCP router could validate them.
- Vercel builds `vercel-api.ts`, which never mounted the legacy `/api/connectors` handler from `server.ts`, so production returned 404 and the UI showed 0 connectors.

## Changes
- Mount CJ MCP before the generic V4 control-plane router so its own Supabase-admin guard is authoritative.
- Add an authenticated production connector directory mounted by `mountAutopilotV4`.
- Include CJ REST+MCP, AliExpress DS, Amazon, Alibaba and governed direct-import status.
- Explicitly disable legacy generative direct-import rather than fabricating commercial facts.

## Safety
No checkout, supplier purchase, auto-order, cron or publication behavior is enabled. CJ MCP remains read-only/shadow and write-capable MCP tools remain blocked.

body:
## The rule

`AGENTS.md` § *User-facing docs terminology* banned an em dash and fixed two words, and said nothing about the writing. The pages had all drifted into the same shape: a not-X-but-Y opener, a triad, a closer restating the paragraph above it. The section now points at the `humanizer` skill, which is the one place those patterns are enumerated.

Paid for inside the 36,000-byte budget by cutting the dash bullet's second clause, which restated its own bold lead. The file is 35,996 bytes.

## The pass

51 pages under `docs/` plus `README.md`. `docs/reference/mcp-api.md` is excluded - it is generated by `scripts/build-mcp-reference.ts`, which the pre-commit hook re-runs.

Six writers worked in parallel, then four reviewers audited the diff against the source. Headings, code blocks, inline code, commands, paths, flags, link targets and frontmatter are byte-identical throughout, verified mechanically: 483 heading lines, 87 fenced blocks, 1,567 inline spans, 533 link targets, 45 frontmatter blocks, one intended heading change.

## Fifteen factual errors, each verified against source before changing

The security ones cluster. Four separate pages asserted, without qualification, a guarantee the code documents an exception to - the model-provider credential the agent's own CLI authenticates with, which `agent-runner.ts` calls "the one exception to the rule that no confidential value enters a run". Two of those pages contradicted the exception stated earlier on their own page.

| Page | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `introduction.md` | "Agents never see real API keys or tokens" | the real value of a secret you store, with the exception named |
| `introduction.md` | "nothing secret enters the sandbox" | scoped to the signing key and the git credential |
| `cloud/overview.md` | "never handed to an agent in the clear" | referenced as placeholders |
| `README.md` | "agents never see your real secrets" | same wording as the security page, exception named |
| `container-isolation.md` | "it can't read your secrets" | the secrets you store |
| `secret-protection.md` | "It never sees them" | plus the exception |
| `cloud/data-and-security.md` | an agent "never reaches the machine holding your instance" | restored to the blast-radius claim it replaced - agents reach that machine every run, through the tunnel |
| `configuration.md` | SSO "without ever being able to read what is in it" | without ever holding the phrase |
| `local-docker.md` | "nothing about a run leaves that machine" | the container sends no run content |

author: vivswan
body:
## What this specifies

```text
Bot review comment arrives (Copilot, any review bot)
  names a concrete input + wrong output in this diff   -> fix in the round, whatever its wording
  speculative hardening (a hostile caller who cannot
    reach the code, "for robustness", a race in a
    single-user tool)                                   -> decline in one sentence, recorded not built
                                                           (rubber-duck-review step 6 owns the >100-star exception)
  style / naming the linter does not enforce, rewording -> decline in one sentence
    (the linter already reports it                      -> resolve, no reply; the red check carries it)
  restated diff, praise, summary                        -> resolve, no reply
  the decline IS the thread's convergence; "Changes recommended" is not a gate
```

```text
pr-landing-discipline        Draft -> Babysit -> Companion Gates -> Line Accounting -> Who Merges
code-standards               Standards -> Workflow -> Review Criteria -> References
craft-skills-and-memories    When to Apply -> Quality Bar -> Creating -> Fixing -> ...
never-twice                  Workflow -> Rung 1 -> Rung 2 -> Rung 3 -> Deleting a Guard -> Review Criteria
no-invalid-states            When to Apply -> Guiding Principle -> Workflow -> Review Criteria
watch-ci-after-push          Workflow -> After a Merge -> Polling Budget -> Sleeping on PR Activity -> Fallback
worktree-hygiene             ... Handing Over -> File Ownership -> One Branch One Worktree -> Shared .git
rubber-duck-review           step 5 (fan out per section) is now step 2; old steps 2-4 are 3-5
```

## How

- **Bot filter:** the check Copilot's `review.instructions.md` asks the bot to apply, run by the author instead, since the bot follows it inconsistently and some repositories have no such file.
- **Section order:** each skill's H2 headings follow the order a cold agent meets them in time. Six skills judged fine and left alone: codex-browser-fix, docs-discipline, natural-writing, orchestrator-mode, pr-and-issue-discipline, verify-with-controls.
- **Pure moves:** every reordered file has the same lines as before, sorted; only pr-landing-discipline gains text, rubber-duck-review renumbers four headings and five citations, and one smoke-test comment follows the renumbering.

## Proof

- **Gate:** `bun run check` green on every commit (1100 tests, validate, smoke); all-green passes on the head.
- **Codex review:** converged on every head; five Copilot rounds, zero open threads.

<details>
<summary>Technical details</summary>

- **Reviewer note (Copilot):** the moves are section reorders; the diff renders them as delete-plus-add blocks. Compare `git show main:<file> | sort` with `sort <file>` to see the content is unchanged.
- **Cross-references checked:** every above/below pointer and step citation in the eleven files, plus the two external citations (pr-landing-discipline cites rubber-duck-review step 7, unchanged; the smoke-test comment moved from step 2 to step 3).
- **Copilot rounds:** round 1 fixed a garbled antecedent; round 2 scoped the hardening bucket so a comment naming input and damage always earns a fix; round 3 pointed the hardening decline at rubber-duck-review's >100-star exception; round 4 fixed the smoke-test citation.
- **Declined (Copilot):** `--find-renames` on the numstat commands (git detects renames by default since 2.9); `pkill -f` versus `--stdin-prompt` and the worktree-hygiene cross-round ownership model (text this PR only moved; a separate change if wanted); dropping the >100-star pointer (round 3 asked for it; one shared disposition beats two).
- **Line accounting:** skill text +132 -122 across 10 files, scripts +1 -1 (a comment); fits a `fix` of skill behavior.

</details>

author: lesanf
body:
Merging this is the release. `master` is the deployment branch and `v0.0.3` gets tagged on it right after.

Everything here came from two things: pushing on what fails *silently*, and building a feature in a generated project instead of reading the template.

## Bugs that would have reached a shipped app

**A crash reporter could kill the boot.** `runStage` called `onStageError` from inside its catch block, so a callback that threw escaped the catch, rejected `runPreloader`, and left the splash up — the app never started. These callbacks run precisely when something has already gone wrong, and the obvious thing to wire into `onStageError` is Sentry. The failure is also recorded before the callback now; a throwing callback used to lose the record it was handed.

**Encoded deep-link params broke routing.** The parser split the path, decoded each segment, joined them, and then re-split the result — so an encoded slash changed the segment count and matched nothing, and the decoded value reached the expo path un-re-encoded (`/(tabs)/menu-4/a b`, a raw space into `router.navigate`). A Korean or spaced id meant tapping a push notification did nothing, in background or killed state, with no log to read.

**Android release signing could fail silently.** The signing patch rewrites `app/build.gradle` by regex against the AGP template. A missed anchor broke two ways, and one of them ships: miss the `buildTypes` rewrite and the release build keeps the **debug key**. One comment line between `signingConfigs` and `buildTypes` was enough to break it — measured, now a regression test. Both anchors throw with the regex to fix.

**The providers boundary was dead where it mattered.** Flat config applies only the last block that sets a rule key, and the cross-feature block reused `no-restricted-imports`, wiping the providers guard for everything under `src/features` — the layer where importing providers is the actual architectural break. The two severities now own one rule key each.

## The structural gap a real app hits

The auth gate pushes `AUTH_LOGIN_PATH` and stores the original intent first so it can be replayed after sign-in. **That route did not exist.** The first app to write `gates: ['auth']` — the ordinary thing to write — landed on `+not-found` with a pending intent already set and no way back. The template ships placeholder screens for every tab; this adds the one its own mechanism requires, and the contract is a single call: `signIn(tokens)`.

Found by building a tab, an API domain, a detail route and a gated deep link in a generated project. Nothing else needed a template change.

## Tests, and then fewer of them

64 tests across 8 suites, and **no native module mocks**. Mocking MMKV, RNFB, notifee and reanimated made keeping the mocks aligned with the real APIs the actual work — MMKV v4 exposes `remove`, not `delete`, and that cost a debugging session. `jest-setup.ts` is gone; what remains runs on pure logic, and screen or store tests belong to the app that needs them.

CI now runs `check-all` on every pull request, which nothing did before.

## Expo decides versions, not npm

`pnpm doctor` and `npx expo install --check` are the standard, written into `AGENTS.md` ④. `react-native` sits at 0.86.3 against npm's 0.87.1 because `bundledNativeModules.json` pins it for SDK 57 — taking npm's number by hand puts codegen and the podspecs out of step.

Xcode 27 replaced `Simulator.app` with `DeviceHub.app`. The fallback is already in `@expo/cli` (expo/expo#46757); verified the `devices://` scheme is registered and `xcrun simctl` still works, so the deep-link and push commands in the docs are unaffected. Nothing for the template to do — recorded so nobody goes looking.

## Verified

```
expo install --check    Dependencies are up to date
expo-doctor             18/18 checks passed
check-all               lint → tsc → 64 tests
```

Earlier in this line: a project generated from this template builds to an installable binary on both platforms, and identity reaches the native projects intact.

**Not verified:** runtime. Nobody has watched the app run — the splash-to-tabs seam, whether `InsetView` removed the tab jank, cold and warm deep links, push, and whether `pnpm ios:development` opens DeviceHub on Xcode 27.
