author: penfoundapps
body:
Closes #713

## Review round 2

- Machine preflight sends each failed check, detail and remediation through the project's logger into `bees.log`. The startup error includes those details for the live view; preflight does not write over the terminal. Project-mode table output is preserved.
- Added a real-process test that holds a machine `--once` pass in a stub `gh`, changes the project list and sends SIGHUP. The original pass finishes normally and the added project never starts.
- Added daemon coverage starting with both a startup failure and a loop error. With Reload open, Run stays alive after both fail; cancellation, closing Reload and reloading a healthy project all finish correctly and preserve both errors. Closing Reload waits for an active project to finish.
- Qualified project-mode preflight exit behavior in the CLI docs and Cobra help; documented per-project machine failures and all-failed machine liveness. Clarified open/closed Reload behavior in the API comments and CLAUDE.md.

## Summary

`bees run` selects one project or a machine's project list from the active config. `-d`/`--daemon` detaches either mode, prints the child pid, and redirects stdout/stderr to an appended log. SIGTERM drains work; machine-mode SIGHUP starts added projects and drains removed ones without restarting unchanged schedulers.

The child owns a pid file and inherited startup lock. Removed schedulers relinquish their queued shared-pool turn while retaining slots held by in-flight work, so removal cannot block the remaining projects.

## Decisions

- Keep existing config precedence and validation, including the nonempty machine list. Reject an invalid reload without changing the running set. Reload membership only: unchanged project settings and the original shared developer pool require a restart to change, as #666 requires unchanged schedulers to stay untouched.
- Rebuild child arguments from Cobra's parsed flags, excluding the detach flag and pinning the resolved absolute config path. This preserves combined short flags and values that look like flags.
- Use `<state_dir>/bees.pid` and `<machine-config-dir>/bees-machine.pid`, exposed as `ProjectPIDFile` and `MachinePIDFile`. Console logs are `bees-daemon.log` and `bees-machine-daemon.log` beside them. A persistent `.pid.lock` file prevents duplicate detached starts; machine configs sharing a directory share this lock/location.
- Apply `--roles`, `--skip-doctor`, and `--once` to every machine project. Normal machine runs stay alive for reloads even if all projects fail; `--once` finishes all single passes and ignores SIGHUP.

## Testing

`dagger check` passed before committing and again after `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main`: lint, code generation, and 1,384 tests; the opt-in real-container test was skipped.

Process tests build the actual CLI with local git clones, disabled roles and a stub `gh`. They cover detach flags, parent exit, process groups, pid paths, duplicate starts, polling, SIGHUP additions and one-pass signal handling, SIGTERM cleanup, console logs, and foreground compatibility. Unit coverage includes reload reconciliation, unchanged loops, shared-pool preservation, queue cleanup, preflight logging and live-view errors, and all-failed daemon liveness.

## Verification

The new preflight regression failed on the previous implementation. Each mutation below compiled and failed the named test; all mutations were restored.

| Disabled behavior | Failing test |
|---|---|
| Project logger for machine preflight | `TestMachinePreflightLogsFailureAndReportsDetailsToView` |
| Machine `--once` reload guard | `TestMachineOnceIgnoresSIGHUPProcess` |
| SIGHUP registration during `--once` | `TestMachineOnceIgnoresSIGHUPProcess` |
| Reload liveness with no active projects | `TestReloadKeepsDaemonAliveAfterEveryProjectFails` |

The first round also verified mutations of mode inference, session detachment, removed-project cancellation, original-pool preservation and shared-queue cleanup.

## Claim sweep and follow-up

Checked docs, code comments and prompts for preflight exit and Reload liveness claims. Updated CLI/configuration/architecture docs, README, docs index, layout notes and affected code comments for the full feature. `git diff --check` passed.

The existing live view takes a fixed project list and does not refresh its selector after SIGHUP. Filed #714 for the separate TUI scope named in #666; documented `--no-tui` for runs that change membership. Detached runs and scheduler reconciliation are unaffected.

body:
The compiler rejected assignments such as `value = try load() catch (error:Dynamic) false`. This blocked the real Neko standard library during exception-provider validation. Variable initializers already accepted the same try expression, but assignment operands became unsupported syntax.

The operand parser now uses the existing try/catch parser, just as it already handles `if` and `switch`. The change preserves assignment precedence and the existing structural recovery. It adds no Math, numeric, or target-specific behavior.

Validation passed:

- Typed-body and native Neko regressions fail before the repair and pass after it.
- Native tests generate source, compile it with `nekoc`, run it, and compare successful and caught-failure local and static-field assignments.
- Typed tests preserve calls, Boolean result types, source lines, and the following return without opaque executable syntax.
- Independent Haxe 4.3.7/Neko controls and `npm run test:m14:hih-expr-text-parser` pass.
- Official formatting, shard registration, mega-file, and typed-backend-body guards pass.

This draft builds on #72. Full local guards and Q3 CI remain pending. A diagnostic replay with the pending String implementation now types the real exception providers and compiles the generated Neko files. Runtime stops at the unresolved stack-trace primitive call during exception construction. Native exception behavior and README readiness claims remain unfinished.

Task: `haxe_ocaml-rkp40`.

## Agent provenance

The native-function-body agent prepared this change while validating real Neko exception dependencies under the reviewed implementation plan. The agent retains responsibility for review fixes, verification, rebasing, and merge. Other agents can review without modifying this branch unless the requester records a handoff.

author: chrischall
body:
First step on #283: a reusable release-please workflow with the `republish_tag` escape hatch built in, **opt-in per repo**, with creditkarma-mcp as the canary. No other repo's rendered stub changes: `validate-render.rb` renders all 82 repos, and `rollout.test.sh` pins the unopted control byte-for-byte.

## What moves, and what deliberately does not

- **`.github/workflows/reusable-release-please.yml`** (new) runs release-please and the contributor credit, then **resolves whether and what to publish**. It does that once, for both paths:
  - a fresh release (`release_created`), or
  - a `republish_tag` dispatch naming an existing tag whose publish never ran (creditkarma-mcp, homes-mcp and onehome-mcp, 2026-09-14).

  It outputs `publish`, `tag` and `version`, and passes release-please's raw `release_created`/`tag_name` through so the deploy fragments keep gating on a real release. A republish never redeploys.
- **The publish job stays in the stub** (`templates/release-please-reusable.yml`). npm validates the caller's workflow file, but `mcp-publisher login github-oidc` has never been proven from inside a called workflow. The composite action already runs in the stub's own job, so its OIDC identity is unchanged. The `workflow_dispatch` input is in the stub too, because a called workflow cannot declare its caller's triggers.
- **`rollout.sh`** renders the new template when `reusable_release` is set. It's a separate template rather than a sed range over the existing one, because an unterminated range runs to end of file and this is the publish path.

## Carried over from the one-off fixes

- **One derivation of the version from the tag, for both paths.** It also handles `<component>-v1.2.3` and `v`-less tags, which the hand fixes' `${TAG#v}` got wrong. It refuses a release-please `version` that disagrees with its own tag.
  - A bare tag is matched first, and a component tag only as `<component>-v<version>`.
  - It is two patterns rather than one with an optional component group, because POSIX leftmost-longest would read `v2.0.0-0.3.7` as version `0.3.7`. Build metadata (`-rc.1+b.2`) is accepted.
- **A republish only reports "does not exist" on a 404.** A 5xx or rate limit says it could not check.
- **Every input goes through `env:`.** Anything that isn't a release tag is refused before a byte reaches `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, so a newline can't define a second output.
- **A republish checks the tag exists**, naming it if not.
- **release-please is skipped on a republish.** The escape hatch shouldn't depend on the next release-please run working.

## Tests

- `scripts/release-ref.test.sh` (new, wired into CI) extracts the shipped step and runs it under `bash -e`: 55 assertions across both paths, component, `v`-less and prerelease tags, version-shaped prerelease suffixes, build metadata, newline and command-substitution injection, a missing tag vs a transient API failure, a missing `tag_name`, and a version/tag disagreement. It also pins:
  - release-please is skipped on a republish
  - no `run:` body contains `${{`
  - the wiring: every output and job-output mapping, the resolve step's env sources, and the credit steps' `if:`

  Mutation-checked: restoring the one-group regex, typing `steps.resolv`, or feeding `RP_TAG` from `version` each fails the suite.
- `scripts/rollout.test.sh` case R covers:
  - the unopted stub is unchanged
  - the opted stub calls the reusable, forwards `republish_tag` and publishes the resolved tag and version
  - every `needs.release-please.outputs.*` the stub or an appended fragment reads is declared by the reusable
  - a pinned `skill-path` still lands inside `with:`
  - `--check` is clean for an opted repo

  130 passed.
- `actionlint` and `validate-render.rb` both pass (661 files across 82 repos).

## Not in this PR, and in order

1. After merge: `scripts/rollout.sh chrischall/creditkarma-mcp --execute --only release-please` (the canary; its hand-edited stub is currently drift).
2. Prove a **real** release end to end on creditkarma through it, and one `republish_tag` dispatch of an already-published tag (idempotent: npm skips a version it has).
3. Only then: flip the default and fan out to the other `release: mcp` repos. The `custom`/`none` repos (fetchproxy, mcp-host, the Swift and nullnet apps) aren't rendered by fleet.json and remain out of scope. Most of the 18 variants in the issue are those.

Refs #283 (not closing: fan-out is still to come).

author: aethr
body:
**Not for merge.** This PR exists to produce a `pr-NNN` image that om-infra
sandbox can point at for the duration of the #244 experiment. Close it when the
experiment is done; if the perturbation turns out to be worth keeping, it should
come back as its own PR off `main`.

## What this adds

`scripts/cmaq_preprocess/perturb_bcon.py`, which offsets a prepared run's
boundary conditions by a known amount in ppb, in place.

[#244](https://github.com/openmethane/openmethane/issues/244) needs to know
whether the residual misfit from #242 is a boundary error or an interior one.
The distinguishing test is whether the *spatial pattern* of the boundary
response covaries with the residual — a uniform offset can absorb a mean bias
either way. Measuring that response needs a forward run against a genuinely
perturbed boundary field.

The forward model reads boundary concentrations from `BNDY_GASC_1` and does not
care how they were produced, so this needs no boundary sensitivity in the
adjoint and no change to `fourdvar`.

## How it fits the pipeline

`correct_icon_bcon` already rewrites BCON in place between `cmaq_preprocess` and
`fourdvar`. The perturbation goes in the same slot, which means no perturbed
copy of the BCON tree and no `BCON_FILE` override. It runs *after* the CAMS bias
correction: the bias correction is part of the standard pipeline and is
identical across experiment arms, and the perturbation is the variable applied
on top.

The forward run itself is the existing `scripts/fourdvar/run_daily_step.py` —
nothing in it is single-day, so under `TARGET=docker-monthly` it runs the month.

Each file records the offset it carries as `OM_BCON_OFFSET_PPB`. The whole
experiment is a difference between runs that differ only in the boundary field,
so a run that used the wrong file is otherwise invisible in its output; reading
the attribute back also makes a second application fail rather than silently
compound.

## Scope

Whole perimeter only, which is what steps 1–3 of #244 need. Per-edge and
per-layer perturbations are steps 4–6, gated on the hypothesis surviving, and
depend on resolving CMAQ's perimeter corner convention first.

## Testing

8 unit tests covering the offset and its units, metadata and format survival,
the recorded offset, refusal on reapplication, refusal on unexpected units, and
no leftover temporary file. Full Docker suite passes (253).

author: mishrasanjeev
body:
## What

Adds the remaining developer entry points from PRD §8.1: `make test`, `make check` and `make e2e`.

- **`make test`** runs `tests/unit tests/security` plus the contract suites `tests/contract tests/connector_harness` in one pytest run with coverage and the 55% floor (the CI unit job), then **`make test-integration`**: `tests/integration tests/regression` against the dev stack's Postgres and Redis. The regression suite runs once, here, so its database-backed test runs. Also `test-unit` and `test-contract`.
  - Integration tests use a separate `agenticorg_test` database, dropped and recreated each run, and Redis index 15. `scripts/reset_test_database.py` refuses any URL whose database does not end in `_test` (some integration tests drop the `public` schema, so pointing them at the dev database would wipe it).
- **`make check`** runs ruff, mypy (preflight's invocation), bandit `-ll`, gitleaks over the branch, the SPDX header check, JSON Schema validation of `schemas/` and pip-audit (project, `requirements.txt`, `requirements-v4.txt`, as CI). `scripts/check_schemas.py` is the schema-validation hook later contract checks extend; it fails closed on unreadable files, missing or unknown `$schema`, or an empty/missing directory. The vendor denylist joins in the next PR.
- Both run in a new **`agenticorg-tools`** image (`Dockerfile.tools`: Python 3.12 as in CI, `.[dev]` dependencies, `requirements-dev.txt`, gitleaks 8.30.1 verified by SHA-256 for amd64/arm64) with the checkout mounted and the host UID/GID, so a clean machine needs only Docker and make. `RUNNER=local PYTHON=...` uses a host interpreter instead. The service is in a `tools` profile, so `make dev` does not build or start it.
- **`make e2e`** runs a new Playwright suite for the local stack (`ui/e2e/dev-stack.config.ts`, 4 tests: API health through the console proxy, sign-in page, signed-out redirect, unknown credentials rejected) in the official Playwright image pinned by digest to the lockfile's 1.63.0, on the stack's network against `http://ui`. It refuses to start when the smoke check fails. The config has no production default, so it cannot reach a hosted environment. npm dependencies go into a container-only volume.
- Docs: "Tests and checks", "Browser end-to-end tests" and a Windows troubleshooting note in `docs/quickstart-local.md`; CHANGELOG entry.
- FINDINGS: A-13 (test runs rewrite tracked `migrations/audit/*.json` and `coverage_report.json`), A-14 (no `.gitattributes`: CRLF shell scripts on Windows checkouts break bash in containers).

This is the first of a stack: the vendor denylist (#1310), OIDC stub (#1311), seed (#1313), model stub (#1318), local Grantex (#1323) and CI gate PRs build on it. Merge in order. Rebased on `main` at 409fc44d.

## Verification

Windows 11, Docker Desktop 29.7 (Compose 5.5), GNU make 4.4.1; compose projects `m0stack-*`, host ports 58310-58336.

In a fresh clone of this branch (`git clone -c core.autocrlf=false`), before the rebase onto 409fc44d:

- `make test` (unit + contract with coverage): **6835 passed, 1 failed**, 10 skipped, 5 xfailed; total coverage 77.05% (floor 55%).

The same test passes in the same image on a Linux filesystem (`git clone` inside the container, then pytest: 63 passed across that file and the two other environment-sensitive files). Documented under Troubleshooting. `make test` on a Linux host is covered by the Local Stack workflow in the last PR of this series.

From the worktree:

- `make dev` then `make e2e`: 4 passed.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_check_schemas.py tests/unit/test_reset_test_database.py`: 20 passed.

Unit + contract alone measured 58.98% coverage against the 55% floor.

author: chinmaydd
body:
CU mode is only meaningful on targets that support WGP execution. However,
`isFullSIMDMode()` currently treats `+cumode` as effective on every target.

On pre-gfx10 targets this incorrectly selects half-SIMD mode, halving both the
physical and addressable LDS sizes. For example, gfx942 reports a 32 KiB limit
instead of 64 KiB, while gfx950 reports 80 KiB instead of 160 KiB. This caused
`CodeGen/AMDGPU/lds-limit-diagnostics.ll` to fail in ROCm CI after #220718.

author: lbjzz-hash
body:
## Why

OD Next Task traces suppressed the legacy Run trace but did not preserve its root input/output and metadata. Full host-composed Prompts could also be truncated at 64 KiB, and the evidence-v2 flags hid missing default-path collection during acceptance.

## Result

Task traces now carry the original user input, final production reply, per-Run metadata, runtime/model/version/error/timing fields, additive current-Turn usage, and the union of trace-owned object manifests. Full policy-redacted Prompt, output and allowed tool content are frozen as immutable `open-design.run-evidence/v1` objects and uploaded through ordinary consented Task delivery. Codex stage and root usage share current-Turn counters; provider-reported cumulative/cache/reasoning counters remain separately available with an explicit scope.

This includes the existing fixes for managed attachments, physical-Run artifact ownership, frozen attachment inheritance, feedback Task ownership, terminal delivery and accepted feedback retry termination. Task-owned canceled Runs use the durable finalization gate without an experimental enable flag.

## Surface area

- [ ] UI / keyboard shortcut / i18n
- [x] API / contract — additive Task root fields, per-Run metadata and trace-owned evidence objects
- [x] CLI / env — existing explicit object `off` / `observe` switches remain; absence of the object mode now enables consented Task evidence delivery. Eval-context-v2 remains separately gated.
- [x] Default behavior — complete consented Task evidence and current-Turn usage no longer require acceptance-only flags
- [ ] New dependency

## Validation

- Real native macOS Electron client built from this branch: attachment selection, initial multi-stage generation, three subsequent edits, rendered counter increment/reset, feedback and stop controls.
- Dedicated synthetic session `523cb064-adb9-42b5-8122-9791964b351b`; the final successful Task is `strategy-task:odnext_f6df6b4ea60b4731846f4cafe7411c24`.
- 14 online objects across the four completed Turns downloaded and SHA/length matched against their local immutable snapshots. All five full Prompt source hashes match the persisted actual send boundary. Final default-mode Prompt: 103,473 redacted UTF-8 bytes, no truncation.
- Final default-mode root/stage usage: 963,631 input + 797 output = 964,428. Provider cumulative total 2,993,516 is retained separately. The preceding default-mode red sample exposed the old usage flag dependency and was not backfilled.
- Real feedback score read back from Langfuse; durable queue accepted once and remained accepted after restart.
- Local modified ODEval read actual online Langfuse and R2 content, validating identity, size and SHA; final successful Task content completeness is complete. R2 GET used a loopback protocol adapter to live authenticated Cloudflare reads, with exact synthetic-session allowlisting, no fixtures.
- 230 focused daemon tests pass; full workspace typecheck and guard pass, with final daemon typecheck after the last terminal-gate edit.

No Vela or telemetry Worker source change is needed. ODEval companion reader/UI: https://code.powerformer.net/core/odeval/pulls/124 ; neither that consumer nor the client has been released by this PR. Existing truncated historical content is not reconstructed. Existing consent, redaction, tool-content policy, object size and retry limits remain enforced; unavailable content is explicit.

Canceled default-mode acceptance: Task `strategy-task:odnext_964654f6396e4371a4dda59aed59b6fe` reached canceled online, retaining input and a Prompt object. The local assistant body was empty, so no output or usage was fabricated.

author: claude[bot]
body:
Fixes #17798

`AGENTS.md`'s merge-queue paragraph named SIX required contexts and called everything else "advisory and rides through". The live ruleset has SEVEN — `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, enrolled 2026-08-27 (#12427) and pinned in `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` by #15233. The sentence a review seat acts on therefore classified the one gate that refuses a zero-review governed PR as advisory, which is verbatim the incident shape that guard exists to prevent.

Nothing reddened on it, and that is the half worth fixing. `mustName` is a FLOOR: it reds when a listed literal goes stale and is blind to one going MISSING. So the registry grew, every surface's list stayed legal, every gate stayed green, and the sentence stayed behind. The same misclassification has now landed twice — 2 to 6 by the #9677 ruling, 6 to 7 here.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

**改了什么。** 两处。一、`AGENTS.md` 的合并队列段落从「六个必需上下文」改成七个,把第七个 `Governed Surface Queue Guard` 写进名单(等行数改写,1075 行没动)。二、`scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs` 的 `INSTRUCTION_SURFACES` 增加一个 `statesTheSet` 声明:声明了它的文件,其名单必须与注册表**逐个且等长**地对上。注册表本身(`REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`)一行未动,那是 #15233 的面。

**为什么改。** 这句话不是描述,是审核席翻 ready / 挂 auto-merge / 入队前照着做的操作指令。它把治理面守卫说成 advisory,而那个守卫的职责恰恰是拒掉零审查的治理 PR —— #12427 的事故形态。更关键的是:上一次入列(#15233 加第七行)时,全部门禁是绿的,没有任何东西提示这句话已经过期。同一个漏洞已经发生两次,所以这次不只是手跟一遍数字,而是把「谁陈述了整个集合」变成机器可查的:下一次(第八个)入列时,加注册行的那个 PR 自己会变红。

**风险与代价(含回滚)。** 风险低。新规则只对**显式声明** `statesTheSet: true` 的条目生效,今天是两个文件(`AGENTS.md` 与 pm-dispatch 的 `platform-readings.md`);`review-checklist.md` 被明确归类为**不陈述集合**(它点名的是审核席亲手确认的两个 job,不是集合),保留它原有的两名下限,集合变大不会误伤它。声明也不能被悄悄摘掉换取豁免:名单已覆盖整个集合却没声明的条目同样变红。代价:每次入列多一处必须同 PR 跟进的数组。回滚 = `git revert`,两个文件都是纯文本,没有生成物、没有发布面、没有数据迁移。

**席位意见。**

**你要做的。** 确认一件事:第七个上下文 `Governed Surface Queue Guard` 今天确实在 Settings 的必需集合里(卡面 2026-09-12 的实测读数是七个,本 PR 不改 Settings)。其余不需要你操作。本 PR 触及受管面 `AGENTS.md`,按 Prime Directive #14 走人工合并或已批准的队列路径。

## What changed

**1. `AGENTS.md` :505-:510 — six to seven.** The seventh name inserted, "six" to "seven" in all three places, equal-line at the 1075 ceiling (before 1075 / after 1075 / ceiling 1075). Each context literal is kept whole on one line: the scan matches them contiguously, and a wrap that split `TypeScript Type Check` across a line break made the surface red. That is a real trap for the next hand-follow, so it is recorded here rather than only avoided.

**2. `INSTRUCTION_SURFACES` gains `statesTheSet`.** An entry that declares it must name the registry EXACTLY — membership *and* count:

- omitting a member reds, naming the omitted literal and the count it is short by;
- padding past the registry length reds on the count, so a duplicate cannot mask a member lost to a typo;
- a full list with the declaration dropped reds ("a list that covers the whole set IS a statement of it"), so the exemption cannot be taken silently;
- ablating every declaration reds rather than ticking (#4690).

`review-checklist.md` is classified the other way and keeps its two-name floor: it names the two required jobs a seat confirms by hand — its own next line sends the seat to `true-green.md` for the rest — so it never claimed to enumerate the set, and the set growing must not red it.

**3. Ten self-test cases, battery floor 31 to 41.** The 6-of-7 omission and its restore-leg ablation; the eighth-row enrolment end to end, plus the hand-off where following the ARRAYS clears the census red and leaves the naming floor demanding the PROSE; the padded duplicate; the undeclared full list; the no-declaration floor; and the two classification pins (which surfaces state the set, by NAME never by count; and the checklist's partial list staying legal).

## Evidence

author: shumoku88-bit
body:
## Question

Can Movement's remaining `relation-` allocator ever exhaust when it allocates multiple RelationUnitIds recursively?

## Observation 248

This PR qualifies the final current production use of the shared numbered-token mechanic.

For one RelationUnit allocation it proves:

```text
used-token count = used.length
fuel             = used.length + 1
-> search cannot return none
```

It then mirrors the production recursion:

```text
choose fresh id
prepend id to used
allocate the remaining ids with the new used.length + 1 budget
```

and proves by induction that this process succeeds for any requested count and returns exactly that many ids.

## Why this matters

Together with Observations 243–247, every current production use of `firstUnusedNumberedToken?` now has a finite totality argument under its existing fuel policy:

- ActualValidity Date Revision
- Correction replacement EventId
- Capacity across two evidence families
- Scheduled occurrence
- Movement record EventId across five evidence families
- Movement recursive RelationUnit allocation

## Deliberate boundary

Production remains unchanged. If this observation qualifies, the next question is no longer caller-specific: whether the shared `Option`/fuel API itself has become an obsolete partial abstraction and can be replaced by a total finite-namespace primitive without importing proof machinery into production.

## Files

- add `Loam/Observations/Observation248.lean`
- import it from `Loam/Observations.lean`

Production files changed: **0**.

NVSwitch firmware updates use SCP to copy firmware onto NVOS. The firmware worker and the `update-strategy ssh copy` command both leave bare IPv6 addresses unbracketed, so SCP cannot separate the host from the remote path correctly.

author: vhadianto
body:
## Why

Turbot Pipes bundles this binary into its `workspace` container image, where trivy reports **CVE-2026-56854 (CRITICAL)** against it. The fix lands in `golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0`; `develop` is currently on `v0.53.0` and the newest release is on `v0.52.0`.

Pipes pins the released version, so this cannot be patched from the Pipes side — it clears only once a release is cut against x/crypto >= 0.55.0.

## What this does

`go get golang.org/x/crypto@v0.55.0 && go mod tidy`. No source changes. As usual for an x/crypto bump, the rest of the `golang.org/x` family moves forward as transitive minimums (`net`, `sys`, `term`, `text`, `mod`, `tools`).

Pipes made the same `v0.54.0` -> `v0.55.0` bump for its own server binary in v1.22.46 with no call-site changes.

## Related

`turbot/steampipe` develop is already on x/crypto `v0.55.0` and needs only a release. This PR brings this repo in line.

Follows the same pattern as turbot/steampipe-postgres-fdw#695 (Go toolchain rebuild for CVE-2026-39821), which Pipes picked up in v1.22.47.

## Verification

`go build ./...` passes cleanly with the bump.

body:
Foundation 16. A página inicial e o catálogo ganham título, descrição e imagem de compartilhamento editáveis no editor (Configurações gerais → "Como a loja aparece no Google"). Até aqui o título da página inicial estava escrito no `app/layout.tsx` e a descrição vinha de `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_DESCRIPTION`, lida no build: mudar o que o Google mostra pedia deploy.

## O que muda na loja gerada

- **`lib/seo-das-rotas.ts`** (novo): `ROTAS_COM_SEO`, a lista que o layout declara ao editor com o título e a descrição que cada rota emite hoje, e `metadadosDaRotaDoCodigo`, que as duas rotas usam no `generateMetadata`.
- **`app/layout.tsx`**: passa `rotasComSeo` ao provider; título padrão e sufixo vêm de `lib/seo-das-rotas.ts` (o CLI carimba o nome da loja lá, `src/theme.js`).
- **`app/(loja)/page.tsx` e `app/(loja)/produtos/page.tsx`**: `generateMetadata` lendo o publicado.
- **`lib/editable/`**: `document.ts` e `provider.tsx` da foundation 16, idênticos ao editor e à esteira.

## As decisões

- **Sem edição, nada muda.**
- **Título da página inicial sai como o lojista escreveu** (`absolute`); no catálogo o `title.template` põe o nome da loja no fim, e o painel mostra isso antes de salvar.
- **Open Graph repetido por inteiro** quando há edição, com a imagem social da loja se o lojista não escolheu outra.
- **Sem "ocultar de buscadores"** nestas rotas.
- **O SEO das rotas não vai ao navegador**: quem lê é o `generateMetadata`.

## Como foi verificado

- Quatro estilos gerados deste branch: `npm run build` = 0 nos quatro, `tsc` = 0, eslint limpo nos arquivos alterados, `check-unbox-brand` e `check-template-neutro` passando. Página inicial e catálogo seguem estáticas com ISR (○, 5 min).
- **Sem edição, comparado com a v0.21.6 no HTML servido** (mesmo estilo, mesma loja): o `<head>` da página inicial e do catálogo sai igual, campo a campo (`title`, `og:*`, `twitter:*`, canônica).
- **Com edição**, loja lendo de um editor falso que serve um documento publicado com `seoDasRotas`:
  - página inicial: `<title>Café Aurora | Café especial torrado na semana</title>`, meta description, `og:title`, `og:image` e `og:image:alt` com o que foi escrito;
  - catálogo: `Todos os cafés · <nome da loja>`, descrição escrita, imagem social da loja no cartão;
  - `/devolucoes` intacta; `rotasComSeo` presente no HTML e `seoDasRotas` ausente.

## Junto, no editor

A PR do editor (unbox-plus/unbox-editor#1) também corrige o **CSS do lojista da v0.21.5, que nunca ia ao ar**: a rota pública não entregava o campo. A loja não precisa mudar nada para isso.

## Loja já gerada

Lista no bloco da v0.21.7 do `CHANGELOG.md`. Só atualizar `lib/editable/` deixa a loja como estava: sem `rotasComSeo` no layout, o editor não oferece o bloco.

author: meziantou
body:
## Problem

A scheduled transaction with a monthly recurrence could generate one transaction per day.

After each generated transaction, the next occurrence was computed with `RecurrenceRule.GetNextOccurrence(previousOccurrence + 1 day)`. The recurrence library anchors the rule on the date it is given, so this restarted the rule from the day after each occurrence. For rules that do not pin a day, that day is itself a valid occurrence:

| Rule | Expected | Before this fix |
|---|---|---|
| `FREQ=MONTHLY` | 08-10, 09-10, 10-10 | 08-10, 08-11, 08-12 |
| `FREQ=WEEKLY` | 08-10, 08-17, 08-24 | 08-10, 08-11, 08-12 |
| `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=10` | correct | correct |
| `…;COUNT=3` | stops after 3 | never stopped |

Schedules created from an existing transaction were not affected because they get `BYMONTHDAY=<day>`, which is why the bug only showed up on some schedules.

## Fix

- Added `ScheduledTransaction.GetOccurrences(minDate)`, which always enumerates occurrences from `StartDate` and skips those before `minDate`. It keeps the existing guard against rules that don't move forward.
- `ProcessScheduledTransaction` uses a single enumerator from that method to advance `NextOccurenceDate`, instead of re-querying the rule from the last date.
- `GetPendingOccurrences` (projected balance) and `GetNextOccurences` (scheduler page list) use the same method, so `INTERVAL` and `COUNT` are relative to the start date everywhere.

## Notes for reviewers

- Existing schedules that already went wrong fix themselves: their next date moves to the correct occurrence after the stored `NextOccurenceDate`. Extra transactions that were already generated are not removed.
- Occurrences are now enumerated from `StartDate` on each processing pass, so the cost grows with the schedule's age. It is negligible in practice, and editing a schedule already resets `StartDate` to the next occurrence.

## Tests

Added 5 tests to `DatabaseTests.cs` (monthly rules with no day, "create next occurrence", `COUNT`, and `GetNextOccurences`). All 5 fail without the fix and pass with it. The core test suite passes (44 tests) and the solution builds with no warnings.

author: knroy
body:
316 commits since `v1.2.2` (2026-09-05). Minor bump: the exported API only
gained surface. `CompileVersion`, `CompileXQuery` and `CompileVersionRefFloor`
are deprecated in favour of `CompileWith` but still present and still
delegating, and `go.mod` is unchanged, so no caller breaks.

### Why this is a PR rather than a push to main

CI runs on `main` and on pull requests, not on `dev`. None of these commits has
been through GitHub CI — they were gated locally on darwin/arm64 only. This PR
is the first time Windows and Linux see any of it, which is the largest
untested gap in the release.

### Conformance at the head of this branch

Measured with `-count=1`, every lane that ran passing:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| XSLT 3.0 | 11492 / 11518 (99.77%) |
| XSLT 2.0 | 6193 / 6201 (99.87%) |
| QT3 XPath 2.0 / 3.0 / 3.1 | 15217 / 19362 / 21898 — 100.00% |
| QT3 XQuery 3.1 | 30345 |
| XSD 1.0 / 1.1 | 39358 / 41567 agree |
| RELAX NG | 965 / 965 |
| DocBook / XSpec | 577 / 225 |

Verdict: `VERIFIED WITH GAPS — every lane that ran passed, 2 did not run`. The
two are UBL and CII, licensed corpora that cannot be cloned in CI.

### Highlights

- **Security.** Two DoS vectors bounded (DTD content-model stack exhaustion,
  RELAX NG pattern-size on the attribute path) and two output-injection vectors
  closed at the serializer (`doctype-system` literal breakout, `media-type` in
  the `<meta>` tag).
- **Memory.** Four quadratic paths made linear: XSD chain walks (370x), the
  namespace count per element (1,327x), adjacent text-node merge (46x), and
  result-tree construction, which was bounded by nothing and is now charged
  against `xpath.MaxNodes`.
- **Conformance.** The §19.8 streamability analysis, all 272 function
  signatures bound against their declared types, and the `map:`/`array:`/`math:`
  families made expressible.

### Risk

The unexercised surface is Windows and Linux path handling. Everything else has
been gated locally, repeatedly, with sabotage verification on each fix.

body:
## Problem

Resource Tag search stopped all key events, so users typing in Literature or Settings could not move through matching Tags or activate Create with the keyboard.

## Proposed change

Use the existing Popover/Input components as a searchable combobox. Up/Down move through matching Tags and the final Create option; Enter toggles the highlighted Tag or creates and assigns the entered name. With no matches, Create is highlighted directly. Keep input focus, show assignment checkmarks separately from navigation, guard IME confirmation and duplicate pending writes, and preserve newer input across asynchronous completion.

## Scope and non-goals

The shared picker covers Literature table/detail and Skills, Connectors, and Specialists. Preserve each consumer's keep-open policy. The full Tag editor and filters are unchanged. No added dependencies, backend/API changes, data migrations, persisted enums, or schema changes. Only transient picker state is added; existing create and assignment writes remain separate operations with recovery coverage for partial failure.

## Acceptance criteria and validation

- Keyboard/search/create/retry/pending/IME/focus/controlled-open/resource-change behavior -> `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/pages/settings/ResourceTagControls.render.test.tsx` -> 13 passed.
- Consumer and store boundary -> focused Vitest run of the above plus LiteratureLibraryPage, TagsPanel, SkillsPanel, ConnectorsPanel, SpecialistsPanel, SettingsPage render tests, tag-store, popover render tests, and i18n/resources -> 10 files, 1,476 tests passed. Owner tests rerun after the final visual edit.
- Renderer typing -> `npm run typecheck:web` -> passed.
- Repository lint and formatting -> `npm run lint`, targeted Prettier check, `git diff --check` -> passed.
- Web bundle -> `npm run build:web` -> passed (existing bundle/CSS warnings).
- Actual authenticated localhost Web in an isolated temporary database -> keyboard selection and creation persisted; Tab advanced to the next table control; Escape retained the Literature detail/Settings parent and returned trigger focus. Literature and Skills screenshots captured. Picker remained within viewport at 320/375/414/768px.

Checks describe the final implementation; lint/typecheck and focused picker tests were rerun after edits. Two independent standards/spec reviews found no actionable findings and confirmed the impact mapping. No full local npm test run, per maintainer request. The impact classifier reports unknown module ownership for this renderer area and therefore requests full CI fallback; PR Gate is authoritative. No main-process, filesystem, or cross-platform persistence code changed, so backend/platform tests are left to CI. Native Electron, screen-reader announcements, and touch input were not directly exercised.

## Review focus

Accessible active-vs-assigned state, nested-popover dismissal, IME Enter, and stale async completion. Existing failure behavior may leave an unassigned Tag when create succeeds but assignment fails; retry selects that existing Tag without creating it again.

body:
## Qué hace

Aplica en producción las migraciones **51, 52 y 53**, que estaban en el repo pero no en el registro, y corrige lo que salió roto al hacerlo.

Estado previo comprobado: la **53 ya estaba aplicada de verdad** por fuera del registro (`clubs.tema` con su CHECK, su comentario y el `WITH CHECK` de `clubs_update`, y 2 de 13 clubes ya en `red`). La 51 y la 52 no existían. El bucket `support-screenshots` no se había creado a mano, así que no había capturas huérfanas.

Cada migración se ensayó antes con `begin; <migración>; <arnés>; rollback;` y una comprobación de que no quedaba rastro.

## Bugs corregidos

**1. `listBlockedUsers()` pedía `profiles.nombre`, que no existe.** PostgREST no omite la columna: rechaza la consulta entera con `400 / 42703`, así que «Usuarios bloqueados» habría quedado vacía sin explicación. Estaba tapado porque antes fallaba con `PGRST205`, que el servicio sí sabía tratar. Es la cuarta vez que el repo tropieza con `profiles.nombre`, así que el `select` pasa a un módulo puro probado contra el esquema versionado, igual que la nómina y los cambios.

**2. El caso 2b del arnés de la 51 no probaba nada.** Medía `count(*)` actuando como B, y `blocked_users_select_own` deja ese conteo en 0 pase lo que pase: no distinguía «no pudo borrar» de «sí borró», y contradecía al caso 2a. Ahora mira el `row_count` del DELETE y vuelve a comprobar como A. La RLS de la migración estaba bien.

**3. `anon` podía sondear el grafo de bloqueos** (migración 95). El `revoke execute ... from public` de la 51 no cerraba nada: Supabase concede EXECUTE a `anon` directamente por *default privileges*. `is_blocked_pair` es SECURITY DEFINER, se salta la RLS y devuelve un booleano para cualquier par de UUID — y la clave anon va dentro del bundle. Verificado: antes `200 false`, ahora `401 permission denied`. `get_advisors` bajó de 67 a 64.

`authenticated` conserva las tres funciones, y tiene que conservarlas: `friendships_insert` evalúa `is_blocked_pair` con el rol de quien inserta. El arnés de la 95 tiene un caso dedicado para que una revocación de más no pase callada.

## Alcance que dejo fuera a propósito

Las **64 funciones SECURITY DEFINER restantes** ejecutables por `anon` son deuda de todo el esquema. Varias podrían usarse sin sesión a propósito (`buscar_complejos`), así que cerrarlas en bloque rompería flujos reales. Requiere revisión una por una.

## Verificación

- `npm run verify`: lint **0 errores**, **1292/1292** pruebas
- Comprobado por el mismo camino HTTP que usa la app: tablas en 200 (se acabó el `PGRST205`), RPC llegando al cuerpo de la función (se acabó el `PGRST202`), `clubs.tema` en el select explícito, bucket existente
- Temas de club intactos: 13 clubes, `red:2` / `green:11`, antes y después

> **Nota para la otra Mac:** las cuatro migraciones ya están aplicadas y registradas en producción. Al hacer `pull` vas a ver archivos que no hay que correr.

body:
Second 0.6.0 item, "files in, results out": a worklist task can take local files as inputs.

## Summary

- **The route is Drive.** Uploads return only an id with no read route, and the worklist API is not publicly documented. The one response that reveals an upload's storage path is the Drive attach response (`value: s3://…`). `client.worklists.upload_inputs(folder_id, paths)` uploads and attaches each file and returns those paths; `DriveFile.value` is a typed field now. Files stay in the folder, visible and deletable, which also answers the orphaned-upload concern in #53.
- **CLI**: `--input FILE` (repeatable) and `--folder` on `worklists create` and `edit`, plus an `input_files` list in the YAML that `--input` pre-fills. On save each file is uploaded and its path appended to `input_s3_file_paths`. Default folder is `worklist-inputs`, created on first use. A missing file fails before any request.
- **Live probe (General agent, everything deleted after)**: a `needs_review` task created with the attach `value` was accepted and read back unchanged. A task created with the bare upload id was accepted too, so the API validates nothing in that field and a wrong path fails at run time. Whether an executing run reads the Drive-attached object needs a real run and is called out as unverified in PROGRESS and TODO.

## Verification

- `tests/test_worklist_inputs.py`: 11 tests over respx covering the client helper (sync and async), the codec, and the CLI flows including folder discovery and creation, the YAML key, edit appending to existing inputs, and the missing-file guard.

author: danhumphrey
body:
The last of Copilot's findings on #107, and the one that needed a protocol rather than a patch.

## The problem

A scan fans out: each frame collects its own elements and publishes them separately. So the first model to arrive is the **first** frame's finish and says nothing about the rest — and the panel treated it as the end, clearing *Scanning the page…* while the tree was still working.

The second half is worse than cosmetic: a frame still scanning when the user pressed **Delete Model** put the model straight back, with a fraction of its rows. That is worse than either keeping it whole or losing it.

## Completion rolls up

- A **delegated** frame reports `SCAN_DONE` to the parent that asked it, once its own collection has finished *and* every child it delegated to has reported.
- The frame the user actually **clicked in** sends `SCAN_COMPLETE` to the background instead. That single message is what ends the indicator.
- A frame that never answers is dropped when its acknowledgement times out, so one unreadable frame cannot hold the scan open for ever.
- The panel also has a 60s ceiling. A frame navigated away mid-scan never reports, and a spinner that never stops is a worse failure than one that stops early.

## Hauls name their session

`ELEMENTS_PICKED` and `ELEMENT_PICKED` now carry the picking nonce — the one the panel already mints per session and every frame already holds. The background learns it by watching `START_PICKING` go past (the only place it can: panels never talk to tabs directly) and drops a haul whose session has ended. **Delete Model ends the session**, which is what stops the revival.

A haul with no nonce is still accepted — that is a message mid-flight across an extension reload, and the nonce is an anti-revival guard, not authentication.

## Verification

End to end on `frames.html`: several hauls, **exactly one** completion, and that completion **last** — re-checked after a further second so a straggler would fail it.

Mutation-checked both ways:

- report without waiting for children → the ordering assertion fails
- drop the session guard → the deleted model comes back

`npm test` green: **78 Playwright + 390 unit**.

Two hand-checks added to `docs/MANUAL-VERIFICATION.md`, since this is the part automation is worst at: the indicator must outlast the first rows on `frames.html`, and Delete Model during a scan must stick.

#1041, comment 5673831824** — the finding's full statement; the seat was
owner-approved this session (recorded on #201, disposition comment 5673240254
item 2). Two of the wave's four absorb conflicts were pure display order over
the same sets, and #995's executed-set growth means every full-gate branch
rewrites the pair — #1040's branch touched no D6 subject matter and carried the
churn anyway. The countermeasure is the one that analysis demonstrated in a
throwaway copy, re-derived here at this branch's own head: a `_disp()` helper
that renders sets sorted at the `eq()` render site, plus the one-time re-record
of the pair. The property, not the instance: an AST scan of every `eq()` call in
the file finds exactly two set-valued callers (C120, C121); every other set
render in the generator already routes through `sorted(...)`. Both render arms
of `eq()` now route sets through `_disp` — the result line (live today) and the
truth arm (latent: no set-valued claim is false today, measured, so the truth
arm's routing changes no emitted byte).

This pull request deliberately leaves **#1041 open** — it is the defect's
standing artifact — and leaves #201 open; its issue faces (#995-class churn, the
wave's absorb conflicts) stay recorded on #1041.

## Head

`c86e5e8` (branch `fix/d11-d6-sorted-sets`, merge base `4f2a90b` =
`origin/main`). Round 1 blocked `eb8463f` merge-prep only (comment 5674372049):
main's rows and this branch's row append at the same plan-table anchor. Main
then moved twice under the absorb — `c62210e` (#1049) and `4f2a90b` (#1050) —
and each was merged with the same resolution: the union in merge order (#1049's
row, then #1050's row, then this branch's #1051 row), every row byte-identical
to its parent, each merge verified by diffing both parents (each side's diff
shows exactly the other's row and nothing else); `git merge-tree --write-tree
origin/main HEAD` now exits 0. All generator figures were first executed at
`4d15d054`, the countermeasure commit; `git diff 4d15d05..HEAD --
tools/audit/round4/D6/` is empty, so the authored content is byte-identical to
the reviewed tree, and every figure was re-executed at `c86e5e8` after both
merges — seeds 1/2/3 byte-identical, two unset-seed generations byte-identical
to the committed pair, RESULT counts base == head, scoped gate re-run green
both times. No figure was carried from the #1041 analysis.

## Mutation proof

Failing first at base `fdd30fa` (the unmodified tree): three runs of the
generator differing only in `PYTHONHASHSEED` produce three pairwise-different
pairs, and the whole diff is the C120/C121 set-order lines. Seed 1 vs seed 2 in
`claims.json`:

```
<   "result": "documented={'heat', 'auto', 'off'} measured={'heat', 'auto', 'off'}",
>   "result": "documented={'off', 'auto', 'heat'} measured={'off', 'auto', 'heat'}",
```

(seed 3 prints `{'heat', 'off', 'auto'}`; C121 churns the same way over its four
elements.) The failing test writes itself, the shape `defect-root-cause.md`
bounds a fix-shaped countermeasure by: two `PYTHONHASHSEED` runs of the same
tree differ before, match after.

Mutation, on a scratch copy of the render line only — `_disp` left defined, the
f-string reverted to raw `!r`: seeds 1/2 re-run and the divergence returns on
the same two C120/C121 lines; the line was restored and the tree re-verified
byte-identical to the committed regeneration. The predicate that moves is the
render, not the helper's mere presence.

## Null control

- **Verdict identity.** All 125 `(id, verdict)` pairs are identical between the
  committed pair at `fdd30fa` and the regenerated pair — 122 true, 1 false
  (C105), 2 unverifiable (C109, C111) on both sides; zero mismatches.
- **No meaning changes.** The only result fields that move are C120's and

- **Migration shape.** `git diff` of the pair is exactly two lines per file —

- **RESULT lines.** `claims_extracted=125 … claims_true=122 …` are identical
  across all three seeds at base and at the fix; only `load1` varies, a machine

- **No-churn (the standing-cost half, #995's face).** At the fix head a second

- **Claims nothing.** `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt` and

## Figures

- Failing-first and after — instrument: the generator itself,
  `PYTHONHASHSEED=<seed> PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round4/D6/claims.py`,
  run at seeds 1/2/3 at `fdd30fa` and at the fix head, pairwise `cmp` of the

author: vhadianto
body:
## Why

Turbot Pipes bundles this binary into its `workspace` container image, where trivy reports **CVE-2026-56854 (CRITICAL)** against it. The fix lands in `golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0`; `develop` is currently on `v0.53.0` and the newest release is on `v0.52.0`.

Pipes pins the released version, so this cannot be patched from the Pipes side — it clears only once a release is cut against x/crypto >= 0.55.0.

## What this does

`go get golang.org/x/crypto@v0.55.0 && go mod tidy`. No source changes. As usual for an x/crypto bump, the rest of the `golang.org/x` family moves forward as transitive minimums (`net`, `sys`, `term`, `text`, `mod`, `tools`).

Pipes made the same `v0.54.0` -> `v0.55.0` bump for its own server binary in v1.22.46 with no call-site changes.

## Related

`turbot/steampipe` develop is already on x/crypto `v0.55.0` and needs only a release. This PR brings this repo in line.

Follows the same pattern as turbot/steampipe-postgres-fdw#695 (Go toolchain rebuild for CVE-2026-39821), which Pipes picked up in v1.22.47.

## Verification note

`go build ./...` cannot complete in my environment — the cgo packages need the PostgreSQL headers (`postgres.h`, `fdw_helpers.h`), which fail identically on unmodified `develop`, so that is pre-existing and not caused by this change. All 5 non-cgo packages build cleanly with the bump. CI should be treated as the real check here.

body:
## What this does

**SQ-21 — upstream connect-error classification.** A bare `ECONNREFUSED`/`ECONNRESET`/`EPIPE` from the local shim looked identical to a fully-dead gateway. This classifies `e.code`, names the failing component ("the local gateway proxy" for a local target, the origin host for an external one), and gives transient error codes wait-and-retry wording versus a concrete `model-gateway status`/`doctor` next step for everything else.

**SQ-22 — codex 429 response rewrite.** A codex 429 previously passed through opaquely, so Claude Code rendered a self-contradictory Anthropic-usage-limit message for a limit that was never Anthropic's. The rewrite names the codex backend, states the limit is upstream's, includes `Retry-After` when the backend sends it, and stops asserting an unverified shared rate pool across all gpt-* picker models. A follow-up commit (f2bb078a) corrected the initial 429 guidance after measured traffic data (2026-09-14) contradicted the shared-pool assumption — one model saw 420 429s across 2423 requests while a sibling model on the same backend served 140 requests with zero, so the message no longer rules out trying a sibling gpt-* model, and a backend change (claude-*, grok-4.5) remains the reliable escape.

Also updates `docs/getting-started/model-gateway.md` with the new 502/429 wording (agent-facing-surface rule in CLAUDE.md), and adds `plugins/model-gateway/test/gateway-upstream-errors.test.js` with unit coverage for both message builders plus end-to-end coverage through a real serve-shim worker, and a regression test asserting the 429 message never again claims a shared rate pool or rules out sibling models without pool-level evidence.

author: marius-kilocode
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A new Agent Manager worktree can display an old merged pull request that it never belonged to, and merge or review actions on that PR fail with `The pull request is no longer open.`

Agent Manager derives a worktree branch from the session title, so a repeated title recreates the branch name of an already merged PR. `gh`'s finder, and the batched lookup that mirrors it, resolve a PR by head ref name and return the newest merged or closed PR of that name. The worktree therefore inherited a merged PR whose commits are not in its history.

Concretely, PR #12726 (`fix(cli): speed up local recall searches`, merged 2026-08-03) used branch `optimize-kilo-local-recall-performance`. Running the same task title again created a worktree with the identical branch name, and the card showed #12726.

## Why This Change Was Made

The branch name is the only key GitHub has, so the lookup itself is correct. The mistake is attributing a non-open PR to a checkout that does not contain it. A merged or closed PR is now kept only when the checkout can contain it:

- open and draft PRs are always kept, with no git calls
- `HEAD` equals the PR head
- the PR head is reachable from `HEAD` and the merge commit is not, which covers a merged PR with local commits on top

It is dropped when the PR head is not reachable from `HEAD` (squash or rebase merges, closed PRs, a recreated branch name), or when the PR's merge commit is reachable (the branch was cut from the base after the merge).

The same guard runs for both the batched result and the legacy `gh pr view` result, because both had the same attribution. The batched GraphQL query gains one scalar field (`mergeCommit { oid }`) and `gh pr view --json` gains the same field, so there is no extra request, no extra rate-limit cost of note, and no lookup at worktree creation. For open PRs the guard adds no git work at all.

Branch name deduplication at creation was deliberately not extended. `WorktreeManager.availableBranch` already suffixes names that exist in `refs/heads` or as a worktree directory, but the old branch was deleted locally and on the remote, so only GitHub still knew the name. A `gh` check at creation would add a network round trip and a dependency to worktree creation, and would only cover that one collision source.

## User Impact

A worktree that only reuses a merged PR branch name no longer shows that PR. Worktrees that genuinely sit on a merged PR keep the merged badge, including PR review checkouts and PRs checked out through `refs/pull/N/head`, and open PRs are unaffected.

Within a running extension session, a card that already shows the wrong PR keeps it until the next reload (`retainPRStatus` intentionally keeps a known PR when an empty result arrives for the same branch). New worktrees are correct immediately.

## Evidence

Agent-executed:

- `bun test` on `am-pr-utils`, `am-pr-status-bridge`, `am-pr-batch`, `am-pr-seed`, `agent-manager-arch`, `gh` from `packages/kilo-vscode`: 321 pass, 0 fail. New coverage: 7 unit cases for the guard, `mergeCommit` parsing, and a batched full-sync case for the recreated branch name.
- `bun run lint` and `bun run knip` in `packages/kilo-vscode`: clean. `parsePRResult` optional OID fields were extracted into a helper to stay under the complexity limit.
- Live check against the reported worktree (`optimize-kilo-local-recall-performance`, HEAD `2d9c6eda1b7`), with the guard fed real `gh pr view` output and real `git` history: #12726 (squash merge, head `1fb15ce`) is rejected, and PR #14135 (merge commit PR whose merge commit is the worktree HEAD) is rejected.
- `bun run typecheck` in `packages/kilo-vscode` reports 216 errors from a stale SDK/dependency build in this worktree (`KiloClient.v2`, missing `@opencode-ai/core/kilocode/zero-id`). The same count and the same errors occur without this change, and none are in the touched files.

## How to Test

Agent-executed manual verification, using the real worktree and live GitHub data (no writes to the repository):

1. In a worktree, run `gh pr view <branch> --json state,headRefOid,mergeCommit` for a branch name that matches an old merged PR. It returns the merged PR.
2. Run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <pr head> HEAD` in that worktree. It exits non-zero, so the PR is not in the checkout.
3. The worktree now shows no PR badge instead of the merged PR.

Reviewer steps:

1. Create an Agent Manager worktree whose session title matches an earlier merged PR's session title, so the generated branch name matches that PR's head ref.
2. Confirm the worktree card shows no PR.
3. Create a worktree from a branch that is at a merged PR's head (or use the PR import flow) and confirm the merged badge still appears for that PR.

author: geoffreycoulaud
body:
Delivers sections 3.B and 3.C of `docs/specs/2026-09-15-raw-sql-audited.md`, deletes the backlog item
the lot closes, and carries the handoff, this being the lot's last code block.

**The import's last activity stopped being nullable.** `lastUploadActivityAt: Instant?` is
`lastActivityAt: Instant` on the entity, the model and the column. The value is the request's instant
before a single chunk arrives, so the "upload" in the name was a lie and the nullability was the model
saying the column should never have been one. The abandonment sweep asks
`.lastActivityAt.lessThan(instant)` where it asked
`raw("coalesce(last_upload_activity_at, requested_at) < ?")`, which was the audit's second symptom.
`UserDataImportCreator` captures `clock.now()` once and gives it to both columns; a second call is a
second instant, and the grace would then count inactivity from one the request never had.

**The record the gate holds.** `RawSqlOutsideInventory` holds the inventory itself, a map from SQL
fragment to the reason the query beans cannot express it, and reports a `raw(` call whose argument is
not one of those fragments, or is not a string literal at all. Four fragments remain, thirteen calls
over eight files, and the first three share one reason. It freezes fragments and not call sites: a
sixth sort strategy reusing `id <= ?` is the same forced call and passes, while a genuinely new shape
is a new fragment by construction.

## Evidence

- **Gate**: `dagger call gate` green at the branch's tip, and again on `pre-push`.
- **The two sweep behaviours**: `UserDataImportRepositoryTest` passes its four abandonment cases
  unchanged in substance, a row whose upload never started swept on its request instant and one whose
  upload stalled swept on its last chunk. The only edit to them is the field's name.
- **One instant, not two close ones**: the new creator case stubs the clock `returnsMany
  listOf(now, now.plusSeconds(1))` and asserts `requestedAt == lastActivityAt`. Restoring the second
  `clock.now()` fails it with `expected: <2026-08-14T10:00:00Z> but was: <2026-08-14T10:00:01Z>`.
- **The rebuild keeps its indexes**: removing the two `create index` lines from `1.26.sql` fails
  `MigratedSchemaIndexesTest` with `expected: <[]> but was: <[ix_user_data_imports_user_state,
  uq_user_data_imports_active]>`, and fails `UserDataImportRepositoryTest`'s second-active-import case
  as well, the partial unique index being the only authority on it. Block 10's guard is what sees the
  first; nothing saw it before.
- **The rule is red on both shapes**: adding
  `.raw("id in (select pin_id from images where content_hash = ?)", contentHash)` and
  `.raw(contentHash, contentHash)` to `PinRepository.pinIdsByContentHashQuery` makes
  `:api-persistence-sqlite:detektMain` report `RawSqlOutsideInventory` at both lines, the first naming
  the fragment and the second saying the inventory can never see the SQL it runs. Both reverted.
- **The rule is green over the real sources**: `:api-persistence-sqlite:detektMain` passes, so the
  thirteen calls that remain are all in the map.
- **The inventory is the measured one**:
  `grep -rhoE --include='*.kt' 'raw\("[^"]+"' */src/main | sed -E 's/raw\("//;s/"$//' | sort | uniq -c`
  gives `5 id <= ?`, `5 id >= ?`, `1 id > ?`, `2 name collate nocase = ?` over eight files.
- **Diff**: 354 counted lines against 600, 178 production under `api/` against 200. The handoff is
  outside the count as a dated document; `1.26.sql` and its model file are inside it, at 60 lines.

## Tier-1 fixes

One, the spec's sixth pitfall. `PartialUniqueIndexStates.kt:28` cited `uq_user_data_imports_active`
as `1.21.sql:2`; it is at line 46, which `grep -n` on that file confirms. Its two sibling pointers are
right and are untouched.

## Tier-2 questions

None asked. One judgement call is recorded under Departures rather than as a question, because it was
inside this block's own scope and not an adjacent defect.

## Pitfalls

- **The generator refuses this migration outright.** Ebean's strict mode throws
  `IllegalArgumentException: DB Migration of non-null column with no default value specified for:
  user_data_imports.last_activity_at` before writing any `.sql`, though `model/1.26.model.xml` is
  already on disk by then. So the model file is generated and `1.26.sql` is hand-written, which is
  what the bodies of `1.22`, `1.23`, `1.24` and `1.25` already are. `DbMigrationModelCoverageTest`
  asks for a model file beside each `.sql`, and there is one.
- **The drop had to leave `pendingDrops`.** The generator records the old column's removal as a
  pending drop, expecting a `<version>__dropsFor_<version>` pair (`1.13`/`1.14`); the rebuild applies
  it inside `1.26`, so the `<dropColumn>` sits in the `apply` changeSet instead, which the XSD allows
  and `1.14__dropsFor_1.13.model.xml` already writes that way. Left as a pending drop it blocks the
  next `generateDbMigration` outright with `Pending un-applied drops in versions [1.26]`, which is how
  it was found.
- **The check that the model file is honest is a second run.** `generateDbMigration` on the committed
  state answers `no changes detected - no migration written`, which is the only thing that says the
  recorded schema and the entity model agree.
- **The fill runs before the copy, not inside it.** `TableRebuildColumnsTest` splits the three column
  lists on commas, so a `coalesce(a, b)` left in the `select` reads as two columns and breaks the
  equality it asserts.
- **`ReturnCount` is two**, and a hand-rolled walk over a string template's entries also left a null
  branch on a platform-non-null array that no test could reach: the package sat at 98.913% against a
  100% bound. `psiUtil`'s own `isPlain()` and `plainContent` answer the same question with no dead
  branch, which is the third commit.
- **A changed detekt rule is not picked up by a live Gradle daemon** (`api/AGENTS.md`):
  `./gradlew --stop` before trusting a local run.

## Departures from the block table

One, and it is the first pitfall above. The block table and section 6 both say the migration is
generated; this one cannot be, the generator stopping before it writes a script. The model file is
still generated, `1.26.sql` is written by hand on `1.24.sql`'s shape, and the `<dropColumn>` is moved
out of the generated `pendingDrops` changeSet into the `apply` one so the history stays replayable and
the next generator run is not blocked. Everything else in the row is as written: the two sweep cases,
the equal instants, both indexes present in `sqlite_master`, the second active import still refused,
and the rule red on each of the two shapes.

author: tomb3214
body:
## Summary

Reconciles query execution in `internal/postgres/search_content.go` by setting `enable_bitmapscan = on` (while keeping `enable_seqscan = off`) in read-only transactions for scoped queries. In PostgreSQL, GIN indexes (such as `idx_messages_content_trgm` and `idx_tool_calls_input_trgm`) only support bitmap index scans. Keeping bitmapscan enabled allows PostgreSQL to leverage the GIN trigram indexes rather than falling back to nested-loop b-tree scans across thousands of sessions, resolving the 47-second query timeout on scoped full-text searches.

author: elias-ouafi
body:
## Ce que fait cette PR

`plan.md` listait huit pistes pour l'étape 1, classées le matin depuis la littérature. Deux ont été implémentées et mesurées, **protocole pré-enregistré avant de lancer quoi que ce soit** pour que les chiffres ne puissent pas être choisis après coup. Les deux sont négatives — et ce qu'elles ont fait apparaître en chemin compte plus que l'une ou l'autre.

## Les mesures

| | ROC-AUC patient |
|---|---|
| Ligne de base (§4.7) | 0,457 [0,369 – 0,544] |
| **Piste 1** — warm start de l'encodeur sur l'étiquette par coupe | 0,426 [0,338 – 0,513] |
| **Piste 3+** — top-k puis score relatif à la médiane de l'examen | 0,465 [0,382 – 0,551] |
| Statistique **sans aucun modèle**, 224 / 384 / natif | 0,433 / 0,431 / 0,451 |

## Le résultat qui compte

Le diagnostic ajouté pour ces runs (AUC par coupe hors-pli, jamais utilisée comme critère de sélection) montre **0,502 après le warm start et 0,510 après MIL, dans les cinq plis**, avec une perte qui converge à 1,2364 contre un plancher calculé de 1,2323 pour un prédicteur qui ignorerait l'image. L'encodeur n'apprend rien, même depuis une étiquette dix fois plus dense et localisée en profondeur : **le goulot n'a jamais été l'agrégation**, ce qui retire les pistes 3 à 5.

En creusant : une statistique d'une ligne (99ᵉ percentile) trie les coupes peintes à **0,732 intra-examen** contre **0,532 mise en commun**, et le CNN entraîné fait 0,592 / 0,464 sur la même séparation — **battu par du numpy sur sa propre tâche**. Sur la vraie question, aucune statistique ne bat le hasard non plus, là où se trouvent aussi les trois têtes entraînées.

**Trouver la lésion annotée n'est pas détecter un cancer** : deux tiers des coupes peintes de ce corpus sont des lésions bénignes.

## Deux hypothèses testées et réfutées, pas supposées

- normaliser sur le tissu plutôt que sur un volume à 54 % d'air : **0,520**, pas mieux que 0,532 ;
- la résolution : identique à 384 px, et **0,451 [0,352 – 0,556]** sur le DICOM brut en résolution native, avec la cellule de grille de 96 px de Buda et al.

La luminosité ne porte pas cette question, à aucune échelle mesurée. La **forme** si — et elle demande des features apprises sous la supervision la plus riche disponible, les **boîtes**. C'est le cadrage avec lequel Buda et al. atteignent 65 % de sensibilité à 2 FP/sein, et la suite retenue.

## Pour le relecteur

- La piste 2 a abouti côté données pendant ce temps : 60/60 patients du split test téléchargés, 121/121 séries, **30 patients cancer complets** → le corpus annoté passe de 56 à 86 patients cancer. Nécessaire, plus suffisant, donc pas la prochaine dépense.
- Le garde-fou à regarder en priorité : `test_the_warm_start_never_reads_a_held_out_patients_slice`. L'étiquette par coupe vient des mêmes annotations que l'étiquette d'examen, donc pré-entraîner sur un patient tenu à l'écart ferait fuiter sa réponse une couche sous la validation croisée.
- **Run B (top-k seul) est annulée**, avec sa raison écrite dans `plan.md` §4.9, pour qu'elle ne se lise pas comme un résultat non publié.
- Trois erreurs de la journée sont consignées plutôt que gommées : la piste 1 citait un chiffre de DCE-MRI pour un modèle DBT, un test de contraste comparait une boîte à une coupe à moitié composée d'air, et un débit de téléchargement a été annoncé depuis un processus figé depuis 40 minutes (`tcia_utils` n'a pas de timeout, il a bloqué 2 h 30).
- Rapports versionnés pour les deux runs, checkpoints non — même règle que le reste de cette tête.
- 208 tests passent, `ruff` propre.

author: ciercier
body:
## Problem - Selecting a clipboard entry with ~1MB binary data (or payloads containing interior null bytes `\0`) caused `glib-rs` to panic with `GStrInteriorNulError` in `gtk::TextBuffer::set_text`, leaving the GTK UI unresponsive. - Non-URI binary payloads with newline delimiters caused `parse_uri_list_bounded` to run `Url::parse()` synchronously on tens of thousands of lines on the main GTK thread. - Monolithic un-broken text payloads up to 1MB pegged the CPU during Pango word-wrapping and layout. - The Nix development shell omitted package dependencies via `inputsFrom`, `import nixpkgs` lacked an explicit `config = { };`, and the NixOS module passed a derivation to `mkPackageOption`. ## Solution - **UI & Preview Protection**: - Bound full preview layouts to 64 KiB (`MAX_FULL_PREVIEW_BYTES`) so large text entries layout smoothly in `TextView`. - Detect binary payloads (`is_binary_payload`) containing null bytes and render `[Binary data — copy the entry for full content]`. - Sanitize any residual null bytes before `set_text` to prevent `glib-rs` FFI panics. - Bound lines scanned in `parse_uri_list_bounded` (`URI_LIST_PREVIEW_MAX_SCANNED_LINES = 1000`). - **Hierarchical Phase & Memory Profiler**: - Add `rsclip_core::profiler` supporting phase timing, memory tracking via `/proc/self/status` RSS, and tree reporting. - Instrument preview and details rendering phases under `RSCLIP_PROFILE=1`. - **Nix & Flake Improvements**: - Adopt `inputsFrom = [ rsclip ];` in `devShells.default` to cleanly share build and native build inputs. - Explicitly set `config = { };` when importing `nixpkgs`. - Fix NixOS module package option using `lib.mkOption` with `defaultText`. - Fix upstream `cargo fmt` formatting in `notify.rs` and `state.rs`. ## Verification - `nix develop --command cargo fmt -- --check`: passed - `nix develop --command cargo clippy --all-targets -- --deny warnings`: passed - `nix develop --command cargo test`: all 108 tests passed - `nix flake check`: all 9 checks passed - `nix build`: package builds successfully ## Limits - None --- Created by Gemini with Antigravity CLI.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The PR appears safe to merge, with a non-blocking inconsistency in profiler totals that should be corrected.

Findings

1.  **Nested Phases Are Double\-Counted** ▶

Summary

This PR bounds clipboard preview work, safely handles NUL-containing payloads, adds opt-in hierarchical profiling, and corrects Nix development-shell and module configuration. - Limits text layout and URI parsing performed on the GTK thread. - Substitutes a safe notice for binary previews while preserving full entry copying. - Adds nested timing and RSS reporting around preview rendering. - Shares package inputs with the development shell and fixes the NixOS package option. Reviews (1) · Last reviewed commit: ["refactor(nix): adopt idiomatic nix best ..."](https://github.com/jr4dh3y/rsclip/commit/c07b76469ddd9a0e9d29cbe3e43f1dc8bc030a8f) ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Binary content in previews now displays a clear notice instead of blank or unreadable output. - Optional performance profiling provides phase timing and memory usage reports. - **Bug Fixes** - Text previews safely handle embedded null characters. - URI list previews stop scanning after 1,000 non-empty, non-comment lines, preventing excessive processing. - **Changes** - Reduced the maximum full preview size to 64 KiB; larger previews are clearly marked as truncated.

author: frankekn
body:
## What

- `review.yml`: the `runner` input has no default. With it empty the workflow passes no `--runner`/`--model`/effort and skips the explicit Codex version check; the runner host's self-managed bundle (its loader) pins the lane.
- `review.yml`: job `timeout-minutes: 75`, a 55-minute `NEEDLEFISH_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_MS` default (host value wins), a 60-minute process watchdog, and a watchdog kill closes the pending Needlefish check as a failure.
- `review.yml`: `codex_reasoning_effort` is exported only when non-empty, so an empty caller input cannot wipe a host-pinned effort.
- `hosted-review.yml`: lane inputs removed.
- Explicit `runner: codex` still requires Codex CLI 0.153.4 and defaults `gpt-5.6-terra` to `high`; explicit `xhigh` keeps the 20-minute timeout and `fast` tier.
- Existing tests, README, README.zh-TW and CHANGELOG updates remain in this PR.

## Follow-up: preserve proxy restrictions (#147)

Closes #147

Commit `efb24013fb1b25b27028627de8451ed8b1d268fc` changes only two existing files relative to `bd77579`: `.github/workflows/review.yml` (+12/-12) and `scripts/review-workflow-release.test.mjs` (+119/-3). No new runtime module, dependency, input, service or routing framework.

- Forward non-empty `codex_proxy_required` independently of runner selection. Leaving the runner empty cannot discard this restriction.
- Empty required input retains a stricter host policy.
- No caller URL/key: retain the host pair. Either caller value: replace **both** fields, including an empty counterpart. Never combine a caller URL with a host credential or silently discard an incomplete caller pair.
- Explicit Codex still rejects a half pair before invoking Needlefish, with a safe message explaining that review has not started and settings must be completed.
- Delegated Codex validates the forwarded configuration through the existing `runCodex` / `resolveCodexProxyConfig` owner. Non-Codex runners do not perform irrelevant Codex validation. No provider/auth fallback was added.

### Tests

- [x] Local: 27/27 shell/selection tests pass (existing 14 plus 13 new forwarding/error cases).
- [x] Regression check: the same 11-case forwarding matrix fails 7 cases against the original workflow and passes with this fix.
- [x] YAML parses and the review shell passes `bash -n`.
- [x] Both uploaded file blobs match the bytes tested locally.
- [ ] Latest-head [full CI run 35065774740](https://github.com/frankekn/needlefish/actions/runs/35065774740): running at last check.
- [ ] Latest-head [automatic review 35065774922](https://github.com/frankekn/needlefish/actions/runs/35065774922): queued at last check.
- [ ] Required delivery qualification / controlled live canary before release.

The 14th new test replays the shell-captured configuration through the **real** `runCodex` boundary. Incomplete Codex pairs must reject before model execution; accepted/non-Codex configurations use an expired deadline to stop immediately after validation. This case needs the repo's tsx/dependencies and is covered by full CI, not the local 27-test claim. No real model/provider calls are made by these tests.

Local network access cannot download the full repository/dependencies. Previous-head CI results are not claimed as proof for the new head. This follow-up is delivery/configuration plumbing; prompts, model context, finding admission and verdict rules are unchanged. Gate classification and actual release evidence still follow AGENTS.md.

## Why

Consumers were re-editing their workflows for each lane change. Lane selection belongs to the runner host; explicit caller safety restrictions must still survive that delegation.

## Consumers and rollout

Consumers recorded previously pin `review.yml@bd775793534c67ea11994b0b3616854c0db2728b`. **Those immutable pins do not receive this fix automatically.** Update to a reviewed fixed SHA during rollout. No consumer repository, operator installation, credential, permission or branch-protection setting was changed by this follow-up; this PR remains unmerged and undeployed.

## Summary

- raise the Axum WebSocket frame limit to the existing 256 MiB request limit
- add a regression test for WebSocket requests larger than 16 MiB

## Root cause

The route already raised `max_message_size`, but Axum still enforced its default 16 MiB `max_frame_size`. A large Codex request could therefore close the socket while the client was writing it and surface as `Broken pipe (os error 32)`.

## Validation

- verified the new test reproduces `Broken pipe (os error 32)` without the fix
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

- 364 unit tests passed, 1 ignored
- 98 `gateway_http` integration tests passed
- release binary black-box check sent a 16,777,435-byte WebSocket message, forwarded 16,777,399 bytes upstream, and received `response.completed`

Two unrelated `gateway_startup` tests hit their existing 3-second local startup timeout during the broad suite.

author: pupiltong
body:
## What

A BTS entry that throws during startup no longer destroys the view. It is reported the way any web worker script failure is: at the MTS `Worker`'s `error` event, surfaced to the embedder as a nonfatal `EngineEvent::WorkerFailed`. The BTS realm stays up and keeps taking messages, `backgroundReady` follows, and `ScriptFinished` is still published.

- `packages/bobcat-element/src/worker-runtime.ts`: the worker global scope gains WHATWG `reportError`. It creates an unhandled rejection, so the checkpoint that ends the current entry reports it through the existing `WorkerPayload::Errored` path.
- `packages/bobcat-element/src/background-thread-runtime.ts`: the bootstrap calls `reportError` for a rejected entry and posts `backgroundReady` once the entry has settled, success or failure. Messages queued behind the import are delivered either way instead of being dropped after a failure.
- `packages/bobcat-element/src/main-thread-runtime.ts`: the `backgroundFailed` branch and the `error` listener are gone. The `__bobcat:close` listener calls the idempotent `notifyReady()`, so a BTS Worker that ended before readiness (`Failed`: realm could not be built, thread trapped) still settles boot rather than leaving the view loading forever.
- `crates/bobcat-core/src/main/runtime/lib.rs`: the `reportStartupFailure` host binding is deleted and `readiness` is a plain `Rc<Cell<bool>>`. `ScriptFinished` now means "MTS boot completed and BTS startup settled" (doc updated in `view/lib.rs`).
- `AGENTS.md` and the four runtime docs describe the new behavior.

## Why

Since #240 a BTS throw was routed `backgroundFailed` → `reportStartupFailure` → `StartupFailed` → view cancelled. In the ReactLynx census this failed 38 pages that native Lynx (`appManager.ts` loadCard catch) and web-core merely log. The BTS is a Worker started by MTS and must have a Worker's semantics: HTML's "run a worker" reports the exception and goes on running the event loop.

## Tests

- `worker_tests`: `a_throwing_bts_entry_reports_at_the_worker_and_leaves_bts_running` pins one `WorkerFailed`, no `StartupFailed`, `is_ready()` true afterwards, the worker still live, and a global event reaching a listener the entry registered before it threw.
- `page_tests`: `a_bts_worker_that_fails_reports_worker_failed_and_settles_boot` sends a `Failed` payload and pins one `WorkerFailed`, one `ScriptFinished`, and an uncancelled view token.
- `lifecycle-runtime.test.ts`: a worker `error` event does not touch readiness, `__bobcat:close` settles it, and a rejected entry calls `reportError` once, posts `backgroundReady`, and still delivers the message queued behind it.
- `cargo test -p bobcat-core` (full crate, 312 lib tests), `cargo clippy -p bobcat-core --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check`, `pnpm -C packages/bobcat-element test` (159) and `test:type` all pass.

## Reviewer notes

- Out of scope but included: the three `verify_react_teardown` tests in `worker_tests.rs` have been red on main since #241 (CI run 34875791220). They indexed `message[0]` on the JSON *object* `wire_json` has produced since #239, so their filter never matched. Changed to `message[..]`.
- Ordering: in practice `backgroundReady` reaches MTS before the `error` event, because the rejection is only surfaced at the checkpoint that ends the entry. Embedders may therefore see `ScriptFinished` before `WorkerFailed`; neither test depends on the order.
