author: carlosjmunoz78
havogt
body:
DON'T REVIEW HERE: changes are split into separate PRs.

## Description

Five compile-time optimizations of the gt4py toolchain that leave the generated code unchanged: byte-identical gtfn C++ and SDFGs on every program checked (list below).

### Motivation: where the compile time goes

[C2SM/icon4py#1460](https://github.com/C2SM/icon4py/pull/1460) merges velocity advection into two programs. In icon4py's CI the slowest stencil test variants of the merged predictor take 525-529 s each on `gtfn_cpu` and 608 s on `dace_cpu`. These are the `none` static variants: the program is compiled with no static arguments, so domains stay dynamic, on the MCH R04B09 grid (`--grid=icon_regional`).

Measured for that program with `GT4PY_BUILD_JOBS=1 GT4PY_BUILD_JOBS_MODE=serial CLANG_FORMAT_EXECUTABLE=/bin/false`, no other load:

| `compute_velocity_advection_in_predictor_step`, gtfn_cpu, R04B09, no static args | seconds |
|---|---|
| total | 355.4 |
| GTIR `apply_common_transforms` | 300.2 (84 %) |
| g++ (one translation unit, compile + link) | 42.1 (12 %) |
| cmake prototype (once per build cache) | 6.3 |
| gtfn lowering + codegen | 6.3 |

So for gtfn the cost is gt4py's GTIR passes, not the C++ compiler. With static bounds on icon4py's simple grid the same program takes 65.5 s (GTIR 40.5 s, g++ 17.0 s).

In a cProfile of the GTIR translation (861 s profiled), three generic costs of the pass infrastructure stood out, besides the domain-bound growth addressed in the follow-up PR:

- 104M `isinstance` checks against eve node classes go through `typing_extensions._ProtocolMeta.__instancecheck__` (109 s cumulative). `eve.concepts.Node` inherits the `Protocol` metaclass of `trees.Tree`, which makes such a check ~300-375 ns instead of ~30-50 ns.
- `copy.deepcopy`, 208 s cumulative: 135 s from `NodeTranslator.generic_visit` copying immutable leaves (`SymbolRef`/`SymbolName` str subclasses and `SourceLocation` go through `copy._reconstruct`), 73 s from `ITIRTypeInference.apply` deep-copying a tree that `SanitizeTypes` has just rebuilt.
- `CombinedFixedPointTransform.transform` evaluates `enabled_transformations & transformation` for every transformation on every node: 11M `enum.Flag.__and__`, 27 s cumulative.

On dace (predictor, static bounds, simple grid: about 144 s through icon4py) the profile matches icon4py's: networkx VF2 `syntactic_feasibility` 2.4M calls, `map_fusion_helper.is_node_reachable_from` 36,624 calls. Most of the pattern-matching time is in the two transformations whose pattern is a pair of unconnected MapEntry nodes, `HorizontalSplitMapRange` (73,887 `can_be_applied` calls, 5 applied) and `MapFusionHorizontal` (86,516 calls, 7 applied). Both called `is_parallel`, which walks the whole state twice, before the checks that reject most pairs cheaply.

### Changes

1. **`perf[eve]: nominal isinstance checks for Node classes`**: `eve.concepts.Node` gets a metaclass derived from the `Protocol` one, with `type.__instancecheck__`/`type.__subclasscheck__`. Node classes are concrete and nothing registers virtual subclasses of them, so the answer is the same.
2. **`perf[eve]: do not deep-copy immutable leaves in NodeTranslator`**: `None`, `bool`, `int`, `float`, `complex`, `str` (including `ConstrainedStr` subclasses), `bytes`, `Enum`, `SourceLocation` and `SourceLocationGroup` are shared rather than copied. The copies were equal objects.
3. **`perf[next]: avoid a second full copy of the tree in type inference`**: `SanitizeTypes` already rebuilds every node. When `inplace=False` it now deep-copies the preserved annex values itself, with one shared memo, instead of `ITIRTypeInference.apply` deep-copying the whole rebuilt tree. The result is equally independent of the input.
4. **`perf[next-dace]: cheap checks before is_parallel in horizontal map fusion`**:
   - `HorizontalSplitMapRange.can_be_applied` now tests the common source and the range split before `is_parallel`.
   - gt4py's `MapFusionHorizontal.can_be_applied` now tests scope, schedule and `find_parameter_remapping` before calling DaCe's `can_be_applied`. DaCe runs these same checks too, but only after `is_parallel`.
   - All checks are free of side effects, so only the evaluation order of a conjunction changes.
5. **`perf[next]: resolve enabled transformations once per fixed-point pass`**: a `cached_property` holds the ordered bound `transform_*` methods of the enabled transformations.

### Effect

Replays of the same translation input (see *Reproducing*), same machine, serial:

| translation time, seconds | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|

author: dereuromark
body:
Closes #1709.

markup-carve/carve#2025 declares `denial` a PROCESSOR-side observable. This
adapter recovered it by asking the engine a second question with the target in
place, which is the right instrument - but two branches in front of that never
reached the engine.

````ts
const candidate = path.isAbsolute(request) ? request : path.resolve(base, request)
if (existsSync(candidate)) return 'outside-root'
if (path.relative(dir, candidate).startsWith('..')) return 'outside-root'
````

`path.resolve` collapses `..` lexically, which is exactly what the new vector
pair exists to distinguish, so both halves were answered without
`fileSystemResolver` being consulted at all.

## What changed

The existence check stays, but only to decide whether a probe has to be WRITTEN.
The refusal itself is the engine's, asked for again with the target in place.

The lexical dot-dot test is gone. It sat behind the existence check and no
vector's candidate resolves outside the fixture tree, so it never fired: dead
code, not behavior. Measured - restoring it in front of the existence check reds
one test and no vector.

The shape the probe genuinely cannot answer - a request resolving outside the
fixture tree, which cannot be made to exist without writing somewhere the fixture
does not own - now throws by name rather than guessing a class.

## The seam, pinned

A per-vector assertion: every filesystem vector stating a denial class must have
consulted the resolver for it. Driven one vector at a time, so the row that stops
asking is the row that reds. `no-root` is the one class with no engine to ask,
and it is gated by its empty `resolverCalls` instead.

The corpus has no vector that reaches the new throw, so a test drives one by
hand. A guard nothing reaches is a guard nobody can trust.

## Mutation proofs

| mutation | assertions that go red |
| --- | --- |
| restore the `existsSync` shortcut | 8, including both halves of the new pair |
| restore the lexical dot-dot shortcut | 1, the unreachable-probe test |
| let the probe leave the fixture tree | 1, the unreachable-probe test |

## Verified

| | |
| --- | --- |
| include-security conformance | 89 assertions, green |
| `test:includes` | 106 assertions, green |
| full suite | 21695 passed, 60 skipped |

No vector was shrunk or skipped.

## Also

The module header still described `chargedBytes` as summed here from what the
resolver handed back. That stopped being true at #1704; the code reads
`result.chargedBytes` and explains why at the site. The header now says so.

body:
## What you asked for (my reading, confirmed)

> "the Total field is not aligned to the left field, so it should be like [a] row"

The **Total (auto)** box in *Crew Attendance (Simple)* was the only cell in the
field row carrying a second line — the `Manual total (rate back-derived)`
checkbox. That made the cell ~40 px taller, and because the row is
`align-items-end`, every neighbour got pushed **down** while Total stayed
**up**:

```
                 ┌──────────────┐
                 │ Total (auto) │ [340000]      ← floated above the row
                 └──────────────┘
                   ☐ Manual total (rate back-derived)
  Worker Type   Days   Workers/Day   Rate/Day   Date   ← pushed down
  [Mason   ]    [17]   [10]          [2000]     [..]
```

## Fix

- **Every crew field cell is now exactly one label + one control.** Nothing
  inside a cell can add a second line, so Total shares one baseline with Days /
  Workers per Day / Rate — on desktop and on the phone's two-per-line wrap.
- **The checkbox moved below the field grid**, next to *Add Crew Entry* (as you
  chose), so the row itself stays straight.
- Project / Stage widened to `col-md-4` so both field rows fill all 12 columns
  with no ragged right edge.

## Bug found while doing it (same field)

The manual switch was wired backwards: ticking *Manual total* **disabled** the
Total box, and a disabled input is not submitted — so a hand-typed total could
never reach the route that expects to read it (`total_manual` + `total_amount`,
rate back-derived server-side).

Now: auto mode fills a **read-only** Total (`days × workers × rate`, worth a
read-only box because the route ignores a typed value anyway); manual mode makes
Total **typable** and shows the rate worked back from it. Unticking restores the
exact rate you had typed, so the 2-dp rounding of the derived rate can never
drift the saved total (without this, 17×10 tap-through drifted 330,000 →
330,000.60).

## Tests

- New `test_crew_field_row_stays_on_one_line`: one label + one control per cell,
  no `form-check`/button inside the grid, the manual switch stays outside it,
  the Total box is never disabled, and the first six cells stay in order
  (Worker Type · Days · Workers / Day · Rate / Worker / Day · Total · Date).
- Full suite **136 tests OK** (was 135); `check_layers`, `check_db_safety`,
  `reorganize_frontend --check`, `compileall` and the fresh-database smoke flow
  (0 errors) all green. Inline page JS passed `node --check`.
- Verified end-to-end against a scratch instance: manual entry (5 × 4 workers,
  total 50,000) posted, showed `50,000` + the `M` badge, labour cost KPI moved
  700,000 → 750,000, row deleted → back to 700,000. No payment/contract code
  touched, no endpoint or field renamed.

Docs: `SUBCONTRACT_SIMPLE_ATTENDANCE_PLAN.md` gained a *Follow-up (2026-09-15)*
section recording both defects and the chosen behaviour.

body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD004 MD041 -->

## Ticket / Issue Number

N/A (reported directly by the downstream repository `avita-co-jp/adt-web-backend`)

## What's changed

Trivy reports 22 HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities against the `secretenv` binary embedded in the container images of the downstream repository `avita-co-jp/adt-web-backend`, which installs it via `go install github.com/hakadoriya/secretenv/cmd/secretenv@v0.0.5`. All of them come from indirect dependencies. This PR bumps every dependency so that the resulting binary satisfies the Fixed Version of all 22 findings.

| Module | Before | After | Fixed Version required by Trivy | Findings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `golang.org/x/crypto` | v0.41.0 | v0.57.0 | 0.55.0 | 11 (`ssh`, `ssh/agent`, `ssh/knownhosts`) |
| `golang.org/x/net` | v0.43.0 | v0.59.0 | 0.56.0 | 5 (`html`, `idna`, `dnsmessage`, `http2`) |
| `google.golang.org/grpc` | v1.74.2 | v1.83.2 | 1.83.2 | 4 (xDS, RBAC, HTTP/2) |
| `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` | v1.36.0 | v1.46.0 | 1.41.0 | 1 (CVE-2026-29181) |
| `golang.org/x/text` | v0.28.0 | v0.42.0 | 0.39.0 | 1 (CVE-2026-56852) |

- `go.mod`, `go.sum`: bumped via `go get -u ./... && go mod tidy`. Direct dependencies (`cloud.google.com/go/secretmanager`, `github.com/1password/onepassword-sdk-go`, `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/*`) are bumped as well, because the affected modules are all indirect and MVS pulls them up through the direct ones.
- `go.mod`: the `go` directive moves from `1.25.1` to `1.26.0`. This is not optional: keeping `1.25.1` makes `go build ./cmd/secretenv` fail with `go: updates to go.mod needed`. The downstream builder image is `golang:1.27`, and the CI workflows here resolve the toolchain from `go-version-file: go.mod`, so both sides are fine with 1.26.
- `CREDITS`: regenerated with `gocredits -skip-missing .`, because `.goreleaser.yaml` runs `make ci` (which ends with `git diff --exit-code`) as a release hook and would otherwise fail the release.

## Check List

- [x] Assign labels (`build`)
- [x] Assign reviewers (`hakadoriya/owner`, `hakadoriyaco`)
- [x] Assign assignees (`ginokent`)
- [x] Add appropriate test cases (no test case is added: this PR changes no production code, only dependency versions)

## Remark

- Verified against the actual Trivy scan target, which is the built binary rather than `go.mod`:
  ```console
  $ CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /tmp/secretenv ./cmd/secretenv
  $ go version -m /tmp/secretenv | grep -E 'otel|x/crypto|x/net|x/text|grpc'
  	dep	go.opentelemetry.io/otel	v1.46.0
  	dep	golang.org/x/crypto	v0.57.0
  	dep	golang.org/x/net	v0.59.0
  	dep	golang.org/x/text	v0.42.0
  	dep	google.golang.org/grpc	v1.83.2
  ```
- `go test ./...` passes. `golangci-lint run` reports the same 12 pre-existing issues (9 `exhaustruct_v5`, 3 `wrapcheck`) on `main` as on this branch, so this PR introduces none.
- Supersedes the open Dependabot PR on `dependabot/go_modules/dependencies-a93014a7cd`, which stops short of the required versions (x/crypto v0.49.0, x/net v0.52.0, x/text v0.35.0, grpc v1.79.3).
- A new tag (`v0.0.6`) has to be released after merging, so that `avita-co-jp/adt-web-backend` can pin to it.
- Note that `govulncheck` in the same downstream CI run reports `No vulnerabilities found` -- none of the affected packages (`ssh`, `html`, xDS server) are reachable from `secretenv`. Bumping is still the requested and cheapest fix; issuing a VEX statement instead was not pursued.

- probe the branch with `Get a reference` before deletion and accept only its HTTP 404 missing-ref result as idempotent success

- GitHub documents missing refs as 404 for Get a reference, while Delete a reference documents 204/409/422 rather than a 404 missing-ref contract

body:
## Qué cambia

Fase 1 · PR-4 del rediseño de plazas fijas. Para vacaciones o una lesión, la plaza fija se **pausa con fechas** en vez de quitarla:

- La plaza sigue **ACTIVA y conserva su sitio** (la exclusión de sitios solo mira las activas). Entre esas fechas no se le reserva la clase y vuelve sola al acabar.
- Poner la pausa suelta **solo** las reservas de esas fechas, por el mismo camino que quitar la plaza: sin penalización, promociona la lista de espera, y mantiene las que ya están dentro del plazo de cancelación.
- Quitar o acortar la pausa pasa el motor por esa plaza: las semanas que vuelven quedan reservadas al momento.
- **Ficha:** botón de pausa en cada plaza con su diálogo. La fila dice «Pausa programada del… al…» o «En pausa hasta el…».
- **Bandeja:** una plaza en pausa ya no sale como «sin clase».
- **App de la alumna:** la próxima clase se salta la pausa y la tarjeta dice que está en pausa.
- Exportación de datos y artículo de ayuda al día.

## Migración — ⚠️ AÚN NO aplicada en producción

`20260915090000_plazas_fijas_pausa_con_fechas.sql`:
- Columnas `pausa_desde` y `pausa_hasta` con CHECK: van las dos o ninguna, y el fin no puede ser anterior al inicio.
- `materializar_plazas_fijas` y `plazas_fijas_sin_materializar` se saltan las fechas en pausa. Misma firma y grants reescritos: solo `service_role`.
- `editar_serie_desde` copia la pausa al partir una plaza. Grants: `authenticated` y `service_role`.

Se aplica antes de mergear, con el OK del fundador; el fichero se renombrará a la versión sellada.

## Verificación

- Drill SQL `scripts/verify-plazas-fijas-pausa.sql` ejecutado en producción dentro de una transacción con ROLLBACK, todo OK. Comprobado después que no quedó nada.
  - Qué cubre: CHECK, el motor saltándose la pausa, sin avisos durante la pausa, al quitarla se reserva al momento, mover la serie conservando la pausa, y grants.
- `tsc --noEmit` limpio.
- Unit tests: 5.504/5.504.
- E2E `plaza-fija-editar`: 11/11, con 3 nuevos que llevan contador de peticiones en el camino de fallo.
- ⚠️ `student-plaza-fija` no se ha podido correr en local: otra sesión ocupaba el servidor de pruebas. Lo valida CI.
- Revisión de seguridad sin bloqueantes. De sus mejoras, está aplicado que no se pueda poner una pausa que empiece dentro de más de un año.

## Límites conocidos

- Quitar la pausa puede reservar la clase de hoy o mañana, si hay sitio. El diálogo pide avisar a la socia. Lo mismo ya pasa al crear una plaza y con el cron.
- Si se guarda una pausa justo mientras corre el cron de las 02:00, podría quedar una reserva dentro de la pausa. La ventana es mínima.

body:
Source-read record, not a behaviour change — read against `main` @ `2e3b48548025f3019c37ebec3b3a972d3a633229` (0.26.3).

Adds `docs/route-parity.md`, covering:
- Which routes have `chatWithTools`/`chatWithToolLoop` at all (Anthropic, Gemini, SambaNova, Mistral — full parity) vs `chat()`-only (direct OpenAI, DeepSeek, claude-cli) — named as a structural fork, not a degradation. No Qwen adapter exists.
- The silent-failure consequence for a caller that falls back to `chat()` on OpenAI/DeepSeek: tools never offered, no error, `chat()`'s own request body has no `tools` field. Same defect shape `aigency-harness` PR #111 found and fixed on its Anthropic adapter.
- **Gemini's tool-call id collision — now fixed by #48.** Section updated to record the fix rather than describe a defect that no longer exists, and updated again once #48's own antagonistic review caught that its first fix only closed the collision within one loop response, not across a `chatWithToolLoop` iteration's whole-loop result aggregate — this record now describes what actually merged, not the first draft of it.
- **`ChatOptions.maxTokens` is silently unread on Gemini** (and three other routes — OpenAI, DeepSeek, the OpenAI-compatible factory). The field's own doc comment discloses exactly one exception (claude-cli, whose file header says so explicitly) and treats every other adapter as expected to honour it. Gemini doesn't, and discloses nothing. Reported, not fixed — this is a seam-contract decision, not an adapter-local one.
- `onProgress` firing only on the Anthropic adapter — silent, not throwing, on the other six routes, including claude-cli.
- Why `assertNoBuiltinToolsReachable` is correctly scoped to claude-cli alone.
- Gemini's timeout/abort behaviour, established by reading the installed `@google/genai@2.21.0` runtime directly. The check-once abort-signal model is this package's design on every adapter (confirmed directly in each adapter's own `throwIfAborted` call sites), not something Gemini does worse than its siblings. What genuinely is unique to Gemini: `@google/genai` has no SDK-level default timeout as a backstop the way Anthropic's and OpenAI's SDKs do — combined with the shared check-once model, Gemini is the one route with no bound of any kind on a hung call. Report-only, for the timeout-contract arm designing one contract for every route — nothing here changes Gemini's timeout behaviour.

**Revision history.** First version was rejected by antagonistic review for an inaccurate "five of seven routes" onProgress claim (omitted claude-cli) — corrected. The Gemini-timeout item was then closed from the installed package's runtime source. A follow-up arm fixed the id-collision defect (#48) and updated this record accordingly, added the maxTokens finding, and corrected the abortSignal-wiring claim to distinguish what's shared across every adapter from what's actually unique to Gemini. #48 was then itself rejected once by its own antagonistic review (its first fix closed the id collision within one response but not across a tool loop's iterations) and fixed again — this record's description of that fix was updated to match the merged version.

No adapter code changed beyond what #48 fixed on its own branch. This is a record of what these adapters do as read on one day against one commit, not settled provider behaviour — flagged as such in the doc itself.

author: mishrasanjeev
body:
## PRD A-7 / US-3 — Screening Disposition reference agent

**Stacked on #1327** (Business Onboarding Underwriter and the provider tool gateway). Review the last two commits; the diff shrinks once #1327 merges.

### What it does

`core/agents/screening_disposition/run_screening_disposition(...)` turns one screening hit into a proposed `screening_disposition`:

1. **Evidence gathering within permitted sources** — re-screens the subject through the provider tool gateway (`screen_person` / `screen_business`, restricted to the hit's list type) to confirm the entry is still returned and cite fresh records. No capability or a provider error → the held result is used (`hit_confirmed: null`); entry gone → `insufficient_information`, band `low`.
2. **Per-identifier comparison** (`comparison.py`): name (normalised, aliases, similarity ≥ 0.85 partial), date of birth (partial-date precision), nationality, address (country/postal code), associated entities (normalised business names). Each non-`not_comparable` result cites the hit record at the compared field.
3. **Proposed outcome by fixed rules**: name mismatch or DOB mismatch → `false_positive`; name agrees + DOB agrees → `true_match`; name agrees, no DOB, associated entity overlap → `true_match`; else `insufficient_information`. Confidence band counts supporting vs contradicting identifiers — metadata only.
4. **Rationale**: the model sees list type, comparison results, outcome and band only (untrusted-content guard + pseudonymisation when `pseudonymisation.pre_model` is on). Refused and replaced by a template rationale when it states another outcome, talks of closing/clearing/dismissing, keeps a placeholder, repeats untrusted text (e.g. a list alias) or is out of bounds.
5. **Assembly**: `review: null`, schema-validated, every cited record traced to the held result or this run's calls.

### No automatic closure, structurally
- `TOOL_SET = {screen_person, screen_business}`; the gateway refuses to build a tool set with anything but read tools (tests try `close_hit`, `resolve_hit`, `dismiss_alert`, `case_decision`, `monitor_delete`).
- A test inspects every callable in the package, the run signature and the config fields for closing/clearing/dismissing/deciding names.
- A parametrised test over configurations and hostile model output (`"close": true`, `"review": {...}`) proves the disposition always leaves unreviewed and only screening tools are called.

### Override capture model (for the A-9 console)
`review.apply_review(disposition, DispositionReviewRequest(action, final_outcome, reason), analyst_id=<from the authenticated session>, reviewed_at=...)`:
accepted must keep the proposed outcome; overridden must change it and needs a non-blank reason; `agent:*` analysts refused; write-once (`already_reviewed`); request body cannot carry an analyst id (`extra=forbid`); output schema-validated. Refusal reasons are stable codes.

### Also
- `core/agents/case_model_call.py`: the underwriter's guarded prose call extracted so both agents share it (no behaviour change; underwriter suite unchanged and green).
- `load_versioned_prompt` for per-agent pinned prompts; `prompts/rationale-1.0.0.txt` pinned by SHA-256 and recorded in `case_record()`.
- Metric `agenticorg_screening_dispositions_proposed_total{outcome,band}`.
- Docs `docs/agents/screening-disposition.md` (snippets extracted from tests, checked by `tests/contract/test_doc_snippets.py`); CHANGELOG.

### Tests
- `tests/unit/screening_disposition/` — every hit fixture (probable false positive, true match person and business, hostile alias); outcome/band rules; rationale acceptance/refusal; model outage; confidence independence; model context contents; re-screen confirmed / delisted / unavailable / capability absent; unknown hit fails closed; grant denial fails closed; prompt integrity; pseudonymisation on; review capture (accept, override, every refusal); replayed cassette plus a miss.
- `tests/security/test_disposition_adversarial.py` — instruction in a screening alias vs sanitised list: identical proposal, rationale, comparisons, tool calls and byte-identical model requests.

Commands (worktree root): `CI=true AGENTICORG_ENV=test python -m pytest tests/unit/screening_disposition tests/security/test_disposition_adversarial.py tests/unit/business_underwriter tests/security/test_underwriter_adversarial.py tests/contract/test_doc_snippets.py` — **192 passed, 1 skipped** (the F-1 skip from #1327). Coverage: disposition agent 94%, comparison 99%, review 100%, case_model_call 100%. `ruff check .` clean; `mypy --ignore-missing-imports` on `core/agents/{screening_disposition,business_underwriter}` and `case_model_call.py` clean; licence headers and enterprise stability gates pass.

### Not verified
- The cassette was recorded from a deterministic stand-in model (no live credentials here); the nightly re-record replaces it.

Flags: none — nothing in the platform runs the agent yet (workflow wiring is the next PR, behind a flag). No schema change.

### Updates
- Merged the updated #1327 (annotation reason, allowlisted skip reason, run-scoped idempotency keys, main).
- `fix(agents): state the degradation in the prose call broad-except annotation`.

CI on the current head: all checks green.

author: erol-orel
body:
## Why

Two reports from testing:

1. **A saved search with two boolean facets did not show the AND between them.** The saved `query` column only holds the main facet, so the default name, the scenario card, the "Saved search:" header and the Strategy tab all showed the first query alone, and the "Boolean queries" list dropped the operator. On the corpus side, a per-facet AND (the toggle next to each sub-query) was honoured by the local re-match but **not** by the source-union rule: boolean-native live records (PubMed/EPMC, which only saw the main query) were still unioned into the corpus unless the *global* combinator was "intersection".
2. **Cluster summaries stayed in French under the English toggle.** The clustering cache (DB, then the in-memory job) was returned as-is regardless of `?lang=`.

## What changes

### Multi-facet searches
- `_combined_query_text()` builds the full expression, parenthesised like the left-to-right fold that is actually applied: `(A) AND (B)`, `((A) OR (B)) AND (C)`. It is returned as `combined_query` by the list, detail and `/activity` endpoints, together with the ordered `facets` (kind, text, effective operator) on the detail.
- Frontend: default scenario name, scenario card, detail header and the activity bar show the full expression; the Strategy tab gains a "Combined search" block listing each facet with its AND/OR badge and the full expression; replaying a saved search restores its facets and combinator.
- `_facets_intersect()` replaces the global-combinator check when deciding whether native live records may be unioned in — any intersected facet now disables it.
- The recent-search purge (`GET /user-scenarios`) and the client dedup key include the facets, so "A" and "(A) AND (B)" are two distinct searches instead of purging each other.

### Cluster summaries per language
- The clustering payload stores each cluster's summary under `clusters[].summaries[lang]`; `summary` is the one for the requested language.
- `GET …/clustering?lang=` serves the cache only when every dense cluster has a summary in that language. Otherwise the UMAP/HDBSCAN structure is kept and a background job regenerates just the summaries (5 nearest-to-centre articles per cluster, 4 parallel LLM calls), then the page polls `…/clustering/status?lang=`. Pipeline-built caches (no summaries) get their summaries on first open, in the interface language.
- Noise-cluster labels and the running/insufficient-corpus messages are localized on serve; the clustering section reloads when the language changes.
- Also replaces a raw NUL byte in `App.tsx` with the `` escape (ripgrep treated the file as binary).

## Tests
- `tests/test_pure.py`: combined expression and per-facet intersection rule.
- `tests/test_clustering_lang.py`: cache served in-language, relocalization job triggered on mismatch (no re-clustering), status endpoint localization, summaries-only regeneration keeps the structure.
- Full suite green on a fresh local PostgreSQL; `npm run build` passes.

## After deploy
Existing scenarios keep their names; their header, card and Strategy tab will show the combined expression. The first English open of a scenario's clustering tab takes a few seconds while the summaries are generated in English (one LLM call per cluster, then cached).

author: vandijcklucas
body:
### 📌 Pull Request Summary

#3 modernised what we tick on a pull request. It did not change what we write, or the order we write it in, and that is what decides how expensive a pull request is to review. Agent-authored diffs arrive faster than a person reads them and carry none of the reasoning that produced them, so the body is the only place that reasoning can land before review. This restructures the template around one idea: the diff already says what changed, so the body should say what to think about.

Three rounds of review on PSQ-UI-APP-BACKEND#347 shaped it. This pull request is written with the template it proposes.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Ticket** | N/A, follows #3 |
| **Type** | Chore |
| **Risk** | Low. A template change cannot break a build. It does change the default writing experience for every repository in the organisation, so a mistake costs annoyance at scale rather than breakage. Nothing is enforced and every optional section says so. No migration, no config, nothing to roll back beyond reverting the file. |
| **Authored** | Agent-assisted. An agent drafted the structure from a review of 1,102 review comments across the two application repositories, and I edited it over several rounds with two other reviewers. |
| **Touches** | every repository in the organisation. This file is the only pull request template we have, and no repository overrides it. |

### 🧭 Review Route

**1. `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (+113 −11)**

*What it is:* the organisation-wide default pull request body, held in `PolySense-BV/.github`. Every repository inherits it, and none overrides it today.

*What changed:* two decisions drove the rewrite, and everything else follows from them.

**The body is deleted at merge, so it cannot hold anything durable.** Both application repositories squash-merge, and neither keeps the pull request body. Commit messages survive; the body does not. So anything a future reader needs belongs in a code comment, a commit message, or a design document. The body serves one reviewer, once. That is why Root Cause and Notes and Caveats are gone: the mechanics of a defect belong at the fix, not in a page that is about to be thrown away.

**A review pointer must invite scrutiny, not limit it.** "The rest is mechanical, feel free to skim" tells a reviewer to stop looking, and the miss it causes is silent. An earlier draft of this template had explicit skim markers. They are gone. Review Route now describes what each file is for and ends on a question the reviewer can answer against the author.

| Section | | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Fact table | added | Ticket, type, risk, who authored it, what it touches. `Touches` is what the reviewer guidance points back at. |
| 🧱 Stack | added, optional | Merge order for stacked pull requests. GitHub shows the base branch and not the order, and merging out of order produces a diff nobody reviewed. |
| 🧭 Review Route | **replaces** 🔍 Changes in This PR | A list of changes repeats the diff. A reading order does not. |
| Risk | now load-bearing | Absorbs migrations, rollback, compatibility and new config. None of that is visible in a diff. An edited migration file is the clearest case: the diff cannot say whether it re-runs in production. |
| What I did not test | added | A diff shows what the tests cover. It can never show what you chose to skip. |
| Two new checklist items | added | Durable knowledge in a code comment, and the sibling check: look for the same mistake elsewhere. |
| 👀 For the reviewer | added, collapsed | Three questions CI cannot answer, plus what a person and an agent are each better at. |
| 🎯 Root Cause, 📝 Notes and Caveats, 👤 Contributors, 🗄 Migrations | removed | The first two are durable content in a disposable place. Root cause survives as the sibling-check item. Migrations folds into Risk. Contributors duplicates what GitHub already shows. |
| ✅ Checklist | 9 items unchanged from #3, 2 added | |

*What to check:* two things I would like challenged.

**Length.** 27 lines becomes 131. Most is HTML comments that never render and four sections are marked deletable, but a one-line typo fix still opens by deleting a lot. If that is the thing people end up hating, Stack, Results and How to Replicate are the three to cut first. Is that trade right?

**Nothing is enforced.** No CI reads this file. It works only to the extent people find the sections worth filling, and `What I did not test` is both the most valuable line in the template and the easiest to quietly delete, because writing it means admitting a gap. Is a template the right carrier for that, or does it need to be a review-time prompt instead?

### 🛠 How to Replicate

Nothing to run. To see it rendered, open a draft pull request in any organisation repository after this merges. The worked example on a real nine-file diff is PolySense-BV/PSQ-UI-APP-BACKEND#347, which uses this exact structure.

**What I did not test:** I have not checked how the template renders in the GitHub mobile app, or whether the collapsed `<details>` block behaves in the pull request creation form as opposed to the rendered body.

### ✅ Checklist

- [x] I have self-reviewed every line of this diff (including AI-generated code).
- [x] Tests are added or updated for the changes (or N/A — explain in Notes). — N/A, a markdown template.
- [x] CI is green (lint, type-check, tests). — N/A, this repository has no CI.
- [x] Documentation is updated where relevant (README, Confluence — link it above). — the reasoning lives in the Confluence page linked below. The `pull-request` skill is updated separately, tracked there.
- [x] Breaking changes, DB migrations, and new env vars are called out. — none.
- [x] No secrets committed (keys, tokens, passwords, connection strings).
- [x] No large, generated, or personal files committed (gitignore updated if needed).
- [x] UI changes include screenshots or a short recording. — N/A.
- [x] This PR covers one concern; unrelated changes are split out. — one file.
- [x] Anything a future reader needs is in a code comment, not only here. — the template documents itself in its own HTML comments, and the reasoning is in Confluence.
- [x] I have searched for this same mistake elsewhere in the codebase. — N/A for a template. Worth noting for the record: no repository overrides this file, so there is no second copy to drift.

### 🔗 Related Issues/Tickets

- Follows #3 (checklist modernisation)
- Reasoning and open questions: https://polysense.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/pd/pages/1220608010/Pull+requests+and+commits+explained
- Worked example: PolySense-BV/PSQ-UI-APP-BACKEND#347

body:
## Summary

Issue #950 — the subagents settings pane lagged its sibling panels: row descriptions truncated behind a native `title` tooltip, the pane header carried text-filled solid buttons, the enablement filter was a native `<select>`, and create/edit ran in a modal dialog that opened with every validation mark already red. This PR realigns the pane with the surfaces around it — the full-page form posture (McpServerForm), the reveal posture (GeneralSection), the touched-validation posture (SkillsSection), and the info-icon tooltip posture (ImportSkillsDialog) — plus a new open-folder action backed by a small read-only IPC.

## Changes

- **Row descriptions** (`AgentsSection.tsx`): long descriptions wrap instead of truncating; the native `title` tooltip is gone. Disabled-row dimming stays.
- **Header actions** (`AgentsSection.tsx`): three borderless ghost icon buttons (create / open folder / refresh) at the documented 28px hit area with 14px glyphs, muted foreground with hover brightening; the labels moved into tooltips riding the shared settings tooltip skin, with `aria-label` and tooltip copy from one source.
- **Open-folder action** (`commands.rs`, `lib.rs`, `api.ts`): new read-only `get_agents_dir` IPC returns the registry root `<app_data_dir>/agents` — the backend stays the path authority (the `get_sessions_dir` posture, result-shaped to match); the frontend reveals it via `revealItemInDir` (no capability growth), and failures land on the pane error face.
- **Filter** (`AgentsSection.tsx`): the native enablement `<select>` becomes the shared Radix Select; the `sr-only` label association and accessible name are unchanged, and the test drives it through the pointer-sequence helpers.
- **Full-page form** (`AgentsSection.tsx`): create/edit now replaces the pane list — a back link, a pane header, the row-based card layout, and an in-card save row with a saving state. The Dialog component, the Cancel button, and the `settings.agents.cancel` entry retire; `DrawerState` becomes `FormState`.
- **Touched validation** (`AgentsSection.tsx`): a field's error surface (red copy + `aria-invalid`) waits for that field's first edit, so a fresh create form opens clean; save gating is untouched — an empty form still cannot save.
- **Field shapes** (`AgentsSection.tsx`): description moves to a 3-row textarea (preamble keeps 8), and the preamble hint becomes an info-icon tooltip after the label (`FieldHint`, single aria-key for the trigger, long copy only in the tooltip).
- **Removed as noise**: the built-in name-locked hint (`settings.agents.nameLockedHint` retires) — a disabled field explains itself.
- **Tests** (`AgentsSection.test.tsx`): opener-plugin mock; reveal success + failure pins; a touched pin (fresh form shows no invalid marks, first edit surfaces the error, save stays gated); the filter test drives the Radix pointer sequence; dialog-era test names updated.

## Files Changed

- `src/components/settings/AgentsSection.tsx` -- modified (header icon trio + open-folder action; full-page form; touched gating; `FieldHint`)
- `src/components/settings/__tests__/AgentsSection.test.tsx` -- modified (opener mock; reveal + touched pins; Radix filter sequence; dialog→form naming)
- `src/api.ts` -- modified (+`getAgentsDir`)
- `src-tauri/src/commands.rs` -- modified (+`get_agents_dir`)
- `src-tauri/src/lib.rs` -- modified (command registration)
- `src/locales/en-US.json` -- modified (+`backToList` / `openDir` / `preambleHintAria`; -`cancel` / `nameLockedHint`)
- `src/locales/zh-CN.json` -- modified (same)

## Testing

- **Frontend** (vitest): AgentsSection suite 20 passed (19 + the touched pin); full suite green — 99 files / 1728 tests. `eslint` and `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- **Rust** (cargo): `cargo test --lib agents::` green (65 passed); `cargo check` clean.

## Related Issues

Closes #950.

Follow-up (out of scope):
- Extract `FieldHint` into `settings-chrome` and adopt it in `ImportSkillsDialog` (single-use today; the two shapes differ only in glyph size).

body:
## Scope — owner P1 coverage ramp: `tools/mcp/mcp_telegram.py` 0% → 100% (test-only, wire-first)

Measured from the main-run coverage artifacts: the Telegram Bot MCP server (`FastMCP("telegram_mcp")`, 4 tools, 69 statements + 12 branches) had **zero tests and 0% coverage**. It is one of the owner audit's explicit remaining P1 ramps (Task-33 list: mcp_server ✓, playwright_browser_agent ✓ #359, **mcp_telegram = this PR**, dependency_manager_agent next).

## Test strategy (no network, no credentials, no owner code touched)

The module's own lazy-load seam is the contract boundary: `_get_handler()` is replaced wholesale with a scripted `FakeTelegramHandler`, so `tools.social.telegram_bot` (which wants a real `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` + network) is **never imported** — CI-safe by construction. `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` is monkeypatched per test.

**24 tests lock every contract branch:**

| Tool | Locked behaviour |
|---|---|
| `telegram_send_message` | explicit chat_id; env fallback; missing-chat guard (no handler call); handler failure → `"failed"` status; empty `parse_mode` → `None` passed through |
| `telegram_get_bot_status` | unconfigured → token-missing payload; configured + online (incl. non-ASCII bot name exercising `ensure_ascii=False`); configured + offline → exact error text |
| `telegram_send_document` | full round-trip (bytes + caption + HTML parse_mode to handler); missing-file guard; missing-chat guard; handler exception contained into `{"success": false, "error": ...}` |
| `telegram_broadcast_alert` | severity icon map — INFO ℹ️ / WARNING ⚠️ / ERROR 🚨 / CRITICAL 🔥 / unknown → 📢 (parametrized); missing-chat guard; failure propagation |
| inputs + wiring | `str_strip_whitespace`, field defaults, FastMCP instance name, and the real `_get_handler()` import-clean property (no token required to import) |

## Verified locally

- 24/24 green; module coverage **0% → 100%** (69 stmts + 12 branches, 0 missed)
- full `tests/tools/` suite: 590 passed / 16 skipped (unchanged)
- Constitution audit on this diff: PASSED, 0 findings

author: jonbridgerapps
body:
## What this PR is

Block 08 of the physics-loop campaign `admissibility-induced-law-20260906`, an **independent PR against `main`** (cut from `5deabeb698`, where the owner's corrected blocks 01–05 live; blocks 06–07 are the open hand-offs #8034/#8035 and are not inputs). It opens for review one bounded-theorem note, its exact runner and pinned cache, the manifest acknowledgment, and the loop pack's block-08 records (contract with the supervisor's four-lens pass, three controls with outputs, the refuting pass, results, review history, certificate, trace gate, queue refresh). Supervisor-run throughout (owner directive 2026-09-15: no subagents; proofs over computation; unworked lanes).

- Claim type: **bounded_theorem**. Surface status: **bounded-support** (exact; conditional on the records-only reading, positivity, the six-axis menu and the monotone class as supplied conditions; audit required).
- Note: `docs/ADMISSIBILITY_RULE_THREE_DIMENSIONAL_MONOTONE_FORMATION_LAW_PLANE_CHAIN_COUPLING_REGION_BOUNDED_THEOREM_NOTE_2026-09-15.md`. Runner: `scripts/admissibility_rule_three_dimensional_monotone_formation_law_plane_chain_coupling_region_2026_09_15.py` (`TOTAL: PASS=33 FAIL=0`; 26 mutations each failing in its own family; exact rationals and integers only; ~27 s).
- Pack: `.claude/science/physics-loops/admissibility-induced-law-20260906/` — `GOAL_block08.md`, `RESULTS_block08.md`, `CHECKER_block08_findings.md`, `CLAIM_STATUS_CERTIFICATE_block08.md`, `specs/supervisor_control_block08_*.py` (+ `.out.txt`), and the appended `HANDOFF.md`, `STATE.yaml`, `TRACE_GATE.md`, `OPPORTUNITY_QUEUE.md`, `REVIEW_HISTORY.md`, `ROUTE_PORTFOLIO.md`, `APPROACH_REGISTRY.md`, `ASSUMPTIONS_AND_IMPORTS.md`, `NO_GO_LEDGER.md`, `LITERATURE_BRIDGES.md`.

## The question and the result, at scope

The owner's corrected queue asked for the three-dimensional formation process as a declared object with its order, initial law and uniqueness quantifier; block 02 had a witness and no theorem for the three-recorded-neighbor sweep; the derivation campaign (#8093) asks whether long-range record correlations arise from the formation law without a supplied tick. This block takes the monotone class (every linear extension of the product order on a box of `Z^3`) and proves:

- **Q1 (structure).** One law per box; internal covariance (uniform one-site marginals, orbit-typed pairs); axis symmetry; down-set consistency in any dimension; the product form `(1/6) Π K / Π K_2 / Π K_3` with a genuine three-body normalizer `K_3` on the predecessor triples — irreducible: the third difference of `log K_3` gives `2160/2197 ≠ 1` at (3,1,2).
- **Q2 (no translate consistency).** Summing out the first plane reproduces the smaller box's law iff the plane transfer preserves the two-dimensional law — refuted exactly on the `2×2` cross-section on all 1296 states at (3,1,2) and (5,2,4) (TV `356696849/806187919680` at (3,1,2)), hence on every larger cross-section; the successor triple of a site is never a predecessor triple (lemma), so the two-dimensional telescoping and 180-degree identity have no analogue. The two-dimensional consistency (#8039's projective argument) is re-proved from block 05's P7(a) for contrast.
- **Q3 (the plane chain).** For every finite cross-section the sweep of planes is a strictly positive Markov chain with a unique stationary law (four-line contraction proof); the column law; its two boundary planes carry the two-dimensional law; cross-section consistency gives the quadrant column for every positive rule; the stationary `2×2` law is computed exactly by orbit reduction (32 orbits) and differs from the two-dimensional law (TV `0.000454716…`; the interior pair is not a `K`-pair).
- **Q4 (the causal coupling theorem).** With `c = max(c_1, c_2, c_3)` the one-neighbor sensitivity: influence `≤ N(x,y) c^d`; `|Cov(g(v_x), h(v_y))| ≤ 4‖g‖‖h‖(3c)^{⌈|x−y|_1/2⌉−1}` for every box and column law; the plane chain mixes at rate `c/(1−2c)` uniformly in the cross-section; for `c < 1/3` the stationary law on the full `Z^2` cross-section exists, is unique and translation invariant, and defines the translation-invariant law on `Z^3` to which every box law converges. `c = 27/110, 10650/63407, 5782/30885` at the silent triples (3,1,2), (5,2,4), (7,3,5): all inside — where the static law's uniqueness is undecided by every criterion tried (blocks 03–04 on main).
- **Q5 (corollary, N-gated).** In the region no record two-point function of the monotone formation law decays slower than exponentially: the record-dynamics reframing returns a negative at scope for positive nearest-neighbor product rules under this order class.

## Verification record

- Supervisor controls first (`specs/supervisor_control_block08_z3.py`, `_b.py`): sensitivities, the `2×2` witness, the third difference, the 48 extensions, the exact stationary law, the cube influence.
- Refuting pass with disjoint machinery (`specs/supervisor_control_block08_refuter.py`; `CHECKER_block08_findings.md`): the transfer's TV from an integer-weighted cube enumeration; `c_3` from the integer `φ` formulation; power iteration against the exact solve; path enumeration; a pair-additive control — all equal. Three drafting defects found and fixed before the census.
- Runner census 26/26 in-family at the final sha; cache pinned; pipeline (two passes), changed-evidence, `audit_lint --strict`, `diff --check`, vocab clean (see `HANDOFF.md`).

## What this PR does not do

No order or corner is selected as physical; nothing about the static law of `Z^3` at the silent triples; nothing for `c ≥ 1/3` beyond the finite-box bounds; the distinctness of the eight corner laws on `Z^3` is not executed; the region's boundary in `(p, q, r)` is not computed; the plane-transfer refutation is executed at two triples with the mechanism lemma, not proved for every nonconstant triple. Hand-off to the owner's review-loop; never merged by the campaign; audit required before any retained status.

author: gatewayj
body:
## Related Issues

N/A

## Summary of Changes

- Preserve the existing intent-before-format safety boundary while allowing automatic replacement to choose a formatted remote survivor when the target node has no other local disk.
- Add an authenticated, body-bound `CompareAndUpdateFile` internode RPC that delegates to the existing atomic and durable disk CAS primitive. Mutation requests are never retried, and absent, unknown, or unsupported outcomes fail before target formatting.
- Discover replacement intents across the erasure set during startup, replacement admission, and blocked recovery retries. Only the node mounting every persisted replacement target may advance or replay the task; other nodes reserve the set without starting a competing ordinary heal.
- Keep ordinary resume selection and existing local replacement intents on the local-only fast path. Remote scans are limited to startup recovery, local replacement candidates, and blocked retry sets.

## Verification

Tested commit: `9caa5562c4e6677b1eb609e42a61edc76357ac45`. The tested source tree is identical to this commit.

- `cargo +1.98.1 test -p rustfs replacement_resume_selection_falls_back_to_a_remote_survivor --lib -- --nocapture` passed. It exercises a real tonic server and `RemoteDisk`, persists the intent on the only surviving remote disk, then rediscovers and reloads it as a restart would.
- The focused CAS and authentication tests passed: `compare_and_update_file_handler_preserves_atomic_outcomes`, `every_mutating_handler_enforces_its_body_digest`, `compare_and_update_wire_outcome_fails_closed`, the 14 protobuf disk-mutation canonical-body tests, and the metric classification/stability tests.
- The five existing `automatic_replacement_` tests and the target-ownership/retry-barrier tests passed. `cargo +1.98.1 check -p rustfs -j4`, `cargo +1.98.1 check -p e2e_test --lib -j4`, `cargo +1.98.1 fmt --all --check`, `git diff --check`, `check_logging_guardrails.sh`, `check_layer_dependencies.sh`, and `check_architecture_migration_rules.sh` also passed.

The full S3Chaos G22 case was not run locally because it requires its dedicated storage classes, physical replacement-volume inventory, device allowlist, and helper image. The focused integration test covers the original no-local-anchor failure and remote persistence/replay boundary, but the prepared G22 environment remains the final deployment-level validation.

## Impact

Automatic replacement can now progress in one-disk-per-server erasure sets by storing recovery state on a healthy peer disk. There is no S3 protocol, object-layout, erasure-coding, bucket, or configuration change.

The internode protobuf change is additive. During a mixed-version rollout, selecting an older peer that lacks the new RPC makes replacement fail closed before formatting; there is no non-atomic fallback. Normal S3 traffic and local resume paths do not use the new RPC.

## Additional Notes

Adversarial validation was performed twice over the final design and diff:

- Correctness: PASS — remote selection, exact-anchor replay, formatted-target restart, duplicate-generation handling, and target-node ownership were traced through the full replacement call chain.
- Simplicity: PASS — the new RPC is the minimum primitive needed to reuse the existing CAS-based resume machinery; no new persistence schema or coordinator was introduced.
- Test coverage: PASS with the deployment-level G22 gap noted above — focused tests cover wire defaults, authentication binding, atomic outcomes, remote persistence, remote rediscovery, and existing intent-before-format invariants.
- Security: PASS — every semantic request field, including optional-field presence, is signature-bound; malformed outcomes and old peers fail closed; no credentials or payloads are logged.
- Concurrency and durability: PASS — the server uses the existing flock/staged-write/fsync CAS, the client does not retry mutations, and only the target-owning node advances state while all observers suppress competing startup heals.
- Compatibility: PASS — the RPC is additive, S3 behavior is unchanged, and mixed-version failure occurs before destructive work. Downgrading during an active remote-anchored replacement may stall replay safely until a supporting version returns.
- Performance: PASS — no request or object hot path changed; existing local intents return before remote discovery, and remote scans are confined to low-frequency replacement recovery paths.

Rollback is a commit revert. Complete or pause any active remote-anchored replacement before downgrading; its on-disk intent uses the existing schema and remains intact, but older code cannot discover a peer-hosted anchor from the target node.

author: lneto
body:
`examples/ifquarantine` explained the netdevice replay on the line that registers the callback, and again beside the flag it sets, while `notifier.netdevice`'s doc block and the example's own README paragraph both already say it. A copy in the caller rots on the next change to the binding, and the reader of an example wants the policy, not the kernel.

The rule goes in "Comments and documentation", next to the one on restating API usage. A mechanical check is not worth it: the pattern is a trailing comment on a call, which every example uses for its own reasons (`control:setbyte(1, 1) -- alive`, `pcall(log.push, log, char) -- drop silently if full`), and only the reader can tell whose behaviour is being described.

author: git-param
body:
This pull request introduces several improvements and bug fixes across both backend and frontend codebases. The most significant changes include a correction to how productivity and quality metrics are calculated for PMS, enhancements to the file attachment experience in the reply composer (including image previews), and improvements to message upsert logic for PostgreSQL compatibility. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme:

**PMS Metrics Calculation and Display:**

* Corrected the calculation of monthly productivity and quality metrics to only include actual WORKING_DAY entries, excluding holidays, leaves, and missing dates from the denominator. This ensures that only days with real entries are considered, and the terminology in formulas and metadata has been updated accordingly. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-86e706fe21501eeb334801d1da216e5aa0f56becdd059d56b4e5b1554553ae56L493-R494) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-86e706fe21501eeb334801d1da216e5aa0f56becdd059d56b4e5b1554553ae56L522-L557) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-86e706fe21501eeb334801d1da216e5aa0f56becdd059d56b4e5b1554553ae56L604-L605) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-86e706fe21501eeb334801d1da216e5aa0f56becdd059d56b4e5b1554553ae56L629-R611) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-86e706fe21501eeb334801d1da216e5aa0f56becdd059d56b4e5b1554553ae56L641-R624)
* Updated the frontend PMS metric tooltips to reference "entry day(s)" instead of "working day(s)" for clarity and accuracy, using the new `entry_days` field. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b2a649b9a639332d9811a5a557258cf5524b5ef214012bcc8f6a92cc7dc2314dR121-R126) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b2a649b9a639332d9811a5a557258cf5524b5ef214012bcc8f6a92cc7dc2314dL134-R136)

**Reply Composer Attachment Improvements:**

* Added image preview functionality for attachments in the `ReplyComposer` component. Image files now display a thumbnail preview with accessible links, and object URLs are properly revoked to prevent memory leaks. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b92ab4b2b1b1e5b704abee4123afdea76d4aeaf4cf0ff261a658ee575bff994dL1-R1) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b92ab4b2b1b1e5b704abee4123afdea76d4aeaf4cf0ff261a658ee575bff994dR20-R26) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b92ab4b2b1b1e5b704abee4123afdea76d4aeaf4cf0ff261a658ee575bff994dR39-R57) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b92ab4b2b1b1e5b704abee4123afdea76d4aeaf4cf0ff261a658ee575bff994dL147-R187)
* Updated attachment chip styling in the reply composer to accommodate previews, including layout and focus states for accessibility. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f9a8751ca165a3b7368d4a5d3477f5bb98efdb02ac5cc72eea181d56616a6526L167-R167) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f9a8751ca165a3b7368d4a5d3477f5bb98efdb02ac5cc72eea181d56616a6526L178-R216)

**Backend Message Upsert Logic:**

* Refactored `MessageRepository` to support efficient upsert operations with PostgreSQL using `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, and improved update logic for existing messages. Added helper methods to avoid autoflush issues and to encapsulate update logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5bb394be0b411388193aa20849640d5c117f85fa3219d217e433b8e964a8342dR6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5bb394be0b411388193aa20849640d5c117f85fa3219d217e433b8e964a8342dR29) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5bb394be0b411388193aa20849640d5c117f85fa3219d217e433b8e964a8342dL117-R127) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-5bb394be0b411388193aa20849640d5c117f85fa3219d217e433b8e964a8342dR137-R179)

These changes improve metric accuracy, user experience with attachments, and backend robustness for message storage.

body:
## 概要

本 PR 取代 #212，基于最新 `main` 整理为单一提交，提供端到端、按 block/按 location spec 的 checksum 能力。

- 接收调用方计算的 opaque `int64_t` checksum，随 `CacheLocation` 持久化，并由 Meta/Admin 查询显式选择返回。
- checksum 的值与 presence 分离，因此 `0` 和负数均是合法值；未提供 checksum 不再用数值哨兵表示。
- 调用方若采用 KVCM 内置算法，可在 `WRITE_INPUT`、`META_ROUND_TRIP`、`READ_OUTPUT` 三个边界 fail-closed 校验，用于定位写前、元数据链路或存储读取阶段的损坏。
- checksum 在 COW 合并、location/spec 更新、ReportEvent、replica 与分层迁移中保持；部分删除只删除所属元数据。
- 未显式启用 checksum 的历史合法调用保持原行为；VCNS 已不维护，本功能不新增 VCNS target 或依赖。

完整设计、API 示例、状态机、兼容矩阵、性能数据及生产门禁见 [`docs/design/data_integrity.md`](docs/design/data_integrity.md)。

## 语义与数据流

checksum 来源与校验策略相互独立：

| 来源 | KVCM 行为 |
|---|---|
| KVCM 计算 | Put 前计算，成功写入后持久化，可在 Get 后严格校验 |
| 调用方自定义算法 | 原样保存并返回；KVCM 不解释算法 |
| 调用方使用 KVCM 算法 | 写前重算比较、元数据往返比较、读后重算比较 |

三个严格校验阶段分别定位：

| 阶段 | 比较内容 | 失败边界 |
|---|---|---|
| `WRITE_INPUT` | 输入 buffer 与调用方可信 checksum | 上游损坏或算法/iov 约定不一致 |
| `META_ROUND_TRIP` | 查询返回值与调用方可信 checksum | FinishWrite、持久化或查询序列化链路 |
| `READ_OUTPUT` | Get 后 buffer 与可信 checksum | Put、存储介质或 Get 链路 |

Manager/Meta 只处理 opaque 值，不持有数据 buffer，因此不宣称在服务端重算内容。严格校验的 trusted root 必须来自独立可信来源，不能把刚从同一 metadata 路径读出的值同时作为 expected 和 actual。

内置算法为 `CA_CRC32_XOR_INT64` / `crc32_xor_int64`，与 `SdkBufferCheckUtil::GetBlocksHash` 一致：每个 iov 独立采样头尾，计算 reflected CRC32，再按顺序经 `HashUtil::HashIntArray` 聚合。它用于发现偶发损坏和路由错位，不是密码学认证。

## 协议兼容与生产加固

- `FinishWriteCacheRequest.locations` 保留在 tag 5 并标记 deprecated；新增按 spec 分组的 `checksum_batches` 使用 tag 6。
- Meta/Admin `LocationSpec` 新增 `checksum` / `checksum_present`；所有查询默认不返回 checksum，只有 `include_checksums=true` 才返回。
- 新 client → 老 server 的未知字段会被静默忽略；必须用后续查询的 `checksum_present=true` 确认能力，不能把 FinishWrite 成功当作能力确认。
- 发布顺序必须 server-first：Manager 全部升级后再启用 writer，presence 覆盖率达到 100% 后才允许 reader strict。
- 非法 FinishWrite（重复/空 spec、shape 不符、instance 不符）不消费 session，调用方可修正后重试；校验与 session 消费在同一锁内完成。
- `SaveKvCaches` 在任何 Put 前拒绝 URI/buffer 为空或数量不等的畸形输入；这是对旧版本未定义畸形行为的主动收紧。
- inline header 尚未实现并会被明确拒绝；checksum pool 拒绝零容量、超上限 iov 和非法重新初始化，并补齐设备切换/清理约束。
- 既有 virtual 声明顺序和 `TransferTraceInfo` 布局未变；下游 subclass 重新编译保持源码兼容。新增 virtual 不承诺可安全调用旧的预编译 subclass。

## 验证结果（最终候选树）

- [x] 外源 ASAN `//kv_cache_manager/...`：126 个 target 通过；1 个真实 GPU target 跳过。
- [x] 内源 ASAN：129/129 个可运行 target 通过；明确排除 GPU-only target，以及已不维护且非本功能依赖的 `VcnsHf3fsBackendTest`、`VcnsHf3fsAllocatorTest`。
- [x] 外源 ASAN 集成测试：17/17 通过，启动真实 Manager，覆盖 HTTP/gRPC、caller checksum、query opt-in、非法 FinishWrite 重试和 instance 隔离。
- [x] `//package/kvcm_ops:storage_util_test`：22/22 通过。
- [x] CUDA/MUSA host 侧 runtime-stub 编译探针通过；这不包含 kernel 编译或设备执行。
- [x] 公共 C++17 legacy subclass 源码兼容探针、header diff、proto tag、buildifier、changed-line clang-format 与 `git diff --check` 审计通过。

`-c opt` 连续 5 次的中位数（4096 blocks，每个 response location 两个 checksum spec）：

| 项目 | 结果 |
|---|---:|
| CPU checksum match | 5.58 µs/batch（1.36 ns/block） |
| CPU checksum mismatch | 6.17 µs/batch（1.51 ns/block） |
| protobuf 大小 | 335899 → 438299 B（+30.49%，+25 B/block） |
| protobuf serialize | 267.92 → 294.57 µs（+9.95%） |
| protobuf parse | 1512.54 → 1600.93 µs（+5.84%） |
| HTTP JSON 大小 | 970868 → 1106036 B（+13.92%，+33 B/block） |
| HTTP serialize | 2103.30 → 2437.14 µs（+15.87%） |

## 尚未解除的生产启用门禁

本 PR 的软件验证已经完成，但本地没有真实 CUDA/MUSA 工具链与设备。以下项目完成前，storage integrity 配置必须保持关闭，不能宣称 KVCM 已提供生产级三阶段数据校验：

- 在每个目标 GPU 发布镜像/设备上完成 kernel 编译与设备执行，补齐并执行 MUSA 等价测试；
- 在目标 storage 完成 write → 精确篡改采样区字节 → read 的端到端故障注入；
- 以生产 block/iov 分布验证 GPU kernel、pool 排队、pinned/GPU memory 与端到端 P99；
- 完成 server-first canary、presence 100% 覆盖确认、结构化告警及回滚演练。

最终 head 的 GitHub normal/ASAN/CodeQL/CLA 和 review policy 仍是动态合入条件。

---

## English summary

This PR supersedes #212 with a reviewed, rebased, single-commit implementation of per-block, per-location-spec checksum support.

- Caller-provided opaque `int64_t` checksums are persisted and returned only through explicit Meta/Admin query opt-in. Presence is separate from value, so zero and negative checksums are valid.
- Callers using the built-in KVCM algorithm can fail closed at `WRITE_INPUT`, `META_ROUND_TRIP`, and `READ_OUTPUT`, localizing corruption to the caller/write boundary, metadata path, or storage/read path.
- KVCM-generated, caller-generated custom, and caller-generated KVCM-compatible checksums are all supported. Manager/Meta remain algorithm-agnostic because they do not own data buffers.
- Checksum state survives COW updates, ReportEvent processing, replicas, and tier migration. Legacy legal calls keep their prior defaults when checksum options are omitted.
- Wire changes are additive: legacy field 5 is retained, checksum batches use field 6, checksum presence is explicit, and query responses are opt-in. Rollout must be server-first and capability must be confirmed by query-time presence.
- Production hardening covers malformed Save input, atomic FinishWrite validation/session consumption, instance isolation, pool bounds, and CUDA/MUSA device-resource lifecycle.

Final candidate verification: external ASAN 126 passed / 1 GPU-only skipped; internal ASAN 129/129 runnable targets passed (excluding GPU-only and the two obsolete VCNS targets); integration ASAN 17/17 passed with a real Manager; `kvcm_ops` 22/22 passed; compatibility/proto/static checks passed. Detailed evidence and five-run benchmark medians are in [`docs/design/data_integrity.md`](docs/design/data_integrity.md).

Real CUDA/MUSA kernel/device execution and target-storage corruption injection remain mandatory production-enablement gates. The feature must stay disabled until those gates in section 12.2 of the design are complete. Final-head GitHub checks and review policy are also required before merge.

author: eteq
body:
In the legacy version (still used in most packages of course since 2.x isn't out yet), it turns out the official ubuntu 26.04 (e.g. docker.io/library/ubuntu:resolute) release breaks distrobox-list (and therfore several other things).  I traced the root problem to the labels they include - ``org.opencontainers.image.description:`` is followed by a string with several newlines, and those newlines confuse distrobox-list which expects each container to be newline-delimited.

A "proper" fix would be to use the json format or similar (as the main branch already does), but this PR just adds a sed filter that removes newlines inside the label section.

If I was supposed to open this up against a different branch, just tell me which - I wasn't clear if "release" is a maintainence branch or if this is the right one.  But if possible it would be good to get a minor point release out to fix this since in practice it means one cannot use the current release of distrobox with ubuntu 26.04 (which is of course a pretty major distribution to not support!)

author: kevincostner17
body:
## Summary
One commit per fix. Builds on #399 (merged).

### #246: classify policy columns from every distinct value
`classify_columns` built its sample from the first 200 non-null cells of each column, so PII after row 200 was never classified and no action reached it.
- Classification now reads every distinct non-null value, de-duplicated in first-seen order.
- Entity detection runs `detect_in_text` over newline-joined chunks of at most 64,000 characters and takes the union. It stops once every reportable entity type has been found.
- The value-regex classifier still reads each value; the Luhn and context checks read each chunk.
- The detectors, patterns and `detect_in_text` are unchanged.
- The report metadata gains `classification_values_scanned` (distinct values read per column).

### #284: inline rules take priority over pack rules
Rules were ranked by classifier specificity across inline and pack rules alike, so an inline rule matching by entity, regex or context lost to a pack column-name rule.
- Matches are now ranked by `(is_inline, specificity)`: any in-scope inline match beats every pack rule.
- Specificity still decides within each group, and ties still go to the earlier rule.
- The `PrivacyPolicy` docstring and the specificity comment describe this.

### #285: a rule's own key before policy defaults
`_resolve_key` checked `policy.key_env` before `rule.key`, so setting an organisation-wide variable silently changed the tokens of a rule with its own key.
- The precedence is now `rule.key_env` > `rule.key` > `policy.key_env` > `policy.key`.
- Rules without a key resolve exactly as before, and tokenize with no key anywhere still raises.
- `PrivacyRule` and `PrivacyPolicy` document the order.

### #232 (part 5): non-string column labels
`apply_privacy_policy` indexed the frame with `str(label)`, so integer labels raised `KeyError`.
- Each report key is now mapped back to its original label for read, write and drop. Report keys stay strings.
- `classify_columns` and `apply_privacy_policy` raise `ValueError` on duplicate labels, or on labels that collide once stringified (`1` and `"1"`).

### Quarantine on nullable integer, boolean and categorical columns
The `quarantine` action substituted its string placeholder with `Series.where`, which raises `TypeError` on nullable `Int64`/`boolean` and categorical columns, failing the whole policy run.
- When the column's dtype rejects the placeholder, the column is cast to object first, matching object columns.
- Missing cells stay missing, and every other dtype is unchanged.
- The two quarantine cases excluded in `tests/test_privacy_missing_and_labels.py` (#399) are re-enabled.

### Behaviour changes
- Columns longer than 200 rows may now be classified where they were not before. Classification cost grows with the number of distinct values.
- An inline rule beats a more specific pack rule.
- A rule's `key` beats `policy.key_env`.
- Duplicate or colliding labels raise `ValueError`.
- Quarantined `Int64`/`boolean`/`category` columns come back as object dtype.

## Tests
New `tests/test_privacy_policy_classification.py`:
- **#246:**
  - the issue repro at 10, 250 and 10,000 rows
  - late value-regex, context and Luhn matches
  - a `detect_in_text` call counter: calls equal ceil(chars / limit), repeated values cost one call, and detection stops early after one chunk
  - oversized-value chunking
  - missing and unhashable cells
- **#284:**
  - the repro
  - an inline context rule beats a pack column-name rule
  - specificity within the inline group
  - an out-of-scope inline rule doesn't override
  - a pack-only policy is unchanged
- **#285:**
  - the repro
  - `rule.key_env` beats `rule.key`
  - fallback to the policy key
  - resolution for a rule without a key is pinned
  - the no-key `ValueError` is pinned
- **#232 part 5:**
  - the repro gives `['<EMAIL>', '<EMAIL>']`
  - string report keys
  - drop, quarantine and tokenize with integer labels
  - `1`/`"1"` collision and duplicate-label errors for both functions
- **Quarantine:** `Int64`, `boolean`, `string`, `category` and object columns with `pd.NA`.

## Verification
- `ruff check .`: passed
- `mypy src/freshdata`: no issues
- `pytest -m "not online and not large"` on main 78b7790 + this branch:
  - Python 3.12 / pandas 2.3.3: 5573 passed, 13 skipped
  - Python 3.9 / pandas 1.5.3: 5569 passed, 17 skipped
- `pytest tests/truthbench`: 250 passed

Closes #246
Closes #284
Closes #285
Refs #232

author: francis-nzi
body:
…ut each gap

Section 06 stated where the client stands -- maturity, then the radar -- but never what to do next. The gaps() builder has always known: shortfall-ordered, stable. It was simply not reaching the report, because ReportSrsSection carried no gap data at all.

It does now, and each gap carries the strategies aligned to it, so the mandatory SRS alignment finally pays off inside the client-facing document: the readiness half names the gap, the plan half names the work, and the report shows them against each other.

Both halves are frozen. The gaps come from the readiness as assessed at issue; the strategies come from the plan THIS report froze, not the live one -- so a report issued last month answers last month's gaps with last month's strategies, however far the plan has moved since. That is why the strategies are read once and shared with the plan section rather than queried again: two reads could straddle an edit and leave one report disagreeing with itself about its own plan.

Nothing new decides what matters. Ordering is gaps() and the alignment is strategiesBySrsRequirement -- the same inversion the readiness screen reads, which already excludes withdrawn strategies, so a gap cannot look answered by work the client stopped doing. Pillars appear in the order their worst gap does, which is that same ordering read through a grouping rather than a second ranking.

A gap with nothing aimed at it says so. That is the useful half of the picture, and filling it in would tell a client work is under way that nobody agreed to.

Optional like the radar: a composition frozen before today carries no roadmap and renders without one. An empty roadmap is a different fact and stays distinct -- it means the client was assessed and nothing sits below its target.

The brief is committed alongside, with its cross-references to #170/#171 corrected.

Contracts, composition and render -- no migration.

author: aniklavida
body:
## Summary

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` said "SQLite uses forward-only migrations" and named nine record types. `storage.rs` was 40 lines: `initialize` was `#[allow(dead_code)]` because it genuinely was dead — `lib.rs` never called it, so **the application opened no database at all** — and the one migration created a `schema_migrations` table that nothing ever inserted into. The existing test passed only because the statement was `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, which proves repeated DDL is harmless, not that a migration system exists.

This gives the application a real database:

- The path is resolved through `PlatformAdapter::application_support_directory()` — landed in the previous card — to the application-support directory for `com.aniklavida.diskclearance`. No hardcoded path anywhere.
- The connection opens once during Tauri setup and is held in managed state, following the pattern already used for the adapter. `#[allow(dead_code)]` is gone because nothing in `storage.rs` is dead.
- A forward-only runner: an ordered `(version, sql)` list, a read of the highest applied version, application of only what is newer, **and the `INSERT INTO schema_migrations` inside the same transaction as the DDL**.
- A downgrade guard refusing to open a database recorded at a version above the binary's maximum.
- Migration `0002` creating scan sessions, findings and rule versions. Plans, operations and restore outcomes come with the cards that need them, each as its own numbered migration.
- `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` and `journal_mode = WAL` on every connection.
- Corrupt-database handling that **renames the existing file rather than deleting it** and surfaces the recovery, as `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` and the *Database recovery* state in `docs/design/STATES.md` require.

No new crates — `rusqlite` 0.37 with `bundled` was already present.

## Truthfulness status

- [x] Implemented and tested
- [ ] Experimental
- [ ] Planned documentation only
- [ ] Unsupported behavior clarified

## Validation

- [x] `npm run check` — format check, vitest, TypeScript build, `cargo fmt`, **17 Rust tests**, `cargo check`. Re-run independently rather than taken on trust.
- [x] Tests use isolated temporary fixtures — every test uses `DisposableTempDir` plus the `TestAdapter` with a scripted application-support path. `grep` for `dirs::`, `home_dir()`, `$HOME` and a literal `/Library/Application Support` in `storage.rs` returns nothing.
- [x] Safety invariants remain intact — no Tauri command takes SQL, no database handle reaches the renderer, and `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json` is untouched.
- [ ] UI changes include screenshots and accessibility notes — not applicable.

One named test per Done-when line:

| Done when | Test |
|---|---|
| Database created in application support on first launch | `application_creates_database_in_application_support_directory_on_first_launch` |
| Migrations apply once, record one row per version, re-run applies nothing | `migrations_apply_once_and_record_in_schema_migrations` |
| A failing second migration leaves version 1 with no partial schema | `failed_migration_rolls_back_and_leaves_previous_version_intact` |
| A database above the binary's maximum version is refused | `downgrade_refuses_database_with_higher_version` |
| A corrupt database is preserved under a new name, fresh one created | `corrupt_database_is_preserved_under_new_name_and_fresh_database_created` |

Two beyond what was asked: `foreign_keys_and_wal_pragmas_are_enabled` and `foreign_key_enforcement_blocks_orphan_findings`.

### The central claim was proven, not assumed

The whole card turns on the `INSERT` sharing a transaction with the DDL. To check the rollback test actually has teeth, the transaction was temporarily removed — DDL and version record committed separately — and the suite re-run. `failed_migration_rolls_back_and_leaves_previous_version_intact` failed with `assertion failed: !table_exists`: exactly the partial schema from a half-applied migration that this card exists to make impossible. Restoring the transaction returned all 17 tests to green, and the working tree is clean.

## Known gap, not introduced here

`.github/workflows/validate.yml` still triggers only on `push: branches: [main]` and `pull_request`, so a merge into `develop` runs nothing on its own. Flagged in the previous PR and still worth its own small change.

## Summary
- Adds `backend/scripts/grant_api_key_category.py`, a general-purpose, reviewable, re-runnable script that grants an `api_keys` document's `categories` array a new entry via `$addToSet`.
- Replaces the ad-hoc `mongosh` one-liners used to do this by hand at least half a dozen times already (`ai_tools`, `seo_tools`, `calculators`, `web_tools`, `image`, ...) — flagged as an obfuscation risk during the 2026-09-05 Tools Metadata CMS cleanup. Standing project lesson: sensitive production-Mongo mutations need a real, reviewable script file in the repo, not an ad-hoc SSH command typed in the moment.
- Immediate motivating use case: granting `frontend-service`'s key the new `analytics` category so `POST /v1/analytics/pageview` (merged to `main` @ `7712e6a`) works through the frontend proxy — but the script itself is not analytics-specific; `--owner`/`--category` are plain CLI args since this class of grant recurs almost every time a new router ships (see CLAUDE.md's "New backend category/router → check the `frontend-service` API key grant" rule, added after the Merge PDF 2026-08-04 and Text-to-Binary 2026-08-13 incidents).

## Safety properties
- Reuses `app.core.database`'s `db` (same convention as `seed_content_categories.py`/`seed_admin.py`) — always picks up `DATABASE_URL` from the environment, never a hardcoded connection string, never reads/prints a `.env` file directly.
- Never reads, prints, or logs the key's `key` field (the actual secret) at any point — identification is by `owner`/`categories` only, matching the precedent in SPRINT_STATUS.md's 2026-08-21 entry.
- `$addToSet` only, never `$set`/overwrite of the whole array — the exact root-cause shape of the two prior production-breaking incidents this is meant to prevent a repeat of.
- If the category is already present: clean no-op ("already granted"), no error, no duplicate, no second write.
- Prints the `categories` array before and after the update, so the operator gets an explicit before/after diff in the same run.
- Fails loudly (non-zero exit, clear stderr message) if `--owner` doesn't match any document — no silent no-op.

## Not done in this PR
- **Not run against production.** This PR is the script only, per the task scope. Running it against `frontend-service` to grant `analytics` (or any other production `api_keys` mutation) is a separate follow-up step requiring explicit founder approval, per CLAUDE.md/the AI Collaboration rules.
- This PR needs `security-reviewer` sign-off before merge — it's a tool capable of mutating production API-key permissions. Not self-merging.

## Test plan
- [x] `python -m py_compile scripts/grant_api_key_category.py` — syntax-checked, no errors.
- [x] Manually reviewed against `scripts/seed_content_categories.py`/`scripts/read_env_field.py`/`scripts/reset_admin_password.py` for house-style conventions (docstring, `sys.path` bootstrap, `app.core.database` import pattern, argparse style).
- [ ] `security-reviewer` pass (requested via this PR).
- [ ] Dry-run against a non-production/staging Mongo instance before the first production run (follow-up, not part of this PR).

**Generate against the newest peers in upstream's range**

The release run got past generation and failed compiling the bindings: `*jsiiProxy_SopsSecret does not implement SopsSecret (ambiguous selector .With)`. `constructs-go` v10.6.0 added `IConstruct.With`, and the proxy embeds both `constructs.Construct` and `awssecretsmanager.ISecret`, which reach it at equal depth.

`jsii-pacmak` emits a forwarder that resolves the diamond — aws-cdk-go's own `Secret` has one — but only when it generates against a `constructs` that actually declares `With`. Generating at the range floor left nothing to disambiguate, and MVS then raised consumers to 10.6 anyway.

- **The floor was not viable regardless** — `aws-cdk-go` v2.227.0 fails to compile against `constructs-go` 10.6 in its own sources, across hundreds of files.
- **Verified locally** — generation, compile, and a synth producing `AWS::SecretsManager::Secret`, `Custom::SopsSync`, the Lambda, role and policy.
