author: skuldwing
body:
## Le constat

Sur les listes importées, le nom de famille apparaît souvent deux fois — et l'attestation l'imprimait tel quel :

```
prénom « Mouhamadou Makhtar Niang »  nom « Niang »   →  Mouhamadou Makhtar Niang Niang
prénom « Rockaya Samb »              nom « Samb »    →  Rockaya Samb Samb
prénom « Babacar SARR »              nom « Sarr »    →  Babacar SARR Sarr
prénom « Niang Khadidiatou »         nom « Niang »   →  Niang Khadidiatou Niang
```

**L'origine n'est pas l'import**, qui a fidèlement recopié ce qu'il a lu, mais les feuilles de présence où chacun écrit son nom entier dans la case « Prénom ». Aucun code ne peut deviner l'intention au moment de la lecture ; en revanche, la répétition se reconnaît après coup.

## Ce que ça ajoute

La répétition est repérée et **le texte corrigé proposé sous la ligne**, plutôt que de laisser deviner quoi retirer. Un clic applique la proposition dans les champs d'édition, où elle reste modifiable avant enregistrement.

Elle est détectée **en fin de prénom comme en tête**, selon que la personne a écrit « Rockaya Samb » ou « Niang Khadidiatou », et la comparaison ignore casse et accents : « Babacar SARR » avec « Sarr » est bien vu.

Au-delà d'une occurrence, un bandeau propose de **tout corriger d'un coup**. Sur une liste de cinquante personnes, cliquer cinquante fois découragerait n'importe qui. La correction en lot n'applique rien d'autre que ce que chaque ligne affiche déjà, une ligne en échec n'interrompt pas les suivantes, et chacune reste tracée dans le journal d'audit.

## Vérifications

**Détection**, sur les quatre cas réels remontés plus cinq contre-exemples :

| Entrée | Résultat |
|---|---|
| `Mouhamadou Makhtar Niang` + `Niang` | → `Mouhamadou Makhtar` |
| `Niang Khadidiatou` + `Niang` | → `Khadidiatou` |
| `Rockaya Samb` + `Samb` | → `Rockaya` |
| `Babacar SARR` + `Sarr` | → `Babacar` |
| `Jean Pierre Ndiaye` + `NDIAYE` | → `Jean Pierre` |
| `Marie Claire` + `Diop` | rien à corriger |
| `Awa` + `Diop` | rien à corriger |
| `Diop` + `Diop` | rien à corriger |
| `Fatou` + *(nom vide)* | rien à corriger |

**Navigateur**, sur une liste reproduisant exactement les données remontées : bandeau « 4 noms de famille sont écrits deux fois », proposition juste sous chacune des quatre lignes, aucun signalement sur `Sokhna Ba`. Après « Tout corriger », les cinq noms sont corrects en base et le bandeau disparaît.

**Journal d'audit**, les quatre corrections en lot :

```
Babacar SARR Sarr              → Babacar Sarr
Rockaya Samb Samb              → Rockaya Samb
Niang Khadidiatou Niang        → Khadidiatou Niang
Mouhamadou Makhtar Niang Niang → Mouhamadou Makhtar Niang
```

Aucune erreur JS.

Remplace la PR #51, dont la branche avait divergé de `main` après l'écrasement de la PR #50.

author: ancienttwo
body:
## Why

A `bun --compile` product binary (Salesko's `salesko-agent` is one) reads `$cwd/bunfig.toml` and runs its `preload` before any program code; `--config=/dev/null` does not suppress it. MCP server children used to inherit the Agent home as cwd — the directory the agent's own tools write by design — so an agent could hand preload code to the very server it was being served by. Controlling the child's cwd is the only control point. Evidence: `.artifacts/c07-launch-cwd/linux-sh-probe/` (negative control reproduces the injection; bootstrap removes it).

## What

- **Directory proof** (`daemon/trusted-launch-cwd.ts`): once per offer, never cached. Write probe must fail `EACCES|EPERM|EROFS`; the directory and every ancestor to the volume root must be owned by another uid and not writable by this uid; symlinks refused; uid 0 refused (`root_cannot_prove_write_boundary`); `os.tmpdir()` refused. Candidate = `DaemonConfig.mcpLaunchCwd.dir` or platform default (`/`, `%SystemRoot%`).
- **Launcher, per Owner ruling 2026-09-15:** POSIX uses the trusted system `/bin/sh` (realpath + symlink both root-owned, no group/other write, regular file) with the bootstrap `cd -- "$0" && exec "$@"` — argv structural, no quoting, exec with no intermediate process. win32 uses `bin/byok-launch-cwd.mjs` on a real Node host only; a non-Node host without a trusted launcher is refused. `launcherInterpreter` is an operator override, not a supported path. No Bun/Deno/SEA detection on POSIX.
- **Binding predicate:** any task that generates ≥1 MCP server of any origin (host toolsets, agent-message / memory / `confirm` approval helpers) is bound; pi (`direct-cwd`), codex and claude (`launcher-wrapped`) all fail closed without a binding.
- **Loader env hard deny** extended with `ENV BASH_ENV SHELLOPTS BASHOPTS CDPATH PS4`, identical in `daemon/environment.ts` and the launcher script, pinned by a test.
- **Attestation:** launcher kind + interpreter + script bound as their own fact beside `definitionRevision` (shell and node launchers never fingerprint equal).

## Breaking (configuration) — Owner ruling 2026-09-15

Every MCP toolset server `command` must be an **absolute path**. `McpToolsetRegistry` rejects bare-name, relative, and option-like commands at load — construction and `toolsets.reload` — before any probe, claim, or start (`mcp_toolset_command_not_absolute`, `mcp_toolset_command_option_like`). No PATH lookup, no normalization. Operators with a bare `salesko-agent` must give the full path; Salesko's current `process.execPath` config is unaffected. The launcher wrapper keeps its own refusals as a second layer, surfaced as `RuntimeExecutionFailure{phase:'start', category:'authority', retry:'non-retryable'}`. An absolute path is **not** executor attestation; that remains the attested-install work.

## Platform evidence boundary (read before trusting the matrix)

| Platform | Launcher | Evidence in this PR |
|---|---|---|
| darwin | `/bin/sh` bootstrap | verified on the development host (real-process test + bunfig preload negative control) |
| linux | `/bin/sh` bootstrap | verified in containers: dash 0.5.12, bash 5.2.37 as `sh`, busybox ash — `.artifacts/c07-launch-cwd/linux-sh-probe/` (manifest with sha256s), `docs/researches/20260915-c07-launch-cwd-shell-bootstrap-evidence.md` |
| win32 | `bin/byok-launch-cwd.mjs` on real Node | **code path + unit tests only; not verified on Windows.** `launch-cwd-launcher.test.ts` is included as a dedicated single-filter step in the `windows-git-workspace` and `agent-memory-helper` (macOS) jobs — that is scheduling, not a result. A skipped or zero-match run cannot pass (single filter exits 1 on a missing file; no `--passWithNoTests` in the repo). Evidence exists only once this PR's CI runs those steps green. |

Finding recorded honestly: `exec -- "$@"` fails on dash (`exec: --: not found`); the macOS result for that form was not a POSIX proof. Darwin `SF_RESTRICTED` is not asserted because Node's `fs.Stats` exposes no `flags` on darwin — documented as a limit, not faked.

## Does not claim

- Launcher/executor identity integrity (attested install) — separate slice.
- G4 counting, S0, Host CAS — separate slices.
- Any Windows run result.

## Gate

Acceptance review r1 (d51b3e17) FAIL → fixes in d29bf6e3; r2 (7a30c4cb) all five prior findings resolved, one new MEDIUM (raw NUL byte in a regex literal, `trusted-launch-cwd.ts:488`) fixed in d2af40b7.

## Verification on d2af40b7 (local, darwin/arm64)

```
bun run build                      → Build success (all packages)
bun run typecheck                  → 15/15 Done
bun run test                       → client 2194 passed | 11 skipped; cloud 384; cloud-dataplane 72 | 107 skipped;
                                     conformance 161; core 304; keys 464; protocol 365; server 373 | 19 skipped;
                                     testkit 4; ui-runtime 20; byok-sdk 4; examples 46 — 0 failed
bun run check:api-surface          → 9 package golden(s) match the built declarations
bun run check:version-authority    → README.md and docs/spec.md agree with byok-sdk@0.18.0 and @byok-sdk/keys@0.5.0
bun run check:release-graph        → OK: 9 aligned manifests at 0.18.0, keys at 0.5.0
bun run check:release-pack         → sourceGitSha d2af40b7f7dc050d507f7aff5379ec757f6017c8
repo-harness run check-task-workflow --strict → [workflow] OK
```

## Stack note

Depends on #190 (`codex/c07-readonly-tools`) → #188 → #187 → #185. Not a dependency of, and not depended on by, #189 (`codex/c07-g4-remote-preparation`, which forked from #187); the next slice merges both.

author: evgunter
body:
D283's ruling, route A, unit (i). The parameter-space ↔ model-space
crossing is a **typed rate**, and the rate's **bound direction** is the
semantic content. Before this, `Margin::metered(span, rate)`'s doc
promised "a certified speed LOWER bound" and three shipped sites pushed
a certified UPPER bound through it — correct in each case, argued in
prose, checked by nothing.

Spec: `docs/RATE-PAIR-SPEC.md` (ratified at dispatch, deleted at merge
per `docs/DOC-LEDGER.md`). Item: `work/scalar/rate-pair-in-geom-core.md`.

> **Blinding note.** Commit `c649d214c` ("RATE-PAIR: the spec"), which
> was already on this branch when the implementer lane took it up,
> carries an auto-appended `Co-Authored-By` trailer naming a model.
> None of the implementation commits do. Flagged rather than rewritten:
> history here is merge-only.

## The two types

`crates/geom-core/src/predicate.rs`, beside `Margin`:

| | |
|---|---|
| `SupSpeed<T>` | a certified **upper** bound on a speed, m per parameter unit |
| `InfSpeed<T>` | a certified **lower** bound, same units |

`#[repr(transparent)]`, `Copy`, no `PartialEq`/`PartialOrd` (the `Real`
surface's rule), `new(T)` / `get()`, and two conversions that are **one
operation each**: `to_meters(span) = span * s`, `to_param(m) = m / s`.
A **dimension-and-direction tag, not a positivity witness** — the 0 / ∞
/ poison guards stay where they are, because the sites disagree about
what a zero rate means. A surface's pair is two values, not a type.

The direction rule, stated once in the module doc and once at the door:
**inf** for a *definitely apart* claim (a lower bound under-states the
length, so it cannot certify a sliver); **sup** for an overshoot or an
escape (an upper bound over-states the displacement, so it can only
refuse).

## The doors

- **`Margin::metered(span, rate: InfSpeed<T>)`** — the doc's promise
  made a type.
- **`Margin::metered_sup(span, rate: SupSpeed<T>)`** — new, the
  sup-side sibling for overshoot and escape metering. Named for the
  bound rather than for one caller's verb, because it serves three
  different claims (a trim escape, an iso row's snap slack, a loop
  gap) and the bound is what they share.

14 shipped `metered` call sites, 15 shipped `metered_sup`.
`docs/predicate-dimension-audit.md`'s clause-(iii) rows now cite the
door that matches the tag, and its head matter gains a paragraph
stating the rule.

## Producers typed at the mint

| producer | type | why that direction |
|---|---|---|
| `NurbsCurve3::speed_lower_bound` (both curve arities, one macro) | `InfSpeed<T>` | every consumer relies on under-statement: a span it proves forward IS forward in metres |
| `pcurve_cache::param_rate` (+ `param_rate_gate`) | `InfSpeed<T>` | line `1`, circle radius, ellipse minor are inf bounds **by being exact**; the net's is `speed_lower_bound` |
| `pcurve_cache::chart_stretch_sup` (pub) | `(SupSpeed<T>, SupSpeed<T>)` | escape metering; its doc already said "emphatically not a lower bound" |
| `pcurve_cache::nurbs_stretch_bounds` | `(SupSpeed<T>, SupSpeed<T>)` | derivative-net sups × the Floater weight-ratio factor |
| `pcurve_cache::chart_arms_at` | `(SupSpeed<T>, SupSpeed<T>)` | the cone arm at the boxes' `v` supremum |
| `pcurve_cache::curve_rate_bound` | `SupSpeed<T>` | the curve twin of the above (see *Deviations*) |
| `pcurve_cache::side_of`'s `arm` | `SupSpeed<T>` | takes the sup through and meters the admission slack with it |
| `topo::pcurves::v_meter` | `SupSpeed<T>` | exact polar radius is a sup by being exact; a spline chart's by derivation |
| `topo::split`'s `scale`, `splitting::classify`'s `meter`, `chord_join`'s `len` | `InfSpeed<T>` | interiority and forwardness are *definitely apart* claims |
| `PatchRegularity::{speed_u, speed_v}`, `speed_lever()` | `SupSpeed<f64>` | max of two sups is a sup; the fold keeps the tag |
| `ssi::plane_nurbs_ssi`'s local `speed` | `SupSpeed<f64>` | minted **after** the #762 finite-and-positive guard; its three divisions go through `to_param` |

`azimuth_arm` keeps a bare `T` and says why at its header: an azimuth
arm is metres per **radian**, so it reaches the band through
`Margin::levered`, not a metric door. Its spline branch takes the tag
off `chart_stretch_sup` at the one place where the same number is read
as a lever — the only `.get()` in the shipped conversion set that is
not a deliberate exit.

`PatchRegularity::thinness()` stays `floor / speed_lever().get()`,
with the doc saying why the door does not apply: `floor` is an **area**
rate (m² per unit parameter area), so dividing it by a linear rate
leaves metres, not parameter units — `to_param`'s dimensional argument
would be a false one.

## Consumers moved

The three blurred sites onto the sup door:
`pcurve_cache::trim_containment` (×4 margins), the `pcurve_iso_*` slack
meters (×8), and the v-channel of `topo::pcurves::pcurve_loop_continuity`
(×3, across the walk, the chart-boundary door and the validator). Every
`metered` caller now passes an `InfSpeed`. The hand-spelled slack
products in the iso lane (`slack_knots`, `side_of`'s two admission
slacks, `slack_affine`, `slack_param`, the two `over * stretch` terms)
go through `to_meters`.

The SSI **receipt** is untouched — `Exhaustiveness`' lane tag is the
second unit's.

## The pin: nothing's bits move

- **The tour digest, committed before the change.** `afd28b98` — the
  first commit on this branch, before a line of the change was
  written — records the merge-base hashes. After the change, the same
  release build of `demos/tour` emits the **same 1766 files** with the
  **same** per-file listing digest
  `87be4dd9df4cc3af9bd44593a6b981608c8e73721c746413a00322ff61e4a892`,
  and the **same 728 lines** of narration (the census, genus,
  validation tiers and exact-vs-meshed mass properties per stop),
  `8522886427381545d312aafd1ff6a1a6757ea4d6500c47278036c2d847ab6712`.
  `diff` on both is empty. The committed receipt carries a correction:
  its narration hash was cut at a fixed line number and kept the
  absolute outdir, so it digested cargo's preamble too; the recipe that
  reproduces is written into the item file, and the **pre-change log,
  unmodified**, re-digests under it to the same `85228864…`.
  *(Superseded — see the fix pass, item 3.)*
- **The D9 differential is the diff itself.** Each door is one
  operation over a transparent newtype, so every retyped expression is
  the same arithmetic in the same order. `crates/geom-core/tests/rate_pair_doors.rs`
  makes that checked rather than asserted: four rows drive
  `to_meters`/`to_param` on both types against the bare `*` and `/`
  over a written-down sample (both signed zeros, two subnormals,
  `MIN_POSITIVE`, `MAX`, `MIN`, both infinities, NaN) and compare
  `to_bits`, not `==` — `==` cannot see a signed zero and calls every
  NaN unequal.
- **The poison row.** A rate of `0`, `-0`, `∞` or NaN goes in and comes
  out; the metred margin is the bare product's bits. The pair is a tag,
  and a door that sanitized a collapsed carrier would hide it from the
  trilean that is supposed to escalate on it.
- **The `Interval` row.** At the certified scalar the doors are the
  interval product and quotient, so the row pins the enclosure property
  (the answer brackets the real product/quotient of points drawn from
  the operands) and the `repr_bits` identity with the bare ops — a bit
  comparison against an `f64` operator is not the claim there and is
  not made.
- **Compile-fail doctests**, each with a twin that differs in exactly
  one respect and compiles: a `SupSpeed` cannot reach `metered`
  (`E0308`), an `InfSpeed` cannot reach `metered_sup` (`E0308`), and a
  rate cannot be compared without `get()` (`E0369`). Codes read off
  `rustc` at the pinned 1.97.0; stable rustdoc does not verify them,
  which is what the twins are for.
- **No predicate name was added, removed or renamed**, so the k-lint
  gate's predicate counts and the audit's measured coverage figures
  (246 names / 223 reached / 121 dimension

author: blairham
body:
Part of #2291, tranche 3.

POSIX gives the fifteen special built-ins two consequences — a prefix assignment
persists, and a failure is fatal to a non-interactive shell — and **neither one
is common ground on this panel.** Measured a line at a time on 2026-09-15:

| question | bash 5.3 | zsh 5.9 | ksh93 | dash |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v=outer; v=inner :` leaves `$v` | `outer` | `outer` | `inner` | `inner` |
| `export 1bad=x` ends the shell | no | no | yes | yes |
| `set -o nosuchopt` ends the shell | no | no | yes | yes |
| `. ./nosuchfile` ends the shell | no | no | yes | yes |
| a write to a readonly name ends it | **yes** | no | no | **yes** |
| the status an ended shell leaves | 1 | — | 1 | 2 |

So `core/builtins-special.tests` asks what the panel does agree on — every one
of these builtins' actual work, and none of its ceremony — and writes the split
down where the cases would have been. A paragraph in place of a case is the
deliverable, not a gap.

Four shells are alone on something here, so each gets a file:

- `ksh/` — `times` is a **preset alias** for `{ { time;} 2>&1;}` rather than a
  builtin, which is also why an assignment prefix in front of it is a syntax
  error
- `dash/` — `. file arg` passes no positional parameters; the other three do
- `bash/` — `return` outside a function is refused with status 2 and the script
  carries on, where zsh, ksh93 and dash all take it as an `exit`
- `zsh/` — `command` runs only an external file, so `command :`,
  `command export`, `command eval` and `command unset` are all 127 in a shell
  where every one of those names exists

### Two divergences of ours, filed rather than papered over

- #2887 — `readonly name` with no value leaves the name unset in ours; zsh gives
  it an empty value, and it is alone on the panel in doing so.
- #2888 — a syntax error in **alias-expanded** text quotes the closing brace in
  ours where ksh93 quotes the opening one. Reached without an alias in sight
  through ksh93's preset `times`.

Both rows are written into the dialect files as prose naming the issue, so they
go back in when it closes instead of being rediscovered.

### Suite

```
column   parsed   strict   before        after
bash     +1/+1    +2/+2    42/42         44/44
zsh      +1/+1    +2/+2    49 (1 bad)    unchanged + 2
ksh93    +1/+1    +2/+2    43/44         45/46
dash     +1/+1    +2/+2    28/29         30/31
ash      +1/+1    +1/+1    28/28         29/29
```

`core/ agreement 1/1`, and `bash/ zsh/ ksh/ dash/ only-here 1/1` each — every
new dialect file's own column is alone in what it wrote.

`make check` green. Note for whoever is watching the board: `main` already
carries three non-strict rows and one BAD CASE that are **not** from this branch
— zsh `jobs.tests` is non-deterministic, and zsh `params.tests`, ksh93
`tokenization.tests` and dash `params.tests` are short of strict. They arrived
with #2882/#2871 and are reported here rather than touched.

Closes #2309

body:
Advances the panel one settled close to **Mon 14 Sep 2026**, and reverses last round's `TOST US` drop now that the vendor has corrected the series.

## ASOF determination (§7a + §10 change-count diagnostic)

| Row | Signature | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Mon 14 Sep | **70/71 US + 20/20 European** moved | settled US close → `ASOF` |
| Tue 15 Sep | **0/71 US changed**, all 20 Europeans moved | §10 stale-US signature on the pull-day row → excluded |
| Sat 12 / Sun 13 | a few vendor estimate tweaks on weekend-stamped rows | weekday filter drops them |

author: nghia-vantrong
body:
searchOutlookMessages could find a message and not read it. Graph's bodyPreview is
capped: a real message came back as 262 characters ending mid-sentence, so the half
that matters was missing. Search also reported hasAttachments with no way to open one.

readOutlookMessage returns the whole body, recipients and the attachment list.
Verified against a real message in the mailbox — 588 characters where the preview gave
262, HTML stripped, Vietnamese and emoji intact. Inline images are excluded from the
attachment list, because signatures and embedded screenshots otherwise make every
signed message look like it carries documents.

Attachment reading covers PDFs and text formats. Office attachments are refused with
an explanation rather than a failure, and the reason is worth stating: Graph converts
Office documents through an endpoint that operates on a drive item, and an attachment
is bytes on a message with no drive item behind it. The same .docx is readable in
OneDrive and not as an attachment, so the message points at searchMicrosoftFiles when a
copy exists there.

The attachment path is not verified against a real attachment: no message in the last
sixty carries one, so there was nothing to try it on. The lookup and its error were
exercised, and the strategy decision is covered by tests. Worth running against a real
attachment when one arrives.

Also noted while probing: `$filter=hasAttachments eq true` is rejected as
InefficientFilter on this mailbox, so finding such a message means scanning and
filtering client-side.

author: flvndvd
body:
## Description

Connects domain grants to Frame sharing and email verification. Sharing `example.com` gives Alice and Bob access through their own verified email addresses, with separate viewer histories. The sharing API returns first and last recorded views and days viewed alongside the access grants. The UI follows separately.

Uses the merged grant and daily viewer Resources, reuses invitation and membership checks, and removes the unused email-only lookup wrappers. Existing email responses and numeric revocation IDs remain supported. Domain creation requires the `frame_domain_sharing` flag and invitation permission, and respects workspace and Frame function restrictions.

## Tests

Sharing API and Resource tests cover exact domain matching, OTP, revocation, separate viewer histories, daily frequency and workspace isolation. Validated the data backfill in a disposable database, including UTC boundaries, revoked grants and reruns. Formatting, audit schemas and Swagger checks pass. Typechecking matches the existing dependency errors on main.

## Risk

Creation is gated behind a feature flag. Disabling it stops new domain grants but keeps existing grants valid. Rolling back the code removes domain access. Historical analytics can only recover the last-view timestamps already stored, not earlier visits or total opens.

## Deploy Plan

Run the data seed before deployment, then reconcile legacy timestamps after all servers have updated. Both domain audit schemas are registered with WorkOS. No schema changes. Enable the flag for testing after deployment, with UI rollout in the following PR.

author: loom-fleet-dispatch[bot]
body:
## Summary

Step 1a of `sweep.md` prose-mandated that a daemon-dispatched `--claim-owned` session run `sweep-lease-renew.sh start <N>` itself to keep its forge lease fresh. A mechanism that only fires when a model remembers a sentence is not a mechanism: one session skipping it aged its lease past `LOOM_LEASE_TTL_MINUTES`, a peer host's reclamation gate (#6286) correctly judged the claim abandoned, and the fleet spent ~2.5 h in claim/yield thrash across four hosts — including a near-miss where a second Builder's claim went live while the first was still working in the shared `.loom/worktrees/issue-N` directory.

`SweepRegistry::finish_issue_dispatch` now issues that one-shot `start` itself, from dispatch code.

## Changes

**`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch.rs`** — `start_lease_renewal_loop`, called from `finish_issue_dispatch` for every `SweepKind::Issue` dispatch:

```
.loom/scripts/sweep-lease-renew.sh start <N> \
  --watch-pid <child pid> --host <published host> --sweep-id <sweep id>
```

- **Placed after the #4689 immediate-preflight-death branch, deliberately.** That branch unwinds the whole claim (label, claim lock, peer-claim ad) for a child that is already dead; starting the loop before it would aim it at an exited pid. Both are still one synchronous `dispatch()` call — there is no deferred tick a daemon restart could drop.
- **`--host`/`--sweep-id` are passed explicitly** (#6485). Without both, `renew-once` falls back to "newest lease wins" and can spend the sweep renewing a *peer* dispatcher's comment while this claim's own `updated_at` never advances — the #6470 mechanism. The daemon knows both values exactly; it published them in `write_lease_comment`.
- **Best-effort**, matching #6179's write-on-dispatch contract: a missing helper, a non-zero `start`, or a spawn error only logs, and dispatch proceeds. Degrades to exactly pre-#7672 behavior (the lease ages out) rather than failing the dispatch.
- **stderr → the sweep's own log file** (#6541), never a pipe: the detached loop holds its inherited fd 9 open for the sweep's whole lifetime, so a piped stderr would make the read-to-EOF hang for hours.

**This does not make the daemon the renewer** — the hazard #6129 forbids and `sweep-lease-renew.sh`'s own header warns about. Only the *invocation* moved: `start` forks one loop, `disown`s it and returns, so the daemon holds no handle, runs no tick, and re-arms nothing on restart. The loop watches the **sweep child's** pid via `--watch-pid` and gets its own process group, so it stops when the sweep stops and survives a daemon restart (or a process-group-targeted teardown of the daemon) untouched.

**`LOOM_SWEEP_LEASE_RENEW_DISPATCHED=<N>` capability marker** (new, `Issue`-scoped like `LOOM_SWEEP_CLAIM_OWNED`). The installed prompt and the daemon binary do **not** roll together: `.claude/commands/loom/sweep.md` is refreshed by an ordinary `git pull` / `resync-installed.sh`, while `loom-daemon` is only rebuilt by `loom update`. "New prompt, pre-#7672 binary" is therefore reachable, and an *unconditional* withdrawal of Step 1a's `start` would leave every sweep dispatched in that skew window with no renewal loop from either side — the same bug this PR fixes, fleet-wide. So Step 1a keeps a **fallback** `start` gated on the marker:

| Prompt | Daemon | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| new | ≥ #7672 (marker set) | session skips — the daemon already started it |
| new | pre-#7672 (no marker) | session starts it itself: pre-#7672 behavior, unchanged |
| old | ≥ #7672 | session also starts one — a duplicate loop, harmless (idempotent PATCH of the same comment, one extra call per interval) |

**Docs** — `defaults/docs/lease-renewal.md` (who starts vs. who is watched, the marker + skew table, the wiring), `defaults/docs/daemon-reference.md` (a dispatch-path subsection), `defaults/docs/lease-record.md` (the #6470 root-cause paragraph now names both `start` call sites), and `defaults/scripts/sweep-lease-renew.sh`'s header — whose "never from `loom-daemon`" sentence the Curator quoted as the governing rationale and which this PR makes literally false. It is amended to state the actual invariant: the daemon may issue the one-shot `start`; what it must never acquire is *ongoing* renewal.

`defaults/scripts/sweep-lease-renew.sh` has **no behavior change** — `--watch-pid` (line 502) and the self-`disown` (line 611) already existed, and its `start` contract was re-verified to hold for a caller outside the sweep's own process tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `finish_issue_dispatch` invokes `sweep-lease-renew.sh start <N> --watch-pid <child_pid> --host <h> --sweep-id <id>` once, immediately after the child is confirmed spawned — Step 1a guaranteed by dispatch code, not prose.
- [x] The daemon retains no ongoing renewal responsibility: no tick, no handle, no restart re-arm; the loop is `disown`ed and its lifetime is the watched child pid's.
- [x] `sweep.md` Step 1a updated — the unconditional session-side `start` is withdrawn, replaced by a marker-gated fallback. Step 1b (#6320, manual/non-daemon) unchanged.
- [x] New tests in `dispatch.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` verifying the `--claim-owned` path invokes the start command with the correct pid/host/sweep-id.
- [x] A daemon restart between dispatch and renewal-loop start cannot leave a claim unrenewed — the spawn is synchronous inside `dispatch()`, not deferred.
- [x] `lease-renewal.md` + `daemon-reference.md` document the dispatch-time start.

## Test Plan

- [x] **New tests** (`loom-daemon/src/sweep_registry/dispatch.rs`), all verified load-bearing by mutation:
  - `claim_owned_dispatch_starts_the_lease_renewal_loop_for_its_own_child` — exact argv (`start <N> --watch-pid <outcome.pid> --host <published_host> --sweep-id <outcome.sweep_id>`), cwd = workspace root (#3928/#3937), and **exactly once** per dispatch. Mutating the call site to `if false` fails it.
  - `immediate_preflight_death_starts_no_renewal_loop` — edge case (a): the #4689 unwind path starts no loop. Moving the call *before* the preflight check fails it with the recorded argv.
  - `the_started_renewal_loop_is_detached_and_outlives_the_registry` — edge case (b): driven through a stub shaped like the real `start` (background subshell + `disown` + print pid); asserts the call returns promptly, the loop is alive, `registry.children` does not retain it, and it survives `drop(registry)`.
  - `missing_lease_renew_helper_is_a_silent_noop` / `a_failing_lease_renew_helper_never_fails_the_dispatch` — best-effort contract; the latter also asserts the helper's stderr landed in the sweep log (#6541).
  - `dispatch_exports_the_lease_renewal_capability_marker` / `pr_set_dispatch_exports_no_lease_renewal_marker` — marker set for `Issue`, withheld from `PrSet`.
  - `sweep_md_doc_lint::sweep_md_step_1a_keeps_a_marker_gated_lease_renewal_fallback` — pins the marker name, the surviving fallback command, and their order, so a later edit cannot simplify the gate away.
- [x] `cargo test` (whole crate): **5074 lib + 207 + all integration targets green**. One `pipeline_snapshot::tests::gh_pipeline_source_records_error_but_keeps_other_metrics` failure appeared in one full-suite run and not in two others (it passes in isolation) — pre-existing `#[serial]`/process-global-`PATH` flakiness in a module this PR does not touch, flagged here rather than fixed.
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` — zero warnings. `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- [x] Shell suites: `test-sweep-lease-renew.sh` 52/52, `test-sweep-lease-publish.sh` 66/66, `test-sweep-lease-fence.sh` 42/42, `test-sweep-lease-convergence.sh` 10/10. `shellcheck` clean.
- [x] Repo checks: `check-vendored-private-refs`, `check-docs-defaults-parity`, `check-dangling-links`, `check-hooks-defaults-parity`, `check-claude-md-budget`, `check-agents-md-sync`, `check-gitignore-convergence`, `check-defaults-version-bump` (VERSION → 0.19.40) — all OK.
- [ ] **Not done: live manual verification.** Dispatching a real `--cla

author: copilot
body:
Dependabot was opening multiple independent upgrade PRs that conflicted at the dependency graph level and created avoidable review noise. This change consolidates the active upgrades into one compatible update set and reconfigures Dependabot to emit grouped PRs instead of parallel single-package bumps.

- **Dependency set consolidation**
  - Combined pending upgrades from open Dependabot PRs into one coherent set:
    - `next` → `^16.3.5`
    - `react` / `react-dom` → `^19.3.0`
    - `@types/react` / `@types/react-dom` → `^19.3.0`
    - `tailwindcss` → `^4.3.3`
  - Updated lockfile to reflect the unified graph and avoid cross-PR peer mismatch failures.

- **Build/tooling compatibility updates for upgraded stack**
  - Switched PostCSS Tailwind plugin to the Tailwind v4 plugin package.
  - Migrated Tailwind config export to ESM to match project module mode.
  - Removed deprecated `swcMinify` key from Next config for Next 16 compatibility.

- **Dependabot policy change (reduce PR pile-up)**
  - Added grouping rules for both `npm` and `github-actions` ecosystems.
  - Reduced concurrent open PR limit to `1` per ecosystem to keep update flow serialized and reviewable.

```yaml
# .github/dependabot.yml
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: "npm"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 1
    groups:
      all-dependencies:
        patterns: ["*"]
        update-types: ["major", "minor", "patch"]
```

author: nickrabit
body:
Four things a real reorganisation ran into, plus the dialog shell underneath two
of them.

### A listed folder could only be walked into, never picked

`Use this folder` is `disabled` whenever `browse.path` is empty — which is
exactly the top level, where the rows **are** the granted roots. Pointing a
library back at its grant was possible only by knowing that opening the grant
first enables the button; the screen said the opposite.

Every row now carries a select control next to the one that opens it, so a
granted root is a destination like any other. Where the button had nothing to
act on it is replaced by a hint instead of sitting there disabled.

### Re-rooting could not create the folder it was moving into

The create-folder control was hidden in re-root mode, so moving a library into a
folder that did not exist yet had to be done outside the app. It is shown in
both modes now, and `PATCH /api/libraries/:id` takes `create` the way `POST`
already did. Re-root still copies, moves and deletes nothing — creating the
destination is the only thing it writes, and `docs/libraries.md` says so.

### The library order was insertion order

The server has always sorted by `order` and `PATCH` has always accepted it.
Nothing ever set it, so a new library took `max + 1` and the list looked
alphabetical only by accident. The rows carry up and down controls, at the right
edge of the card past the badges.

A move rewrites the whole sequence rather than swapping two numbers: existing
records can share an order or leave gaps, and a swap does not always move
anything in that state.

### Both dialogs scrolled in two places at once

The picker and the identify dialog share a shell: a card with `overflow:auto`
holding a list with its own `max-height` and `overflow:auto`. The wheel moved
the inner list until it bottomed out and then jolted the card.

The shell is now opt-in as `dialog-split` — head and action pinned, one
scrolling body between them — and the two dialogs that were complained about
take it. The other four keep what they have.

The picker's selection summary moves into the footer, beside the button that
acts on it. It used to sit below a folder list forty rows long, so while
browsing you could not see what was selected.

### And the last library loses its removal buttons

An empty library set breaks every unqualified path until a restart, and the
restart seeds an id that matches nothing the old library remembered. The
server-side refusal is #139; this is the half the user sees.

---

Unit tests cover picking a grant from the list, re-rooting into a folder that
does not exist yet, the reorder writing a sequence, and the structure of both
dialogs. `npm test` passes (190 web + server). Verified in the browser against
a local container with two libraries: the reorder round-trips through the API,
the picker selects a grant without opening it, and the card no longer scrolls
inside itself.

Playwright was not run — the layout baselines are regenerated once for the
whole block of work, not per change.

author: alaskantuna
body:
## What changed

Shared links to Layerhand currently preview blank, because the page carries
no link preview tags (#30).

- **Preview tags.** `withSocialMeta` adds these to the page's `<head>` when
  it is served:
  - `og:type` `website`, `og:title` `Layerhand`, and `og:description` with
    the tagline;
  - `og:url`;
  - `og:image`, `twitter:image`, and `twitter:card`
    `summary_large_image`.

  Every URL is absolute and built from `PUBLIC_URL` at render time, never
  written into the page. Without `PUBLIC_URL`, as in development, they use
  the address the page was requested from. Credentials in `PUBLIC_URL` are
  dropped.
- **Banners.** `og-image.png` is the light, on-brand banner, used for
  `og:image` and `twitter:image`. `og-image-dark.png` is served at a stable
  path for the Product Hunt gallery, and no tag references it. Both are
  1200x630 PNGs of about 650 KB.
  - They are served at `/og-image.png` and `/og-image-dark.png`.
  - They are imported as files, so `bun build` copies them next to the
    bundle.
- **How the page is served.** Bun serves the bundled page at
  `/page-shell`. The `/` route fetches it from the same server and adds the
  tags with `HTMLRewriter`, because an HTML bundle cannot be changed where
  it is served. The page's design and assets are unchanged.

## How it was verified

- `bun test`: all pass, and there are two new test files:
  - `social-meta.test.ts` checks the exact tag set, that the rest of the
    page is untouched, and that credentials are dropped.
  - `page-routes.test.ts` checks, over a real `Bun.serve`, that the
    rendered page carries an absolute `og:image` from the public address
    and still contains the app. It also checks the fallback to the request
    origin, and that both banner paths return 200 with `image/png` and the
    full file.
- **Production container.** `docker build` from this branch, run with
  `PUBLIC_URL=https://layerhand.test`:
  - `/` carries
    `<meta property="og:image" content="https://layerhand.test/og-image.png" />`
    and the app's `<main>`;
  - `/og-image.png` returns 200 `image/png`, 678,057 bytes;
  - `/og-image-dark.png` returns 200 `image/png`, 654,561 bytes.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bun run lint`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] The title follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] Every commit follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] Commits are atomic: one reason to change each, and each one builds.
- [x] Breaking changes are marked with `!` and explained in the body.
- [x] `bun run lint` passes.

author: mike-axiom-mir
body:
## ROLE
Gameplay Engineer — bounded gamepad Start/retry recovery reliability on the accepted Blackline Relay runtime.

## OBSERVED PROBLEM
A pre-blur held gamepad Start can remain latched across focus loss even after Start is released while unfocused. If focus returns while Start is observably neutral and the player presses Start again before the first post-focus simulation update, accepted `main` classifies that genuinely fresh press as already held and leaves terminal `BLACKOUT` unchanged.

Exact current-main reproduction sequence:
1. Enter terminal `BLACKOUT` and press Start once to establish the ordinary held-Start latch through a real retry.
2. Blur while Start remains held.
3. Release Start while unfocused; no gamepad poll/update occurs while unfocused.
4. Restore `BLACKOUT` and return focus while Start is observably released.
5. Press Start again before the first post-focus simulation update.

Expected: the neutral observation at focus return retires the old latch, so step 5 is a fresh retry edge.
Observed on current accepted composition before repair: step 5 leaves mode `BLACKOUT` rather than entering `RUNNING`.

## DELTA
Smallest repair in `guardFocusedGamepadCarryover()`:
- if the focused guard observes Start held for the selected standard gamepad, preserve the existing held latch;
- if it positively observes Start released, delete any stale held latch for that pad.

The branch also carries QA #122's exact 90-line regression onto current accepted `main` so the defect is preserved as current-composition RED -> GREEN evidence.

No movement tuning, retry rule, resource rule, collision, relay logic, world geometry, presentation language, progression, dependency, or identity change.

Current exact head: `e5eff4bd651480e66a946559d86c8656e1d50064`.
Current accepted base: `524cf5359fff28a74bfd59ffd002bea31763a5e9`.
Exact tested synthetic merge: `33d8b22a375e1c2d26a64dc54faeb3e8c18d950d`.

## PLAYER VALUE
After focus returns and has already observed the controller's Start button released, the player's next genuine Start press retries immediately instead of being silently discarded by stale bookkeeping. Held Start is still protected from becoming a counterfeit fresh edge.

## FILES / SYSTEMS TOUCHED
- `game.js` — only the Start-latch update inside `guardFocusedGamepadCarryover()`.
- `tests/qa-focus-return-start-release-edge.mjs` — exact deterministic reproduction from QA #122.

Effective proposal: 2 files, +94/-1, 2 commits.

## VERIFICATION
**TESTED — RED:** reproduction head `7383bad0e8a39a723d3bddef726af12ec10a67f5`, exact synthetic merge `d9da07e27936049326204e1f3d3d462f40503aaa`, workflow `34960892616`. GitHub Actions checked the reproduction against accepted base `524cf535...`. Every pre-existing deterministic target reached before/after the new case remained green; the suite failed with exactly one target: `qa-focus-return-start-release-edge.mjs`. The exact assertion was `actual: BLACKOUT`, `expected: RUNNING` for the fresh post-focus Start retry.

**TESTED — GREEN:** repaired head `e5eff4bd651480e66a946559d86c8656e1d50064`, exact synthetic merge `33d8b22a375e1c2d26a64dc54faeb3e8c18d950d`, workflow `34961148001`. `game.js` syntax plus **41/41 deterministic test files passed**, including focus/input parity, focus-time retry atomicity, controller-selection retry edges, multi-controller retry neutrality, restart neutrality, retry-input neutrality, startup controller swap neutrality, and the new focus-return Start-release regression.

**MEASURED:** RED had exactly 1 failing verification target and preserved `BLACKOUT` where the fresh retry expected `RUNNING`; GREEN passed 41/41 deterministic test files. Effective proposal size is 2 files, +94/-1.

**VISUALLY INSPECTED:** NOT TESTED for this repair.

**PLAYTESTED:** NOT TESTED with a human or physical USB/Bluetooth controller.

**INFERRED:** existing held-Start carryover protection is preserved because the focus guard still adds the latch when Start is observed pressed; surrounding deterministic focus/retry/takeover coverage remains green. Movement, resource, world, and presentation semantics are unchanged because their runtime paths were not modified.

**BLOCKED:** physical-controller focus timing and Chromium/Firefox/Safari/OS-specific Gamepad lifecycle behavior remain unavailable. A direct local repository checkout was also unavailable in this execution container because GitHub DNS resolution failed, so exact executable evidence comes from GitHub Actions on the PR merge composition.

**NOT TESTED:** subjective responsiveness/control feel, fresh-player comprehension, accessibility quality, fairness, balance, tension, polish, or fun.

## TRUTH BOUNDARY
This proves one deterministic simulated standard-gamepad focus-return ordering on the exact current-main composition. It does not prove how often physical controllers/browsers expose this ordering, does not establish cross-browser Gamepad lifecycle behavior, and does not justify broader controller ownership/input architecture.

## KNOWN LIMITATIONS
- The regression uses one standard-mapped controller at index 0.
- Immediate fresh-edge recovery requires the release to be observable when focus returns; if the browser does not expose a neutral controller state then, this test does not describe that environment.
- Real hardware/browser behavior remains evidence debt.

## DEPENDENCIES
Directly based on accepted `main` `524cf5359fff28a74bfd59ffd002bea31763a5e9`, which already includes merged Experience #121's semantically distinct terminal-success wording change. QA draft #122 remains the provenance-only RED reproduction lane; this PR is the Gameplay implementation lane. No external package, backend, account, asset, paid service, or runtime network dependency.

## OVERLAP CHECK
Immediate pre-publication rescan found accepted `main` still exactly `524cf5359fff28a74bfd59ffd002bea31763a5e9`. Open work is this Gameplay PR #123 plus QA reproduction PR #122. #122 intentionally contains no runtime repair and explicitly hands implementation to Gameplay. No competing Gameplay repair or newly occupied semantic lane appeared. An Experience review on this PR also identifies the defect as input-edge reliability and requests no presentation workaround or parallel implementation.

## SUGGESTED NEXT LANES
QA can independently verify exact repaired head `e5eff4bd...` and, when hardware is available, exercise the same release-during-unfocus -> focus-neutral -> immediate fresh Start sequence with physical controllers across representative browsers/OSes.

Draft and unmerged. Per the externally supplied standing task instruction governing this Gameplay lane, Mike remains merge/CANON authority. No merge, auto-promotion, overwrite of a human decision, or CANON declaration was performed; repository governance files with conflicting historical wording were not rewritten by Gameplay.

author: ndreas
body:
## Problem

`wml.CT_Picture` only decoded `w:movie` and `w:control`; every other child was logged and skipped. That includes all VML (`v:shape`, `v:shapetype`, `v:rect`, `o:lock`, …), which the Transitional schema allows via `xsd:any` wildcards.

Opening and saving a document therefore turned every VML picture into an empty `<w:pict/>`. The most visible victim is Word's **Design → Watermark → Picture**, which is always written as VML in the header, so letterhead backgrounds disappeared while the image part and its relationship stayed orphaned in the package.

## Fix

Keep unknown children in `CT_Picture.Extra []unioffice.Any` (as `unioffice.XSDAny`) and write them back out, the same pattern `CT_R` and `CT_SdtPr` already use. Extra content is written before `w:movie`/`w:control`, matching the schema's wildcard order. `XSDAny` declares the namespaces it uses on its own root element and derives the conventional `v:` / `o:` / `r:` prefixes, so the output is well-formed even though `w:document`/`w:hdr` don't declare VML namespaces.

## Tests

- `document/pict_vml_test.go` — builds a DOCX in memory with a `v:rect` in the body and a full Word picture watermark in the header; after two read/save round-trips it checks the XML is well-formed, VML elements/attributes survive, and `v:imagedata r:id` still resolves to `media/image1.png`. Both tests fail without the fix.
- `schema/soo/wml/CT_Picture_extra_test.go` — Extra content is written before `w:control` and re-decodes cleanly.

`go test ./...` passes; gofmt / vet / golangci-lint clean on changed files.

## Not yet verified

- Manual check that Word / LibreOffice render the round-tripped watermark.

## Out of scope

The same log-and-skip `default:` exists in ~210 other generated `wml` types (e.g. `CT_RPr` drops `w14:ligatures`).

author: rkarabut
body:
## Problem
The BLOCK_TXS handler seeds its response from `request.txHashes` and serves them even when it can't find the block (the intended fallback). Nothing caps that list, so a peer can send an empty bit list plus ~2,045 explicit hashes (inside a ~64 KB frame) and force one full tx (up to 512 KiB) to be serialized per hash — ~1 GB of response from one request. The size estimator also counted only bit-list positions, so it under-reported these requests.

## Fix
- Cap the explicit-hash count at a shared `MAX_BLOCK_TXS_PER_REQUEST`, rejecting over-cap requests with `BADLY_FORMED_REQUEST` before the pool lookup.
- Clamp the batch requester's `txBatchSize` to the same constant, so an honest (even reconfigured) requester never sends more than the responder will serve — no config-vs-cap conflict.
- Count explicit hashes in `calculateBlockTxsResponseSize` so the estimate reflects the real response size.

## Test
Adds a handler regression test: an over-cap explicit-hash request (empty bit list) is rejected before `getTxsByHash`. Verified red→green against the built base (block_txs 42/42 green, batch-tx-requester 37/37 with the clamp; the reject test fails without the cap), prettier clean, `tsgo -b` exit 0.

Addresses the LabsBox audit finding "[aztec-node] BLOCK_TXS explicit tx hashes bypass response-size accounting" (and its near-duplicate). A responder-side output-byte ceiling before compression remains a broader follow-up.

author: l4xb
body:
## Summary

`cancel-in-progress: false` on the CLA workflow, so it stops cancelling itself on
the sequence `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks every contributor to perform.

Seen on #144, and on every pull request before it:

```
Canceling since a higher priority waiting request for cla-144 exists
CLA acceptance verified for @L4XB on pull request #144.
##[error]The operation was canceled.
```

The run had already verified the acceptance and published the status. It was
cancelled during cleanup by the next event in the same concurrency group, and
GitHub reports a cancelled run as a failed check.

## Behavior and compatibility

### What was happening

1. `pull_request_target: opened` starts run A.
2. The author posts the acceptance sentence — because `CONTRIBUTING.md` tells
   them to — which fires `issue_comment: created` and queues run B.
3. B enters group `cla-<number>`, `cancel-in-progress: true` kills A.
4. A is reported as a failed check named **Publish CLA status**, sitting next to
   the green **CLA / acceptance** it produced moments earlier.

The required check was never in danger: `CLA / acceptance` is the required
context and it was green, and `Publish CLA status` is not required, so nothing
was ever blocked. Nothing on the pull-request page says that. A first-time
contributor sees a red X next to the word *CLA* immediately after doing exactly
what they were asked.

### Why queueing is correct here, not just quieter

Cancelling would be the right choice if a superseded run's work were wasted.
It is not, and it was never safe:

- `check_cla.py` reads the head SHA from `GET /pulls/{n}` at the start of each
  run, not from the event payload, and posts the status against **that** commit.
  Two runs therefore write per-commit statuses that cannot clobber each other
  wrongly.
- With the group serialized, the run that finishes last is the one that read the
  newest comments and the newest head. Convergence, not a race.
- Cancelling, by contrast, left a real window: a run could publish `pending`, be
  killed before publishing the verdict, and leave a pull request pending on a
  check that nothing would re-trigger until the next event.

`issue-claims.yml` already reaches the same conclusion for its own reason ("Two
people claiming the same issue in the same second must not both win"). This
brings the second workflow that reacts to comments into line with it.

### Cost

One job of about eight seconds per comment event on a pull request, instead of
collapsing them. They run one at a time, so a chatty pull request queues rather
than fans out.

### Residual case, stated rather than hidden

With `cancel-in-progress: false`, GitHub still cancels a *pending* run when a
newer one queues behind an already-running one. That needs three events in quick
succession — open, comment, comment — and cancels a run that never started
rather than one mid-flight. The common sequence this issue is about, open then
accept, produces no cancellation at all. Eliminating the remaining case would
mean not triggering on ordinary comments, which would also stop noticing a
deleted acceptance; that trade is not worth making here.

### Not changed

The verifier itself, the status context, the acceptance sentence, the reminder,
the permissions, the checkout of the protected default branch, and the triggers.
Rollback is reverting one line.

## Validation

```console
$ uv run pytest -q tests/test_repository_automation.py   # 74 passed  (72 before)
$ uv run pytest -q                                       # 357 passed
$ uv run ruff check src tests .github/scripts            # All checks passed!
$ uv run ruff format --check src tests .github/scripts   # 24 files already formatted
$ uv run mypy src/sixsentences                           # no issues found in 40 source files
$ python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/cla.yml'))"
  concurrency: {'group': 'cla-…', 'cancel-in-progress': False}
```

Two new tests, one per acceptance criterion that can be asserted locally:

- `test_the_cla_workflow_queues_its_runs_instead_of_cancelling_them` pins the
  setting and the reason, in the same shape as the existing claim-workflow test.
- `test_repeated_cla_runs_repeat_the_result_without_repeating_the_reminder`
  plays the real serialized sequence against a stubbed API — open (reminder
  posted), the reminder's own event (no second reminder), acceptance (success),
  and one more run (still success, still one reminder). This is the criterion
  about idempotency and the one about not reminding twice.

The criterion about a `synchronize` mid-run is covered by construction and by
the existing `test_cla_status_is_bound_to_the_exact_pull_request_head`: the
status is always posted against the head SHA read from the API during that run,
so the queued `synchronize` run ends with the newest commit carrying a verdict.

The end-to-end criterion — "opening a pull request and posting the CLA sentence
immediately afterwards leaves no failed check" — can only be observed on a real
pull request. **This pull request is that test:** it was opened and the
acceptance sentence posted immediately afterwards. Note that the workflow that
runs for *this* pull request is the one on `main`, so the red X is expected here
and should be gone on the next pull request after the merge. I will confirm it
on the following one.

- [x] Engine checks pass, or the engine is unaffected.
- [x] API, migration, worker, and web-contract checks pass, or they are unaffected. — unaffected
- [x] Web type-check, tests, and production build pass, or the web app is unaffected. — unaffected
- [x] Browser-extension contracts and a deployment-bound build pass, or the extension is unaffected. — unaffected
- [x] macOS Companion boundary check, locked resolution, tests, and release build pass on the pinned Xcode toolchains—or the Companion is unaffected. — unaffected
- [x] Self-hosting tests and container builds pass, or deployment is unaffected. — unaffected
- [x] User-facing behavior has a focused test or the omission is explained.

## Review boundaries

- [x] Security and privacy effects were reviewed. The workflow keeps
      `pull_request_target` reading only the protected default branch, still
      checks out no contribution ref, still executes no contributor-controlled
      code, and keeps the same `permissions:` block. Concurrency changes when a
      run executes, never what it is allowed to do. Serializing removes a
      cancellation window in which a pull request could be left permanently
      `pending` on a required status.
- [x] New network calls and processors are operator-configurable, fail closed, and document data egress, cost, retention, and failure behavior—or none were added. — none
- [x] Dependencies and bundled assets are justified, locked, and redistribution-compatible—or none were added. — none
- [x] Native-client changes include explicit origin, local-retention/deletion, permission, signing, update, and binary-distribution implications. — none
- [x] Research-method assumptions, limitations, and provenance remain visible—or no research-facing behavior changed. — none
- [x] Accessibility and keyboard behavior were reviewed for UI changes—or no UI changed. — no UI
- [x] Browser permissions, capture bounds, pairing callbacks, extension storage, and generated host access were reviewed—or the extension is unaffected. — unaffected

## Source-release hygiene

- [x] No secret, private key, production configuration, customer/participant data, user upload, database dump, log, private prompt, or non-redistributable research content is included.
- [x] The change belongs in the community stack; payment, subscription, commercial-plan, hosted-administration, and marketing-site code remains separate.

author: kirangathani
body:
## Why

`bin/fm-assert-tests-kept.sh` check 2 compares the assertion names two runs emitted, and can only do that while a name is stable. Two assertions in `tests/fm-fix-instructions-check.test.sh` built their name from a value measured at run time:

```
pass "fix-instructions acceptance matrix: ${#MATRIX_IDS[@]} cases x 5 harness entry forms, block/allow all correct"
pass "substance floor: named constant MIN_INSTRUCTIONS_CHARS=$floor, boundary exact, justified in a comment"
```

The first expands to the case count *of the tree under test*, so it is a different string on any branch that adds a case. The gate then reads one passing assertion as an assertion that vanished, reports it as `unstable:`, and **blocks the landing while never having verified the assertion at all**. Observed on PR 87, which grows the matrix from 35 to 41 cases: `unstable: 2`, and by that script's own rule (its header, and the exit-code contract at `bin/fm-assert-tests-kept.sh:254`) that blocks.

The remedy is the one that script's header prescribes: "name the assertion with a constant string and put the runtime value in its fail message."

## What this changes

Only those two `pass` names, nothing else. Each case's own failure already names the case, and both substance-floor boundary checks already carry `$floor` in their own fail messages, so no observable information is lost — the totals move to a diagnostic line beside the assertion:

```
# matrix: 35 cases x 5 harness entry forms
ok - fix-instructions acceptance matrix: every case blocks or allows correctly through every harness entry form
# substance floor: MIN_INSTRUCTIONS_CHARS=120
ok - substance floor: named constant MIN_INSTRUCTIONS_CHARS, boundary exact, justified in a comment
```

No behavior, no coverage, and no other assertion is touched. `tests/fm-fix-instructions-check.test.sh` passes (18 ok), `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean.

## This PR will itself be refused by the keep gate, and that needs a decision

Measured, not predicted. Running the gate's own extractor (`extract_shell`, `bin/fm-assert-tests-kept.sh:552`) over `origin/main` and this branch:

```
=== base names absent on branch (check 1 "missing") ===
fix-instructions acceptance matrix: ${#MATRIX_IDS[@]} cases x 5 harness entry forms, block/allow all correct
substance floor: named constant MIN_INSTRUCTIONS_CHARS=$floor, boundary exact, justified in a comment
```

Check 1 is a plain static-name set difference (`comm -23 "$TMPD/base" "$TMPD/branch"`, line 624) with no exemption for a name containing `$`. So retiring a runtime-named assertion necessarily reports it `missing:` — which blocks by the same exit rule.

**That is a genuine gap between two of the gate's own rules: its header prescribes a fix that its own check 1 refuses.** There is no shape of this change that satisfies both checks. Keeping the old line alongside a new constant one clears both checks today, but leaves the interpolation in place, so the next branch that changes the case count is `unstable:` again — it defers the problem rather than curing it.

So retiring a runtime-named assertion structurally requires a captain-approved entry in `data/supersessions/firstmate.md`. Two exact entries with `kind: missing` cover it, per the grammar in `bin/fm-pr-merge.sh`'s header:

```
- id: tests/fm-fix-instructions-check.test.sh::fix-instructions acceptance matrix: ${#MATRIX_IDS[@]} cases x 5 harness entry forms, block/allow all correct | project: firstmate | kind: missing | date: 2026-09-15 | reason: <captain's reason>
- id: tests/fm-fix-instructions-check.test.sh::substance floor: named constant MIN_INSTRUCTIONS_CHARS=$floor, boundary exact, justified in a comment | project: firstmate | kind: missing | date: 2026-09-15 | reason: <captain's reason>
```

Both identifiers are free of the ` | ` sequence the grammar reserves, so neither is ambiguous.

body:
## Problem

Header sorting seemed to work only on a couple of columns per table (on Sources: Source and Created). Two column-definition patterns defeated it:

- **Accessor keys naming fields that don't exist on the row.** `type`, `assets`, `destinations`, `resources`, `cron`, `target_ids`, `events`, `watches` and hooks' `enabled` are derived values, not `ComponentRecord` fields, so TanStack compared `undefined` for every row and the click reordered nothing.
- **Created columns sorting on the formatted date.** Their accessor returned "15 Sep, 12:04", so ordering was by day number and month name as text: right within a day, wrong across months. Job and hook state datetime columns (Next run, Last run) did the same.

## Fix

- Every derived column gets an explicit `id` and an `accessorFn` returning the value it displays: type name, asset count (numeric), joined target / destination / watch / connection names, schedule summary, enabled flag. The relation lookups moved into small per-page helpers shared by accessor and cell.
- `dateColumn` in `utils/table.ts` replaces the five copied Created columns: sorts on the raw ISO value, formats in the cell. State datetime columns now do the same.
- The resource page matched its state columns by `accessorKey`; it matches by `id` now.

Admin, tokens, members, runs and backfills tables already sorted on real fields and are untouched.

## Verified

Live on a seeded throwaway instance with two sources of different types: Type, Assets, Created and Source reorder correctly both ways; Jobs' Schedule and Targets sort without error. `nuxt typecheck` passes; lint shows only pre-existing warnings.

author: aganatsu
body:
Follow-up to #530. Two problems surfaced by trying to redraw a leg on TradingView.

## Times were thrown away

`impulseZoneEngine:192` did `startCandle.datetime.slice(0, 10)`, discarding the time it already had. A 1H leg reading `2026-09-14 → 2026-09-15` over 7 bars can't be located on a chart from that.

`startTime`/`endTime` now keep the full datetime. `startDate`/`endDate` stay for anything already reading them.

## The direction was printed backwards

The panel rendered `low → high` unconditionally, so a **bearish** leg showed:

```
↓ BEARISH  1.34647 → 1.35058
```

when price actually travelled `1.35058 → 1.34647`. Now `origin → terminus`, derived from direction — `high` and `low` alone never said which way price went.

## Retracement grid

23.6 / 38.2 / 50 / 61.8 / 70.5 / 79, computed **direction-aware**. A retracement travels back toward the leg's origin, so a bullish leg retraces *down* from the high and a bearish leg *up* from the low. Computing both the same way would put every bearish level below the low, where price has already been. A test asserts the two directions mirror about the midpoint.

61.8% and 70.5% are highlighted as the OTE band.

## Result

```
1H Impulse: ↓ BEARISH  1.35058 → 1.34647  (41.1 pips)
            Displacement: moderate  body 61% · max 2.3× avg range · 1/7 bars
            23.6% 1.34744  38.2% 1.34804  50.0% 1.34853  61.8% 1.34901  70.5% 1.34937  79.0% 1.34972
            BOS: 1.34647  2026-09-14T21:00:00 → 2026-09-15T04:00:00  (7 bars)
```

519 tests pass, `deno check` clean, frontend builds.

author: excelius-wang
body:
# PR type
- [x] Bug Fix
- [ ] New Feature
- [ ] Document Updates
- [ ] More Models or Datasets Support

# PR information

Ray sampling dispatch currently sends only `messages` to each worker. This drops separate media fields and other dataset columns. It also changes the row hash: a valid local sampling cache can miss after dispatch because the automatically added `dataset` column is absent. With `--sampler_engine no`, that miss attempts generation and raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'infer'`.

Slice every input column using the existing row boundaries in both `VanillaSampler.generate` and `DistillSampler.generate`. This preserves worker inputs and cache keys while keeping RayHelper, worker assignment, and result collection unchanged. It does not add separate media-field conversion to the distillation OpenAI client.

## Experiment results

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python -m pytest \
  tests/general/test_sampler_ray_dispatch.py \
  tests/general/test_sampler_engine_kwargs.py -q
pre-commit run --all-files
```

- 35 tests pass. Coverage includes both samplers, cached/generated responses, text/media/metadata columns, empty and uneven partitions, workers outnumbering rows, and parity with local outputs and inference requests.
- Before the fix, 16 extra-column cases fail while 16 messages-only controls pass.
- A separate CPU probe generates a cache through the native sampling pipeline, then reads it through two recording worker handles. The upstream dispatch loses the loader-added `dataset` column and misses the cache; the fixed dispatch writes both correctly scored rows.
- All pre-commit hooks pass.

Tests run the actual driver/worker decorators, dispatch, worker methods, and collection logic. Ray transport and model outputs are simulated; no live Ray cluster or full model inference was run.

author: vaniell0
body:
## Summary

The last piece of series item 3. A node now carries a `RenderLevel`, and a renderer asks the object rather than guessing.

| level | what it is | per ray |
|---|---|---|
| `Exact` | the closed form — the real surface | torus 20.9 ns |
| `Tessellated` | triangles in a BVH | 40.8 ns, plus the build |
| `Newton` | Newton's method on the `(u,v)` map | **23 612 ns** |

**Inference lives in one place**, so a renderer cannot drift from it: an exact form when the node has one, tessellation otherwise, and **Newton never inferred**. A default that reached for Newton would hand a caller three orders of magnitude they never asked for.

**`rendered_as()` refuses on the spot**, in the pattern `offset()` established — `Exact` on a node with no closed form, `Newton` on one with no `(u,v)` map, tessellation of a group that is many objects rather than one. Quietly substituting something else is exactly how a caller ends up paying Newton without asking.

## The number, measured through the DSL rather than on hand-built shapes

A `Trace` of 64 tori, materialized, bucketed by `render_level()`. The two buckets differ by **one `.rendered_as()` call**.

| | build | per ray | leaves |
|---|---|---|---|
| exact | **0.011 ms** | 44.2 ns | 64 |
| tessellated | **78.8 ms** | 48.5 ns | 147 456 |

Seven thousand times the build cost, for a tenth of the per-ray cost back.

## Two corrections this forced

**PR #36 over-claimed and is corrected here.** Its comment read the dough's 2× per-ray win as the speck scene's result reversing. It is not: one leaf against 25 600 is an extreme ratio, and at 64 tori the per-ray numbers come back to a wash. Across all three measurements the per-ray figure points wherever the leaf ratio pushes it — 20% slower for specks, 2× faster for the dough, level here — so it supports nothing on its own. What survives is that **the tessellation never exists**.

**The first version of this benchmark was wrong, and I caught it before concluding.** Laid out on a 42-unit grid, it reported the exact path as *slower*. `make_rays()` fires from `(3,3,3)` toward the origin, so a scene spread wider than that gets a ray set that mostly misses it — the comparison became one of hit rates, not of leaf cost. The reason is now a comment in the file so nobody re-derives it.

## What the demo says, kept rather than hidden

```
render levels: 0 exact, 19809 tessellated, 0 newton
```

**No exact objects at all** — and that is the mechanism working, not failing. The dough is an `Offset` carrying a noise bump, so it stopped being a torus the moment it got bread texture. An exact form is a promise about the shape, and a bumped torus cannot keep it. This is the visible report that keeps a downgrade from being something you infer from a frame time.

## Test plan

- Inference: torus → `Exact`, `space(make_torus(...))` → `Tessellated`, cube → `Tessellated`.
- Newton is never inferred on any path, and asking is enough to get it.
- An explicit level overrides, and the exact form survives the override.
- `rendered_as()` refuses all three impossible cases, leaving the node unchanged.
- `.moving()` dropping the exact form drops the inferred level with it.
- Full local `ctest`: 955/955. Both doc-freshness scripts clean.
- `donut_demo --photo` renders byte-identical (`f70084505b375edb79ff725651f5cd69`).

author: andrew01234567890
body:
## Why

A cluster with `spec.internalTLS.issue: true` could not work end to end (PGS-860), and no suite ran one:

- The router dials a pooler at its member host (`<member>.<cluster>-<group>-peers.<ns>.svc`). The issued pooler certificate names only role-wide names and one-label wildcards, so hostname verification failed and every statement through the router failed.
- The operator's agent and controller clients were process-wide and took credentials only from flags the manifest never sets, so they dialled an issuing cluster's mTLS agents in plaintext. Each issuing cluster has its own CA, so one process-wide certificate could never work. The `<cluster>-tls-operator` Secret was issued and never read.
- Agents are dialled by pod IP, and peers resolve IPs; issued certificates carry no IP SANs.

## What

- **Callers verify a role-wide name plus the peer's role.**
  - Router to poolers, and controller to agents, verify `<cluster>.<ns>.svc`. Router to peers verifies the router Service host.
  - Every issued-TLS dial also authorises the certificate's pgshard identity with `pki.Serves(role)`, so a certificate of another role in the same CA cannot answer.
  - The operator renders `--pooler-tls-server-name`, `--peer-tls-server-name` and `--agent-tls-server-name` when it issues.
  - Pooler and agent certificates now carry only the cluster's own names (`<cluster>`, `<cluster>.<ns>`, `<cluster>.<ns>.svc`, `*.<cluster>.<ns>.svc`). The namespace-wide wildcards, which made a member certificate valid for the controller and router Service hosts, are removed.
- **The operator dials with per-cluster credentials.**
  - `IssuedCredentials` builds agent and controller client credentials from each cluster's `<cluster>-tls-operator` Secret, cached by ResourceVersion.
  - The agent client and scheduled-barrier client dial with those credentials.
  - Process-wide flags remain the fallback for clusters that bring their own certificates.
- **Reissue on name changes.** A certificate whose DNS names differ from what its role now needs is reissued, so upgraded clusters drop the old wildcard certificates.
- **New e2e cell `{pg: 18, suite: tls}`.** It provisions an issuing cluster, routes a statement through the router to a pooler over mTLS, fails over, and routes again.

## Verification

- Unit tests:
  - `TestEveryCallerVerifiesANameTheIssuedCertificateCarries` checks each rendered server-name flag against the issued certificate, shows the dialled address alone fails, and shows member certificates are not valid for the controller or router hosts.
  - `operatorcreds_test.go` runs real mTLS handshakes against issued listeners: per-cluster agent and controller credentials, reload on Secret change, and refusal of another role's certificate.
  - `dialnames_test.go` and `agentdial_test.go` pin the flag wiring.
  - `TestAChangeToWhatARoleServesReissuesItsCertificate`.
- Mutation-checked on file copies. Each of these fails its test: a wrong pooler, peer or agent server-name flag; the agent credentials authorising the wrong role; the controller credentials authorising any role; dropping the reissue-on-names check.
- The local kind run of `TestAnIssuedTLSClusterRoutesAndFailsOver` passed (PG 18).
- Review: Fable 5.1 medium. Its criticals (reissue on name change, the controller server name) are fixed in the last commit.

## Not in this PR

- CA rotation overlap (`ca.crt` holds only the current CA) belongs to the staged rollout, PGS-236.
- The issued-TLS cell does not yet take a backup or a barrier. That is PGS-861.

author: hugo-vrijswijk
body:
Split `QueryCompiler.compile` into `prepare` (parsing and document-level validation, depends only on document text and schema) and `compilePrepared` (variable coercion, directive validation, elaboration, depends on the per-request `Env`).

Add `CachingQueryCompiler` and `QueryCache`, which cache the `prepare` result by document text, including parse failures. Default: 1024 documents, one-hour TTL, LRU eviction. Both are configurable, and callers can supply their own `QueryCache`.

Add docs for setup and configuration.

**Backend infrastructure and database integration:**

author: colin-gourlay
body:
## Summary

The existing forms require software-oriented detail that does not fit many archive and editorial reports. Simplify the chooser to three lightweight forms, each with one required answer:

- Bug Report captures what happened, with optional expected behaviour, reproduction context, device/browser and supporting details.
- Feature Request focuses on the problem and desired outcome without requiring an implementation or alternatives.
- Content Correction / Missing Content covers archive, metadata, editorial, links and imagery, with optional location and sources.

Explicitly preserve blank issues. Retain the existing `bug` and `enhancement` labels; leave content reports unlabelled because existing content labels only cover particular page types. No new labels or default assignees are introduced.

Closes #705.

- Parsed all four YAML files with PyYAML and checked form structure, unique field IDs, exactly three unique forms, one required field per form, existing default labels and enabled blank issues.
- Reviewed wording against the issue acceptance criteria and GitHub Issue Forms documentation.
- `git diff --cached --check` passed.

No website pages changed. Form prompts use plain language and descriptive labels; technical details and supporting sources are optional.

author: mechsterrd-maker
body:
## Problem

Trying to issue **500 mm** (0.5 m), the user typed `0.5` in the **rods** box and got a browser error: *"Please enter a valid value. The two nearest valid values are 0 and 1."* — because the rod **count** must be a whole number (you can't issue half a rod). A part-length is a *cut*, not a fractional rod.

## Fix

- **Rod count box now accepts whole numbers only** (digits-only text input) — no more browser popup.
- Added **column labels** to each rod line: *Rods (whole) · Length · Cut*.
- Added a hint for issuing a part-length: keep **Rods = 1**, pick the rod, and type the length in **Cut** (offcut returns to stock) — or just use **📏 Metre** mode and type `0.5` (e.g. 500 mm = 0.5 m).

So the two correct ways to issue 500 mm are now obvious: Metre mode `0.5`, or Rods `1 × [rod] cut 0.5`.

body:
## Summary

Closes the last gap `0013_muatan_jual_purchase_persistence.sql`'s own comment flagged: `rpc_buy_from_lot` only ever reserved stock (`carrier_stock_lots.qty_reserved`) and recorded intent (`public.lot_purchases`) — nothing ever converted a reservation into a completed sale, moved `qty_sold`, or posted a sen to `internal.ledger_*`.

**Why now, given MJ-01 ("escrow vs BNM") is explicitly listed as blocking "everything monetary"**: I flagged this tradeoff before building and the user confirmed building it dormant — same posture as every other Muatan Jual/Kongsi & Untung piece merged in #43: fully built and tested, but unreachable until `ref.compliance_state.status = 'PRODUCTION_ACTIVE'` and the relevant `ref.feature_gates` flip on, neither of which this PR touches.

## What this does

`rpc_confirm_lot_handover(p_purchase)` — a carrier's own confirmation that a reserved `lot_purchases` row was physically handed over and paid for:

- Reuses the exact same trust model and accounts `internal.fn_record_cod_collection` (0004) already uses for a Kirim/Jualan COD delivery — "cash exists in the world before it exists in the system" — rather than inventing a second cash-collection mechanism. The carrier's `cod_held_sen` and `CARRIER_CASH_RECEIVABLE:{carrier}` account move exactly the way they already do for any other COD collection, so the existing `internal.fn_remit_cod` remittance sweep nets Muatan Jual proceeds together with regular COD cash with zero changes.
- Settles per `ADDENDUM-COMMERCE.md` §5.4's own worked example, in the same ledger transaction: the sale (escrow in, commission + carrier payable out) and cost of goods sold (carrier payable out, carrier inventory out).
- Idempotent the same way `internal.fn_settle_delivery` is (`ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING` on the ledger transaction) — a retried confirm returns `ALREADY_SETTLED` rather than posting twice.
- Re-checks `internal.fn_marketplace_gate(checkout := true)` — the same call `rpc_buy_from_lot` already makes — and the carrier's own float-limit exposure (`ck_carrier_exposure`, 0006), since the cash just collected and the inventory it came from move in the same breath.

**A real correctness bug this exposed**: `carrier_stock_lots.qty_sold` has been permanently 0 since 0006 — nothing ever wrote it. `internal.fn_expire_lots`'s own perishable write-down reads `qty_total - qty_sold` to compute a carrier's loss, so every expiring lot was written down as if not one unit had ever sold, even a fully reconciled one. This RPC is also the fix for that.

## Verification

- [x] Applied to production; confirmed `ref.compliance_state.status = 'NOT_READY'` and `muatan_jual_enabled`/`muatan_jual_checkout_enabled`/`kongsi_untung_enabled` all `false`, before and after.
- [x] `39_muatan_jual_settlement.test.sql` (plan 13): authorization, the ledger transaction balancing to zero, `qty_reserved`/`qty_sold` moving correctly, `cod_held_sen`/`inventory_at_risk_sen` moving together, an idempotent retry posting nothing twice, the float-limit refusal, and that turning `muatan_jual_checkout_enabled` back off refuses settlement outright ahead of any other check (proving the gate call is real, not decoration).
- [x] CI green (Database verification gate, Secrets, Schema + RLS matrix, Typecheck + size gate)
