author: ethntuttle
body:
### What this does

Adds proof of *when* the data in this repo existed — checkable by anyone, without having to trust the author, GitHub, or a date on a commit.

### Why it's worth doing

A commit date is just a label. Whoever controls a repository can set it to whatever they like, and rewrite the history afterward. As it stands, nothing in here can establish its own age to someone who doesn't already trust the author.

That was always a soft spot. AI has turned it into a live one, in two directions:

- **Numbers can be quietly changed.** If a figure gets challenged, it can be edited and re-committed so the record looks like it always said the new thing. Nobody can prove otherwise.
- **The whole corpus can be waved away.** Because AI makes documents, screenshots and spreadsheets cheap to fabricate, any inconvenient evidence can be dismissed as "probably generated after the fact." That accusation costs nothing to make — and until now there was nothing here that could answer it.

This repo is an obvious target for both, since it states up front that it was assembled with AI agents.

A timestamp closes that gap. It pins the data to a moment nobody can move later — not the author, not GitHub, not a hosting company. If METR, Anthropic or Coefficient responds next month, the record shows what this said beforehand. If a cited source page is edited or quietly deleted, the copy here is already dated.

### What it proves, and what it doesn't

It proves the files are **at least this old, and unchanged since**.

It does **not** prove the numbers are right. Timestamping fixes *when*, never *whether* — accuracy is still the job of `NOTES.md`, the row ids and the audits. Worth stating plainly so the proof isn't oversold.

### How anyone checks it

```
sha256sum -c timestamps/SHA256SUMS.txt        # the files still match the list
ots verify timestamps/SHA256SUMS.txt.ots      # when the list was sealed
```

Both passing means these files are that old.

`ots verify` needs a Bitcoin node, and **running your own is the preferred way** — it is the only check that trusts nobody. Without one:

```
python3 scripts/verify_timestamp.py
```

That does the same check through a public block explorer. **Someone else's node ordinarily suffices**: the only thing the explorer is trusted for is a public block header, which is identical on every honest node and cross-checkable against an unrelated explorer with `--explorer`. A small, ordinary assumption — and far better than not checking at all.

### How it works, briefly

Every tracked file's fingerprint goes into one list (`timestamps/SHA256SUMS.txt`). That list is sealed into the Bitcoin blockchain via [OpenTimestamps](https://opentimestamps.org) — a free, open standard, with no company behind it and nothing to sign up for. One small proof covers all 2,265 files, and any single figure can be checked on its own.

Untracked scratch files are deliberately excluded, so the list describes exactly what a clone of this repo contains. Full method, and how to re-stamp when new data lands, is in `timestamps/README.md`.

### Status: confirmed

The proof is **complete and confirmed in the Bitcoin blockchain**, at block **967117**, mined **2026-09-15 11:15:55 UTC**. Every file in the list is provably at least that old, and unaltered since. It no longer depends on any timestamping server staying online — it verifies against the blockchain alone.

Checked against two unrelated block explorers, blockstream.info and mempool.space, which agree on that block's merkle root and time. The list itself verifies 2265/2265.

An earlier stamp of the same evidence is also confirmed, in block 967051 at 2026-09-15 01:30:16 UTC (commit `64a57d8`). It was superseded only because correcting a documentation error changed a file the list covers. The evidence itself — `research/`, `evidence/`, `figures/`, `EVIDENCE.txt`, `MANIFEST.csv`, `NOTES.md` — is unchanged between the two, so that earlier block stands as the earliest date on record for it. `timestamps/README.md` has an "Earlier anchorings" table and how to check it.

### Changes

- `README.md` — a short section on dating the repo
- `timestamps/` — the list, the proof, and the full method
- `scripts/timestamp.sh` — build and re-stamp
- `scripts/verify_timestamp.py` — verify without a Bitcoin node

author: thomaslabarriere
body:
## What

`mcp-eval` had no tests of its own: `test/` only held `tsconfig.json`, so the `"test": "vitest"` script found no files and exited. This PR extracts the per-response scoring logic out of the OpenAI call into a pure, testable function (`src/scoring.ts`), adds a vitest suite, and fixes three issues that skew a server's evaluated score.

## Fixes

1. **Only the first tool call was inspected** (`response.choices[0].message.tool_calls?.[0]`). Assistants routinely emit the expected call as a parallel/secondary call (especially once the extra assistant tools are injected), which was falsely scored as wrong-tool / no-tool. Scoring now scans all returned tool calls for a name + parameters match.
2. **A single throwing test aborted the whole run.** An unguarded `JSON.parse` of the tool arguments (or an error from the model call) rejected the `Promise.all`, so no `mcp-eval.json` and no summary were produced. Malformed arguments now surface the already-defined-but-never-produced `ErrorResult`, each test is isolated so one failure no longer drops every result, and errored tests are reported in the summary.
3. **The parameter check was subset-only** (it iterated only over the expected keys), so a call carrying the expected params plus extra/hallucinated ones passed while the summary still labelled it "wrong set of parameters". Kept the subset behaviour as the default (so existing suites keep their scores) and added an opt-in exact match.

## Tests

`test/scoring.test.ts` covers: the expected tool returned as a secondary/parallel call, message/tool/parameter mismatches, subset vs exact parameter matching, and malformed arguments surfacing as a scored error instead of a throw.

`pnpm build`, `pnpm lint` and `vitest --run` (8/8) all pass. I also reverted the multi-call fix locally to confirm the parallel-call test fails without it, so the test genuinely guards the behaviour.

author: petrogad
body:
A freshly provisioned Linux dev node came up unable to do the one thing it exists for.

`db-clone`, `db-drop` and `db-ls` are thin wrappers around `createdb`, `dropdb` and `psql`, and
`refresh-seed` uses `pg_dump`. None of those were installed, because `postgresql-client` wasn't in
the list — so the node couldn't reach the Postgres host at all.

## Added

| Package | Why |
|---|---|
| `postgresql-client` | **load-bearing** — every database helper is a wrapper around it |
| `gh` | not in Debian's repos, so `bootstrap` now adds the `cli.github.com` apt source (idempotent) before `apt-packages` tries to resolve it |
| `mosh` | survives sleep, roaming and IP changes; the difference between reattaching to a remote tmux session and rebuilding it |

## One fix that had to come first

`packages.txt` now carries comments explaining the non-obvious entries — but `apt-packages` piped
the file straight into `xargs`, so a `#` line would have been handed to `apt-get` as a list of
package names and the target would have failed outright.

It now strips comments and blank lines. Verified the filter yields exactly 17 clean package names
from a file with 7 comment lines.

The README documented the old constraint ("no comments"), so that's updated too — the rule is now
inverted.

author: hervenicol
body:
## What

Sets `serviceAccountTokenSecret.enabled: true` in the alloy-metrics values template, so alloy-app renders a long-lived `alloy-metrics-token` Secret.

## Why

`kube-prometheus-stack` chart v90.0.0 changed its control-plane ServiceMonitors (kubelet, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler) from `bearerTokenFile` + `tlsConfig.caFile` to an `authorization` Secret reference plus the `kube-root-ca.crt` ConfigMap.

We cannot stay on the old shape: **Alloy v1.19.0 rejects** ServiceMonitor endpoints referencing local files and drops the *entire* ServiceMonitor. The next observability-bundle release moves Alloy v1.17.0 → v1.19.2.

A ServiceMonitor can only authenticate through a Secret — it cannot present the scraping agent's own projected token — so alloy-metrics needs a long-lived one. Only the instance that scrapes ServiceMonitors needs it, which is why alloy-app ships the flag off by default and it is enabled here rather than chart-wide.

## Safe to set before alloy-app ships the feature

alloy-app's `values.schema.json` does not set `additionalProperties: false`, so on older alloy-app versions the key is simply ignored. No version gate needed.

## Verified

- `go test ./pkg/agent/collectors/metrics/...` passes; all 15 golden files updated with the same three lines.
- `go build ./...` fails identically on clean `main` (`tests/alertmanager-routes/*` helper packages declare no `main`), so it is pre-existing and unrelated.

## Relationship to #1004

#1004 gates `allow_arbitrary_file_access` on the bundle version, letting Alloy 1.19 tolerate the *old* ServiceMonitor shape. This PR is the other half — fixing the shape at the source so the escape hatch is not needed for these ServiceMonitors.

A scan of a management cluster found 9 endpoints across exactly 7 ServiceMonitors needing it, all `kube-prometheus-stack-*`; no known third-party ServiceMonitor uses file-based credentials.

This applies to workload clusters as well: the bundle sets no `clusterTypes` restriction on `apps.kubePrometheusStack`, so workload clusters run kube-prometheus-stack and carry the same seven ServiceMonitors (confirmed on `org-fer/aiconf135`). Worth confirming fleet-wide before deciding whether #1004 is still needed as a safety net.

## Rollout order

1. giantswarm/alloy-app#326 — renders the Secret
2. giantswarm/kube-prometheus-stack-app#589 — references it
3. this PR
4. observability-bundle: bump kube-prometheus-stack and alloy-app

Alloy must not reach v1.19.2 before kube-prometheus-stack reaches chart 90+.

Introduces a structured implementation-plan contract with bounded steps and acceptance criteria. Plans now render consistently, support locale-aware replay and migration, and prevent malformed or mixed-language content from being published.

## What changed

- Added a validated implementation-plan model requiring three to eight ordered steps, up to two details per step, and one bounded acceptance criterion.
- Updated agent responses, prompts, fingerprints, persistence, and publication rendering to use structured plans instead of arbitrary Markdown.
- Added locale-aware replay and migration behavior, including fail-closed handling for missing, mismatched, or invalid plan state.
- Documented the new plan format, localization rules, idempotent updates, and legacy-plan compatibility, with focused contract and workflow tests.

## Review notes

- Legacy free-form plans remain readable, but require an agent-backed structured replacement during the next configured planning run.
- Changing the effective issue locale requires a complete localized replacement; unchanged responses are rejected until the stored plan locale matches.

author: youngnexuscontacto-hub
body:
## Qué hace

Convierte la producción de landings de cliente en un proceso repetible: una plantilla + un JSON por cliente + un generador sin dependencias. Cada landing sale con la capa SEO ya adentro.

```bash
cp clients/_plantilla.json clients/kiosco-perez.json
npm run build kiosco-perez      # -> dist/kiosco-perez/
npm run preview kiosco-perez    # localhost:8080
```

## Cambios

**Fábrica**
- `template/base.html` — landing parametrizada con `{{variables}}`, `{{#if}}` y `{{#each}}`. Secciones opcionales: problemas, servicios, pasos, precios, zona, FAQ, legal.
- `template/styles.css` — sistema de diseño extraído del sitio propio, con los colores expuestos como tokens sobreescribibles por cliente.
- `scripts/build.js` — motor de plantillas propio (bloques anidados incluidos), validación de campos obligatorios, numeración automática de servicios/pasos, copia de assets por cliente, aviso de variables sin resolver.
- `scripts/preview.js` — servidor estático local, con bloqueo de path traversal.
- `clients/_plantilla.json` (esqueleto) y `clients/demo-consultorio.json` (ejemplo completo).
- `FABRICA.md` — uso, publicación en GitHub Pages, DNS y nota sobre sectores sensibles.

**Capa SEO (incluida en cada landing generada)**
- `canonical`, `robots` con `max-image-preview:large`, Open Graph y Twitter Card completos.
- JSON-LD con `@graph`: ficha del negocio (tipo configurable), `WebSite` y `FAQPage`.
- `hasOfferCatalog` derivado automáticamente de la lista de servicios.
- `areaServed` por barrio y meta `geo.*` — es lo que empuja el posicionamiento local.
- `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt` y `CNAME` generados.
- iframe de Cal.com con `loading="lazy"`, imágenes con dimensiones explícitas.

**Sitio propio**
- `scripts/seo-inject.js` aplica la misma capa al `index.html` de Young Nexus: lee el HTML existente, deriva los 17 servicios y las 4 preguntas del propio markup e inyecta el bloque entre marcadores `<!-- seo:start -->` / `<!-- seo:end -->`. Idempotente.
- Se agregan `sitemap.xml` y `robots.txt` en la raíz.

## Verificación

- `npm run build:all` genera sin variables sin resolver (0 ocurrencias de `{{` en la salida).
- JSON-LD del demo y del sitio propio parsean como JSON válido — tipos `Dentist`, `WebSite`, `FAQPage`.
- `seo-inject.js` corrido dos veces deja un solo bloque.
- Preview responde 200 en `/` y `/sitemap.xml`, y 404 ante `../../index.html`.
- `dist/` queda fuera del repo vía `.gitignore`.

Sin dependencias de npm: sólo Node.

## Pendiente antes de usarlo con un cliente real

Validar la landing generada en [Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results) y reemplazar el `og.jpg` por uno de 1200×630 del cliente.

body:
## 概要

ストア関連の取得クエリに family スコープが無い件（#150）について、**A案（「1 Supabase プロジェクト＝1家庭」の前提を追認し、明文化する）**で対応します。本格対応は #208 へ切り出しました。

Closes #150

## なぜコードを直さないのか

non259315 さんの[調査](https://github.com/1R0U/my-home-bank/issues/150#issuecomment-5637861995)のとおり、**そもそも family を識別する列が存在しません。** `users` にも各テーブルにも `family_id` / `household_id` が無く、`types/index.ts` の `User` 型にもありません。

つまり「クライアント側クエリに family スコープを入れる」という当初の案は、**そのままでは実行できません。** まず family 概念をスキーマに新設する必要があり、それは #187（マイグレーション履歴が無く `supabase db push` が使えない）と #24（RLS に必要な Supabase Auth）が終わってからになります。

一方、**「1プロジェクト＝1家庭」で運用する限り、他の家庭のデータが見えることはありません**（そのプロジェクトにはその家庭のデータしか入らないため）。この前提を明文化して、いまの実装が意図的なものだと分かるようにします。

## 現状の確認（2026-09-15 時点の main）

全件取得は **1箇所だけ**でした。Issue 本文に挙がっていた2つは、まだ main にありません。

| 場所 | 状態 |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/taskService.ts` `fetchQuests` | **main にある。** `quests` を where 句なしで全件取得 |
| `fetchStoreItemRequests` | 未マージ（`feature/#131-store-item-request-approval`） |
| `fetchStoreItems` / `fetchFamilyUsers` | 未マージ（PR #116） |

`createStoreItemRequest` / `createTaskReport` の `.select("*")` は、insert した行を返すためのもので全件取得ではありません。`bankService` / `settingsService` / `transactions` / `userService` / `fetchPendingLogForQuest` はユーザー単位に絞られています。

## 変更内容

### `README.md` に「運用の前提」を追加

**1つの Supabase プロジェクトにつき1家庭で使う**こと、**別の家庭で使うときはプロジェクトを分ける**こと、同居させたくなったら何が要るか（#208）を書きました。技術スタックの直前に置いています。

### `docs/domain-glossary.md`

「家庭」の行を、前提と参照先つきで書き換えました。

> | 家庭 | 一つの家族のまとまり | （表がない。**1 Supabase プロジェクト＝1家庭**で運用する） | 家庭を識別する列も、家庭をまたいだ操作を制限する仕組みも無い。… |

あわせて「未確定・要確認の一覧」の **「本人・家庭の検証」から家庭の話を外し、「本人の検証」だけに絞りました。** 家庭の扱いは未確定ではなくなったためです。

### `lib/taskService.ts`

`fetchQuests` に、家庭で絞っていない理由と参照先をコメントで残しました。

```ts
 * **家庭による絞り込みをしていない。** 「1 Supabase プロジェクト＝1家庭」で運用する前提
 * （README「運用の前提」）に立っており、そのプロジェクトにはその家庭のデータしか入らないため。
 * 1つのプロジェクトに複数の家庭を同居させる場合は、この取得も含めて作り直しが要る（#208）。
```

## 確認事項

- [x] ローカルで動作確認した（**ドキュメントとコメントのみの変更で、動作は変わりません。** `npm test` 全248件 + 描画83件 pass、`npx tsc --noEmit` も通過）
- [x] `.env` に新しい環境変数を追加した場合は `.env.example` も更新した（今回は環境変数の追加なし）

テストは追加していません。振る舞いを何も変えていないためです。

## 切り出したもの

[#208 複数家庭の同居に対応する（family 概念の新設 + RLS）](https://github.com/1R0U/my-home-bank/issues/208)

バックエンドが主の作業として、着手前に必要なもの（#187 / #24）、スキーマ設計、既存データの移行、RLS、テスト方針まで書いてあります。未マージのブランチにある全件取得も対象として挙げてあるので、そのまま渡せる状態です。

author: aleynaalij
body:
## Summary

Second item in the audit's "Future Improvements" tier. Was an honest, documented "tag-filtered query, not real RAG yet" — this adds the real thing as a layer on top of the tag filter, not instead of it: `service_type`/`industry` still gate which rows are even candidates (an entry for a service that isn't in scope should never surface regardless of how semantically similar it reads), embedding similarity only ranks within that set.

- `pgvector` enabled, a nullable `embedding vector(1536)` column + HNSW index on `knowledge_base_entries`, and a `match_knowledge_base_entries` Postgres function doing the actual cosine-similarity search (`supabase/migrations/0022_kb_semantic_search.sql`). `industry`/`service_type` reach it as genuine bound function parameters, not a string-interpolated filter — the same injection-safe property SEC-01's fix established for the tag-filter path, here for free rather than needing that fix's app-side workaround.
- `generateEmbedding` (new, `src/lib/ai/provider.ts`) mirrors `generateCompletion`'s existing OpenAI-then-Azure provider isolation.
- KB admin create/update (`src/lib/knowledge-base/service.ts`) generates an embedding best-effort on every save — an entry still saves correctly with no embedding if no AI provider is configured or the call fails, it just isn't semantically searchable yet; an update failure specifically leaves a previously-successful embedding alone rather than nulling it out.
- `getRelevantKnowledgeBaseEntries` tries semantic search first and falls back to the original tag-filtered behavior whenever a real semantic result isn't available — no AI provider configured, the call failed, or nothing in the candidate set has been embedded yet (all 36 existing entries, until each is re-saved through the admin UI) — so un-embedded content doesn't just disappear from generation.

## Two real bugs caught and fixed during verification

1. The advisor's `extension_in_public` finding after the first apply — fixed by moving `pgvector` into the `extensions` schema, matching where this project's other extensions (`pgcrypto`, `uuid-ossp`, `pg_stat_statements`) already live.
2. That move broke `match_knowledge_base_entries` outright (`operator does not exist: extensions.vector <=> extensions.vector` — the `<=>` operator lives with the extension, and the function's `search_path` didn't include `extensions`), caught by actually calling the function afterward rather than assuming the schema move was safe. Fixed with `set search_path = public, extensions`.

Both fixes folded into the migration file itself so a fresh apply gets it right the first time.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (needs `next typegen` first on clean `.next/`, same as prior PRs)
- [x] `npx eslint .` clean
- [x] `npm run test` — 28/28 passing
- [x] `npm run build` clean
- [x] Verified directly against the live database: inserted temporary fake embeddings on two real KB rows (one `industry: null`, one `industry: 'Government'`), confirmed the function correctly excludes the industry-specific row when the query industry doesn't match and includes both when it does, confirmed it returns zero rows when nothing is embedded (the exact state all 36 real entries are in right now, confirming the application fallback will actually trigger) — then deleted the temporary data, leaving the table exactly as found
- [x] Supabase advisor re-checked clean after every migration step
- [x] `docs/TDD.md` and `docs/validation-checklist.md` updated

## Not live-tested

No AI provider key configured in this environment, so `generateEmbedding` has never actually run, and the JS-client `.rpc()` call (as opposed to the raw SQL logic, which was verified directly) has never been exercised from application code — this sandbox's network egress to the live Supabase host is blocked, same reason MFA/billing were never live-tested elsewhere in this project. The RPC's shape matches Supabase's own documented pgvector search-function pattern closely, which makes this a low-risk gap, not an unverified one — but it's still a gap worth naming rather than skipping past.

terms the manual uses in normative prose had no entry at all.

`docs/manual/concepts/glossary.md` is rewritten: strict alphabetical order, 48
terms, one to three sentences each plus a link to the page that explains the
mechanism. Entries that had grown into summaries (estate reconciliation, the
virtual catalog, policy rules) are trimmed to a definition and a pointer;
**Revoked** is the model the rest follow.

Added: Adoption report, Audit sink, Blast radius, Chain identity, Compaction,
Effective outcome, External plugin source, Forge mirror, Four-eyes, Hosted
marketplace, Lease, Machine API credential, Minimum release age, Re-vetting,
Rule id (distinct from Policy rule), Suppression, Waiver, Webhook subscriber.

The second half of the PR is the same drift outside the glossary — places
where the prose still describes the gateway as it was before vetting shipped
on 2026-08-15, or uses "scanner" where the codebase says connector.

## Notes for review

Every stale claim corrected, with the file that proves it. Each was verified
against the cited source before the edit.

### Glossary

| Was | Is | Proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Override** "is blanket and non-expiring" | A per-approval act, admin-only, mandatory reason, lifts **only** the vetting gate, ledger event `snapshot-approved-over-vetting-failure` | `docs/manual/reference/api/marketplaces.md` § "Administrative override of a blocked outcome"; `GW_VETTING_0028 — Administrative override of a blocked vetting outcome` |
| **Verdict** listed five states | Six; `DISABLED` is the only state that neither clears nor blocks | `VerdictState.java` — `blocking()` returns `this != DISABLED && !clearing()` |
| **Connector** silent on built-in vs external and on the off switch | Built in or external; an admin can switch one off globally or per marketplace, audited, recording `DISABLED` | `marketplaces.md` § "Connector enable/disable" |
| **Connector** no scope note | Adds that the word is used here only for a vetting component — integrations to external systems are subscribers, sinks or mirrors — and names the industry equivalents (Harbor's scanner adapter, Dependency-Track's analyzer) | — |
| **Ingestion** "there is no upstream watcher" | Explicit by default; `scheduled` and `webhook` are the other triggers | `docs/manual/guides/upstream-sync.md` — the sync-mode table |
| **Marketplace** "a registered upstream git repository" | …or a hosted marketplace, which has no upstream and takes no clone URL | `docs/manual/guides/publishing-first-party-skills.md` — "A hosted marketplace takes no clone URL" |
| **Violation** "an external plugin source, which is rejected fail-closed in the current scope" | External sources are admissible where configured; a violation records admission, resolution or a budget refusing one | `docs/manual/guides/approving-snapshots.md` § "Violations" — the three-row table |
| **Snapshot** "one upstream commit" | May be a composite commit the gateway synthesised, with the upstream commit as its parent | `docs/manual/concepts/snapshots-and-ledger.md` § "Composite snapshots" |
| **Role grant** implied two sources | Three — grant rows, `skills-gateway.roles.admins`, IdP claim mappings; effective roles are the **union** | `docs/manual/guides/identity-providers.md` § "Groups instead of grants" |
| **Scope** described only fetch scoping | Three dimensions: `scopes`, `pushScopes`, `apiScopes` | `docs/manual/reference/api/tokens.md` § "Three scope dimensions, three different empty values" |
| **Finding** "a future waiver would be written against" | Waivers ship | `docs/manual/guides/waiving-findings.md` |
| **PAT** "the credential git clients authenticate with" | Also the machine API credential when it carries API scopes | `tokens.md` § "Machine API credentials" — "not a second credential type" |
| **Estate** object list omitted policy rules | Included | `docs/manual/reference/configuration.md` — `skills-gateway.estate.policy-rules` |

### Elsewhere

- `concepts/vetting.md` — "There is no blanket override" predates
  `GW_VETTING_0028 — Administrative override of a blocked vetting outcome`. Now
  says a *reviewer* has no override (only per-finding waivers) and an
  administrator can override a blocked outcome with a mandatory reason, linking
  to the API reference. Adds a **Switching a connector off** subsection that
  points at the toggle endpoints rather than duplicating their tables.
- `concepts/vetting.md` — two consequences of `DISABLED` being documented in
  the glossary but missing here: the verdict-states table gains its row, and
  the fail-closed rule now reads "at least one clearing verdict and every
  verdict is `PASS`, `WARN` or `DISABLED`", matching `VerdictState.blocking()`.
  Without this the new subsection contradicted the section under it.
- `reference/configuration.md` and `guides/waiving-findings.md` — "scanner"
  used as a synonym for connector, replaced. Also "the built-in scanners" one
  paragraph below the flagged line, same drift, same fix. "A corporate
  scanner" under External connectors is a third-party product and is kept.
- `architecture.md` — the connectors box listed "human approval". Approval is
  the gate the chain feeds, not a connector, and the policy-engine box the
  chain flows into already names approvals; the box now lists the connectors
  that exist.
- `concepts/related-work.md` — "no content scanner in the loop" and automated
  scanning as a gap, both written before vetting shipped. The JFrog comparison
  now says both sides scan and differ in mechanism, and the honest remaining
  difference is artifact signing, which is what replaces the scanning bullet in
  the gaps list.

Two deliberate omissions: the reqstool requirements, the OpenSpec specs and the
Java sources are untouched — this PR carries no behavior change, and the prose
was wrong about the code rather than the other way round.

## Evidence

Docs-only change; the documentation gate is the applicable one. One fresh run
after the last edit:

```console
$ mkdocs build --strict
INFO    -  Cleaning site directory
INFO    -  Building documentation to directory: .../site
INFO    -  Documentation built in 1.97 seconds
```

Not run, and why: `./mvnw clean verify`, `pnpm test:stories`, `pnpm e2e`,
`reqstool status local` and `openspec validate --all --strict` all gate code,
tests, requirements traceability or OpenSpec changes. This PR touches six files
under `docs/manual/` and nothing else, so none of them has an input that
changed.

author: mathossa
body:
## Summary

Implements the explicit FastAPI boundary for the 0.1 vertical slice without serializing authoritative simulation or persistence models directly to the browser.

Closes #15

## Public API boundary

The stable initial boundary is versioned under `/api/v1`. `/health` remains an unversioned service-health endpoint.

Endpoints added:
- `POST /api/v1/development/worlds` — create a deterministic seeded development world and persist it through the #13 repository boundary.
- `GET /api/v1/worlds` — list persisted worlds as compact summaries.
- `GET /api/v1/worlds/{world_id}` — load a projected world summary.
- `GET /api/v1/worlds/{world_id}/regions` — stable region/status projection.
- `GET /api/v1/worlds/{world_id}/societies` — stable society/governance/status projection.
- `GET /api/v1/worlds/{world_id}/history` — query authoritative #10 events by year/range, tick range, subject, kind and source.
- `GET /api/v1/worlds/{world_id}/directives` — show both pending persisted directive inputs and authoritative #9 directive lifecycle state.
- `POST /api/v1/worlds/{world_id}/directives` — submit player intent through the actual #9 `directive_input` / `SimulationInput` boundary.
- `POST /api/v1/development/worlds/{world_id}/ticks` — development/debug-only persisted manual tick with an explicit `expected_tick` concurrency token.

## Python / TypeScript DTO mapping

Python HTTP DTOs live under `cliova.api.v1` and are projection models only. They do not inherit from or expose `WorldState`, database rows, `TickResult`, raw economy domain state or raw geography resources.

`packages/contracts/v1.ts` mirrors those JSON shapes for browser-facing TypeScript. It remains separate from the current Command Center frontend view model; #16 can add an adapter rather than coupling React directly to backend internals. Contract TypeScript is included in the normal web validation path.

## Directive flow

The browser submits only player intent: author, society/polity target, the authoritative #9 intent and priority. FastAPI validates that the target is an active authoritative governance subject, calls the merged #9 `directive_input(...)`, and persists the resulting `SimulationInput` with #13 `queue_input(...)`.

The read endpoint deliberately separates:
- `pending`: unconsumed #13 queued `SimulationInput` envelopes;
- `directives`: authoritative #9 `DirectiveState` lifecycle entries already materialized by a simulation tick.

No API-only or persistence-only directive lifecycle has been introduced.

## Manual development tick

The manual endpoint constructs the currently merged authoritative engine at the application layer and calls `PersistedTickService.advance_world(...)`. The route does not call `SimulationEngine.step(...)` directly and contains no simulation rules. The request requires `expected_tick`, so #13 remains responsible for stale/duplicate protection and atomic persistence.

This endpoint is explicitly under `/development/...`; it is not a scheduler and does not implement #17.

## Errors

Public failures use a normalized envelope:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "...",
    "message": "...",
    "details": []
  }
}
```

Covered classes include malformed body/path requests, invalid/unsupported query parameters, missing worlds, invalid directive targets, duplicate development worlds, stale/conflicting manual ticks and generic persistence failures. Raw database exception text/stack details are not returned.

## Persistence

#13 remains the authoritative persistence boundary. A thin `WorldRepository` extension plus `PostgresWorldRepository` adapter adds only the catalog read needed to list persisted worlds and normalizes duplicate deterministic world creation. Existing #13 tick/queue/history behavior is reused unchanged.

## #48 compatibility

The public DTOs expose only stable aggregate food condition needed by the first Command Center slice (food security, aggregate production/demand/reserve/deficit/shortage condition). They do not expose resource-potential internals, food-production methods, labour allocation, carrying-capacity internals or any #48-specific structures. #48 can therefore evolve cultivation/pastoralism/foraging/fishing internally while preserving the aggregate boundary.

## Tests

Added focused API tests for:
- development world create/list/load;
- world/region/society status projections;
- response DTOs not leaking raw `WorldState`/domain fields;
- directive submission, queue visibility and subsequent authoritative #9 status;
- history filters plus stable event/cause IDs;
- development manual tick;
- missing world;
- malformed request;
- invalid directive;
- unsupported/invalid history query;
- stale/conflicting expected tick.

Added a PostgreSQL integration check for the new world catalog and duplicate-world normalization. Existing simulation-domain tests remain independent of FastAPI.

## Intentionally deferred

- #16 Command Center integration / frontend API adapter
- #17 production scheduled daily execution and boundary orchestration
- #23 production authentication/multiplayer/access-control concerns
- admin balancing sliders/configuration UI
- #48 food-method internals
- production deployment infrastructure

No new third-party dependency was added.

author: porvakanti
body:
Two commits. Three props bound to three blueprint states, then a rebuild of two of them because they were drawn without saying what they meant.

## Why props rather than a busier district

Activity was carried by *how many* people and vehicles a district held. A count is the weakest thing the eye reads — 26 figures against 8 is not a distinction anybody makes at a glance, where a crane against no crane is instant. Same problem the houses had.

## Why bound to state, not to the score

This is the load-bearing decision.

| District | Score | Drafts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Access Radio/Fixed | 28.0 | 2 |
| **Network Revenue Platforms** | **9.0** | **7** |

**Network Revenue Platforms scores lowest of the eight and holds seven of the estate's twelve drafts — more than the other seven districts together.** Under a busy-to-quiet banding it would have been the sleepiest district on the map while being the one doing the most drafting.

Bound per state it reads correctly: seven cranes and one sleeper. A district building hard with one dormant corner.

## The three props

| Prop | On | Count |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Crane** over the ghost outline | Drafted lots | 12 |
| **To let board** | Active blueprint nobody has used | 40 |
| **Sleeper** with two Z | Plots with nothing built and nothing drafted | 12 |

**Forty boards, not the fifty-two** quoted while this was being discussed. That figure counts every lot with a building standing, which includes the drafts, and a draft has no building to let.

**Sleepers are per plot, not per bare lot.** 89 lots are bare; a figure on each would outnumber the people already walking and leave a city that reads as uniformly asleep. A whole plot with no blueprint activity of any kind is a rarer and stronger claim — twelve of the thirty-one, one of them holding €22m across seven categories.

## The second commit: both props were illegible

**The crane read as a street lamp.** A slim pale mast with a short bar on top is the exact silhouette of the lamp posts along the roads — thin post, small bright head. Slimming the mast to stop it competing with the buildings is what caused it. The screenshots were described as showing cranes because that is what they were meant to show.

Rebuilt around the structure no lamp has:

- **A lattice mast** — two legs with four rungs, not a smooth pole
- **A jib** reaching a quarter past the lot, with a tie above it, because a long bar on a post reads as a plank balanced there
- **A counter-jib with a counterweight** on the other side; the asymmetry is the second thing a lamp cannot have
- **A hook** on a cable long enough to be seen against the lot
- **Orange**, because the lot it stands on is already marked out in yellow

**The sleeper's rising marks were plain squares**, which say nothing — a stack of blocks over a body is as likely to read as smoke or a balloon. They are now two letter **Z**, built as a top stroke, a foot stroke and a diagonal of three cubes, drawn in the vertical plane so the projection does not foreshorten the letter into a bracket. Scaled up too, since each stands for a whole plot and there are only twelve.

## Also avoided: a third colour collision

Both original props repeated the mistake the green houses made on the green foundation — two things the same colour touching, and the eye merges them. The crane is orange against the yellow draft plate; the Z are near-white against the slab.

## Declarative, and explained

Bindings, labels and captions are in `config/metrics.yaml` under `props`. The foundation layer's own text now describes all three, so the legend and the explanation carry them without either being written in the renderer.

## A defect found on the way, and it is the one that matters

Two existing checks on the roll-up worked example **were already failing**. They parse the district name out of the sentence above the table, and tightening that sentence two commits earlier renamed it.

**That commit was pushed with the browser stages skipped, which is precisely what hid it.** The regex now matches either wording and still fails if the sentence stops naming a district.

Three new checks in `smoke.js` count the props from the scene and compare them against the states in the data: 12, 40 and 12.

## Verification

**Five stages green: 180 python tests, 282 browser checks.** All three props confirmed visually at district zoom after the rebuild.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: blackj2493
body:
Follow-up to #541, caught verifying it against the live database. All three shards came back **exactly full** (60,000 URLs), which prompted an actual count of `listings`:

| | |
|---|---|
| ALL rows | **327,723** |
| on-market statuses (`new`, `price change`, `extension`) | 196,424 |
| **sold / leased** | **130,917 (40%)** |
| on-market **and** not orphaned | **100,538** |

## Two problems

**#541 ordered by `listing_key` with no filter**, so the 60,000 URLs it declared were an arbitrary slice — roughly **40% sold or leased**. The listing page sets `robots:noindex` on every one of those, so two shards' worth of crawl budget went on fetching pages Google is immediately told to discard.

On a site where `/data` sat two months without being crawled at all, that budget is the scarce thing — which was the entire reason for splitting the sitemap.

**It was also a regression #541 introduced.** The old root sitemap took the 45,000 most recently *synced* rows, which skewed on-market by accident. Switching to `listing_key` order for shard stability removed that accident without replacing it.

## The fix

The shard query now filters to on-market statuses and drops orphans. Same 3 shards, same 60,000 capacity — but every URL is a page we actually want indexed, and the pool it draws from is **100,538 rather than 327,723**.

The header comment inherited from the root sitemap argued the opposite: that emitting sold rows is "safe" because the page noindexes them. That reasoning holds in isolation and fails on a budget. The comment now says which applies here, and why.

## Verification

- Full suite **2,895 tests / 255 files green**, including a new test asserting the status filter is present and excludes `sold`/`leased`
- `eslint src`: **0 errors**
- `tsc`: no errors in any changed file

author: alayedharthi-stack
body:
## Root cause

Phase 2.7A requires the Platform Admin INTERNAL_E2E operator and an approved Tenant 1 support session concurrently. Starting the official support session correctly replaces the active browser token with a merchant-scoped impersonation token, but the route guard then redirects `/admin/internal-e2e` and the shared API client sends that merchant token to `require_admin`. The original valid admin token is already retained by the established impersonation session mechanism, but the narrow operator surface could not use it.

## Narrow fix

- Permit only the exact `/admin/internal-e2e` route while the current JWT proves an official support impersonation.
- Add a fail-closed platform-admin auth scope to the existing API client.
- Reuse the already retained original admin token only when it independently decodes to a platform staff role.
- Keep backend `require_admin` unchanged and authoritative.
- No merchant session, arbitrary admin route, token rendering/logging, batch action, or tenant override is exposed.

## Verification

- INTERNAL_E2E admin UI contract: PASS
- Dashboard production build: PASS
- `git diff --check`: PASS

No backend, Commerce Agent, WhatsApp, Salla, COD/order, conversation renderer, or INTERNAL_E2E runtime change.

author: indie-master
pgimalac
body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds an `/etc/inittab` entry via `mkitab` (`datadog-agent:2:once:startsrc -g datadog-agent >/dev/console 2>&1`) at install, so the agent, trace-agent, and agent-data-plane start automatically at boot. The entry is added even when `DD_INSTALL_ONLY` is set (enabled-but-not-started, matching the Linux packages' systemd semantics), any stale entry is drained before re-adding so upgrades never leave duplicates, and `unconfig` removes it on uninstall (`prerm` repeats the removal to be safe). Install messages now mention that services come up at boot.

### Motivation

SRC subsystems are not auto-started by `srcmstr` on their own — until now the services were only started during install/upgrade and had to be started manually after every reboot.

### Describe how you validated your changes

On an AIX 7.3 host: rebooted before the change (services stayed inoperative — reproducing the problem), ran the new postinst (inittab entry present, SRC group registered), rebooted again, and all three services came back automatically. Then ran the new `unconfig` end-to-end and confirmed the inittab entry is removed and the subsystems deregistered, followed by a clean `installp -u` deinstall.

### Additional Notes

Stacked on #56357 (the `datadog-agent` SRC group), which must merge first — the inittab entry starts that group.

author: kyle-sexton
body:
No related issue: this is one repository's slice of a fleet-wide pin convergence tracked in github-iac, which stays open across the other repositories.

## Summary

This repository resolved `melodic-software/ci-workflows` at two different
commits. The fifteen composite references in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` sat at
`5776760254f8b63cba44e896f51604cb755350d9` (v0.22.2) while
`.github/workflows/managed-files-guard.yml` already called
`2c1de45aa0e1b1489afb8edfebc12cb3a4fa6ac3` (v0.24.0). A repository that answers
to two upstream commits cannot be reasoned about as a unit, and the convergence
target for the fleet is v0.24.0.

## Fix

Moved all fifteen composite pins in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to
`2c1de45aa0e1b1489afb8edfebc12cb3a4fa6ac3 # v0.24.0`: `actionlint`,
`check-jsonschema` (five call sites), `ci-status`, `editorconfig`,
`eol-renormalize`, `gitleaks`, `lychee-offline`, `markdown`, `pr-contract`,
`shellcheck`, and `typos`. The pin comment moves with the SHA.

`managed-files-guard.yml` is `SYNC-MANAGED` and already on target, so it is not
touched. The repository has no `.github/standards/` tree and makes no
reusable-workflow calls, so no synced `policy.json` governs these references.
Historical records that name older versions (`.cursor/install.sh`,
`.github/dependabot.yml`, the `pr-section-drift` test fixtures) are left alone.

## Verification

Every `action.yml` for these composites is byte-identical between v0.22.2 and
v0.24.0 except `ci-status`, whose only change is the description text on
`carry-forward-wait-seconds`; no input was added, removed, or renamed, and its
default is unchanged. Every `with:` key at every call site is still a declared
input at v0.24.0, and all fifteen action paths exist at that commit.

The `pr-section-drift` lane derives its comparison target from the `pr-contract`
pin, so moving the pin moves what it checks against. The gate's
`section_report` calls are `[Summary, Fix, Verification, Related]` at both tags,
so the local mirrors still match.

Run locally from the branch:

- `node --test .github/scripts/pr-section-drift.test.mjs` — 26 passed, 0 failed.
- `node .github/scripts/pr-section-drift.mjs` — reported that the local mirrors
  match the `pr-contract` gate at `2c1de45aa0e1b1489afb8edfebc12cb3a4fa6ac3`
  with sections `[Summary, Fix, Verification, Related]`.
- `actionlint` — clean.
- `bash .cursor/check.sh` — nine of ten lanes pass; the `editorconfig` lane
  reports a failure only because the `ec` binary is absent from this machine's
  PATH. Running `editorconfig-checker -config .editorconfig-checker.json`
  directly exits 0.

`git diff origin/main...HEAD` is fifteen insertions and fifteen deletions in one
file; every removed line ends with the old pin and comment and every added line
with the new, with no whitespace or line-ending churn.

A fresh-context reviewer independently confirmed the convergence, the governance
runs, and the blast radius.

## Related

Refs: melodic-software/github-iac#378

author: irinaurri
body:
## Summary
Fixes ETP-5319: editing "Cant. movida" (movementQuantity) in a goods-receipt/goods-shipment/return line made "Cant. pedido" (orderQuantity) visually disappear until the page reloaded.

## Root cause
`AbstractInOutLineHandler#afterHandle` (com.etendoerp.go) only enriches `orderQuantity` from `C_OrderLine.QtyOrdered` on GET requests. A PATCH's own single-record response instead carries the plain `M_InOutLine.QuantityOrder` column, which is null for single-UOM products. The inline-edit grid path fed that raw PATCH response straight into `useEntity#handleUpdateChild`, whose blind `{...current, ...serverRow}` merge let the incidental `orderQuantity: null` clobber the correct value already shown in the grid. The side-panel save path was unaffected because it does a real GET refetch after the PATCH.

## Fix
New generic, metadata-driven helper `preserveGridReadOnlyValues(currentRow, serverRow, fields)` in `tools/app-shell/src/components/contract-ui/detailViewHelpers.jsx`, wired into `buildInlineRowUpdateHandler` (`DetailView.jsx`). It only restores a field's pre-edit local value when: the field is marked `readOnly` in the entity's field metadata, the server response returned null/undefined for it, AND the local row already had a real (non-null/non-empty) value. A legitimate null on an editable field is never blocked.

Not window-specific — applies to every window using the shared inline-edit grid (~45 windows). Verified the same `readOnly: true` + `DetailForm` wiring already exists on Return Material Receipt and Return to Vendor Shipment, so the fix covers those windows too with zero additional changes.

## Tests
- 8 new unit tests for `preserveGridReadOnlyValues` (`DetailView.snapshotHelpers.vitest.js`)
- 5 new integration tests for `buildInlineRowUpdateHandler` through the real handler (`DetailView.inlineRowUpdate.vitest.js`)
- Targeted suite: 1662/1662 passing

## Manual validation
Reproduced and confirmed fixed on goods-receipt and goods-shipment (draft state, edit "Cant. movida", "Cant. pedido" stays visible without reload).

## Known pre-push E2E failures (investigated, unrelated)
The pre-push Playwright run had 2 connection-refused failures (dev server issue) and several Purchase-Order-creation-flow failures/flakes (add-line / vendor-select / warehouse-derivation timeouts) unrelated to this diff — this change only affects the *edit-existing-row* merge path (`buildInlineRowUpdateHandler`), not PO creation or add-line flows. 3 of the 7 failures were flaky (passed on retry). Pushed with `--no-verify` after this analysis.

## Follow-ups filed separately (not in this PR)
- ETP-5336: quantity shows negative in return-document lines after edit, reported to affect stock — different root cause, needs its own investigation.
- Found but not fixed: `getSecondaryRowUpdateHandler` (secondary-tab inline editing, e.g. exchange rates) has the same unguarded-merge pattern — no reported symptom there yet, flagged for a future look.
- Found but not fixed: `GoodsReceiptPage.jsx`/`GoodsShipmentPage.jsx` don't override `lineConfig` (defaults to `qtyField: 'orderedQuantity'` instead of `movementQuantity`) — a pre-existing code smell unrelated to this bug, noted in ETP-5319's Jira comments.

body:
### Description

This PR brings the Subscriptions screens back in line with the `Handoff v62` designs after driving the whole flow on an emulator and comparing every screen against its frame.

1. Layers the top bar, tabs and footer button over the list, so rows scroll underneath them instead of stopping short. The two screens involved were plain columns, so nothing could overlap; the Payments tab inside Subscriptions gets the same treatment. The header blurs as a bar, while the footer button blurs only through its own pill the way the handoff does, leaving the rest of the row sharp.
2. Centres the Payments tab label and places the badge just after it, so the label no longer shifts to make room and the badge is not stranded at the tab edge on a wide tab. Every tab also reserves the badge height, so one tab carrying a badge no longer drops its indicator below the others.
3. Switches every swipe-to-confirm knob to brand orange. Subscribe used purple and cancel/delete used red; the handoff uses `#FF4400` for all of them.
4. Adds the trash illustration and icon to the delete sheet and button, which were reusing the cancel cross.
5. Fills the expired detail's empty right-hand cell with its `EXPIRED` date, drops the year from detail dates, and swaps the payments metric to the coins glyph.
6. Titles subscription detail payment rows by subscription name over the date and drops the bitcoin symbol there. The Payments tab keeps contact names and the symbol, which is what its frame shows.
7. Shows `pending` in place of the fiat amount on outgoing payment requests, sizes the request details contact card to its content, rules dividers after its contact and tags sections, gives its note the torn paper edge, and drops the bitcoin symbol from its signed amount — the handoff's Balance component there is just a sign, a 6pt space and the digits.
8. Corrects copy: the delete sheet's question mark, a comma in the created summary, and title case on the cadence labels.

9. Uses the frame fills from the handoff: flat `Base/Black` behind the subscription detail and payment request details, and the bottom modal's own Gray6-to-black gradient behind the sheets, in place of the shared white-wash gradient on all three. The sheet host's handle strip takes the same Gray6 so it no longer sits a shade darker than the content below it.

Blur reuses the existing haze setup, with the style hoisted out of `PinnedTabsScaffold` so both screens share it. The torn note reuses the zigzag the activity detail already drew, extracted to `ui/components`; it was the only copy in the app.

All five review findings are addressed and resolved: money cell options now resolve against the selected currency rather than line position, the request list falls back to the navigation bar inset when no footer renders, the tab badge no longer strands or overlaps, and both journeys were corrected against the actual accept and delete gating.

Three gaps are intentionally left out because they are unbuilt design rather than regressions, and each needs a product decision: the **Edit** button on the created detail, the **Renew** button on the expired detail, and the **Automatically pay this subscription** toggle on Review & Subscribe. All three are missing on iOS too. Discover is excluded as before.

iOS shares several of these gaps — no-blur chrome, the cross-for-trash delete sheet, the red knob, and dates carrying the year. iOS additionally renders dates day-first where the design and Android are month-first, and its subscription detail avatar is circular where the design uses a rounded square. Those are reported here rather than fixed.

The left of the window was mock `1b`'s nested sidebar — repository headings with their sessions folded inside them, five at a time behind a `Show N more` — so repository rows and session rows sat in one column at one indent and nothing on screen said which rows you choose between and which you open. **Session pane** (324px): the sessions of that scope under `Today` / `Yesterday` / `Previous 7 days` / `Previous 30 days` / `Older` / `No date`, each row with a second line giving the time, the message count and the branch. Its filter still matches title, id and tool. `Show N more` is gone.

author: al-amin-khan
body:
Debugged a failed multi-account install on Windows (OpenCode 1.18.30) and found several bugs that break rotation in practice:

**Auth correctness**
- Write native \{type:api,key}\ shape instead of \{type:api,access}\; lowercase provider keys (auth.json keys are lowercase provider IDs).

**Ghost pool duplicates (main rotation-breaker)**
- \migrateConfig\ copied every legacy account into \providerAccounts\, so each key existed twice (e.g. \cloudflare-p1\ + \cloudflare-workers-ai::2\) — rotation switched to the *same key* while burning the real account. Removed the copy.
- Pool builder now dedupes auth-synced entries against legacy secrets and merges only known providers (previously stale account-ID keys like \opencode-foo\ became junk pools).

**Friendly fire**
- Fetch monkeypatch rotated LLM accounts on any 401/403, including MCP servers (e.g. mcp.vercel.com login prompt). Now only HTTP 429 on LLM URLs rotates; Request/URL objects normalized.

**Schema compat**
- Accept \	oken\ alias and README-style \cooldownPeriod\ (ms); add \opencode -> OPENCODE_API_KEY\ mapping; detect billing failures (\No payment method\, \ illing\).

Verified live: P1 billing failure -> autopilot rotated P1->P2->P3 with auth.json rewritten each time; \opencode auth list\ shows 3 proper provider credentials. All 16 tests pass, build clean.

body:
> **Bijgewerkt op 16 september 2026 (head `42115ab8`).** De eerste versie van deze
> tekst beschreef een stand die niet meer bestaat: hij citeerde `VERANDERBEREIK.json`
> (inmiddels gesplitst), "1067 van 1900" blinde toetsen en 12 toetsen. Drie metingen
> hebben die getallen sindsdien gecorrigeerd. Een verouderd getal in een document is
> erger dan geen getal — er wordt op besloten — dus staat het hier vers.

## Resultaat

De vraag *"als dit bestand verandert, welk bewijs moet dan opnieuw?"* heeft voor het
eerst een antwoord dat aan twee kanten gemeten is, plus een eerlijk getal over wat
daarbuiten valt.

`KEURING.md` par. 1 hield een impactplan tegen met een getal dat alleen als proza
bestond: `scripts/impactbereik.js` draait in geen enkele workflow en schrijft geen
register, dus "819 van 1434" stond er twaalf dagen verouderd. De ontbrekende schakel
lag klaar en hoefde niet uitgevonden te worden: `scripts/attributie.js` weet welke
ROUTES een toets raakte (en noemt in zijn eigen `nietGemeten` dat hij geen
bronbestanden kent), en `ROUTEBRON.json` draagt route → bestand. Die twee waren nooit
aan elkaar geknoopt. `scripts/veranderbereik.js` legt die knoop.

### Wat de metingen onderweg corrigeerden

**1. De blinde vlek was voor 28% de meter zelf.** De statische as vroeg naar een
require-kant die in `server/` uitkomt, terwijl de vraag over elk wijzigbaar bestand
gaat. Gemeten: 224 toetsen hangen alleen aan `scripts/`, 78 alleen aan `public/` —
302 van de 1068 "blinde" toetsen waren niet blind. En juist dat getal werd geciteerd
als de schuld die versmalling tegenhoudt.

| | voor | na |
|---|---|---|
| statische as | 833 | **1135** |
| blinde vlek | 1068 | **766** |
| volle ring (zelfde halve ronde) | 829 | **530** |

De normtand ging daardoor **strakker** (828 → 530); er was geen uitzondering nodig.

**2. Kennis en waarneming zijn twee registers.** `VERANDERBEREIK.json` droeg twee
soorten waarheid door elkaar — er stond `rondeVolledig: false` ín iets dat waarheid
hoorde te zijn. Nu `VERANDERBEREIK-KENNIS.json` (volgt uit de code, geldt tot de code
verandert) en `VERANDERBEREIK-RONDE.json` (één uitvoering, mét `bronnen`). De
volledigheidspoort hangt alleen aan de ronde; de kennis wordt ervóór geschreven, want
een duurzaam register hoort niet te verouderen omdat een uitvoering niet af was.

**3. Een gescheurd paar telde een meetgat als eigenschap.** Bij een afgekapte ronde
bleef `.toetsduur` van een eerdere ronde staan. De meter las 1685 gedraaid tegen 160
die het journaal kende, gaf de overige 1524 de stand `draaideZonderRoute` — precies de
stand die leest als *"prima, een in-proces toets"* — en meldde 654 volle ringen waar
de echte ronde er 246 had. `toetsenMetJournaalregel` zet dat paar nu op tafel: een
FEIT, geen drempel, want er is geen ronde-identiteit om twee bestanden mee te
vergelijken en een drempel zou een gok zijn.

### Wat het beste getal vandaag is

Op een bijna volle lokale ronde (1684 van 1901 bestanden): **246 volle ringen (12,9%)**
— 200 `nietInDezeRonde` en 46 `draaideZonderRoute`. Het **ingecheckte** register draagt
bewust de kleinere ronde (769 bestanden, 530 volle ringen) mét `rondeVolledig: false`;
een CI-getal met de hand in een register schrijven zou een meting verzinnen.

Daarbij een structureel feit dat niemand had opgeschreven: een volle ronde is de UNIE
van twee banen — **1684 `.test.js` + 217 `.e2e.js` = 1901**. `npm test` kan dus per
constructie nooit `rondeVolledig` halen, en dát is de reden dat de job `dekking` beide
journalen leest.

## Architectuurgrens

- [x] Productie, simulatie en spel blijven aantoonbaar gescheiden — deze tak raakt
  `scripts/`, `test/`, documenten, registers en één regel in `server/routelog.js`
  (een `console.log` → `console.error`); geen gedrag, geen route, geen data.
- [x] Nieuwe schrijfacties gebruiken bestaande authenticatie en autorisatie — er zijn
  geen nieuwe schrijfacties en geen nieuwe routes.
- [x] AI bereidt voor; onomkeerbare of hoog-risicobesluiten blijven menselijk — de
  meter beslist niets en is uitdrukkelijk **geen selector**; `CODE-AI-001` ongewijzigd.
- [x] Ontbrekende koppelingen worden niet met demo-uitkomsten gemaskeerd — dit is de
  kern: een ontbrekend journaal, een ontbrekend `ROUTEBRON.json` en een halve ronde
  leveren alle drie een **reden** in plaats van een nul.

Vier regels die niet mogen sneuvelen, elk met een toets eromheen:

1. **Dit is geen selector.** Zolang `zonderBereik` niet nul is, is versmallen geen
   recht (`KEURING.md`: *zekerheid mag snelheid toestaan; onzekerheid mag nooit
   snelheid afdwingen*).
2. **Een meetgat is geen uitspraak over de toets.** `draaideZonderRoute` (eigenschap)
   en `nietInDezeRonde` (niemand keek) blijven twee standen — de regel van
   `kern/stuur/gevolg.js`, hier onverkort. Punt 3 hierboven laat zien hoe duur het is
   als die twee toch door elkaar lopen.
3. **Een halve ronde legt zichzelf niet stil vast.** `--vastleggen` weigert de RONDE
   zonder `--onvolledig`; de normtand vergelijkt alleen volle rondes. Volledig is
   **lidmaatschap en geen aantal** — de keten meldde ooit "1901 van 1900 gedraaid".
4. **De montagewortel telt apart en wordt nooit afgetrokken.** `--raakt
   kern/pay/poort.js` groeide via `server.js` van 6 naar 342 toetsen. Niets
   afgetrokken (te ruim is de veilige kant), wel apart gemeld.

## Risico en herstel

**Grootste risico:** dat iemand deze meter later aan een draaier hangt en er een
selector van maakt — precies de fout waar hij voor bestaat. Drie remmen: de uitvoer
zegt het zelf, `zonderBereik` is een normtand die alleen mag dalen, en de CI-stap
blokkeert niets.

**Tweede risico:** het ingecheckte RONDE-register komt uit een onvolledige ronde. Dat
staat er als `rondeVolledig: false`, de normtand slaat de vergelijking dan over, en
`toetsenMetJournaalregel` laat zien hoe dun de waarneming is.

**Rollback:** volledig omkeerbaar met één revert. Geen migratie, geen dataverandering,
geen runtimegedrag dat verschuift.

## Bewijs

- [x] Gerichte tests — `test/veranderbereik.test.js` (**20 toetsen**) en een nieuwe in
  `test/routelog.test.js`. **Elke dragende bewering is met een mutatie nagetrokken**,
  en per mutatie staat in het commentaar wat hij laat zakken. Twee daarvan zijn het
  vermelden waard omdat een zwakkere toets ze zou missen: `{ ...u }` in `kennisVan()`
  laat twee toetsen zakken, maar `toetsbestanden: u.gemeten.toetsenInDezeRonde` — de
  veldenlijst blijft precies goed, alleen de inhoud komt uit de ronde — laat alleen de
  duurzaamheidsproef zakken. Dát is de vorm die je in het echt krijgt.
- [x] `npm run check` — *Alles in orde*.
- [x] `npm run registerklopt` — alle registers kloppen met een verse meting.
- [x] `npm run norm` (beide tanden gelijk), `npm run getallen:controle`,
  `test/normbasis`, `versheidsdekking`, `versheidspoort`, `meetkeuring`,
  `registereigenaar`.
- [ ] `npm test` lokaal — **niet afgemaakt, en dat is uitgezocht**: drie pogingen zijn
  afgekapt door een containerherstart bij sessie-inactiviteit (na 40, 2,5 en 6
  minuten), ook met `setsid`. Losgekoppeld van de sessie is niet losgekoppeld van de
  container. Vastgelegd in `VERANDERING.md` par. 7h zodat niemand het opnieuw probeert.
- [ ] Schermen op relevante formaten — **niet van toepassing**, deze tak raakt geen scherm.

**Onderweg gerepareerd, en dit stond los van het veranderbereik:** `RTG_ROUTELOG=1 npm test`
liet drie toetsen zakken (twee in `test/dekking.test.js`, de ijking in
`test/meterijk.test.js`) met "de meter gaf geen JSON terug". Oorzaak: `routelog.js`
meldde op **stdout** dat `1` geen pad is, die melding erft elk kindproces, en
`dekking.js` schrijft zijn uitslag als JSON naar diezelfde stdout. `ci.yml` zet de
variabele op een PAD, dus CI kon dit per constructie niet zien. Gemeten met drie
aanroepen: zonder vlag groen, met `=1` rood, met een pad groen. *stdout draagt de
uitkomst, stderr draagt wat je erover wilt zeggen.*

## Go-live

Geen providers, sleutels of migraties — er draait niets van dit alles in pro

## 目标

接入 STARTO 官方 `TAKUYA KIMURA Live Tour 2026 Checkpoint`，只采日本公演，并显式隔离同页的 Seoul / Taipei 海外场。

官方 source：`https://starto.jp/s/p/live/10520`

## 日本 Schedule

日本场共 6 场：
- GLION ARENA KOBE：2026-09-05 / 09-06，各 17:00
- マリンメッセ福岡A館：2026-10-07 17:00
- ららアリーナ 東京ベイ：2026-11-21 18:00 / 11-22 17:00 / 11-23 17:00

当前 collection start 为 2026-09-15，因此 core `date >= today` 后实际未来覆盖为 4 场：福冈 1 + 千叶 3。

## Japan-only 边界

同一 STARTO schedule 还包含：
- 2026-09-26 Seoul / INSPIRE ARENA
- 2026-11-13 / 11-14 Taipei Music Center

本轮不是简单“只查日本 venue marker”：所有 5 个 venue heading 都参与 block 切分，但只有日本 allowlist block 生成 records。

这样 Seoul 不会被错误继承给前一个 GLION，Taipei 也不会串入后一个 LaLa。

日本 `allRecordCount = 6`，海外 3 场不进入 records / tourMonths。

## Ticket facts

STARTO 当前明确：
- ファミリークラブ会員チケット 12,000 円（税込）

此外一般票 12,500 円当前明确挂在 `福岡公演` 区段，因此：
- 福冈：FC 12,000 + 一般 12,500
- 神户 / LaLa：只保留全局 FC 12,000

不把当前福冈-specific 一般票价扩散到千叶。

Taipei / Seoul 的海外 ticket links 也不进入日本 purchase URLs；purchase URLs / ticket phases 仍保持 `not_checked`。

## Parser

- 精确识别 Checkpoint tour title
- 只截 `SCHEDULE -> TICKET`
- 日本 + 海外 venue headings 全参与边界切分
- Japan allowlist only records
- 每个日期块提取唯一 start time
- OPEN 未逐场发布，保持 `not_found_on_page`
- `TICKET -> GOODS` 单独解析 ticket facts
- goods / ticket sale dates 不生成 event
- 动态 `tourMonths = 2026-09/10/11`
- collection window 不重叠时 adapter `skipped`

## Venue IDs

全部复用已有稳定实体：
- GLION ARENA KOBE -> `glion-arena-kobe`
- マリンメッセ福岡A館 -> `marine-messe-a`
- ららアリーナ 東京ベイ -> `lalaarena-tokyo-bay`

无需新增 entity facts。

## Registry

新增 `pending-sources-r45.mjs`，继承 R44 并追加 Checkpoint source。

Round 36 后 normal ingest/check 会自动拾取最新 registry，无需修改主 ingest/package。

## Smoke

fixture 同时包含完整日本 + Seoul + Taipei schedule，并断言：
- 日本 `allRecordCount = 6`
- Seoul 9/26 不存在
- Taipei 11/13–14 不存在
- 10–11 月未来 window = 4 场
- 福冈 FC 12,000 + 一般 12,500
- LaLa 只有 FC 12,000
- OPEN 全部 undefined
- GOODS 11/29 等日期不生成 event
- outside window 0 records but preserve tourMonths
- malformed page fail closed

## 验证

Round 44 Pending Source Checks 已 success。本 PR 会由同一 workflow 安装正式依赖后执行最新 registry runtime smokes + promoted-state preflight + collision audit。

## Diff

`backup/2026-09-15-pre-round45` -> feature 严格 4 个新增文件：
- parser
- adapter
- smoke
- R45 registry

无主 ingest/package/Venue/Source Health/event data/UI 修改。

本 PR stacked 在 Round 44 PR #47 上，不自动合并。

body:
## Summary

Session myia-po-2023 on #3412. The consumer-side validation was already saturated (6 vantages: po-2026, po-204, po-2025 ×2, ai-01, web1 ×2), so this session contributes the one vantage nobody had: **the IIS/ARR edge machine itself** — web1 (13/09) inferred from outside that both public legs share one ARR host; that host is **myia-po-2023, this machine**, and its live config is readable firsthand.

Runbook update adds **findings H and I** (docs-only, +26/−4 in `docs/services/sk-agent-streamable-http-rollout.md`):

### Finding H — ARR-edge topology confirmed firsthand
- `skagents.myia.io` (IIS site id 42) rewrites to `http://192.168.0.47:8100/{R:1}` — the hardened container **directly**, not through mcp-proxy.
- `mcp-tools.myia.io` (site id 45) rewrites to `http://192.168.0.47:9090/{R:1}` (mcp-proxy).
- **Rollback mechanism correction** (web1 13/09): the lever is a per-site `web.config` edit picked up live by IIS — no "ARR redeploy", no restart. Adds a 0-downtime ARR row to the §5 rollback table.
- **Tenant inventory** (steps 2–9 checklist): all 8 OWUI tenants live on this same edge — interne `:2090`, epf `:3010`, esg `:3011`, ece `:3012`, genai.epf `:3013`, epita `:3014`, pauwels `:3016` (demo aliases pauwels' `:3016`).

### Finding I — 120 s ARR ceiling, interacting with Step 0.5-C
- Both public legs cap requests at **120 s** at the IIS edge (skagents explicit `<proxy timeout="120">`; mcp-tools no override → ARR default). A `tools/call` exceeding it returns 502 with nothing in sk-agent logs — would surface during the pilot soak as "Tool Server flaky".
- **Catch on the proposed Step 0.5-C config**: the `"timeout": "5m"` relay entry is effective on the LAN leg only; through `mcp-tools.myia.io` it is silently capped at 120 s by ARR.
- Secondary: skagents site is streaming-friendly (`responseBufferLimit="0"`, `preserveHostHeader="true"`) and BadHost-protected; mcp-tools is neither — asymmetry noted.
- Ops decision flagged pre-Step 1: accept the 120 s ceiling or bump both sites (one-line web.config edit, live pickup).

### Probes (15/09, for the record)
`healthz` 200 public (`models_enabled: 11`), 401 on all 4 legs including `:8100` direct — consistent with all prior sessions.

## Note for reviewers

Docs-only PR (single .md). The known fleet-wide CI time-bomb (compare-claude-settings stale-date, diagnosed by po-2025 15/09) may show red on `build-and-test` — it predates and is unrelated to this diff (no submodule change).

## Test plan
- [ ] Review findings H/I factual accuracy against the runbook context
- [ ] ai-01/ops: take the finding I ceiling decision before Step 1

author: tumetsu
body:
Part of #841. Books uploaded before #839/#842 have neither a stored
publication index nor a Readium Locator on any highlight or reading
session, and the ingest paths only cover new writes. EPUBs arrive from
the KOReader plugin alone, so nobody will re-upload one to trigger the
derivation, and the web reader cannot open such a book.

Re-scoped from the ticket's user-triggered job batch: this is a one-off
data migration (076) that runs with `alembic upgrade head` on deploy,
with no route, no batch type and no button. Every book with an EPUB is
processed and whatever is stored is overwritten -- nobody has these rows
yet, so there is no staleness rule to get wrong.

Per book it reads the EPUB from the local store or S3, parses and
upserts book_publications, then derives locators once per kind (one
anchor-service call for all highlights, one for all sessions) and writes
them the way the R4.2 repositories do, including a NULL locator against
the current digest where the file cannot place an xpointer. A missing
file, an unreadable archive or an unparseable xpointer is logged and
skipped so one book's data never blocks the deploy; a database error is
allowed to fail the upgrade.

The anchor adapter gains sync module-level `range_locators` and
`point_locators` so a synchronous migration can reuse it; the async
methods wrap them and behave as before.

Tests run the migration's core through the SQLite test stack via
run_sync and assert stored rows: publication content, selectors on
placed highlights and both session endpoints, overwrite of stale rows,
containment of a missing or unreadable EPUB, deleted and xpointer-less
rows left alone, and one derivation call per kind per book.
