author: kage1020
body:
Closes #348.

`stdlib.md` §2.4 gives the type-member calls a result type:

```
TypeName.fresh()           : T            ; a new ID for a nominal type (UUIDv7)
TypeName.parse(text)       : Option(T)    ; string parsing of a nominal type
```

`inferType` implemented neither. Its `Call` case looked the callee up in `CALL_RESULT`, answered the `Duration.` and `Bytes.` qualifiers, and otherwise fell through to `sym.fns.get(callee)` — which holds no dotted name. So `TodoId.fresh()` was undecidable, and an undecidable expression is accepted wherever it lands:

```kumiki
type PostId = nominal Text where uuid
type UserId = nominal Text where uuid
slot p : PostId = "a"

reducer mk on=ui.click(B) do= p := UserId.fresh()              # was ok
slot found : Option(PostId) = UserId.parse("x")                # was ok
```

That left the nominal identity telling `PostId` and `UserId` apart everywhere *except* at the call that mints one — and `.fresh()` is how an id is normally created, so the unchecked position was the one that mattered most. `.parse` was the same gap one level in.

Both are reported now:

```
E0201 type-mismatch at 6:36: Expected PostId but got UserId
E0201 type-mismatch at 7:31: Expected Option(PostId) but got Option(UserId)
```

### Spec ⇆ implementation

The spec was right and the implementation was wrong, so nothing normative changed direction. `language.md` §1.3.5 gains a sentence naming the position the identity now reaches and the limit `fresh` is read under — the same thing #347 did for the comparison operators — and `docs/ja/spec/language.md` mirrors it.

### How the qualifier is read

**Resolved, not matched.** A primitive answers as a `TypePrim` (the grammar resolves those itself, so `sym.types` has no `Int`); a `type` definition that needs no arguments answers as a `TypeRef`; anything else answers nothing.

The arity half of that is the load-bearing one: an unapplied `TypeRef` to a `type Box(T)` unaliases into an unsubstituted body and mismatches against real types, so `Box.fresh()` would report `Expected Int but got Box` — a type nobody wrote. An **unresolvable** name costs nothing by comparison: `relate` short-circuits on a `TypeRef` it cannot unalias, so E0117 (#276) is the single report either way, measured both ways. Answering `null` there keeps the function honest rather than keeping the count at one.

All three type members are read through the one spelling rule codegen and `builtinArity` apply, so `Post-Id.fresh()` is E0116 — the callee that does not resolve — not a type member.

**`fresh` is narrower than `parse`, because its lowering discards the qualifier.** Codegen answers every `T.fresh()` with the same `_s.freshId()` — a uuid `Text`, whatever `T` says — so the qualifier is believed only for a type a `Text` inhabits, which is what §2.4.1's "for a nominal type" amounts to when the ids it scopes `fresh` to are `nominal Text`. Read without that test, the inference asserted types the lowering never produces:

| program | without the test | with it | value at runtime |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot a : UserId = PostId.fresh()` | E0201 | E0201 | — (the #348 case) |
| `slot b : Text = Int.fresh()` | E0201 ✗ | clean | a uuid string, i.e. a `Text` |
| `slot c : Text = Point.fresh()` | E0201 ✗ | clean | a uuid string |
| `slot g : Cents = Cents.fresh()` | believed a `Cents` ✗ | clean | a uuid string |
| `slot e : Text = PostId.fresh()` | clean | clean | — (AC3) |
| `slot h : Url = Email.fresh()` | E0201 | E0201 | — |
| `slot i : Int = Text.fresh()` | E0201 | E0201 | a uuid string, which is not an `Int` |

The narrowing also reads the alias and the narrowing rows for free: `Money.fresh()` on `type Money = Cents` and `Deep.fresh()` on `type Deep = nominal PostId` land where their declarations say, and `d := PostId.fresh()` on a `Deep` is E0201.

`parse` keeps the full answer: its lowering does produce the `Option`.

`Duration` and `Bytes` keep their own answers, ahead of the rule — their members are constructors rather than these two. `parse` is the one spelling they share, and both get it wrong the same way: `Duration.parse(t)` and `Bytes.parse(t)` answer a bare `Duration` / `Bytes` where the spec gives them `Option(…)`, so the documented spelling is E0201 and the wrong one is clean. That is #424, left as it was rather than widened into this fix and now pinned **in both directions** in `spec-divergences.test.ts`, so a fix moving only one of them fails. The qualified `show` is unchanged: it is `v.show` under another spelling and always a `Text`.

### The corpus, measured

Giving these calls a type can produce new diagnostics in programs that compile today, which #348 flagged as a corpus question rather than a one-line change. It was measured, not assumed: every `.kumiki` file under `packages/` and `docs/` — **126 of them**, the examples, the benchmarks and the `packages/mcp` / `packages/cli` / `packages/vite` fixtures — checked before and after, comparing code, position and message.

**The diagnostic lists are byte-identical: 39 diagnostics, same files, same positions, same sentences**, re-measured after the `fresh` narrowing. The ` ```kumiki ` blocks under `docs/spec/` are covered by `packages/tests/spec-blocks.test.ts`, which is green.

### Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `<Type>.fresh()` infers `<Type>`, `<Type>.parse(t)` infers `Option(<Type>)`; `Duration.*` / `Bytes.*` unchanged | `type-member-call-type.test.ts`, first four `describe`s |
| 2 | `p := UserId.fresh()` is E0201 naming both types; `p := PostId.fresh()` is clean | "reports one nominal's fresh id assigned to another" / "accepts the fresh id of the slot's own type" |
| 3 | `slot t : Text = TodoId.fresh()` stays clean | "accepts a nominal's fresh id where its base type is required" |
| 4 | An unresolvable qualifier infers nothing; E0117 owns the report | "reports the undefined type once and nothing about the value" |
| 5 | The corpus is measured | above — 126 files, identical output |

AC1 is met for the qualifiers `fresh` can actually mint a value of; the narrowing above is the deviation, and its reasoning is in the [resolved thread](https://github.com/kumikijs/Kumiki/pull/430#discussion_r4016936669).

### Known gaps pinned rather than fixed

Each reproduced, filed, and cited from the test that pins it:

| | |
|---|---|
| **#424** | `Duration.parse` / `Bytes.parse` answer `T`, not `Option(T)`. |
| **#431** | `parse` converts only `Int` / `Float` / `Time` — `Cents.parse("12").get-or(0)` is `"012"` at runtime. |
| **#432** | `Box.fresh()` / `List.fresh()` are silent; E0117, E0116 and E0201 each decline. |
| **#433** | `refinementToJs` defaults to `(_v) => true`, so `uuid` / `url` / `email` never run. |
| **#434** | `freshId` mints v4 where §2.4.1 promises v7. |
| **#435** | `inferType` has no `MatchExpr` case, so a `match` in **value** position is undecidable — `p := match ou with \| Some(id) -> id` is unchecked where `p := ou.get-or(p)` reports. The binder itself *is* typed, and both halves are pinned. Found writing AC1's positions test. |

### Changes

- `packages/compiler/src/typecheck.ts` — the `fresh` / `parse` arms, the `qualifiedType` resolver, and `freshResultType`.
- `packages/compiler/src/stdlib-types.ts` — `isPrimTypeName` narrows to `PrimName`, so the resolver builds the `TypePrim` without a cast.
- `packages/compiler/test/type-member-call-type.test.ts` — 24 cases, each asserting the whole diagnostic list, including the positions the minted type is read in: a `let` binder, a `fn` return, `==` (the #347 path), and alias/narrowing.
- `packages/compiler/test/spec-divergences.test.ts` — the `Duration.parse` / `Bytes.parse` pin.
- `packages/examples/features/66-value-types.kumiki` — two id types and the accepted `fresh` / `parse` forms, with every rejected form its comments name verified to produce the E0201 claimed; the scenario asserts the minted id reaches the slot, the record field and the parse, and was checked to fail when either

author: yabmas
body:
## Design

**Shape.** fukan's model-explorer commands lived in `dev/user.clj`, off the shipped
classpath. A project depending on fukan got the library and none of the surface you
actually work a model through. This ships that surface as `fukan.repl`: `go` builds the
model and **holds** the config (`:src`, `:title`, `:spec-dirs`, `:reload-dirs`), and the
nineteen commands read it back out, so every command stays bare. `dev/user.clj` becomes
fukan's own consumer of it — 314 lines down to 33, supplying fukan's defaults and nothing
else.

**Holds:**
- *fukan-on-itself is the first consumer, not a privileged one.* The consumer surface is
  driven on every REPL start, so it cannot rot while fukan's own loop keeps working. This
  is checkable: `dev/user.clj` reaches nothing in `fukan.*` that a consumer cannot.
- *The model and the code agree.* `canvas/architecture/orchestration/repl.clj` declares an
  `Operation` per command with its `:signature` and `:delegates`; `src/fukan/repl.clj` is
  extracted and checked against it like any other `src/` module. `repl_test.clj` asserts
  `(empty? (law/check …))` over the self-model, so a command added to one side and not the
  other fails the suite.
- *Nothing in the shipped path is fukan-specific.* `fukan.infra.model` is the default
  composition root for any Clojure project; the banner takes the project's name from `go`.

**Considered and rejected:**
- *A `title` parameter on `architecture-overview` as the way to name a consumer's system.*
  It made the function 2-arity while its `:malli/schema` claimed nullary, so fukan's own
  model misdescribed its own command — and the malli dialect cannot express multi-arity, so
  the spec could not be made faithful while the parameter existed. The title moved into
  `go`'s config instead; the function keeps the arity, the cockpit command stays bare.
- *Reloading with `{:only :loaded}`*, carried over from the old `dev/user.clj`. That was
  safe only while `canvas/` was untracked, and tracking it is the point. `:only :changed`
  is also simply the right semantics for `refresh`.
- *A two-pass reload* (`src/` then specs) as a workaround for the remaining mis-ordering
  window. It does not throw — it silently builds a **smaller** model with spurious
  violations (338 structures/897 relations/2 violations against a correct 509/1511/0).
  Documented as never-do rather than left as folklore.

**Deliberately left:**
- The reload mis-ordering window is narrowed, not closed: clj-reload's static graph cannot
  see edges crossing an untracked dir like `common/`. `reload-code!`'s docstring states the
  exposure and the recovery (restart the REPL). It is fukan-on-itself's only — a consumer's
  `reload-dirs` are its spec dirs, and it never touches fukan's `src/`.

## What else is here

Three fixes the consumer path forced:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| requiring the cockpit from brian's root | ~8 min at 100% CPU, then OOM | 4 s |

- **clj-reload 0.7.1** ends with an unconditional `(init {:dirs (classpath-dirs)})` at
  ns-load, so merely requiring the cockpit walked the consumer's whole tree —
  `node_modules`, `target`, `.git` — before any fukan code ran. 1.0.0 gates it behind
  `-Dclj-reload.auto-init=false`. It cannot live in fukan's own `deps.edn` on a consumer's
  behalf (a `:local/root` dep's `:jvm-opts` are not inherited), so the recipe in CLAUDE.md
  documents it as **required, not tuning**.
- **Spec-dir discovery** is filesystem-based while loading is classpath-based, so the cwd
  fallback could find files that then could not be required. It now names that cause
  instead of surfacing as a downstream "failed to load canvas namespace".
- **An unclustered model** degrades to a plain statement rather than a bare header over
  nothing — a fresh consumer authors specs before clustering them.

## Verify

```
clojure -M:test                                   # 443 tests, 904 assertions, 0 failures
clojure -M:lint --lint src common canvas test dev # 0 errors, 0 warnings
```

The interesting one is `fukan.repl-test/changed-reload-survives-a-touched-canvas-spec`: it
touches every `canvas/**/*.clj` mtime, calls `refresh`, and asserts the rebuilt self-model
has **zero** law violations — which is what proves the canvas spec and the shipped code
still describe the same surface.

## Summary
- preview Rapport/Favor changes in the Popup Text Editor against a real repository avatar
- keep the mobile 3D preview visible using a preview-first `dvh` layout and collapsed diagnostics
- replace the old bespoke single 360×112 relationship billboard with a chathead-style group: one square heart child + one independent signed-value child
- use the canonical PNG-plane rendering path for the heart (`HobunjiSpritePngSurface`) and CORS-safe image loading (`crossOrigin = 'anonymous'` before `src`)
- replace the relationship popup's bespoke diagonal grow/fade animation with Float+ sway/rise/late-fade behavior
- make relationship placement read the **live Float+ settings** on every frame, so changing Float+ X/Y/size in the Popup Text Editor affects the relationship popup exactly like ordinary Float+ placement
- use the current authored Float+ defaults: `worldHeight 0.13`, `xOffsetPercent 50`, `yOffsetPercent -10`, `lifetimeMs 1150`
- keep the heart + signed-number semantic colors (`Rapport = yellow`, `Favor = pink`, gain = green, loss = red)
- keep relationship-heart styling persistent under `relationshipHeart`: `opacity 0.9`, `glowPx 29`, plus a new `spacingPercent` control
- add a live **Heart ↔ number spacing** slider (`-50%` to `50%` of heart world size); lower values pull the number closer and negative values can pull it into the heart/glow margin
- active relationship popups relayout immediately when spacing changes
- retain `noOutline`, world-text overlay tagging, depth-disabled materials, and the tiny PNG alpha cutout
- keep Favor heart→point conversion in gameplay while the editor can preview literal ±10 values
- add root `AGENTS.md` documenting the non-obvious PNG/CORS/WebGL invariants for future coding/LLM sessions

## Why
The gameplay bug reproduced in the real 3D Popup Text Editor as a missing/black heart while the independently rendered signed number worked. The image-backed heart had omitted the CORS-safe loading rule used by the normal portrait path. That was fixed and documented.

The relationship presentation now keeps only its necessary heart+number composition. Placement and animation follow Float+, and the editor bridge observes the same live `applySettings(...)` calls used by ordinary popup text. Relationship-only visual styling remains independently tunable without forking Float+ placement.

## Validation
- `scripts/test-world-popup-relationship-editor.js` syntax-checks the browser helpers
- regression assertions cover the authored popup JSON, live Float+ X/Y capture, Float+ sway/rise/fade math, canonical/CORS-safe PNG heart rendering, persistent opacity/glow/spacing controls, active spacing relayout, and removal of the old diagonal grow animation
- the Popup Text Editor exercises the same relationship bridge used by gameplay

author: dsaffars
body:
JIRA ID: AIHPBLAS-4739

Convert 162 Aldebaran and Arcturus library logic YAML files from list to dict format.

## Motivation

TensileLite is migrating library logic YAML from the legacy list format to the canonical dict format. The dict format uses explicit root keys (ArchitectureName, CUCount, ProblemType, Solutions, etc.) and is the format TensileCreateLibrary now emits by default.

## Technical Details

This PR converts 162 library logic YAML files under:
`projects/hipblaslt/library/src/amd_detail/rocblaslt/src/Tensile/Logic/asm_full/aldebaran`
`projects/hipblaslt/library/src/amd_detail/rocblaslt/src/Tensile/Logic/asm_full/arcturus`
Format changes (no semantic changes intended):
* Root metadata moves from positional list entries to named keys (MinimumRequiredVersion, ScheduleName, ArchitectureName, CUCount, DeviceNames, ProblemType, …).
* ProblemType fields are nested under a ProblemType: mapping instead of inline list items.
* Solution entries move from list-of-flow-mappings to a Solutions: dict keyed by solution name.
* Boolean literals are normalized (True/False → true/false).

**Scope summary:**

| Libraries | Files | Lines before | Lines after |
|--------|--------|-------|-------|
| aldebaran (104CU, 110CU — GridBased, Equality) | 107 | 10,774,323 | 9,656,854 |
| arcturus (GridBased) | 55 | 16,048 | 22,359 |
Total | 162 | 10,790,371 | 9,679,213 |


## Test Plan
- [x] For each of the 162 converted files, compare pre-conversion list-format YAML against post-conversion dict-format YAML using compare_wrapper.py (same parser/compare path as Tensile library logic tooling).
- [x] Confirm no files added/removed; only in-place format conversion.
- [x] Verify all files were list format before conversion (no pre-existing dict files skipped).

## Test Result

* 162/162 files: semantically equivalent.
* File integrity: no adds/removes; only format conversion within existing logic files.
* Line count: 10,790,371 → 9,679,213 net (~10% reduction overall), with no intended change to kernel selection behavior.

author: kknr8367
body:
Found by reading its own output against a clean run:

```
completeness: COMPLETE   succeededSteps: 1000 / 1628   failed: 0
```

**1,628 step rows exist and all 1,628 succeeded. The endpoint saw 1,000.**

The route selected every step row with `limit: 5000` and counted statuses in memory. PostgREST caps a response at ~1000 rows **server-side** regardless of the app limit — the same cap that made 1,805 resources render as 1,000 elsewhere in this product.

## The count was the harmless half

The dangerous half: **a failure sitting beyond row 1000 was invisible.** This endpoint would then have answered `COMPLETE` with `countIsAuthoritative: true` over a scan that had failed — publishing a verified-looking total for a half-collected estate.

That is exactly the class of defect `scan-health` was built to expose, reproduced inside `scan-health`.

## Fix

Failures are fetched as their own filtered query (`status=eq.failed`) — they are the only rows needing detail (they group by scanner) and they are bounded in any healthy run. Successes need a number, not rows, so totals come from `count=exact` headers instead of a page.

`buildScanHealth` takes optional exact counts and falls back to counting rows when none are supplied, so nothing else that calls it changes.

3 tests, including the load-bearing one: **PARTIAL is reported from an exact failed count even when no failed rows were paged in.**

**509 tests pass.**

author: rdoyle1010
body:
The opening offer was September only and had no code. It now runs across September and October and carries a code a campaign can be printed with.

## The code is not a gate

Somebody who finds the site on their own still gets both courses inside the window. A gate would mean the person who came looking gets less than the person who saw an advert, which is the wrong way round.

What the code buys is **a number**. Every campaign that carries it can be counted afterwards, which is the only way to learn which campaign was worth running.

## Matched the way a person types it

Case, spaces, hyphens and underscores are thrown away before comparing, so `SPA-WELL26`, `spa well 26` and `spawell26` are one code. A link with `?code=SPA-WELL26` fills the box in so nobody types anything at all, and the box says "if you have one" because a field that looks compulsory and is not is a field people abandon a form over.

## The hour at each end

British Summer Time ends on 25 October 2026, so the close is midnight **UTC** on 1 November while the open is an hour before the UTC date changes on 1 September. An offer that says "to the end of October" and stops on the thirtieth for everybody reading it in this country is a broken promise, not a rounding error. A test holds both ends.

## Migration

One column, `candidate_profiles.signup_code`, with a partial index. The SQL is in the commit and has been given to Rebecca to run.

## Checks

1,229 tests, 46 readiness checks, production build clean.

author: adamswbrown
body:
## Summary

The Calendar→Notion upsert could write two rows for one `Apple Event ID`. This adds two layers that stop it at write time, plus tests.

Found while cleaning up five duplicated rows of the *Weekly Cadence Dr Migrate UK/Europe* series, created on 2026-06-30 in two bursts 106s apart. Those rows have been archived separately; this PR is the prevention.

## Root cause

`CalendarSyncUpserter.run` resolves create-vs-update against `existing` — a snapshot of Notion taken **once at run start and never updated**. The CREATE branch fired purely on `existing[appleID] == nil` and never recorded what it had just created. So any repeat of an Apple Event ID produced a second page rather than an update.

Two hypotheses were tested and **falsified**, so they are not what this fixes:

- **Missing concurrency guard** — there isn't one missing. `run()` is `@MainActor` with `guard !isRunning`, so in-process overlap was already impossible.
- **Notion index lag** — measured directly against the live API: a created page is visible to `/data_sources/{id}/query` in **~1.9s**, not minutes.

The exact 2026-06-30 trigger is **unrecoverable** — that day's log rotated away on 7 Sep. Rather than guess, both layers below close every remaining route to it.

## The fix

**1. `CalendarSyncRunRegistry`** (new, pure value type) — records every `appleID → pageID` the run writes. A repeat PATCHes that page and logs `duplicate appleID within run`.

This is not hypothetical. `CalendarEventMapper.compositeAppleID` has no calendar component, so one event shared by two opted-in calendars yields the same ID twice in a single run's input. Only one calendar is opted in today, which is why it hasn't bitten yet — but the Calendars tab invites adding more.

**2. `CalendarSyncNotionQueries.findPageID`** (new) — queries Notion filtered on `Apple Event ID` immediately before `POST /pages`. A hit is adopted and PATCHed, logging `adopted pre-existing row … snapshot was stale`. This is the layer that would have caught 30 June under any surviving hypothesis, because it checks at write time instead of trusting a snapshot taken up to a minute earlier.

Steady-state cost is nil — the lookup only runs on the create path, and steady-state runs report `created=0`.

## Testing

- **6 new tests**, written first. Watched them fail with `cannot find 'CalendarSyncRunRegistry' in scope`, then pass.
- `xcodebuild … test` → **240 tests, 0 failures** (234 before).
- Live sync after deploy: `created=0 updated=2 unchanged=337 skipped=53 failed=0` — identical to pre-change, no spurious adoptions.
- That run made no creates, so neither new branch executed and the Notion filter syntax was still unproven. Verified separately against the live API: existing ID → returns the expected row; unknown ID → 0 results (creates still proceed); previously-duplicated ID → exactly 1 row, archived twin excluded. Had `rich_text.equals` been invalid for that property, the next create would have thrown and aborted the sync.

author: cygnusb
body:
Measured against the real provider with one sample text, all four tones came back near-identical — differing only in word choice ("hierauf" vs "darauf") — and `concise` was not shorter. Three causes, all in the prompt plumbing rather than the model.

## What was wrong

**Temperature was never set**, so the client default of `0.2` applied and the model converged on one "best" rewrite regardless of the tone line. Tone shifts now run warmer (0.4–0.5); `standard` stays at 0.2, since it is only meant to fix language.

**The tone sat after the JSON output contract** — the last thing the model reads, competing with ~20 lines of very specific hard rules that simply out-argued it. The prompt is now built in three parts with the tone block between the rules and the contract.

**The instructions named a mood, not a behaviour.** "Use a warm, approachable tone" is not checkable. Each tone now names sentence-level choices (nominal style, short active sentences, "at least a third shorter") and says what it is *not*, so the model has a direction to move away from instead of one ideal to converge on.

## A regression this introduced, and the fix

Re-measuring caught it: at the higher temperature, `friendly` appended *"Wir schauen aber weiterhin nach."* to a text that said the opposite. An invented commitment in customer correspondence is worse than a bland tone. Both the shared hard rules and the friendly instruction now forbid promising a follow-up, next step, check-back or timeline the agent did not write. Three further runs produced none.

## Before / after

Same input (48 words), same provider:

| Tone | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| standard | 44 w, polished away the agent's own register | 44 w, keeps "drauf", "hängen komplett an", "Mehr Infos" |
| formal | 46 w, ≈ identical to friendly | 44–50 w, nominal: "Der Ausfall ist uns bekannt", "derzeit" |
| friendly | 51 w, ≈ identical to formal | 46–47 w, "Das ist ärgerlich –", active, no form-letter formulas |
| concise | 46 w, **not shorter** | 31–33 w, ≈ a third shorter |

Stable across three consecutive runs.

## Also

`_coerce_section_id` now accepts a single number anywhere in the id — the same measurement caught the model answering `{"id": "SECTION 1"}`, echoing the label, which would have cost a needless retry. No number or several numbers still reject, so tolerance about spelling never becomes tolerance about *which* section is meant.

## Verification

- `TIQORA_STRICT_DB_LEAKS=1 pytest -q` → 1876 passed, 25 skipped
- `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `mypy` clean
- Tone differentiation measured against the live provider, before and after, three runs each

body:
## Problème

Le workflow échoue presque chaque matin (et un jour sur trois à midi) depuis fin août, avec un mail à chaque fois. Les logs montrent que la cause n'est pas YouTube depuis les runners, mais le site du Collège lui-même : redirection 301 vers `/maintenance.html` (d'où le `ParseError: mismatched tag` sur le flux RSS), 502, 504. Le job `build-retry`, qui relançait 8 s plus tard sur un autre runner, ne changeait rien face à une maintenance qui dure des heures.

## Changements

- `build.py` : nouvelle exception `SourceUnavailable` et code de sortie 75 (`EX_TEMPFAIL`) pour maintenance, 5xx/429, erreurs réseau et tout échec YouTube ; un vrai bug sort toujours en 1. `get()` passe à 4 essais avec backoff 5/10/20 s et détecte la redirection vers `maintenance.html` via l'URL finale. Une panne survenant sur une vignette ou une page de chaire abandonne aussi le build au lieu de produire une page dégradée.
- Workflow : code 75 ⇒ run réussi avec un `::warning::`, pas de déploiement, la page en ligne reste. Une étape lit le `Last-Modified` de la page Pages et ne fait échouer le run que si elle a plus de `MAX_STALE_DAYS` jours (3). Le job `build-retry` est remplacé par un troisième cron à 18:07 UTC. L'input `workflow_dispatch` permet de simuler `sources-indisponibles` ou `bug`.
- README mis à jour.

## Vérifications

- Test unitaire de `get()` contre un serveur HTTP local (200, 503 puis 200, 502 ×4, redirection maintenance, 404, connexion refusée).
- Run réel de `build.py` contre le site en maintenance : sortie 75 en 39 s, aucun fichier écrit.
- Logique shell du workflow exercée localement pour les codes 0, 75, 1, 2 et les deux simulations ; étape de fraîcheur testée contre la vraie page Pages et contre une URL 404.
- Non vérifié : un build complet réussi, le site étant resté en maintenance pendant la session. Le chemin nominal n'est pas modifié, seulement enveloppé.

author: phmatray
body:
Implements #622.

Closes #622.

Executing the implementation plan task-by-task; the checklist below — and the plan on the issue — are ticked as each task lands. Opened as a draft — will be marked ready after the final task and a code-review pass.

> **On the shape of the fix.** `app/github-actions` is *not* sufficient evidence on its own — any workflow using the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` opens PRs under that login. The new accept path is a **conjunction** of three facts an outside contributor cannot forge together: the author, a `release-please--…` head branch, and a diff confined to the paths this repo's own `release-please-config.json` declares release-please will touch. Everything else still refuses, fail-closed.

### Plan
- [x] Task 1: accept the release PR on three independent facts, and nothing less


### Fixed along the way

- **`gh api` was being passed `-R`, which it does not accept.** `REPO_FLAG=(-R "$REPO")` was forwarded to four `gh api` calls; real `gh` answers `unknown shorthand flag: 'R' in -R` and exits non-zero, which every caller here then read as a failed API read. Three of those call sites pre-date this PR, so `approve-runs.sh -R <slug>` could never list or approve a run at all — and the new allowlist read would have been dead on arrival. `gh api` takes its repository from the URL path, and `GH_HOST` (exported by `gh_host_resolve`) reaches it, so the flag is simply removed. **The suite's `gh` stub now refuses `-R` on `api` exactly as the real tool does**, which turns every existing case into a guard against it creeping back.
- **The Windows `jq` binary emits CRLF**, so each approved run id reached the POST loop as `12345\r` and would have been sent to `…/runs/12345%0D/approve`. `tr -d '\r'` on the id list; this also repaired the suite's pre-existing `happy` case, which had been failing on Windows for the same reason.
- **A `{}` config parsed but declared nothing**, and the unconditional `.release-please-manifest.json` entry kept the allowlist non-empty — so the emptiness guard could never fire on a parseable config. The check now runs before the manifest is appended.

### Follow-ups

- **The branch conjunct carries little weight on a fork.** `release-please--*` is the contributor's to choose on a cross-repository PR, and nothing checks `isCrossRepository` / `headRepositoryOwner`. There is no live widening — the `app/github-actions` author conjunct still has to hold, and a fork PR is not authored by it — but the pattern is looser than release-please's actual `release-please--branches--<base>--components--<pkg>` shape, and tightening it plus refusing a cross-repository PR outright would make the conjunct mean what its comment says.
- **`.files` is a page, and this PR handles it by refusing.** A release PR touching more paths than GitHub returns in one page will now be refused rather than approved — correct, but it means a very large release cut still needs the manual `gh api … /approve`. Paginating the file list would remove that ceiling.

author: lei-tzuy
body:
## Why

The existing OCI bundle tests prove parsing, admission, persistence, and config routing, but replace the runtime runner with a test closure. The first real full-stack run exposed a production ordering bug: the re-executed child applied `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` from a package initializer, before it mounted proc, the rootfs, and volumes.

## What changed

- move no-new-privileges marker consumption to an explicit `ContainerInit` boundary after privileged setup and before capability drops, seccomp, and payload exec
- fail closed on malformed runtime markers and test the exact kernel state in a helper process
- build a minimal static BusyBox rootfs on the disposable privileged runner
- execute a real OCI bundle through `minictl oci-run`
- carry evidence out through a real bind mount
- require distinct PID and mount namespace identities
- require the minictl PID-1 supervisor
- require live `memory.max=134217728` and `pids.max=32`
- require `NoNewPrivs: 1` and seccomp mode 2 inside the payload
- keep the six named subsystem kernel regressions, including the distinct cgroup-namespace test, as separate evidence

## Scope

This is one bounded acceptance path, not an OCI/Docker conformance claim and not a multi-kernel matrix. Cgroup namespace isolation and bridge/veth ownership remain focused live-kernel tests rather than being combined with every subsystem in one global-host test.

author: kyle-sexton
body:
No related issue: PR-template ownership follows the decision recorded on melodic-software/standards#245

## Summary

This repository kept its own local pull-request template even though PR
templates are not standards-sync managed and the fleet inherits the org
default from `melodic-software/.github`. The local copy steered `## Related`
to the placeholder `N/A`, which is text an author can leave in place without
ever supplying a real signal, and told authors that a PR closing nothing
should carry a no-issue line with no reason attached. This repository's own
`.claude/rules/pr-body-contract.md` states the literal
`No related issue: <reason>`, so the template contradicted the rule the
repository already ships. Its file name also used the lowercase spelling,
where the other repositories in this organization that still ship a local
template use the uppercase one.

## Fix

Deletes the local template. GitHub's community-health-file fallback then
serves `melodic-software/.github/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, which
asks for a reason on the no-issue line it puts above the first heading,
offers no placeholder for `## Related`, and leaves each of `## Summary`,
`## Fix`, `## Verification` and `## Related` holding only an HTML comment.
Deleting also retires the casing split between the two spellings of the file
name.

A second commit drops the PR template from the `.github/` inventory in
`README.md`, which would otherwise keep asserting a file this change removes.

Deleting rather than editing in place: the local copy carried nothing the org
default does not. Its header comment restated the same contract already
stated in `.claude/rules/pr-body-contract.md`, which this change leaves
untouched and which remains the agent-facing statement of the body contract.
Standards' `pr-convention-lockstep` lane drift-checks the org template and
not any local copy, so a local copy is drift nothing watches. This follows
the precedent set when medley deleted its local template.

## Verification

Ran the `pr-contract` composite's own body analyzer, extracted verbatim from
`run.sh` at `5776760254f8b63cba44e896f51604cb755350d9`, the SHA
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins, over the deleted template and over the org
default that replaces it. Both, unfilled, report all four required sections
empty, so neither passes a section vacuously and this change does not
regress that:

```
section-empty	Summary
section-empty	Fix
section-empty	Verification
section-empty	Related
```

One audit claim did not survive checking and is not asserted here. The
composite recognises both no-issue phrasings, through the pattern
`no (linked|related) issue` applied to the masked body, and
`components/pr-convention-policy/policy.json` in `melodic-software/standards`
lists both as accepted markers. So the deleted template's phrasing was
recognised by the gate; what it actually got wrong was dropping the reason
the org default and this repository's rule both require, and steering
`## Related` to a placeholder.

A correctly filled body, this one, reports no empty section and carries a
non-closing marker.

On the fallback, the check worth running is the one read on a target
repository, not on the source: that the source exposes a template says nothing
about what a consumer receives. This repository's own profile still resolves to
its local file until this merges, so the evidence here is by proxy. Queried on
medley, a repository in this organization that already deleted its local
template, `repos/melodic-software/medley/community/profile` returns a
`pull_request_template` resolving to
`melodic-software/.github/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` while medley's own
`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` is absent. Every repository in this
organization with no local template resolves the same way. GitHub documents the
rule as applying "regardless of the destination repository's visibility", with
the public requirement falling on the `.github` repository, which this
organization's is. This repository is public in any case.

Swept the repository for references to the deleted path. One was live, the
`.github/` inventory line in `README.md`, and the second commit fixes it. The
rest are historical changelog entries plus generic source-control plugin
documentation about how a consuming project's template is treated; none points
at this repository's own file, and all stay as written.

author: farfromrefug
body:
## Summary

- The main forecast list could keep a stale item count after switching to a provider or model with a longer forecast range: the extra days stayed unreachable until something forced a layout pass (reporter's workaround: open and close the favorites drawer).
- `CollectionView.refresh()` early-returns without `notifyDataSetChanged()` while the view is unloaded (`index.android.js:974-977`, same on iOS), and its only replay — `onLoaded()` in `index-common.js:383-388` — is gated on `_effectiveColWidth`/`_effectiveRowHeight`, which are only set for lists using `colWidth`/`rowHeight`. The main list uses neither, so the refresh is dropped for good.
- `WeatherComponent` now flags an `items` update that lands while the list is unloaded and replays `refresh()` on the `loaded` event. Covers `WeatherPage`, `BottomSheetWeatherPage` and `FontSizeSettingScreen` in one place.

Changing the provider from the settings page is one path that hits this: `onProviderChanged` runs `refreshWeather()` while the weather page is unloaded (NativeScript unloads it on forward navigation).

## Testing

- Instrumented run confirmed the dropped update: changing the provider from settings logs the new `items` length with `isLoaded === false`, so `refresh()` returns early.
- The visible symptom needs a second condition — no layout pass following the reload — so it is timing dependent and could not be reproduced on demand locally. Reporter confirmation on the next build is still needed.
- `npx eslint` and `yarn svelte-check` clean. No unit test: the behaviour lives in a `.svelte` component driven by the native list, with no extractable pure part. **A visual check on device is still required** — switch to a longer-range provider from settings, go back, and scroll the full range without touching the drawer; re-check pull-to-refresh, favorite switching and font scale changes.

## Follow-up (separate repo)

The root cause is upstream in `@nativescript-community/ui-collectionview` (6.0.27): `onLoaded()` should honour `_isDataDirty` regardless of `colWidth`/`rowHeight`.

Fixes #506

author: pg-hub-mirror[bot]
body:
> **Read-only mirror.** Reply and review on pgsql-hackers; activity here is not sent upstream.

- Original author: Nikolay Samokhvalov <nik(at)postgres(dot)ai>
- Mailing list: `pgsql-hackers`
- Message-ID: `CAM527d-gHX4zZOhi9vvX+OsgEb+b2+fPbLUq8XRjAPYWQxDWjw@mail.gmail.com`
- [Original email](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/CAM527d-gHX4zZOhi9vvX%2BOsgEb%2Bb2%2BfPbLUq8XRjAPYWQxDWjw%40mail.gmail.com)

Patch files:
- [0001-postgres_fdw-Make-statistics-import-atomic.patch](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/attachment/203822/0001-postgres_fdw-Make-statistics-import-atomic.patch)

---

Hi hackers,
postgres_fdw can leave partial pg_statistic changes behind when statistics
import fails and analyze falls back to sampling.
My AI correctness harness found this while I was testing new PG19 features.
It also prepared and tested the attached patch.  I have not fully reviewed
that patch by hand because I am testing many PG19 areas in parallel.  I
nevertheless think it is useful to post: I mostly trust this harness, and
the exact reproducer and patch passed its independent execution and review
gates.  Please treat the patch as AI-prepared and review it in the usual way.
import_fetched_statistics() deletes and updates one attribute at a time.
attribute_statistics_update_internal() can update a partial row and return
false after a conversion warning.  Earlier attributes have already been
updated too.  If the fallback sample is empty, analyze does not replace
attribute statistics, so those changes commit.
Here is a complete reproducer.  Run it with psql as a superuser against a
fresh PG19 server that accepts a loopback connection on its Unix socket:
  create extension postgres_fdw;
  create table remote_t (a, b) as values (11, '21'::text), (11, '21');
  analyze remote_t;
  create server loopback foreign data wrapper postgres_fdw
    options (host :'HOST', port :'PORT', dbname :'DBNAME');
  create user mapping for current_user server loopback options (user :'USER');
  create foreign table ft (a int, b int) server loopback
    options (table_name 'remote_t', import_stats 'true');
  analyze ft;
  update remote_t set a = 111, b = 'bad-x';
  analyze remote_t;
  delete from remote_t;
  analyze ft;
  select attname, coalesce(most_common_vals::text, 'NULL') as mcv
  from pg_stats
  where tablename = 'ft'
  order by attname;
On REL_19_STABLE at e7c1b57012b the decisive output is below (psql's file
and line prefixes are omitted):
  WARNING:  invalid input syntax for type integer: "bad-x"
  WARNING:  could not import statistics for foreign table "public.ft"
--- attribute statistics import failed for column "b" of this foreign
table
   attname |  mcv
  ---------+-------
   a       | {111}
   b       | NULL
  (2 rows)
The attached patch runs the local catalog import in an internal
subtransaction.  It releases the subtransaction on success and rolls it
back when the import returns false.  Errors are rolled back and rethrown.
The remote fetch stays outside the subtransaction.
The new regression test fails without the code change with the same partial
update.  With the patch, the old coherent statistics survive:
   attname | mcv
  ---------+------
   a       | {11}
   b       | {21}
  (2 rows)
postgres_fdw regression and isolation tests pass.  I also applied the exact
attachment to a clean REL_19_STABLE checkout and reran both suites.
Nik

author: rhamzatov
body:
### Related Issues/PRs Closes #25781 ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? `GeminiAdapter.chat_to_model` builds a Gemini `functionResponse` for every `role: "tool"` message with `json.loads(message["content"])`. OpenAI tool message content is free-form and in practice usually plain text, so an ordinary tool result such as `"Status: 200 OK"` raised `JSONDecodeError` and the request failed with a 500 before it reached Gemini. That breaks any multi-turn tool-calling conversation through the gateway as soon as the first tool result is in the history. Checking the other shapes the gateway schema accepts for tool content turned up two more cases of the same bug: - An empty string, a list of content parts, or `null` content also fail to parse (`JSONDecodeError` / `TypeError`). - Valid JSON that is not an object (a number, string, list or `null`) parses, but is sent as `response` as is, while Gemini requires `response` to be an object. This PR replaces the bare `json.loads` with a small `_tool_result_to_response` helper, following the approach suggested in the issue: content that parses to a JSON object is passed through unchanged, and anything else is wrapped as `{"result": }`. The adapter method is shared, so the fix also covers streaming chat and Gemini models on Vertex AI (`_VertexGeminiAdapter` calls `super().chat_to_model`). Parallel tool-call grouping (#25788) is left for a separate PR. ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Existing unit/integration tests - [x] New unit/integration tests Added `test_gemini_chat_function_calling_tool_result_content` in `tests/gateway/providers/test_gemini.py`, modeled on `test_gemini_chat_function_calling_second_turn`. It is parametrized over plain text, an empty string, a JSON object, a JSON number, a JSON list, and a list of content parts, and asserts the `functionResponse` sent to Gemini. Without the fix, every case except the JSON object fails. ``` uv run pytest tests/gateway/providers/test_gemini.py tests/gateway/providers/test_vertex_ai.py tests/genai/judges/adapters/test_gateway_adapter.py ``` ### Does this PR require documentation update? - [x] No. ### Does this PR require updating the [MLflow Skills](https://github.com/mlflow/skills) repository? - [x] No. ### Release Notes #### Is this a user-facing change? - [x] Yes. Give a description of this change to be included in the release notes for MLflow users. The AI Gateway no longer fails requests to Gemini (including Gemini on Vertex AI) when a tool message's content is plain text or any value other than a JSON object; such content is now sent to Gemini wrapped as `{"result": ...}`. #### What component(s), interfaces, languages, and integrations does this PR affect? Components - [x] `area/gateway`: MLflow AI Gateway client APIs, server, and third-party integrations #### How should the PR be classified in the release notes? Choose one: - [x] `rn/bug-fix` - A user-facing bug fix worth mentioning in the release notes #### Is this PR a critical bugfix or security fix that should go into the next patch release?
What is a minor/patch release? - Minor release: a release that increments the second part of the version number (e.g., 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0). Minor releases are expected to contain larger changes, such as new features and improvements. Non-critical bug fixes and doc updates can be included as well. By default, your PR should target the next minor release. - Patch release: a release that increments the third part of the version number (e.g., 1.2.0 -> 1.2.1). Patch releases are typically only performed when there has been a major regression or bug in the latest release. For the sake of stability, your PR should not be included in a patch release unless it is a critical fix, or if the risk level of your PR is exceedingly low.
- [ ] This PR is critical and needs to be in the next patch release - [x] This PR can wait for the next minor release --- This fix was done on behalf of @Nantina, who reported the issue and handed it over to me. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: gurdenbatra
body:
The How drew nothing on the learning-system lens and said **"No mechanism nodes in this export yet."** There are seven.

The diagram is keyed on the **role** tag — `demand`, `supply`, `accelerator`, `capital`, `procurement` — not on `layer: mechanism`. So a wiki can carry mechanism pages and still assemble no diagram. Reporting that as "no mechanism nodes" is not merely vague; it is false, and it sends the reader looking for pages that are already sitting in the wiki.

The hint underneath was always right. The headline above it was wrong, and the headline is what people read.

## The change

The view now counts mechanism pages before deciding what to say.

- **None at all** → the original message, unchanged.
- **Some, but none carrying a role** → says how many, and names them, so the next move is a tag rather than a search.

Rendered against the real learning-system cut (12 pages, 7 mechanism, 0 roles):

> **7 mechanism pages, none carrying a role yet**
>
> The diagram is assembled from roles, not from the layer alone — these pages are here, they just have no side to stand on. Tag each one `demand`, `supply`, `accelerator`, `capital` or `procurement` and it will draw. Goal, Target, Search · Inquiry-Native Organising (INO) · Personal-to-collective wiki federation · Question-Native Organising (QNO) · The three databases · The three interfaces · and 1 more

## Verified, all three paths

Checked in the browser against real fixtures, not by reading the diff:

| fixture | renders |
|---|---|
| 7 mechanism pages, 0 roles (the live learning-system cut) | the new message, naming six and counting the seventh |
| 0 mechanism pages (same cut, layer stripped) | the original message, unchanged |
| 9 mechanism pages, 9 roles (the committed sample) | the matching diagram, as before |

The first row is the one that matters: it is the exact data that produced the false message in production.

`tsc -b` and `vite build` clean. `check-classes` clean where the repo has it.

## Why this lands in three repos

`src/views/matching/Matching.tsx` was byte-identical across all three lenses, so the defect was in all three. The other two wikis populate the view and never hit the empty state, so it never showed there — a message that is wrong only when a corpus is thin, which is exactly when somebody is looking at it for the first time.

author: lironco11
body:
## Summary

`code_comment` tool-call arguments containing a well-formed JSON value followed by trailing non-JSON content fail the whole parse in `parseToolArgs`, and a tool call that keeps failing the same way for the same task retries indefinitely with no backoff — burning tokens re-attempting an identical finding rather than either succeeding or giving up.

Fixes #1276

## Changes

1. `internal/llmloop/tool_args_json.go` (new) — `extractTopLevelJSON` scans for the first balanced top-level `{}`/`[]` JSON value, correctly skipping over string contents (including escaped quotes). `parseToolArgs` tries a whole-string parse first, and only on failure retries against the extracted span; if no balanced value exists at all it falls back to the original error unchanged (no regression for genuinely non-JSON input).

2. `internal/llmloop/tool_failure_streak.go` (new) — tracks a per-`(taskKey, toolName)` failure streak. 1st failure: unchanged error text. 2nd: same error plus an explicit instruction to fix the arguments or call `task_done`. 3rd and later: a non-error "skipped, won't be retried" result, so the loop stops burning rounds on a call that's already failed twice in a row. Any success resets the streak. `task_done` itself is excluded (telling it to "call task_done" would be circular).

Both changes are generic — no model-specific string matching (e.g. nothing gpt-oss/harmony-format specific) — since any provider can produce trailing content after valid JSON or retry a failed call without making progress.

## Tests

- `tool_args_json_test.go` — reproduces the original bug (valid JSON followed by trailing control-token-style content, confirms it now parses), confirms genuinely invalid input still errors, and unit-tests the extraction helper directly (trailing garbage, quoted braces, escaped quotes, unbalanced input).
- `tool_failure_streak_test.go` — asserts the exact 1st/2nd/3rd/4th-failure wording, confirms the streak is scoped per `(taskKey, toolName)` (a different task or tool starts fresh), and confirms a success resets the streak.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean
- `go test ./...`: all packages passing
- `go test -race -count=1 -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...`: all green under the race detector, 91.6% coverage (CI gate 90%)
- `gofmt -s -l .` empty, license/English-only checker scripts clean, `go mod tidy` produces no diff
- One pre-existing, unrelated skip (`TestInterruptChildHarness`), untouched by this change

author: mikker
body:
Make the Escape key match `esc` again in real terminals.

## TL;DR
Pressing Escape on its own produced a key that spelled itself `alt+escape`, so `key.matches(msg, 'esc')` stopped matching it once chords were compared whole (#6). `KeyMsg` now clears the modifier for a lone escape byte; a real alt+escape (two escape bytes) keeps it.

## Problem
bare-ansi-escapes emits the Escape key from its 500ms timeout with the meta flag it uses for ESC-prefixed keys. Before #6 the bare-name fallback hid that; after it, every app that closes something on `esc` lost the key.

## Desired outcome
`esc` means the Escape key, whether it arrives alone or followed by other bytes.

## Solution
In `KeyMsg`, `meta` is cleared when the name is `escape` and the sequence is the single escape byte. Test covers both the lone key and a two-byte alt+escape.

## Context for agents
Found driving keet-tui in a pty: `esc` closed nothing after the upgrade to 0.3. Headless tests craft KeyMsgs by hand and never hit the decoder's timeout path, which is why #6's suite passed.

author: hobbyiq
body:
Drew ruled **R49**: `Encased X` is the same rung as `Pristine X`. One list for `relocate-pool-rows-by-list.cjs`, **REPORT ONLY** until dispatched.

## It is a list, not a vocabulary entry — and the mechanism is why

I read how #2174 commit `8b9f0572` wired the adoption. `checklistSpellingAdoption.ts` reads `data/checklist-parallel-names.json` and adopts only a **strict extension** of the stated text (`"Silver"` → `"Silver Prizms"`); its own contract states the stated colour must survive into the answer.

`Encased Aqua Refractor` → `Pristine Aqua Refractor` **substitutes** the leading word. It is not an extension, so that mechanism cannot carry it, and adding it there would violate the module's invariant. The adoption code also reads only `parallel.name` and never the `spellings` array that exists in the data.

So the rows move by the committed-list lane, where every one is reviewable in the diff — **no code changed**.

## The mappings

1,323 rows, all `baseball/2025/topps-pristine`, all **REPOINT**:

| rows | mapping |
|--:|---|
| 405 | `encased-aqua-refractor` → `pristine-aqua-refractor` |
| 235 | `encased-blue-refractor` → `pristine-blue-refractor` |
| 227 | `encased-gold-refractor` → `pristine-gold-refractor` |
| 201 | `encased-purple-refractor` → `pristine-purple-refractor` |
| 112 | `encased-orange-refractor` → `pristine-orange-refractor` |

author: geekshiv
body:
Closes #512

Observed on #510: the guardrail check sat on `running` / `Scanning...` with **no scan log**, indefinitely. Three defects behind that, one of them mine.

## 1. The scan log was written too late to be useful — my bug from #502

`PRGuardrailScan.tool_log` was assigned **after `_run_guardrail_tools` returns**, i.e. after every tool had finished. So:

- a scan **still running** had an empty log;
- a scan that **died mid-run** never reached the assignment and had an empty log permanently.

Those are the two cases someone opens a scan log to understand. The feature was blank for exactly the situation it was built for.

Now emitted **after every tool** and committed by the caller, with un-reached tools shown as `pending` so the scan's current position is visible. The progress callback swallows its own exceptions — persisting progress must never become the cause of the outage it was added to diagnose, and there is a test for that.

## 2. A deploy orphaned the scan

#510's scan started at `15:26:35`; the deploy was queued at `15:26:22` — **13 seconds earlier**. `deploy.sh` runs `docker compose up -d --build`, so the Celery worker restarted underneath it. The row then stays on `running` until `mark_stale_if_needed` disowns it 15 minutes later, indistinguishable from a healthy slow scan until then.

## 3. No way to re-run

`POST /api/pr-guardrail/{pr_scan_id}/retry`, dispatched through the same Celery task the webhook uses — the synchronous `/scan` route would time out, since these take minutes.

A genuinely-running scan is refused with **409** rather than duplicated: two runs over one PR race each other's findings and commit status. "Retryable" means old enough for the existing staleness sweep to disown, reusing that definition rather than inventing a second one. The UI offers the button on `error` and `running` rows.

## A bug worth recording

The route first used `require_workspace_role(WorkspaceRole.DEVELOPER)` and **404'd every request**. That dependency resolves the workspace from a `target_id` / `workspace_id` / `finding_id` **query** parameter, and this route is addressed by `pr_scan_id`, so it had nothing to resolve. The override route immediately below already uses `current_user` plus the scoped lookup for that reason; this now matches it and enforces the role explicitly against the scan's own workspace.

## Deliberately not fixed

**Defect 2's root cause.** Draining or requeueing in-flight scans across a deploy is real work — the worker would need to finish or hand back what it holds before the container goes down. The retry button makes the symptom recoverable in one click; it does not stop deploys orphaning scans. Worth its own issue if it recurs outside an afternoon that deployed eight times.

## Verification

- **Full backend suite as CI runs it: 2786 passed, 1 skipped.** (Running only targeted sweeps is how a stale test double slipped through on #503, so this ran end to end before pushing.)
- 28 frontend tests across the guardrail-log and pr-history suites; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

author: andrescrz
body:
## Details

The span usage and BI queries excluded demo data with an inline `project_id NOT IN [...]` literal holding one UUID per demo project across every workspace. One demo project is created per signup, so that literal grows without bound, and a `Distributed` table re-parses the query text per shard — on traces that is what eventually pushed the equivalent queries past `max_execution_time`, after which the daily counts silently stopped being produced and under-billed. They failed silently because every consumer of these endpoints cannot tell an empty result from a failed one. This applies the same fix to spans **before** the spans wrap rather than after it.

The queries now `GROUP BY project_id` and `SpanService` drops demo projects in Java, via `DemoDataExclusionUtils`:

- `workspace-span-counts` folds the per-project rows by workspace
- `bi-spans` folds them by workspace and user
- `workspace-span-counts-breakdown` reports them as they are, so it only filters

The query text becomes constant, so growth in the demo set can never reintroduce the failure. Response shapes are unchanged, so nothing outside this repo moves with it, and the generated SDK clients need no regeneration.

Counts are preserved: `COUNT(DISTINCT id)` at project granularity sums back to the workspace and workspace/user totals, because a span id has exactly one project — `INSERT` and `PARTIAL_INSERT` reject a mismatched project with a sentinel that overflows the column, and `BULK_UPDATE` writes the stored `project_id` back unchanged.

Also here:

- The BI and breakdown queries were the same previous-day count under two texts differing by a column. One text now, behind two DAO methods, so the consumers keep distinct log comments in `system.query_log`.
- The `OR created_at > :demo_data_created_at` branch is dropped, as it was for traces. The cutoff is `max(createdAt) + 1 minute`, so where demo projects are created continuously it is effectively now and cannot match a row in the previous-day window. On a single install it could, so demo-project activity after install is no longer counted.
- `ProjectService.getDemoProjectIdsWithTimestamps` was the last unscoped demo-project fetch and is removed, along with the `ProjectDAO.findByGlobalNames` overload that defaulted the workspace scope away — the capability is gone rather than fenced.
- Three build-time guards, each verified by mutation: no DAO SQL constant anywhere may reference the exclusion placeholders; every demo-project lookup must bind a workspace scope; and the usage queries must render text that cannot vary, which is the name-independent form of the first.

**No `id_at` week bound, recorded as a decision on the SQL constants.** A bound is derivable in principle — the window is on `created_at`, and UUIDv7 ingestion validation keeps an id's embedded timestamp within a window of ingest — but that premise is a runtime setting rather than an invariant, and this is a billing count. Validation has a kill-switch and an audit mode that deliberately admits out-of-window ids, its window is operator-tunable with a wider per-workspace bypass on top, and none of it applies to rows already written. A bound would have to be correct for whatever configuration was in force when each row was ingested, which a query over a past day cannot know. The partition cost is answered by reducing the partition count instead.

**Deliberately not here:** a metric for a usage or BI collection that comes back empty. Making a silent-empty collection detectable is worth doing, but it is a cross-cutting concern over all seven internal usage and BI endpoints rather than part of moving the span exclusion into Java, and is better scoped and alerted on as its own change.

## Change checklist
- [ ] User facing
- [ ] Documentation update

## Issues

- Resolves #
- OPIK-8375

## AI-WATERMARK

AI-WATERMARK: yes

- Tools: Claude Code
- Model(s): Claude Opus 5
- Scope: full implementation, plus iterative code review and test review
- Human verification: author-directed review across several rounds, with reviewer-requested changes to scope, test design and documentation; build-time guards verified by mutation

## Testing

Commands run locally (CI re-runs everything):

- `mvn test -Dtest='UsageResourceTest,SpanServiceImplTest,TraceServiceImplTest,ProjectServiceImplTest,DemoDataExclusionUtilsTest,DemoDataExclusionLiteralArchTest'` — 68 passing
- `mvn spotless:check` and the `java-sql-narrow-datetime` semgrep hook

Scenarios validated:

- **Exclusion, black-box through the endpoints** — parameterised over one demo project and all of them; the BI fold summing a user's projects while excluding demo; the BI fold keeping two users in one workspace apart; the breakdown keeping projects apart while dropping demo rows
- **Fold arithmetic** — a workspace spanning several projects sums back to one row
- **The premise the fold rests on** — a span id cannot move between projects, pinned by both routes: a create is ignored, and a patch is refused with the project-mismatch conflict asserted by message rather than by bare status
- **Behaviour change** — demo activity is excluded even where the demo project predates the removed cutoff
- **Error cases** — a failing query and a failing demo lookup each surface as an error rather than as an empty collection, which is the exact shape of the incident this change prevents. Verified by mutation: answering an empty response instead of failing breaks these tests
- **Service-level cases integration cannot reach** — a day with no spans, the demo lookup scoped to the workspaces that had spans, multi-workspace response mapping
- **Build-time guards** — each mutation-checked: reintroducing the literal, adding back an unscoped lookup overload, and adding a differently-named placeholder each fail the build

Not run locally: the full backend suite, left to CI.

Post-wrap execution against a `Distributed` `spans` is covered by the harness in the spans mutation-routing PR (OPIK_7799) rather than duplicated here, and by a wrapped staging environment, which has the shard count and data volume to make it meaningful — a single-shard testcontainer cannot exercise cross-shard aggregation.

## Documentation

N/A — no user-facing documentation changes. The rationale that matters for posterity lives in javadoc on the SQL constants and the build-time guards: why the exclusion cannot render into the query text, and why no `id_at` bound is added.

author: rcjlabs
body:
The entry named `campaign/monologue.js`, 4.2 KB, as the largest line on the eager graph's exemption bill. Measuring it first was the milestone.

## Three claims, checked before building

| the entry said | measured |
| --- | --- |
| `monologue.js` is eager "only because `wire.js` imports it" | **four** eager modules import it |
| that line is worth 4.2 KB | **1.3 KB** — moving code between two eager modules saves nothing |
| the bill is 11.0 KB across four modules | true, and it is **6%** of the real number |

## The bill counts modules. Nobody was counting bytes.

`RUNS_NOTHING_BUT_BELONGS` excuses a module that runs **no** function at boot, so the cheapest way off the list is to run one. Asked per **function** instead — every top-level function in the eager graph that no boot ever calls — the answer was **174.2 KB of 559.4**. Thirty-one percent, against an 11.0 KB bill. The worst offenders were never on the list, because none of them was idle:

| | eager | what boot actually calls |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `splice/theater.js` | 19.5 KB | `isSettled`, **73 bytes** |
| `battle/statblock.js` | 17.4 KB | two predicates, **195 bytes** |
| `campaign/rivals.js` | 22.2 KB | four functions, **1.3 KB** |

## What ships

- **`splice/chimera.js`** (2.7 KB) — the settling clock, `renameCreature` and the `TRAINING` price, the only three things six eager modules wanted from the Theater. **`splice/theater.js` is now lazy.** No re-export from it: an import path back in is how 19.5 KB returns without a decision.
- **`campaign/identity.js`** — the name roll, the philosophy menu and `duelBarks`, whose only caller is the lazy War Room. `monologue.js` 4.1 → 2.8 KB.
- **`DEAD_AT_BOOT_KB = 170`** — the second rule, in a different unit, printed on every run.
- Every exemption paid or re-justified **by name**. `battle/statblock.js` stays eager at 17.4 KB for 195 bytes of predicate, because deferring it makes `resolveBattle` async and breaks CLAUDE.md's harness rule — written down rather than rediscovered.
- `wire.js` imported `philosophyOf` and never used it. Dropped.

| | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| first paint | 1034 KB | **1016 KB** |
| `FIRST_PAINT_KB` | 1034 | **1034, unmoved** |
| eager JS | 559.4 KB | **541.3 KB** |
| `KB_CAP` | 560 | **543** |
| functions no boot calls | 174.2 KB | **160.3 KB** |
| the exemption bill | 11.0 KB | **9.8 KB** |

## Then break 248 went MISSED, which was the real finding

After a green baseline, a green suite and 292 matching anchors, I ran the 44 breaks aimed at what this milestone moved. Break 248 — R153's `export * from './director.js'` — had gone MISSED. Reproducing it by hand, only one of four numbers moved:

| | clean | with break 248 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| eager modules / KB (static walk) | 48 / 541.3 | **48 / 541.3** |
| modules running nothing | 4 | **4** |
| functions no boot calls | 160.3 KB | **160.3 KB** |
| first paint (real browser) | 1016 KB | **1028 KB** |

`eagerGraph()` matched `import … from` and nothing else, so **a re-export was invisible to the static walk** — and `KB_CAP`, the module-runs-nothing list and this milestone's own dead-byte budget all read that walk. Three rules blind at once, leaving the browser waterfall as 248's only reader at 1046 over 1034. Take the measurement to 1016, keep the cap at 1034 on purpose, and 1028 fits.

I had argued in this same milestone that tightening a budget cannot blind a break. True, and beside the point: **leaving a cap still while the measurement falls under it is loosening by omission.** The fix is the hole, not the budget — both walks follow `export … from` now, 248 is caught by three rules, and the slack survives. The clean tree does not move, because the tree's one real re-export names a module already imported on the line above.

## One budget keeps its slack and two do not, on purpose

`FIRST_PAINT_KB` does not come down onto 1016. It went red once at 1034 against 1034 — a slow afternoon, not a regression — so the 18 KB is the deliverable. `KB_CAP` and `DEAD_AT_BOOT_KB` stay tight: a file-size walk reads the same number twice, and the dead-byte walk read 160.3 three times to the byte.

## A break I wrote, missed, and deleted

Dropping the nesting filter moves 160.3 → 163.8 only, because V8 reports no coverage inside a function nobody called. Tightening the budget until my own break fired would have been tuning the gate to its test, so the break went and the measurement is written where the filter is.

## Verification

- **Full battery: 292 breaks, 291 caught, `BATTERY_EXIT=0`** (triggered: the walk change is existing gate logic)
- `--anchors` 292/292 · baseline `BATTERY_EXIT=0` · `roadmap ✓` · `boot ✓`
- `npm test` green — 786 CPU-seconds of 1246 budgeted, 4m13s
- Breaks 297 and 299 go red on demand; 125, 126, 127 and 248 all caught

The one miss, **break 262**, is not this milestone's: the same break run against `main` itself in a worktree at `e3fd32f` misses identically. Queued as **R170** — R168 raised `CPU_BUDGET_S` above the break, and its box-independent share rule is guarded `rebuilt === 0`, so it is skipped for every battery break, always.

**The lesson:** *a bill that counts whole modules will always be smaller than the debt, because the cheapest way to stop being on it is to run one function. When a rule stops catching things, suspect its denominator before its threshold.*

author: jelmer
body:
`Error::Socket` only carried the bare errno extracted from a Python
`socket.error`/`OSError`, discarding everything else the exception held --
including the filename or socket path. A real `socket error: No such file or
directory (os error 2)` gave no indication of which path was actually missing.

Capture the Python exception's own string representation alongside the errno and
surface it in `Display` when present. The Python round-trip conversion is
unaffected, since it only ever used the errno.

Note that this changes the arity of the `Error::Socket` variant, so external code
matching on it needs updating.

Navazuje na sloučený PR #63.

## 1. Sazba platební brány 6,50 Kč + 1,5 %

**Skutečné poplatky Stripu vzorci odpovídají na haléř** — ověřeno proti produkci:

| Platba | Skutečný poplatek | Vzorec | Počet |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 499 Kč | 13,99 Kč | 13,99 Kč | 24× |
| 998 Kč | 21,47 Kč | 21,47 Kč | 8× |

Sazba proto **nenahrazuje** naúčtované poplatky — ty zůstávají zdrojem pravdy.
Slouží ke kontrole a k plánování:

- **Finance** srovnají naúčtované poplatky se sazbou a rozdíl pojmenují. Za září
  je −85,88 Kč, protože 141,84 Kč poplatků je `pending` a do součtu se správně
  nepočítá.
- **Bod zvratu** poplatek brány konečně zná: proměnný náklad 83,99 Kč
  (13,99 brána + 70 materiál) místo 70 Kč, takže se posunul z 24 na 25 míst.
  Model navíc funguje i bez pravidla „za zaplacené místo".
- **Nastavení** sazbu zpřístupňují k úpravě (`business_settings.payment_fee`);
  bez uloženého nastavení platí ověřená výchozí hodnota v JS i v SQL.

## 2. Ověřování vazby na rezervaci (původní obsah PR)

První produkční běh synchronizace Stripu spadl na cizím klíči — metadata nesla
UUID rezervací, které už neexistují. `business-sync` teď vazby ověřuje proti
tabulce `bookings` a neznámou zahodí na `null`.

## 3. Dvě chyby zobrazení, které našla kontrola

- **Chybějící částka svítila jako nula.** `Number(null)` je 0, takže
  `formatMoney(null)` vracelo „0 Kč" místo „—". V Přehledu se u návrhu rozpočtu
  zobrazovalo **0 Kč** vedle věty „Výsledek není úplný, proto automatický návrh
  nevznikl". Stejně `num()` u nespočítaného bodu zvratu. Opraveno `finiteNumber`.
- **Sazba se zaokrouhlovala na koruny** — poplatek 13,99 Kč svítil jako „14 Kč".
  Pro sazbu vznikl `formatMoneyExact`.

## Křížové ověření SQL proti JS

Audit vytýkal, že `business_period_summary` a `computeFinancials` jsou dvě
nezávislé implementace a testy pokrývají jen druhou. Nasazená SQL funkce byla
spuštěna pod identitou majitelky (`set local role authenticated`, celé
v transakci s rollbackem) a stejná produkční data prošla JS implementací.

**Všech 16 metrik ve dvou obdobích vyšlo identicky** — včetně
`expected_fees_minor`, `fee_gap_minor`, `unmatched_income_entries`
i `missing_payment_amounts`.

## Stav v produkci

Migrace `business_summary_payment_fee_tariff` a `business-sync` v7 jsou
**nasazené**. Klientská část se dostane živě až merge tohoto PR.

## Ověření

```
npm run check                 → 53/53 testů
npm run test:business-browser → 8 sekcí, graf, mobil, náklad, CSV import
```

Platebního toku se změna nedotýká.

author: fadhln
body:
## Problem

`PLAN-ADMIN.md` feature 7 (role change with history) and the remaining part of feature 1 do not exist. A user cannot be listed, read, changed, or given a role, and there is no role history. The Owner also cannot issue a password reset for a staff member.

This pull request delivers backend phase BA4, the last phase of the administration plan.

Stack:

1. `ba1-identity` -> `main` (#42, merged)
2. `ba2-account` -> `main` (#43, merged)
3. `ba3-orgs` -> `main` (#44, merged)
4. `ba3b-stations` -> `main` (#45, merged)
5. `ba4-roles` -> `main` (this pull request)

## New behavior

- `GET /api/v1/users` — an Owner reads the users of the own organization. A Superadmin sends `org_id` and reads the users of that organization.
- `GET /api/v1/users/{id}` — one user, with the roles and the stations.
- `PATCH /api/v1/users/{id}` — changes `display_name` and `enabled`. An Owner cannot change a user who holds the Owner role or the Superadmin role: that is 403 `protected_user_forbidden`.
- `POST /api/v1/users/{id}/roles` — adds one role for one station.
- `DELETE /api/v1/users/{id}/roles` — removes one role for one station. Result: 204.
- `GET /api/v1/users/{id}/role-history` — the role events for that user in sequence order.
- `POST /api/v1/users/{id}/password-reset` — issues a reset token and returns `{"link": "..."}` one time. An Owner cannot issue a reset for an Owner or a Superadmin.

Authority rules:

- An actor without the Owner role and without the Superadmin role receives 403 on every path.
- An Owner cannot assign or remove the `Owner` role or the `Superadmin` role: 403.
- An Owner cannot change the own role: 403 `self_role_change_forbidden`.
- The last Owner of an organization cannot lose the Owner role: 422 `last_owner_forbidden`.
- A role that is already granted is 409 `role_exists`. A role that is not granted is 404 `role_not_found`.
- A role change is active on the NEXT request automatically, because `ReadSession` reads the roles from the database on every request. The service does not revoke a session for a role change.

## Role history

The history reads `audit_log`. There is no second history table. Each assignment and each removal appends an audit event in the same transaction as the change, with:

- the event type `role.assigned` or `role.revoked`;
- the actor, the target user, the station, the role, and the before and after values in the payload.

The response fields are `sequence`, `actor`, `target`, `station_id`, `station`, `role`, `before`, `after`, and `created_at`.

## Plan reference

`PLAN-ADMIN.md` sections 4.1, 5.4, 6.1, 6.3, 6.4, 10, and 11.

## Migration impact

New migration `000016_role_history_index` (up and down) adds a partial expression index:

```sql
CREATE INDEX audit_log_role_history_target
    ON audit_log ((payload ->> 'target'))
    WHERE event_type IN ('role.assigned', 'role.revoked');
```

The history query filters on `org_id`, on the two event types, and on `payload ->> 'target'`, so this index matches the query shape instead of indexing the whole payload. The down file reverses only this up file.

## Contract impact

`docs/openapi.json` documents the new endpoints. `go run ./cmd/openapi -check` passes.

The field names match the Svelte frontend that is already merged, so the two sides agree on the first run. The user view sends `user_id`, `email`, `username`, `display_name`, `enabled`, `roles` (`role`, `station_id`, `station_name`), and `stations` (`station_id`, `name`).

## Review size

20 files, 2619 added lines and 58 removed lines. The test files hold 341 lines and `docs/openapi.json` holds the largest share of the rest, and neither counts toward the 900-line review cap under the agreed rule.

## Verification

```
docker exec pomkita-pg psql -U pomkita -d postgres -c "create database ba4_final"
DATABASE_URL="postgres://pomkita:pomkita_dev@127.0.0.1:5432/ba4_final?sslmode=disable" make check
```

Result: exit code 0, zero failing packages, against a FRESH database. The command covers `gofmt`, `go vet`, the unit tests, the PostgreSQL integration tests, the race tests, and the OpenAPI check. The migration round trip passed.

The red step was observed for each behavior before the production change.

## Second commit: constructor type safety

The first commit loosened the identity service constructor to take an untyped parameter and to discard two type assertions:

```go
func NewService(repository any, ...) *Service {
	identityRepository, _ := repository.(Repository)
	adminRepository, _ := repository.(AdminRepository)
}
```

That removes the compile-time check on the dependency: a caller can pass a value that implements neither interface, and the field then holds a nil interface, so the failure appears later as a panic at an unrelated call site. The second commit restores two explicit typed parameters and updates every call site. `cmd/server/main.go` passes the one repository value that satisfies both interfaces. A test that exercises only one side passes `nil` for the other side, which keeps the existing nil-guard behavior.

Proof: `grep -n 'repository any' internal/service/identity/service.go` and `grep -n ':= repository.(' internal/service/identity/service.go` both print nothing, and `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.
