body:
> Stacked on #1 — base branch is `docs/deep-dives`, so this PR shows only the new file. GitHub retargets it to `main` automatically when #1 merges.

## The number

**14 points claimable today.** The subject requires 14. That is a pass with **zero margin**, and the subject warns against exactly this: *"aiming for more than 14 points in total may be a good idea, especially if some modules aren't validated during the evaluation."*

| # | Module | Cat | Type | Pts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Framework for both frontend and backend | Web | Major | 2 |
| 2 | ORM | Web | Minor | 1 |
| 3 | SSR | Web | Minor | 1 |
| 4 | Custom design system | Web | Minor | 1 |
| 5 | OAuth 2.0 | User Mgmt | Minor | 1 |
| 6 | Complete RAG system | AI | Major | 2 |
| 7 | Complete LLM system interface | AI | Major | 2 |
| 8 | ELK | DevOps | Major | 2 |
| 9 | Prometheus + Grafana | DevOps | Major | 2 |
| | **Total** | | | **14** |

Scored against **subject v21.1** (`../ft_transcendence/en.ft_transcedence_v21_1.pdf`, section IV), and against code on `main` — not against intent. A module is listed as claimable only if every bullet in its description is met, because the subject is explicit that an incomplete module is worth 0, not partial credit.

## The risk you should look at first

**Module #4 is the weak one.** The subject asks for "a proper color palette, typography, and icons (minimum: 10 reusable components)". We have 13 components, a one-token re-skinnable palette, and Geist Sans/Mono. We have **no icon set** — the UI uses text glyphs (`♡ → ✕`). A strict evaluator rejects it, and **without #4 the total is 13, which is a fail.**

Second risk: #6 and #7 both live inside `/search` and can be read as one system. The doc says how to demo them as two distinct things.

## Cheapest points available

| Module | Pts | What's missing |
|---|---|---|
| Custom module: ingestion pipeline | +2 | **Only the README justification.** The code and docs are done. |
| Standard user management (Major) | +2 | One bullet — "users can update their profile information". No `PATCH /me` exists; name and email can't be edited. |
| 2FA (Minor) | +1 | The email-code infrastructure exists; it runs at registration, not as a second factor at login. |
| File upload (Minor) | +1 | A progress indicator, and a delete control — `DELETE /me/avatar` exists but nothing calls it. |

Roughly a day of work takes 14 → 20, i.e. enough margin to survive two rejected modules. The doc has the ordered path.

## Also found while checking

The **Terms page tells users they can delete their account "from your profile"**, and no such endpoint or UI control exists. That is a live inconsistency in a published legal page, independent of module scoring.

## What's definitively out

Everything gaming (no game — which also blocks Game statistics and AI Opponent), microservices (a deliberate decision in the opposite direction, per `architecture.md`), blockchain, WAF/Vault, roles, organizations, ML recommendations. The doc explains why each one would mean building a different product rather than finishing this one.

Also flagged: claiming the Data & Analytics "advanced analytics dashboard" Major would reuse the same Grafana dashboards that are the evidence for module #9 — claiming one artifact twice risks losing both.

## Resumo

FlowVoice **0.4.8**: `temperature` 0 explícito na transcrição (P137), fechamento da bolha de outro app no retorno do Início (P130) e registro da validação da 0.4.7 no S26.

### P137 — `temperature` 0 explícito
- Nem a OpenRouter ("Sampling temperature between 0 and 1", sem padrão) nem o SDK da OpenAI documentam o valor padrão de `temperature` na transcrição.
- `OpenRouterConfig.temperature` = 0.0 (validado em [0, 1]) agora vai em todo pedido. O resultado deixa de depender do padrão de cada provedor.

### P130 — bolha de outro app
- O Wispr Flow não roda no S26 e não tem permissão de sobreposição.
- Pelo `dumpsys accessibility`, a bolha do FlowVoice (mesmo tipo de janela de sobreposição de app) é `TYPE_SYSTEM`, inativa e sem foco, tanto parada quanto tocada e aberta como barra.
- Como o `PreviousAppTracker` exige janela ativa `TYPE_APPLICATION`, bolha de app nunca vira destino.

### Validação da 0.4.7 (P136)
- Com `openai/gpt-transcribe`, os três ditados curtos saíram corretos ("Primeiro ditado pelo início.", "Segundo ditado pela bolha.", "Terceiro ditado pela bolha."). A revisão não mudou nada.
- A entrada pelos Recentes também voltou às Notas.

body:
## 概要

`isSafeWebdavUrl` 原为 `/^https?:\/\//i` 一行正则，形同虚设。webdavUrl 来自 `POST /backup|restore/webdav` 请求 body——端点有 `isWriteAllowed` 门禁，但**回环免 token 意味着本机任意进程可调用**：对能过门禁的调用方这是真 SSRF 原语（`169.254.169.254` 元数据端点/内网探测，restore 的状态码与 diff 输出构成 oracle；push 还会把调用方给的 Basic 凭据 PUT 向任意主机）。另有 `redirect:"follow"` 的「校验 A 实际打到 B」重定向洞。

## 改动

- `lib/domain/validation.js`：新增 fail-closed `isSafeWebdavUrl` + IPv4/IPv6 网段分类（私网保留 http——NAS 刚需 `192.168/16`、`10/8`、`172.16/12`、ULA `fc00::/7`、`.local`/单标签内网名；**公网强制 https**——Basic 凭据禁走明文；回环/链路本地/CGNAT/组播/保留/文档段/Teredo/6to4/NAT64 一律拒绝；IPv4-mapped 按内嵌 v4 同规则；内嵌 `user:pass@` 拒绝）
- `lib/app/backup.js`：新增 `requestWebdav`——`redirect:"manual"` + 逐跳 URL 复核（≤4 跳）+ 跨 origin 剥 `Authorization` + 303 降级 GET；push/restore 统一改走它
- `lib/index.js`：注入真函数替换弱正则；`i18n.js`：`webdavBadUrl` 双语文案

## 测试

- `lib-pure.test.mjs` +66 条表驱动（合法 LAN/https、169.254/回环/CGNAT/保留段、IPv6 走私、混淆 IPv4、畸形/内嵌凭据、端口边界、大小写归一）
- `app-backup.test.mjs` +32：受限 URL `invalid-url` 且零外发、LAN http 放行 + manual、302 相对路径跟随、跨 origin 剥凭据、受限目标仅首跳、重定向环封顶
- `lib.test.mjs` +18：计数 fetch 桩断言「受限 URL → 400 且零外发」「302→受限目标仅首跳」「合法 302 两跳跟随」
- 全量：unit+integration 87/87、smoke 192/192、syntax/TOC/secret 全绿

## 已知残余

域名解析结果不在校验范围（DNS rebinding 理论可绕，DNS 预查同样有 TOCTOU）；靠端点门禁 + 响应只回传 diff 兜底，函数头注释已写明。

author: sunfish-shogi
body:
## 説明 / Description

This PR adds comprehensive license management for bundled WebAssembly engines in ShogiHome's Web distribution. Since engines are included as part of the distributable package, their licenses must be presented within the package itself rather than relying on external links.

### Key Changes

**Specification & Documentation:**
- Added "9. ライセンス" section to `specs/wasm-engine-abi.md` defining the license declaration format in engine manifests
- Updated `specs/wasm-engine.md` with license display architecture and caching strategy for license files
- License files are now required in engine directories and cached alongside engine modules

**Manifest Schema:**
- Added `EngineManifestLicense` type with fields: `spdx` (SPDX identifier), `file` (path to full license text), `subject` (optional display name), and `source` (optional source code URL for copyleft licenses)
- Added `licenses` array field to `EngineManifest` (required for conformance testing)
- Implemented validation: `file` must be a safe relative path, `source` must be an HTTPS URL, and `licenses` must be non-empty if declared

**Runtime Support:**
- Added `resolveEngineFileURL()` to safely resolve engine file URLs with path traversal protection
- Added `loadBuiltinEngineLicenses()` to collect licenses from all builtin engines' manifests
- Licenses are loaded asynchronously and gracefully handle manifest read failures

**UI Integration:**
- Updated `openCopyright()` in `copyright.ts` to display bundled engine licenses alongside ShogiHome's own license and third-party libraries
- License display shows `<subject> (<spdx>)` as clickable links to bundled license files
- Source code links are displayed separately when available (for copyleft licenses)
- Web-only feature (Electron version does not bundle engines)

**Service Worker:**
- Added caching rule for `*.txt` files in engine directories using the same `StaleWhileRevalidate` strategy as engine modules

**Testing & Conformance:**
- Added unit tests for license parsing, validation, and URL resolution
- Added conformance test requiring all engines to declare licenses with non-empty license files
- Updated test fixtures with MIT license declaration for sunfish4-lite engine
- Added `LICENSE.txt` file to sunfish4-lite engine directory

### Design Rationale

- **Full text bundling required**: External links are unreliable (may disappear, inaccessible offline). License compliance must be self-contained in the distribution.
- **Optional in parser, required in conformance**: Allows gradual migration while enforcing the requirement for public engines
- **Array of licenses**: Supports engines with multiple components under different licenses (e.g., engine binary vs. evaluation parameters)
- **HTTPS-only source URLs**: Prevents security issues from arbitrary URL schemes while allowing legitimate source code links

## チェックリスト / Checklist

- MUST
  - [x] `npm test` passed
  - [x] `npm run lint` was applied without warnings
  - [x] changes of `/docs/webapp` not included
  - [x] `console.log` not included
- RECOMMENDED
  - [x] unit test added/updated (manifest parsing, URL resolution, license loading)
  - [x] i18n (Japanese documentation and comments; English comments for code)

author: luqmanbello
body:
### Make sure these boxes are checked! 📦✅

- [ ] You ran `./run_tests.sh`
- [ ] You ran `pre-commit run -a`

Neither applies cleanly. `run_tests.sh` exercises the Python app and cannot validate a workflow file. `pre-commit run -a` fails on `main` for unrelated reasons: the license hook rewrites 50 files under `app/`, and mypy is not installed. `pre-commit run --files .github/workflows/ci.yml` passes, and `actionlint` reports nothing on the changed lines.

### What was wrong? 👾

CI publishes only to `safeglobal/safe-decoder-service` on Docker Hub, but devstaging and production both read `ghcr.io/safe-global/safe-decoder-service` now. Every release needs `mirror-to-ghcr.yml` run by hand before the new tag exists where the charts look.

v1.17.0 is that gap today: it is on Docker Hub and returns 404 on GHCR. Production is pinned to v1.16.1 so nothing is broken, but bumping `imageTag` before someone runs the mirror would put the new pod in ImagePullBackOff.

### How was it fixed? 🎯

The `docker-deploy` job now pushes to both registries in the same build.

- `packages: write` added to the job, needed to push with `GITHUB_TOKEN`
- A GHCR login step beside the existing Docker Hub one, same pinned `docker/login-action` SHA
- `ghcr.io` tags appended to all three push steps: `staging` on main, `develop` on develop, and the release tag plus `latest` on a release

One build, both registries, so the digest is identical on each.

This is a dual push, not a cutover. auth, network and billing switched outright because their images are private with no external consumers. decoder is public and actively consumed, so Docker Hub keeps receiving pushes for the full deprecation window.

When the window closes: drop the Docker Hub push, drop `DOCKER_USER` and `DOCKER_PASSWORD`, and delete `mirror-to-ghcr.yml`.

Two pre-existing things on untouched lines, for whoever is next in here: `actionlint` flags SC2086 at line 92 in the `test-app` job, and `setup-qemu-action` is pinned to a different SHA than the other migrated services use.

- Reuses `POST /api/habits/suggest-setup` and applies only the emoji.

- Shares an immediate request lock between full-setup and emoji suggestions while preserving field-specific loading feedback.
- Keeps the web empty-title emoji action keyboard-focusable with `aria-disabled` and a guarded click handler.

2. Either suggestion action blocks the other in the UI and in the request coordinator.

## Data Recovery Runtime Proof

Adds the next post-roadmap hosted runtime proof for Aetheris data durability and backup/restore behavior.

### Live checks
- gateway, identity-service, and user-service readiness
- synthetic identity, user, and refresh-hash persistence
- PostgreSQL container restart durability
- core application service restart durability
- Redis users-list cache population, clearing, authoritative recovery, and reconstruction
- real PostgreSQL custom-format backup creation
- backup SHA-256 and byte-size evidence without publishing the raw backup
- restore into a fresh isolated recovery database
- exact recovered identity/user/refresh metadata comparison
- temporary Identity Service backed by the recovered database authenticates the restored identity
- pre-backup refresh credential works against the recovered identity database
- temporary User Service backed by the recovered database reads the restored user
- primary gateway path remains operational after isolated recovery validation

### Added
- `.github/workflows/data-recovery-runtime-proof.yml`
- `tools/data_recovery_runtime_smoke.py`
- `build-evidence/runtime/data-recovery-runtime-contract.json`
- `docs/data-recovery-runtime-proof.md`

### Truth boundary
This is `HOSTED_RUNTIME` evidence on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu + Docker Compose. It is not production disaster-recovery certification, PITR/WAL-archive validation, encrypted/off-site backup validation, cross-region DR, an RPO/RTO guarantee, Kubernetes PVC/CSI recovery validation, or physical-PC validation. The raw backup remains inside the ephemeral CI database container and is not uploaded.

`BLOCKED_PENDING_HARDWARE` remains authoritative for target-PC-dependent Syntra/Aetheris functionality. There is still no Stage 35; this is a normal post-roadmap engineering capability pass.

author: hernloh
body: ## Summary Fixes rtl_buddy#551. A suite carries one `compile:` block (rtl_buddy#497), which is the wrong granularity when two testbench entries verilate an order of magnitude apart: the reporter's small geometry peaks at ~6 GB, the product geometry at ~130 GB, and the suite-level `compile.mem` had to state the large number on every pull request, so the suite was split into two files that differ only in the reservation. - `testbenches[].compile: {cpus, mem, time}` is now the most specific layer of the compile reservation, over the suite's `compile:`, over `cfg-dispatch.compile`, over `cfg-dispatch.resources`. It is typed `DispatchResourcesFile` (no `parallel`; serde drops it) and validated in `TestbenchConfig.__post_init__` with the testbench named. It rides into the build and sim jobs through the plan round-trip. - The suite's single build job reserves the **field-wise maximum** over the testbenches the plan actually selected tests from (new `max_compile_resources`), with `cpus × parallel` applied afterwards; an unselected testbench contributes nothing. A sim job that compiles for itself is sized from its own testbench's block. - Per-field provenance records which testbench supplied each winning field, so right-sizing emits appliable `edit_hint` paths: `testbenches[name=X].compile.`, `compile.`, or `cfg-dispatch.compile.`, mixed within one run when the max took `mem` from one entry and `time` from another. `--dispatch local` and every suite whose testbenches declare no block resolve exactly as before. Docs: `docs/concepts/dispatch.md` (layering + the two-geometry example + the planned-testbench max rule), `docs/reference/yaml.md` (testbench `compile` row), dispatch SKILL.md. ## e2e (Slurm 26.05.2 in the Apple container) Suite block `{cpus: 2, mem: 1G, time: "00:10:00"}`; second testbench `tb_top_big` with `compile: {mem: 3G, time: "00:20:00"}` and one test pointed at it. | run | build job | ReqCPUS | ReqMem | Timelimit | |---|---|---|---|---| | regression, both testbenches planned | 250 | 2 | 3G | 00:20:00 | | `rb test basic` (only `tb_top` selected) | 257 | 2 | 1G | 00:10:00 | The build-job time advice in run 1 carried `edit_hint.path = testbenches[name=tb_top_big].compile.time` pointing at the suite tests.yaml; in run 2 it fell back to `compile.time`. All tests PASS, exit 0. ## Tests 22 new or extended tests across `tests/test_dispatch_config.py`, `tests/test_regression_dispatch.py`, `tests/test_dispatch_rightsize.py` and `tests/test_config_loaders.py` (schema binds/validates/drops `parallel`; layering order; max over planned entries only; scaling by `parallel`; in-job compile uses its own testbench; attribution shapes). ## Review rounds Four Codex/Devin rounds are folded in. The reservation is no longer a field-wise maximum: the suite block is the whole-job floor, testbench blocks are per-build summands (`cpus` max, `mem` summed over the builds that overlap, `time` = the greedy list-schedule makespan the build job's pool actually runs), and a `reduce` no single edit can apply is withheld (`compile-origin-tied` / `compile-aggregate`) while an aggregated `raise` is translated to the contributor's own new value. Two things to know when reviewing: - **Machine-output surface.** `reservation-advice` events gain two additive keys, `suggested_total` and `aggregate_delta` (null on ordinary rows). - **Behaviour change once a testbench states its own `mem`.** Until then the suite-level `compile.mem` is the whole-job reservation, exactly as rtl_buddy#497 defined it. Once any planned testbench declares `compile.mem`, builds that declare none bid the suite figure as their per-build memory into the overlap sum (so an annotated 256G build sharing a slot with an unannotated one under an 8G suite value reserves 264G at `parallel: 2`). A project adding its first testbench block to a suite with `parallel > 1` will see the build reservation grow; the docs say so in both places. - **The planned-build key is an approximation** of the build job's real grouping (`compile_group_dir`, which the head cannot see without writing filelists on the submit host, rtl_buddy#458). It covers testbench, plusdefines, builder, model, assertions and the per-test split for a builder that cannot share; a future head-visible compile input has to be added there too. The failure mode is an over-count (reserving for a build that does not run), never an under-count. ## Note `src/rtl_buddy/skill/rtl-buddy-dispatch/SKILL.md` sits at 8188 of its 8192-byte cap after this change; the next edit to that skill must free space first. ## Stack PR 5 of the Slurm-triage stack; based on the rtl_buddy#534/#535/#536 branch (#576). Closes rtl_buddy#551. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) (claude-ethan) ---

## What

- New tool field `busy_footer`: the row a CLI paints under its activity cutoff only while a turn runs. A working rule that matches while that footer is back in its resting form belongs to a turn that died before its end marker, and reads `errored`.
- opencode sets it to its knight-rider spinner (`■■■⬝⬝⬝⬝⬝`), which the footer keeps through provider retries.
- The poller's hung-turn fixtures carry the spinning footer, so the 15s stuck grace still covers a pane frozen mid-turn.

## Why

Closes #509. An opencode turn that dies on a provider error leaves its bare `▣  Build · <model>` header behind, which matches the working rule; the stuck grace settles it finished after 15s and the next poll matches working again, so the row flaps working/finished every 20s with a notification each cycle. The footer is the one thing on screen that says whether a turn runs.

## Verified

- `TestDefaultRulesRealPanes` gains five real opencode 1.18.31 captures: provider error → `errored`, turn cut short during a retry → `errored`, slow model → `working`, retry banner → `working`, esc interrupt (`· interrupted`) → unmatched, settled by the quiet path as before.
- Real binary under a fake HOME on an isolated tmux socket, opencode 1.18.31, quick-prompt spawns:

body:
## What

MemoryStore.list() read the entire append-only per-kind \.jsonl\ memory log, \JSON.parse\d every line, and only afterward sliced to the last \limit\ entries. Since this log is append-only and grows unbounded over the service's lifetime, every read paid full-file parse cost for entries it immediately discarded.

## Fix

Slice the split lines to the requested tail *before* parsing, so only the retained entries are ever \JSON.parse\d. Same return value/order/limit semantics, no behavior change for callers.

author: nathaelb
body:
Closes #1322, closes #1323, closes #1324, closes #1325. Part of #1329.

## The problem

Reported on 0.7.2 from a live deployment running FerrisKey in front of LimeSurvey: clicking "sign in with OIDC" on the second application asks for the password again, even though the user is signed in to the IdP. The code is identical on `main`, so nothing shipped since fixes it.

FerrisKey had no SSO session. What played that role was a cookie holding a raw access token, set on the response of the token endpoint and replayed at `/auth`. Three consequences:

1. The SSO window was exactly the access token lifetime, 300 seconds by default.
2. The cookie had no `Max-Age`, so it died with the browser while the console still looked signed in, which is why the behaviour read as random.
3. A confidential client exchanges its code from its own backend, so the `Set-Cookie` landed in LimeSurvey's HTTP client and never reached the user. Signing in through such an application bootstrapped nothing at all.

## The change

The SSO session is now opened in `finalize_authentication`, at the interactive step where the browser is still on the line, and handed out as a `FERRISKEY_SSO` cookie whose `Max-Age` follows `user_sessions.expires_at` (24 hours by default).

At `/auth` that cookie is resolved and checked: session alive and not revoked, right realm, account still enabled, client not under maintenance, no required action pending. Anything else falls back to the login page, which knows how to handle each of those cases. The code exchange then joins the session recorded on the auth session instead of opening a second one for the same sign-in.

`FERRISKEY_IDENTITY` is still read as a fallback so live sessions survive the upgrade, and a browser still carrying only it is migrated onto the new cookie the first time it signs in anywhere. Removing it is #1326.

### The cookie holds a secret, not the session id

The obvious cookie value would be `user_sessions.id`. It cannot be: `list_sessions` hands that id to any holder of `view_users` (`libs/ferriskey-domain/src/session/services.rs:120`), so a read-only permission would have been enough to impersonate the session's owner. The cookie carries a 43 character secret instead and only its SHA-256 is stored. A test asserts the cookie value is none of the session ids in the table.

### Two guards that were missing

`handle_token_refresh` skipped `user.enabled` and the maintenance whitelist, which every other authentication path enforces. A disabled account could still complete an authorization as long as its cookie had not expired, and the same hole was reachable from `/login-actions/authenticate`. The maintenance check is now a shared method rather than twenty lines duplicated.

### Audit

Reusing a session means `create_user_session` no longer runs on the second application, and the `LoginSuccess` event it emits would have gone with it. The SSO path emits its own, tagged `"method": "sso_session"`.

## Migrations

- `auth_sessions.user_session_id`, nullable, `ON DELETE SET NULL` so revoking a session drops the link rather than the row.
- `user_sessions.sso_token_hash`, nullable, unique.

Both entity files were regenerated with `sea-orm-cli --expanded-format` and match the codegen output. Note for whoever does this next: `sea-orm-cli` 1.1.19 hangs on schema discovery against PostgreSQL 18, so the entities have to be generated against a throwaway PostgreSQL 17 with the migrations applied.

## Testing

`api/tests/sso_session_test.rs`, 7 integration tests against PostgreSQL:

```bash
cargo test -p ferriskey-api --test sso_session_test -- --ignored
```

They cover the reported scenario end to end (sign in through client A, then `/auth` for a confidential client B with its own redirect URI, and get a code without the login form), the refusals (disabled user, unknown session, no cookie), the cookie shape, session reuse and the audit trail.

1090 unit tests green across 40 suites. `session_management`, `token_revocation`, `seawatch`, `mfa_bypass`, `device_flow`, `saml`, `registration` and `nonce_id_token` all still pass.

Six integration suites fail on this branch (`login_aliases`, `organization`, `pkce`, `portal_theme`, `refresh_token_rotation`, `token_basic_auth`). They fail identically on `main` with the same counts: the global Prometheus recorder only tolerates one `router()` per binary (#1086), plus a `block_in_place` from a current-thread runtime. Unrelated to this work, but worth its own issue.

## Not covered here

The MFA terminal steps (OTP, passkey, WebAuthn, magic link, recovery code) finalize inside `TridentServiceImpl` without going through `finalize_authentication`, so they do not hand out the cookie yet. Nothing breaks for those users, the identity cookie fallback keeps their current behaviour, they simply do not get the fix. That is #1330, split out because it means adding a generic parameter to `TridentServiceImpl`.

Also still open: #1326 (drop the identity cookie), #1327 (`remember_me_enabled`), #1328 (the OIDC `prompt` parameter).

- **New Features**
  - Added browser-based single sign-on, allowing users to move between applications without signing in again.
  - Sessions can now be resumed when returning to an application.
  - Added secure, HttpOnly SSO cookies with expiration controls and HTTPS protection.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Disabled users can no longer resume existing SSO sessions.
  - Stale SSO sessions now prompt users to sign in again.
  - Logging out now also clears the SSO session cookie.

author: aa362ce
body:
## Summary
- The quick-hash and full-hash stages now spread file reads/hashing across a thread pool (`concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor`) instead of hashing one file at a time, defaulting to one thread per CPU core (`os.cpu_count()`).
- Cancellation and resume still work exactly as before, just checked once per batch of in-flight files rather than between every single file.
- Adds a `-j`/`--threads` CLI flag to override the worker count (e.g. `--threads 1` to hash sequentially).

## Why
Hashing was previously strictly sequential, so large scans left most CPU cores idle during the (often disk- and hash-bound) quick-hash and full-hash stages. Threading lets multiple files be read and hashed concurrently -- file I/O releases the GIL while waiting on the OS, and hashlib's C implementation releases it per chunk too.

## Test plan
- [x] Ran `find_duplicates` with `workers=1`, `workers=8`, and the default (auto-detected) worker count against the same fixture directory (mix of duplicate and unique files) and confirmed identical duplicate groups across all three
- [x] Cancelled a scan mid quick-hash stage, resumed it, and confirmed the resumed result matches an uninterrupted threaded scan
- [x] `python -m file_sorter -j 4 <dir>` runs end-to-end via the CLI; `--help` shows the new flag with the correct default

body:
## Summary

Architecture-level unification study between Yana AI and BMAD-METHOD, per explicit request: audit both repos from real source code (not README claims), classify every capability, design a unified engineering architecture, and implement the low-risk phases. Does not touch anything under `tools/yana-studio/` or `docs/` — this branch is deliberately separate from the concurrent studio work on `codex-based-studio`.

## Deliverables

- `BMAD-YANA-CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md` — 30 capabilities classified (KEEP_YANA / ADOPT_BMAD_CONCEPT / UNIFY / REJECT / NEEDS_RESEARCH) against real code in both repos.
- `BMAD-YANA-GAP-ANALYSIS.md` — what BMAD genuinely offers Yana (concentrated in pre-execution planning) vs. what Yana must not let BMAD duplicate (the entire execution/authority/safety kernel, where BMAD has no equivalent at all).
- `YANA-UNIFIED-ENGINEERING-ARCHITECTURE.md` — target architecture: one WorkUnit (`mission::Task`, unchanged from `task.rs::Task`), a 10-state lifecycle, SPEC-to-authority wiring, an extended evidence model.
- `YANA-UNIFIED-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` — phased plan with per-phase goal/files/tests/risk/rollback; phases 1, 3, 4, 5 are implemented here, phase 2 is resolved as cancelled, phases 6-9 remain design-only.

**Headline finding:** Yana's `src/runtime/authority.rs` + `src/capability/lease.rs` already implement the "probabilistic proposes, deterministic decides" split this study required, more rigorously than BMAD's own advisory-only mechanisms. BMAD is fundamentally a prompt-engineering framework with a narrow (~6,900 line) real deterministic layer underneath; its genuine contributions are concentrated in pre-execution planning, not execution/authority/safety.

Three findings were corrected mid-implementation after reading real code that contradicted the initial audit, documented in place rather than silently fixed — see the commit message for detail. Most consequential: the planned Task/Mission merge (Phase 2) was cancelled after finding `task.rs` backs its own live CLI subsystem (`yana-rt task`, `yana-rt eval`) with a real eval-judge quality circuit breaker, not a duplicate of `mission::Task`.

## Implemented and tested

`cargo test --bin yana-rt`: 828/828 passing, +28 new tests, zero regressions.

- **Phase 1** (`src/spec/mod.rs`): extend `spec validate` with optional authority-contract fields (`commands.allow`, `network.allow`, `limits`, `approval_required`), additive to the existing schema.
- **Phase 3** (`src/mission/mod.rs`): `transition_status` guards `TaskStatus` writes across all 5 command handlers so `Done` cannot be silently reopened; scope narrowed from the original rank-table design after finding it would have blocked previously-legal transitions.
- **Phase 4** (`src/evidence/git_measure.rs`, new): real `git diff --numstat` measurement as a fourth evidence signal alongside the existing HMAC-signed receipts, `ToolEvidence`, and regex-heuristic mechanisms.
- **Phase 5** (`src/spec/mod.rs`): `to_intent_declaration` translates a validated spec's authority fields into a real `IntentDeclaration`, reporting (not silently dropping) fields with no honest mapping yet (e.g. `network.allow`, since no `network.*` capability exists in the registry today).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --bin yana-rt` — 828/828 passing (fresh run before this PR)
- [x] No changes to `src/runtime/authority.rs`, `src/capability/lease.rs`, or any `core/hooks/`/`core/gates/` file (deterministic kernel untouched, confirmed by the diff itself)
- [x] No changes under `tools/yana-studio/` or `docs/` (confirmed separate from concurrent studio work)
- [ ] Human review of the WorkUnit-base and task.rs-preservation decisions (already discussed and confirmed in the originating session, recorded in `YANA-UNIFIED-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md`'s Phase 0 resolution)

## What was wrong with the guard #1214 shipped

The "is it global" check was a typed list:

```js
const ZIP_SCOPED = ['alerts.html', 'development.html', 'homesignalmap.html'];
```

A ZIP-scoped page added later would declare no Place and **nothing would fail**. That is the same shape as the defect it guards — an instrument that only sees the cases someone typed into it, which is exactly why the Viewing-chip defect survived its first fix. #1214's description claimed *"the next one cannot be added without a declaration"*; that was not true of the code. This makes it true.

## What it does now

The page set is **read off disk** — every `*.html` that loads `shell.js`. Each must either declare a Place (`declareRouteZipPlace` / `setViewPlaceType`) or appear in `EXEMPT` with a written reason:

| Exempt | Reason |
|---|---|
| `community.html` | declares through its shared runtime, `lib/community-page.js` |
| `dashboard.html` | names ALL MY PLACES — an all-places briefing, not one Place |
| `properties.html` | the My Places list — no single Place is in view |
| `reports.html` | not ZIP-scoped |
| `index` / `about` / `contact` / `how-it-works` / `privacy` | marketing — no Place subject, saved-address default applies |

Fail-closed in both directions: a **new** page is in scope the moment it exists, and an exemption **naming a page that no longer carries the chip** also fails, so the escape hatch cannot rot into a silent hole.

## Proven load-bearing — three mutations, each caught on exit code and each naming the offender

```
M1  new chip-bearing page, no declaration
    FAIL — every chip-bearing page either declares its Place or is exempt
           with a stated reason   detail: ["newtool.html"]

M2  shipped page loses its declaration
    FAIL — alerts.html declares the route ZIP Place
    FAIL — it declares BEFORE the first await …
    FAIL — every chip-bearing page … detail: ["alerts.html"]

M3  exemption goes stale
    FAIL — no exemption names a page that no longer carries the chip
           detail: ["retired-page.html"]
```

Baseline restored clean after each.

## Scope

- **No product file is touched.** `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` → `test/viewed-place-declaration.test.mjs`, and nothing else.
- No view-place declaration, label, routing or saved-address fallback logic changes.
- No cleanup, refactors or unrelated fixes folded in.
- **No generated or cache artifacts required** — `shell.js` and `lib/community-page.js` are unchanged, so no `?v=` restamp; `test/lib-cache-keys.test.mjs` passes as-is.
- Offline suite: **206/206 files pass.**

## One thing stated rather than buried

An exempt page that **later starts declaring** is deliberately *not* failed — it is harmless, and tightening it is outside this guard's scope. The first draft's comment claimed that case was covered; it was corrected rather than left overclaiming, since a guard whose comment promises more than its code is how the last one slipped through.

## Scope

Plan 001 Task 5/7C follow-up, issue #18, Slice A in
`docs/plans/001-macos-process-visibility.md`.

- Select a Darwin-native source for both scan and plan; preserve gopsutil on
  Windows and other platforms, along with required native Windows CI.
- Bracket field inspection with fresh native PID/creation-identity snapshots.
  Retry whole changed attempts up to three times under a 20-second deadline;
  never merge rows across attempts or clear remaining unknown evidence.
- Positively validate kernel-only PID 0 and confirmed zombie records inside
  the Darwin source. Shared invalid-PID and global-unknown safeguards remain
  unchanged. Preserve microsecond native creation identity and use numeric
  effective UID rather than username lookup.
- Add native contract/unit tests and a regression running actual installed
  binaries against disposable Git fixtures.
- Bound native sysctl sizing and growth retries before allocation. The
  already-pinned purego module becomes a direct dependency; no dependency
  version is added or upgraded.

## Verification

Local native macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Go 1.26.5, Git 2.50.1:

- RED: `go test -count=1 -run '^TestInstalledPreviewRunsNativeScanPlanExplain$' ./tests/e2e`
  fails before the implementation for the real kernel PID 0 misclassification.
- GREEN: same command passes after the change. Scan remains exit 1 /
  `complete=false` (192 observed warnings); plan remains an authenticated
  partial result with exit 1. Explanations, tamper rejection, owned child
  correlation, and fixture non-mutation pass.
- `go test -count=1 ./...` — PASS, 17 tested packages, two without tests.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` — PASS, same package coverage.
- `go vet ./...` and `go build ./...` — PASS.
- `gofmt -l .` — empty; `git diff --check` — PASS.

## Review and limitations

Independent AI design review identified the ordinary-user path-validation
boundary as well as kernel/enumeration defects. R1 code review found one P2:
the pinned x/sys helper had an unbounded ENOMEM retry and allocated before our
cap. Commit cc02ff2651815005a4b65f98090a7146f5a92c3a replaces that path with
bounded native reads and fault-injection tests. R2 closed the finding and
reported no new actionable findings. All local commands listed above passed
again after that correction. The reviewer did not independently rerun tests
or certify CI. **AI review is not human approval.** Final-head native
macOS/Windows CI remains required before merge.

**#18 remains open.** No sudo invocation, privileged helper, daemon, sudoers
change, policy relaxation or release qualification is introduced. Permission
handling requires a separately proven/reviewed slice; matching observations
are not an atomic process freeze. Raw process tables, paths, command lines,
plans and keys remain private and are not attached. PR #14 is excluded.

author: chojona
body:
[SCRUM-484](https://carpoolnu.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-484) — phase 3 of [SCRUM-477](https://carpoolnu.atlassian.net/browse/SCRUM-477).

Two places that assumed a tall viewport. Both come from the same shape: `#__next` is `100dvh`, `HeaderDiv` is `height: 8.5%` of it, and every desktop content row is the `91.5%` remainder — so a landscape phone's row is 343px and its header bar is 31.9px. Three commits, the first two separately reviewable as the ticket asked.

## The header — `Logo` had a height unrelated to its parent's

`HeaderDiv` is a percentage of the viewport; `Logo` declared a fixed `111px`. Measured at 667x375 against the compiled stylesheet: the bar is **31.875px** around a **111px** logo, and `align-items: center` splits the overflow into 39.5625px clipped off the top of the screen and 39.5625px painted over the content row. The logo is cut through the middle of its letters.

**The ticket has this as a landscape-phone defect and it is not.** At **1440x900** — an ordinary desktop window, not a short one — the bar is 76.5px and the same 111px box still overhangs **17.25px each way**. It stops only above ~1500px of viewport height, so every real viewport had it. What is landscape-only is the *visible* clipping.

The fix gives the logo the bar's height and caps its font rather than replacing it:

```
height: 100%;
font-size: min(48px, calc(100dvh * 0.085 / 1.15));
```

`min()` picks the design size wherever it fits. At 1440x900 the font is still 48px and the text box is still `top 10.75, height 55` — **identical before and after**, and now centred in the bar exactly rather than by two errors cancelling. The cap starts binding below ~649px of viewport height, so a 1366x768 laptop is on the unchanged side of it. `line-height: 77px` went with the fixed box, being a third independent number a 31.875px bar could not hold either; the base `normal` now applies at every width.

`1.15` is **measured, not assumed** — the font box Chromium reserves per `1em` for this logo's stack, from `TextMetrics` and confirmed against a `Range` over the rendered element. Lato and its fallback both give 115 per 100px.

## The admin console — a width-only gate

`showMobileNotice = isHydrated && isMobile` is width alone, so a landscape phone is 667px wide, lands above the breakpoint, and was served the full console into a 343.125px row. The charts are the tallest fixed blocks in the repo, so what arrived was a 600px chart showing 57% of itself with its axis 305px below the fold.

`useIsViewportShorterThan` is the height half, in SCRUM-474's shape: a caller passes its **own** derived threshold and no existing layout moves. A hook rather than a `desktop-tall:`-style screen because this branch decides which subtree *mounts* — rendering both and hiding one would fire `getAllUsers` on a phone, which is the request SCRUM-452 went to some trouble to stop.

The threshold is **582px**, composed from the console's own numbers: the shortest chart it declares (500px) plus `AdminData`'s `my-4`, over the row's 91.5% share. **This is the one decision worth a reviewer's attention.** Deliberately not the tallest chart, which would put it at 691px — the notice removes a capability, so a gate set too high costs a manager on a 1366x768 laptop (~650px of viewport) a console that works for them today by scrolling. 582 clears the tallest landscape phone (430px) and that laptop with room either side, and both bounds are asserted rather than described.

Two things the notice itself assumed and no longer does, both found by measuring:

- It reserved `MOBILE_NAV_SPACE` unconditionally. `Header` renders its fixed bottom bar at mobile *width*, so a viewport arriving on the height term gets the in-flow desktop bar and the reservation was 60px of room for a bar that is not there. The height moves with it: the fixed nav takes no space in flow so `h-full` is right there, but the desktop bar is in flow at 8.5% and the notice is its sibling, so it takes the 91.5% remainder.
- The heading said "Admin needs a **wider** screen". A landscape phone is 667px wide and lands here on height alone, so that was telling the user to do the one thing that would not help.

## Corrections to the ticket

- **The overlap was a paint defect, not a stolen-click defect.** The footprint hit test came back `reachable: false`, obstructed by the content row's own button — `z-index: 10` on `HeaderDiv` is inert because the element is `position: static`. The logo painted over the row's background and *under* its controls. Less severe than Impact implies, in the safer direction.
- **`SigninLogo` is not the same defect and is deliberately untouched.** `sign-in.tsx:68` renders `Header` inside a `w-fit` card in an auto-height flex column, so `HeaderDiv`'s 8.5% has no definite containing block and resolves to `auto`. Measured: the bar computes to **111px** there and the logo overflows it by **zero**. Both halves of the header fix would be regressions on that page — `100%` collapses to the line box and halves the card's header, and a `dvh` cap shrinks a logo whose bar is not a share of the viewport. A test pins this so nobody "finishes the job".
- **The chart axis was *permanently* below the fold, not merely below it.** See SCRUM-488.

## Also here: a height term on the SCRUM-481 harness

These are its first vertical criteria, and a fixture holding a percentage height could not otherwise state the viewport its figures came from — the one number the whole measurement turns on would have lived in prose beside it. `--height` shares `--width`'s validation, `viewportHeight` is optional so a horizontal fixture need not invent one, and the banner labels a dimension the fixture never recorded rather than letting the driver's default read as a measurement. Two fixtures added: `header-logo-bar` and `admin-console-chart-fold`.

## Validation

- `yarn lint`, `yarn tsc`, `yarn check:format` clean. `yarn test` 2838 passed / 144 suites, up from 2809.
- **Measured in Chromium** against the compiled stylesheet at 667x375, 667x582, 1280x650 and 1440x900, before and after, with the figures recorded on the fixtures.
- **Mutation-tested**, because the important new assertions are negative ones. Reverting the admin gate to width-only fails 2 of the new page tests; reverting `Logo` to its fixed heights fails 3, including the fixture drift guard. Both restored and green.
- **AC 5, the selector-set diff.** The compiled CSS is **byte-identical** to `origin/main` — 744 selectors and 77853 bytes on both sides, empty diff on the selector set and on the full stylesheet.

Two notes on that last one, since both are easy to get wrong. The first attempt compiled the baseline from a `git archive` tree in `/tmp` and reported an empty diff that was **pure artifact** — a control class added to that tree never appeared in its output, so it was never scanning it; checking `origin/main` out into the worktree and compiling there is what makes the runs comparable. And the method was proved sensitive before its result was trusted: a control class in the worktree does show up as one added selector. That control is also what caught the third commit — the new fixture's axis marker was shipping one utility only it used, 39 bytes applying to nothing, which is the effect `tailwind.config.js` documents at length.

## Known limitations and risks

- **`min()` and `dvh` are runtime CSS from styled-components, so the selector-set diff cannot see the header change at all.** That half is covered by the Chromium measurements above and by stylesheet-reading unit tests, not by the CSS diff. Worth knowing when reading AC 5 as satisfied.
- `100dvh` **reconstructs** the bar's basis rather than reading it — a CSS length cannot ask its parent how tall it turned out. It is composed from the same constant the bar declares, and a test pins the composition, but a future change to the bar's *containing block* would not be caught. author: georgepapagapitos
body:
`/decks/compare` rendered two copies of the deck-detail panels side by side and left the reader to do the comparison. Reported as: *"no idea what the values mean."*

### What was actually wrong

| Symptom | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `Forest 19 → 16` | No column header named which deck each number belonged to |
| `Avg mana value 3.2 → 3.1 −0.0` | Values rounded to 1dp, delta subtracted from the raw pair |
| `White · Demand 0 · Sources 5` on a Golgari deck | Two-up mana panels rendered every colour, zero or not |
| `Distribution 74` | The colour donut's centre count with no label, on a page that never asked for it |
| `13 added · 10 removed` | Version language — B is not a revision of A |
| Bracket `—` | A missing value with no next step |
| Two `Curve balance by phase` blocks | Two charts the reader had to diff by eye |

### What it is now

- **Overlap header** — "79 of 81 cards are in both decks", a stacked bar, and a three-way legend naming both decks.
- **A \| B \| Difference tables** for totals, card types, roles, curve phases and mana base. The `thead` carries the two deck names, so no value appears without its side. `th scope="row"` / `scope="col"` give AT the same orientation.
- **One paired mana-curve chart** — two bars per mana value, keyed by colour to the deck names, replacing the two independent charts.
- **Deltas come from the displayed values**, so nothing prints `−0.0`; an unchanged value reads the word `same` (§ Money deltas' zero-reads-as-a-word rule, generalised).
- **Diff groups read "Only in \<deck>"**. `DiffGroup` gains optional `title` / `caption`; its default tone words stay for `BulkEditDeckDialog`'s resync diff, where one list genuinely *is* a revision of the other.
- **Rows that are zero on both sides are dropped**, and the unexplained Demand/Sources pair became "Cards that need it" / "Sources that make it" with one info tip.
- **"Bracket 4"**, and an unestimated deck says what to do about it.
- **Identical deck names disambiguate** to `<name> (A)` / `<name> (B)` — a deck and its copy usually share a name, which otherwise defeats the whole point.

### Guards (per the standing "a fix ships its guard" rule)

New assertions in `DeckComparePage.test.tsx`: the deck-named column headers exist, the diff-group titles name their deck, and an unchanged stat renders `same` and never a signed zero.

`STYLE_GUIDE.md` gains **"Comparing two of anything"** so the next A-vs-B surface starts from these rules.

### Verification

Full gate green — typecheck, lint (0 errors), stylelint, format:check, 9,745 tests, production build, boot budget (JS 291/410 KB, CSS 77/80 KB).

Driven in a real browser against the local `dev` account (two same-commander decks) at 1440px and 400px; the phone table was retuned so the Difference column — the reason the page exists — stays on screen rather than scrolling out of view.

author: arkadiuszneuman
body:
## Problem
On the native Android app, BLE scanning found zero devices (both filtered and unfiltered), even though Chrome's Web Bluetooth on the same phone, at the same moment, found the same heart-rate watch immediately.

## Cause
`ensureNativeBleInitialized()` called `BleClient.initialize({ androidNeverForLocation: true })`. On Android 12+ that makes the plugin request only `BLUETOOTH_SCAN`/`BLUETOOTH_CONNECT` — the documented-correct option when an app doesn't derive location from scan results. Confirmed on-device (Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra, Android 16) that `BluetoothLeScanner` silently delivers zero `onScanResult` callbacks under this permission combination, despite `BLUETOOTH_SCAN` being granted — a known category of OneUI-specific BLE scan bugs. Chrome's Web Bluetooth implementation holds location permission and isn't affected.

## Fix
Drop `androidNeverForLocation` so the plugin also requests `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` (same as classic pre-Android-12 BLE scanning always required). This should trigger a one-time location permission prompt the next time the app initializes BLE.

## Testing
`pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` clean (217/217).

Not yet re-verified on-device after this specific change (needs the user to grant the new location permission prompt) — please test after this deploys and grant Location when asked.

author: chriskellet
body:
A graphical fidelity pass over the whole game, in two parts: the world the
level is seen through, and the characters standing in it. Two colour bugs fell
out of the work along the way.

Everything here was driven from screenshots — Playwright and Chromium capturing
all six worlds before and after, plus a 3.2× sprite sheet for the cast — rather
than from reading the drawing code and hoping.

## Bugs fixed

- **The backdrop's depth was collapsing.** Hills were generated alternating
  far/near and drawn in that order, so a distant hill routinely painted over a
  near one. Most visible on Cobalt Coast, where a blue far hill sat in front of
  the green near hills.
- **Snow on a summer beach.** The snow cap was gated on `hill.far || snowy`, so
  every far hill in every world wore an alpine cap — including the hills behind
  the coast level.
- **Brick platforms ignored their theme.** They drew their mortar in the
  overworld's brown whatever world they were in, putting warm seams through
  cave rock and blue ice alike, while every other surface read `theme.mortar`.

## Atmosphere

Added as one theme-driven layer rather than more per-object detail, so a new
world gets its own look by filling in six fields:

- Three depths of backdrop, painted far first, with a horizon haze settling
  between the layers.
- One shared relief routine models hills, buttresses, stalagmites and clouds —
  clipped to whatever shape it is given, so it never needs to know the colour.
- Light in the air: sunbeams, cave-roof shafts, furnace glow — additive, and
  fading along their length.
- Weather per world: pollen, sea spray, cave motes, high wisps, snowfall,
  embers, each moved against the camera by its own depth.
- A vignette in each theme's own colour, and distant cloud banks for the sky
  levels, which had an empty horizon.
- Ground rebuilt with strata, a surface cap with real thickness, two-tone
  tufts, lit grit, and turf curling over ledge edges so a chasm reads as a hole
  rather than a missing rectangle.

## The cast

The characters were the last flat thing in the game: one red shirt, one blue
overalls, one beige face, no light direction anywhere.

- The cast now shares the same modelling routine as the backdrop. None of the
  bodies knows what colour it is, which is what lets a star-powered player
  change hue every frame and still be lit from above.
- Depth inside the sprite: the trailing arm, hand, leg and foot are painted a
  shade darker than the leading ones, the cap's peak throws a shadow across the
  forehead, and a mushroom's cap throws one onto the stem it overhangs. This,
  not extra detail, is what stops a character reading as a cut-out.
- The face: two-lobe moustache with a parting and a lit top edge, narrower
  sideburn, highlight on the nose. One flat brown ellipse beside a flat brown
  sideburn was reading as mud across the whole lower face.
- Weight: the torso rides over planted feet as it walks, and a skid leans into
  the stop.

## Cost

Measured before and after, in a tight render loop across all six worlds.

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Frame (tick + render), worst world | 0.94ms | 1.37ms |
| Frame with nine characters on screen | 1.37ms | ~1.6ms |

Against a 16.7ms budget. Some of it is paid back: viewport-sized gradients are
built once per theme instead of per frame, and ground texture is only drawn for
the stretch on screen rather than for all 900px of a ledge.

One measurement was worth chasing. Modelling each body part by clipping to it
put nine characters — the multiplayer worst case — at **2.6× the cost** of
drawing them flat (1.5ms → 4.0ms). Filling the path twice instead of
filling-then-clipping gets that back. It works because a path is fixed in
device space the moment it is built, so translating afterwards moves the
gradient and not the shape — which is what keeps one cached gradient per height
enough for every body in the game.

## Tests

156 → 170, all passing.

Two new suites. **Scenery and Atmosphere** holds the backdrop to the things
that are easy to get wrong and hard to notice: every theme must describe its
own atmosphere, the backdrop must be queued far layer first, snow only lands on
peaks meant to be snowy, the drifting weather is seeded inside the frame and
wraps back into it, and motes move against the camera by their depth rather
than all at one speed. Two of them earn their place on their own — every world
in the campaign is rendered, which catches a theme missing anything a renderer
reads, and a whole frame is drawn with `save`/`restore` counted, because canvas
state is a stack and a draw that saves without restoring corrupts every frame
after it rather than its own.

**Character Modelling** reads the drawn sprite back off a canvas: the chest must
be brighter at the top than at the hem, and the trailing hand darker than the
leading one, so neither the modelling nor the depth cue can be quietly lost to a
refactor.

Four of the new assertions were mutation-tested — the code was broken on purpose
and each one confirmed to fail. The existing hitbox-fidelity tests also still
pass, which matters here: they hold the drawn silhouette to the collision box,
so none of the shading widened a sprite past what it collides with.

author: iribarnesy
body:
Le dernier grand absent du module biotique, et le seul herbivore qui puisse **favoriser** la régénération.

## Un module à part, et pourquoi

L'issue proposait d'élargir `gibier.ts`. Après lecture, **non** : ce module est bâti de bout en bout sur le BROUTAGE — hauteur de dent, fourrage par cellule, appétence, longueur de pousse mangée — et un sanglier ne broute pas. Généraliser aurait produit une abstraction qui ne décrit ni l'un ni l'autre.

Ce qui se partage n'est pas le code mais le PATRON : densité de CONTEXTE imposée par le paysage (domaine vital de 500 à 2000 ha selon l'OFB, donc la parcelle n'a pas de population, elle en reçoit une part), répartition locale au prorata de ce que la cellule offre, comptabilité qui tient.

## Deux effets de signe opposé, aucun écrit par espèce

- **il mange ce qui tombe et reste** — les glands, les châtaignes, les noisettes ;
- **il ouvre un lit de germination** en retournant le sol, ce dont profitent les petites graines.

Mesuré sur quarante ans : **97 recrues de chêne sans sanglier, 60 à densité ordinaire, 22 sous forte densité.** Difficile, jamais impossible.

Chiffres : 2 % de la parcelle retournée par an à la densité de référence, boutis de 5 à 15 cm, activité de la mi-automne au printemps. Aucun tirage dans le flux principal — le test prouve que deux parties, l'une avec sangliers et l'autre sans, gardent le même état de RNG au bit près.

## Ce qu'on n'attend pas d'un dégât

Un boutis est un **enfouissement**, pas une destruction : la litière passe au pool lent, l'azote au pool minéral, le stock d'humus MONTE avec la densité de sangliers, et la croûte cassée rend de la porosité. Ce que le sanglier coûte est ailleurs — la terre est à nu.

## Six conclusions tombées, et ce qu'elles ont appris

Les neuf tests du lot passaient tous. La suite entière a trouvé trois erreurs :

| Symptôme | Cause |
|---|---|
| Un pin abrité par six ajoncs passe de 1,38 m à **0,92 m**, sous un pin nu | le trait portait le bon nom et pas la bonne chose : `gravite` ne dit pas le poids, il dit que la graine tombe sous sa mère — l'ajonc et le genêt y sont, avec leurs graines de 2 mm. `geai` seul est le bon marqueur |
| La callune d'une lande **disparaît entièrement** | une normalisation au prorata sans plafond : deux cellules humides sur cent étaient retournées 2,6 fois par an, indéfiniment. Le total annuel restait juste — c'est une somme |
| Le sol retourné trop vite partout | anchor tiré de porcs **féraux** de Californie et d'Argentine (7-11 %/an), sans prédateurs ni chasse. La prairie européenne donne 0,2-0,7 % ; 2 % situe un massif français entre les deux |

La première est la deuxième réutilisation ratée de la session, après `windShelterAt` : **relire la définition de ce qu'on réutilise, jamais son nom.**

Et le couperet évité pour la **troisième** fois : la consommation de la glandée soustrayait linéairement, si bien qu'à 1,8 fois la densité de référence il ne restait exactement rien. Avant c'était l'anémone à pH 4,0, puis le chêne-liège à pH 4,50. Une forme exponentielle dit « presque plus rien » sans dire « plus jamais ».

## Un résultat que personne n'a demandé

Cas de Saumos, seize graines, vingt-six ans :

| | pin | feuillus | écart |
|---|---|---|---|
| sans sanglier | 821 m² | 525 m² | **296 m²** |
| à la densité du paysage | 720 m² | 747 m² | **27 m²** |

**Le sanglier annule l'atténuation qu'apporte la plantation feuillue.** Le châtaignier est en `geai`, donc sa châtaigne se mange, donc le mélange ne se ressème pas, donc il ne referme pas le couvert, donc il n'étouffe plus la lande qui porte le feu. Un gestionnaire qui plante des feuillus contre l'incendie sans compter ses sangliers plante pour rien.

L'essai de Saumos met le sanglier de côté pour continuer de mesurer la composition seule — comme il isole déjà le voisinage semencier. L'interaction est écrite au référentiel.

## Le référentiel

**G10** et **G11** écrits en ✅. 114 ✅ / 26 🟡 / 4 ❌ sur 144.

## Vérification

**852 tests verts sur 83 fichiers**, `tsc --noEmit`, Biome et `check-boundaries.sh` propres. `tests/ecology/sanglier.test.ts` ajoute 9 tests.

Closes #73

body:
### Motivation
- Reduce O(n²) behavior in policy burst detection and avoid repeated per-policy scans that become expensive on large exports.
- Precompute and reuse parsed/normalized column values to avoid repeated `Object.keys(...).find(...)` lookups and array copying during counting.
- Move heavy analysis off the main thread and support cancellation and progress so the UI remains responsive for large inputs.
- Add deterministic benchmarks and edge-case tests to detect regressions and verify equivalence with the legacy behavior.

### Description
- Index input headers once and expose `value(row, headerIndex, names)` so column aliases are resolved with a single map lookup instead of `Object.keys(...).find(...)` on every access, and precompute `row.__*` normalized fields in `prepareRow`. (Updated `docs/js/policy-tuning.js`.)
- Replace the O(n²) burst scan with grouping by `__signature` and a two-pointer sliding window per signature via `findBurstIds`, avoiding repeated full-policy filters; also replace `countBy` concatenation with an array `push` allocation strategy. (Updated `docs/js/policy-tuning.js`.)
- Add `analyzeAsync` that batches row preparation and per-policy work with yield points, cancellation checks, and progress callbacks, and expose a dedicated worker `docs/worker/PolicyTuning.worker.js` to run analysis off the main thread. (Added worker and `analyzeAsync`.)
- Update UI to invoke analysis in the worker, show per-phase progress, and provide an English `Cancel analysis` control; ensure main thread is not blocked by heavy analysis. (Updated `docs/js/policy-tuning-ui.js` and `docs/PolicyTuningAdvisor.html`.)
- Add deterministic tests: an edge-case test that compares new sliding-window burst detection with the legacy algorithm, and a benchmark test that runs `PolicyTuning.analyze` on synthetic 40,000 and 100,000 row datasets. (Added/updated `tests/policy-tuning.test.js` and added `tests/policy-tuning-benchmark.test.js`.)
- Register the new worker in the offline cache and increment `CACHE_VERSION` in `docs/service-worker.js` to `dlp-analyzer-v43`. (Updated `docs/service-worker.js`.)

### Testing
- Static checks: `node --check docs/js/policy-tuning.js`, `node --check docs/js/policy-tuning-ui.js`, and `node --check docs/worker/PolicyTuning.worker.js` completed without syntax errors.
- Full test suite: `node --test` executed the repository tests and all tests passed (52 total), including the new equivalence and benchmark checks.
- Benchmark results (reported by the tests) show `PolicyTuning.analyze` ran the synthetic datasets in ~1370ms for 40,000 rows and ~2680ms for 100,000 rows (ratio ~1.9x), satisfying the sub-quadratic scaling guard in the benchmark.

## Summary

- **#554** — `run-scan.handler.ts` wrote `Lesson.videoPath` absolute while every reader (`derived-path.ts`, `lesson-file-locator.ts`, the column's own doc comments) already treated it as library-relative — the same convention `Material.path`/`Subtitle.path`/`Transcript.sourcePath` claim for themselves. `#529` had already patched one symptom (a generated transcript unreachable at the wire) by re-normalising at the read site instead of the write. `LibraryRelativePath` makes the convention a type: `Lesson.create()`/`reconstitute()` now require it for `videoPath`, so a future write site cannot regress to absolute the way this one did. The two `#529` normalisations are removed as dead weight. Existing rows get a hand-written SQL migration (`lesson -> section -> course -> library`) stripping each lesson's own library's `rootPath` prefix.
- **#555** — every `generated` Transcript row written before `#501` taught `LocalWhisperAdapter` to record whisper's real detected language stayed `language: 'und'` (~1945 rows on the maintainer's library), shown as "Unknown" in the CC menu. Re-transcribing is weeks of CPU; the cue text is already in the DB. `classifyTranscriptLanguage` classifies a row's own concatenated cue text (Cyrillic vs Latin majority), restricted to `en`/`ru` via `resolveDetectedLanguage` (`#501`) with a configurable default for anything else. `BackfillTranscriptLanguageCommand`/`Handler`, driven by `src/backfill-transcript-language.ts` (compiled by `nest build`, not run via `--experimental-strip-types` — `#480` already proved that trap for two other scripts), renames each row's derived `.srt` and only then updates the row (order matters — see `#529`). Dry-run by default.

Landed as two commits in this one PR — #555's rename depends on the path convention #554 fixes, so the order matters, but splitting into two PRs doubled the review/CI overhead for two tightly-coupled changes.

## Honesty about what was and wasn't run

No `course_shelf` Docker/Postgres stack exists on this machine (`docker ps` shows only unrelated projects), so none of this was exercised locally against a live DB. It has, however, now run in CI:

- **The SQL migration for #554 did apply**, indirectly confirmed: `apps/backend/Dockerfile`'s `CMD` runs `prisma migrate deploy` before the server starts, and this PR's own "E2E smoke" workflow brought up a real `postgres:18.1-alpine`, built the backend image, and the "Verify backend health" + "Seed the catalog" + "Spec contract test" steps all passed — which is only possible if every pending migration, including `20260915120000_lesson_video_path_relative`, applied cleanly. Not the same as running it against a library with real (pre-#554, absolute) `videoPath` rows to migrate, though — CI's DB is freshly seeded, so the migration's `WHERE` clause never had a matching row to rewrite there. The maintainer's own production data still needs a first `migrate deploy` to confirm on real rows.
- **The real ~1945-row #555 backfill was not executed.** `src/backfill-transcript-language.ts` was verified to boot under the real Nest DI container via a compiled `dist/` smoke run (it correctly fails only on a missing `DATABASE_URL`, proving the `#480` DI trap was avoided) — but never against real data.

Everything else (unit tests, `pnpm --filter @app/backend build`, `turbo run lint test typecheck --filter=@app/backend`) is green: 197 test files, 2143 tests. CI (lint/typecheck/test/specs/security) and E2E smoke both passed on this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `LibraryRelativePath` unit tests (`.from`/`.reconstitute`/`resolveAbsolute`/escape guard)
- [x] `Lesson` domain tests updated + new `absoluteVideoPath()` coverage
- [x] `run-scan.handler.spec.ts` updated end-to-end for the new relative-storage convention (~30 sites)
- [x] `classifyTranscriptLanguage`/`classifyScript` unit tests
- [x] `BackfillTranscriptLanguageHandler` unit tests (reclassify, ambiguous-stays-und, configurable default, dry-run, per-row error isolation)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @app/backend lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `build` all green
- [x] CI green (lint/typecheck/test/specs/security/codegen-drift)
- [x] E2E smoke green — migration applied cleanly against a real Postgres via the backend image's own `migrate deploy` entrypoint (fresh DB, no pre-existing absolute rows to rewrite)
- [ ] `migrate deploy` against the maintainer's real (pre-#554) production rows, to confirm the `UPDATE ... WHERE videoPath LIKE rootPath || '/%'` actually rewrites them — needs a real deploy, not possible from this machine
- [ ] Real `--apply` backfill run against the NAS's ~1945 `und` rows, spot-checked against the player's CC menu

Closes #554
Closes #555

author: billmal071
body:
## The bug

`version-check.yml` asked "did these FILES change", not "did the VERSION change":

```bash
if git diff --quiet "$BASE_SHA" -- $VERSION_FILES; then   # package.json app.json
```

So any PR touching `package.json` at all — a dependency, a script — was classified as a version bump and then failed on the tag the unchanged version already owns. Live example: storytime_be#590 adds one dependency and fails with *"This PR sets the version to 1.3.0, but tag v1.3.0 already exists"*.

## The fix

Read what the error asserts: **"this PR sets the version to $PKG"**, where `$PKG` is the root `package.json` version, because that is what the tag is built from. The claim is true in exactly one case — the base branch declared something else — and that is now the whole test.

`package.json`'s declared version at the base is compared with the head's:

- inside `jq`, rendered with `tojson` and compared with `cmp` on files, so a value differing only by a NUL byte or a trailing newline (the two things `$( )` silently drops) is not mistaken for equal;
- against the **merge commit's first parent**, not the event payload's `base.sha`, so a release someone else merges into the base while this PR sits open is not attributed to this PR;
- following a symlinked manifest through the base tree the way a checkout would (relative targets, `.`/`..` folded, 8-hop limit), because `git cat-file` returns the link text rather than the target;
- failing closed when the base commit cannot be resolved, or when `jq` itself cannot run — an unreadable base must not silently turn the gate off.

The composed tag name is validated with `git check-ref-format` rather than trimmed, so the tag looked up is always the tag configured, and passing that check is what makes it safe to echo.

## Deliberate behaviour changes

- **Deleting `app.json` no longer runs the tag check.** It cannot produce an untagged release, which is the harm this check exists to prevent, and the drift check still holds `app.json` to `package.json`'s version while the file exists. The old rule fired on `package.json`'s version — a version the PR had not touched.
- **`version_files` is deprecated and ignored**, default now empty, still declared so any caller passing it keeps working. No caller in the org sets it (checked all six). Nothing but root `package.json` can make this check's claim true: each caller's `release-tag.yml` reads `.version` from the root `package.json` and tags `v$VERSION` — verified, not assumed.
- **Known gap, accepted:** a base branch already sitting on a reused tag goes unreported until the next bump, instead of failing every unrelated PR until a human notices. Likewise two open PRs that both bump to the same version: once the first merges and tags, the second's bump matches the base and is skipped. A pre-merge gate cannot distinguish that from the ordinary post-release PR; the place to catch it is `release-tag.yml` refusing to skip when the existing tag does not contain the merge commit. Worth a follow-up.
- **Known gap, accepted:** if the base `package.json` is a symlink this step cannot follow (through a symlinked directory, or out of the repository root), it warns and skips rather than failing. Failing closed there would fail *every* PR in that repo with a false and unactionable message. No caller has a symlinked `package.json`.

## Test plan

Fixtures are throwaway git repos with real two-parent merge commits, running the step's `run:` block verbatim (extracted with pyyaml).

- [x] (a) dependency-only edit to `package.json` → skips the tag check (exit 0; the old step failed it)
- [x] (b) genuine bump 1.3.0 → 1.4.0, untagged → check runs and passes
- [x] (c) genuine bump 1.3.0 → 1.2.0 with `v1.2.0` present → still fails with the existing error
- [x] (d) `app.json` deleted, `package.json` untouched → skips (deliberate narrowing, above)
- [x] base `package.json` absent / malformed / two JSON documents / version carrying a NUL or a trailing newline
- [x] base branch releases 1.9.0 while a docs-only PR is open → skips
- [x] symlinked manifest: target bumped while the link is untouched → fails; `../` in the target resolves correctly; symlinked directory and root-escaping link → warn and skip; cycle → hop limit, no hang
- [x] empty / unresolvable `BASE_SHA` → runs the check rather than comparing against the index
- [x] `jq` unavailable → step fails with a message instead of passing silently
- [x] `tag_prefix` containing a newline → rejected by `git check-ref-format`; a valid 42-character prefix is not truncated
- [x] a PR-authored filename containing a newline or `::` cannot form a workflow command
- [x] `actionlint` clean; `bash -n` clean

Reviewed locally across seven rounds (CodeRabbit CLI plus independent reviewers); findings fixed in the commits above.

## Note for the caller repos

Callers pin this by SHA, so nothing changes anywhere until each caller bumps its pin. No caller pin is touched in this PR.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved version-change detection by comparing the declared package version with the base branch.
  * Version checks now correctly handle merge commits, missing or malformed manifests, symlinked manifests, and formatting differences.
  * Invalid release tag names now produce a clear validation failure.
  * Unresolvable base commits or manifests now trigger warnings and continue with the appropriate safety check.

* **Chores**
  * Deprecated the `version_files` configuration; it remains accepted for compatibility but is no longer used.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: starefossen
body:
Følger opp #879. `instructions/output-style.instructions.md` har `applyTo: "**"` og lastes på hver eneste tur. Anti-slop-seksjonen var 821 av fila sine 1625 tokens (tiktoken `o200k_base`), altså halvparten, og den var ordlister.

## Dette er en sletting, ikke en flytting

Saken antok at listene måtte flyttes til `klarsprak`. De lå der fra før. Jeg gikk gjennom hvert eneste element i anti-slop-seksjonen mot `skills/klarsprak/SKILL.md`:

| Blokk i instruksjonen | Elementer | Dekket i klarsprak |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Puffery | 16 | 16 av 16 (`### Svulstige ord og uttrykk`, som også har flere) |
| Åpnings- og avslutningsfraser | 14 | 13 av 14 |
| Retoriske mønstre | 6 | 6 av 6 |
| Strukturelle markører | 6 | 6 av 6 (`### Strukturelle mønstre` + `### Overgangsord`) |
| Tegnsetting | 5 | 5 av 5 |

Skillen har i tillegg synergi, paradigmeskifte, vitnesbyrd, vage kilder, chatbot-fraser, falske spenn, synonymveksling og reklamespråk, som instruksjonen ikke hadde.

Bare ett element manglet: «det finnes flere aspekter ved dette». Det er lagt inn. Det andre reelle hullet var at klarsprak er skrevet på norsk, mens instruksjonen sa «Language-neutral, applies to Norwegian and English alike». En linje under `## AI-markører` sier nå at markørene er de samme på engelsk, med engelske eksempler.

Skillen vokser derfor med 3 linjer, ikke med 800 tokens. Det var nødvendig: `scripts/lint-skills.sh` feiler på 5000 tokens (chars/4), og klarsprak lå på 4514. En ekte flytting hadde tatt den til rundt 5300 og brutt linten.

## Målt før og etter

tiktoken `o200k_base`, ikke bytes/4.

| Fil | Før | Etter | Diff |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `output-style.instructions.md` | 6749 B, 1625 tokens | 4785 B, 1109 tokens | **-516 tokens per tur** |
| anti-slop-seksjonen alene | 3224 B, 821 tokens | 1279 B, 305 tokens | -516 |
| `skills/klarsprak/SKILL.md` | 18533 B, 5430 tokens | 18842 B, 5507 tokens | +77, og bare når skillen lastes |

Lint-tallet for klarsprak (body chars/4, som linten bruker): 4514 til 4591. Advarselsgrensa er 4500 og var allerede passert før denne endringa. Feilgrensa på 5000 er ikke i nærheten.

## Hva som blir stående, og hvorfor

Tegnsettingsreglene er ikke ordlister, de er fem regler på 69 tokens, og `norwegian-text.instructions.md` peker eksplisitt på dem: «Kolon på slutten av overskrifter er forbudt av `output-style.instructions.md`». Å slette dem ville brutt den krysshenvisninga.

Stubben som erstatter listene:

```markdown
## Anti-slop

The AI-marker lists live in the `klarsprak` skill: puffery, opening and closing
formulas, rhetorical patterns and structural tells, with the rewrite for each.
**Load `klarsprak` before writing or editing prose a human will read**:
documentation, README, ADR, commit message, PR description, issue, review comment,
and any chat answer longer than a couple of paragraphs. The lists are written in
Norwegian, but the markers are the same in English. Scrub both. Norwegian spelling
and compound-word minimums live in `norwegian-text.instructions.md`.

Recognise these four without the skill. Any one of them means the text needs the
full wash:

- A word that praises instead of describing: robust, seamless, banebrytende, helhetlig.
- An opening that delays the point: "it is worth noting", "i dagens verden".
- A closing that repeats the text above it: "in conclusion", "oppsummert kan man si at".
- Symmetry that was not in the facts: "not only X, but also Y", three nouns in series.
```

## Hva dette koster

AI-markørvasken slutter å være automatisk på hver tur. Den skjer når `klarsprak` lastes.

Det er en reell nedgradering, ikke en ren gevinst. Tidligere lå listene i kontekst uansett hva agenten skrev. Nå må agenten selv kjenne igjen at den skriver menneskerettet tekst og hente skillen. Stubben er hele mitigeringa: derfor står triggeren først, derfor er lista over teksttyper eksplisitt, og derfor står fire tells igjen, så agenten kan kjenne igjen at teksten trenger vask uten å ha lista i hodet.

De fire er valgt som de vanligste, ikke som en komplett liste. En markør utenfor de fire går gjennom hvis skillen ikke lastes. Om det skjer i praksis er ikke målt.

## Kjørt

```
gofmt -l .                          rent
go vet ./...                        rent
go test ./...                       ok, alle 9 pakker
staticcheck ./...                   rent
generate-docs --check               All docs are in sync with customizations
scripts/lint-skills.sh              33 skills, 1 advarsel (klarsprak, fra før)
```

Lukker ingenting. #879 har flere punkter igjen (`deliberate-ai-use.instructions.md` og personaen).

Resolves [The metric line when two plugins have something to say](https://github.com/nodqora/nodqora/issues/107), on the map [Tier 1 finished, and the bar for Community 1.0](https://github.com/nodqora/nodqora/issues/102).

- The metric line becomes a **strip of at most three captioned figures**, ranked by key (`ready`, `rate`, `lag`, `mean`, `tasks`), with the rest counted as `+N more`.
- The phrase table lives in the **frontend, keyed by metric key and never by plugin**.
- A node only Prometheus observes reads **`measured 45s ago`**, never beside the health glyph.
- Amends ADR-0018.

The prototype the choice was made on is on the throwaway branch `prototype/metric-line-two-plugins` (four variants, `?variant=A|B|C|D`, `?scenario=incident`). It is not for merging.
