author: alicia5574188-del
body:
Research-only audit. No production strategy, PAPER state, LIVE state, credentials, or deployment files are changed.

Hypothesis: frozen `tide_relay:2` shows a persistent positive pre-friction edge across discovery/validation/evaluation, but the modeled 14bp round-trip friction exceeds its average edge. This audit does not assume maker fills or reduce costs. It freezes the original detector/exits and tests only five predeclared, entry-time structural opportunity/cost-burden thresholds.

Selection discipline: discovery ranks the predeclared thresholds; only the top two may enter validation; the highest discovery-score validation survivor is locked; evaluation is computed only for that locked threshold. Base parity must exactly reproduce the existing 44-month frozen tide-relay counts and metrics before any result is valid.

This PR is draft and has no production authority.

author: adamsilverstein
body:
Fixes https://github.com/adamsilverstein/my-skills/issues/32

_Claude did the digging and the typing on this one:_

> `feature-status.sh` built its compare ref from the bare head branch name, which 404s for any PR from a fork. `gh api` prints the error body on stdout, so the old `|| echo FALLBACK` appended a second JSON object to the error body and the caller parsed the pair as one value.
>
> Qualifying the head as `OWNER:BRANCH` from `headRepositoryOwner` resolves the fork's branch, and the qualified form is valid for same-repo branches too, so there is no fork/no-fork branch in the code. The response shape is validated rather than the exit code trusted, and a compare that genuinely fails now warns on stderr instead of reporting null counts silently.
>
> A note in SKILL.md covers the matching gap in `cascade-update.sh`: it only sees branches in `origin`, so a fork PR in a stack exits 2 rather than being carried up. That is a limitation worth reporting to the user, not something the script should paper over.
>
> ## Types of changes
>
> - Qualify the compare head ref with `headRepositoryOwner.login`.
> - Validate the compare response shape, and warn on stderr when it fails.
> - Document that the cascade cannot update branches that live in a fork.
>
> ## How this was tested
>
> Against the live API, since the bug is in how the request is built.
>
> Cross-fork and same-repo PR together, which is the case that used to produce invalid JSON:
>
> ```
> $ feature-status.sh WordPress/gutenberg 77484 79864 | jq -c '.prs[] | {number, behind_by, ahead_by}'
> {"number":77484,"behind_by":1379,"ahead_by":14}
> {"number":79864,"behind_by":0,"ahead_by":37}
> ```
>
> Before the change #77484 reported `null` for both; before the fallback guard it crashed the caller outright.
>
> The qualified and unqualified refs were checked against each other for a same-repo branch and agree, so the single code path is not costing anything:
>
> ```
> $ gh api "repos/WordPress/gutenberg/compare/trunk...try/notes-in-canvas-margin" --jq '{ahead_by, behind_by}'
> {"ahead_by":37,"behind_by":0}
> $ gh api "repos/WordPress/gutenberg/compare/trunk...WordPress:try/notes-in-canvas-margin" --jq '{ahead_by, behind_by}'
> {"ahead_by":37,"behind_by":0}
> ```
>
> Full 11-PR suggestion-mode stack as a regression check: all counts sane, nothing on stderr, 11s wall clock.
>
> The failure path was exercised by pointing a copy of the script at a head owner that does not exist. It warns on stderr, leaves `ahead_by`/`behind_by` null, and stdout stays valid JSON:
>
> ```
> WARNING: compare trunk...nope-does-not-exist:try/notes-in-canvas-margin failed for #79864; ahead_by/behind_by unknown
> ```

## AI Use

Claude Code did the typing here, I did the asking. I will review and test.

- [ ] **Tier 2** — Sub-feature / technical task (part of a larger feature)

AGR-1259

## Tier 3 — Refactor / small change

### What & why

`idle` is a canonical value of the standard `mode` / `hvac_mode` attributes (a thermostat with no current heating or cooling demand), but the shared HVAC-mode vocabulary had no entry for it, so fleet chips, inline values and the history timeline showed the raw `idle` key. This adds the `idle` entry (fr "Veille", en "Idle"), an icon and a semantic colour. Every renderer that goes through `common.hvacMode` picks it up without further changes.

Regression test: `apps/ui/src/components/AttributeValue.spec.tsx` — "renders the idle mode with an icon and a translated label".

None expected: additive entries in the locale files, the icon map, the label-key map and the colour registry. Values without an entry still render raw, as before.

author: caulshiver
body: Jotline’s writing app, vault I/O, settings merge, and CLI were concentrated in a few oversized modules with mixin inheritance and duplicated view/action CRUD. This refactor keeps the same user-facing behavior while giving each concern a single owner. ## What changed - `app.py` is under 1k lines. Palette, prompts, preview/find screens, and command records live in `modal.py`, `screens.py`, and `commands.py`. - Mixin inheritance is gone. `Views`, `ActionWorkflows`, `Workflows`, `Encryption`, `Review`, and `RecoveryImport` are bound onto `Jotline` without an MRO. - Saved views and action recipes are typed (`SavedView`, `ActionStep`). Views own view CRUD; action workflows own recipes, including JSON-from-buffer save. - Settings merge uses a per-instance `_baseline` instead of a process-global table, so `replace()` and Preferences keep the last published values. - Filesystem primitives (`create_private_temp`, `publish_new`, lock/read helpers) live in `filesystem.py`. Shared size/scan budgets live in `limits.py`. `store.py` re-exports the names tests monkeypatch. - Vault scans once per sidebar refresh (`notes=` on search/backlinks). Wiki links, task toggles, and Markdown format transforms have canonical helpers. Encryption UI calls `Vault.set_encrypted` for existing notes. - CLI doctor/IO are split out of `cli.py`. `Palette` / `TextPrompt` remain importable from `jotline.app`. `check_managed_directory` is still exported from `jotline.cli` for Windows junction checks. ## Validation - `python3 -m pytest -q`: **552 passed, 30 skipped** (Linux) - GitHub Actions: **18/18 checks passed** on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows for Python 3.11–3.13 ## Compatibility Note files, settings JSON, shortcuts, and the public CLI stay the same. No migration is required. Tests that import `Palette`/`TextPrompt` from `jotline.app` or monkeypatch `jotline.store.create_private_temp` / `publish_new` keep working.

author: amoabakelvin
body:
`set_docker_hosts` and `set_coolify_hosts` replace the whole list, so two agents or admins reading and saving around the same time meant the later write dropped the earlier one. `GET /settings` now returns a `revision` per hosts section, and the PUT rejects with 409 if it no longer matches.

The revision is a hash of the stored list, so it is per section and survives restarts. It is optional on the HTTP endpoint to keep old clients working, and required on the two MCP tools since agents are the writers most likely to race. The web UI sends it too.

Only the host lists needed this. Auth and API token updates already mutate under the manager lock.

author: 1morr
body:
## 起因

播放中停用 FMP 指定的輸出裝置時，AO 失敗會分兩條路走：一條正確地出
`t.audio.audioOutputFailed` 的 toast，另一條被 premature-end 當成「這條串流提
前結束」而排了一次重試。重試撞上同一個壞掉的裝置，最後留下一行
`Retry playback succeeded` 而實際上完全沒有聲音（issue #106）。

**兩條訊息誰先到是量出來的，不是推出來的。** 修之前在 Windows 上重現（2026-09-15，
系統預設是 Creative Stage SE，FMP 指定 Realtek(R) Audio，播放中停用它）：

```
23:20:56.224 [D] [MediaKitAudioService] Track completed: EndedPrematurely(at: 0:01:33.416804, expected: 0:05:40.822494)
23:20:56.225 [W] [AudioController] Track ended before its natural end; scheduling retry: at=0:01:33.416804, expected=0:05:40.822494
23:20:56.228 [E] [MediaKitAudioService] media_kit ao error: Failed to initialize audio driver 'wasapi'
23:20:57.228 [I] [AudioController] Retrying playback for: RAYE, Amma, Absolutely - 'Joy.' (Official Video), savedPosition: 0:01:33.416804
23:21:06.727 [E] [AudioController] Audio output device failed: Could not open/initialize audio device -> no sound.
23:21:07.296 [I] [AudioController] Retry playback succeeded for: RAYE, Amma, Absolutely - 'Joy.' (Official Video)
```

mpv 先宣告 completed，4ms 後才吐第一條 `ao` 錯誤 —— 也就是說單靠「裝置失敗之後
不再排重試」擋不住，重試那時候已經排好了。

## 修法

`AudioController` 多兩個「請求世代 + 當前歌曲」標記（沿用 `lib/services/audio/AGENTS.md`
那條「重試抑制必須是世代與當前歌曲感知的」），兩個方向各擋一種順序：

- `_outputDeviceFailure` —— 裝置失敗之後，同一個世代與歌曲的 premature-end 不
  再排重試，連那行 `scheduling retry` 都不印。
- `_prematureEndRetry` —— 已排定但還沒起跑的 premature-end 重試；裝置失敗時把
  它收回（`_resetRetryState()`），這是實機那個順序真正需要的那一半。

不新增協作者：兩個標記要讀的 `PlaybackRequestSession` 世代與 `_playingTrack` 都
只有控制器拿得到。重試起跑會換一個 requestId，所以標記不必手動清 —— 使用者換歌
或重按播放時抑制就自動失效。

`test/support/audio_provider_size_static_rule_test.dart` 的上限跟著從 2,160 調
到 2,178，理由寫在該常量的 dartdoc 裡。

## 沒有做：自動切回 `AudioDevice.auto()`

#41 建議修法的第 2 點（裝置掛掉時自動改用系統預設裝置重試）**這次刻意沒做**。
它是產品決定而不是 bug 修正：做了能無縫接到系統預設裝置，但也等於在使用者沒有
要求的情況下把聲音送到另一個喇叭；不做則維持現在的「停止並提示」。

要做的話大致是：`MediaKitAudioService` 收到 AO 失敗時呼叫一次既有的
`setAudioDeviceAuto()`，把使用者的裝置偏好標記成「暫時被覆寫」而不是改寫它，
再決定什麼時候切回去（裝置重新出現時？還是等使用者自己選？）—— 那是另一張
issue 的範圍。

本 PR 只解 issue #106 標題講的那兩件事（多餘的重試與誤導的日誌），所以這張 PR
直接關掉它；自動 fallback 若要做，請另開一張新的 issue。

電台路徑的「RadioController 自己重連一次」同樣沒有動：那是 RadioController 的
重連邏輯，不是 `_onPlaybackEnded` 的 premature-end 重試（電台擁有播放時，
`_onPlaybackEnded` 對 `OutputDeviceFailed` 以外的結束原因本來就早退）。

## 測試

新增 `test/services/audio/audio_controller_output_device_failure_test.dart`，三條：

1. **實機順序**（premature end 先、裝置失敗後）—— 排好的重試被收回；睡過那個
   1 秒的重試計時器之後，fake 上沒有第二次 `playMedia` / `setMedia` / `playUrl`，
   日誌沒有 `Retrying playback for` 也沒有 `Retry playback succeeded`，toast 只
   有一則。
2. **反過來的順序**（裝置失敗先）—— 連 `scheduling retry` 都不會印。
3. **世代邊界** —— 使用者重按播放（換一個世代）之後，premature-end 仍然正常重試。

只用 `pumpUntil` / `drainEventQueue`，沒有 `pumpEventQueue`。

- `flutter test test/services/audio test/services/radio test/support` → 426 passed
- `flutter analyze` → No issues found
- `dart format lib test tool` → 594 files, 0 changed

## Windows 實機驗證

從本 worktree `flutter run -d windows`，在播放器裝置選單選 `Realtek(R) Audio`
（系統預設是 `Creative Stage SE`），播 YouTube 曲目，再到 `mmsys.cpl` → 播放 →
右鍵 → 停用 該裝置。修好之後的日誌（`%USERPROFILE%\Documents\FMP\logs\fmp.log`）：

```
23:40:37.110 [D] [MediaKitAudioService] Track completed: EndedPrematurely(at: 0:00:24.656714, expected: 0:04:46.209160)
23:40:37.111 [W] [AudioController] Track ended before its natural end; scheduling retry: at=0:00:24.656714, expected=0:04:46.209160
23:40:37.113 [I] [AudioController] Scheduling retry 1/5 for: Slipknot - Arsenal [OFFICIAL VIDEO]
23:40:37.114 [E] [MediaKitAudioService] media_kit ao error: Failed to initialize audio driver 'wasapi'
23:40:37.115 [E] [AudioController] Audio output device failed: Failed to initialize audio driver 'wasapi'
23:40:37.115 [W] [AudioController] Output device failed; cancelling the premature-end retry
23:40:37.121 [E] [AudioController] Audio output device failed: Could not open/initialize audio device -> no sound.
23:40:37.152 [D] [WindowsDesktopService] [WindowsDesktopService] Tray menu updated
```

**那之後日誌就停了** —— 1 秒後的重試計時器過去 70 秒都沒有動，整份檔案裡不再出
現 `Retrying playback for` 或 `Retry playback succeeded`。toast 是
「音訊輸出裝置無法使用，播放已停止」一則，播放鍵翻回 ▶（已暫停）。

重複一次（23:43:43）結果相同：`Scheduling retry 1/5` 之後緊接
`Output device failed; cancelling the premature-end retry`，沒有任何重試。

收尾：`mmsys.cpl` 裡把 `Realtek(R) Audio` 重新啟用（回到「就緒」），FMP 的裝置
選單設回「自動（跟隨系統）」並以截圖確認。

**沒有做的部分**：電台情境沒有實機覆測 —— 需要在使用者的正式資料庫裡新增再刪除
一個直播電台，而這條路徑的行為本來就不受本次改動影響（電台擁有播放時
premature-end 根本走不到重試）。

Closes #106

body:
Closes #211.

## Problem

The Slack client shows at a glance that a teammate is in a meeting, on vacation, in Do Not Disturb or in a huddle. slk showed only the online/away dot for DM peers, so none of that was visible.

This PR shows custom status and huddle indicators on DM rows, next to message authors (main pane and threads), in the channel finder, and in an open DM's header. DND replaces the presence marker on DM rows and finder results and also appears in the DM header; Slack does not show it beside message authors.

**It reverses one existing contract, so that first.** `dnd_updated_user` was dispatched to the self-DND handler together with `dnd_updated`, and `TestDispatchWebSocketDNDUpdatedUserEvent_NoDND` asserted that. The event is about another user, so routing it there would let a teammate's DND change slk's own status-bar segment. It now goes to a new `OnUserDNDChange`, and one that names no user is dropped (`internal/slack/events.go:452`). The old test became `TestDispatchWebSocketDNDUpdatedEvent_NoDNDActive` for `dnd_updated`. The event was never seen on the socket in the captures below, so this was latent rather than something users hit.

## How Slack reports other users' state

Measured from debug logs of real sessions (counts only):

- The browser-protocol socket does not push other users' `user_change`. Over 12 hours of one workspace, every `user_change` and `user_status_changed` came from a single user, the signed-in one as far as the log can tell.
- Other users' profile changes arrive as `user_invalidated` (328 events across 65 users in those 12 hours) and DND changes as `dnd_invalidated`. Both carry only `{type, event_ts, user:{id}}`, so the client has to refetch.
- `huddle_state` is `in_a_huddle` during a huddle and `default_unset` otherwise, with `huddle_state_expiration_ts` about 22 minutes after joining. `user_invalidated` arrived for every huddle join observed, but for one of two huddle endings no event arrived at all.

## Changes

**Events.** `user_change` / `user_status_changed` decode the status and huddle fields into a `UserStatus` (`internal/slack/events.go:463`). `user_invalidated` / `dnd_invalidated` hand the ID to the handler (`internal/slack/events.go:471`). `SlackAPI` gains only `GetDNDTeamInfoContext`.

**Refetch.** `peerStatusRefresher` (`cmd/slk/peer_status.go:56`) coalesces invalidations for 2 s into one call to the existing `userResolver.ResolveNow` (edge users/info, at most 80 IDs per request, `internal/slack/edge/cache.go:45`), which already writes the cache and emits the status for every user it returns. Users it does not return, including all of them when edge is degraded or the call fails, are refetched one at a time over users.info (`cmd/slk/peer_status.go:177`). Both paths end in exactly one status message per user; the users.info side goes through `applyProfileStatus` (`cmd/slk/peer_status.go:201`). It refetches only users already in the cache and never the signed-in user, whose own events carry the state. Users last seen in a huddle are refetched every minute until a result says the huddle ended (`cmd/slk/peer_status.go:37`, `cmd/slk/peer_status.go:255`).

The first-sight resolver persists and emits the status and huddle fields when an unknown message author becomes visible (`cmd/slk/main.go:464`, `cmd/slk/main.go:654`), and so does the per-user fallback of the unresolved-DM sweep (`cmd/slk/main.go:2995`, `cmd/slk/main.go:3024`).

**DND.** `dnd.teamInfo` requests are split at Slack's documented 50-user limit; a failed batch leaves only its own users unknown (`cmd/slk/peer_status.go:282`). Within a burst of invalidations, DND is refreshed before the per-user profile fallback, with a 2 s bound, so a slow users.info call cannot hold it up (`cmd/slk/peer_status.go:153`). DM peers' DND is fetched on connect (`cmd/slk/main.go:4116`), because the socket replays nothing, and after a workspace switch. The switch itself does not wait for it: `WorkspaceSwitchedMsg.RefreshPeerDND` (`internal/ui/msgs.go:293`, built at `cmd/slk/main.go:2075`) is appended to the switch reducer's batch after `ResetPresence` has cleared the previous workspace's live state (`internal/ui/reducer_workspace.go:390`), and its results carry the team ID, so a result that arrives while another workspace is active is dropped.

Request volume: one `ResolveNow` per burst of invalidations (plus one users.info call per user it misses, which is every user in the burst while edge is degraded), one `dnd.teamInfo` per 50 DM peers at connect and switch, one call per 50 users in a `dnd_invalidated` burst, and one refetch per minute only while someone is in a huddle.

**Cache.** `users` gains `status_emoji`, `status_text`, `status_expiration`, `huddle_state` and `huddle_expiration`. Conditional revalidation only returns users whose version moved, so users cached before the columns existed would never be refetched to fill them: the migration zeroes `users.version` once for the status columns and once for the huddle columns, whenever any column of that group is missing, and does so before adding them, so an interrupted migration resets again on the next start (`internal/cache/db.go:265`, `internal/cache/db.go:290`). **Blast radius:** the first start after upgrading refetches every cached user once.

`UpsertUser` writes the new columns on insert but not on conflict (`internal/cache/users.go:40`), because several callers upsert placeholder records that carry no profile and would blank a real status. `EdgeUserUpdate` always writes them, empty included: unlike `image_original`, users/info carries these keys empty when nothing is set.

**UI.** A new `internal/ui/peerstatus` package decides expiry, glyph resolution and the DM header summary once for all four surfaces. The status emoji resolves through `emoji.CodeMap` after `StripSkinTone`; a custom workspace emoji or a text-only status shows 💬, and 🎧 takes the emoji's place during a huddle.

- DM rows start from the cached status, both at startup and when a DM opens mid-session (`seedDMFromCache`, `cmd/slk/channelitem.go:15`, called at `cmd/slk/main.go:2743` and `cmd/slk/main.go:4951`).
- Sidebar: `statusByUser` follows `presenceByUser`'s contract of surviving `SetItems` rebuilds (`internal/ui/sidebar/model.go:979`). `⊘` replaces the presence dot during DND, and the emoji's width is charged to the name budget so long names truncate instead of wrapping.
- Channel finder: statuses live in a map keyed by channel ID (`internal/ui/channelfinder/model.go:68`) rather than on `channelfinder.Item`, fed from the sidebar when a workspace becomes active (`internal/ui/presence.go:305`) and on every change, and pruned to the current rows (`internal/ui/channelfinder/model.go:88`). The glyph is charged to the name's budget the same way as in the sidebar (`internal/ui/channelfinder/model.go:640`).
- Message and thread panes: the emoji follows the author name (`internal/ui/messages/model.go:1466`), and the render cache is only invalidated when that user authored something in the pane.
- The presence reducer handles the new messages (`internal/ui/presence.go:195`), updates the header of every window showing the DM, not only the focused one (`internal/ui/presence.go:329`), and runs a once-a-minute expiry tick only while some status, DND or huddle has a deadline (`internal/ui/presence.go:349`).

**Docs.** `wiki/Features.md` and `docs/STATUS.md` describe the indicators. The "Not planned" line in `wiki/Tradeoffs-and-Non-Goals.md` now says joining or starting huddles, since slk shows who is in one. `AGENTS.md` lists `slack.DNDStateFromStatus` and `ui/peerstatus` in the shared-helper table.

## Ordering with #210, #212 and #162, and the refactor plan

**#210 should merge first.** This branch does not include it and does not need it to build, but refetches preload avatars mid-session, which made that kitty interleaving bug frequent enough that avatars showed other images.

**#212 conflicts on one import line.** A trial merge against #2

author: mdfarhankc
body:
## Summary

First of three PRs for the 0.16.0 security release. Fixes the high-severity findings from the security audit, each with a regression test that fails on `main`. One of them uncovered a further flaw in refresh-token reuse detection, which is fixed here too.

## Changes

- **OAuth login CSRF (breaking):** the `state` is now bound to the client that started the login, as RFC 9700 requires. `/authorize` returns a `binding`; `/callback` requires it (422 missing, 400 mismatch). Frontends must store the binding and send it back; migration notes are in the CHANGELOG and the frontend guide.
- **Session revocation:** logout, device revoke, revoke-others, password change, and password reset now invalidate access tokens already issued to those sessions, by blacklisting the session family. No schema change.
- **Refresh-token reuse detection:** with the blacklist on, a replayed refresh token was rejected at decode and never revoked the family, so a thief who refreshed first kept the session. Reuse now revokes the family and its access tokens.
- **Lockout bypass:** failures were counted per casing of the email; lockout now keys on the normalised email.
- **`PATCH /me`:** updates are validated against the user schema before writing; previously constraint-violating values were persisted and the request then returned 500.
- **Timing enumeration:** duplicate registrations do the same password hash as new ones, and `after_register` plus the two email hooks run as background tasks after the response.

## Test plan

- [x] All existing tests pass (478 passed, 9 skipped)
- [x] New tests added for new functionality: a regression test per finding, each confirmed to fail before its fix
- [x] Lint and format clean (`ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .`)
- [x] `mypy --strict fastapi_fullauth` clean
- [x] `mkdocs build --strict` clean
- [x] Touched test modules pass on Python 3.10

author: geruh
body:
fixes #8831

`BlobFile` forwarded each small sequential read to storage, making file-like consumers expensive on object stores.

This adds a 4 MiB `BufferedReader` at the Python file interface, allocated on the first sequential read. Unused handles don't allocate the buffer. `buffer_size=0` keeps reads unbuffered.

`read_range` and `read_ranges` bypass the buffer without moving the cursor. Callers loading complete blobs across many rows should continue to use `read_blobs` for batched reads.

## Testing

* Ruff checks on the three changed Python files.
* Isolated BlobFile tests covering read coalescing, lazy allocation, `read1` / `TextIOWrapper`, seeks, and range reads after a partial sequential read.
* The 4 MiB default has not been benchmarked against object storage.

cc: @wjones127

author: dholbach
body:
## What does this change?

You asked to squash. **I tried that first and it made things worse**, so this resets instead. Both measured:

| Approach | Files | Lines |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Today | 35 | 4,388 |
| `squashmigrations` | 36 | **6,591** ❌ |
| Reset (this PR) | **3** | **1,003** ✅ |

**Why squashing fails here:** four interleaved `RunPython` operations act as optimizer barriers. Django collapsed *353 operations to 349* — four — and emitted a 2,203-line file which, per its own output, must sit **alongside** the original 4,388 until every install has applied it. That's 6,591 lines to fix a complaint about 4,388.

**The reset** keeps one generated `0001_initial` plus the two data migrations a fresh database genuinely needs — the GebüH Ziffern seed and the cache table. The two historical data fixes are dropped: retiring the missing-session-log tag and migrating supervision notes into `SupervisionItem`s are both no-ops on a fresh DB and ran long ago on existing ones. It also clears out a merge migration and a duplicated `0015` left from an old branch collision.

## A ruff bug found along the way

The first pass landed `0001_initial` at 3,106 lines instead of 806. Cause: **`pyproject.toml` has excluded `*/migrations/*` all along, but ruff does not apply `exclude` to paths passed explicitly on the command line unless `force-exclude` is set** — and `.githooks/pre-commit` passes staged files explicitly.

So the hook reformatted migrations the config says to leave alone, while CI's `ruff format --check .` (discovery-based, exclusion honoured) never looked at those files. Nothing could flag the divergence from either side.

Fixed with `force-exclude = true`, which repairs every invocation at once rather than patching the hook and leaving the same trap for the next caller. The hook now reports `No Python files found under the given path(s)` for a migrations-only commit.

`./dev.py format` was **never** affected — it runs `ruff format .`, which is discovery-based, so the exclusion already held there. Verified by running it and confirming the files are byte-identical afterwards.

## Privacy check

- [x] No real names, contact details, or practice data in code, tests, fixtures, or commit messages
- [x] Fictional data uses placeholder names (`Max Mustermann`, `AB-1`, `mail@example.com`)

## Testing

- [x] `./dev.py test --fast` — full Django + JS suites pass, re-run against the final compact file. The test runner builds its database from these migrations, so a wrong schema fails here.
- [x] `./dev.py lint` — clean
- [x] `makemigrations --check` — no model drift

Schema equivalence verified rather than assumed:

- **678 schema facts compared** — every column (type, length, precision, nullability, default), every index, every constraint — between a fresh install and a database built from the original 35 migrations. **Identical.** A raw `pg_dump` diff shows ~114 lines, all of it physical column ordering, which is exactly why the comparison runs against `information_schema` and `pg_constraint`.
- **In-place upgrade rehearsed** on a fully-migrated database with a canary row planted before switching migration sets. Canary intact, row counts unchanged, resulting schema identical to a fresh install.
- **AST comparison** between the schema-verified file and the final regenerated compact one: the only delta is import ordering, from the isort pass `ruff check --fix` had applied. No operation, field or option differs — so the schema verification carries over rather than needing a re-run. (This check is the reason the difference was caught at all; the two files are not byte-identical.)
- All throwaway databases dropped afterwards.

## Notes for reviewer

**Upgrading needs nothing special — a plain `migrate` does it.** No `--fake-initial`, no manual step. The replaced `0001` was also named `0001_initial`, so Django reads it as already applied and plans only `0002` and `0003`, both idempotent (`get_or_create` and `createcachetable`). Stale `0004`–`0034` rows in `django_migrations` are ignored. Rehearsed, not reasoned.

**For the release notes:** self-hosters have nothing to do. Worth stating explicitly, since a migration reset is the kind of change people expect to need manual intervention for.

**The rationale lives in `0001_initial`'s docstring**, not just here — including why squashing was rejected, so nobody re-attempts it in a year and rediscovers the 349-operation result.

**One-way door:** the pre-reset migrations are gone from `main` after this. They remain in git history, and any database that hasn't applied through `0034` would need an older tag checked out first. Yours is at `0034`; an unknown self-hoster on an older version would need that note, which is why the constraint is written into the docstring.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: assay-worker-app[bot]
body:
## What

`deskdisposition sweep -R <owner/name>` listed a repo's open changes by shelling
`gh pr list`, whatever forge actually served the repo. On a GitLab project that slug is
not a GitHub repository, so the call answered `Could not resolve to a Repository with the
name '<owner/name>'` and the verb reported the project's WHOLE queue as could-not-check
(exit 6). A GitLab adopter's orphan sweep could therefore never look at all — and an
unreadable queue that reads as an empty one is exactly the failure the verb's three-state
exists to prevent.

The sweep now reads through the forge that SERVES the repo, via the enumerated
`ListOpenChanges` op: GitHub pull requests, GitLab merge requests. No new op was added to
the frozen surface — `ListOpenChanges` landed with the bulk board read and is implemented
on both backends. The sweep classifies on number, title and labels only, and GitLab's
degraded open-change shape serves all three for real, so nothing is approximated.

Identity is unmoved. This is a READ under the session-role App token the tool already
minted for its `read` verb; `set`'s writes still shell to `gh` under the caller's ambient
identity, because routing a write through the seam changes WHO performs it — a
token-custody question this change does not open. The tool's forge-CLI register row is now
write-only and says so, and the ratchet ceiling is unchanged at 6.

Truncation reporting is preserved and sharpened: the warning now names which ceiling
clipped the page (the forge read's own cap, or `--limit`) instead of only `--limit`.

## Fail-first

Both changed behaviour tests were run against the pre-fix `verbs.go` (restored from the
commit this branch was cut from), with the new test file in place:

```
$ git show HEAD:tools/desk/cmd/deskdisposition/verbs.go > cmd/deskdisposition/verbs.go
$ go test ./cmd/deskdisposition/ -run 'TestSweepReadsGitLabMergeRequests|TestSweepClassifiesFromTheIndex|TestSweepFailureIsCouldNotCheckNotEmpty' -count=1 -timeout 120s

--- FAIL: TestSweepClassifiesFromTheIndex (0.01s)
    deskdisposition_test.go:250: want exit 0, got 6: could-not-check  medici-finance/assay  PR list unparseable — this repo's queue is UNKNOWN, not empty
        ERR: sweep: could-not-check for medici-finance/assay: unexpected end of JSON input
--- FAIL: TestSweepReadsGitLabMergeRequests (0.01s)
    deskdisposition_test.go:322: a GitLab project's queue must be READABLE, not UNKNOWN (#1123); got exit 6: could-not-check  medici-finance/assay  PR list read failed — this repo's queue is UNKNOWN, not empty
        ERR: sweep: could-not-check for medici-finance/assay: gh pr list -R medici-finance/assay --state open --limit 100 --json number,title,labels: exit status 1 (stub-failure)
FAIL
```

That second failure IS the reported defect, reproduced: the pre-fix sweep sends
`gh pr list` at a GitLab project and reports the queue UNKNOWN. The third case
(`TestSweepFailureIsCouldNotCheckNotEmpty`) is a control that holds on both sides — it
pins that neither a failed forge resolution nor a failed list read may ever print as an
empty queue — so its two new sub-cases are stated as controls, not as fail-first evidence.

## Tests

| Test | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `TestSweepReadsGitLabMergeRequests` | a GitLab project's queue is READABLE: a REAL `GitLabForge` against an `httptest` instance serving the project merge-requests endpoint, so the backend's own mapping (MR iid to number, flat GitLab labels, draft-prefix strip) is exercised rather than a double. Asserts the classification per MR, that the read hit the merge-requests endpoint, and that no `gh pr list` was constructed even though an ambient `gh` stub is installed and failing. |
| `TestSweepClassifiesFromTheIndex` | GitHub regression: the same three-state classification through `ListOpenChanges`, exactly ONE open-change read per repo (the N+1 fan-out that trips secondary rate limits), zero writes, and now zero shell-outs of any kind. |
| `TestSweepFailureIsCouldNotCheckNotEmpty` | the three-state control, widened to both halves of the read — forge resolution failure, list-read failure, and a nil result — each exit 6 with "UNKNOWN, not empty". |

Green after the fix:

```
$ go test ./cmd/deskdisposition/ -count=1 -timeout 180s
ok  github.com/medici-finance/assay/tools/desk/cmd/deskdisposition  0.395s
$ go test ./internal/forgeban/ -count=1 -timeout 180s
ok  github.com/medici-finance/assay/tools/desk/internal/forgeban  0.224s
$ go test ./internal/deskkit/ -run 'TestNoForgeCLIShellout|TestForgeNoPassthrough|TestForgeSingleConstructionSite' -count=1 -timeout 300s
ok  github.com/medici-finance/assay/tools/desk/internal/deskkit  0.536s
```

`TestNoForgeCLIShellout` reports 10 shipped forge-CLI call sites across 6 registered
declarations (ceiling 6) — one site fewer than before, the row retained because `set`
still shells. `go test ./cmd/deskclose/` (the tool that consumes `deskdisposition read`)
is green. Per the bounded-run rule these are targeted package runs with explicit
timeouts; the whole-module matrix is CI's.

## Also updated

- `docs/streams/forge-gitlab/inventory.md` — op 23 (`ListOpenChanges`) records its second
  consumer, and the "no enumerated op" class no longer lists `pr list` for this tool.
- `tools/desk/internal/forgeban/allowlist.go` — the row's reason now states what is
  actually left behind it (`set`'s writes and `label list`), rather than the now-stale
  `pr list`.
- `changelog/fix-issue-1123-0915.md`.

## could-not-check

- No live GitLab instance was contacted: the GitLab case runs against `httptest`, per the
  offline envelope. Behaviour against a real instance is asserted only to the extent the
  backend's existing both-backends coverage asserts it.
- No board row: this is issue-only work with no stream brief, so there is no Status cell
  to flip.

  10:00–11:00 ET CPI-digestion hour's. Confidence high. Kill: equal or larger, with the close-out
  confirming the morning hour was not itself degenerate. Score by 2026-10-15.

Both carry their disclosed counter-evidence in the fragment, including the case FT-2 cannot
distinguish on arithmetic alone (a quiet CPI handing the afternoon the larger hour by default).

**Calendar.** No new dated entry proposed. The corridor grew 5 → 28 adjacents, and every id is
already canonical or another lane's proposal; the one Board-calendar item not obviously ours,
G.19 Consumer Credit 10-07, is already `consumer-credit-2026-10-07.json`. The October calendar's
listing of FOMC Minutes Oct 7 would promote `fomc-minutes-2026-10-07` from `estimate`, and is left
to that event's own lane per one-file-per-owner (#1449).

**Honesty labels.** The event is `confirmed` (two federalreserve.gov primaries, re-verified today).
Every trading-adjacent line carries that label, and nothing here licenses an entry — the stance is

Batch 07 — Promotion Unification + Promotion Terms Wiring.

Keep the existing Promotion engine. Unify qualification so any confirmed Darmelk property booking in an eligible campaign window qualifies the same way, regardless of Darmelk Bank vs Pay by Merchant.

## Outcome
- Qualification remains a single `confirmBooking` side-effect after inventory consume. Payment method is not a promotion filter.
- Growth Bank path: pending booking and payment submission do not qualify. Admin bank payment approval reaches `confirmBooking` and then qualifies if the campaign is eligible.
- Growth Merchant path: Merchant approval still only reserves credit. It does not qualify, consume inventory, or confirm. Later authoritative confirmation qualifies through the same engine.
- Request to Book / Contact still do not qualify. There is no admin create-booking-for-user path, so General assisted promotion automation is **deferred** rather than invented.
- `PROMOTION_TERMS` v1 is now readable from promotion UI (`/terms?key=promotion` and `GET /api/terms/promotion`). Current campaigns continue to auto-qualify without a blocking consent gate (`PROMOTION_CONSENT = NOT_REQUIRED`).
- Campaign-specific terms remain snapshotted on qualification. Copy avoids guaranteed-gift wording.
- `PROPERTY_BOOKING_TERMS` enforcement at `createBooking` is **deferred**. Pay-by-Merchant extra checkbox is **deferred** (would redesign PaymentForm).
- No migration. No Mark User Qualified. No second qualification engine.

## Out of scope
- Does not start Batch 08.
- No Promotion engine rebuild, commission/3×5/qualification/Leadership change, inventory/payment-route/Merchant accounting rewrite, public checkout, or Pay to Vendor.
- No other projects.

body:
# Summary

Two decrees from 2026-09-15: "remove the call sheet. we're going full steam
ahead with the triptych version (the new one) i selected. and do no
redactions."

**The Call Sheet comes out.** The bank pane, the lineup, the live card, their
34 stylesheet rules, and the `?open=` deep link that fed them. The tab row is
two now: the products, and what we've learned. The learned register (lessons,
market facts, prospect asks) and the second record's draft queue are untouched.

Its bank survives as a library. The 113 discovery questions still feed the
battlecard harvest, the ask room's citations and the intranet — they simply
have no browsable surface any more. One consequence, handled rather than left:
`askLinks` used to offer "The Playbook card." on a playbook citation, pointing
at `/playbook?open=<questionId>`. There is no card to land on, so that door is
gone. A link labelled for a page that cannot show the question is exactly the
dead end the click-depth law bans; the citation still carries the question's
own text, and the brain's own room remains the last door.

**No redactions on the country wing**, recorded as decided rather than open.
The 97 statutory values that carry a figure stand as authored — 64 wage floors,
plus social security, retirement, maternity, healthcare, severance, sick leave
and overtime. Our own money is unchanged: pricing, deal figures and what a
client pays still never render, and the suite fails the build if a figure
reaches the product copy.

Nothing about The Sheet itself changed in this PR.

# Plan Approval

- Related plan: `docs/plans/playbook-face-product-first-2026-09-14.md`
- Plan status: Approved
- Approved by: Antaeus (2026-09-15, in the two decrees quoted above)

# Decision Log

- Decision: The Call Sheet's UI is deleted; `src/lib/intel/bank.ts` and
  `src/lib/intel/branches.ts` are kept.
- Grounding: Canon. The decree retired a face, not the discovery bank. Those
  modules are still imported by `tests/read-absorption.test.ts` and
  `tests/playbook-program.test.ts`, and the bank's questions still feed the
  battlecard harvest and the ask room.
- Owner: Antaeus
- Validation plan: Both test files still pass; typecheck and lint are clean
  with no unused imports left behind.
- Unknowns: Whether the 113 questions should eventually be retired as data
  too. Not assumed here.
- Tags: playbook, call-sheet, retirement

<!-- -->

- Decision: `askLinks` no longer offers a door on a playbook citation, and its
  test now asserts the absence rather than the link.
- Grounding: Canon (click-depth law — nothing compressed is ever a dead end).
- Owner: Antaeus
- Validation plan: `tests/ask-links.test.ts` inverted and passing; the
  fallback door (the brain's own room) still fires, so no answer is left
  without one.
- Unknowns: None.
- Tags: click-depth, ask-room

<!-- -->

- Decision: Statutory country figures render as authored, permanently.
- Grounding: Canon, now settled by decree (it was an open question on
  2026-09-14 and I shipped a position on it in #323).
- Owner: Antaeus
- Validation plan: The money scan over authored product copy stays in the
  suite, so our money still cannot render. The country sheet is exempt by
  decree, recorded in CLAUDE.md.
- Unknowns: None.
- Tags: money-doctrine, country-wing

# Relationship / Permission Impact

- Relationship owner affected: No
- Permission state affected: No
- Off-limits or boundary rule affected: No
- Direct-contact behavior affected: No
- Private CSM debrief or sensitive note affected: No
- Next safest action preserved: N/A

# HML Impact

- HML rules or classifications affected: No
- Categories affected: None
- Explanation output preserved: N/A
- Confidence output preserved: N/A

# Internal Unknowns

- New unknowns added: Whether the discovery bank should be retired as data,
  now that it has no surface.
- Existing unknowns resolved: Both of the open questions from #323 — the Call
  Sheet's fate, and the country wing's figures.
- Does any unknown block implementation: No

# Testing / Verification

- [x] Docs reviewed
- [x] Typecheck
- [x] Lint
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Manual verification
- [ ] Not applicable; docs/config only

Verify chain green on the rebased head: prettier → tsc → eslint (0 warnings) →
140 tests → `next build`.

Beyond the chain I also ran the three suites that guard this page and are not
in the `npm test` list — `ask-links`, `intranet`, `read-absorption`,
`playbook-program`. The Playbook guards all pass: the page still carries "What
prospects ask" and "Ours, not theirs", every class the client asks for exists
in the stylesheet, and the 2026-08-22 binding retirement still holds.

Manual verification was a browser pass: two tabs and no third, the products
face unchanged (doors, a cue opening and pinning Philippines, the country
wing), the learned register intact across all three registers, and
`/playbook?open=gp-funding` landing on the products arrival with no bank pane

The dead CSS was computed, not guessed: I diffed the class references between

earlier retirements — the bind dropdown, the filter chips, the old card grid.

purge into a decree.

- Relationship-motion risk: None. Nothing on this surface files, composes or

author: rubencarvalho
body:
## Description

In `handleBeforetoggle` (`packages/picker/src/Picker.ts`), the branch that handles an external close (e.g. tapping outside the mobile Tray) while `strategy.preventNextToggle === 'no'` set the host's `open` to `false` but never synced the interaction controller's `open` state:

```ts
} else if (this.strategy?.preventNextToggle === 'no') {
    this.open = false;
    this.strategy.open = false; // added
}
```

Because the controller's `open` stayed stale at `true`, the next `MobileController.handlePointerdown()` set `preventNextToggle = 'yes'` and `handleClick()` skipped `toggle()`, so the Tray never reopened. The fix syncs `strategy.open`, matching the sibling `if (!this.open)` branch just above it.

Desktop was unaffected because `DesktopController.handleActivate()` unconditionally calls `host.toggle()`, which self-heals the controller state.

## Motivation and context

On a mobile/touch device, dismissing an `sp-action-menu` Tray by tapping outside left the action button unresponsive to taps until focus moved elsewhere and back. Tapping the action button should always reopen the menu.

## Related issue(s)

- fixes #6678
- SWC-2543

## Testing

New end-to-end test `packages/action-menu/test/action-menu-reopen.test.ts`: opens the Tray by tapping the button, dismisses it by tapping outside (no selection), then taps the button again and asserts the Tray reopens. This exercises the real outside-tap close path (where `open` is still `true` at `beforetoggle`, hitting the patched branch). The test fails without the fix and passes with it.

Note on browser coverage: with synthetic pointer events the reopen failure reproduces on Firefox; Chromium/WebKit take the already-synced branch under synthetic events. The fix targets the exact branch the outside-tap close takes on real touch input.

## Author's checklist

- [x] I have read the **CONTRIBUTING** and **PULL_REQUESTS** documents.
- [x] I have added automated tests to cover my changes.
- [x] I have included a well-written changeset if my change needs to be published.

---

### Manual review test cases

- [ ] Mobile Tray reopens after outside-tap dismiss
  1. Open the `main` [Action Menu docs](https://opensource.adobe.com/spectrum-web-components/components/action-menu/) with Chrome DevTools device emulation (e.g. iPhone) and then compare to this fix: https://swcpreviews.z13.web.core.windows.net/pr-6749/docs/gen1-docs/components/action-menu/.
  2. Tap the action button; the menu opens in a Tray.
  3. Tap outside the Tray to dismiss it (without selecting an item).
  4. Tap the action button again.
  5. Expected: the Tray reopens.

author: vanyastaff
body:
`UpdateScheduler::end_of_frame` had two independent defects: it registered an awaiter **without ever
requesting a frame**, so an idle caller waited forever unless something unrelated drove one; and the
future parked a `Waker` in a strongly-shared `Arc` that nothing removed on drop, so a cancelled wait
pinned executor resources until the next completion.

## What ships

**Cancellation — the registry holds a `Weak`.** The future keeps the only `Arc`, so dropping it
frees the stored `Waker` immediately, **with no lock taken** and no registry mutation. The drain
skips an entry that fails to `upgrade()` — that means *cancelled*, never *error*, so it is
deliberately not traced. A bounded compaction on the push path keeps dead entries from accumulating
while no frame completes.

Lock-free cancellation is not incidental: AOSP shipped the locking version of this same design in
`BroadcastFrameClock`, hit a production deadlock when a wait was cancelled while a frame was
dispatching, and fixed it the same way (b/407027032).

**Demand — the registry's own live population is the memo.** `end_of_frame` requests a frame when
no live waiter was present before its push, deciding and registering inside one critical section and
releasing the guard before it demands.

Four earlier designs read a scheduler phase or a per-frame flag instead, and every one of them
reproduced this issue's own hang: the drain wakes waiters *before* the phase reset, and `abort_frame`
orders those two the opposite way from `end_frame_impl`, so no per-frame bit is correct on both
paths. The registry has no such clear point — the drain empties it unconditionally. This is also
what the ecosystem does: Compose's `BroadcastFrameClock` fires its demand hook on the awaiter set's
0→1 transition, and `Choreographer.postFrameCallback`, `requestAnimationFrame` and Unity's
`Awaitable.NextFrameAsync` all make registration itself the demand.

The invariant has two halves. *Issuance* the registry decides, by induction on the drain. *Survival*
it cannot: `finish_async_pump` clears the frame latch with no drain, so a demand can be revoked, and
the frames-disabled→enabled edge is what re-issues it. That edge already existed in
`handle_app_lifecycle_state_change`; `set_frames_enabled` gains it as the API-surface mirror.

**Lock order — written down and enforced.** `FrameCompletionFuture::poll` no longer performs any
`Waker` operation under the `state` guard (the displaced waker was previously dropped in place, and
the clone ran there too). `completion_waiters` is now documented as strictly preceding
`FrameCompletionState`, never nested, with neither held across any `Waker` operation or across
`schedule_frame_if_enabled()`. The completion-waker family gains the lock-discipline test it was the
only one in that file to lack.

## Evidence

The issue's own 3-test reproducer, red on `main` before any production edit — 1 passed / 2 failed,
matching the issue. Ten further tests were written and confirmed red **before** the fix
(`4 passed, 10 failed`), including the two that pin the case four plan revisions kept breaking: a
registration made from inside a completion waker, and from inside an aborted frame's waker.

Four tests are labelled **guards** rather than evidence — they are green both ways and defend against
a future wrong shape. One is labelled new-code coverage: it cannot compile against `main`.

Two gaps were found *after* the code was written and closed by tests that fail without the fix: the
demand-suppression branch (stub the predicate to `false` and 984 tests stayed green) and the
`completed` re-check between `poll`'s two lock acquisitions (delete it and 985 stayed green). Both
were found by review, confirmed by measurement, then pinned.

```
just gate                                                → exit 0
cargo nextest run -p flui-scheduler -p flui-app --locked  → 986 passed, 0 skipped
cargo test -p flui-scheduler --doc --locked               → 44 passed, 2 ignored
cargo +nightly miri test (Stacked Borrows + Tree Borrows) → 1 passed
```

Miri covers the one new test that builds a `RawWakerVTable` by hand (the file already carries
`#![expect(unsafe_code)]` for four such wakers; none had been run under miri before).

## Documented, not fixed here

Three pre-existing hazards that this change makes *reachable* by turning `end_of_frame` from "always
hangs, so nobody calls it" into a usable idiom: a future whose scheduler is dropped never resolves;
a panicking `on_frame_scheduled` hook loses the demand permanently; `FrameCompletionFuture` is not
fused. `finish_async_pump` also gains the warning it lacked — it is `pub`, takes `&self`, and clearing
the latch outside the frames-disabled arm strands every live waiter until a lifecycle resume.

`Output` stays `FrameTiming`. The three-arm outcome type and `impl Drop for SchedulerInner` are
**#1162**, with the review findings attached.

## Also

`finish_async_pump`'s doc claimed `handle_begin_frame` was the only place that clears the frame
latch, and then cleared it itself three lines further down; corrected.

Plan and research: `.rust-studio/specs/1055-end-of-frame-demand-and-cancellation/`. Six successive
revisions of that plan contained an error — the last one found by the implementer, by measurement
rather than argument, and the spec was corrected to match the code rather than the test to match the
spec.

Closes #1055. Refs #1161, #1162.

body:
## Problem

GitHub Actions deprecated Node 20 runners on Sept 19 2025 — they are now forced to run on Node 24. Two things broke:

1. **Workflows declared `node-version: 20`** but runners were silently forced to Node 24, producing deprecation warnings.
2. **`node-expat` is a native C++ module that cannot compile on Node 24.** `npm ci` in the release job tried to build it via `node-gyp`, causing the `semantic-release` step to fail with exit code 1 and block all new releases.

## Changes

- **Workflows** (`branch.yml`, `release.yml`): set `node-version` to `24`/`24.x` explicitly.
- **`node-expat` → `sax`**: replaced the native XML parser with `sax@1.6.1` (pure JavaScript, same streaming SAX model). The `sitemap.ts` event handlers are functionally identical — `startElement`/`endElement`/`text`/`error` map 1-to-1 to `onopentag`/`onclosetag`/`ontext`/`onerror`. No logic change.
- Removed `__mocks__/node-expat-stub.js` and its `jest.config.ts` mapping (no longer needed).
- Added `eslint-disable-next-line no-console` on the `console.error` calls in error handlers (`crawl.ts`, `sitemap.ts`) to silence CI lint annotations.

author: nicolasalt
body:
## Summary

The turn-settlement slice of the session status card (docs/303-session-status-card, checklist items 7–9): at the end of every turn ShipIt decides whether the agent updated or confirmed its status card, marks the card stale when it did not, and sends a visible follow-up turn asking for the update. Plus the card's lifecycle on conversation reset, rewind and fork.

The `session_status` tool itself, its route, the system-prompt section and the client card are other sessions' slices of the same wave, so the nudge has nothing to call until those merge. That is the design (plan.md → Turn settlement); the whole feature sits behind `advanced.sessionStatusCard`, off by default.

## Rationale

**The facts must be taken before the drain, and the snapshot must not be able to skip the commit.** A drained successor resets `statusUpdated` and `wasInterrupted` and starts before the network post-turn work, so `settleTurnFacts()` snapshots them at the head of each of the four terminal paths CLAUDE.md invariant 2 names. That position is also *before* the post-turn hold and outside `postTurnStep`, so the helper cannot throw: its status read is guarded and skipped entirely while the setting is off, or a failed SQLite read would abandon the commit behind it (invariant 3).

**It runs after the adoption handover, not before.** A turn adopted from the CLI owns the terminal path it lands on; snapshotting first captured the predecessor's facts, which the re-arm then discarded, leaving the adopted turn's card reading current through its whole commit and PR flow. For the same reason the settlement reads a separate `sawOwnResult` rather than `receivedResult`, which adoption deliberately keeps from the predecessor — a crashed adopted turn produced no result of its own to judge.

**Deciding and dispatching are two steps.** A system turn still holds `systemTurnInProgress` when the decision is made, and an ordinary streaming turn whose CLI stays resident never reaches `finishTurn` until the process exits — so both points try the dispatch and the first to find the runner free wins.

**The nudge goes through `runner.dispatch`, not an enqueue plus a drain entry.** Only that path owns recovery when turn setup rejects; without it a user message that queued during setup had nothing left to start it. Two gates are pre-checked rather than queued behind — a runner with no dispatch dependencies, and a resident agent with background work a system turn would destroy — because one attempt is all a missing update gets (req 15).

**The nudge is a successor like any other, and that exposed an older hazard.** It starts inside the predecessor's post-turn sequence and replaces the resident process, so that process's own late `done` was clearing `runner.running` on a runner the nudge already owned: the live turn read as idle and its runner became reclaimable (invariant 5). The streaming `done` branch now carries the `turnIsCurrent()` guard that `tryDrain` two lines below has always had. Any successor drained during a streaming turn's post-turn had the same exposure; the nudge is what made it reachable on every turn.

**The reset mark lives in `clearAgentSessionId`.** Nine call sites reach it — a helper each of them had to remember would have been forgotten by some — so the stale mark sits beside the goal's clear, in the same method, and returns whether the card changed. `clearConversationThread` pairs that with the `session_list` broadcast so no viewer keeps a card that reads current.

**The setting is read at each use, never captured.** It takes the tool with it, so a nudge decided while it was on must not start a turn asking for something the agent can no longer call (req 21).

## Changes

- **Settlement** (`turn-executor.ts`): `settleTurnFacts()` — memoized, non-throwing, after any adoption handover and before the drain, on the clean `agent_result`, the abnormal `done`, the adapter `error`, the failed auth heal and the quota-retry fallback. It snapshots `{ statusUpdated, wasInterrupted, receivedResult, silent, statusNudge, postTurn, writeSeq }` and marks the card stale immediately under the `writeSeq` guard, so the card never reads as current between a missing update and the end of the network flow (req 11). Reset on adoption with the other memoized work.
- **The decision and the prompt** (`services/session-status.ts`): `shouldNudgeForStatusCard` carries every "no" condition in plan.md — updated, interrupted, no result, silent, already a nudge, driver-owned, a later write, or a successor running or queued (a deferral: that turn is checked afresh when it ends). `statusNudgePrompt` composes the offer list with their taken state around `prompts/status-card-nudge.md`, loaded once at module load.
- **Invariant 5 fixes** (`turn-executor.ts`): the streaming `done` branch clears `runner.running` only while this turn still owns it; and the nudge holds its post-turn lease until its `TurnHandle` settles rather than until `dispatch()` returns, because `dispatch` sets `running` synchronously while the turn epoch only advances when the successor enters its executor — a predecessor exiting during the setup in between still read as current.
- **Dispatch option**: `statusNudge` through `AgentDispatchOptions`, `AgentDispatchInit`, `DISPATCH_FIELDS`, `QueuedMessage`, the hand-written `toQueuedMessage` and `queuedMessageToDispatchOptions`; `silent` now forwarded to `TurnInput` from both dispatch paths, which it was not before.
- **Lifecycle**: `SessionManager.clearAgentSessionId` marks the stored card stale and reports whether it changed; `clearConversationThread` adds the broadcast and is used by the rollback handlers, missing-conversation recovery and credential repair (`SessionAgentEnvDeps` gained an optional `sseBroadcast`). `forkSession` copies the parent's card marked stale — the fork's starting point.
- **The flag**: `SystemTurnDeps.statusCardEnabled` reading a new `credentialStore.getSessionStatusCard()`, wired in `runner-registry-factory.ts` and `ws-handlers/agent-execution.ts`. With the setting off, neither the mark nor the decision runs.
- **Docs**: `plan.md` updated where the build differs from the design (the two dispatch points, the dispatch mechanism, the flag's route in, the centralized reset mark, the snapshot's ordering and non-throwing constraint); checklist items 7–9 ticked.

## Test plan

`npm test` (1122 files, 19780 tests), `npm run lint:dev` and `npm run typecheck` all pass, on the branch rebased onto current `main` (which carries the card slice and its `needsYou: string[]` shape change).

New: `turn-status-settlement.test.ts` drives the settlement and the nudge through the real executor and runner — stale at once plus one nudge with a persisted `[ShipIt]` user row; the nudge turn not nudged again; no nudge after a question, a crash, a silent compaction, a driver-owned turn, with the setting off, or with it turned off mid-turn; a queued successor deferring with nothing left in the queue; a streaming `agent_result` + `done` giving one nudge; a predecessor's late exit leaving the successor's card current and not disowning the live nudge turn; the commit still running when the status read throws; the mark landing before the commit that follows it; and the adopted turn settling its own facts.

Also `services/session-status.test.ts` (the decision table, the prompt, `clearConversationThread`), `sessions.test.ts` and `integration_tests/rewind-fork.test.ts` (the reset mark), `services/session-fork-merge.test.ts` (copy-as-stale), and the `statusNudge`/`silent` round-trips in `prepared-dispatch.test.ts` and `queue-drain.test.ts`.

Every guard was proven red by restoring the pre-fix line, one at a time — including the adoption-ordering one, which needed the predecessor's post-turn parked on its commit while the handover was in flight. One exception, stated plainly: the mid-turn-disable test goes red only when **both** the decision-time and dispatch-time re-reads are removed, since they cover ea

## Resumo

Repaginação de `assets/style.css` (compartilhado por todas as telas) e do template de `index.html`. Começou como polimento de tokens (cor/raio/sombra) num estilo "Apple" e terminou indo além — usando a skill `redesign-existing-projects` para auditar e mudar a composição/hierarquia visual de verdade, não só cor e sombra.

Formulários e login/2FA:** anel de foco suave nos campos, auth card alinhado ao modal (raio/sombra), marca duplicada (login+2FA) consolidada em CSS, título do 2FA deixa de usar a tipografia condensada maiúscula (frase longa em caixa alta contrariava o próprio objetivo de reduzir texto "gritado"), campo do código 2FA vira um campo OTP de verdade (dígitos grandes/espaçados).

**5. Reestruturação de layout (skill `redesign-existing-projects`):**

author: skymly
body:
Closes #361.

## What was wrong

`FromReceive` started its own reassembly loop per subscription. `ClientWebSocket` forbids concurrent receives, and when several `ReceiveAsync` calls are pending the BCL hands each message to exactly one of them. So two `[WebSocketReceive]` members on one interface — a shape the design doc advertises — or two subscribers to one member meant one of them silently never received. Nothing throws and nothing spins; the subscriber just sits there.

## What changed

`WebSocketReceivePump` owns one reassembly loop per `ClientWebSocket`, keyed by a `ConditionalWeakTable` so the pump dies with the socket. Both `WebSocketObservable.FromReceive` (R3) and `SystemReactiveWebSocketAdapter.FromReceive` (System.Reactive) become sinks over it and keep doing their own `T` deserialization, so a `string` member and a `byte[]` member on the same socket still work.

The size cap is set by whichever subscription starts the pump; later sinks inherit it. The two `FromReceive` overloads already defaulted to the same 1 MiB, so this only shows up when a caller passes an explicit cap on a second subscription.

## The pump does not stop when the last sink leaves

Worth calling out because it is the part that isn't obvious. Cancelling a pending `ReceiveAsync` aborts the whole `ClientWebSocket`, not just the read — which means on `main` today, disposing a receive subscription kills the socket for sends too, and a follow-up `SendAsync` throws `WebSocketException: The WebSocket is in an invalid state ('Aborted')`. So the refcount only governs starting. The loop runs until the socket closes or fails, and reads and discards while no sink is attached, which a WebSocket client has to do anyway to keep control frames moving.

## Tests

Added to both E2E suites: two subscribers see the same message (fails on `main`), and a subscriber arriving after the previous one detached still receives. The Reactive dispose test was renamed from `FromReceive_dispose_cancels_the_pump_without_completing` to `FromReceive_dispose_detaches_without_completing_and_leaves_the_socket_usable` and now asserts a send succeeds afterwards.

`docs/design/websocket.md` §4.4 and §7 record the pump and the reason it outlives its sinks.

Stock ready (protected seeds only) becomes golden without a player. Extra jars, pin, or loader changes become golden only after ready and a player join. If an attempt crashes before it is proven, the next start boots the golden snapshot and **does not rewrite** the upload folder. Empty-server restarts stay on golden. A Copyparty modset change or HA pin change starts a new attempt. If even golden crash-loops, `/healthz` fails and Home Assistant can recycle the add-on (watchdog enabled; `hold_on_crash_loop` off). Also: drop unused `incoming/` lock-era paths, stage mods once per JVM start, Copyparty sweeps any empty drop file (not just `.jar`).

author: monteirodemolay
body:
## Crítica

A aba "Trajetória e Honrarias" empilhava todos os painéis (Caminho na Loja, Títulos e Condições, Honrarias e Condecorações, Graus Filosóficos, Irmãos Gêmeos) em largura cheia, um embaixo do outro — independente de quanto conteúdo cada um tinha. Resultado (visível no caso real do Eduardo Rodrigues Lima): um Irmão com uma única Honraria/Título ficava com um cartão minúsculo esticado numa linha inteira de tela, criando uma coluna desproporcional e "disforme", com muito espaço morto ao lado de cada cartão curto.

## Solução

- "Caminho na Loja" é o único bloco realmente sequencial/longo da aba — passa a ocupar sozinho uma coluna mais larga (7/12).
- Títulos e Condições, Honrarias e Condecorações, Graus Filosóficos e Irmãos Gêmeos/Colegas de Cerimônia são todos "contexto secundário" — cartões curtos, tipo selo — e ficam agrupados numa coluna mais estreita ao lado (5/12), mesmo espírito de grade 8/4 já usado na aba Visão Geral.
- **Adaptativo**: colapsa pra uma coluna só quando só um dos dois lados tem conteúdo (só trajetória, ou só honrarias/títulos sem cargos) — nunca reserva espaço vazio pro lado sem nada.
- Grades de selos (Títulos/Honrarias) perdem o `md:grid-cols-4` (dimensionado pra largura cheia) e os cabeçalhos ganham `compact`, proporcionais à coluna mais estreita.
- `CeremonyMatesPanel` ganha um novo parâmetro opcional `compact`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` em `@vl6/web`
- [x] `eslint --max-warnings 0` em `@vl6/web`
- [x] `next build`
- [x] `turbo run test` (suíte completa, incluindo pre-push hook)

author: damianvtran
body:
## What and why

`/goal <text>` typed from the desktop app set the standing goal and never started a turn. The TUI does both on one Enter (`app.py::_cmd_goal`: store the goal, then submit the argument as an ordinary user turn), so the desktop path was performing half the command in silence.

### The seam

`SLASH_ACTION_RECEIPTS` (`local_operator/session/runtime/types.py`) names the receipts that carry a `request` for the INVOKING client to submit as a user turn, and `runtime_must_complete(receipt_type, consumers)` is the one ownership rule: the runtime admits the request itself only when the dialing client did NOT declare that type in its auth frame. The desktop viewer declares all of them — `AttachedSession` dials with `slash_consumers=list(SLASH_ACTION_RECEIPTS)` on every surface, `desktop` included — so for those receipt types the runtime deliberately stands down and the desktop host owes the submit.

`local_operator/server/routes/desktop_sessions.py::command` spelled the types out by hand:

```python
attached = outcome.data.get("type") in {"team_attached", "agent_attached"}
```

`9223b7c4b` (#796, "submit goal text as an ordinary user message") added `goal_set` to the tuple and taught both other hosts of the rule to complete it — the runtime (`serving.py::_complete_unconsumed_action`) and the TUI (`app.py::_render_authoritative_slash`). This route is the third host and was not updated, so for a goal it stored the goal, returned `"goal set"`, and dropped `data["request"]`: no user row, no turn, no error — exactly the silent drop the declaration exists to prevent.

## Reproduction (before the fix)

The e2e cell added in `4a6873026` was written first and run against the unmodified route. It asserts what the existing cell never did — an admitted turn, not just a stored goal:

```sh
$ cd ~/local-operator-worktrees/desktop-goal-submission
$ env -u NO_COLOR TERM=xterm-256color .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
    tests/e2e/test_desktop_sessions.py -m e2e -n0 -q -k test_canonical_desktop_over_http
```

```
>                   assert result.json()["result"]["result"]["admission"]["status"] == "admitted"
E                   TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
tests/e2e/test_desktop_sessions.py:170: TypeError
1 failed, 4 deselected in 8.47s
```

`admission` is `null` because nothing was admitted: the goal landed on the runtime, the receipt came back, and the request never became a turn. The same point, driven through every new unit guard with the route temporarily restored to `origin/main`'s version:

```
=== BEFORE (route at origin/main) ===
FAILED tests/unit/server/test_desktop_goal_admission.py::test_a_goal_command_admits_its_argument_as_a_user_turn - TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
FAILED tests/unit/server/test_desktop_goal_admission.py::test_a_type_added_to_the_shared_vocabulary_is_completed_here - AssertionError: assert [] == [('Do the new thing', '22222222-...')]
FAILED tests/unit/server/test_desktop_goal_admission.py::test_every_declared_action_receipt_is_completed_by_this_route - AssertionError: goal_set is declared in SLASH_ACTION_RECEIPTS but this route does not submit its request; the runtime stood down on the declaration, so the turn is dropped in silence
FAILED tests/unit/server/test_desktop_goal_admission.py::test_the_command_handler_decides_through_the_shared_helper - AssertionError: the desktop command route no longer reaches its completion decision through desktop_viewer_must_submit; a hand-written set of receipt types is how /goal <text> lost its turn
FAILED tests/unit/server/test_desktop_goal_admission.py::test_the_shared_helper_is_derived_from_the_shared_vocabulary - KeyError: 'desktop_viewer_must_submit'
5 failed, 3 passed in 1.60s
FAILED tests/e2e/test_desktop_sessions.py::test_canonical_desktop_over_http - TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
1 failed, 4 deselected in 8.47s
```

## The fix

The route's decision is derived from the shared vocabulary through one helper:

```python
def desktop_viewer_must_submit(receipt_type: Any) -> bool:
    from local_operator.session.runtime.types import (
        SLASH_ACTION_RECEIPTS, runtime_must_complete,
    )
    return not runtime_must_complete(receipt_type, SLASH_ACTION_RECEIPTS)
```

`runtime_must_complete` is `False` exactly when the client declared the type, and the desktop bridge declares the whole list — so the inversion is this host's half of the same rule, never a second reading of it. The helper's function-local import reads the tuple at CALL time, which is what makes the drift guard real: a test can extend the vocabulary and watch the answer change, where a module-level binding would freeze the answer it set out to check.

Behaviour preserved for every other receipt: the `images` pass-through and the `admission` field on the receipt are unchanged, the empty-request guard (`/agent clear`'s accept-with-no-action shape, and the goal show/clear forms) still submits nothing, and a receipt type outside the vocabulary is still left alone.

Order matches the TUI's: the goal is stored and the receipt built before the admission, and the admission is reported inside that same receipt. Two deliberate differences from the TUI path are written down beside the branch:

- the text submitted is the receipt's own `request` and the body's structured images are passed straight through — there is no composer on this host, so there is no attachment map to resolve `[Image #N]` markers or collapsed pastes against (the TUI's `_submit_command_prompt` has one);
- a turn already running QUEUES the admission behind it (the runtime's `prompt` op) where the TUI steers. Queued, never dropped — the behaviour the `/team` and `/agent` branches in this route already have.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/server/test_desktop_goal_admission.py` (new; real router + fake bridge, no provider): the goal command admits its argument with the caller's own request id; the receipt keeps `stored`/`request`/`text` beside the admission; an empty-request receipt and a typeless status notice admit nothing; **every** name in `SLASH_ACTION_RECEIPTS` is completed through the route; a type added to the vocabulary tests itself without editing the file; a static audit of the real source refuses a handler that names receipt types itself, or a helper that stops reading the shared list.
- `tests/e2e/test_desktop_sessions.py`: the goal block now asserts the admitted turn, one durable user row keyed by the request id, exactly one scripted provider turn, and no second turn on a replayed request id.
- `tests/e2e/test_desktop_controls.py` (`4b452825f`): the control census states provider calls absolutely, so the goal command's new turn moves it by one at each of its three sites (`3→4`, `6→7`, `7→8`) and the controlled stream gains a turn for it. The block also asserts the receipt's admission directly. **The first CI run is what found this file** — the stage was the only thing that could, because a `/goal` POST from a second e2e module is exactly the neighbour a scoped local run does not see. That first run is also the honest record of the diff before the fix-up: `tui-e2e (macos-latest)`: `1 failed, 155 passed, 7 skipped`, the failure being `test_desktop_control_surface - AssertionError: assert 4 == 3`.

## Gates (on the head, whole tree exactly as CI)

```
.venv/bin/python -m flake8 .                                  -> clean (rc=0, no output)
uvx --from black==26.1.0 black --check .                      -> 1419 files unchanged
uvx isort==5.13.2 --check .                                   -> clean
.venv/bin/python -m pyright --pythonpath .venv/bin/python .   -> 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations
```

Test runs (macOS, `env -u NO_COLOR TERM=xterm-256color`, isolated config dir):

```
tests/unit/server/test_desktop_goal_admission.py                               8 passed
tests/unit/server tests/unit/session/runtime tests/unit/tui/test_noop_consumers.py

body:
Bumps every `@fetchproxy/*` dependency to `^3.0.1`, with the lockfile updated to match. 3.0.1 ([fetchproxy#374](https://github.com/chrischall/fetchproxy/pull/374)) fixes:

- **Peer frames are capped:** the peer socket now has the same `maxPayload` limit as the host.
- **Load-induced drops are logged:** a frame refused because too many are in flight gets its own warning, instead of a drop that looks like a replay.
- **Identity writes are atomic:** the file is staged and renamed, so a crash can't leave a torn identity. The directory is also tightened to 0700 each time it is opened.

First-party dependency, so `fix` rather than `chore`: it ships the fixes to this MCP's users.

Verified on the branch before opening: `npm ci`, build, typecheck (where present) and `npm test` all pass.

author: corex0n
body:
## El caso

COT 15092601 / OT 796863, 15-09-2026. SMU Procurement exige una nomenclatura en la cotización (CT) y en la hoja de servicio (HS) para emitir la HES. La versión en producción (`943888e`) tenía dos problemas:

- **La HS no se descargaba.** El supervisor de SMU veía `ERR_INVALID_RESPONSE` y a Pedro le quedaba en "descarga pendiente". El archivo estaba bien; lo roto era el enlace. `fl_attachment:<nombre>` llevaba el texto libre del trabajo ("…Venta Asistida.-"), y Cloudinary responde **400** con `.` `,` `(` `)` `'` `#` `&` `+` `;` `=` `@` `~` `%` `"` `/` `:` o con cualquier carácter no-ASCII. Se midió con curl, carácter por carácter.
- **El nombre de la CT salía `COT - 15092601 - ceco SIN-CECO - …`.** El supervisor escribió que debía decir `CT - 15092601 - ceco 3164 - …`.

## Qué cambia

- **Nombre del archivo en la URL.** Se limpia con lista blanca en un solo lugar (`_nombreAdjuntoSeguro`, dentro de `_urlPDFDescarga`), y `_urlDescargaCot` delega en esa función. Una URL que ya traiga un nombre sucio se vuelve a armar limpia.
- **Formato** que escribió el supervisor de SMU (decisión de Bastián):
  - `CT - <folio> - ceco <CECO> - <texto breve>`
  - `HS - <OT> - CT <folio> - ceco <CECO> - <texto breve>`
- **CECO.** Se usa el del documento; si no tiene, se busca en el catálogo con `_indexarCadenas` + `ALIAS_LOCALES` ("S10 Concepcion" → M10 CONCEPCION, 3164). Sin escrituras en producción.
- **Texto breve y CECO iguales en la CT y su HS.** Salen del `nombreServicio` de la cotización. El preventivo usa `MP Transpaletas <Mes> <Año>`.
- **Correo "Enviar hojas" de preventivos:** ahora lleva la nomenclatura; antes mandaba el enlace crudo.
- **Enlace a la app** (`?pdf=`): ya no se le pega `.pdf`.
- **Respaldo de descarga:** un 400 abre el archivo sin nombre; un corte de red reabre el enlace con nombre.
- **Vínculo `cotizacionId`/`cotizacionNumero`:** ya no se pisa con `''` al cerrar, editar ni sincronizar la cola.
- **`_obtenerHojaDeCot`:**
  - Cae a `pdfs` también cuando la OT solo tiene el link a la app.
  - Se queda con la generación `_vN` más alta.
  - Por N° de OT solo acepta la HS del mismo local (lo mismo en "Ver OTs por técnico").
- SW **v57**.

## Evidencia

- **Barrido de 920 enlaces reales de producción** (HEAD a Cloudinary): **0 fallos y 0 regresiones** con este código. Con `943888e` fallaban 95 HS y 1 CT.
- **25 tests unitarios en verde.** Nuevo `tests/la-hs-se-descarga.js`; con `--prod` hace HEAD real a los casos del punto, el paréntesis y la coma, y responden 206. `nombre-pdf-cotizacion.js` usa los datos reales, con el CECO vacío.
- **Mutaciones:** 17 regresiones simuladas, y los tests detectan todas.
- **Chromium** (`tests/offline/prueba-nombre-pdf.js`, contra Cloudinary real): bajan `CT - 15092601 - ceco 3164 - Destape piletas y camara.pdf` y `HS - 796863 - CT 15092601 - ceco 3164 - Destape piletas y camara.pdf`. **Contraprueba contra `943888e`:** la app arma exactamente la URL rota de la captura de Pedro.
- **Recorrido en Chromium de todas las salidas:** Ver PDF, Compartir, compartir varias, correo con CT y HS, Ver OTs, preventivos y cierre con y sin señal.
- **Pruebas offline del cierre en verde:** A/B/C, hoja regenerada, firma, aviso duplicado y baja de activo.

## Pendiente (anotado en CLAUDE.md, fuera de este PR)

- La CT no imprime el nombre de quien la emite (lo pide SMU).
- CECO rellenado a 4 dígitos, sin confirmar.
- Flujo "previa aceptada → OT en espera" (0 usos): esa CT sale sin HS.
- El link a la app abre la HS sin la nomenclatura.
- 2 pares CT/HS antiguos siguen sin calzar.
