author: youdie006
body:
Rendering a slice that holds a `nil` element crashes the calling process:

```go
t, _ := gonja.FromString("{{ xs }}")
out, err := t.ExecuteToString(exec.NewContext(map[string]any{"xs": []any{nil, 1}}))
// panic: reflect: call of reflect.Value.Interface on zero Value
```

`exec/value.go:271` calls `reflect.Value.Interface()` directly on the element:

```go
item, ok := v.Index(i).Val.Interface().(*Value)
```

`v.Index(i).Val` is a zero `reflect.Value` for a nil element, and raw `reflect.Value.Interface()` panics on that. This is a plain render with no filter involved; a decoded JSON array containing `null` is enough to reach it. `|list`, `|unique`, `|sort`, `|reverse` and `|batch` all go through the same line.

The package already ships the guard. `Value.Interface()` at `exec/value.go:865-870` checks `IsValid()` and `CanInterface()` and returns `nil` otherwise, and `String()` itself guards the same way at `:228`. Of the four raw `.Val.Interface()` calls in the package, `:206` is guarded by `CanInterface()` at `:205`, `:229` by the check at `:228`, and `:867` is the guard; `:271` is the only one with nothing in front of it.

Going through the accessor makes the `*Value` assertion fail for a nil element, which falls into the `ToValue(v.Index(i).Val)` branch already sitting on the next line.

A literal `{{ [none, 1] }}` already rendered as `[, 1]` before this change, so the fix makes a nil element from the context agree with the literal rather than inventing a new output.

<details>
<summary>Verification</summary>

Go 1.26.3, `go test ./tests/integration/ -count=1 -args -ginkgo.v`. `md5sum exec/value.go` on every row.

| `exec/value.go` | md5 | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| this PR | `8179aba6e4ab` | `Ran 297 of 302 Specs`, `SUCCESS! 297 Passed, 0 Failed` |
| pristine `HEAD` (revert) | `9399e1082229` | `296 Passed, 1 Failed`, panic line present |
| drop the `*Value` fast path (force `ok = false`) | `0c39f7d5b5fe` | passes, **survives** |
| `Value.Interface()` without `IsValid()` | `4eecd94e7637` | `292 Passed, 5 Failed` |
| `Value.Interface()` without `CanInterface()` | `9b1f365d26cc` | passes, **survives** |

Two mutants survive and I could not kill either:

- Dropping the `*Value` fast path leaves `ToValue(v.Index(i).Val)` to produce the same string for every input I could construct, including `{{ ['a', 1] }}` and `{{ [['a'], 1] }}` where I expected the two branches to disagree on quoting. That is a pre-existing gap in coverage for that branch, not one this change introduces, but it does mean the new test pins the nil guard only.
- Dropping `CanInterface()` needs a valid-but-unexported value routed through `Index()`, which I could not build.

The `IsValid()` row kills five specs where the revert kills one, so the two failures are not the same set.

Also run: `go test ./... -count=1` all `ok`, `go vet ./...` clean, `gofmt -l` clean on both changed files, `go mod tidy` leaves `go.mod`/`go.sum` unchanged, and `-race` green on `./exec/` and `./tests/integration/`. `gofmt -l .` does report `builtins/methods/pystring/str_title.go`, `tokens/position.go` and `utils/ellipsis.go`, but those are untouched by this change and CI does not run gofmt.

The test is a ginkgo block in `tests/integration/lists_test.go` next to the existing list cases.

</details>

Disclosure: this change was written with AI assistance (Claude). The measurements and mutants above were reproduced and checked by me before opening this PR.

author: ccurme
body:
Resolves https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/33787

HITL tool call edits currently work by editing the underlying `AIMessage.tool_calls`. This has two effects:
- ✅ It changes what tool is executed.
- 🤔 It changes the model-generated tool call in message history. On follow-up turns, the model sees that it generated the edited tool call.

This second point is questionable. Reasoning models often have reasoning traces pointing to a tool call that we are modifying. This may contribute to the behavior flagged in https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/33787, in which a model retries edited calls.

Here we change how this works:
- Tool call `edit` actions in HumanInTheLoopMiddlware edit `ToolCallRequest`, not `AIMessage.tool_calls`
- We add a notice to the resulting ToolMessage telling the model that there was an intervention and giving the name and args of the tool that was executed.
- We update `ToolNode` to prefer the tool named in `tool_call["name"]` (unless `ToolCallRequest.tool` was modified).

Due to the last point, this change requires an update in langgraph-prebuilt here: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/compare/cc/hitl-tool-edits-toolcallrequest

I find that this resolves the pathological retry behavior from https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/33787 across a range of models (OpenAI Luna, Sol; Anthropic Haiku and Opus; Gemini 3.7 Flash; GLM 5.3 Flash).

Note that there are existing bugs in `ChatOpenAI(..., use_responses_api=True)` and `ChatAnthropic` such that we have not been updating the `function_call` or `tool_use` block the model sees on round trips. For these chat models we are effectively just adding the notice. This PR brings other models into alignment.

body:
# Vercel Speed Insights Installation Report

## Summary
Successfully installed and configured Vercel Speed Insights for the CyberLab project following the latest official documentation from Vercel.

## Changes Made

### 1. Package Installation
- **Installed**: `@vercel/speed-insights@^2.0.0`
- **Updated**: `package.json` with the new dependency
- **Updated**: `package-lock.json` with dependency lockfile information

### 2. Created Speed Insights Initialization Script
- **File**: `vercel-speed-insights.js`
- **Purpose**: Initializes the Speed Insights queue and loads the tracking script
- **Implementation**: 
  - Sets up the `window.si` function queue for event tracking
  - Dynamically loads the Speed Insights script from `/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js`
  - Includes environment detection to only load on production (not on localhost)
  - Uses defer loading for optimal performance

### 3. Updated HTML Files
Modified all HTML files to include the Speed Insights initialization script:
- **index.html**: Added script tag in `<head>` section
- **admin.html**: Added script tag in `<head>` section
- **404.html**: Added script tag in `<head>` section
- **offline.html**: Added script tag in `<head>` section

Each file now includes: `<script src="/vercel-speed-insights.js" defer></script>`

### 4. Updated Express Server Configuration
- **File**: `server.js`
- **Changes**:
  1. Fixed `PUBLIC_DIR` to serve from root directory (`__dirname`) instead of non-existent `public/` folder
  2. Added route handler for `/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js` to serve the Speed Insights module from node_modules during local development
  3. Added QAT 10.5 section with proper documentation

## Implementation Details

### Framework Detection
The project uses vanilla HTML/JavaScript with an Express.js backend (not a framework like Next.js or React), so the implementation follows Vercel's guidelines for static sites with npm packages.

### How It Works
1. When a page loads, `vercel-speed-insights.js` initializes the tracking queue
2. The queue allows events to be captured before the main library loads
3. On production (Vercel deployment), the script loads from `/_vercel/speed-insights/*` routes (automatically handled by Vercel)
4. On local development, the custom route serves the module from node_modules
5. Speed Insights automatically tracks Web Vitals and performance metrics

### Production Deployment
When deployed to Vercel:
- The `/_vercel/speed-insights/*` routes are automatically handled by Vercel's infrastructure
- No additional configuration is needed
- Data will appear in the Vercel Dashboard under Speed Insights section after user visits

### Local Development
- The script detects localhost and skips loading to avoid tracking development traffic
- The server includes a fallback route to serve the module for testing purposes
- No Speed Insights data is collected in development mode

## Testing Performed
✅ Server starts successfully without errors
✅ HTML pages load correctly with Speed Insights script tag
✅ Speed Insights initialization script is served at `/vercel-speed-insights.js`
✅ Speed Insights module is served at `/_vercel/speed-insights/script.js`
✅ No console errors or warnings
✅ Package dependencies installed and locked properly

## Files Modified
- `package.json` - Added @vercel/speed-insights dependency
- `package-lock.json` - Updated with new dependency tree
- `index.html` - Added Speed Insights script tag
- `admin.html` - Added Speed Insights script tag
- `404.html` - Added Speed Insights script tag
- `offline.html` - Added Speed Insights script tag
- `server.js` - Fixed PUBLIC_DIR path and added Speed Insights route handler

## Files Created
- `vercel-speed-insights.js` - Speed Insights initialization script

## Next Steps
After merging this PR and deploying to Vercel:
1. Performance data will start appearing in the Vercel Dashboard
2. Web Vitals (LCP, FID, CLS, etc.) will be automatically tracked
3. Monitor the Speed Insights dashboard to identify performance improvements

## Notes
- The implementation preserves all existing code structure and functionality
- Speed Insights only tracks data in production, not during local development
- The package adds minimal overhead (~4KB gzipped) to page load

author: amichai-bd
body:
## TL;DR

Records the owner's go decision on the flash-resident game library (single compressed image mode, all 17 images plus catalogue in the MAX 10 internal flash) as a contract: a new storage MAS for the flash layout, on-chip flash IP boundary, boot copier, host precedence and `.pof` programming path, with the measured capacity facts that drove the decision.

## Issues

Closes #669

## Specification

- [Ownership map](wiki/ownership.md): `src/rtl/storage` row now names [MAS_flash_library](wiki/src/rtl/storage/MAS_flash_library.md) beside MAS_sdram.
- [MAS_flash_library](wiki/src/rtl/storage/MAS_flash_library.md) (new): configuration mode, flash layout mirroring the SDRAM layout from word `0x00800`, IP boundary with the `VERILATOR` double and Questa stand-in, boot copier sequence and bounds, precedence over host loads, programming path, fixtures, assertions, measured facts.
- [MAS_loader_profile](wiki/src/rtl/cartridge/MAS_loader_profile.md): boot source now names both sources; `$A000` bit 5 gated by the copier, bit 3 `flash_boot`; host retry bound during the boot copy; reset edge case.
- [MAS_sdram](wiki/src/rtl/storage/MAS_sdram.md): catalogue writers now include the boot copier.
- [Charter](wiki/src/project-charter.md#game-library): boot-source bullet records the go decision.
- `src/` and `tools/`: no change; nothing implements this contract yet. The implementation and verification gap is tracked by the open epic #658, linked from the new page's header and the ownership map. The n2m builder SPEC is unchanged: the builder setting and `.pof` programming path are stated as planned behavior in the new MAS and become SPEC facts when the slice lands.

## Known misalignment

Planned behavior: `src/rtl/storage` has no flash reader or copier, `tools/n2m/fpga.py` sets no `INTERNAL_FLASH_UPDATE_MODE`, and `fpga program` accepts only `.sof`. Side ahead: wiki. Tracked by #658; closes when the flash boot slice lands with the fixtures named in the MAS.

## Changes

- New `wiki/src/rtl/storage/MAS_flash_library.md`.
- Boot-source, status-byte, host-interaction and edge-case updates in `wiki/src/rtl/cartridge/MAS_loader_profile.md`.
- One sentence in `wiki/src/rtl/storage/MAS_sdram.md`; charter bullet; ownership row.

## Ownership

- Author agent: issue #669 author (Claude Fable 5.1)
- Branch and worktree: `669-flash-library-decision`, `worktrees/669-flash-library-decision/`

## Validation

- `python3 tools/wiki/check.py` on `f0ea3d5` — OK: 48 tests, 1178 tracked files checked, 197 documents published (links and anchors validated).
- Review round 1 (reviewer report on `4890899`, all findings applied in `abafbe5`; leftover host-reload sentence removed in `f0ea3d5`; reviewer `ready` on `f0ea3d5`): one whole-boot bound (`CHECK` <= 20 clocks, `COPY` <= 700,000 clocks, swap <= 80,000 edges: menu within 32 ms of `initialized`) and the same 32 ms host `LOAD_BEGIN` retry on both pages; `flash_boot` has one setting event (the edge `COPY` leaves); boot copier added as the storage arbiter's third client with its priority rule; `reset_sys` edge case names the flash reload with host reload as fallback; `flash-blank` states `sdram_ready` within 20 clocks of `initialized` (clock 5056 at the latest); ADC double convention cited from `wiki/src/fpga-controls.md`; the spec links the charter bullet instead of the closing issue.
- Measurement evidence (Windows, Quartus Prime 25.1std.0 Build 1129 Lite, fresh clone `C:\Users\abendavid\n2m-669` at `5da9148`): `python tools/build.py fpga build v05-board --quartus-bin C:\altera_lite\25.1std\quartus\bin64 --tag fpga-669 --timeout 3600 --json` — PASS in 188 s; 10,222 LEs, 761,704 memory bits, UFM 0/1; `.pof` 1,450,252 B with 455.9 KiB erased, 870.0 KiB programmed. Copy recompiled with `INTERNAL_FLASH_UPDATE_MODE "Single Comp Image"` (`quartus_sh --flow compile design`) — PASS in 154 s; `.pof` 743.9 KiB erased, 339.1 KiB programmed. Reports retained under the clone's `workdir\builds\fpga-669\...\cef641acc88f\output\` and `workdir\669-compressed\output\` until merge.
- Rebase: `main` moved by #670 (`.github/workflows/pr-policy.yml`, `tools/ci/tests/test_pr_policy.py`, `wiki/agents/pull-requests.md`; no overlap with this PR). Branch rebased onto `34ed4f7`; head `022b06fa145fc900892707a86d6a3df7561eae6d`. `git diff origin/main <head>` is byte-identical to the reviewed diff `git diff 5da9148 f0ea3d5` (`cmp` equal), so the reviewed content is what merges.
- Decision packet and owner decision: https://github.com/amichai-bd/nand2mario/issues/669#issuecomment-5685339998

## Risk

The copier bounds (4 flash words per 7 clocks; one SDRAM line per 18.6 clocks) derive from the shipped IP RTL and the SDRAM contract, not from hardware; the implementing slice must confirm them with the fixtures named in the MAS. Programming time is the Intel table value until measured.

author: thiagovbs
body:
## O que muda

O titular autoriza **outra conta** a ler **saldo** e **extrato** das contas que ele escolher, pelo prazo que ele definir. Contratos no padrão do Open Finance Brasil: `Consents v3` para o consentimento e `Accounts v2` para a leitura.

## Decisões

- **Escopo conta a conta.** O consentimento vale para as contas marcadas na autorização, não para "as contas do titular". Contas criadas depois ficam de fora.
- **Prazo opcional.** `expirationDateTime` ausente ou nulo = prazo indeterminado, válido até a revogação; com data, no máximo 12 meses.
- **Dois modos de autorização, um serviço só.** Tela de redirect (o chatbot abre o navegador) e modo texto (o chatbot já tem o token do titular) caem no mesmo `authoriseDataSharingConsent()`, com as mesmas validações.
- **Sem status `REVOKED`/`EXPIRED`.** Como no OFB, ambos são `REJECTED` distinguidos por `rejectReason` — uma máquina de estados só.
- **Expiração aplicada na leitura**, não por job: o consentimento vencido é gravado como `REJECTED`/`CONSENT_EXPIRED` na própria requisição que o encontrou.
- **Conta fora do escopo responde 404**, não 403: ela não deve existir aos olhos da receptora.

## Endpoints

| Método | Rota |
|---|---|
| POST | `/open-banking/consents/v3/consents` |
| GET / DELETE | `/open-banking/consents/v3/consents/{consentId}` |
| GET | `/v1/data-sharing/consents/{consentId}/authorise` (tela) |
| POST | `/v1/data-sharing/consents/{consentId}/authorise` (modo texto) |
| GET | `/v1/data-sharing/consents/{consentId}/accounts` |
| GET / DELETE | `/v1/me/data-sharing/consents` |
| GET | `/open-banking/accounts/v2/accounts[/{accountId}[/balances|transactions]]` |

## Correções incluídas

- **Parser de form-urlencoded** colapsava chaves repetidas: marcar duas contas na tela compartilharia só uma.
- **`redirect_uri` do enrollment JSR** perdia a porta (`request.hostname`). Essa URL é persistida no enrollment e usada para devolver `code`+`state`, então o callback ia para a porta 80. Commit separado, com teste de regressão.

## Verificação

- 178 testes verdes (19 arquivos), `tsc` limpo.
- Migration conferida contra o SQL que o Prisma geraria (`prisma migrate diff`) — idênticos. Já aplicada no RDS.
- Jornada testada ponta a ponta contra o banco real: ambos os modos de autorização, leitura de saldo e extrato, e os negativos (antes de autorizar, sem `x-consent-id`, conta fora do escopo, permissão faltando, titular errado, após revogação, após vencimento).

## Fora deste PR

O `openapi.yaml` foi atualizado para 1.17.0 com as 10 rotas novas, mas vive um nível acima da raiz do repositório e não é versionado aqui.

author: widgetii
body:
The app that shipped with the camera worked from anywhere because the camera
dialled out to the manufacturer's server. Flashing OpenIPC removes that server,
which is usually the point — and also removes the convenience, because RTSP
waits to be connected *to*. Watching from outside then means a forwarded port,
dynamic DNS, or a VPN on every device you want to watch from. On mobile
broadband, or on any connection with no public address, there is no port to
forward at all.

The camera can dial out to a relay of the owner's own instead, over an open
standard, and nothing here said so. The configuration key is documented in the
Majestic configuration page; what to point it at, and what to run at the other
end, was not written down anywhere.

Written for somebody who has just flashed a camera and misses the app: a relay
on the cheapest VPS, locked down before anything is pointed at it, the camera
configured from the web interface, and a browser at the far end.

Three caveats decide whether a reader has a good time, so they get their own
section rather than a footnote:

- This path carries no sound. Readers building a doorbell are sent to the
  doorbell guide instead.
- These cameras often default to H.265, and browser support for it over WebRTC
  depends on the viewing machine's hardware. That is the most likely reason a
  reader gets a player that connects and shows nothing, so it is called out
  where they will be looking.
- The camera serves a small fixed number of these connections at once. That is
  the argument for letting the relay serve the audience rather than pointing
  ten browsers at the camera, and the page makes it rather than leaving readers
  to discover the limit.

The credential is the part most likely to be got wrong. The camera presents a
bearer token, and MediaMTX's own users are reached through that same header
written `user:pass` — the same accommodation it documents for OBS Studio. Said
explicitly, and the diagnostic `ffmpeg` command at the end uses the same form
so a reader comparing the two sees one credential, not two.

Verified against MediaMTX's current configuration reference and
`ffmpeg -h muxer=whip` (n8.1.1) rather than from memory: the authentication
section, the WebRTC settings and their defaults, the two ports, and the
`-authorization` option taking a bare token.

English only, matching the other integration guides.

author: rjmendez
body:
Turns `docs/pool-backup-restore.md` (the G0 gate of Phase 3, closing risk-register R6) into working
repo-local mechanism **without taking a backup, mounting anything, or changing the cluster.**

Nothing here runs against the live pool. No backup exists yet. Every path is fail-closed by
construction rather than by operator discipline, because the plan's §14.2 (who holds the offline
passphrase copy) and §14.3 (`F:` ownership) are questions only a person can answer, and a
scheduled job that writes archives nobody has proved are decryptable is worse than the gap it
closes -- it manufactures the appearance of a backup.

## What ships

* **`tools/hear_pool_backup.py`** -- backup / verify / restore, stdlib only plus one `gpg` call.
  * dry-run is the default; `--execute` is required before a byte is written anywhere
  * **no passphrase is ever created, derived, defaulted, logged or stored.** It is only ever a
    path handed in from outside, opened and streamed to `gpg` on a pipe fd -- never argv, never an
    env value, never in a receipt. `redact()` scrubs every string the tool emits
  * a `--pool` that resolves to `/pool` is refused before anything is read
  * sentinel-before-write, and a target sharing a device with its source is refused
  * allowlisted roots (`corpus/`, `models/`, `sketch_corpus/`), `pylib*`/`*.tmp` excluded
  * frozen-prefix reads of the append-only streams; `unstable`/`vanished` recorded, never torn
  * SQLite backup API for the live-WAL database; canonical JSONL manifest; path-free cleartext receipt
  * a generation is published whole by `os.replace`; a failure removes staging and appends no index row
  * restore requires `--i-understand`, an empty target, and refuses `/pool` or the source tree
* **`deploy/k8s/hear-pool-backup.yaml`** -- every schedule `suspend: true`, pool `readOnly: true`
  on both volume and mount, `hostPath type: Directory`, no `secretKeyRef` in the namespace, and a
  restore drill that mounts **no** `hear-pool` volume at all.
* **`deploy/k8s/hear-pool-backup-code.yaml`** -- generated by `gen_configmap.py`, the repo's only
  supported way to ship code into a pod.
* **`tests/test_pool_backup.py`** -- the G0.1-G0.13 ladder on synthetic fixtures built in
  `tmp_path`: a miniature pool, a live-WAL database with an open writer, a torn JSONL tail,
  multi-member gzip, a pruned clip, a flipped archive byte, an induced mid-write failure.
* **`docs/pool-backup-restore.md` §15** -- what is implemented, the two forced deviations, and the
  exact four decisions required before anything is unsuspended.

## Found while testing

`sqlite3.connect("file:...?mode=ro")` **creates `-shm` next to the source**. The snapshot the plan
documents would have written into the pool it promises never to write to, and failed outright on
the read-only mount. The triple is now staged into the job's own `emptyDir` and snapshotted from
the copy; `PRAGMA integrity_check` on the copy catches a torn stage and fails the run.

## Two forced deviations from §4

1. **Namespace `dama`, not `backups`**: a PVC is only mountable from its own namespace, so the
   object the plan describes could not have read the volume it backs up. Isolation comes from the
   restore job mounting no pool volume.
2. **SQLite staging**, above.

## Still blocked (policy, not code)

1. A named passphrase holder and a physical location for the offline copy (§14.2) -- G0.9 cannot
   pass without it.
2. A decision that `F:` is owned by this system, with the stale Syncthing `.stfolder` re-checked
   (§14.3, G0.1c), and the sentinel uuid written by hand into the volume and the ConfigMap.
3. A custody delivery path for `/custody/passphrase` that is not a plain `Secret`, because
   `k3s-manifest-backup` dumps every Secret in cleartext nightly (§13.4).
4. The erasure-latency answer (§14.5).

Retention/GFS enforcement and the V5 `--stats` ladder are deliberately not implemented; both act on
generations that do not exist yet, and land with the unsuspend commit.

## Verification

`python -m pytest -q` -> 4940 passed, 46 skipped, and the only 2 failures are the same
`test_the_declared_size_matches_what_the_api_server_stored[hear-score-code|hear-tag-code]` pair
that fails identically on `main` on this workstation (they read the live cluster).
`recoupling_guard`, `check_contract_layout`, `freeze_contracts --check` and `coord_guard` are all
clean; the frozen k8s layout baseline was refreshed in its own commit.

## Entrega 4 de 4 dos Pedidos Internos — envio, recebimento e histórico

### A discussão que isto encerra
"Mandei tudo" contra "chegou faltando", por telefone, sem registro de nenhum dos dois lados. Agora as duas versões ficam gravadas lado a lado: o que o CD **separou** e o que a unidade **recebeu**. Quando divergem, o pedido fecha como **Concluído com divergência** e quem deu saída na carga é avisado.

### O CD dá saída
Só com todos os setores prontos. Enquanto falta item — de qualquer setor — a tela **diz quantos faltam** em vez de esconder o botão: o separador que terminou a parte dele precisa saber que está esperando outro setor, e não que o sistema quebrou. Depois do envio, a separação vira registro.

### A unidade confere
A conferência **começa em "tudo certo"** e o gerente aponta só a exceção — motivo, detalhe e foto tirada na hora. O caminho inverso viraria trinta toques para dizer "nada aconteceu", e a conferência não seria feita. Cada item mostra **o que o CD separou**, que é contra o que se confere. A divergência **não impede** fechar.

### O romaneio
A folha que viaja com a carga, agrupada **por setor do CD**, com quadradinho para conferir na caneta e **o que faltou impresso junto, com o motivo**. É a **mesma folha** para os dois lados — dois romaneios divergiriam com o tempo, e conferir carga contra papéis diferentes é pior do que não conferir.

### Acompanhar e repetir
Linha do tempo com as quatro etapas **sempre visíveis**, inclusive as que ainda não aconteceram: "onde está meu pedido?" é a pergunta que traz o gerente ali. **Repetir** preenche o carrinho e **diz qual produto ficou de fora** por ter saído do catálogo, em vez de devolver uma lista menor em silêncio.

### Detalhes
- Duas rotas (`/api/products/envio`, `/api/products/recebimento`) porque a matriz cobra módulos diferentes dos dois lados.
- O caminho da foto é o que o **servidor** salvou; o que o cliente mandar em `photo` é ignorado.
- Refazer a conferência limpa o apontamento retirado.
- **Sem migração**: os campos desta perna já entraram no schema na entrega 1.

### Verificação
As quatro portas **por código de saída**: `tsc` 0 · `next lint` 0 (os mesmos 7 avisos antigos de `no-img-element`) · `lint:ds` 0 · `npm test` 0 — **111 arquivos, 1077 testes**.

30 testes novos. Um deles **achou uma falha real**: `divergenciaLabel` devolve o próprio código quando não conhece (para um motivo antigo não sumir da tela do histórico), o que o tornava inútil como validador — motivo inventado passava. A validação virou `ehDivergencia`, com verificação de verdade.

## What

**1. The R416 flip's justification is retracted (audit, not a code change to the default).**
`REGENOLD_KG_POINT_TEXT` was flipped default-ON on a single-turn read of `ans_correctness_strict` **+8.0 pp**. Re-scored on the same 25 paired rows with `score_rows` (the published instrument, on a subset):

| variant | n | OFF | ON | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| published | 25 | 88.00 | 96.00 | **+8.00** |
| excl. judge-rep unstable (`rg_045`) | 24 | 91.67 | 95.83 | +4.17 |
| excl. generation-unstable (`rg_010`, `rg_045`) | 23 | 95.65 | 95.65 | **+0.00** |

The whole answer-correctness movement is **2 criteria out of 87**. `rg_045`'s credited limb appears in 2 of the judge's own 3 repetitions (`F T T`); **10 fresh generations per arm** credit `rg_010`'s Art. 14 *aim* limb at the same rate with the lever off (KG=0 6/10, KG=1 5/10; atomic 18/30 vs 15/30, Fisher p=1.00). The −3.3 pp conciseness cost is likewise not significant (ON longer on 14/25 rows, sign-test p=0.69), so the corrected board's −0.42 pp is not a measured cost either. The default is **unchanged**; the +8.0 is retracted in `kg_context._kg_point_text_enabled` and R416 §3, both of which said the lever buys it.

**2. Two defects that void a hard-mode batch.**
- `_trim_assistant_echoes`: our own >4 000-char answer 422d the pushback turn that replays it (Pydantic's per-message cap runs before the route), which froze the rolling history — **17 of 44 multi-turn rows scored zero on every axis**. The echo is now trimmed to the cap and recorded; the hard 422 stays for over-cap `user`/`system` content.
- The route now puts `stage2_served_by=` on the wire, so a post-hoc audit never infers the serving leg from the model name (the inference that mis-read `rg_010` as three fallback samples).

Bumps every `@fetchproxy/*` dependency to `^3.0.1`, with the lockfile updated to match. 3.0.1 ([fetchproxy#374](https://github.com/chrischall/fetchproxy/pull/374)) fixes:

- **Peer frames are capped:** the peer socket now has the same `maxPayload` limit as the host.
- **Load-induced drops are logged:** a frame refused because too many are in flight gets its own warning, instead of a drop that looks like a replay.
- **Identity writes are atomic:** the file is staged and renamed, so a crash can't leave a torn identity. The directory is also tightened to 0700 each time it is opened.

First-party dependency, so `fix` rather than `chore`: it ships the fixes to this MCP's users.

author: dominik-galus
body:
Token contract: typ: "access" | "refresh" on every token. common.auth.decode_access_token now refuses anything else, which closes the gap where a 7-day refresh token was a valid bearer for chat-service. decode_token is the new lower-level verifier (signature/exp/iss/aud only) that /refresh uses.

AUTH-5 POST /auth/refresh: {"refresh_token"} -> new {access_token, refresh_token, token_type}.
- new column refresh_tokens.family_id (migration 0003, backfills family_id = jti for existing rows), login starts a family, rotation carries it forward
- presented token already revoked -> whole family revoked, uniform 401 invalid_refresh_token
- access token, garbage, hash mismatch, deactivated user -> same uniform 401
- roles re-read from DB so the new access token reflects current roles
- refresh_limiter (rate_limit_refresh = 30, same pattern as the other three)

AUTH-6 POST /auth/logout: Authorization: Bearer <access> required, body {"refresh_token"} optional -> 204.
- access jti -> Redis denylist via existing revoke_token, TTL = exp − now + jwt_leeway_seconds, the verifier tolerates 30s past exp, without the leeway there's a 30s window where a logged-out token still works
- refresh family revoked only if the token belongs to the caller's sub; foreign/garbage/already-dead tokens still return 204. Idempotent.
- enforcement needed no new code: common.auth._resolve_identity already checks the denylist before every protected route

Tests (12 new + updates): rotation, replay kills family, replay only kills its own family, access-as-refresh, garbage, deactivated user, logout TTL bounds, require_auth rejects the logged-out token with "revoked", family revoked, missing bearer 401, foreign refresh ignored, idempotent.

Things worth knowing
- Concurrent refresh of the same token is treated as reuse, the loser kills the family. That's the strict, standard choice, if a client double-fires refresh it will get logged out.
- Chat-service tests needed "typ": "access" in their token helpers: expected consequence of the contract tightening, not a regression.

Captures the 2026-09-15 bench diagnosis of the i.MX8M warm-`reboot` hang so a future focused session starts from the finish line.

- **Ruled out (don't re-chase):** PMIC reset-target state — removed `rohm,reset-snvs-powered` from the active-slot DTB, verified gone from live `/proc/device-tree`, warm reboot **still hung**.
- **Already fixed (keep):** eMMC `RST_n_FUNCTION` 0x00→0x01 (bake into provisioning).
- **Root cause:** u-boot/SPL warm-boot DDR re-init limitation (matches NXP community reports) — needs imx-boot/TF-A/u-boot work, not a DT/runtime change.
- Candidate approaches, the proven serial + fast-DTB test methodology, and the deployment reality (imx-boot is not updated by A/B OTA — needs a separate flash).

**Workaround until fixed:** OTA installs remotely; activation via cold power-cycle.

author: dbn1972
body:
## Summary

Tranche 1 of **UX-012** — the follow-up gap filed by UX-002 (PR #1126) for its contradictory-badge pattern repeating fleet-wide: a page renders `<DataSourceBadge source={source} />` fed straight off the raw server `source`, while a sibling table/client component in the same directory independently derives cache state from its own `useSeededResource` call. A failed fetch with a usable offline cache can show both "Couldn't load — showing nothing" (page) and "Showing saved data" (table) at once for the same request.

The gap report estimated **"102 more" pairs**, explicitly flagged as "not yet individually verified per-instance." This PR does that verification and fixes as many as could be cleanly done in one pass.

## Real count vs. the gap report's estimate

Built `scripts/ci/contradictory-badge-guard.mjs` — enumerates every `page.tsx` that imports `DataSourceBadge` with the legacy `source=` prop AND has a sibling file in the same directory that independently imports `useSeededResource` (the exact necessary condition for the contradiction). No detection tool existed yet for this specific gap.

An earlier draft restricted siblings to filenames ending in `Table.tsx`/`Client.tsx` (mirroring the gap report's own wording) — found by hand-checking that this missed real pairs using other naming (`UserManagementPage.tsx`, `QueryResultsView.tsx`, `UsageDisplay.tsx`). Fixed to check every sibling file regardless of name.

**Real count as of this branch's fork point (`ac258e42`): 88 directory-sibling pairs across 16 modules, not 102** — plus 1 shared-component pair the gap report calls out separately (`_components/ModuleListPage.tsx` + `ModuleListTable.tsx`, a generic list-page scaffold consumed by 62 real pages). **89 total**, not 102. The guard's `--write-baseline` output is the authoritative per-module list, committed at `scripts/ci/contradictory-badge-baseline.json`.

## Fixed this tranche: 43 of 89 (14 modules, all fully cleared)

| Module | Fixed / Total |
|---|---|
| `_components/ModuleListPage`+`Table` (shared, 62 downstream pages) | 1/1 |
| billing | 1/1 |
| assets | 1/1 |
| helpdesk | 1/1 |
| analytics | 2/2 |
| hr | 3/3 |
| legal | 3/3 |
| citizen | 3/3 |
| platform-admin | 1/1 |
| projects | 1/1 |
| crm | 5/5 |
| grants | 7/7 |
| procurement | 7/7 |
| works | 7/7 |
| **Total** | **43/89** |

Fix pattern (identical to UX-002's own 5 repro sites): remove the page-level `<DataSourceBadge source={source} .../>`; the sibling table/client destructures `provenance`/`offline`/`cachedAt` from its own (already-present) `useSeededResource` call and renders `<DataSourceBadge provenance={...} .../>` itself. Two variants needed real judgment rather than a blind mechanical edit:
- **i18n preservation** (`hr/attendance`, `hr/attendance/regularisation`): these tables already had next-intl-translated cache-note text from UX-017. Piped that translated string through `DataSourceBadge`'s `message` override instead of letting it fall back to the component's hardcoded English default, so this fix doesn't regress UX-017's coverage.
- **Multi-tab tables with two independent hook calls** (`works/approvals` AA/TS registers, `works/execution` progress/issues): each tab has its own cache entry and can genuinely disagree with the other even though the page feeds both the same upstream `source`. The badge tracks whichever tab is actually visible, not an aggregate.

## Not done (46 remaining, left for a follow-up tranche)

The three largest modules, left as a clean follow-up scope given their size: **admin (11)**, **tenant-admin (10)**, **finance (25)**. Finance alone is more than half of what remains. `scripts/ci/contradictory-badge-baseline.json` is refreshed to 46 so the next tranche can re-verify fresh (counts drift as other PRs land) rather than trust this number blindly.

## Verification

- Every commit in this branch was individually verified before moving to the next module: scoped `vitest run` for the touched directory/module, plus a full `tsc --noEmit` re-run.
- **Final consolidated pass** (this PR's actual merge-base state): `npx vitest run` across every touched top-level directory — **346 of 347 test files pass, 1712 of 1715 tests pass**. The one failing file (`procurement/tenders/[id]/documents/page.test.tsx`, 3 tests, "No PageHeader export... on the `_components/ds` mock") is confirmed **pre-existing and unrelated**: `git diff ac258e42 HEAD --stat` for that file and for `_components/ds` is empty — neither was touched by any commit on this branch, and the mock was already incomplete at this branch's fork point, before UX-012 work started.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` for `apps/web`: clean, 0 errors (re-confirmed as the final step before opening this PR).
- Pre-existing tests that exercise the old page-level badge were updated in place where the coverage moved (`_components/ModuleListPage.test.tsx`, `crm/accounts/page.test.tsx`) — same call UX-002's own PR made for `crm/contacts/page.test.tsx`; no coverage lost, verified by re-running each updated file.
- No render-through-the-real-backend verification (this repo's `useSeededResource`/offline-cache path needs the full multi-service backend + IndexedDB up to exercise a genuine fetch failure) — same reasoning UX-002's own PR gave for using component-level tests instead of a manual click-through; every fixed table's data trace was verified by reading the actual code (not assumed): each one now derives `provenance` from its own `useSeededResource` call, the exact same call producing its visible rows.
- `docs/ENTERPRISE-GAP-REPORT-2026-09-07.md` intentionally not touched (out of scope for this PR per instruction — status update left for the gap owner).

Per this repo's own gap-report §5, this needs an independent review before merge — not self-merging.

author: yuldashevsardor
body:
Closes #108

Часть issue уже закрыл #41: типизированный доступ по «точечному» пути даёт `configValue()`, декоратора `@ConfigValue` нет. Этот PR доделывает остаток и по комментариям владельца перестраивает конфиг.

## Раскладка `src/bootstrap/config/`

- `config-container.ts`: `ConfigContainer<Values>(storage, builder)`, тип значений передаётся явно, без ограничения. В `async init()` он собирает значения, а через `get("bot.token")` отдаёт их. `get()` до `init()` — `ConfigContainerIsNotInitialized` (`config-container.errors.ts`).
- `config-container.types.ts`: общие типы конфига — `RawConfig` (снимок источника, с ним работают и storage, и builder), `Paths`, `ValueByPath`, `ConfigPath`, `ConfigValue` и алиас `CC = ConfigContainer<ConfigValues>`.
- `config-values.ts`: `ConfigValues` и собственные типы конфига `Environment`, `LoggerConfig`, `TelegramLimits`.
- `storage/`: интерфейс `ConfigStorage` с `load(): Promise<RawConfig>`, отдающим все переменные разом, и `ConfigEnvStorage` — копия `process.env` после `dotenv`.
- `builder/`: интерфейс `ConfigBuilder<Values>` с `build(raw): Values` и схема приложения `ConfigValuesBuilder`.
- `parser/`: `ConfigParser` (бывший `ConfigReader`) — строгий разбор снимка. Его создаёт билдер в `build()`.

## Поведение

- `ApplicationContext.create()` асинхронный: `new ConfigContainer<ConfigValues>(new ConfigEnvStorage(), new ConfigValuesBuilder())` и `await cc.init()`. Вызов посреди сборки ждёт её промис, упавшая сборка забывается, и следующий `create()` начинает с нуля.
- `Application` собирает контекст первой частью `setup()`. `stop()` посреди этой сборки сначала ждёт её, вне общего срока: срок и логгер берутся из конфига. Если сборка упала, `stop()` отдаёт её отказ.
- `configValue(path)` — обёртка над `get()`, восемь потребителей в умолчаниях конструкторов не менялись. Зависимость от контейнера везде называется `cc` и имеет тип `CC`.
- Проверки остались на старте, в `build()`. Проверка сна Runner стоит в `getRunner()`, поэтому её отказ по-прежнему приходит до чтения `BOT_TOKEN`. Проверка сроков остановки идёт после сборки всех значений. Если неверны сразу несколько переменных, первым может прийти другой отказ.

## Тесты и документация

- Спеки повторяют раскладку в `test/bootstrap/config/`. Добавлены тесты:
  - снимок `ConfigEnvStorage`;
  - `get()` до `init()`;
  - параллельный `create()`;
  - `stop()` посреди упавшей сборки контекста.
- `config.md`, карта директорий в `docs/architecture/README.md` и `application.md` (контекст, старт, остановка) обновлены.

## Проверки

`make check` — зелёный, 660 тестов.

⚠️ **Risk:** Untrusted or corrupted JSON payloads in `localStorage.getItem("profile")` could cause type errors or unexpected runtime behavior when accessing `profile?.auth?.key` without runtime type validation.

🛡️ **Solution:** Added explicit runtime type and schema checks after parsing `profileStr` to verify that `profile` is a non-null object (and not an array), `profile.auth` is a non-null object (and not an array), and `profile.auth.key` is a string before assigning `authKey`. Added corresponding unit test coverage in `src/content/index.test.ts`.

body:
## Summary

A wiped install (empty vault, no subscriptions, no VAPID key yet) previously showed a bare `Enable notifications` button sitting in scaffold markup and flat `No tasks in the vault.` / `No files in the vault.` lines — status statements with no path forward.

- **`FirstRunGuide`** (new component): shown at the top of `App.tsx`, ahead of the feed/vault toggle. Explains the two steps in plain language ("add a task to a Markdown file", "turn on notifications"), shows Home Screen install guidance when `isStandalone()` is false (SDD.md §6 risk: "the Home Screen install requirement is a real UX cliff"), and hosts the existing enrolment dialog. Once enrolled, it collapses to a quiet one-line confirmation ("Notifications are on for this device.") instead of disappearing or re-prompting — matching UX.md §1's "no motivational copy, no celebration" voice.
- **`push.ts`**: added `hasEnrolledPush()`/`markPushEnrolled()`, a `localStorage`-backed signal for "has this device enrolled before." There's no `GET /subscriptions` endpoint to ask the server (only `POST` create/unsubscribe in `schema/openapi.yaml`), so this is a client-only, best-effort memory — no backend change made or needed.
- **`push-enrolment-dialog.tsx`**: reads that flag to initialize state (`success` instead of `idle` for a returning enrolled device), calls `markPushEnrolled()` on a successful subscribe, and the trigger button now reads "Notifications on" once enrolled instead of always "Enable notifications." Copy was otherwise already plain-language and jargon-free (no "VAPID"/"service worker" leaks) — this task polishes wiring, not copy.
- **`task-feed.tsx` / `vault-browser.tsx`**: one-line empty-state copy changes only (no logic touched) — "No tasks yet. Add a `@directive`..." / "Your vault is empty. Add a Markdown file...".

Explicitly out of scope and untouched: quick actions, vault browser internals/tree logic, SSE, `schema/openapi.yaml`, generated types, and Go backend.

## What I verified live vs. by reading

- Started the real daemon (`go run ./cmd/vaktd`) against a genuinely empty `/tmp` vault dir and empty `/tmp` config dir — confirmed via `curl` that `GET /api/v1/tasks` → `[]`, `GET /api/v1/directories` → empty `children`, and a VAPID key was freshly provisioned.
- Ran `npm run dev:real` against that daemon and used headless Playwright (Chromium) to load the real page and screenshot/inspect it:
  - Fresh, non-standalone context: the guide card renders with the "Getting started" copy, the Home Screen instructions, and the enrolment dialog opens with the same Home Screen guidance (dialog correctly gates on `isStandalone()`).
  - Simulated standalone + a pre-set `localStorage` enrolment flag: the guide correctly collapses to "Notifications are on for this device."
  - Switched to the Vault tab: confirmed the new empty-state copy renders.
- `npm run build`, `npm run lint` (oxlint), `npm run format:check` (prettier) all pass — no new warnings introduced (two pre-existing `only-export-components` warnings in `ui/badge.tsx`/`ui/button.tsx` are unrelated).
- No Go files touched, so `make lint`/`go vet`/`go test` weren't run for this change.

## Test plan

- [x] Empty vault + empty config → daemon starts, provisions VAPID key
- [x] First-run guide renders above the feed on a fresh, non-standalone load
- [x] Home Screen guidance appears both in the guide and in the dialog when not standalone
- [x] Enrolment success (simulated via localStorage) collapses the guide to a quiet confirmation
- [x] Feed and Vault empty states show explanatory copy
- [x] `npm run build` / `lint` / `format:check` pass

author: juacker
body:
## The bug

The Anthropic entry in the provider catalog curated `claude-opus-4-1`.
Anthropic **retired that model on 2026-08-05**, and per Anthropic's own docs
"requests to retired models will fail". The provider form offered it anyway.
`claude-sonnet-4-5` was also curated; it is still active, but retires no sooner
than **2026-09-29**, two weeks out.

Source: <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations>
(checked 2026-09-15).

## Why it matters more than "a stale fallback"

I first wrote this up as the pre-key / probe-failed fallback. That was wrong,
and the review caught it. Nothing probes the live models endpoint on its own:

- `probeModels` is filled only in `handleLoadModels` (`AssistantProviderSettings.tsx:429`),
- which is wired to exactly one thing, the "Load models" button (`:937`),
- and is reset to `[]` on every entry into the form — `beginCreate` (`:323`),
  `chooseCatalogEntry` (`:332`), `chooseCliAdapter` (`:352`), `beginEdit` (`:374`),
  `closeForm` (`:407`).

`quickPickModels` (`:554`) is `probeModels` if non-empty, else `curatedModels`.
So the curated list is the **default** model quick-pick for every Anthropic
connection — creating one and editing an existing one — for users with a
perfectly valid key, unless and until they press that button. It is not a
degraded path; it is the path.

## The change

`claude-sonnet-4-5` → `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-opus-4-1` → `claude-opus-5`.
`claude-fable-5-1` (from #206) and `claude-haiku-4-5` are unchanged — Haiku 4.5
is still the current Haiku.

Plus a **revert guard**: no anthropic-protocol catalog entry may curate a known
retired id. Each retired model is listed as its dated snapshot plus the aliases
Anthropic published for it, and matched **by equality, never by prefix** —
`claude-opus-4-8` and `claude-sonnet-4-6` are active and both have a retired id
as a prefix.

The test is honest about its limit, in its own doc comment: it catches a
*revert*, not a *future* retirement, because the list only changes when a human
edits it. The nearest such date is `claude-haiku-4-5`, retiring no sooner than
2026-10-15. Closing that hole properly needs a live call to Anthropic, which
needs a key the app does not have at catalog-build time.

## Deliberately out of scope

- **`src-tauri/src/providers/mod.rs:439`** lists `anthropic/claude-opus-4`
  (retired 2026-06-15) in the OpenCode model table. That table reaches
  `get_provider_models` (`commands/provider.rs:116`, registered at `lib.rs:421`)
  and `src/api/client.ts:102`, but its only consumer is `ProviderSettings.tsx`,
  which is exported from the Settings barrel and **mounted by nothing**. No user
  can reach it. Refreshing a table whose only reader is unmounted would be
  maintaining a fiction; the right fix is to delete the chain, which I have on
  the backlog as a separate change.
- **`assistant/providers/cli.rs`** (Claude Code) curates bare family aliases —
  `fable` / `sonnet` / `opus` / `haiku` — which carry no version and are
  structurally immune to retirement. Correct as-is.
- Test fixtures using `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` are opaque strings never sent
  anywhere.
- Ordering: Fable 5.1 leads the list ahead of Opus 5, which Anthropic
  recommends as the general default. Pre-existing from #206, and the `<select>`
  preselects nothing, so it changes no default. Happy to reorder if you prefer.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.
- `cargo test --lib`: **1063 passed / 0 failed** (+1).
- `src/generated/bindings.ts` untouched.
- Mutation-checked, 4/4 killed: reintroducing `claude-opus-4-1`; reintroducing
  `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`; dropping the negation in the assert; narrowing the
  entry filter away from `anthropic`.
- Adversarial pre-PR review returned `ship_with_changes` on both shape and
  correctness. Every must-fix and should-fix is applied except the two scope
  decisions stated above, which are argued rather than silently skipped.

author: rmusser01
body: ## The bug A `⇄ Both ways` sync root reported **✓ Up to date** while a note edited in Chatbook had never reached the file on disk. Critique #4's P0. **Proven independent of wave 4 before a line was written.** The finding landed directly beside wave 4's own diff, and its symptom was the mirror image of a bug wave 4 had just fixed on the same surface — every available shortcut pointed the wrong way. A standalone probe built the *production* runtime, executor and controller over a real DB and a real folder, and the identical file was run against a `git archive` of the pre-wave tree. Same row, same status line, same plan on both. Pre-existing, proven. ## The fix `note_changed(note_id)` on `NotesSyncRuntimeOwner` maps a note to its admitted roots through the store's existing binding index and calls the existing `schedule_hint`. Link 2 of the chain was a **missing read**, not a missing publisher — building the publisher the triage implied would have recreated the two-publishers bug this wave hit twice. Three rounds of review found more than the original finding: - **A stopped runtime wore "✓ Up to date".** `refresh_roots` already read `runtime.status` one line above the projection and threw it away — the *same* missing-read shape as the P0 itself. A root whose runtime is not watching now wears **⚠ Sync stopped**, and only that reassuring label is rewritten, so **Check changes** — the way out — stays offered. - **A *starting* runtime then wore "⚠ Sync stopped".** `_reconcile` publishes per-root `up_to_date` throughout its root loop and sets `active` only after it, so a just-reconciled root read as stopped mid-startup. A wrong reassuring label is the defect this task exists to remove; a wrong alarming one is the same defect wearing the other hat. It uses the existing **◌ Starting**. The pin parametrises all six statuses and shows only that case changing, with `(status, next_action)` asserted unmoved. - **`_restate_root` looked the row up in one page.** Fixed inside `_restate_root` rather than at the call site, which also repairs a pre-existing pause/resume miss — one word, both callers. ## Scope, stated rather than implied This closes the path the critique walked: an editor save of an already-bound note, and every path after a check. It does **not** close the other note-write seams. The enumeration is **18 live write seams — 1 covered, 17 not (6 updates + 11 creates) — plus 2 dead**, and the uncovered ones are filed as **task-32633**, which AC#2 names. That number moved three times inside this task (12+1 → 14/1/13 → 17 → 18). It was finally settled by two independent derivations from opposite directions — a four-pass AST sweep verb-inward, and a reviewer's SQL-outward reverse-reference index — meeting at 18. So the docstring no longer carries a bare number: it dates the count, says it moved three times, and says re-derive. The method is written beside it, with the two traps that caused every undercount — including one this branch shipped **wrong** and corrected in the last commit, because a wrong trap is worse than no trap once it gets trusted. ## Evidence - Every pin's RED captured by reverting the fix, not by assertion. `assert '⚠ Sync stopped' == '◌ Starting'`; `assert 'Checking changes…' == '⚠ Offline · Next: Reconnect folder.'` - Guide copy: three of five bolded control labels in the touched block had **zero** hits in the tree (`Save as document` cut, `Save as note` → **Save as Note**, `Import notes from files` → **Import once**). The rest of the page was then audited — 225 bolded strings; the four stale labels found there are pre-existing and left to their own task. - `Tests/Library/` against a detached `origin/dev` worktree at the same commit, same command both sides: **4 failed / 3575 passed / 2 skipped on both, exact name identity.** Zero branch-only reds. `./scripts/preflight.sh` exit 0. - The dev merge was proved clean by **content**, not by a conflict list: normalised hunks show `diff(dev→HEAD)` ≡ this branch's own lines and `diff(branch→HEAD)` ≡ dev's own lines, byte-identical. A dry-run conflict list has missed silent bad merges in this repo before. ## Merge note Touches `tldw_chatbook/Notes/notes_sync_runtime.py`, which PR #2691 also changed. dev is merged in and both sides were checked — #2691's `TYPE_CHECKING` block and `_receipt_ledger_reader` sit top-and-bottom of this branch's `note_changed`/`schedule_hint` region. `UI latency guardrails` is red at the base (ADR-097 ratchet, 977 vs 975 on dev itself) — tracked as **task-32644**. Compare its *number*, not its pass/fail bit. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01CGqZiB3yVKnbqnRNR28p2L --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes task-32604's P0: a note edited in Chatbook inside an active "Both ways" root never reached its file on disk, while the root row kept reading "✓ Up to date." - A save in the Library editor now writes the note to its synced file on its own, without needing **Check changes**. - A root whose sync runtime has stopped now says "⚠ Sync stopped" instead of "✓ Up to date"; **Check changes** stays offered as the way out. - A runtime still starting now reads "◌ Starting" rather than a false "⚠ Sync stopped". - **Check changes** now opens the review it built when there are effects; a clean root reads "Nothing to review." - The review count now includes deletion and managed-placement groups, and row lookups work across all pages rather than just the visible one. **Scope** This covers the editor save of an already-bound note plus everything after a manual check. The other 17 note-write seams — new note, Console Save as Note, import, delete, restore, and assistant tools — still don't signal sync and are tracked in task-32633, which now carries the settled enumeration with its derivation method. dev is merged in. Written for commit 31b6f7e5c561d308971aabdd191b64144a423bf0. Summary will update on new commits.

Tranches 6–14 are validated and archived locally, while merged PRs #6 and #7 contain the temporary archive-upload staging content. This PR publishes the recovered checkpoint and removes that staging content from the proposed tree.

## Changes

- Publish the recovered Tranches 6–14 source, original owner evidence archives, native reference results, acceptance reviews, and documented limitations.
- Include NWK freshness and MAC reservation/timing corrections, repeatable campus and multiseed diagnostics, and controlled contention, relay, loss/recovery, and ACK-boundary fixtures.
- Remove the 13 temporary transport files introduced through PRs #6 and #7, including the archive-upload workflow and split archive parts; preserve the complete original evidence archives under their final evidence paths.
- Exclude Tranches 15–16. Preserve the accepted PHY/ECC implementation and baseline exclusions for battery, supervisory behavior, and BBN routing.

## Validation and provenance

The independently verified recovered payload contains **1,869 files**, with Git tree `5f82983bbde655c77228c6b9367803037a6728d2`. Published checkpoint: [`6c31d033187889764bd09bf7d9f6d50987168c68`](https://github.com/mjburke4/CSR-Project-MATLAB-Sim/commit/6c31d033187889764bd09bf7d9f6d50987168c68). GitHub’s full recursive tree was fetched back and all 1,869 file paths, modes and blob hashes matched.

- All 1,869 recorded Git blob hashes match the recovered files.
- All 1,847 issued-package SHA-256 bindings match.
- All 285 owner-validated source bindings, including 144 MATLAB files, and all 317 reference bindings match.
- The Tranche 14 r2 candidate SHA-256 is `4bb51710031ead9d8d7c6b718fb41fd9224156b46076111e4e9c161aebbcc69f`.
- The original accepted T14 owner archive is preserved at `evidence/t14/owner.zip`: 177,661 bytes; SHA-256 `1b351bc8cf356ace8fe5e60413cba30812b5c3fcb4d71cede29d356102fe4241`.
- The owner’s MATLAB R2025a focused T14 gate passed **109/109 tests**, **222 structural checks**, all **6 cases**, and **18/18 prescribed application deliveries**. Final diagnostic MAC DATA/ACK queues drained.
- The publication-time supplemental audit rechecked the archive CRC, all 53 returned artifact hashes and sizes, all 42 per-case artifact files, and reconstruction of the six aggregate tables. All 271 validated T13 source files, including 138 MATLAB files, remain unchanged.
- The three large original T7/T8/T10 archive blobs were verified and uploaded by successful [transport run 34997194947](https://github.com/mjburke4/CSR-Project-MATLAB-Sim/actions/runs/34997194947).
- All 16 carried ZIP member inventories were inspected; none contains T15–16 paths.

The earlier handoff cited tree `8273b24daec722bcab02820ba72866879d940cd5` and 1,871 files. That exact earlier tree was not independently reproduced. This publication identifies the recovered, verified payload explicitly and does **not** claim equality to the earlier tree. Original candidate/package metadata remains unchanged; `evidence/t14/milestone.json` records the final focused milestone disposition.

No fresh MATLAB or ns-3 execution was performed for publication. The owner’s runtime results and their limitations remain distinguishable from the publication integrity checks.

## Remaining engineering limits

T14 retains **28 strict unmatched comparison rows** across overlapping comparison families. Its continuous-arithmetic case produces a one-ULP ingress residual and one extra ACK; the local nanosecond-conversion fixture restores the native event sequence in that case. This is a focused diagnostic, not full-network or exact numerical parity acceptance. Campus, RF interference, routing convergence, native MATLAB packet integration, and broader performance gates remain separate work.

This PR is for owner review. No merge or auto-merge is authorized.

🚨 **Severity:** ENHANCEMENT
💡 **Vulnerability:** Found `Math.random()` being used to generate unique keys for React components.
🎯 **Impact:** While used for React keys and not currently a high-risk vector, `Math.random()` is not cryptographically secure and can be predictable. Replacing it ensures better defense-in-depth and eliminates a pattern that could be copied to security-sensitive contexts.
🔧 **Fix:** Replaced `Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)` with `crypto.randomUUID()`.
✅ **Verification:** Ran `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, and `npm run test` successfully.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## What this answers

> *"Find me a new production free hosting tool other than Netlify."*

The earlier shortlist contained five claims that are wrong or stale. This PR replaces it with a verified decision, then makes the move mechanical instead of a rewrite.

### Recommendation

**Northflank Sandbox** — permanently free, **always-on compute (no cold-start sleep)**, commercial use permitted, 2 services + 1 PostgreSQL addon + 2 cron jobs. Runs this repository unchanged via the new portable runtime. Runbook: `deploy/NORTHFLANK.md`.

**Runner-up:** Oracle Cloud **Always Free** (2 OCPU / 12 GB ARM, 200 GB disk, 10 TB egress) with the included `deploy/docker-compose.yml` + Caddy TLS. Runbook: `deploy/ORACLE_CLOUD_ALWAYS_FREE.md`.

### Corrections to the previous advice (all verified 2026-09-15)

| Previous claim | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| Fly.io has 3 free VMs | Free allowances retired for new organisations on 2024-10-07; new accounts pay from the first machine-second |
| Vercel is the closest equivalent to Netlify | Vercel **Hobby is non-commercial only**; a subscription product requires Pro. Eligibility rule, not a traffic limit |
| Render has a free 1 GB Postgres | It is **deleted 30 days** after creation; the free web service sleeps after 15 idle minutes (750 h/month) |
| Supabase free tier works in production | Free projects **auto-pause after 7 idle days** until a human resumes them |
| Oracle Always Free is 4 OCPU / 24 GB | **Halved to 2 / 12** for new non-PAYG tenancies (June 2026); storage and egress unchanged |
| Cloudflare Pages is the top pick | Functionally strong, but the Self-Serve Subscription Agreement **§2.2.1(h)** forbids processing/collecting credit-card information on Free Services — a payments-specific caveat documented in `HOSTING_OPTIONS.md` |

### What was built

The handlers were only ever Netlify-coupled through two primitives, both now shimmed — **`netlify/functions/**` is unchanged**:

- `runtime/loader.mjs` — maps `@netlify/database` to a portable driver, resolves Netlify-style extensionless TS imports
- `runtime/database.mjs` — the `db.sql` tagged-template contract over `pg` with real bind parameters, TLS policy, connection discovery, single-connection transactions and the migration engine
- `runtime/router.mjs` — routes derived from each function's own `config.path`, static allow-list (404 for archives/sources/dotfiles), `netlify.toml` header + cache parity, gzip, ETag/304, traversal defence
- `runtime/migrate.mjs` — applies the existing `netlify/database/migrations/*/migration.sql` files to any PostgreSQL, tracked in `commercial_schema_migrations`, idempotent and drift-detecting
- `runtime/server.mjs` + `Dockerfile` — binds `0.0.0.0:8080` first, then reports database/config readiness

Also fixed: `authProviderConfig()` returned an opaque **500** when Supabase variables were missing; it now throws a **503** with an actionable hint, consistent with `verifyCommercialUser`.

### Verification

`npm test` → **54 assertions green** (19 pre-existing Netlify, 5 Stripe signature, **30 new**), `npm run check` clean, `npm ci` consistent.

The new suite boots the real server against a stub Supabase instance and asserts: routing parity for all 15 declared routes, session cookies (Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite), refresh + sign-out, Stripe HMAC verification over the real signing path, fail-closed 503s for unconfigured billing/auth, migration idempotency + drift detection, path-traversal and archive-exposure defences.

**Not verified here:** execution against a live PostgreSQL (no server available in this environment — the SQL path is exercised through a mock driver) and the Docker image build (no Docker daemon). Both are the first steps in the runbooks.

### Distribution artifact

`LearnForge_COMMERCIAL_MONETIZATION_COMPLETE_v17.1.zip` — 53 files, 2,297,699 bytes, sha256 `44bbbe9a02cd1fd31dfc31315f132f677a6337ca2a7488c7258532560b933fae`. `npm run package` now emits the SHA-256 and includes `runtime/`, `deploy/`, `Dockerfile` and `HOSTING_OPTIONS.md`.

### Security note worth acting on

`netlify.toml` sets `publish = "."`, so the whole repository root is the publish directory — the two committed ~2.2 MB release archives, the `.mts` handler sources and CI config are *eligible* for static serving. Recommend confirming with `curl -I https://<site>/LearnForge_COMMERCIAL_MONETIZATION_COMPLETE_v17.0.zip` and adding deny rules if it returns 200. The portable runtime blocks all of it by allow-list (asserted by tests).

## Changes

Grouped experiments now retain distinct well and field identities from discovery through report generation. Repeated field basenames use source-relative identities, saved output stems resolve the correct images and masks, and resumed native reports must match the current attempt and source digests.

Reports resolve the RNA spot-count alias and support optional significance brackets, readable footer lines, and configurable speaker-note trailers. New pure postrun helpers validate channel indices, transform individual image planes, preserve sampling flags, and integrate supplied raster-footprint unions without counting duplicate pixels twice.

The light test matrix now installs required report dependencies, treats optional GUI and external recorded-data fixtures explicitly, and tests frozen-output guards with temporary junctions or symlinks. Frozen markers are detected regardless of filename case, and overlay annotations have a portable font fallback.

## Validation

- Relevant hierarchy and report suite: 151 passed, 1 deselected.
- Postrun helpers after independent review and additional boundary checks: 18 passed.
- Compatibility checks: 14 passed.
- External recorded-data tests use explicit fixture environment variables and skip when those fixtures are unavailable; generic frozen-output and report tests remain active.
- The full repository passes Ruff. GitHub CI passes the light test/build/wheel-smoke matrix on Windows and Ubuntu with Python 3.10 and 3.12, plus dependency-resolution checks. The optional weekly heavy-stack jobs are skipped on this PR.
- Independent review covered hierarchy/report behavior, strict channel inputs, two-dimensional transforms, and footprint overlap accounting. Outgoing history starts from public main and contains no run datasets or acquisition presets.

| | from | to |

| Workflow `java-version` | 17 | 25 |

The workflows move with the build deliberately: a build targeting 25 is no use if CI still hands it a 17 JVM.

`./gradlew clean build` passes on JDK 25 (Zulu 25.0.4).

author: gmcdowelljr
body:
## Summary

Fix a safety bug where uncolorable or failed-filter link categories present anywhere in a linked document—but with zero elements in the current view—would hide entire link instances, taking down genuinely colorable categories sharing that placement.

The fix scopes the hide decision to categories actually present in the view by collecting view-scoped link element proxies once per capture and checking category presence against that list, rather than relying solely on document-wide category discovery.

## Key Changes

- **New function `_collect_view_scoped_link_proxies()`**: Wraps `collect_all_linked_elements()` with error handling, returning `(proxies, ok)` to distinguish "scan failed" from "this view genuinely has no LINK elements"

- **New function `_instances_to_hide_for_uncolorable_categories()`**: Implements the scoped hide decision:
  - When view-scoped scan succeeds: hides only placements whose uncolorable categories actually have elements in this view
  - When scan fails: falls back to conservative document-wide hide (fails safe, never open)
  - Logs diagnostic warnings for both spared placements and fallback scenarios

- **Updated `_collect_near_face_w_data()`**: Accepts optional `link_proxies` parameter to reuse the per-capture scan, avoiding duplicate collection work

- **Updated `export_color_id_buffer_view()`**: 
  - Collects view-scoped proxies once per capture
  - Passes them to both the uncolorable-category hide decision and near-face-W collection
  - Ensures hide decision is final before near-face-W runs

- **Expanded `_FALLBACK_EXCLUDED_CATEGORY_NAMES`**: Added empirically confirmed non-physical reference categories (Internal Origin, Project Base Point, Survey Point, Sheets, Project Information, Material Assets, Materials, Legend Components) that report as Model but carry no visible geometry

## Implementation Details

- The view-scoped scan is paid exactly once per capture, maintaining the module's "deliberate, view-local cost for correctness, only when needed" bargain
- Comprehensive test coverage added for the new hide decision logic, including edge cases (absent categories, multiple placements, DWG proxies, scan failures)
- All error paths record diagnostics per CLAUDE.md's "no silent failure" principle
- Follows existing patterns for exception handling and diagnostic reporting

---

## Addendum — revisions after review (commits `fa42f91`, `757e71b`)

Everything above describes the first commit (`544c060`). Two rounds of Codex review found real defects in it, and the design changed materially in response. Where the two disagree, this addendum is current.

### What changed from the description above

**`_collect_view_scoped_link_proxies()` returns `(proxies, status)`, not `(proxies, ok)`.**

**The hide decision no longer reads the proxy list at all.** It reads a presence set carried on the status object. The proxy list remains near-face-W's input only. The two deliberately disagree, for the reason in the second finding below.

**The category exclusions are in both lists, not just the names one.** `_EXCLUDED_BIC_NAMES_GLOBAL` now carries the matching `OST_*` ids alongside the human-readable names.

### Finding 1 — partial link scans reported as success (P1, fixed in `fa42f91`)

`collect_all_linked_elements()` does not raise for most of its failure modes. Enumeration failure, an unresolvable placement transform, a per-placement exception, the 2024+ collector's outer `except`, the clipping collector's early returns, and per-element swallows all produce a quietly **short** list. The original `(proxies, ok)` only caught an escaping exception, so a truncated scan reported `ok=True` and the hide decision read "absent from the list" as "absent from the view" — the exact fail-open its own docstring prohibits.

New `LinkCollectionStatus` threads a completeness signal down the RVT collection chain as an optional `status=` argument. Additive: every existing call site is unchanged. Each shortening path marks it incomplete and records `(callsite, detail)`, so a `False` can say *what* was missed.

Two paths are deliberately **not** marked: the spatial-filter fallback over-includes rather than truncating, and an unloaded link never reaches `link_category_to_instances` in the first place, so it can never be the subject of a hide decision.

### Finding 2 — geometry failures misread as category absence (P1, fixed in `757e71b`)

After an element passes the inclusion policy and the view-scoped collector has already resolved it as visible, three further skips still discard it: `skip_no_bbox`, `skip_bad_bbox`, `skip_transform_failed`. Each produced a complete-looking scan with the element missing.

The review offered two remedies. Marking every proxy-construction failure incomplete was rejected as self-defeating — a single bbox-less element anywhere in any link would degrade the whole scan, forcing the conservative document-wide hide often enough that view scoping would stop meaning anything, reinstating the over-hiding this PR exists to fix.

The root cause was that presence was being derived from a structure built *after* the geometry step. A bbox failure is not a presence fact. So `LinkCollectionStatus.link_presence` records `(category_id, link_instance_id)` pairs at the candidate site in both collectors, upstream of all bbox and proxy work. `rvt_complete` now covers only the failures that occur *before* presence can be recorded: a link that never enumerated, a placement with no transform, an element that raised before its category could be read.

Side effect: DWG imports can no longer enter the presence set structurally — `_collect_from_dwg_imports` takes no `status` argument — so what was a `source_type` filter is now enforced by signature.

### Finding 3 — localized category names (P2, fixed in `fa42f91`)

`Category.Name` is localized. The 8 English literals match nothing on a non-English Revit, so without stable-id coverage those categories re-enter LINK discovery as uncolorable and reintroduce the bug this PR fixes. Added `OST_InternalOrigin`, `OST_ProjectBasePoint`, `OST_SharedBasePoint`, `OST_Sheets`, `OST_ProjectInformation`, `OST_MaterialAssets`, `OST_Materials`, `OST_LegendComponents`. Names retained as coverage for a BIC that does not resolve on a given Revit version.

### Verification status

Unit-tested: 541 passing, with the same 2 pre-existing failures this branch inherited (`test_occlusion_contract`, `test_single_areal_extraction_contract` — both unrelated to this change).

**Not verified, and should not be read as verified:**

- Whether view 19293485 actually renders Walls post-fix. That needs a live Revit run.
- The `OST_InternalOrigin` and `OST_MaterialAssets` spellings, which could not be checked outside Revit. An unresolvable `BuiltInCategory` name is skipped by `_try_get_category_id`, so a wrong spelling degrades to name-only coverage rather than breaking — but it degrades *silently*, so it warrants a glance on the next live run.

author: davideweaver
body:
## Summary

Agents working in this repo tended to explain their work in file and symbol
names rather than in terms of the system — which made it hard to tell, at a
glance, whether a change was architecturally right.

The cause was a gap in the docs: the project glossary described the product in
detail but never named the platform layer underneath it — the host, what
extensions are allowed to reach, and the contract between them. With no shared
words for that layer, the only precise thing left to point at was a filename.

Two changes, both documentation only:

1. The glossary now defines that vocabulary, so a change to the host/extension
   contract can be described in shared terms.
2. The agent guide now asks for the architectural implication first, with file
   paths as supporting evidence rather than the explanation.

No code or behavior changes, and nothing here needs sequencing against other
work. This applies to every coding agent used on the project, not just one —
the guidance lives in the tool-neutral agent guide the others already read.

## Details

### Glossary — `docs/domain-language.md`

New `### Platform Architecture` section, placed first under `## Language`
because every other cluster sits on it. Nine terms in the existing
`**Term**: / _Avoid_:` format, each cited to the ADR it derives from:

| Term | Anchored to |
| --- | --- |
| Host | — |
| Extension Host | ADR 0001 |
| Extension | ADR 0007 |
| Public surface | ADR 0004 |
| `ctx` (ExtensionContext) | — |
| Privileged surface | ADR 0013 |
| Trust tier | ADR 0013 |
| Bundled extension | ADR 0019 |
| Boundary | — |

Two distinctions the section makes explicit, both of which are live traps:

- **"Extension Host" does not carry its VS Code meaning here.** ADR 0001
  rejected process isolation and runs extensions in-process, but the package
  inherited the name. Anyone reasoning from the VS Code sense assumes a sandbox
  that does not exist. The entry says so, and the `Boundary` entry reinforces it
  — the boundary is enforced at build time by the package graph and at lint
  time, not at runtime.
- **Bundled is about delivery; trust tier is about capability.** A `silo.*`
  extension is bundled yet no more privileged than a third-party one, which is
  the property that keeps "first-party = third-party" mechanically true rather
  than aspirational.

### Agent guide — `AGENTS.md`

New `## Explaining your work` section ahead of `## Engineering principles`:
lead with what moved on the host/extension boundary (including "nothing moved",
which is often the most useful sentence), use the glossary's nouns and add a
term when the right one is missing, treat paths as supporting evidence, and be
brief. Scoped to prose — explicitly not a reason to reduce the precision of a
code comment or an ADR.

`## Architecture boundaries` picks up a pointer to the new glossary section, so
the mechanics and the vocabulary stay linked rather than drifting.

### No ADR

Documentation of decisions already recorded in ADRs 0001/0004/0007/0013/0019 —
it introduces no new decision, and fails all three prongs of the
ADR-worthiness test in `docs/decisions/README.md`.

### Test plan

- `pnpm lint` (boundary gate) — clean, via the pre-commit hook.
- `pnpm test` — 11/11 tasks green, including `apps/docs`
  `doc-indexes.sync.test.ts` (202 assertions) and `architecture.sync.test.ts`,
  which are what would catch a docs-index or architecture-map desync.
- `npx prettier --check` on both files — clean.
- Docs-only: no source, SDK surface, or generated API reference touched, so no
  `pnpm docs:api` run and no roadmap badge to flip.
