author: mriss
body:
## Description

Fixes a pre-existing defect found during live validation of `staging.yml` (issue #55): snapshot staging builds of `dsh` failed with a PDF/skin-version incompatibility.

### Root Cause

`dsh/pom.xml`'s own `deployment` profile binds `maven-pdf-plugin:pdf` against `${project.build.directory}/generated-site`, expecting that directory to be populated (via `copy-site-resources-for-pdf`) and its `site.xml` skin version patched (via `fix-pdf-skin-version`, `2.0.0` → `1.12.0`, for compatibility with the bundled Doxia Sitetools `1.11.1`).

However, both of those generic helper steps previously lived **only** in `products/pom.xml`'s `product-release-deployment` profile, which is not activated during snapshot staging (`project-staging.yml` only passes `-Ddeployment`). As a result, `dsh`'s PDF generation during staging read an unpatched/incomplete `generated-site`, causing:
```
RendererException: Cannot use skin: has 2.0.0 Doxia Sitetools prerequisite, but current is 1.11.1
```

This is **not** specific to `dsh` and is **not** introduced by the GitHub Actions migration — the legacy `ProjectStagingJenkinsfile` used the same `-Ddeployment -Drelease.type=rcs` flags and would hit the identical failure for any product whose own `deployment` profile runs PDF generation.

### Fix

Moved `copy-site-resources-for-pdf` (maven-resources-plugin) and `fix-pdf-skin-version` (maven-antrun-plugin) from `product-release-deployment` into a new, generic `deployment` profile in `products/pom.xml`. Since `-Ddeployment` is always passed alongside `-Dproduct-release-deployment` during `release:perform` (see its `<arguments>`), this covers both snapshot staging and full releases without duplicating executions. Both steps are safe no-ops (`failonerror=false` / no `site.xml` present) for products that don't run the PDF plugin at all (e.g. `mail-processor-service`, which has it commented out).

### Validation

- `mvn -f products/pom.xml validate` — POM is well-formed.
- Installed the fixed `parent-poms`/`products` locally and ran `mvn -Ddeployment package` against a disposable clone of `dsh`: PDF generation now succeeds, producing `target/site/pdf/README.pdf` and other site PDFs (previously failed with the `RendererException` above).

### References
- Parent issue: MRISS-Projects/parent-poms#55

author: richardfergusoniv
body:
Automatic review is firing on every PR, but producing nothing. This fixes that.

## Symptom

PRs #70 and #71 looked un-reviewed. They weren't — `claude-review` ran on both and finished **green having posted nothing**, which is indistinguishable from the workflow never firing.

| PR | Result | Duration | Turns | Denials | Posted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #70 | success | 29s | **3** | **1** | nothing |
| #71 | success | ~49s | — | — | nothing |

No reviews, no issue comments, no inline comments — only Vercel's bot comment on each.

## Cause

The workflow `/install-github-app` generated allowed exactly one tool:

```yaml
claude_args: '--allowedTools "mcp__github_inline_comment__create_inline_comment"'
```

That is an **allowlist**, so the reviewer:

- **could not open a single file** — no `Read`, `Grep` or `Glob`. It only saw whatever diff reached its prompt, with no ability to check a caller, a test, or the surrounding code.
- **had no output channel except line-anchored inline comments** — nothing it could say about the change as a whole.

`num_turns: 3` with `permission_denials_count: 1` on #70 is the signature: it reached for a tool, was refused, and stopped. Three turns is not a review.

#70 is the worst case for this — a research PR that is mostly a new document. Nothing worth pinning an inline comment to, and no way to say so. Silence.

## Fix

```yaml
claude_args: '--allowedTools "mcp__github_inline_comment__create_inline_comment,mcp__github_comment__update_claude_comment,Read,Grep,Glob"'
```

- `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob` — the reviewer can read the code it is reviewing.
- `update_claude_comment` — a summary channel for findings that don't belong on one line. In agent mode (this workflow sets `prompt:`) the `github_comment` MCP server is installed **only when the allowlist names it**, so listing the tool is what enables it. Verified in `src/mcp/install-mcp-server.ts`: `shouldIncludeCommentServer = !isAgentMode || hasGitHubCommentTools`.
- `github_ci` deliberately left out — that server additionally requires a workflow token this job does not grant (`(!isAgentMode || hasGitHubCITools) && isPR && hasWorkflowToken`), and this workflow has no `additional_permissions: actions: read`. Adding CI-log access would be a separate, wider change.

`Bash`, `Write` and `Edit` stay withheld, so there is still no path to push a commit or call the merge API — consistent with the constraint set in #68.

## Note on #68

#68 widened `claude.yml`'s allowlist for the assistant and left this file alone, on the reasoning that it "already carried the equivalent restriction and needed no change." That was wrong in a way worth naming: for the *assistant*, tight bounds were the goal; for the *reviewer*, the same bounds remove the ability to do the job. Same mechanism, opposite intent.

## Triggers unchanged

Drafts are still reviewed on open — `types: [opened, synchronize, ready_for_review, reopened]` is untouched, per the preference that drafts get reviewed.

## Verification

- File parses; `allowed_bots` still `cursor`; trigger list unchanged
- MCP server install conditions checked against `src/mcp/install-mcp-server.ts` rather than assumed
- Tool name `update_claude_comment` confirmed in `src/mcp/github-comment-server.ts`

**After merge:** the next PR opened (or pushed to) should produce either inline comments or a summary. If it still posts nothing, the remaining suspect is the `code-review` plugin's own expectations rather than the allowlist, and I'd want the run's full output (`show_full_output: true`) to go further.

No application code, tests, projection knobs, or sealed-release settings touched.

author: jaylfc
body:
## Card

tsk-szzkro (P90 blocker: a real tester's phone install is failing on this right now)

## Defect

`pyproject.toml`'s `proxy` extra pinned:

```
"pyroscope-io>=0.8.16,<1.0; sys_platform != 'win32'",
```

That range contains exactly one release, 0.8.16, which publishes only macOS and manylinux (glibc) wheels — no musllinux wheel and no sdist. On any musl host (Alpine, postmarketOS) that resolves to zero installable files and `pip install -e ".[proxy]"` fails, killing the controller install. This is not device-specific — Alpine x86_64 fails identically. musllinux wheels only exist from 1.0.3, which the `<1.0` cap excluded.

Verified before making any change: `git grep -n pyroscope origin/dev` returns only `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` — no `.py` file in the tree imports or references it.

## Fix

Removed the `pyroscope-io` line from the `proxy` extra (not widened to `>=1.0.3`) and regenerated `uv.lock` with `uv lock`. Widening was rejected deliberately: nothing in the codebase calls this library, so there is no reason to accept 0.x→1.x API-compat risk for an unused dependency — deleting it is strictly safer than repinning it.

## Red evidence

Reproduction against the bare offending range on a musllinux target:

```
$ pip install --dry-run --only-binary=:all: --platform musllinux_1_2_aarch64 --python-version 3.13 --target /tmp/pyro-probe 'pyroscope-io>=0.8.16,<1.0'
ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement pyroscope-io<1.0,>=0.8.16 (from versions: 1.0.3, 1.0.4, 1.0.5, 1.0.6, 1.0.8, 1.0.9, 1.0.10, 1.0.11, 1.0.12, 1.2.0, 1.2.1, 1.2.2, 1.2.3)
ERROR: No matching distribution found for pyroscope-io<1.0,>=0.8.16
```

This confirms the claim directly: every musllinux-wheel-bearing release is >=1.0.3; nothing in the `<1.0` range has one.

Dry-run against the whole fixed `proxy` extra on the same musllinux target (from repo root, `pip install --dry-run --only-binary=:all: --platform musllinux_1_2_aarch64 --python-version 3.13 --target /tmp/pyro-probe-full -e '.[proxy]'`): `pyroscope-io` no longer appears anywhere in the resolution (confirmed by grep on the full output). However, the full extra does **not** fully resolve on this platform/Python combo — it now fails on a separate, pre-existing, unrelated package:

```
ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement granian<3.0,>=2.7.4; extra == "proxy" (from tinyagentos[proxy])
ERROR: No matching distribution found for granian<3.0,>=2.7.4; extra == "proxy"
```

**CORRECTION (lead, post-review): the `granian` failure above is a PROBE ARTEFACT, not a real blocker. Do not card it.**

`granian` publishes `musllinux_1_1_aarch64` wheels across the entire pinned range — verified directly from the PyPI release listing for 2.7.4, 2.8.0 and 2.8.3 — and ships an sdist as well. It is installable on the target device.

The dry-run failed only because `--platform musllinux_1_2_aarch64` makes pip do **exact platform-tag matching**, so it refuses a `musllinux_1_1` wheel that a real musl 1.2 host accepts normally (musllinux tags are backward compatible; `--platform` does not expand the compatibility chain). The flawed probe command originated in the card, so the miss is mine, not the implementer's.

The `pyroscope-io` conclusion is unaffected and stands on evidence that does not depend on this probe: release 0.8.16 publishes exactly four files — `macosx_11_0_arm64`, `macosx_11_0_x86_64`, `manylinux2014_aarch64`, `manylinux2014_x86_64` — with **no musllinux wheel of any tag and no sdist**, enumerated straight from the PyPI release listing. The pinned range contains only that one version, so it genuinely has zero installable files on musl.

Net effect: `pyroscope-io` was the tester's only dependency-resolution blocker, and this PR removes it.

## Test — before/after

New offline regression test: `tests/test_proxy_extra_no_pyroscope.py`. It parses `pyproject.toml` with `tomllib` and asserts `pyroscope-io` is absent from the `proxy` extra's dependency list.

Before (original pyproject.toml checked out from `origin/dev`, ran with `python3 -m pytest tests/test_proxy_extra_no_pyroscope.py -v`):

```
FAILED tests/test_proxy_extra_no_pyroscope.py::test_proxy_extra_does_not_depend_on_pyroscope_io
AssertionError: pyroscope-io is back in the proxy extra: ["pyroscope-io>=0.8.16,<1.0; sys_platform != 'win32'"]. ...
assert ["pyroscope-i...m != 'win32'"] == []
1 failed, 2 warnings in 0.31s
```

After (fixed pyproject.toml restored):

```
tests/test_proxy_extra_no_pyroscope.py::test_proxy_extra_does_not_depend_on_pyroscope_io PASSED [100%]
1 passed, 2 warnings in 0.24s
```

Also ran the broader packaging/metadata-adjacent suite plus the new test (`python3 -m pytest tests/test_proxy_extra_no_pyroscope.py tests/test_version_lock_sync.py tests/test_install_licences.py tests/test_doc_gate.py -v`): 110 passed.

## Changelog

`changelog.d/tsk-szzkro-drop-pyroscope-proxy-extra.md`

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Fixed installation failures for the proxy option on musl-based systems, including Alpine and postmarketOS.
  - Removed the unavailable `pyroscope-io` package from the proxy installation requirements.
  - Proxy installations no longer attempt to resolve a package that lacks compatible distribution files.

- **Tests**
  - Added coverage to ensure the proxy option remains free of the unavailable package.

author: omrishiv
body:
Merge after #1642 

Follow-ups from a review of the Entra OBO identity work (#1642). None of these are
required to attribute a caller, which is why they are separate — but two of them
close exposures that the identity work widens, so this should land with it or
immediately after, not later.

Two data-exposure fixes:

- `emit_audit_event` serialized the WHOLE audit record and logged it on
  `registry.audit`, which propagates to root handlers: stdout, a rotating file,
  and the `application_logs` MongoDB collection. Application logs have a different
  retention (a day by default) and a different access boundary than the audit
  collection the compliance documentation reasons about. The `username` leak
  predates this; the durable IdP identifiers (UPN, `oid`, `tid`, `appid`) are new,
  and shipping them into three extra sinks contradicts the data-minimisation
  rationale used to justify dropping the `name` claim. The record stream now goes
  to a dedicated `registry.audit.records` logger with `propagate = False` and its
  own handler, and the operator-facing payload masks the durable identifiers.
  `app_log_excluded_loggers` was NOT usable as the fix: it is only consulted by the
  MongoDB handler, so the console and file copies would still have received the
  values, and an operator can unset it. `registry.audit` itself could not be made
  terminal either — it is the parent of `registry.audit.service`, which emits the
  CRITICAL "AUDIT RECORD DROPPED" line. Full-fidelity claims remain in the durable
  audit store, which is where the audit UI and the identity feature read them.
- `_forward_headers` filtered the hop-by-hop and proxy-context header sets, but
  `x-internal-token` was in neither: it was stripped only on the vault/OBO
  branches. So for a plain registered MCP server, the gateway's own SECRET_KEY-
  signed hop JWT reached the registrant's backend — a credential replayable
  against `/mcp-proxy`, and now also a carrier of the caller's identity. It is
  stripped unconditionally, including when `relay_authorization` is set, and the
  `_EGRESS_STRIP_HEADERS` comment that claimed otherwise is corrected. The
  non-egress path had no coverage at all; it does now.

Correctness and robustness:

- `_claim_str` guarded only 2 of the 7 `_emit_token_mint_audit` call sites; a
  duplicated resolver fed the other five. `email` arrives from
  `registry/auth/dependencies.py` as `claims.get("email") or ""`, so a multivalued
  Keycloak mapper put a list into the record, `ValidationError` fired inside the
  best-effort emit, and the whole audit record was silently DROPPED. Both identity
  values are now coerced once, inside `_emit_token_mint_audit`, so every site is
  covered by construction, and the duplicated resolver is gone.
- The OBO mint record used a fresh `request_id` and a null `correlation_id`, so it
  could never be joined to the `mcp_server_access` record for the same request —
  even though the unique `(request_id, log_type)` index exists precisely so records
  of different `log_type` can share one id. `/validate` now signs its `request_id`
  into the hop claim as `rid`, and the mint record records it as `correlation_id`.
  A token minted before this change still audits.
- `_audit_provider` fell back to the configured IdP even for a `self_signed`
  token — one the gateway minted itself, which no IdP ever saw. That fallback is
  skipped now; such a token still reports the provider its originating session
  recorded.
- `_csv_safe` missed formulas behind leading whitespace or a newline. Spreadsheets
  trim a cell before deciding whether it is a formula, so `" =HYPERLINK(...)"` was
  live content in an export. The `username` query parameter was also unbounded
  while being interpolated into a regex; it is now length-limited.
- An `if audit_identity:` branch documented as "omitted when empty" could never be
  false, because the claim builder always seeds a display value. Its test passed a
  call shape no caller produces, so it would have kept passing if the branch were
  deleted. Both are gone.

Observability:

- The degradation paths were silent — an absent hop claim falling back to the
  opaque `sub`, and a claim coerced away or truncated. They now increment
  `audit_integrity_degraded_total`, labelled by a bounded `reason`, so they are
  alertable as a rate instead of invisible; the only prior signal was a
  `logger.critical` line, which cannot be alerted on as a rate. Deliberately no
  unbounded label dimensions: no tenant, app, principal or request id as an
  attribute. An ABSENT claim counts nothing — normal for any IdP that omits it —
  which is what keeps the series meaningful.
- The Status Distribution card is hidden for the `token_mint` stream, which
  structurally has no `response.status_code` to bucket, rather than rendering a
  titled card containing "No data available".

Verified: 8221 passed. Both exposure fixes re-proved independently of their own
tests — a record's six claim values reach the durable store intact and no root
handler (re-enabling propagation leaks them again, so the guard is load-bearing),
and no `x-internal-token` variant survives `_forward_headers` on the non-egress
path.

Refs #1642

author: hansondr
body:
## Problem

Scroll direction is inverted between macOS and non-macOS peers: `CGEvent`'s sign convention
is the opposite of `wl_pointer`/libei's (positive = down/right).

## Fix

- **Capture** (macOS sender): fixed negation, matching #470. Real hardware already has Natural Scrolling applied before the event reaches this tap, so no preference read is needed.
- **Emulation** (macOS receiver): negates based on the receiver's `com.apple.swipescrolldirection` preference. Revives #460's approach, now caching the `CFString` preference key instead of allocating it per scroll tick.

## Why the receiver needs the preference and the sender doesn't

A synthetic `CGEvent` posted at the HID tap produces the same on-screen direction for a given sign regardless of Natural Scrolling (confirmed on hardware, consistent with #470/#481) - but a *real* trackpad's delta sign is flipped **before** the CGEvent exists, specifically because of that preference. A fixed conversion therefore desyncs a real trackpad from Lan Mouse's forwarded input whenever Natural Scrolling is on; reading the preference keeps them in sync either way.

## Testing

Verified on real hardware, both directions, against the exact `0.11.0` release protocol:
- Windows → macOS (Apple Silicon): correct with Natural Scrolling on and off; forwarded scroll stays in sync with the receiving Mac's own trackpad in both states.
- macOS (Apple Silicon) → Windows: correct with Natural Scrolling on and off; forwarded scroll stays in sync with the sending Mac's own scroll direction in both states.

## Prior art

#470 (capture fix reused), #460 (emulation approach revived), #481 (symptom report), #415 / #347 (via #470).

author: zbennett10
body:
Campaign missions could not be won. The engine treated all fourteen condition keys as victory conditions and required every one of them to hold at once.

## The two lists

The original keeps two. Eleven victory conditions combined with AND, and seven defeat conditions where any one ends the mission. It asks victory first and only then defeat, so a tie goes to the player.

`AllUnitsKilled` is a defeat condition, and twenty nine of the seventy four shipped missions carry it. Treating it as a victory condition meant the player had to destroy his own army to satisfy it, which no mission carrying it could survive. That is the bug.

Four condition types the original supports were not parsed at all: building a unit type, capturing a unit type, and any unit passing a line in either axis. The wildcard that means any type is in too.

The implicit defaults are in as the original has them. A mission outside a campaign with no victory conditions gets an implicit "destroy everything", and a mission with no defeat conditions gets an implicit "you lose when your army dies". The second is where losing by being wiped out actually comes from.

## The rest of the chain

Defeat never fired in a campaign mission at all, because the skirmish rules step aside when objectives exist. A finished mission now reaches the end screen and returns to the Book of Deeds with the chapter advanced on a win. The save records which mission it is and the per-condition flags, and the save schema moves up a version, so an older save is refused rather than misread.

## Missions with no victory condition

Twenty three shipped missions name no victory condition and are not made winnable by the implicit rule, which the original applies only outside a campaign. They are not broken and they are not a deviation. Every one of them ships a mission script, sixty three of which are in the archives, and the original loads that script for every campaign mission and lets it end the mission. Those twenty three become winnable when mission scripting lands. Nothing here should paper over them with an implicit condition, which would change how a fifth of the campaign plays.

## Determinism

Everything feeding a verdict is integer state read from the unit snapshot at a fixed tick, with no floats in the decision, no wall clock and no iteration-order dependence. The defeat flag and the per-condition flags join the simulation hash beside the victory flag, so hash values move for every world, consistently on every machine. The per-seat result and the reason stay out of the hash, under the existing rule that a per-seat verdict may differ.

## Tests

Twelve mission cases driven off real shipped missions, seven of which fail before the change against a kept pre-change binary, including the corpus census that finds sixty four files misclassified. Two end screen cases for the return path.

Full suite, both data layouts, on the committed head.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added support for separate mission victory and defeat conditions, including additional objective types and wildcard unit matching.
  * Campaign missions now evaluate outcomes during play, track completed conditions, and prioritize victory if both outcomes occur simultaneously.
  * Added dedicated campaign victory and defeat end-screen flows with appropriate continuation behavior.
  * Mission progress and condition state are preserved in saved games.

* **Documentation**
  * Added reference documentation describing mission condition parsing and evaluation.

## What

The geocoding schema rejected invalid input with French messages:

- `Le nom doit contenir au moins 2 caractères`
- `Le code pays doit être au format ISO-3166-1 alpha2 (ex: FR, DE, US)`

These aren't internal strings — Zod validation errors surface verbatim through the MCP error response to the client and the calling LLM, so a model debugging its own bad `geocoding` call got French while every other message in the server is English.

Also translates the three remaining French code comments (`client.ts`, `index.test.ts`). `Météo-France` in `tools.ts` stays — proper noun.

## Why now

Found while auditing the server against Anthropic's connector pre-submission checklist. The criteria require actionable validation messages; these were actionable but inconsistent with the rest of the surface.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run` — 133 passed (7 files). One assertion in `index.test.ts` referenced the French string and was updated with it.
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint` — clean
- Smoke-tested all 17 tools against the live Open-Meteo API over stdio: 17/17 return successfully, no tool publishes an empty input schema, all carry `title` + `readOnlyHint`.

No behaviour change beyond the message text.

author: arthurkeen
body:
## Summary

Sprint 2 of the Federation Forge (contextual-data-fabric **ADR-0006**, D-2..D-5; r2g plan `docs/internal/PLAN-federation-forge.md` §"S2 dialects"): the remaining three launch-set dialects — **`snowflake`**, **`clickhouse`**, **`arango`** — behind the **unchanged** seam `generate(ontology, dialect, seed) -> ForgeArtifacts(ddl, load_sql, rows)`, each with a live roundtrip `introspect(generate(O)) ≡ O` through the real analyzers.

### Structure (D-4: "new dialects arrive as plugins behind one seam")

`r2g.forge` is now a package; `r2g.forge.*` public names are unchanged (re-exported).

| module | role |
|---|---|
| `forge/core.py` | ontology contract (unchanged), `plan_schema()` → dialect-independent `SchemaPlan` (canonical snake_case tables/columns with roles pk/fk/property), `synthesize_rows()` (seeded, once) |
| `forge/dialects/base.py` | `ForgeDialect` / `SqlDialect` hooks, `sql_literal`, `split_sql_statements` |
| `forge/dialects/{postgres,snowflake,clickhouse,arango}.py` | one projection per target |
| `forge/dialects/__init__.py` | `DIALECTS` registry, `get_dialect`, `SUPPORTED_DIALECTS` — adding a dialect is one module + one registry line; the shared unit tests parametrize over the registry |
| `forge/generate.py` | composes plan → rows → dialect |

**Postgres output is byte-identical** to the S1 skeleton (DDL, loader, rows; only the `(walking skeleton)` header tag dropped) — verified against `origin/main`'s `forge.py`.

### D-2: data synthesized once, projected per system

`rows` is keyed by canonical names in every dialect and is **byte-identical across all four** for the same `(ontology, seed, rows_per_entity)` — asserted in `tests/test_forge_dialects.py` and via the CLI in `tests/test_cli_forge.py`. Snowflake uppercases at emit time; Arango adds `_key` at load time.

### Dialects

- **`snowflake`** — unquoted **UPPERCASE** identifiers (the folding reality real schemas have; `singularize`/`convert_identifier` are case-insensitive since #2, so `ACCOUNTS` → `Account`, `ACCOUNT_NAME` → `accountName`); `NUMBER(38,0)/FLOAT/BOOLEAN/VARCHAR`; declared PK/FK (recorded, unenforced — exactly what RSA's `SHOW PRIMARY KEYS`/`SHOW IMPORTED KEYS` reads); one multi-row `INSERT` per table.
- **`clickhouse`** — `MergeTree ORDER BY (id)` (PK surfaces via `is_in_primary_key`), `Int64/Float64/Bool/String` with `Nullable(...)` properties; **no FK syntax exists**, so the FK intent is recorded as a column `COMMENT 'forge:foreign-key -> accounts(id)'` plus loader header comments — the ADR's constraint-stripped shape.
- **`arango`** — one document collection per entity, one edge collection per relationship named as the forward Auto-Map derives it (`contacts_to_accounts`, `_from`/`_to` on the spine ids). `ForgeArtifacts` fields are reinterpreted (documented): `ddl` = JSON collection manifest (`forge.collections.json`), `load_sql` = standalone python-arango loader (`forge.load.py`, env-driven, idempotent). `project_documents(manifest, rows)` is the same projection as a library call; a unit test execs the generated script in isolation and checks both agree.

### Live roundtrips (all run green locally today)

| dialect | introspection leg | result |
|---|---|---|
| postgres | `PostgresConnector` → Auto-Map → CSI; `rsa_ontology` | 3 passed (docker compose) |
| snowflake | **RSA `SnowflakeConnector`** over a throwaway schema `FORGE_RT_<seed>_<pid>_<hex>` in the real account (dropped in `finally`) → Auto-Map → CSI; `rsa_ontology` | 5 passed (~18 s) |
| clickhouse | **r2g `ClickHouseConnector`** over `system.columns` (RSA has no ClickHouse connector) → `infer_foreign_keys` / `rsa_ontology` → Auto-Map → CSI | 7 passed (new compose `clickhouse` service) |
| arango | generated `forge.load.py` run via subprocess → **ASA `AgenticSchemaAnalyzer`** deterministic baseline, `auto` and `collection` strategies | 4 passed (docker compose) |

The `≡` comparison is factored into `tests/integration/forge_support.py` (names through the real `owl_*` normalizers; plumbing `id`/FK labels the only tolerated extras) and the Postgres test now uses it too.

**D-3 two-branch contract on ClickHouse, asserted both ways:** `get_schema()` reports FKs *absent* (never invented from the comment) and the PK present; r2g's and RSA's inference both *recover exactly* the planned edges; with no keys applied, Auto-Map derives **no** edge rather than a wrong one.

### Known gap, pinned by name (D-3: never silently wrong)

Snowflake's only integer type is `NUMBER(38,0)`; `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` reports bare `NUMBER` and `pg_type_to_json_type("number")` is `float` (RSA's connector does not carry `NUMERIC_SCALE`). `KNOWN_TYPE_GAPS` in the Snowflake roundtrip names it; the test fails if the gap widens **or silently closes**. Follow-up (not this PR): RSA reports scale; r2g maps scale-0 `NUMBER` → `integer`.

### Skips

- Snowflake skips with a reason when creds are unset (collection time) **or when the role may not `CREATE SCHEMA`** — the fabric's `CDF_RO` cannot; `SNOWFLAKE_FORGE_ROLE` selects a role that can (I ran with `ACCOUNTADMIN` against the CDF `.env` creds). RSA's connector is URL-driven and cannot carry a private-key path, so the fixture shims `snowflake.connector.connect` for **auth only**; every introspection statement is RSA's.
- ClickHouse skips when `CLICKHOUSE_DSN` is unreachable (default: the new compose service on **8124**, so a developer's other stack on 8123 survives).
- Arango skips without `arangodb-schema-analyzer`; the CI integration job now installs `[dev]` for it.

### Deliberately out

- **Temporal** (`TIMESTAMP_NTZ`/`DateTime64`): the forward map collapses every temporal type to `string`, so no honest roundtrip exists yet — plan §S2-5.
- Partitioner / denormalizer / goldens: S3 (CDF orchestration).

### Also

- `r2g forge generate --dialect` help lists the four dialects and their output files; `write_to` uses per-dialect file names (SQL dialects unchanged).
- `docker-compose.yml`: `clickhouse` service + CI env; `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased/Added; PRD **P12.11** row after P12.10.
- Verified: `ruff check src tests`, `mypy src/r2g`, 1746 unit tests passing, 19 live roundtrip tests passing; no throwaway schema/database left behind on Snowflake, ClickHouse, Postgres, or ArangoDB.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

`publish(rkey, { move: true })` drops the draft once it is written, and `{ to: airspace.review.projects }` publishes into another space instead of the public repo. _Unpublishing is just `airspace.projects.delete(rkey)`._

`to` is also checked at runtime: lexicon objects are open, so a record from one collection can validate in another, and the type alone would let a project land in `categories`.

```text
feat(installer): hide dashboard tabs for deselected optional services

Give the dashboard a node-side source of truth for which optional
services are installed. A new bootstrap step (65-dashboard-config.sh)
derives installed_services in config.json from selection.json on every
bootstrap run and restarts the dashboard so the change takes effect
immediately, instead of only on the next reboot.

The dashboard reads the block via a "missing means on" default at every
layer (Go config, HTTP handler, templates) and hides the Automationen
tab plus the Tailscale/TinyTuya settings subpages, including their
fragment routes, when their service is deselected.

Also hardens the new step against real failure modes found in review:
an atomic config.json rewrite, a distinct failure for an unreadable
selection.json instead of silently treating it as "nothing selected",
a checked manifest parse instead of a silently-swallowed one, and a
forward-compatible schema so a future optional service can't prevent
the dashboard from starting.

Implements Installer-Spec E7 / Komponente A / Abnahmekriterium 11.
```

author: tomberek
body:
## Summary
- dyn-drvs has a permanent, documented limitation on this exact package (`discovertree-exec-bit-bug.md`): a Makefile recipe that execs a binary it just linked, in the same `buildPhase`, finds unresolved placeholder text since dyn-drvs' deferred stubs only resolve once, at the very end of `buildPhase`.
- nixgg hits the **identical wall** for the identical reason -- confirmed directly: a one-phase `mkNixggBuild` compiling+linking+self-execing in one `buildCommand` fails with the same `Permission denied`. nixgg's own DESIGN.md calls this "the synchronous-realize wall" (inherent to `builder-rpc-v0`, not a nixgg-specific gap).
- nixgg's mechanism has a real escape hatch dyn-drvs has none for: mkNixggBuild's two-phase pattern (phase 2 = an *ordinary* `stdenv.mkDerivation`, with `buildInputs` forcing phase 1 to resolve to real bytes first) sidesteps the wall entirely.
- `libb64-nixgg`: phase 1 accelerates libb64's 2 real per-TU compiles; phase 2 links `c-example1` against the real, resolved `libb64.a` and runs it directly -- confirmed via the build log's own real output (`encoded: aGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=` / `decoded: hello world`, not a stub).
- Requires bumping the nixgg pin (`976a930` -> `5e86dba`), same as the nixgg-lua-batching PR.

author: lexyondigital-boop
body:
Corrige el error `Invalid requests[0].repeatCell: No grid with id: 0` que aparecía al exportar contactos, reportado en la primera prueba real contra Google.

## La causa

Google asigna el id `0` **solo** a la pestaña que crea por su cuenta cuando no se declara ninguna. En `crearHojaConDatos` sí se declara una (`"Contactos"`, para poder congelar la primera fila desde el inicio), así que Google le asigna un id aleatorio — en la prueba salió `1840572933`. El `batchUpdate` de formato iba con `sheetId: 0` fijo y moría.

Era un id inventado por mí, no leído de la respuesta. El `PUT` de valores sí funcionaba porque direcciona por título (`Contactos!A1`), no por id.

## Por qué dolió más de lo que parece

El fallo caía **después** de escribir los datos. La petición terminaba en 502, pero la hoja ya existía y estaba llena en el Drive del usuario — sin registro en `hojas_generadas` y sin forma de encontrarla desde la plataforma. Cada intento de exportar dejaba una hoja huérfana.

## Qué cambia

**El `sheetId` se lee de la respuesta de creación** en vez de asumirse.

**El bloque de formato pasa a ser no fatal.** Es cosmético (negritas en el encabezado, ancho de columnas) y corre cuando los datos ya están escritos: tirar la petición entera por él reproduce exactamente la hoja huérfana de arriba. Vale más entregarla sin negritas que perderla. La escritura de datos sigue siendo fatal, que es la que sí importa.

## Cómo se verificó

Se probó `crearHojaConDatos` contra un `fetch` simulado que devuelve la forma real de la respuesta de Google, con un `sheetId` no-cero. Nueve comprobaciones, todas en verde:

```
OK   devuelve id y url
OK   usa el sheetId real, no 0
OK   autoresize usa el mismo id
OK   escribe con RAW
OK   teléfono va como texto crudo
OK   encabezado en la primera fila
OK   formato fallido no tira la exportación
OK   nombre con fecha
OK   sin slug cae al nombre
```

Las dos primeras cubren el bug directamente; la séptima cubre el modo de fallo que dejaba huérfanas las hojas.

También `npm run build` compila y pasa TypeScript, y `google-sheets.ts` sigue sin avisos de ESLint.

## Limpieza manual

Los intentos fallidos dejaron hojas en el Drive de `gilbertosotelocob@gmail.com` con los contactos dentro pero sin formato. No están registradas en la plataforma, así que hay que borrarlas a mano desde Drive.

author: brettdavies
body:
## Summary

`GET /api/score`, `/api/score.json`, and `/api/score.md` stop answering. Each still served a real scorecard from the `input` query key the unified funnel retired, so a target could be read two ways: the result route the funnel exists to be, and this one. The previous release declared the lane retired in its own postflight gate and left the router dispatching it, which is how the gap surfaced on the first production postflight run. This closes it.

Read a scorecard at `/score/<target>`, or its `/md` and `/json` representations, which carry the same envelope the MCP tools return. `POST /api/score` is unchanged: that is the transact endpoint, matched before this lane ever was, and it remains the only caller the web app has.

With nothing dispatching the lane, its handler and content-negotiation module were reachable only from their own tests, so both go, along with the seven suites that existed to exercise them.

The rest is release tooling. It ships but changes no served behavior: preflight gates report how many files they found instead of an unmarked first few, the postflight distribution gate checks `/scorecards` for a marker the merged board actually renders, and withholding the telemetry lake is a script rather than a hand edit. That script's residue check found a stale `TELEMETRY_ENVIRONMENT` declaration in the generated bindings that the previous release shipped, where `wrangler.jsonc` no longer defines the var; this release drops it.

The telemetry lake stays withheld. Its stall alert still has no `EMAIL` binding to send through, so the blocker is unchanged.

## Changelog

### Removed

- Retire the legacy `GET /api/score`, `/api/score.json`, and `/api/score.md` read lane, which still answered the superseded `input` query key. Read a scorecard at `/score/<target>`, or its `/md` and `/json` representations. `POST /api/score` is unchanged.

### Fixed

- Fix the postflight distribution gate to check `/scorecards` for a marker the merged leaderboard renders, so a healthy page stops reporting as a failure.
- Drop a stale `TELEMETRY_ENVIRONMENT` declaration from the generated Worker bindings, which named a var the configuration no longer defines.

## Type of Change

- [x] `fix`: Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues/Stories

- Story: n/a
- Issue: n/a
- Architecture: n/a
- Related PRs: #358 #369 #373 #374 #375

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Integration tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing completed
- [x] All tests passing

**Test Summary:**

- Unit tests: 2333 passing on the release tree, with lint, the TypeScript project checks, and the build clean
- Integration tests: this release commit was deployed to staging from its own branch and every preflight gate run against that build. 30 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped: the Sandbox DO path on a fresh non-registry binary, the 10-gate MCP suite including a fresh container audit and an R2 cache hit on `figlet`, the four live Playwright projects at 79 passing, cross-repo version coherence, build and asset integrity, and the distribution surfaces.
- Coverage: n/a

Verified against the deployed build: all three retired shapes return 404, `POST /api/score` returns 200, and `/privacy` returns 404 confirming the lake is withheld.

## Files Modified

**Modified:**

- `RELEASES.md`, `RELEASES-PREFLIGHT.md`, `RELEASES-RATIONALE.md`: the staging-deploy step, the live-suite gate, and the withheld-features record
- `scripts/release/_lib.sh`, `preflight.sh`, `postflight.sh`: gate reporting and the corrected `/scorecards` marker
- `src/worker/index.ts`, `src/worker/score/core.ts`: drop the legacy dispatch, move `_resetIndexCache` to its new owner
- `src/worker-configuration.d.ts`: drop the stale generated declaration
- `tests/worker.test.ts`, `tests/audit-api.test.ts`, `tests/audit-job-attach.test.ts`

**Created:**

- `scripts/release/withhold-telemetry-lake.py`

**Renamed:**

- None.

**Deleted:**

- `src/worker/score/handler.ts`, `src/worker/score/content-negotiation.ts`
- `tests/score-handler.test.ts`, `tests/score-handler-branch-and-norelease.test.ts`, `tests/score-handler-share-url.test.ts`, `tests/score-handler-share-url-post-discovery.test.ts`, `tests/score-telemetry.test.ts`, `tests/score-vary.test.ts`, `tests/score-contract.test.ts`

## Breaking Changes

- [ ] No breaking changes
- [x] Breaking changes described below:

`GET /api/score`, `/api/score.json`, and `/api/score.md` stop answering and return 404. A client reading a scorecard from that lane moves to `/score/<target>`, `/score/<target>/json`, or `/score/<target>/md`. The lane was already declared retired by the previous release, so this closes a gap rather than opening one, and `POST /api/score` is untouched.

## Deployment Notes

- [ ] No special deployment steps required
- [x] Deployment steps documented below:

This release retires public paths, so the edge needs a zone-wide purge-everything after the deploy and before postflight. A retired path's cached entry carries the cache tag of the route that used to serve it, and that route is gone, so a tag purge does not reach it. Run `scripts/release/postflight.sh --env prod retired` after the purge; that gate reads raw status with no retry, so a stale answer fails instead of being retried away.

No Durable Object migration in this release, so `wrangler rollback` is available and needs a second purge if used.

Staging is serving this release commit rather than `dev`. The next push to `dev` redeploys it.

author: traviscomber
body: Hardening follow-up after production QA. When the server access cookie expires, middleware redirects a protected route to `/`, but the client PasswordGate could keep its previous authenticated state because it stayed mounted. This leaves the UI looking authenticated while privileged navigation keeps redirecting. Wrap PasswordGate in a pathname-keyed boundary so route redirects remount it and force server-session revalidation. No auth policy, password, DB, or API behavior changes.

author: olleala2023
body:
По замечанию к статье справки.

## Скат дома

На чертеже кровля дома поднималась от навеса к коньку — то есть снег с неё сходил бы в противоположную сторону, а весь смысл схемы Б.8 именно в том, что он сходит на навес. В самом калькуляторе разрез нарисован верно (`views.js`: скат от конька вниз к свесу над навесом, подпись «снег сходит отсюда»), ошибка была только в статье.

Теперь скат спускается к навесу, свес нависает над ним, подпись стоит у свеса, а не у конька. Заодно разведены подписи, которые налезали друг на друга.

## Зона мешка b = 6000 при навесе 4800

Выглядит странно — и это стоило объяснить, а не только подписать на чертеже. Добавил в статью абзац:

> b считается от стены по формуле (Б.6) и ограничена 5h и 16 м. Это про то, как далеко от стены вообще может лечь наметённый сугроб, — о размерах навеса формула ничего не знает. Здесь 5h = 6 м, а навес 4,8 м: значит, мешок накрывает его целиком, а «хвост» зоны приходится уже на воздух за краем. Практический вывод неприятный: облегчения к дальнему краю, на которое можно было бы рассчитывать, нет — эпюра не успевает спуститься до μ₁ = 0,59, у края навеса она ещё 0,93.

Расчёт при этом верный: в плане калькулятора полоса мешка и так обрезается по глубине навеса (`Math.min(H, driftLength·sc)`), лишнего не рисуется.

## Мелочь

В статье про связи снеговой район был указан как IV, хотя все числа считались для расчёта по умолчанию — район III. Поправлено в двух местах.

## Summary
This PR refactors the dispute resolution system to allow both task posters (`posted_by`) and task takers (`taken_by`) to raise disputes on active tasks, transitions disputes to a `withdrawn` state upon withdrawal instead of hard-deleting database records, and ensures dynamic notification targeting to the opposite counterparty.

## Key Changes
- **Model Updates (`basic/models.py`)**: Added `('withdrawn', 'Withdrawn')` to `Dispute.STATUS_CHOICES` while retaining the `OneToOneField` mapping to `Task`.
- **View Updates (`basic/views/dispute.py`)**:
  - `raise_dispute`: Authorized both `task.posted_by` and `task.taken_by` when `task.status == 'in_progress'`. Handles re-opening previously withdrawn disputes without relational integrity conflicts. Dynamically targets notifications to the opposite counterparty.
  - `withdraw_dispute`: Restricted to `dispute.raised_by` (or staff). Sets `dispute.status = 'withdrawn'` and `task.status = 'in_progress'` without deleting the row. Dynamically targets notifications to the opposite counterparty.
- **Interface Updates (`basic/templates/my_tasks.html` & `dispute_detail.html`)**:
  - Rendered "Raise Dispute" button for task posters on `in_progress` tasks.
  - Conditionally rendered "Withdraw Dispute" button only for the user who initiated the dispute.

- **Migrations & Tests**:

THE OLD ANGLE WAS SELF-GUIDED. SHE IS NOT A SELF-GUIDED COMPANY

The page turned on "self-guided in the Himalaya is the hardest thing on your list". Root runs four hosted group departures a year - Patagonia Nov 2026, Mexico Feb 2027, Ecuador May 2027, Peru May 2027 - eight or nine days, one country, twelve travelers, with a trip leader. The lede also claimed her product list overlaps ours "most closely" of anyone we are meeting, which was flattery rather than an argument.

WHAT THE PAGE ARGUES NOW

Their sustainability page is the loudest thing on the site: "Sustainability Embodied, Not Outsourced". It rejects carbon offset credits ("an easy out"), bucket-list itineraries and multi-stop flights by name. Those three positions disqualify essentially every Himalayan trip on the market, which is the honest reason Root has no Himalaya product - not a gap in her catalogue, a standard the catalogue could not meet.

So the page makes two arguments she cannot get from another supplier at that table:

  1. Bhutan's Sustainable Development Fee is a state levy funding health, education and forest cover - a fee, not an offset. It is the closest thing in travel to the argument her own page makes.
  2. "We work exclusively with local guides" is on her destinations page. Most Himalayan programmes reach a U.S. operator through a wholesaler in Delhi or Kathmandu, at which point that promise is someone else's roster. Our crews have been ours for twenty years.

Then three specifics sized to how she actually operates: twelve people at altitude needs an operator who can move a night without asking a third party; her eight-week pre-trip programme is already the acclimatisation habit most operators install in the first three days; one country for ten days is the least-sold shape in the Himalaya and the one it suits.

THE LODGE IS A TEASER HERE

No name, no village, no district, no altitude, no key count, no date. Khotokha is named on Cate Collins' page alone, by Will's decision of 15 Sep, and the build fails if it appears anywhere else.

HER PERSONAL HISTORY IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT

Her About page is candid about PTSD, depression, dyslexia and postpartum depression, and it is the origin story of the company. It is hers to tell. The build now fails if any of it reaches a built page.

OPEN, FOR THE ROOM

Does the eight-week pre-trip programme cover physical preparation or only mindfulness? Root includes all gear rentals in the trip price - find out what we would have to provision in region before anyone claims we can. ALSO IN THIS COMMIT
main did not yet have the following when this was written, so it rides along here rather than in a commit of its own:

  - the Cate Collins Bhutan/wildlife update
  - the Andrea Vinyard rewrite (Going Places / Cruise Planners)
  - the Monica Price / Meagan Coates cycling-page corrections
  - the Tilghman Whitacre / Fora rework
  - the Breanne Kiefner rewrite (if the closed branch was never merged)

author: sivert-io
body:
## Review-required path

This adds a migration under `packages/server/src/db/**` (persistence), so it needs a read of the whole diff before it merges. The changed files are the new `tokenReissueMigration.ts`, its test, and one call plus one import wired into `connection.ts`.

## Why

server#194 (GRYT-1239) stops `server:clients` and `server:details.clients` from leaking every member's live access token, but it cannot recall a token that already leaked. While the bug was live an attacker could roll a captured access token forward indefinitely by refreshing inside each fifteen-minute window, so an upgrade that only stops new leaks still leaves the captured ones working.

## What it does

`reissueAccessTokensAfterLeak` bumps `server_config.token_version` by one, once, inside `runMigrations`. That counter is what `requireAuth`, session restore and `token:refresh` compare a token against, so every access token minted before the bump is refused from then on.

- **Fires once.** A `schema_meta` marker (`access_token_reissue_gryt1239`) records that it ran, in the same transaction as the bump, so a later boot never repeats it.
- **Skips a fresh install.** It only bumps a database that already has member rows. A server nobody ever joined never issued a token to leak, so there is nothing to retire; the marker is still written so it never reconsiders.
- **Refresh tokens keep working.** The bump touches only `server_config`. A live client whose access token is now refused falls back to its refresh token and re-mints at the new version on its own, so the sign-out is a brief reconnect rather than a re-login. Refresh tokens were never exposed by the leak.
- **One log line** names the new counter value when it fires.

## Tests

`tokenReissueMigration.test.ts`:

- bumps the counter once on a server that had members;
- does nothing on the second boot;
- spares a fresh install that never had a member;
- an old access token is refused at `requireAuth` and at `token:refresh` afterwards;
- a refresh token still mints a new access token, and that new token is accepted where the old one was refused.

Verified end to end on a throwaway server: joined on `origin/main` (the code before this migration), captured the access and refresh tokens, then restarted onto this branch against the same data directory. The migration bumped `token_version` 0 to 1 and logged one line; the captured access token came back `token:revoked` (`token_version_mismatch`) and got no session; the refresh token minted a fresh access token; the fresh token restored the session. A second restart did not bump again.

Local CI: `yarn test` (1336), `yarn test:examples` (9), `npx tsc --noEmit`, `yarn build`, `npx eslint .`, `node scripts/check-comment-length.mjs`, all clean.

## Release

This is the recall half of the `server:clients` fix. It should ship together with server#194 (GRYT-1239), and with #192 (GRYT-1238) and #193 already on `main`.

author: thenathanb
body:
## Problem
On the Settings page, the chunk size/overlap inputs give confusing feedback:
- The inline validation error (\"chunk overlap must be less than chunk size\", etc.) was only set when clicking Save, and cleared on *every* keystroke (\`handleChunkSizeChange\`/\`handleChunkOverlapChange\`). So typing an invalid value showed no feedback at all until Save was clicked, and the message disappeared the instant the field was touched again.
- The validation rule itself was duplicated inline here, instead of reusing \`getIngestChunkSettingsError\` (\`frontend/components/cloud-picker/types.ts\`), which already implements the same two checks and is used by the upload/connector dialogs.
- A separate \`useEffect\` resyncs local chunk-size/overlap state from \`settings.knowledge\` whenever that query object's reference changes — including background refetches unrelated to the user's edit. If a refetch happened while the user had an unsaved edit in progress, it silently overwrote it, appearing as an inputs \"snapping back\" to the old value.

## Fix
- Replace the imperative \`chunkValidationError\` state with a value derived every render via \`getIngestChunkSettingsError({ chunkSize, chunkOverlap })\`, so the existing inline error UI (already wired to this variable) now reflects live input instead of only post-Save state.
- Add the derived error to the Save button's \`disabled\` predicate so an invalid combination can't be submitted.
- Simplify \`handleKnowledgeIngestSave\`'s validation to reuse the same derived value instead of duplicating the two checks.
- Guard the \`settings.knowledge\` resync effect with the existing \`userEdited\` flag (already used for dirty-tracking) so a background refetch can't clobber an in-progress edit. Read it via a ref rather than a dependency, so flipping \`userEdited\` back to \`false\` on save success doesn't itself trigger a resync against stale, pre-refetch data before the invalidated query resolves.

## Tests
- \`npx tsc --noEmit\`: no new errors introduced by this change (confirmed identical pre-existing error count with the change reverted via \`git stash\`).
- \`npx biome check\` on the changed file: clean.
- Manually verified in the dev server: typing an invalid overlap/size combination now shows the inline error immediately and disables Save; fixing the value clears it and re-enables Save; an in-progress edit is no longer overwritten by a background settings refetch.

Fixes #1220

body:
## Что сделано

Пункт **D-3** зонтика #871 — граф вызовов: подключён резолвер пути, разобраны действия снятого `code.graph`.

**Резолвер.** Анализатор называет модули форм и команд файлом, а служба передавала резолверу личности `path: None`: метод формы отвечал `unsupported_section` («the call graph route does not resolve the path yet»), а соседи-формы в ветвях `Caller`/`Callee` уходили в `limits: unaddressablePeer`. Теперь путь даёт та же раскладка, которой живёт `unica.resolve`:

- адрес → файл: форма размещена дескриптором `…/Forms/<Имя>.xml`, её модуль — `…/Forms/<Имя>/Ext/Form/Module.bsl`; команда — каталогом и `Ext/CommandModule.bsl` (`module_file_for_placed`);
- файл → адрес: обратный перевод для соседей из ответа анализатора, узел из раскладки плюс роль модуля `…Module.Form`/`…Module.Command` (`placed_for_module_file`);
- раскладка строится один раз на запрос и только когда нужна: для личности формы или когда среди соседей есть названный файлом (`names_a_peer_by_file`); чужой набор исходников адреса не получает; кого раскладка не размещает, тот остаётся в `limits`.

Наружу путь по-прежнему не отдаётся: он живёт между службой и анализатором.

**Действия снятого `code.graph`** (записка `2026-09-10-call-graph-branches-design.md` дополнена): `callers`/`callees` — ветви; `neighbors` — обе ветви; `node` — узел метода с `callGraph` в `props`; `source` — тело метода через `view`; `resolve` — `unica.resolve`. Без входа остаётся только `overview` — он про конфигурацию целиком, и его предмет решает владелец.

## Проверено

- RED → GREEN: `form_and_command_modules_translate_between_placement_and_analyzer_file` (перевод в обе стороны для формы и команды, отказ для объекта).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings` — чисто.
- `infrastructure::daemon` целиком, `interfaces::mcp`, `application::v13` — зелёные.

**Умова, якої стадія чекала, виконана.** Звіт власника 2026-09-15, 22:36: «Дані перенесено й безпечно збережено у профілі», `vfs=opfs-sahpool`, черга 1356 → 0. Перенос пройшов наскрізь на реальному iOS-PWA.

**Коміт 2 (`2e7aa2f`)** — тумблер прибрано з апки зовсім. Ця частина з'явилась після питання власника «Налаштування про пробу теж прибрати ж треба з апки?», і воно виявило, що тумблер-«відкат» був гіршим, ніж здавався, причому з двох незалежних боків.

**Перший бік: гейт «Експериментального» ламав саму обіцянку.** Секція тримає тумблери **заблокованими**, доки людина не поставить галочку «Я розумію, що це ранні можливості», і завжди показує банер про нестабільність. Тобто після перемикання дефолту, щоб **вийти** з поведінки за замовчуванням, треба було спершу прийняти ризик експериментальних функцій. «Відкат — один тумблер» ставав двома діями з брехливою рамкою навколо.

**Другий бік, вирішальний: вимикання РОЗЩЕПЛЮЄ дані.** Записи, зроблені в OPFS, у старе сховище не повертаються (стадія 2: старе сховище не чіпаємо). Людина, яка вимкнула тумблер «щоб перевірити», лишалась би з двома половинами історії й без натяку про це. Тумблер, що мовчки ділить дані навпіл, відкатом не є.

Тому прибрано не видимість, а механізм:

| Річ | Стан | Чому |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Тумблер у Налаштуваннях | **прибрано** | Гейт ламав відкат, а вимикання розщеплює дані |
| Гілка воркера | **безумовна** | Прапорця більше немає |
| Pre-boot машинерія (стадія 2.2) | **прибрана** | Пішла разом із єдиним своїм споживачем |
| kvvfs-гілка | лишається | § «Рішення дизайну»: «Фолбек лишається і лишається тихим» |
| Фолбек | автоматичний | `openWorkerBackedDb` віддає `null` на будь-якій невдачі |
| Відкат | реверт коміта | Один і чесний |

**Фолбек не постраждав** — він ніколи й не був ручним.

## Governing Skill

- Primary skill: `sergeant-web-ui` (поверхня `apps/web/**`)
- Secondary skill (if truly needed): `sergeant-feature-flags` — правка видаляє запис із `FLAG_REGISTRY`

## Playbook

- Primary playbook: n/a
- Why this playbook: —
- If no playbook matched, why: правка веде спеку `docs/work/specs/sqlite-opfs-worker.md`, її § «Стадії» і є рецептом.

## Verification

```bash
pnpm format:check              # All matched files use Prettier code style!
pnpm lint                      # exit 0
pnpm check:typecheck-and-test   # Tasks: 35 successful, 35 total
pnpm build                     # Tasks: 4 successful, 4 total
```

`apps/web` — 1214 файлів, 12387 тестів пройдено (6 skipped).

Пін проти повернення тумблера: тести перевіряють, що `storage_sqlite_worker` немає в реєстрі і що жоден експериментальний тумблер його не показує.

Дизайн-лінт спіймав власне довге тире в описі тумблера ще в першому коміті (канон §1.9: читається як ШІ-текст) — переписано на кому; сам опис потім пішов разом із тумблером.

Additional checks:

- [x] Local smoke / manual validation completed — підстава для стадії це звіт власника з пристрою (успішний наскрізний перенос, `vfs=opfs-sahpool`)
- [x] Surface-specific checks completed
- [x] **New or reworked UI surface:** секція «Експериментальні функції» втрачає один рядок. Нових поверхонь немає, слоп-тест не застосовний.

## Docs and Governance

- [x] I updated docs that changed with the behavior, contract, workflow, or rollout.
- [x] I checked whether `AGENTS.md` needed an update. — не потрібен
- [x] I checked whether a playbook or skill needed an update. — не потрібні
- [x] I checked whether governance docs or review docs needed an update. — ні

Updated docs:

- `docs/work/specs/sqlite-opfs-worker.md` — § «Стадія 3», рядок 3 у таблиці стадій, `Last touched`
- `docs/engineering/architecture/feature-flags.md` — рядок `storage_sqlite_worker` видалено

**Реєстр тумблерів суперечив спеці — суперечність зникла сама.** Він обіцяв, що на стадії 3 «воркер стає єдиним шляхом, а прапорець зникає разом із kvvfs-гілкою». Половина виконана буквально (прапорець зник), друга половина лишається помилковою і НЕ виконується: kvvfs-гілка це фолбек, а не спадок, і прибрати її означало б лишити частину пристроїв без робочої бази.

## Risk and Rollout

- **User-visible risk.** Усі пристрої при першому запуску дістануть перелиття стадії 2: стара база копіюється в OPFS цілком, старе сховище лишається недоторканим. Невдача на будь-якому кроці ковтається і веде в kvvfs, тобто найгірший наслідок дорівнює стану до стадії 1. Механізм перевірений наскрізь на пристрої власника.
- **Окремо варте уваги:** ті, хто раніше СВІДОМО вимкнув тумблер, тепер теж переходять на OPFS — прапорця, який їх тримав, більше немає. Осиротілий ключ `sergeant.flags.preboot.v1.storage_sqlite_worker` лишається в localStorage, ні на що не впливає (його ніхто не читає) і важить одиниці байтів; окремий код прибирання додав би більше ризику, ніж користі.
- **Rollout / deploy order:** звичайний web-деплой, порядку не потребує.
- **Backout plan:** revert обох комітів. Дані, уже перелиті в OPFS, лишаються на місці; старе сховище не чіпалось, тож ревертнутий застосунок читає його як раніше.

## Hard Rule #15

- [x] I read `AGENTS.md` before coding.
- [x] Internal docs I touched are in Ukrainian.
- [x] I did not use `--no-verify`.

## Reviewer Notes

**Урок стадії 2.2 не втрачено разом із кодом.** Машинерія pre-boot прапорців пішла, але запис про те, чому `hub_flags_v1` лише ВИГЛЯДАЄ як localStorage-ключ (а `resolveStore()` після boot-у підміняє сховище на SQLite), лишився у § «Стадія 2.2» спеки. Якщо колись знадобиться прапорець, який читають до відкриття бази, починати треба з того запису, а не з нуля.

Заодно оновлено два докстрінги в `sqlite.ts`, які розійшлись із кодом: один казав, що дані при вмиканні не переїжджають (стадія 2 це змінила), другий описував головнопотоковий OPFS як робочий варіант №1, хоча той не спрацьовує ніколи (`installOpfsSAHPoolVfs` вимагає `FileSystemSyncAccessHandle`, доступний лише у воркері).

**Борг, що лишається відкритим:** генератор `bodyWeightBootstrap.ts` досі солить id значенням `userId` без перевірки, чи воно спільне (стадія 2.4), і прибирання старого kvvfs-сховища після доведеного переїзду.

This change removes the standalone `tools/dump-json` tool and integrates single-payload dumping directly into `icu4x-datagen`.

With `--format single`:
- Users can export/dump a single data struct directly to stdout (when `--out` is omitted) or to a file specified by `--out <PATH>`.
- Supports `--syntax {json, bincode, postcard}` (defaulting to `json`).
- Supports `--pretty` formatting when `--syntax json` is used.
- Validates that exactly one payload matches the query, returning an error if 0 or multiple payloads match.
- Gains full access to all `icu4x-datagen` configuration options (`--cldr-root`, `--icuexport-root`, `--unicode-rscd-root`, `--tzdb-root`, `--input-blob`, etc.).

author: krzysztof-smartdataengines
body:
The machine is ordered tomorrow, so this is the page that has to be right first. It is preparation,
not results: nothing here publishes a number.

### One factual error on that page would have chosen the wrong instance

The storage bullet offered `c7gd` as a local-NVMe option. That is **Graviton**, and
`include/orderbook/crc32c.hpp` guards its hardware path with
`#if (defined(__x86_64__) || defined(_M_X64)) && (defined(__GNUC__) || defined(__clang__))`, computing
the checksum with `_mm_crc32_u64`. There is no ARM path, so every WAL record there falls back to the
byte-at-a-time table — and roadmap **#81** measured exactly that difference when it added the
intrinsic: **361.7 ns → 23.8 ns** per 112-byte record, **+17.6%** on `BM_IngestionThroughput` from
the one change. A comparative table produced on Graviton would publish the cost of a missing
intrinsic as a property of the engine.

### The prediction is now numbers rather than a direction

The page already said "expect the gap to widen", and a direction cannot be wrong. Against the last
published run (`2026-09-12-ece487a1`, i3-7100U, control floor 21.2%):

| | measured | predicted, 8 vCPU x86_64 |
|---|---|---|
| orderbook ingest | 66,072 rows/s | **80,000 – 95,000** |
| ClickHouse ingest | 428,842 rows/s | **650,000 – 850,000** |
| TimescaleDB ingest | 116,438 rows/s | **140,000 – 170,000** |
| ClickHouse ÷ orderbook, ingest | 6.5× | **7.5× – 10×**, wider |
| orderbook `time_range` p50 | 9.32 ms | **6.5 – 8.0 ms** |
| ClickHouse `time_range` p50 | 5.26 ms | **3.7 – 4.5 ms** |
| TimescaleDB `time_range` p50 | 8.67 ms | **6.0 – 7.5 ms** |
| orderbook in process | 446,219 updates/s | **530,000 – 650,000** |
| control floor | 21.2% | **under 10%** |

Ingest should widen because our figure is bound by single-connection round-trip latency, which
improves with core speed and not with core count, while ClickHouse's insert path sizes itself to the
machine. That is a true statement about this engine — it has no bulk-load path over the wire — and it
is already the first line of `ENGINE_LIMITATIONS`.

### The query column is what a quiet machine is for, and it is not the ratio

Every query figure contains a measured p50 of about **4.8 ms of Python-side parsing** for 4000 rows,
identical for all three systems. Subtract it and 4.5 ms of engine time stands against about 0.46 ms
of ClickHouse time — but **that subtraction is not publishable from this machine**, because 21.2% of
9.32 ms is ±2.0 ms and ClickHouse's remainder is not separable from zero at this resolution. The
published 1.77× is a ratio between two numbers dominated by a constant neither system controls. A
floor under ten percent is what makes the residuals separable, and that — not a bigger number for us
— is the result worth having.

The page also says which way to read a ratio that moves: **wider** means the Python constant scaled
better than the server-side work and the table has started to show what was always underneath, not
that the engine got relatively slower. Either way the number to quote about the engine is the
residual with the floor beside it, never the ratio alone.

### And the floor stays a gate rather than a statistic

Today's control ratios include a 0.643 and a 1.212, measured on a laptop with other work on it. If a
dedicated instance does not bring the floor under ten percent then the instance is noisy and
**nothing is published from that run**, because a difference smaller than the floor is not a
difference. The harness measures the floor inside the run it governs, so that is a decision the run
makes for itself.

Plus a runbook: competitors started natively (no Docker — a container between the engine and the
hardware contradicts the point of the engine), one harness invocation that produces every number in
the table, and the in-process `BM_IngestionThroughput` beside it, because a table carrying only the
wire figure describes a protocol and one carrying only the in-process figure describes a library
nobody can reach over a socket.

Docs only; the four document checkers are clean.

author: mukherso
body:
## Summary

This change restores the source-side BGP session to eBGP and corrects the generated AS_PATH.

## Problem

A change was made to the test `bgp_remote_private_as_test` to use an iBGP session between ateSrc and dutSrc: https://github.com/openconfig/featureprofiles/pull/4987 . This configuration could generate an unordered peer ASN, leading to inconsistent behavior across traffic generators and making the test depend on iBGP-specific behavior.

## Fix

This change restores the source-side session to eBGP for all vendors and encodes the source ASN as an `AS_SEQUENCE` instead of an `AS_SET`. The generated path now begins with the source peer ASN in an ordered sequence, matching normal eBGP behavior and the test description. Expected AS paths were updated accordingly, while the destination session remains eBGP so the test continues to validate outbound private-AS removal.

### Changes

  - Uses eBGP for the ATE source-to-DUT session for all vendors.
  - Sets the source ATE ASN to 100, while the DUT remains AS500.
  - Changes the source AS-path mode from INCLUDE_AS_SET to INCLUDE_AS_SEQ.
  - Ensures the generated path begins with the source ASN as an ordered AS_SEQUENCE.
  - Updates expected AS_PATH validation to include both the DUT ASN and source ASN.
  - Removes vendor-specific iBGP handling and simplifies helper function arguments.
  - Keeps the destination session as eBGP and continues testing outbound private-AS removal.

Step 36 の i18n 基盤に **韓国語 (ko) / 中国語簡体 (zh-Hans) / 中国語繁体 (zh-Hant) / フランス語 (fr)** を追加。要件どおり **スケルトン + 一部実訳** で導入し、主要画面（nav / Settings / Media の運用文言）を実訳、段階導入のため未訳キー（動画種別ラベル `media.kind.option.*`）は **en へフォールバック**する。

  - `i18n.switch.test.tsx` — ko/fr でラベルが訳され、未訳キーは en 値で表示されること。
  - `settings.test.ts` — ko/zh-Hans/zh-Hant/fr が検証を通ること。
- **③ 最小修正 (Green)**:
  - `language.ts` — union 拡張、`detectLocale` で `zh` の地域サブタグ（tw/hk/mo/hant）→簡体/繁体を分岐。
  - `locales/{ko,zh-Hans,zh-Hant,fr}.json` を追加（主要画面のみ実訳）。
  - `ja/en` に言語選択肢のネイティブ表記（한국어 / 简体中文 / 繁體中文 / Français）を追加。
  - `renderer/i18n.ts` に 4 ロケールを登録し、`fallbackLng` を `"ja"` → **`"en"`** に変更。
- **④ 影響範囲**: i18n リソースと言語ドメインのみ。設定検証は `LANGUAGE_SETTINGS` 包含で自動追従。**IPC 契約・main ロジックは不変**。既定表示（ja/en）は両者とも完全訳のため fallback 変更の影響なし。
- **⑤ 確認手順**: `npm test` (**248**) / `npm run typecheck` / `npm run test:a11y` (**5**) / `npm run e2e` (**9**) すべて緑。

## 段階導入の境界（意図的な保留）

`i18n.spec.ts` に French 切替ケースを追加し、①主要ボタン/ナビがフランス語化、②未訳の動画種別ラベルが en フォールバックされることを固定。全 E2E は `--lang=ja` 起動で locale を決定化。

author: maximiliankhan
body:
Both of these came out of your two questions — and one is you correctly refusing my suggestion.

## 1. No pin. But provenance was broken, which is the real issue.

You're right that pinning fights this repo's actual needs — we've repeatedly needed a fresh llama.cpp for a new model architecture. **That makes provenance the only thing preserving reproducibility, so I checked it. It doesn't work.**

The parser knew one upstream format:

```
old: version: 8893 (6217b4958)
new: version: 0.4.0-dev (build 10865, commit d4389a4dd)   ← what it prints today
```

So `build` and `commit` have been **absent from every row** since upstream changed that line — silently, because the parse failure was a quiet `if m:`. What rows *did* carry is `source_head`, the llama.cpp source **tree's** HEAD, and that isn't what the binary was built from:

| field | value on this rig |
|---|---|
| `source_head` (recorded) | `8e126574…` — the tree *now* |
| the binary that actually ran | build **10865**, commit `d4389a4dd` |

**The field naming what produced a measurement was empty; the populated one named something else.** Fixed: both formats parse, an unrecognised third is recorded as `version_raw` + `version_parse: UNRECOGNISED` rather than vanishing (the silent miss is the actual lesson), and the parse is now a pure `parse_engine_version()` testable without a binary. Rows now carry build+commit **and** source_head — which is the point of keeping both, since they can legitimately differ.

## 2. `serve-bootstrap.sh` — you were right to ask

It **cannot bite your rig**, which is exactly why it survived. Here's the evidence:

- `scripts/serve-bootstrap.sh:15` hard-codes `$WEIGHTS_DIR/Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf`
- it **is** registry-pinned (`weights.registry:30`), conf-exposed, and documented
- **nothing downloads it** — `grep` finds only *users* of that path, never a fetcher; `bootstrap.sh` fetches only the default model
- `start.sh` under FAST_BOOT calls `wait_llama_health` and on failure `exit 1`, with the comment *"Phase 1 is the tiny bridge — it IS the fallback, so no rollback here"* — so there is no fallback
- your copy has been on disk since **2026-07-08**

So: fresh install + `FAST_BOOT=true` → whole stack dies with *"bootstrap model failed to load"*, a message pointing at llama-server rather than at a file nobody fetched. `FAST_BOOT` defaults false, so the blast radius is operators who opt in on a fresh box.

**Fixed two ways:**

- **Fast boot now degrades.** It's an optimisation; a missing optimisation must fall back, never fail a boot. Proven both ways by lifting the gate out of `start.sh` and driving it with and without the file — no server, no GPU:

```
--- bridge MISSING ---  ACTIVE=0 SCRIPT=serve-real.sh
    Fast boot is on but its bridge weight is missing: …/Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf
      Nothing downloads it — bootstrap.sh fetches only the default model.
      Get it:  ./scripts/fetch-weight.sh Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf
      Continuing WITHOUT fast boot; the configured model loads directly.
--- bridge PRESENT ---  ACTIVE=1 SCRIPT=serve-bootstrap.sh
```

- **`scripts/fetch-weight.sh` now exists** — nothing could fetch any of the ~20 non-default registry weights by name, which is the gap *underneath* this bug. It resolves the row, downloads from the pinned HF repo (handling a remote filename that differs from the local one), verifies size and sha256 against the pin, and **deletes a mismatch** rather than leaving it: a corrupt weight fails somewhere inside inference, which is far worse than an absent one failing at load. Offline it says so in a sentence and prints the sideload procedure instead of burning five retries into a traceback. `--list` shows the registry and what's present.

## Verification

169 script checks (up from 165), 5 new provenance tests. **Both fixes mutation-checked** — revert the bridge-weight check or the new regex branch and a named test fails. Full suite green, shellcheck and ruff clean. No GPU.

body:
# Description

Adds `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, triggered on `release: published`, to publish every publishable `@graphql-markdown/*` package to npm using [npm's OIDC trusted publishing](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-07-31-npm-trusted-publishing-with-oidc-is-generally-available/) — no `NPM_TOKEN` secret involved, ever. The job runs behind a required-reviewer `npm-publish` GitHub Environment, and always runs a dry-run rehearsal before the real publish.

Also consolidates the existing `publish-package.sh` + `publish-release.sh` pair into a single `packages/tooling-config/scripts/publish-release.mts`:
- Same approach (pack with `bun pm pack` to resolve `workspace:` specifiers, verify none remain, publish the tarball via `npm publish`).
- Dependency order now comes straight from `getBuildSequence()` instead of a second hand-maintained list.
- Adds an "already published" skip check (idempotent reruns) and a `--yes` flag so it can run unattended in CI while keeping the interactive confirmation for local/manual use.

**Manual one-time setup needed before this can actually publish** (not part of this PR, can't be automated from here):
1. Create the GitHub Environment `npm-publish` with required reviewers.
2. On npmjs.com, for each of the 11 packages, add a Trusted Publisher: repo `graphql-markdown/graphql-markdown`, workflow `publish.yml`, environment `npm-publish`.

JSR publishing is intentionally out of scope for this pass — it needs a `jsr.json` per package and JSR's stricter source-level type-checking is unverified across all 11 packages. Planned as a follow-up once npm publishing is proven on the 1.37.0 release, which will be the first release to go out through this pipeline.

author: mattfanning90-sudo
body:
Two independent fixes, both closing a path where the system already knew
something was wrong and nothing acted on it. Neither changes how any signal is
computed; both change what is allowed to reach a live book, and what you hear
about it.

## 1. The ML promotion floor

`train.py` has been grading the neural model honestly every week. The
2026-09-14 run scored it:

```
strategy        Sharpe     CAGR    MaxDD    PSR    DSR
neural_oos       -0.62   -3.64%  -55.45%   0.01   0.00
```

`ml_pool()` loaded it anyway — because nothing connected the grade to the
decision. The model traded `matt` and `partner` on the strength of being the
most recent file on disk.

The subsystem had two promotion paths failing in opposite directions:

| path | gate | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| swarm → live | DSR ≥ 0.95 (~3.8 Sharpe needed; best bred is 0.96) | promotes nothing, ever |
| neural → live | none | promotes everything, including −0.62 |

New `forex/promotion.py` holds the floor as the **one** gate, so `champions.py`
can call the same function in phase 3 instead of growing a second copy.

**An ungraded model is refused too.** "We did not check" must never read the
same as "it passed" — that equivalence *is* the defect.

The other half was that the grade never reached the model: `train_models()`
saved the bundle and `run_ml_backtest()` graded it afterwards, so the score
lived only in stdout. `record_evaluation()` now stamps it onto the bundle.

Synthetic runs record that they were synthetic and no Sharpe, which the floor
treats as ungraded (invariant #5). Verified end to end — a synthetic run
produced a fabricated **6.30 Sharpe** and the floor refused it:

```
Promotion floor: REFUSED — evaluation records no out-of-sample Sharpe
  The live books will run the 5 technical agents only.
```

## 2. Audit errors reach the alert channel

`verify.py` has been right, and unread. `never-traded: sleeve ASX` fired every
day for **52 days**. The FTSE cash discrepancy fired on the very day the book
was liquidated on a phantom loss. Both went only to the GitHub step summary.

`alert_on_errors()` routes ERROR findings through the same channel the drawdown
breaker uses. Deliberately **not** gated behind `--strict`: a scheduled run
should not have to opt in to being told its books are broken, and failing the
job after the trade has happened would not undo it. WARN and INFO stay quiet —
a channel that fires on everything gets muted, and then the next real error is
invisible again. `--no-alert` opts out locally.

Live run against the real books:

```
🔔 [ALERT] audit_errors: live-book audit found 5 error(s) across 5 book(s):
   full — never-traded: sleeve ASX is funded (33% of the book, 33,333 AUD)...
```

## Tests

5 new, each written failing first. The two that matter most:

- a challenger that is merely *less bad* than the incumbent is still refused by
  the floor — the scenario where a −0.44 model gets promoted because the
  incumbent was −0.62;
- a clean audit sends nothing, so the channel stays worth listening to.

## CI note

`tests/test_fx_sessions.py` fails locally on pandas 3.0.2 but passes in CI,
which installs the `requirements.txt` minimum of ≥3.0.5. The helper
`_panel_ending` assumes `pd.bdate_range(end=…, periods=n)` returns `n` labels;
older pandas returns `n-1` when `end` lands on a weekend. Local environment
issue, not a defect on `main`.

## Summary

Closes the feature gaps between the native `legaia-engine play-window` and the browser play page. All seven host-drift gate tiers were green at the start of this branch; five side-by-side audits (field/camera, battle, menus/save/boot, audio, minigames/cutscene) still found about forty gaps, and this branch closes them from both directions. The tail of the branch also records a regional finding about the PAL and JP executables.

## Browser play page (now matches the native window)

- **Audio**: `BgmDirector` body drift fixed (the id-only restart guard meant field BGM never returned after a battle; master volume 127 vs 100; loop policy; stop/pause gate). SFX cue ids widened from u8 to u16 with `classify_cue`, so the cast cues that were being truncated now fire. Battle duck, the PROT 0889 level-up reward bank, and the XA lane (arts shouts XA2/XA4/XA6 and the XA27/XA30 clips) over the shared `StreamResampler`.
- **FMV**: STR/MDEC + XA playback for story beats and the title attract loop (`play_fmv.rs`, `site/js/play-fmv.js`). The page slices raw sectors from its own disc bytes; the runtime keeps no second copy. Retail skip rule is engine-side (`fmv_id 0` only, face buttons / Select). Movie audio is staged on the engine mixer's XA lane, so it sits behind the same master trim and volume slider as every other sound.
- **Title**: the session is stepped at 60 Hz (the attract countdown is 0x5DC retail frames, 25 s), and the countdown runs at the Press Start prompt as well as on the menu, since retail has no prompt phase to wait behind. New Game now calls `begin_new_game` and starts the title BGM.
- **Minigames**: the four in-world minigames (slots, Baka Fighter, Muscle Dome, dance) the page entered but never drew, bridged to the standalone renderers through a compact PROT image.
- **Battle**: mid-battle VRAM re-upload channel (face stamps animate, Stone recolours, effect CLUTs stage) with a serial-keyed residency twin; battle tools panel (party, force battle, battle BGM, auto-battle, no encounters); `set_active_party_spec` / `learn_spell` exports; the double-drawn level-up banner.
- **Field**: field-event queue drain (the queue leaked: only the BGM router drained it and it handed non-BGM events back), field FX drawn on field frames, script-spawned actor meshes, projected HUD Y, precise-movement checkbox, the three kingdom overworlds in the picker with the decoration layer and the kingdom CLUT walker, the lead's rig kept on the overworld.

- Save-select slot model unified in `legaia_save` (`leader_summary`); LGSF `LGX5` resume trailer so Continue re-enters the saved scene; SC-block `LGXE` engine-ext blob in the 0x1A18..0x1FFC tail retail composes but never reads (the page's save clock and chains survive a card round-trip).
- Menu cues 0x21 / 0x20 / 0x37.

## Regional finding (PAL + JP executables)

Decoded SCES_019.44/.45/.46 and SCPS_100.59 against the pinned SCUS routines. Monster records (PROT 0867) are byte-identical across the discs; the executables are not. NTSC-U alone adds the second gold halving, the 3/4 EXP cut, and the battle-load stat boost. Every PAL localisation and the JP original pay the larger spoils and fight with the raw record. Recorded in `battle-formulas.md`, `battle.md`, `pal-localizations.md`, `builds.md`, `gamedata.md` and the monsters page; the engine kernels are marked NTSC-U.
