`docs/tooling/host-drift.md` gains "Gaps the tiers were blind to" (the six gap shapes no drift tier could see) and a rewritten known-gaps table. Crate README sections for FMV, in-world minigames and field effects. author: geoscabio
roger-in-kiva
body:
## What

Adds two analytics events so we can tell when a lender reached checkout through the lend-after-goal-set feature rather than on their own.

| Page | Category | Action | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| Checkout | `basket` | `view` | `from-lend-after-goal-set` |
| Thanks | `post-checkout` | `view` | `lend-from-after-goal-set` |

The label asymmetry (`from-lend-…` vs `lend-from-…`) is taken verbatim from the ticket.

## Why it needs a cookie

Both events fire on pages reached after the app has been left behind. `/basket` is not a route here: `router.push('/basket')` falls through to the catch-all, which does `window.location = to.fullPath`, the monolith resolves it to `/checkout`, and completing that order is another full page load to `/checkout/thanks`. Nothing in memory survives, so a cookie (`lend_after_goal_set`) carries the mark.

## Why the cookie holds a transaction id

The thanks page the lender leaves from and the one that ends the new order are the same component. `/checkout/thanks` matches `'checkout'` in `server/util/protectedRoutes.js`, so it is served `no-store`, which disables bfcache — pressing Back from checkout genuinely re-mounts the first thanks page and re-runs `onMounted`.

With a boolean, that Back press fired the event for the order the lender came *from* and consumed the cookie, so the order they actually completed was never counted. The cookie now stores the `kiva_transaction_id` it was marked on, and `isLendAfterGoalSetOrder` fires only for a different order, leaving the mark intact on a Back visit.

It also expires after an hour, so a lender who abandons checkout and never reaches a thanks page to clear it stops being credited.

## Changes

- `src/util/thanksPage/expressCheckoutUtils.js` — `LEND_AFTER_GOAL_SET_COOKIE` and the set / has / is-other-order / clear helpers.
- `src/composables/useExpressCheckoutModal.js` — `redirectToBasket()` folds the two basket redirects together and marks on the navigation, so a failed add-to-basket leaves nothing behind.
- `src/pages/Checkout/CheckoutPage.vue` — fires the basket view and deliberately does not clear it.
- `src/components/Thanks/ThanksPageSingleVersion.vue` — fires and clears, read above the goal-data awaits so a slow or failing load can't strand the mark.

## Scope

Thanks-page flow only, covering both branches that end in the basket: the express-disabled path and the non-empty-basket redirect. The MyKiva goal modal and Goals page already emit their own `go-to-checkout` events from MP-2748.

Note this is not strictly variant-A traffic once the A/B test is live. A variant-B lender whose basket already holds items is still redirected to the basket and marked, which is the intended scope: they reached checkout through the feature.

## Tests

23 added, all green.

- `expressCheckoutUtils.spec.js` — the cookie records the originating order and its one-hour expiry, falls back to a placeholder that stays truthy, credits only a different order, and survives a missing cookie store.
- `useExpressCheckoutModal.spec.js` — both redirect branches mark; the express modal path and a failed add do not.
- `CheckoutPage.spec.js` — fires with the mark, silent without, never clears.
- `ThanksPageSingleVersion.spec.js` — fires and clears; still fires when goal data never settles; stays silent on the order it was marked from.

Two pre-existing suite-wide flakes (`possibleTypesCacheIntegrity.spec.js`, `GoalInReviewModal.spec.js`) fail on a clean `main` worktree too and pass in isolation. Neither file is touched here.

## Known gaps, pre-existing and out of scope

The `lendingRewardOffered` redirect skips `CheckoutPage` before mount, and a `DONATION_ONLY_VIEW` / `LOGIN_REQUIRED_VIEW` thanks page never mounts the component.

body:
#### Short description of what this changes or resolves:

Part of #12343 (do not close). Adds HTTP-level API tests for the two FHIR Location routes, which the inventory in that issue lists as 0/2 covered:

- `GET /fhir/Location`
- `GET /fhir/Location/:uuid`

Third one in the series after #14032 (Practitioner) and #14034 (Organization); coordinated with @sjpadgett on #14032, one resource per PR against master.

#### Changes proposed in this pull request:

- `tests/Tests/Api/LocationFhirApiTest.php` (new): 9 tests driven through `ApiTestClient` with a real OAuth token, following `ConditionFhirApiTest`. Location has no `POST` route and is a read-only view over facilities, practitioner addresses and patient home addresses, each keyed by its own uuid in `uuid_mapping` (minted on demand by `LocationService`). So `setUp` installs the facility fixtures through `FacilityFixtureManager`, the tests find the seeded facility's Location over HTTP with `?name=test-fixture-Your Clinic Name Here`, and `tearDown` deletes the `uuid_mapping` rows for the seeded facilities before removing the facilities themselves, so no orphan mappings are left behind.

What the tests pin (current server behavior, not the FHIR spec, same approach as the Condition tests):

| Request | Expected |
|---|---|
| `GET ?name=<seeded facility>` | 200, `Bundle` of type `collection` with exactly one `Location`: name, status `active`, San Diego / CA / 90210 address, facility phone as telecom |
| `GET ?_id=<uuid>` | 200, exactly that Location |
| `GET ?address-city=San Diego` | 200, bundle includes the seeded Location |
| `GET ?_id=<unknown>` | 200, `total` 0, no entries (not 404) |
| `GET /:uuid` | 200, the full `Location` resource |
| `GET /not-a-uuid` | 400 with `validationErrors` |
| `GET /<well-formed unknown uuid>` | 404 with an empty JSON array |
| `GET` / `GET /:uuid` without a token | 401 with the OAuth "denied the request" body |

`managingOrganization` is deliberately not asserted: `FhirLocationService` sets it to the system's primary business entity, which depends on the database the suite runs against (absent on a fresh dev install), not on the seeded fixture.

Verified locally in the `development-easy` stack: `vendor/bin/phpunit --testsuite api --filter LocationFhirApiTest` → OK (9 tests, 167 assertions). To check the assertions are live, three protected values were mutated (expected city, bundle type `collection`, status `active`): the tests guarding them failed, then the file was restored. `phpcs` clean on the new file; full pre-PR gate (phpunit targeted, isolated suite, phpcs, PHPStan on the whole codebase, php -l) green.

author: poteat
body:
## What the mod did

`mods/diff` pinned the repository inside its `session.start` hook: one
`git rev-parse`, then `git status --porcelain -z --untracked-files=all` over
the whole working tree, both awaited. The engine holds the first prompt until
`session.start` settles, so in a very large repository (millions of files,
or a large untracked tree) every session's first turn waited on that walk, up
to the mod's 5 s git timeout, whether or not the diff pane was ever opened.
The built-in `/diff` panel runs no git at a session's start. The awaited pin
(then a lone `rev-parse`) dates from the mod's first publication on Sep 9;
the working-tree walk was added to it on Sep 12 (`883b12c`, in #94184).

## What it does now

Git runs when the built-in panel's would, and not otherwise:

| moment | built-in panel | this mod, before | this mod, after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| session start | nothing (the repository is found by a filesystem walk for `.git` on first render, kept per directory) | `rev-parse` + a full `status` walk, awaited; the first prompt waits | nothing |
| `/diff`, open | filesystem check, then one fetch round awaited (up to 2 s) before the panel flips: shortstat, numstat, `ls-files --others`, shortstat, one `git diff` | pinned already; open, then a floated fetch: shortstat, numstat, `ls-files`, one `git diff -- <path>` per file in view | one `rev-parse` (first time only), open, then the same floated fetch; the first fetch also reads the `status` baseline once (see below) |
| `/diff` outside a repository | filesystem check, message; the answer is kept until `/clear` | `rev-parse` every time | `rev-parse` once; the answer is kept until `/clear` or `/resume` |
| first successful edit, pane closed | preference, layout and width first, then the filesystem check, then one fetch round and the panel opens | after every edit until one opened the pane: a store read and the pin (`rev-parse` + `status`) *before* the width check | preference, layout and width first; then `rev-parse` (first time only); then open and fetch. No room, no git |
| edit or shell command, pane open | 150 ms debounced fetch round after Edit/Write/NotebookEdit and after non-read-only Bash/PowerShell; nothing after a permission-denied tool | debounced fetch after those tools, refused or not | debounced fetch after an edit that landed, and after a shell command unless it was refused (a failed or interrupted one still refreshes, as with the built-in); read-only shell commands still refresh, since the mod cannot tell which commands are read-only |
| edit or shell command, pane closed | nothing | edits: store read + pin attempt; shell: nothing | edits: store read + width check; shell: nothing |
| end of a turn | nothing | pane open: one fetch round | nothing |
| HEAD moves outside the session | file watcher on `.git/HEAD` and the ref, then a fetch | 2 s stat poll of the same files while the pane is open (git only if `HEAD` is not a plain file), then a fetch | unchanged |
| `/clear`, `/resume` | repository answer dropped, found again on next need | pane closed, state reset, pin kept | pane closed, state reset, pin dropped (its baseline with it) |
| base cycle (`ctrl+x b`), pre-session toggle | fetch round | fetch round | unchanged |

Two differences remain and are deliberate for now: the mod finds the
repository with one `git rev-parse` where the built-in walks the filesystem
(it pins `--git-dir`/`--work-tree` for every later child), and its first
fetch for an open pane reads `git status` once, because a hooks module's
`$.fs.stat` has no change time and the built-in dates a moved-in file by
`max(mtime, ctime)`; that baseline is what tells a file moved in since from
one that was dirty already. Neither runs at a session's start or with the
pane closed. `/cd` and worktree moves are not followed by either version of
the mod (the built-in re-keys by directory); unchanged here.

The first commit alone (`733a0de`) is the minimal fix: `session.start` stops
pinning. The second moves the walk into the first fetch, orders the
first-edit check like the built-in's, keeps a "no repository" answer, drops
the pin on `/clear` and `/resume`, drops the turn-end refresh, and finds the
repository in the directory the session started in. The third settles the
tool rows: a shell command that failed or was interrupted still refreshes an
open pane (as the built-in's does), a refused one does not, an edit that was
refused or failed neither refreshes nor opens the pane, and a probe that a
`/clear` overtook pins nothing.

## Tests

Kit tests beside the mod (`claude plugin test mods/diff`, 140 pass): the
start spawns nothing and registers `/diff`; a lifecycle test asserts the
exact git invocations per moment (start, footer, an edit with no room,
`/diff`, an edit and a shell command with the pane open, a turn's end, the
pane closed by hand, `/clear`); two `/diff` typed together probe once; a
probe git never answers is asked once more; no repository is an answer kept
until `/clear`; a refused or failed edit opens nothing; the working tree is
walked once, by the first fetch, pinned like every child; base-mode restore,
the moved-in file dating, standing down when another `/diff` is listed, and
the rest unchanged. Driven end to end in tmux against a built binary: start
in the large repositories, open/close/reopen, outside a repository, the
inline dialog, `/clear`, a rejected write with the pane open and closed.

Measured on a synthetic repository with 1.5 million untracked files (where
`git status --short` takes 0.02 s and the mod's `--untracked-files=all` walk
6 s): `session.start` settled in 2.5-5.6 s before, 5-9 ms after; a headless
`-p` run's first API request moved from a median 5.2 s after launch to
1.5 s, the same as with the mod off. On a 600k-tracked-file repository
(4 s walk) `session.start` went from a median 4.3 s to under 10 ms, and an
edit in a headless or narrow session no longer spawns anything.

author: kiro-agent[bot]
body:
## Problem — audit P0-07

`BACKUP_MAP` was an **old 8-database list** while the deployment binds **nine**, and it omitted 12 tables added since (`mgmt/backend/src/backup.js:33-67`). Anything missing from it is never exported and therefore **cannot be restored** — while the UI called the download a *"Full Backup"* and the reset runbook offered it as an alternative to the CLI export.

Missing: the whole of `DB_AUDIT` (`user_sessions`, `login_attempts`), plus `journey_entries`, `push_subscriptions`, `loan_email_templates`, `email_message_templates`, `email_messages`, `official_emails`, `ai_fixes`, `ai_providers`, `collection_jobs`, `render_jobs`.

Second defect: `restoreOneTable` treated **every** empty table as suspicious and skipped it (`:347-356`). That is right for a v1 file — an empty array might be an export glitch — but it means restoring a legitimate backup does **not** reproduce the state it captured: rows added after the backup survive.

## Fix

- **Complete coverage.** `BACKUP_MAP` now lists all 9 bindings and every table in the committed schemas.
- **It cannot drift silently again.** `SCHEMA_FILE_FOR_BINDING` maps each binding to its schema file, and `test/p0-backup-coverage.test.mjs` parses `mgmt/db/schema/*.sql` and fails if the schema and the map disagree **in either direction** (a Worker cannot read files at runtime, so the guard lives in the test that CI runs).
- **Manifest v2** (`formatVersion: 2`): per-table `{ rows, present }`, `coverage` (bindings / tables / missingBindings) and `excludedColumns`. A binding the server does not have is now recorded as a gap **and** surfaced as an operator warning, instead of a quietly absent database.
- **Faithful restore.** A table the manifest records as *present and empty* is cleared, so the restore reproduces the captured state. A v1 file keeps the old lenient skip, and the report says which rule applied.
- **One deliberate exclusion:** `collection_jobs.filled_base64` — ~700 KB of transient, re-generable document bytes per job. The job rows are exported; the manifest records the omission.
- The #312 warning is replaced on both Backup screens with an accurate *"what this covers / files are separate"* note, and the reset runbook no longer steers operators away from the UI backup.

## Tests

New `test/p0-backup-coverage.test.mjs` (13 tests):

- **the drift guard**: every schema table is in `BACKUP_MAP`, and `BACKUP_MAP` names no table the schema lacks — this is the test that would have caught the original regression;
- all nine bindings covered, and each of the 12 previously-missing tables asserted by name;
- the export contains `DB_AUDIT` rows, `push_subscriptions`, `ai_providers`; `formatVersion` 2; coverage counts;
- the manifest separates *present and empty* from *not on this deployment*; a missing binding produces `missingBindings` **and** a warning;
- the job blob is excluded while the job row is kept;
- restore: present-and-empty **clears** the live rows (on `main` the row survives), a v1 file does **not**, a normal round-trip restores rows, the planning call walks all nine bindings, and the typed confirmation / acknowledged-backup / Superadmin gates still hold.

## Verification

```
mgmt/backend:         npm test -> 713 tests, 712 pass, 1 fail
                      npm run lint:errors -> pass
mgmt/frontend-svelte: check 0 errors, 46/46 tests, build pass
mgmt/frontend:        build pass (main chunk 218.32 kB)
```

The single failure is the pre-existing `H-6 … WITHOUT decoding` timing flake (`base64.js`, load-sensitive), unchanged from `main`.

## Tracker

`AUDIT_FIX_PROGRESS.md` updated in this commit: #325 added to the merged table, this PR described in §2, **W1 is now 15/15** (the remaining two P0 items are the public-portal ones, PR-16/17), and C11 stays open.

## Rollout / rollback

Backups written after this deploy are `formatVersion: 2`; **v1 files still restore** with their original semantics, so nothing in hand becomes unusable. New backups are larger because they now contain the tables that were missing — that is the point. The only behaviour change on restore is that a v2 backup will clear a table it recorded as empty, which is what makes it a real restore; the report names every such table. Single-commit revert.

author: dastratakos
body:
## What

Prunes the delegation vocabulary in `@sidecar/runtime` and the four session tools in `@sidecar/brain` down to the shape the hosted brain will fill. The child id is the child conversation's uuid and its session key derives from it, so `childRunId` goes; context is isolated only, so the context modes, the fork snapshot, and the context note go; per-child policy metadata, timeout, cleanup mode, completion destination, depth, model, and action counts go; the completion record and its delivery bookkeeping go, since nothing reads them and the record's own terminal slice (status, result text, failure detail, settled instant) is what a parent is told; and the status set drops `timed_out` and `unknown`, which nothing used. `sessions_spawn` takes `task`, `label`, and `expects_completion`; its receipt is `child_id` and `child_session_key`; the `subagents` listing drops `depth`, `context`, `delivery`, and `attempts`. The two spawn refusals whose concepts went (`fork_other_agent`, `blocked_completions`) go with them.

## Why

The Mac-side delegation (the OpenClaw `b7528507` port) was deleted in LUKE-206, and what remained was the port's vocabulary, most of it filled by nothing. This is the precursor for the hosted sub-agent series: no behaviour changes, and no hosted behaviour is added here. The desktop tool row reads only `task`, `label`, `action`, and `child_id`, all of which stay.

Linear: LUKE-228

## Test plan

- `./scripts/check.sh` green (lint, knip, typecheck, discarded-effect, all four test shards, build).
- `grep -rn "childRunId\|requestedContext\|completionDestination" packages apps` returns nothing.
- `session-tools.test.ts` covers the new spawn input and receipt shape, an unreadable `expects_completion` left out rather than guessed, and the shrunk `subagents` listing; `vocabulary-schema.test.ts` covers the five-word status set.

## Cross review

Codex (gpt-5.6-sol, high) raised two should-fix findings, both pushed back on: (1) keep a reduced `ChildCompletionRecord`: nothing reads it, knip refuses an unread export, and the acceptance for this PR is that knip names nothing, so the PR that delivers completions declares it where it is read; (2) pin the `sessions_spawn` schema as a JSON-schema golden: the brain's tool catalog has no goldens on `main` apart from the planner's tool, and starting that convention for one tool is a separate change.

CI runs the portable check on Linux alone; this PR touches no macOS or UI surface.

author: tolgaarseven46-arch
body:
Live Gemini Flash Lite hard-conversation matrix exposed two measured canonical semantic gaps after the pre-AI freeze:

1. First-person user plans could be emitted with `subjectId: kaira` instead of `current_user`.
2. Nested reported speech such as “Ali bana Mert'in X dediğini söyledi” could promote the embedded quote to a durable direct world-memory fact, losing report provenance.

Method:
- Historical RED: Fast CI run 35023060861 reproduced both missing contracts.
- Minimal fix: extend the production server semantic-provider boundary only.
  - Freeze user-owned first-person subject/actor as `current_user`.
  - Reserve `kaira` only for utterances that explicitly make Kaira the subject.
  - Treat nested hearsay as a typed grey zone: preserve utterance/proposition evidence, but do not promote the embedded claim to durable world memory without direct provenance.
- No regex patch, no downstream reparsing, no schema expansion.
- Fast CI after fix: run 35023432890 GREEN.

This is a permitted architecture reopening under the frozen rule because the issue was measured in production as an attribution/ownership invariant violation.

author: arrkkkk
body:
## Summary
- Real Render error: opening a stock's chart raised `ValueError: Tz-aware datetime.datetime cannot be converted to datetime64 unless utc=True, at position 24` in `bars_to_frame()`.
- Root cause: yfinance localizes daily bars to the exchange timezone, so a year of bars crosses at least one DST transition. Bars before/after it carry different fixed UTC offsets (EST vs EDT) once each one becomes its own aware `datetime` on the wire — pandas refuses to infer a single index timezone from a list mixing those offsets unless told to normalize to UTC.
- Fix: route the bar timestamps through `pd.to_datetime(..., utc=True)` before building the `DatetimeIndex`.

## Test plan
- [x] Added a regression test reproducing the exact DST-boundary scenario against real `OHLCVBar`/`HistoryResponse` objects
- [x] `pytest -q` (full suite) green

- [x] `lint-imports` contracts kept

body:
Reportado: *"Subi products and skus pero no me boto nada en los otros excel porque pasa eso?"*.

Reproducido cargando **solo** esa planilla: las dos de especificaciones salen con **0 filas**.

## No es un fallo

La lista de campos de cada categoría —Género, Marca, Material, Talla, Color— y **el ID de cada valor de su dominio** (`141 = talla 39`, `78 = Rojo`) viven SOLO dentro de esos dos exports. `campos_de_la_categoria()` devuelve `[]` y `campo_de_sku()` devuelve `None`, así que no hay ni un ID que escribir y el motor **se niega a inventarlo**: un ID de especificación inventado en VTEX escribe encima de otro campo. Las imágenes sí salen, porque vienen del catálogo de Shopify.

## Lo que estaba mal era DÓNDE se decía

El aviso de la subida ya lo advertía, pero ahí todavía no se ha generado nada; quien llega al panel de resultado ve tres archivos en cero y ninguna explicación al lado. Es la misma regla que *"un botón que no se dibuja y no explica por qué se lee como no funciona"*.

- **`planillas_sin_origen`** devuelve como DATO qué planilla sale vacía y **qué export hay que subir**; la pantalla solo lo dibuja junto al conteo.
- **La señal es `catalogo.cabeceras`**: hay una entrada por cada export que de verdad se leyó, así que su ausencia significa que ese archivo no se subió.
- **Una planilla vacía CON su export subido NO se reporta.** Eso es otra cosa —categorías sin campos dados de alta en VTEX— y decir "falta un archivo" mandaría a buscar lo que no falta.
- **Las claves del conteo se escriben una sola vez** (`FILAS_EN_EL_RESUMEN`): `generar` las pone y `planillas_sin_origen` las lee. Escritas dos veces, un `.get()` con la clave mal escrita **no revienta** —devuelve `None`— y el aviso simplemente no saldría nunca.

## Pruebas

`scripts/test_vtex_generator.py` pasa de 73 a **78**. Las 5 nuevas **EJECUTAN** la generación con solo *Products and SKUs* subido: comprueban que las dos planillas salen en cero, que se nombra el export que falta por cada una, que con las cuatro no se avisa de nada, que una planilla vacía con su export subido no se reporta, y que las claves del resumen son las que `generar` escribe.

Verde también: `test_pantallas_reales.py` (10) y `test_navegacion.py` (22).

author: ingedavid2209
body:
## El problema

Una pantalla de arqueos con **«+$41,949.70 FALTAN»** en cada fila. La diferencia era **exactamente** `esperado − cajón`: la corrección por sangrías no se aplicaba.

No era dinero faltante. El retiro se estaba publicando como faltante de la cajera.

| 11 cierres con corte de Kepler | Pantalla | Real |
|---|---|---|
| Faltante acumulado | **$387,085.43** | **−$13,564.57** (sobrante neto) |
| Filas en rojo | 11 de 11 | 8 |

Las tres filas de arriba cuadraban al centavo: **−$0.30 · +$0.01 · +$9.77**.

## Causa: la identidad vivía escrita tres veces a mano

```
Σ retiros + cajón contado = esperado
```

`armarComparacion()` la tenía **correcta**, con el comentario que ya avisaba que restar directo *«acusa a una cajera honesta de un faltante del tamaño de sus retiros»*. `list()` y `porCajera()` la tenían **mal**.

O sea: al **guardar** el arqueo la cajera veía el número correcto, y en el **historial** el falso.

⛔ **Y no se quedaba en pantalla.** De `porCajera()` salen `faltante_total` —el ranking que señala a personas por nombre— y el `diff_real` que `imprimirTicket()` estampa **en papel** con la etiqueta FALTANTE.

Dos más de la misma familia:

- **`tipo='retiro'` no se neutralizaba** (sólo `'relevo'`). El índice único incluye `tipo`, así que cierre y retiro son **dos filas** que se restaban del **mismo** esperado: el mismo dinero acusado dos veces. 20 retiros con diff 100 % falso; el peor, «+$49,583.70» sobre un retiro de $8,250 que es exactamente lo que tenía que salir del cajón.
- **`kepler_enmascaro` heredaba el diff falso** → la etiqueta ENMASCARÓ prendía en el **100 %** de las filas (Kepler declara cuadrado el 89.7 % de sus cortes), saturando la única señal que `arqueo_ciego_divergente` existe para dar.

**Fix:** un solo `cuadreTurno()` en `libs/reconciliation/src/lib/cash-cut-identity.ts`, que los tres consumen.

## El hallazgo que salió al escribir el veredicto

Iba a declarar «no medible» el 36.6 % de cortes cuyo desglose no cuadra — y eso habría **borrado diferencias reales**. El «hueco interno» del corte de Kepler **es** nuestro `diff_real`: `953.83 = 953.83`, `69.52 = 69.52` en los turnos donde nuestro conteo coincidió con el cajón que Kepler declara.

Entonces `c15 − (c43+c44+c48)` es la diferencia real **y existe para todos los cortes, sin que nadie arquee**. Por qué:

- `c35 = c15 − c25` en el **100 %** de 3,553 cortes → es una **resta**, no una medición.
- `c25 = c15` exacto en el **75.8 %**, **1,700 de ellos con retiro** → cuando Kepler dice «cuadrado», muchas veces significa que se escribió el esperado en la casilla del contado.

⭐ **Kepler publica $699,811 de faltante y su propio desglose implica $2,698,325. Hay 1,066 cortes (30.0 %) por $2,204,552 que salen como cuadrados y su desglose los contradice** — suc01 $901,871 · suc03 $453,788 · suc05 $366,051.

`c25`/`c35` quedan **informativos**; el árbitro pasa a ser `c43`/`c44`/`c48`.

## El sync descartaba turnos enteros, en silencio

El folio `c3` se **reusa** dentro del mismo día y la misma caja: **15 claves duplicadas, las 15 con dinero distinto**. Verificado — suc01 caja1 del 03/09, folio **68**, son **dos turnos de dos cajeros**:

| cajero | esperado | retirado |
|---|---|---|
| `10C01` | $53,474.85 | $49,000 |
| `26VHGH` | $12,184.01 | $0 |

El `DISTINCT ON` se quedaba con uno: **16 filas, $485,076.32 de esperado y $278,900 de retiro** que nunca llegaron a `analytics.cash_cuts`. No faltaba una columna, faltaba el turno.

La clave gana `cajero_cierre` en el sync **y en su gemelo** `load-cash-cuts-from-ods.js`, más `uq_cash_cut_cajero` (`NULLS NOT DISTINCT`). Y dos lookups que ligaban sólo por folio (`compare()` y `retirosContados()`) ahora van por caja + fecha + cajero — el segundo **tapaba** faltantes reales en vez de inventarlos, que es el más peligroso de los dos.

## Lo pedido encima: la sangría y el corte se piden solos

`c46` **es** el umbral del retiro, y está medido con la curva:

| esperado / `c46` | turnos | con retiro |
|---|---|---|
| <50 % | 451 | 2.4 % |
| 80–100 % | 185 | 14.1 % |
| **100–150 %** | 387 | **70.8 %** |
| >300 % | 809 | 99.9 % |

Función escalón centrada en `c46`, no correlación. **NO son $15,000 para todos**: suc01 caja4 corre en **$70,000** y suc04 caja2 en **$8,000** — el código lo tenía escrito como constante. El límite manda *cuándo*, no *cuánto*: 0 de 2,234 casos dejan el cajón exacto en el límite.

⛔ **El disparo no se puede calcular con `c15`: viene en 0 en los 34 turnos abiertos** (Kepler lo escribe al cerrar, y `c15 − c48` da basura negativa). Se usa `c49 − c48`, los dos vivos; `c49` es efectivo (coincide con `c15` al peso en 930 de 975 cortes, contra 307 si fuera todos los medios). Es **estimación** (54.4 % dentro de $50, sesgo +$671 porque no incluye el fondo inicial): **dispara el aviso y nunca alimenta una diferencia**.

El arqueo sigue siendo **ciego** (SM.8): `turnosPendientes()` devuelve `pide_retiro` / `retiro_sin_contar` / `pide_cierre` como **banderas**, y los montos sólo viajan con `revela` (supervisor). El límite sí se le muestra a la cajera — es la política de su caja, que ya conoce.

## Pruebas

Los gates se corrieron **en local** (el workflow de CI sigue `disabled_manually`).

- **`nx test reconciliation` → 20/20.** Target de `test` nuevo: la lib sólo tenía `lint`, y la identidad que decide si a una cajera se le imputa un faltante no tenía ni una prueba. Fixtures = los números reales de prod, y **prueba negativa en cada bloque**: la fórmula vieja da otro número, un corte realmente cuadrado **no** se marca como enmascarado, y `esperado = 0` devuelve `null` y no `0`.
- **`test-newdb-arqueo-cuadre.js` → 12 ✓ / 0 ✗ / 1 ⊘ NO MEDIDO.** El bloque del ODS se **declara** cuando la DB no tiene los datos, no se pinta verde. Sus tres aserciones se verificaron aparte contra prod (read-only) y pasan.
- Ese smoke además ejercita el **`ON CONFLICT` del sync de verdad**: `test-newdb-cash-cuts-sync` no lo toca (0 cortes en su ventana), así que un target de conflicto que no resolviera habría pasado inadvertido hasta correr en una sucursal con datos — y ahí deja de traer cortes **enteros**.
- `nx build api` + `nx build view` OK.
- Migración validada contra Postgres local: idempotente al re-correr, y con prueba negativa de la clave (mismo folio + mismo cajero **rechazado**, con el control positivo de que otro cajero **sí** entra).

⚠️ `landing-guards.spec.ts` falla 6 tests (SN.4) **en `main`, antes de este PR**: importa `permission.guard` / `suite-map` / `permissions` y ninguno está entre los 17 archivos de este cambio.

## Antes de mergear

1. **Aplicar `20260915210000` primero, y después desplegar.** El código **exige** la migración: sin el índice nuevo, el `ON CONFLICT` del sync no resuelve y deja de traer cortes.
2. No la apliqué a Railway: reemplazar un índice único en prod pide confirmación. Hoy `analytics.cash_cuts` tiene **0 filas** que colisionen con la clave nueva (medido), y la migración **aborta con mensaje** si aparecieran.
3. Tampoco a `platform_test`: mi rol `dev_david` no es owner de `analytics.cash_cuts`.
4. Redeploy **api + view**. Sin permisos nuevos → **sin re-login**.
5. **Validación visual pendiente** del aviso de sangría en la pantalla de arqueo.

## Lo que queda abierto

- El `$2.2M` de faltante oculto es un **hallazgo de negocio**, no una tarea de este PR: ahora es visible, pero nadie lo ha revisado todavía.
- `c47` se guarda **sin afirmar qué hace**: no está en el decode y no se contrastó contra la UI de Kepler. Se ve como un segundo escalón (el cajón rebasa `c46` en 11.7 % de los turnos y `c47` en sólo 1.77 %), pero eso es inferencia por comportamiento.
- No se pudo probar desde la DB si Kepler **le pide** el retiro a la cajera (modal/bloqueo) o si es una política que la gente cumple. El dato es idéntico en los dos casos. Se cierra preguntándole a la encargada de 8ESQ.

📋 Detalle en [`FASE_SM`](docs/IMPLEMENTACION/FASES/FASE_SM_SUPERVISOR_MOVIMIENTOS.md) · trampas nuevas en `GOTCHAS` §50–51.

author: sherwinski
body:
# Description

## 1 Line Summary

Add a multi-user `JwtTokenStore` in localStorage and remove the dead single-slot `jwtToken` IndexedDB row.

## Details

Fourth and last M1 pull request for [Identity Verification for Web SDK](https://linear.app/onesignal/project/identity-verification-for-web-sdk-800ed255b785). Covers SDK-5225 and SDK-5226 in one change, as SDK-5226 asks. Stacked on #1488 (SDK-5223). Targets `sherwin/sdk-5223` now; retarget to `feat/identity-verification` after the earlier PRs merge.

Follows decision D3 in the design doc: localStorage, one JSON map under one key. Mirrors Android `user/internal/jwt/JwtTokenStore.kt`.

**`src/core/JwtTokenStore.ts`**

- In-memory map `externalId -> jwt`, lazy loaded from localStorage key `os_jwt_tokens`. Persisted as one JSON object. Malformed JSON logs a warning and starts empty. Non-object values and non-string entries are dropped on load.
- `_getJwt(externalId)` returns `undefined` when absent. Android returns `null`; `undefined` matches the map lookup on web and avoids a conversion.
- `_putJwt(externalId, jwt)`: a missing token is a no-op. Persists and fires the internal update listener only on change.
- `_invalidateJwt(externalId)`: removes, persists, then fires the developer-facing invalidated listener with `{ externalId }`, only if an entry existed. Does not fire the internal update listener. Each listener runs in its own try/catch, so one throwing listener cannot break the others or reach the operation queue. The store updates its state before it fires, so a listener that calls `_putJwt` during the event sees the removal first.
- `_pruneToExternalIds(activeIds)`: drops tokens for users not in the set and fires the internal listener for each removed id. No production caller yet; the prune-on-init caller needs operations to carry `externalId` (M2, SDK-5227).
- Two listener audiences, like Android: `_addInternalUpdateListener` and `_addUserJwtInvalidatedListener`, each with a remove. No replay for late subscribers.
- Storage is unconditional. Use of the tokens is gated by `IdentityVerificationService` in M2 and M3.
- Listeners fire synchronously. Android dispatches the public event on a background thread because its operation queue runs on a dedicated thread; web has one thread and the per-listener try/catch gives the same isolation.

**Wiring**

- `CoreModule` constructs the store. `CoreModuleDirector._jwtTokenStore` exposes it.
- `LoginManager._login` writes through `_putJwt(externalId, token)` before the "externalId already set" check, so `login(sameId, newToken)` stores the new token. The "wake the queue" half of that behavior is SDK-5240 (M4).

**SDK-5226: dead row removal**

- Removed the fire-and-forget `db.put('Ids', { id: token, type: 'jwtToken' })`. Nothing read it.
- Removed `'jwtToken'` from the `IdKey` union.
- No one-time cleanup of a stale `jwtToken` row. The ticket rates it low value, and the row is harmless.

Not in this PR: the cross-tab `storage` listener (D6) is SDK-5248 in M5. The public `userJwtInvalidated` event on `OneSignal.User` is SDK-5241 in M4; it will subscribe to this store.

**Bundle size.** Adds about 338 B to `page.es6.js`. The page limit moves to the measured 43.63 kB, per the repo convention. Across the 4 M1 PRs the page bundle grows from 42.78 kB to 43.62 kB (about 840 B). SDK-5252 (M6) tracks the budget for the whole IV project.

# Systems Affected

- [x] WebSDK
- [ ] Backend
- [ ] Dashboard

# Validation

## Tests

### Info

New `src/core/JwtTokenStore.test.ts`, 25 cases, mirrors `JwtTokenStoreTests.kt:18-293`:

- get missing, put and replace, put null or undefined no-op, invalidate, invalidate absent.
- Persistence: round trip through a fresh instance for put and invalidate, exact persisted shape, malformed JSON recovery with a warning, non-object and non-string entries dropped.
- Prune: removes inactive, fires per removed id, no-op when nothing to remove.
- Internal listener: fires on change only, not on invalidate, not after unsubscribe.
- Public listener: fires with `externalId`, not for an absent token, throwing subscriber isolated, late subscriber gets nothing, removed listener stops, re-entrant put sees the removal first.
- The director exposes the store.

`LoginManager.test.ts`: the token test now asserts the store call and the stored value. New case: `login(sameId, newToken)` stores the token.

`vp check`, `vp test` (605 tests), and `vp run build:prod` pass.

### Checklist

- [x] All the automated tests pass or I explained why that is not possible
- [x] I have personally tested this on my machine or explained why that is not possible
- [x] I have included test coverage for these changes or explained why they are not needed

**Programming Checklist**
Interfaces:

- [x] Don't use default export
- [x] New interfaces are in model files

Functions:

- [x] Don't use default export
- [x] All function signatures have return types
- [x] Helpers should not access any data but rather be given the data to operate on.

Typescript:

- [x] No Typescript warnings
- [x] Avoid silencing null/undefined warnings with the exclamation point

Other:

- [x] Iteration: refrain from using `elem of array` syntax. Prefer `forEach` or use `map`
- [x] Avoid using global OneSignal accessor for `context` if possible. Instead, we can pass it to function/constructor so that we don't call `OneSignal.context`

## Screenshots

### Info

Not needed. No UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have included screenshots/recordings of the intended results or explained why they are not needed

---

## Related Tickets

- [SDK-5225](https://linear.app/onesignal/issue/SDK-5225/add-a-multi-user-jwt-token-store)
- [SDK-5226](https://linear.app/onesignal/issue/SDK-5226/remove-the-dead-single-slot-jwttoken-row-and-idkey-entry)
- Decision: [SDK-5214](https://linear.app/onesignal/issue/SDK-5214/decide-jwt-token-storage-localstorage-or-indexeddb)

author: whazzark
body:
## Summary

A planned discharge's trucks were only seeded. This PR lets an operations lead or admin choose which trucks a planned discharge holds and which of those each planned shift uses, then correct everything planned for a shift, and correct all the product lots of one customer at once. Planned discharges may compete for the same truck, and the competition stays visible on every pool entry.

## Issue and feature artifacts

Issue: Closes #55

Spec: `specs/discharge-preparation/discharge-resource-planning-and-activation-conflicts/plan-the-discharge-truck-pool-and-shift-subsets/spec.md`

The plan, research, data model, contracts (`truck-pool.openapi.yaml`, `ui-state.md`), quickstart, and tasks sit beside it. The customer lots correction, delivered under the same issue, has its own set in `correct-a-customers-product-lots-at-once/`.

## Reviewer focus

- **Concurrency.** Every write locks the discharge `FOR UPDATE`, then only the resources it newly uses `FOR SHARE`, in one order: users, trucks, warehouses and their doors, weighing areas. The pool, shifts, and selections take no lock of their own, since every writer locks the discharge first.
  - **Hardened outside the slice.** The truck transport-company change now checks usage under a lock, as GH-53 did for the dock and customer archives.
  - **Test gap.** The local test database is SQLite, which ignores row locks. Lock order is asserted in unit tests with stubbed repositories, and the races themselves are covered by design and review.
- **Shift correction.** `PUT /discharges/:dischargeId/shifts/:shiftId` replaces the period, responsible, trucks, doors, and weighing areas in one transaction and renumbers shifts by planned start. Renumbering parks shifts above the highest sequence first, because the unique index is checked row by row. A resource that stays selected is not re-checked, so it may stay after being archived or suspended.
- **Customer lots correction.** Lot identity is judged on the lots as they will be after the change, so swaps are legal. Lots whose identity changes are parked under their own id before their final values are written, for the same row-by-row index reason.
- **One refusal shape.** Entered values that are refused are `422 E_VALIDATION_ERROR` with the offending field path (`truckIds.N`, `warehouseDoorIds.N`, `productLots.N.*`, …). State refusals are `404 E_SHIFT_NOT_FOUND`, `409 E_SHIFT_NOT_PLANNED`, `409 E_DISCHARGE_NOT_PLANNED`, and `409 E_DISCHARGE_LAST_PRODUCT_LOT`.
- **Commits.** The commits can be reviewed one at a time: the truck pool, the shift correction with its calendar, the customer lots correction, the seeds, and the fixes from a fresh-session review.
- **Kept on purpose.** `PUT …/shifts/:shiftId/trucks` has no web caller any more, since the panel corrects the whole shift. It stays in the contract and now shares its selection logic with the shift correction; removing it is a separate decision.

## Delivered changes

- **API**:
  - `GET …/truck-pool/candidates` lists the available trucks the discharge does not hold, each with the other planned or active discharges holding it.
  - `POST …/truck-pool` and `POST …/truck-pool/withdrawals` reserve and withdraw sets of trucks. A withdrawal also deletes the trucks' current selections in the planned shifts.
  - `PUT …/shifts/:shiftId/trucks` replaces a planned shift's truck selection, and `PUT …/shifts/:shiftId` corrects the whole shift.
  - `POST …/product-lots` now adds several lots at once, and `PATCH …/customers/:customerId/product-lots` corrects, adds, and removes one customer's lots, optionally moving them to another customer.
  - Every write is idempotent as a set operation and answers with the discharge detail, whose pool entries gain `otherHoldings`.
- **Web: discharge detail**:
  - Split into tabs, with a preparation summary.
  - **Truck pool**: `Add trucks` sheet with candidate search, row selection, and a `Withdraw trucks` confirmation that names the affected planned shifts. Other holdings show as an `Also held` marker for every role.
  - **Shifts**: a calendar of 24-hour columns opening at the expected start, with the expected start and the current time drawn and the hour gutter kept in view while it scrolls. Choosing a shift opens a side panel with its details and, for preparers, its correction form.
  - **Product lots**: `Add product lots` for several lots, and `Edit` on a customer's group, which opens the whole group in one sheet with removal blocks explained in tooltips.
- **Seeds**: a larger fleet so several discharges hold eight to sixteen trucks at once, with suspended trucks still selected by a planned shift.
- **Vocabulary**: `CONTEXT.md` gains the exclusivity rule and the Truck Pool Withdrawal term.
- **Not included**: activity log entries, and the start confirmation that settles competing holdings (GH-56, GH-65).

## Database

- [x] No migration in this PR

## Verification

- **Automated checks**: `pnpm check` and `pnpm typecheck` pass. API: 1696 tests passed, run with `PORT=3399`. Web: 332 files, 1705 tests passed.
- **Per commit**: the shift correction and customer lots commits were each type-checked and tested on their own (web discharge tests, API `shifts/*` and `preparation/*` suites).
- **Review**: a fresh Claude Code session reviewed the diff. Its seven findings were fixed in the last commit, each with a test: adding lots through a customer without lots, an ineligible responsible blocking the correction, a refused removal leaving the sheet stuck, calendar drift on clock-change days, a period rounded to the minute, the duplicated truck selection logic, and two duration formats.
- **Browser journeys**: not exercised end to end. The sticky hour gutter fix was checked on a reduced reproduction of the calendar layout in Chromium.

## Ready-for-review checklist

- [x] The linked issue and spec describe the delivered scope without duplication
- [x] Spec, plan, tasks, and implementation are aligned when Spec Kit artifacts apply
- [ ] Acceptance criteria were verified against the delivered result
- [x] `pnpm check && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` run locally and pass
- [ ] Affected browser journeys were exercised when `apps/web` changed
- [ ] A fresh Codex session reviewed the final diff
- [x] Confirmed review findings were resolved or explicitly justified
- [x] New domain terms and durable architecture decisions are documented where applicable

author: copilot
body:
This introduces the first test scaffold for evaluating whether XC can serve as a semantic interlingua for deterministic, stateful, history-dependent adaptive systems. It establishes the core harness, starter fixtures, and boundary annotations needed to compare backend behavior and document known non-expressible cases.

- **Harness and execution model**
  - Adds `test_harness.py` to discover `.xc` fixtures, parse test metadata, run multiple backends, and aggregate equivalence outcomes.
  - Treats known non-expressible fixtures as explicit boundary cases instead of runtime failures.

- **Reference backends**
  - Adds `backends/` with a shared backend interface and deterministic reference implementations for multiple placeholder language targets.
  - Produces normalized traces with state, observation, measures, action choice, and memory size per cycle.

- **Equivalence and invariant oracles**
  - Adds `oracles.py` for:
    - trace equivalence
    - absolute/relative numeric error
    - structural invariant checks
    - branching consistency across backends

- **Starter XC fixtures**
  - Adds 5 initial fixtures in `fixtures/` covering:
    - simple linear dynamics
    - nonlinear policy selection
    - episodic memory / decay shape
    - flattened hierarchical state
    - stochastic boundary classification

- **Reporting and methodology**
  - Adds `report.py` to render a compact markdown summary of fixture coverage, equivalence results, and expressiveness boundaries.
  - Adds `METHODOLOGY.md` and updates `README.md` to define scope, assumptions, and the intended testing philosophy.

- **Focused test coverage**
  - Adds small standard-library unit tests for fixture discovery, harness classification, oracle metrics, and deterministic backend equivalence.

Example fixture metadata now drives the harness directly:

```xc
# xc-test:name=linear_4d
# xc-test:category=semantic-equivalence
# xc-test:expressible=true
# xc-test:state_dim=4
# xc-test:cycles=4
# xc-test:operator_complexity=linear
# xc-test:memory_capacity=0
# xc-test:policy_actions=2
# xc-test:measure_count=2
state x[4]
operator step = tanh(Wx + b)
policy select = argmax(measure)
```

author: rpinset
body:
Forward-port of #287462 to 19.0.

Description of the issue/feature this PR addresses:

Odoo task 6560278: after the French e-invoicing reform, customers who only issue standalone commercial credit notes (avoirs francs, no original invoice) cannot emit/send them in UBL 2.1 because `l10n_fr_pdp` requires `reversed_entry_id` (BT-25).

XP Z12-012 **BR-FR-CO-03** documents UNTDID 1001 code **262** for that case: contract (BT-12) + invoicing period (BG-14), no preceding invoice (BT-25). CDAR flux 10 stays on TypeCode **381**.

CI-safe implementation (same as 18.0 after CI fixes):
- No extra `account.move` columns (upgrade clones fields onto `account.bank.statement.line`).
- Type 262 is inferred for French companies only (`account_fiscal_country_id.code == 'FR'` + `out_refund` without `reversed_entry_id`). This avoids leaking `InvoicePeriod` / `ContractDocumentReference` onto other l10n golden files when `l10n_fr_pdp` is auto-installed on all-l10n CI.

## Summary

* Skip the BT-25 constraint and `cac:BillingReference` when the refund is a standalone commercial credit note.
* Export TypeCode `262`, `ContractDocumentReference`, and `InvoicePeriod` on UBL BIS3, UBL 2.1 FR, CII and Factur-X.
* Keep CDAR `_get_move_typecode` at `381`.
* Help text on the credit note form (no extra stored fields).

## Test plan

* `odoo-bin -u l10n_fr_pdp --test-enable --stop-after-init --test-tags=credit_note_262` (Docker local: 9 tests, 0 failed, 0 error)
* Create a customer credit note without reversing an invoice, set customer ref / dates, send UBL 2.1 FR
* Create a standard credit note from an invoice: still TypeCode 381 with BillingReference

## Reviewers & code owners

* Requested review: @smetl @chklop
* Prior authors on touched code: @malb-odoo @gawa-odoo @jbw-odoo

author: josuealmonasi
body:
A cashier adds ten Calamari, presses charge, and is told *"ya no queda"* — with a customer standing there and no way to find out how many they could have had. The count was on the tile's own row in the database the whole time, and nothing showed it.

## Three parts

**The tiles carry it** — on the till and the waiter's pad, for the dishes that track stock. Most do not, and a tag on those would be a number nobody can act on. Quiet grey; accent when it is down to the last few.

It is a **reading, not a promise**: between seeing it and pressing it somebody else can take the last one, and `reserve_stock` settles that. Nothing trusts the number, which is what makes showing it safe.

**The count follows the kitchen.** `useLiveStock` is `useLiveOrders` pointed at `menu_items`, which joins the realtime publication. Measured: **2.5s** from the shelf changing to the tile changing. The diner's menu keeps polling instead, for the reason already written into `useMenuFreshness` — their read policy is `available AND menu active`, so a dish selling out takes the row out of their reach and the event with it.

**The refusal says the number.** `reserve_stock` has always returned how many are really left, and every screen threw it away:

> No alcanza: Calamari (sólo quedan 4); Ribeye (ya no queda). Ajusta la venta antes de cobrar.

Zero gets its own words, because "ya no queda" is not "quedan 0". The diner's checkout already did this (`apiErr.onlyLeft` names the count) — it was only the two staff screens that were guessing.

## The RLS cases took three attempts, each wrong in an instructive way

1. *"No anonymous listener may hear a menu change."* Called the result a leak and nearly pulled the feature. Wrong: anon already reads those rows, `stock` included, by plain select — deliberately, and the schema says so.
2. *"No foreign till may hear one."* Same mistake: a live menu is public to anyone who scans a QR, and a plain select from foreign staff proves it.
3. What is **actually** private is a dish the neighbour has taken *off* their menu — `available = false` puts it out of reach of a plain select, and realtime has to agree.

That is what the check asks now, and the comment records why the first two were not findings so the next reader doesn't repeat them.

```
ok  a stock change reaches the till it belongs to
ok  and a dish another restaurant has hidden stays hidden on the socket
```

Gates: `pnpm test` ✓ · `pnpm api` ✓ · `pnpm rls` ✓ · `pnpm money` ✓ · `pnpm layout` ✓ · looked at the tiles with real counts on them.

**Migration:** `alter publication supabase_realtime add table menu_items`. Production is migrated before this merges.

body:
On a phone the cover fills the height left over, so it shrank each time something arrived below it: hints, a guess history row, the last round's four choices. On short screens the guess box also started below the fold.

**Changes**
- The guess history no longer shows during a round. A note ("Right artist · <song>", "Wrong · <song>") floats over the cover's lower edge for a few seconds after each guess, taking no space. The list still shows under the reveal.
- The hint row and the guess box hold their final height on a phone from the start. Hints scroll in one row, and a last-round choice's title is one line.
- The mode pills scroll in one row on a phone, and the set panel sits outside the scroller so it is not clipped.
- The round's root used `overflow-y-auto`, which made it the scroll container and stopped the guess box from pinning to the screen. It now clips horizontally only.
- The cover's minimum on a phone is 96px, down from 160px, so a short screen fits without overlap.
- The cover frame gets `isolate` and a WebKit mask, the usual fix for Safari dropping a rounded clip on a blurred child.

Fixes the tractable quick-win subset of the #136 failed ports whose name starts with a letter in **[m-r]**. All 13 recipes were built natively on a Graviton arm64 builder (from the builder-canonical AMI), verified RC=0 with a **non-empty** hpkg, and harvested to `s3://haiku-graviton-668984504585-us-west-2/hpkg/arm64/`. Part of #136.

author: siy
body:
A full audit of all 608 tracked files, after the ruling that **published work is history but sensitive information stays sensitive**.

## What this removes

**Two files carrying named third parties' private material** — the substantive part:
- `book-arch-meta/ENGAGEMENT-2026-07-06.md` (170 lines) — an engagement log with a *"Ready-to-paste replies"* section, seven named individuals with platform attribution, one entry recording a **personal DM**, and per-person send/permission status.
- `book-pfd-meta/reviewer-feedback.md` (792 lines) — a named reviewer's round-by-round private read of an **unpublished draft**, self-headed *"author reference — not shipped"*. It said it was not shipped; it was in a public repo.

Both are preserved in the project's private record. Neither is deleted.

**33 private repository path references across 13 files** — replaced with descriptors that keep the notes usable (*"the PFD book spec (private)"*) while dropping repo layout. Four of these were **absolute paths including the username**, disclosing home-directory structure.

## The limit, stated plainly

**This removes both files from `HEAD`. It does not remove them from git history**, where they remain fully retrievable in every existing clone — and the same is true of the handovers archived in #84. A history purge requires a force-push that breaks every clone, and that is the owner's decision, not something this PR does or implies. A reader should not take "removed" here as "unrecoverable".

## What was deliberately left alone

- **Published attributions.** The books credit several of these same people in acknowledgments and references. Those are intended public credit; the same person can be credited in a book and not have their DMs published, and stripping the credits would damage the work rather than protect anyone.
- **False positives on the job title.** `MANAGEMENT_PERSPECTIVE.md`, `book-pfd/closing.md` and `book-arch/derivation.md` matched a "CTO" pattern because it is the job title in book and marketing prose.
- **16 handover files** still holding private paths are exactly the set #84 deletes — verified by set comparison, so editing them here would only create modify/delete conflicts.

## Untracked and gitignored files

Asked and answered, with the space stated: **512 untracked/ignored files, 382 of them text**. Three contain the same patterns, all under `.claude/` (local session scratch, gitignored, never published). Gitignored is not the same as safe — a `git add -f` or a change to `.gitignore` would publish them — but nothing there is currently exposed. My first run of this audit was **invalid** and I redid it: it grepped binaries whose empty output passed the test, and skipped directories entirely.

## Verification

`All internal links resolve (89 pages checked)` · 170 tests pass, 0 fail · `check-drift.sh` exit 0 · `sync-book-blocks.py --check` in sync · 0 residual private-path hits outside the set #84 deletes · both halves of the file move confirmed sha256-identical before either side was committed.

Every replacement was re-read individually afterwards, which caught eight mangled sentences the scripted pass produced — including `CLAUDE.md` rendering as "live in the private `a private document` repo".

author: lucashamburguru
body:
💡 **What**
Replaced string allocations (`.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase()`) in `is_rocket_league_name` and the `read_dir` loop of `replays.rs` with `eq_ignore_ascii_case`. Replaced `to_lowercase().replace('\\', "/")` in `rocket_league_argument_match` with an inline `.as_bytes().windows(len)` matching closure that normalizes casing and slashes on the fly. 

🎯 **Why**
When the application runs system-wide process scanning to monitor for the game's executable, these string parsing functions are executed repeatedly across hundreds of active process arguments. Allocating a new `String` for every checked argument causes excessive memory allocation and deallocation pressure, dragging down overall loop performance and increasing baseline memory usage over time.

📊 **Impact**
Eliminates hundreds of unnecessary short-lived `String` heap allocations on every polling tick, shifting the cost to an O(1) allocation path operating directly on the native underlying byte slices.

🔬 **Measurement**
Run the test suite `cargo test` and confirm all previous process tracking tests complete normally. During application execution, the background scanning loop overhead should be measurably reduced.

author: seflue
body:
Closes #440

## Bug

A keybinding configured as a literal uppercase letter never matches. Ten
defaults are uppercase: `J` and `K` for global `scroll_down` / `scroll_up`,
plus `A`, `D`, `G`, `M`, `P`, `R`, `S` and `W`. None of them can be remapped.

Nine of them still work, because each is also dispatched through a paired bare
`KeyCode::Char(...)` check. Rebinding one reports no error and has no effect,
and the old key keeps working.

`G` has no such pair. `drill_into_scope` is reached only through
`keybinding_matches`, at `src/handlers/tabs.rs:360` for issues and `:527` for
MRs, so the action is unreachable.

## Root Cause

The `other.len() == 1` arm in `keybinding_matches` required
`event.modifiers.is_empty()`. crossterm 0.29 attaches `KeyModifiers::SHIFT` to
every uppercase character event, so the comparison could never succeed for an
uppercase binding.

The arm now derives the expected modifiers from the binding character:
`SHIFT` when it is uppercase, none otherwise. Lowercase bindings keep
rejecting a shifted event, which the new test
`lowercase_single_char_binding_does_not_match_shifted_key` asserts.

Needs #453, merged.

## Verification

- [x] Added/updated tests

`uppercase_single_char_binding_does_not_match_shifted_key` asserts the old
behaviour. Its comment calls that behaviour "documented, current, intentional"
and says not to change the assertion but to fix the call site instead. This PR
does the opposite, so that is the call to make on it. Fixing the call sites
leaves every uppercase binding unremappable and `G` unreachable, which is what
#440 reports. This PR inverts the test and renames it to
`uppercase_single_char_binding_matches_shifted_key`.

## Still open

author: zarcen
body:
## Summary

bink CLI, cluster, and DNS images are amd64-only, blocking arm64 support for bootc-operator (bootc-dev/bootc-operator#145). None of the three cross-compile: the CLI links CGO, cluster/DNS are pure RPM installs. This builds each arch natively (`ubuntu-24.04`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`), then assembles a v2s2 manifest list in a separate `push` job, mirroring bootc-operator's existing pattern (bootc-dev/bootc-operator@7b3b091).

## Testing

Dispatched all three workflows with `push: false` on this branch from my fork. Both arches built successfully for all three images, including the CGO build. The `push`/manifest job itself needs GHCR write access and wasn't exercised here; its logic mirrors bootc-operator's already-merged manifest job.

## How to validate

```sh
gh workflow run build-bink-image.yaml --ref bink-arm64-ci-images -f push=true
gh workflow run build-cluster-image.yaml --ref bink-arm64-ci-images -f push=true
gh workflow run build-dns-image.yaml --ref bink-arm64-ci-images -f push=true
```
on a fork, or merge and watch the real push run on `main`.

### Validation result
- bink-image: https://github.com/zarcen/bink/actions/runs/35033958933
- cluster-image: https://github.com/zarcen/bink/actions/runs/35034015294
- dns-image: https://github.com/zarcen/bink/actions/runs/35034030326

Also tested to really push to my ghcr so I can sanity check the image manifest:

```sh
docker pull ghcr.io/zarcen/bink/dns:latest
docker pull ghcr.io/zarcen/bink/cluster:latest
docker pull ghcr.io/zarcen/bink/bink:latest
```

Started a local bink cluster locally on Apple Silicon (arm64) :
```sh
# loading arm64 images to podman
podman machine ssh -- podman pull ghcr.io/zarcen/bink/bink:latest
podman machine ssh -- podman pull ghcr.io/zarcen/bink/cluster:latest
podman machine ssh -- podman pull ghcr.io/zarcen/bink/dns:latest
podman machine ssh -- podman tag ghcr.io/zarcen/bink/bink:latest    ghcr.io/bootc-dev/bink/bink:latest
podman machine ssh -- podman tag ghcr.io/zarcen/bink/cluster:latest ghcr.io/bootc-dev/bink/cluster:latest
podman machine ssh -- podman tag ghcr.io/zarcen/bink/dns:latest    ghcr.io/bootc-dev/bink/dns:latest

# start cluster locally
bink cluster start --cluster-name test --api-port 0
bink cluster list
Found 1 cluster(s):

  ✓ test (1 node(s), running)
bink node list --cluster-name test
Found 1 cluster node(s):

  ✓ node1 (role: control-plane, status: running, created: 2026-09-15 16:33:43)
```

## Out of scope

`ghcr.io/bootc-dev/bink/node` (the bootc VM disk image, built in `integration-tests.yml`'s `build-node-images` job) is not covered here. Turns out getting it to arm64 is bigger than expected: the current `bcvk to-disk` step hard-requires `/dev/kvm`, and GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners don't expose one at all. There's a promising KVM-free path via `bootc-image-builder`, but that means swapping the actual disk-build tool, a bigger architecture change than fits here. I will track it in a follow-up PR.

Partially addresses #140: covers the bink CLI, cluster, and DNS images

---

I'm knowledgeable in this problem domain and reviewed the diff and CI run logs carefully. Besides, to ensure the PR quality, several rounds of manually validation and test are conducted

## What this does Publishes four Eastern Panhandle service+city pages for queries the site **already ranks for** but gets no clicks on, and fixes a class of no-op metadata override found while building them. New combos: | Page | Query evidence (Search Console) | |---|---| | `basements-ranson-wv` | `basement remodel ranson wv` — pos 5.1, 15 impressions
`basement remodeling ranson wv` — pos 3.2, 5 impressions | | `basements-inwood-wv` | `basement remodeling inwood wv` — pos 5.7, 14 impressions | | `basements-charles-town-wv` | home turf; adjacent to the two above, no standalone page before | | `decks-martinsburg-wv` | `composite decking martinsburg` — pos 26.4, 29 impressions | Every one of these was previously answered by a generic `/service-areas/` page whose snippet read "Expert basement finishing services in X". Position 3.2 with zero clicks is a snippet problem, not a ranking problem. `ranson-wv` and `inwood-wv` are added to `COMBO_CITY_SLUGS`. ## Titles now match the query language Three of the basement `metaTitle` values initially shipped byte-identical to what the fallback template already produces — the override rendered the same string and bought nothing. Worse, the generic title says "Basement **Finishing**" while the queries say "basement **remodeling**", so there was no query term for Google to bold. Titles now carry both terms, inside the 60-char budget: - `Basement Finishing & Remodeling in Ranson, WV | Real Elite` (58) - `Basement Finishing & Remodeling in Inwood, WV | Real Elite` (58) - `Basement Finishing & Remodeling in Charles Town, WV` (51) ## Small refactor: one definition of the fallback The generic title/description templates were inlined in `generateMetadata`. They move into `service-city-content.ts` as `defaultComboTitle` / `defaultComboDescription`, next to the overrides they back. The route calls them; the test compares each override against the **real** template rather than a duplicated copy that could drift. This is a pure refactor — verified that a combo with no override (`/services/kitchens/vienna-va`) renders byte-identical metadata. ## On prices The basement descriptions quote the **egress window** cost ($3,500–$6,500), which the site already publishes. They deliberately do **not** quote a whole-basement price range for WV — no such figure is published anywhere on the site, and inventing one to fill the snippet is exactly the kind of claim that gets a contractor held to a number they never quoted. The deck description reuses the per-square-foot rates the deck pages already carry. ## Tests Added a guard that fails when an override merely restates the fallback. I verified it fails on the old Ranson title before restoring the fixed one, rather than assuming it works. The basement rules that landed in #118 now also apply to these three WV pages (dollar figure present, description ≤165 chars) — they pass. ## Validation - `tsc --noEmit` — clean - `npm run lint` — 0 errors (3 pre-existing `` warnings in test files) - `npm test` — 554 passed, 42 files - `npm run build` — 250/250 static pages; all four new routes confirmed rendering their own titles ## Note This branch merges `main` (through #118). The merge had one conflict in the test file where my describe block and #118's landed in the same position — both were kept, they test different things. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01UBYrx5NkmeC9eWDrDEcYUD --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01UBYrx5NkmeC9eWDrDEcYUD)_

author: mahabayana
body:
## Summary
 
 Adds a native Windows ARM64 build job for `upscayl-bin` using GitHub's `windows-11-arm` runner. The job verifies the complete ARM64 toolchain and runtime closure before publishing a diagnostic artifact.
 
 ## What changed
 
 - Selects Visual Studio 2022 with the ARM64 C++ toolchain.
 - Verifies the ARM64 compiler, Windows SDK import libraries, and `dumpbin`.
 - Downloads a pinned Windows ARM64 Vulkan SDK and verifies its SHA-256.
 - Verifies that `glslangValidator` can run natively and that `vulkan-1.lib` targets ARM64.
 - Configures CMake with the official `Visual Studio 17 2022` generator and `-A arm64`.
 - Builds `upscayl-bin` in Release mode.
 - Locates the Microsoft ARM64 OpenMP runtime and verifies its architecture and Authenticode signature.
 - Rejects x64 binaries and debug runtime dependencies.
 - Uploads the ARM64 backend, OpenMP runtime, build logs, and architecture report as a diagnostic artifact.
 
 ## Validation
 
 The equivalent workflow completed successfully on a GitHub-hosted Windows ARM64 runner:
 
 - CI run: https://github.com/mahabayana/upscayl-ncnn/actions/runs/34900090037
 - `upscayl-bin.exe`: PE machine `0xAA64`
 - `vcomp140.dll`: PE machine `0xAA64`, valid Microsoft signature
 
 The resulting backend was also tested on a physical Windows-on-Arm device with a Qualcomm Adreno X1-85 GPU. It selected the native Qualcomm Vulkan provider and completed an offline 256×256 to 1024×1024 upscale successfully.
 
 ## Scope and limitations
 
 - This PR changes CI only; it does not publish a production release.
 - The Vulkan SDK version and checksum are intentionally pinned and will require maintenance when upgraded.
 - Physical validation covered one Snapdragon-class device, one model, and one fixed fixture.
 - The successful device run required an explicit tile size of `200`; that is a device-specific validated setting, not a universal default.

author: olafkfreund
body:
Closes #1835

## Artifacts

- Intent: `intent/2026-09-15-1835-npm-global-path-order.md` (approved)
- Spec: `spec/2026-09-15-1835-npm-global-path-order.md` (approved)
- Plan: `plan/2026-09-15-1835-npm-global-path-order.md` (approved)

Review compares this diff against `plan/`.

## What changes

`~/go/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` are **appended** after the Nix profiles instead of prepended, so a tool installed by `go install`, `cargo install` or `npm i -g` can never shadow the Nix command of the same name. `~/bin`, `~/.local/bin` and `~/.config/rofi/scripts` still come first — Home Manager's `claude` launcher lives in `~/.local/bin`.

- `home/development/npm-prefix.nix`: `home.sessionPath` (which prepends) → a guarded append in `home.sessionVariablesExtra`.
- `home/development/languages.nix`: the go and cargo appends, behind the same `languages.{go,rust}.enable` conditions as `GOPATH`/`CARGO_HOME`.
- `home/shell/bash.nix`: the same three in `bashrcExtra`, because `ssh host cmd` shells never source `hm-session-vars.sh`. A `case` guard keeps each directory to one entry when both files run.

Side effect: zsh now sees the go and cargo tools at all — it previously had neither on PATH.

## Duplicates removed (plan D4, runtime)

- razer: `cargo uninstall bottom fd-find globe-cli` → `fd`, `btm` and `globe` now resolve to Nix.
- Empty `@openai` (p620) and `@anthropic-ai` (razer) npm scope directories removed.
- p620 had no duplicates.

## Tests

| # | Result |
| --- | --- |
| T1 `check-syntax`, `test-host` p620 + razer, p510 eval | pass |
| T2 PATH order in 4 shell kinds × 2 hosts (zsh login, bash login, bash interactive, ssh non-interactive) | **OK ×8**: Nix profile before all three dirs, each dir once, `~/.local/bin` still first |
| T3 tools that exist only in those dirs still resolve | pass: jshint, neovim-node-host, sqlx, cross, zoe, staticcheck, spofi (razer, login and ssh); golangci-lint, tokio-console (p620) |
| T4 duplicate inventory on both hosts; `cargo install --list` | 0 duplicates; no bottom, fd-find or globe-cli |
| T5 `type -a -p fd btm globe claude` on razer | Nix first for all; `claude` → `~/.local/bin/claude` (the HM link) |
| T6 `npm i -g prettier` on razer | `prettier` still resolves to `/etc/profiles/per-user/olafkfreund/bin/prettier` first; probe uninstalled |

Deployed to p620 and razer (announced on the agent bus), no failed units, `home-manager-olafkfreund` active on both. p510 was evaluated only.

author: dahagag
body:
## Summary

Closes the latent bootstrap deadlock behind #218's release-order guard — the root cause that PRs #308, #309 and #310 each worked around a symptom of, and that was resolved one-time yesterday by importing the parameter into `infra/platform` state.

**The conflict**: both the guard and `infra/platform` created `/platform-administration-stack-api/deployed-commit`, and the guard always won. `record-deployed-commit` runs *before* `tofu apply` — deliberately, per the review on #306 — and `put-parameter --overwrite` creates the parameter when it's absent. Terraform's own create then failed with `ParameterAlreadyExists`. It deadlocked the first bootstrap and would deadlock again on any rebuild of `infra/platform`'s state.

**The fix** restores the split [`ssm.tf`](infra/platform/ssm.tf) already documents — *Terraform owns existence, CI owns value* — by making CI stop creating. The action reads the parameter first and skips its write when it doesn't exist yet, leaving creation to the apply later in the same job. The record-before-apply ordering is untouched.

Only `ParameterNotFound` is tolerated; any other read failure still fails loud rather than silently skipping the claim and letting a stale job win the race — the same distinction `check-release-order` already draws on its own read.

**Why not adopt from the Terraform side** (the option that looks obvious): `overwrite = true` is deprecated — the AWS provider v5 upgrade guide says to import existing parameters instead, and that creating an existing parameter will fail outright in a future version. Worse, on create it would write the resource's own `value = "unset"` straight over the commit the guard had just recorded, breaking the guard exactly when it matters.

**Cost**: on a virgin account the watermark reads `unset` for exactly one run, until the next push records onto the now-existing parameter — the window `check-release-order` already treats as "first-ever deploy, nothing to compare against".

**No IAM change**: `ssm:GetParameter` is already granted to this role, so unlike #309/#310 this needs no human-operator apply and lands entirely through CI.

## Test plan

- [x] `action.yml` parses; embedded script passes `bash -n`
- [x] `tofu fmt -check -recursive infra/`
- [x] Stubbed-`aws` harness over all three branches of the new logic:
  - parameter exists → records (exit 0, `put-parameter` called)
  - `ParameterNotFound` → skips, leaves create to tofu (exit 0, no `put-parameter`)
  - `AccessDenied` → fails loud (exit 1, no `put-parameter`)
- [ ] Post-merge: staging deploy stays green against the existing parameter (the update path — the skip path only exercises on a virgin account)

Permite gestionar estados desde la cola y la ficha por empresa, sin abrir cada ticket: selección explícita de visibles, cambio individual y cambio masivo atómico. El lote reutiliza la mutación de detalle, valida cada ticket y revierte completo ante un error. Conserva prioridad y responsable bajo lock. Límite técnico: 100 tickets. La selección se reinicia al cambiar filtros/ruta; no hay selección de resultados ocultos.
