author: downfallz
body:
## What

`baselineR2` read **0.07054 on five consecutive runs** — `ci-72`, `ci-74`, `ci-78`, `ci-80`, `ci-81` — while the lambda moved from 1.0 to 0.5 and back. Every lambda below 1.0 takes its advantage as `V(next) − V(here)` (ADR 0046), so that number was capping the whole mechanism. This is the measurement of what was constraining it, and the two fixes that came out of it.

Measured on the exact 1000-match exploring dataset those runs used, re-recorded locally and identical to them (53.9% / 45.6% / 0.5%, 8.0 rounds), held out by match:

| | all held-out steps | rounds 15-30 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| as fitted, alpha 10 | +0.0705 | **−0.2179** |
| alpha 1000 | +0.0824 | −0.1383 |
| alpha 10000 | +0.1021 | +0.0200 |
| gradient boosting, same features | **+0.1215** | **+0.3760** |

**The alpha was shared and far too low.** `--alpha` also sets the pull on the action rows, which are fitted on a median of sixty examples each and want the small number. One knob served neither. `--baseline-alpha` separates them, **and defaults to sharing**, so every earlier run reproduces unchanged.

**The fit predicted returns that cannot happen.** `Returns.Of` pays ±1 plus a tenth of the health margin, so nothing here is outside 1.05; the linear fit predicts from **−1.78 to +2.19**. In rounds 15 and beyond that made the baseline **worse than predicting a constant** — `r2` −0.2179 against −0.0014 for the training mean. Clipping to the range the training returns take is not a knob: a prediction the target cannot take is wrong by construction.

**End to end on the same dataset**: `baselineR2` **0.0705 → 0.0806** from the clip alone **→ 0.1053** with `--baseline-alpha 10000`, and rounds 15-30 from **−0.2179 → +0.0685**. This is the part of the change that is measured rather than sampled: it is held-out `r2` on data, not a win rate.

**Why it was cheap.** The baseline never changes which action is played: `LinearScorer.scores` adds it to every candidate of a decision alike, and the code already said so — *"The same number for every candidate, so it never changes the winner."* It is a **training-time device**, so no format, engine or feature-schema change. ADR 0048 records that, because it had not been treated that way.

## What the runs on this branch found, including about themselves

Seven loop runs ran on this pull request. Read this section before the numbers in the commits: **`ci-86` through `ci-89` were each a single dataset seed, and `ci-90`/`ci-91` showed that a single seed does not measure anything here.**

Three runs of one configuration — lambda 0.9, this baseline, `search-4` as teacher and baseline, 1000 matches — differing only in the dataset seed, evaluated on the same fixed benchmark seeds:

| by dataset seed | 1 (`ci-88`) | 2 (`ci-90`) | 3 (`ci-91`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value against `search-4` | **0.6625** | **0.0975** | 0.30375 |
| value against `Greedy` | 0.0325 | 0.15375 | 0.03375 |
| clone against `Greedy` | 0.725 | 0.79875 | **0.82125** |
| clone against the champion `ci-69` | 0.5 (itself) | **+0.53625** | **−0.42375** |

**A 56-point spread from the seed alone**, larger than every effect this project has measured. So:

- `ci-88` beating `search-4` — the first time any agent had — is inside the spread and **is not a result**.
- **This PR's own win-rate headline does not stand either.** `ci-86` read 0.29625 against `Greedy` where `ci-72` read 0.10125, one seed each; 19 points is inside the spread. The fit improvement above is real and held-out; **the win-rate claim was a sample and I withdraw it.** ADR 0048 is Accepted and immutable, so the correction lives in **ADR 0049** and in the journal.
- `ci-91`'s clone beats `Greedy` **0.82125**, better than any policy the loop has produced, and **loses to the committed champion at 0.42375** — where that champion beats `Greedy` only 0.725. A third-party score does not order two players. The champion bar refused it, its second correct refusal on this branch.

**ADR 0049 (Proposed)** is what follows: run a configuration on at least three dataset seeds, report a spread, and have the gate require every seed. It names its own cost — three to five times the wall clock per turn — and it is a decision for the maintainer, not something this PR implements.

What does survive more than one seed: the clone beats `Greedy` better at seeds 2 and 3 than at seed 1, and the value policy loses to `Greedy` on every seed.

## Checklist

- [x] `dotnet build`, `dotnet test`, and `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` pass locally
- [x] New behaviour has tests — three, pinning the separate pull, the clip, and that the clip narrows the advantage
- [x] Domain names match `docs/domain/glossary.md` — nothing outside `learning/`, `scripts/`, the workflow and docs changes
- [x] Hard-to-reverse decisions have an ADR — ADR 0048, and ADR 0049 as Proposed
- [x] `AGENTS.md` and docs still describe reality — the journal, `iterate.sh --help`, the workflow input

Verified: build clean (0 warnings), **781 .NET tests**, **321 Python tests**, `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, the workflow YAML parses, `iterate.sh` passes `bash -n`. The shipped change reproduces the probe numbers exactly (0.0806 shared, 0.1053 at 10000), and `ci-86`/`ci-87` reproduce each other to the digit on the same seed.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **The shippable part of this PR is small and inert.** `--baseline-alpha` defaults to `None`, meaning "keep sharing `--alpha`", so every earlier run reproduces unchanged. The clip is not a knob. Everything else here is docs, journal and ADRs.
- **One of my two hypotheses was wrong and is recorded as wrong.** The natural story was that the baseline cannot express "health decides more as the cap approaches" (ADR 0011), since that is an interaction between `round_fraction` — which *is* feature 0 — and the health features, and the model is linear. Adding those terms made it **worse**: 0.0705 → 0.0574 overall, −0.2179 → −0.4375 late. It is in the ADR's Alternatives and in the journal because it was refused, not despite it.
- **A stalling story I wrote and then had to withdraw.** `ci-88` was read as beating `search-4` by dragging it to the round cap. `ci-89` plays `search-4` nearly as long — 16.7 rounds and 29.2% capped against 17.1 and 38.2% — and scores less than half as much. Reaching the cap is not what wins those matches.
- **`baselineR2` is not comparable across this change.** It is now measured on the values actually used, clip included. The step on identical data is 0.0705 → 0.0806, recorded in the journal so the series stays readable — but it is a break, and future runs will not line up with the five that reported 0.07054.
- **The ceiling is the features, not the linearity.** Gradient boosting reaches 0.1215 where a well-regularised linear fit reaches 0.1021 — so little is left for a better *model*, and the remaining signal is in the observation. That is a feature schema change, which invalidates every trained model, so it wants its own decision.
- **A door this opens and does not walk through.** Because the baseline never reaches the engine, a nonlinear baseline is now permissible and would supply the advantage at 0.1215 with no format consequence. ADR 0048 leaves it open on purpose.
- **SonarCloud still reports 2 new issues** and the gate passes. I have not identified them: this session's proxy refuses `sonarcloud.io` with a 403 on the tunnel, and the one candidate I found by reading my own diff (an unquoted `${var:+...}` in `iterate.yml`, now an array) did not change the count. Worth a glance by someone who can open the page; I did not refactor anything else on a guess.

author: cbirkbeck
body:
Roadmap: NumberFieldArithmetic

<!--tauceti-target:v1 {"focus":"NumberFieldArithmetic","id":"TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithmetic/README.md#layer-7/7.3-monogenicity"}-->

Layer 7.3. A number field `K` is **monogenic** when its ring of integers admits a power
integral basis, `𝓞 K = ℤ[θ]`.

```lean
def IsMonogenic (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] : Prop :=
  ∃ θ : 𝓞 K, Algebra.adjoin ℤ {θ} = ⊤
```

### What is here

Both criteria the roadmap asks for:

* `isMonogenic_iff_exists_exponent_eq_one` — via the conductor exponent, on Mathlib's
  `RingOfIntegers.exponent_eq_one_iff`.
* `isMonogenic_iff_exists_index_eq_one` — via the index `[𝓞 K : ℤ[θ]]` of Layer 3.4.

And the examples:

* `isMonogenic_of_isCyclotomicExtension` — cyclotomic fields, from Mathlib's
  `IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.adjoin_singleton_eq_top`. The case `n = 4` is `ℚ(i)`, with
  `𝓞 K = ℤ[i]`, so it needs no separate statement.
* `isMonogenic_of_mod_four_ne_one` / `isMonogenic_of_mod_four_eq_one` — quadratic fields,
  generated by `θ` or by `(1 + θ) / 2`, consuming the existing
  `NumberField.adjoin_gen_eq_top_of_mod_four_ne_one` and its `halfGen` counterpart.
* `isMonogenic_rat` — `ℚ`, whose ring of integers is `ℤ = ℤ[1]`.

### Why this also touches `Index/Basic.lean`

The index criterion needs a direction the existing API did not have. Every declaration in the
repository *consumes* an `IntegralPrimitiveElement`; nothing *builds* one. Going from
`𝓞 K = ℤ[θ]` to an integral primitive element means upgrading a `ℤ`-generation statement in
`𝓞 K` to a `ℚ`-generation statement in `K`, which is the new

```lean
theorem adjoin_rat_eq_top_of_adjoin_int_eq_top {θ : 𝓞 K}
    (h : Algebra.adjoin ℤ {θ} = (⊤ : Subalgebra ℤ (𝓞 K))) :
    Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤
```

proved by writing an arbitrary element of `K` as a quotient of two algebraic integers
(`IsFractionRing.div_surjective`), both of which lie in `ℤ[θ]`, and observing that the
intermediate field `ℚ(θ)` is closed under division. `ofAdjoinEqTop` packages it as the
constructor, with `coe`/`adjoin`/`index` simp lemmas.

This is a prerequisite of the target rather than a second topic, so it ships here; it is
placed next to the definition it constructs rather than kept private beside its first caller.

### Two deliberate deviations from the roadmap text

* **Namespace.** The roadmap says to put `IsMonogenic` in the `NumberField` namespace, warning
  that a bare `IsMonogenic` would collide with the ring-theoretic predicate. This repository
  puts its own number-field material in `TauCeti.NumberField` — that is where
  `IntegralPrimitiveElement` and the index API live — so the predicate is
  `TauCeti.NumberField.IsMonogenic`, which honours the warning and matches the neighbours.
* **Dedekind's cubic is deferred.** The roadmap lists it as the non-monogenic edge case. Its
  non-monogenicity is witnessed by a common index divisor, which is Layer 3.11 — currently in
  review as #6955 and not yet on `main`. The module docstring records the omission, and the
  rest of 7.3 rests only on the merged Layers 3.1 and 3.4.

`ℚ(i)` is subsumed by the cyclotomic case; no `IsMonogenic` existed in Mathlib or in this
repository before this PR.

Provenance: statements follow `TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithmetic/README.md` @ `ce02686a0c05`,
Layer 7.3; proofs are new, built on mathlib @ `30a58f795ae8c95b8299fe3c9ded1e6498a9e9fe`.

author: pmoust
body:
The first round of #1720 pinned deploy/docker-compose/ravel.yml but left
deploy/docker-compose/minio.yml on bare :latest tags for the same two
images, even though ravel.yml documents minio.yml as its exact MinIO and
bucket-creation mirror. The guard only read ravel.yml, so the two files
could diverge with nothing to catch it. Pin minio.yml's minio and mc
images to the exact tag and digest ravel.yml already carries, and extend
the guard's fourth category to scan both files: 8 image lines total across
the pair, 6 requiring a digest (the two ${RAVEL_IMAGE:-...} references in
ravel.yml stay exempt). Each file missing now fails its own check rather
than silently scanning whatever is left.

The first round also justified scoping the category to compose files
alone with the claim that deploy/k8s carries only locally built
placeholders with no registry manifest to pin. That is false: minio.yaml
lines 49 and 140 pull quay.io/minio/minio:latest and
quay.io/minio/mc:latest, and floci.yaml lines 74 and 157 pull
floci/floci:latest and curlimages/curl:8.11.1. Only ravel-server and
ravel-operator are placeholders. Replace the claim everywhere it appeared
(the guard's own comments, deploy/README.md, deploy/metricsbench/README.md)
with the true one: the guard covers the two quickstart compose files, and
the four k8s registry images are an open follow-up, not something this
change touches.

Make the guard's own test suite portable and wire it into CI. It used
GNU-only `sed -i` (no backup suffix, which is a GNU sed default but not
BSD sed's), so every mutation case reported "exit 0, wanted 1" on a BSD
userland. Replace it with a `mutate` helper that runs sed without -i,
writing to a fresh temp file and renaming it over the original; the sed
scripts themselves already used only POSIX BRE syntax. Add cases for a
bare tag on either image in minio.yml, a missing minio.yml, and a wrong
count that spans both files, alongside the existing ravel.yml cases
(updated for the new 8/6 counts). The suite ran in no CI job before this
change; add a cases step in ci.yml's doc-scripts job immediately before
the guard step, matching the shape of the job's other guard-and-cases
pairs. It was run here only against GNU sed and GNU coreutils (this
executor is Linux); the sed scripts avoid GNU extensions so the BSD path
is believed but not directly verified.

Confirmed the fix matters, not just the rationale: running the pre-fix
guard (commit 3647d94b) against a copy of the tree with minio.yml's minio
image mutated to :latest exits 0 with "RESULT: PASS", because that guard
never reads minio.yml. The new guard catches the same mutation and exits 1
naming the line.

Out of scope, left for a follow-up: the ticket's Proof asked for two
predicates, digest-present and not-on-Docker-Hub. The second is not done
for grafana/grafana, which stays on Docker Hub: no anonymous mirror exists
on quay.io, ghcr.io, or ECR Public (checked and recorded in ravel.yml's
comment), so the orchestrator supplied the docker.io digest pin as fixed
text instead. The ticket's "repoint Grafana off Docker Hub" item is
therefore still open. Also unaddressed here, reported rather than fixed
per task scope: two telemetrygen :latest references (ci.yml around line
1993, quickstart-published.yml around lines 173 and 196), and the four
deploy/k8s registry images named above.

Refs: #1720

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [urllib3](https://pypi.org/project/urllib3) from **1.26.9** to **2.8.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.8.0
   ```
   ==================

Security
--------

Fixed the following security issues:

- The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden.
  (High severity, `GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77>`__)
- ``HTTPResponse.stream()`` and ``read_chunked()`` could buffer a chunk-size
  line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity,
  `GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw>`__)
- Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity,
  `GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g>`__)

.. caution::

    urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or
    overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that
    behavior may require changes.

    Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in
    ``proxy_ssl_context``, and proxy identity checks with
    ``proxy_assert_hostname`` or ``proxy_assert_fingerprint``.
    Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer
    apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.


Deprecations & Removals
-----------------------

- Deprecated using an empty collection as the ``Retry`` option
  ``allowed_methods`` to retry any verb.
  (`5044 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5044>`__)


Features
--------

- Added ``Url.auth_decoded`` and ``Url.auth_decoded_joined`` convenience
  properties to the result of ``parse_url()``.
  (`4945 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/4945>`__)
- Added ``basic_auth_encoding`` and ``proxy_basic_auth_encoding`` parameters to
  ``urllib3.util.make_headers()``.
  (`5092 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5092>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines
  (`obs-fold`) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF
  sequences from appearing in header values such as ``Set-Cookie``.
  (`1362 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/1362>`__)
- Fixed usage of ``proxy_ssl_context`` with ``ProxyManager`` when
  ``use_forwarding_for_https=True``. Passing ``ssl_context`` instead of
  ``proxy_ssl_context`` for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a
  ``FutureWarning`` and will raise an error in v3.0.
  (`2577 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/2577>`__)
- Changed behavior of the default ``ConnectionPool.pool`` initialization.
  ``LifoQueue`` is now resolved from the ``queue`` module after the
  ``ConnectionPool`` is instantiated instead of using the default cached
  ``QueueCls`` class property. This is done because sometimes the
  ``queue.LifoQueue`` is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent.
  (`3289 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3289>`__)
- Raised ``UnrewindableBodyError`` instead of ``ValueError`` when retrying a
  request whose body had ``tell()`` but not ``seek()``.
  (`3779 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3779>`__)
- Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with
  the proxy server.
  (`3785 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3785>`__)
- Fixed ``HTTPResponse.drain_conn()`` to discard unread response data in 64 KiB
  chunks (same as the default ``amt`` when doing ``HTTPResponse.stream(...)``).
  (`5019 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5019>`__)
- Fixed ``is_ipaddress()`` to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by
  ``socket.connect``, such as hex (``0x7f000001``), octal (``0177.0.0.1``), and
  decimal integers (``2130706433``), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses
  the correct mode for these addresses.
  (`5029 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5029>`__)
- Fixed ``HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen`` raising a misleading ``FullPoolError``
  instead of ``ValueError`` when called with an invalid ``timeout`` argument on
  a pool created with ``block=True``.
  (`5059 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5059>`__)
- Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit ``:0`` values instead of
  substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection,
  proxy configuration, ``connection_from_url()``, and HTTP/2 request authority.
  (`5071 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5071>`__,
  `5101 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5101>`__)
- Fixed a bug where ``PoolManager`` passed the ``assert_hostname`` and
  ``assert_fingerprint`` parameters to HTTP connection pools.
  (`5077 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5077>`__)
- Fixed ``HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen()`` and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL
  fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests.
  (`5079 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5079>`__)
- Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security
  issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers.
  This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when
  the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions
  should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes.
  (`5091 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5091>`__)
- Fixed ``HTTPSConnection.connect()`` overriding ``ProxyConfig.ssl_context``'s
  certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS
  settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

  ``HTTPSConnection`` no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client
  credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its
  ``ssl_context`` as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target.
  (`5093 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5093>`__)
- Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting
  invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed
  percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts
  and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host
  normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for
  percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and
  uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets.
  (`5095 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5095>`__)
- Fixed an ``AttributeError`` on Python built with OpenSSL 4+, where
  ``ssl.PROTOCOL_TLSv1`` no longer exists.
  (`5097 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5097>`__)
- Fixed ``urllib3.contrib.pyopenssl`` to use cryptography APIs when reading a
  certificate subject and loading encrypted private keys, avoiding
  ``DeprecationWarning`` raised by pyOpenSSL 26.3.0+.
  (`5103 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5103>`__)
- Fixed handling of HTTP 303 redirects for requests with chunked or file-like
  bodies.
  (`5161 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5161>`__)
- Fixed ``assert_fingerprint()`` to raise ``SSLError`` instead of
  ``binascii.Error`` when a fingerprint has a supported length but contains
  non-hexadecimal characters.
  (`5211 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5211>`__)


Misc
----

- Added a ``test`` dependency group containing the minimum dependencies needed
  to run the test suite, intended for downstream packagers. The ``dev-base``
  and ``mypy`` groups now include this new group via ``include-group``,
  removing duplication.
  (`3594 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3594>`__)
- Fixed test failures with pytest >= 9.1.
  (`5094 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5094>`__)
- Enabled JSPI tests with Firefox in the Emscripten test suite.
  (`5166 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/5166>`__)

author: adityashett
body:
## Automated Root Cause Analysis

### 1. Root Cause

The task `call_partner_api` failed because the HTTP request to the partner's `/reconcile` endpoint exceeded the configured client-side timeout of 60 seconds. This timeout value is intentionally misconfigured, as it was copied from a different, faster API endpoint and is insufficient for the `/reconcile` endpoint, which can legitimately take longer than 60 seconds, especially under varying load conditions, despite its typical "normal load" duration of around 20 seconds.

### 2. Evidence

*   **Code Line:** `resp = requests.get("https://partner.example.com/reconcile", timeout=60)`
    *   This line shows that the `requests.get` call has a hardcoded timeout of 60 seconds.
*   **Code Comment:** `# --- BUG (intentional): partner's /reconcile endpoint legitimately takes ~20s under normal load; this timeout was copied from a different, faster endpoint ---`
    *   This comment explicitly identifies the `timeout=60` parameter as an intentional bug. It states that the `/reconcile` endpoint, while normally taking around 20 seconds, was assigned a timeout value copied from a *faster* endpoint. This directly implies that 60 seconds is an inadequate timeout for this specific endpoint, leading to failures when the request duration exceeds this limit.
*   **Log Lines:** No specific log lines for this particular failure are provided. However, if logs were available, we would expect to see an error similar to `requests.exceptions.Timeout` indicating that the request exceeded the 60-second timeout.

### 3. Confidence

**High**

The DAG code contains an explicit, intentional bug comment directly pointing to the `timeout` value as the problem. This is the most direct and undeniable evidence of the root cause, given the absence of actual log data for this specific failure.

## Proposed Fix
```diff
--- a/dag6.py
+++ b/dag6.py
@@ -8,4 +8,4 @@
     import requests
     # --- BUG (intentional): partner's /reconcile endpoint legitimately takes ~20s
     # under normal load; this timeout was copied from a different, faster endpoint ---
-    resp = requests.get("https://partner.example.com/reconcile", timeout=60)
+    resp = requests.get("https://partner.example.com/reconcile", timeout=120)
     context["ti"].xcom_push(key="response", value=resp.json())
```

**Confidence score:** 0.56 (medium)

**Diff applied:** True

**Estimated LLM cost:** $0.00000 USD (~$0.00000 CAD) -- 0 input / 0 output tokens on gemini-2.5-flash. Rates and FX are estimates from config/pricing.json, not a billed invoice figure.

Klaus mit Bild: Sushi stand in den Ordnern mit **0 Rezepten**, während die

**Beide Zahlen waren richtig gerechnet — sie rechneten aus verschiedenen Quellen:**

|---|---|---|

author: kevmorpain
body:
## Contexte

Cloudflare Workers Builds a basculé son défaut sur **Node 24 le 2026-07-30**. Sans `NODE_VERSION`, `.nvmrc` ni `.node-version` dans le dépôt, la prod a suivi : elle construit sur **24.18.0** (confirmé par le dernier log de build) pendant que `.github/workflows/tests.yml:32` validait encore sur **22**.

Le code déployé tournait donc depuis six semaines sur une version que rien ne testait.

## Changement

- **`.nvmrc`** → `24`.
- **`tests.yml`** → `node-version-file: .nvmrc` à la place de `node-version: 22`. Une seule valeur au lieu de deux à synchroniser à la main : c'est cette duplication qui avait laissé la divergence s'installer.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** → section « Version de Node », et retrait de la mention « Node 22 » devenue trompeuse.

### Pourquoi 24 et pas 22

C'est ce que la prod fait déjà, et Node 24 est vérifié vert (tableau ci-dessous). Épingler `22` aurait fait **reculer** un système en fonctionnement pour l'aligner sur une valeur arbitraire.

### Alternative écartée

Poser `NODE_VERSION=24` dans les variables de build Cloudflare : la valeur vivrait dans le dashboard, invisible du dépôt et illisible en revue, et le CI GitHub ne pourrait pas la lire — on garderait deux valeurs désynchronisables.

## Vérifications sur Node 24.18.0

Binaire officiel téléchargé et chaîne complète rejouée dessus :

| Contrôle | Résultat |
|---|---|
| `npm ci` | exit 0 |
| `npx vitest run` | 470 tests / 65 fichiers verts (état de `main` à ce moment-là) |
| `npm run build` | exit 0 — **3,45 Mo / 862 ko gzip, identique à Node 22** |
| `wrangler deploy --dry-run` | exit 0, bindings `DB`/`KV`/`BLOB`/`ASSETS` résolus |

Et sur la branche, en Node 22 (le conteneur) : **517 tests verts**, `eslint` exit 0.

Le CI de cette PR est le premier à tourner sur Node 24 — c'est lui qui valide réellement le `node-version-file`.

## Ce que ça ne corrige pas

Le **conteneur des sessions cloud reste sur Node 22** : il sert un Node système (`/opt/node22/bin/node`, `~/.nvm` absent), donc `.nvmrc` y est inerte et l'écart n'est pas corrigeable. Documenté explicitement plutôt que tu.

## Effet de bord documenté

Node 24 embarque **npm 11**, qui **bloque par défaut les scripts d'installation des dépendances** — 12 paquets ici, dont `workerd`, `sharp`, `@parcel/watcher`. Sans conséquence aujourd'hui (le postinstall du projet racine `nuxt prepare` tourne quand même, `esbuild` reçoit son binaire par ses optional deps), mais une future dépendance qui a réellement besoin de son script d'install échouera de façon peu lisible. Noté dans `CLAUDE.md` avec le remède (`npm approve-scripts`).

## Second commit

`docs(torts)` consigne, au format de `docs/torts.md`, l'erreur que l'utilisateur a dû relever en amont de cette PR : j'avais prescrit un `.nvmrc` en nommant la mauvaise surface (la session cloud, qui ne le lit pas) et en présentant comme un risque futur ce qui était déjà réalisé en production. Commit séparé, comme l'exige la procédure du registre.

author: lambo-n
body:
Phase C2 of [`GPU-VM.md`](../blob/main/GPU-VM.md). **Cannot be applied until the host prerequisites exist** — see below.

## What this is

`tofu/proxmox-llm-vm.tf` creates VM 105 (`llm`), the guest that gets the whole Intel Arc Pro B70. It is the **one guest authored in tofu rather than imported**: the other four were generated from live machines because an import that proposes changes to a running database VM is a hazard. 105 does not exist and holds nothing, so a wrong attribute costs a rebuild — which is what makes authoring it safe, and worth doing for a machine with this many non-default settings.

## Choices worth reviewing

| Setting | Why it is not the default |
|---|---|
| `machine = "q35"`, `bios = "ovmf"` | The other four are SeaBIOS + i440fx. PCIe passthrough needs q35, and the 64-bit MMIO window a 32 GiB BAR needs is an OVMF property. Changing either later means rebuilding the guest. |
| `cpu { type = "host" }` | Passes the physical address width through (46-bit here), which is what OVMF sizes that window from. Also gives llama.cpp's CPU fallback AVX-512 and AMX. |
| `memory { floating = 0 }` | A passthrough guest pins **all** its RAM — ballooning cannot work. This is a statement of fact, not tuning. |
| `hostpci { mapping = "arc-b70" }` | PVE only lets `root@pam` attach a raw `0000:53:00.0`. A raw address here would make this file unappliable by any scoped token. |
| Cloud image + cloud-init | No interactive install, so the guest is reproducible from this file. Ubuntu rewrites `current/` in place, hence the required checksum variable. |
| `agent { enabled = false }` | Ubuntu's cloud image has no `qemu-guest-agent`. With it on, the provider waits for an agent that cannot answer until the timeout expires. Flip to `true` after C3 installs it — a legible second diff instead of a 15-minute hang on the first. |
| `prevent_destroy` from commit one | The token that creates this VM holds `VM.Allocate` on `/vms/105`, which includes delete. |
| models disk `backup = false` | Weights are re-downloadable; vzdump of them would only burn space. |

## Verification done here

```
tofu validate   -> Success (only the known network_device.enabled deprecations)
tofu fmt -check -> clean
tofu plan -refresh=false -> Plan: 2 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy
```

Nothing proposed against the four existing guests. Every attribute used (`hostpci.mapping`, `initialization`, `import_from`, `efi_disk`) was read from the 0.113.1 provider schema rather than from memory.

## Blocked on, and deliberately not in this PR

None of these can be created by this file — they need `Sys.Modify`, `Mapping.Modify` or root, all of which the scoped token deliberately lacks (GPU-VM.md A3–A5):

- [ ] ZFS pool `llm-pool` on `sde`, registered as a PVE zfspool storage
- [ ] PCI mapping `arc-b70` → `0000:53:00.0`
- [ ] `0000:53:00.0` bound to `vfio-pci` — **the VM will not start otherwise**
- [ ] token `tofu@pve!llm` and its ACLs
- [ ] `TF_VAR_ubuntu_noble_image_sha256` and `TF_VAR_llm_ssh_public_keys`
- [ ] confirm nothing answers on `192.168.50.107`, and that the gateway is `.1`

## Apply, when those are done

```bash
export PROXMOX_VE_API_TOKEN='tofu@pve!llm=<uuid>'
export CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN='<token>'
tofu plan  -refresh=false
tofu apply -refresh=false
```

`-refresh=false` is required, not lazy: `PVEAuditor` cannot refresh a QEMU guest, so an unqualified apply 403s on VMs 101–104 before reaching 105. Skipping refresh is safe for a create — there is no prior state to go stale. **Do not "fix" it by granting this token `VM.Config.Disk` on the other guests.**

author: copilot
body:
The `test` GitHub Actions job was executing the Playwright workflow from the wrong repository path, causing `npm ci` to fail before tests could start. This updates the workflow location and preserves execution from the `app/` subdirectory where the Node project actually lives.

- **Root cause**
  - The Playwright workflow was defined under `app/.github/workflows/`, which GitHub Actions does not load as a repository workflow.
  - As a result, the active workflow did not run with the intended `app` working directory, and `npm ci` executed without access to the app lockfile.

- **Workflow fix**
  - Move the Playwright workflow to `.github/workflows/playwright.yml`.
  - Keep `defaults.run.working-directory: app` so install and test commands continue to run against the app project.

- **Security hardening**
  - Add an explicit minimal token permission set:
    ```yaml
    permissions:
      contents: read
    ```

- **Resulting workflow shape**
  - Repository-level workflow discovery now works.
  - Node/Playwright commands still execute from the correct project root:

    ```yaml
    jobs:
      test:
        defaults:
          run:
            working-directory: app
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Install dependencies
            run: npm ci
          - name: Run Playwright tests
            run: npx playwright test
    ```

author: mannes
body:
Node-side network primitives for plan 17 (thermal-label/brother-ql#7), plus the `enumerateUsbDevices` lift from plan 15 that was never released. Drivers opt in; nothing changes for existing consumers. Depends on `@thermal-label/contracts@0.6.2` (published).

## What

`@thermal-label/transport/node`
- `snmpGet(host, oids, opts)` / `snmpBroadcast(oid, opts)` — SNMPv1 GET over `node:dgram`, hand-rolled BER, no dependencies. `retries` = resend after `timeoutMs`. Responses are accepted only from the target address and agent port, GetResponse PDU, matching random request id. Broadcast goes to the directed broadcast of every non-internal IPv4 interface, dedupes by responder, skips `/32`.
- `PRINTER_MIB` — the standard Printer-MIB / Host-Resources-MIB OIDs used (model, serial, state, error bits, media name and dimensions, dimension unit, page counter).
- `enumerateNetworkDevices(registries)` / `identifyNetworkDevice(host, registries)` — match `hrDeviceDescr.1`, falling back to `sysDescr.0` when absent or unmatched, against `DeviceEntry.modelNames`. `identify` returns `undefined` for "answered, not in this registry" and rejects for "could not be asked", so drivers can tell the two apart. Neither opens TCP.
- `enumerateUsbDevices` (e85cf04, plan 15): USB listing lifted behind transport so drivers stop carrying their own `usb` walk.

`@thermal-label/transport` (root)
- `matchModelName(reported, registries)` — case-folded, whitespace-collapsed, vendor-prefix-tolerant, longest whole-token match.

## Why

Brother's port 9100 is write-only (reference §5.9, bench-measured), so model, media and status for a network QL are only available over SNMP; every Brother NC print server answers the standard MIB with community `public`. Keeping the primitives here means labelwriter and future network drivers get discovery and status without their own copy.

## Checks

- `ci.yml` order from a clean `dist` against npm contracts 0.6.2: typecheck, lint, prettier, 196 tests (99.55 % lines), build. `dist/node` exports verified.
- BER decoder fuzzed with 200k mutated datagrams plus crafted length/depth/int edge cases in review: no hangs, no uncaught throws beyond `RangeError`.
- Bench: QL-820NWBc identified by broadcast in < 1 s and by unicast; `prtInputDimUnit` on this printer claims micrometres while sending 1/100 mm, so consumers should trust the media name string first (documented for brother-ql).
- Version 0.6.1 (patch; drivers pin `^0.6.x`). `DECISIONS.md` D14, README and API docs updated.

author: nvuillam
body:
Three repositories move together now: sfdx-hardis, vscode-sfdx-hardis and [sfdx-hardis-training](https://github.com/hardisgroupcom/sfdx-hardis-training/pull/1). This adds the machinery that keeps them in step, and fixes the two bugs that writing the training found.

## The skills

The existing rule that every change states its VS Code extension impact gets a sibling: **every change states its training impact, even when it is "none"**.

- **`training-impact`** decides whether a change breaks a lab and names which ones. It reads `training-manifest.json` from the sibling clone, cloning it there if it is missing, and classifies the impact.
- **`training-update`** performs the edits once `training-impact` says there is an impact: the lab text, the fiction, the audit rules, the link map, and the Helios screenshot capture in the sibling extension clone.

Both live here and only here. The training and extension repositories carry no skills: one place to write them, one place to fix them. The extension's CLAUDE.md gets a pointer line, not a copy.

The case they exist for is not the obvious one. A renamed command breaks a lab loudly. What breaks it silently is **a behaviour change under an unchanged name**: the training seeds failures on purpose (a field excluded by `.forceignore`, a field that cannot be made required, a hardcoded id that trips PMD), and one that stops failing turns a lab into a page describing something that does not happen. No test anywhere notices.

`scripts/check-training-impact.mjs` does the mechanical part from the diff. It covers names only, and says so.

CLAUDE.md gains a Training section; `analyze` and `design` gain a **Training impact** output item next to the VS Code extension one.

## Two fixes

**Backpromote refused a Developer Edition org as production.** The rule was "a developer sandbox or a scratch org", which rules out every project whose developers work in Developer Edition orgs rather than in sandboxes. It is now "a development environment", and a Developer Edition org that **is** the org of a major branch stays refused by the check that already existed. Unit tests cover both directions.

Found because the training runs entirely on Developer Edition orgs, which made `hardis:work:backpromote` refuse the one org its Level 2 lab 0 is built on.

**`sf commands` crashed for every user** with `ReferenceError: DS_PROMETHEUS is not defined`.

A command description ends up verbatim in `oclif.manifest.json`, and oclif runs its own template interpolation over the descriptions it reads back from that manifest. A description whose **rendered** text contains `${something}` therefore makes oclif evaluate `something` as a variable. Escaping it in the TypeScript source is not enough: the manifest stores the evaluated string.

Two commands had one, `hardis:org:configure:grafana-dashboards` documenting the alert pack placeholders and `hardis:project:clean:manageditems` documenting its glob. Both are reworded.

`test/command-descriptions.test.ts` now walks every compiled command and fails on any `${...}` in a `description` or a `summary`. It found the second one immediately, which is the argument for having it.

**CI authentication with `SFDX_AUTH_URL_<ALIAS>` left the job with no default org.** The JWT and web login branches both pass `--set-default` unless the caller opted out. The auth-URL branch relied on a variable that is only computed when the hook also checks the existing connection, so in a CI job it was always false: the job authenticated, reported success, and the next command died with `NoDefaultEnvError: No default environment found`.

Found by running a real Pull Request check on a real fork against a real org, which is the only way it could have been found. It is not a training-only problem: this is the documented shortcut path for scratch orgs and Dev Hubs too. Verified fixed by re-running the same check, which now validates 31 components with 4 passing tests.

## Also

`specs/trailmix-salesforce-devops.md`, the specification the training was built from, kept here because the skills above are the part of it that lives in this repository.

## Verified

- `yarn compile` clean, `backpromoteRules` 24 passing, the new description test passing.
- `node scripts/check-training-impact.mjs` correctly flags Level 2 lab 0 as affected by the backpromote change.

Cross-links: hardisgroupcom/vscode-sfdx-hardis#514, hardisgroupcom/sfdx-hardis-training#1

author: decapent
body:
## Le diagnostic

Le parseur excluait deja la liberation, alors la capture d'ecran ne collait pas. Le vrai journal du match a livre deux causes, pas une.

**1. L'objectif n'etait plus reconnu du tout.** Des qu'un joueur pose un `!alias`, le serveur ecrit :

```
Notice (all): Moi_Eva (W1ALTTP) (Team #1) has completed their goal.
```

La regex attendait l'emplacement seul. Consequence en cascade : le joueur passait pour un abandon, la taille de son monde restait inconnue — d'ou la colonne Completion vide — et ses 218 lignes comptaient toutes comme des checks trouves. Le saut vertical en fin de courbe, c'etait ca.

**2. La collecte credite des checks au mauvais joueur.** Celle-la, aucune regle fondee sur l'objectif ne pouvait la voir. A la completion, le serveur ramasse les objets du vainqueur *partout ou ils sont*, et les lignes portent le nom du monde qui detenait la localisation — souvent un autre joueur, qui n'a rien fouille et n'a pas encore termine :

```
00:58:56,114  Moi_Eva (W1ALTTP) (Team #1) has completed their goal.
00:58:56,114  W1ALTTP (Team #1) has collected their items from other worlds.
00:58:56,121  (Team #1) W1SM sent Big Key to W1ALTTP (Ice Beam)      <- pas un check de W1SM
```

Sur le journal `test log`, cela gonflait un joueur de 36 checks fantomes.

## La correction

Les deux rafales sont annoncees par une ligne dediee, et on les suit maintenant a leur sens : la collecte converge vers celui qui termine, la liberation part de lui. Toute ligne qui n'est pas un envoi clot la rafale. La regle « avant l'objectif » disparait — elle ne voyait pas la collecte, et elle ecartait a tort le check gagnant emis dans la meme milliseconde que l'objectif.

Le total du monde se lit desormais sur **toutes** les lignes emises par le joueur : chaque localisation de son monde en produit exactement une, qu'il l'ait trouvee, qu'elle ait ete collectee par son proprietaire ou qu'il l'ait liberee.

### Avant / apres, sur les trois journaux

| Journal | Joueur | Jeu | Avant | Apres |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Game 1 | W1ALTTP | A Link to the Past | 218 trouves, total inconnu, *abandon* | **139 / 218**, termine |
| Game 1 | W1SM | Super Metroid | 100 trouves, total inconnu, *abandon* | **57 / 100**, termine |
| deln-ogopo | W2SM64 | Super Mario 64 | 116 / 164 | **110 / 164** |
| deln-ogopo | W5DKC2 | DKC2 | 110 / 175 | 110 / 175 |
| test log | W2FF4 | FF4 Free Enterprise | 217 / 446 | 217 / 446 |
| test log | W7Z1 | The Legend of Zelda | 146 trouves | **110 / 155** |

Super Metroid tombe sur **100 pile**, le nombre exact de localisations du jeu — la meilleure confirmation externe qu'on pouvait esperer. Les corrections de 116 → 110 et 146 → 110 sont les collectes d'un coequipier, qui n'etaient pas detectables avant.

## Le graphique

Un seuil en pointille par jeu, a la taille de son monde, avec une etiquette directe a droite. Le pointille est assume : sur une grille ce serait du bruit, mais ici c'est justement un seuil, et le trait discontinu est ce qui le distingue d'une graduation. Le trait reste en encre discrete plutot qu'en couleur de serie, pour ne pas concurrencer les donnees ni empieter sur la charte des equipes.

Les courbes ne finissent plus par un saut vertical : elles s'arretent la ou le joueur s'est arrete, et l'ecart restant jusqu'au trait se lit d'un coup d'oeil.

## Au passage

- Les familles `viewing` / `stopped viewing` (spectateurs) et les connexions refusees sont classees, ce qui vide a nouveau le fourre-tout `inconnu`.
- Les lignes de rafale sont comptees comme collecte ou liberation dans le tableau des signaux, au lieu d'etre confondues avec des checks.

## Verification

`dotnet test` : **108 verts**. Deux tests figeaient l'ancienne regle et ont ete remplaces ; cinq nouveaux couvrent l'objectif avec pseudonyme, la collecte qui ne credite pas l'autre joueur, le total sur les lignes emises, l'absence de rafale dans la progression, et les spectateurs. Le parseur a par ailleurs ete confronte aux trois journaux reels, qui donnent les chiffres du tableau ci-dessus.

`npm run typecheck`, `lint`, `build` : verts. Le rendu du seuil n'a pas ete verifie visuellement.

## A refaire de ton cote

Les matchs deja importes gardent leurs chiffres gonfles : il faut **reimporter les journaux**. L'import remplace au lieu de cumuler.

author: radialmonster
body:
Proposal for #22292.

Implementation and testing are done on Windows (see **Tested** below). This
stays a draft while I look for macOS and Linux testers (see **Not tested**
below) and for any suggestions or corrections before asking for a full
review.

### What this adds

A `cachedir` preference in preferences > storage > cache, so the cache folder
(disk thumbnails and full previews, compiled OpenCL kernels, AI caches) can be
chosen without the `--cachedir` command line option. It is a string preference
with an empty default, stored in `darktablerc-common`, `restart="true"`.

- empty means today's default location, which is shown as placeholder text
- the folder must already exist when darktable applies the preference; typing
  the path to a folder that does not exist will not create it. The folder
  button's picker does let you create a new folder there, since that is the
  OS dialog's own "new folder" feature, not something darktable does. This
  means a disconnected drive, a drive letter taken by another drive or an
  unmounted mount point cannot silently receive the cache
- `--cachedir` still takes priority over the preference, and the preference
  over the default
- when the entry does not name the folder in use, an icon and a short line
  under the entry say which folder is in use and why: started with
  `--cachedir`, set with `--conf` for this session, not usable, or used after
  a restart. The line refreshes when the entry loses focus, on Enter, after
  the folder button and after the double-click reset, so an unusable folder is
  flagged before preferences are closed
- if the folder is unavailable at startup, a dialog asks before anything uses
  the cache: retry, choose another folder (saved as the new preference), use
  the default folder for this session, or quit. Headless runs (`darktable-cli`,
  `darktable-generate-cache`) log it and fall back to the default
- cache files already in the old folder are left behind there, unused;
  nothing moves or deletes them. The new folder starts empty, and darktable
  creates thumbnails, previews and OpenCL kernels there again as it needs
  them, the same way it would for a new library
- local copies keep using the folder resolved at startup (`--cachedir` or the
  default), never the preference. A changed cache folder therefore cannot
  strand images flagged as local copies, the objection raised in #5012
- a value from an older darktable, which saved the unknown key to
  `darktablerc`, is migrated to `darktablerc-common` on the next start

The message line is a visible label rather than a tooltip on the entry icon:
`gtk_entry_set_icon_tooltip_text` is never shown, because the global
`query-tooltip` class handler (`dt_shortcut_tooltip_callback`,
`src/gui/accelerators.c`) always shows the widget's own tooltip.

### Public API

This adds 12 public functions and 2 enum types. Upstream AGENTS.md asks for a
discussion before changing a public API, so please say if any of these should
be file-local, named differently, or shaped differently:

`src/common/file_location.h`
- `gchar *dt_loc_expand_user_path(const char *value)` -- trim, one pair of
  quotes, `~`; NULL when nothing is left
- `gboolean dt_loc_path_is_absolute(const char *path)` -- GLib absolute, and
  on Windows a drive letter or UNC path, not `\folder`
- `dt_loc_cache_dir_check_t dt_loc_check_user_cache_dir(const char *cachedir)`
  -- usable, not absolute, missing, or no access; never creates the folder
- `gboolean dt_loc_set_user_cache_dir(const char *cachedir)`
- `dt_loc_cache_dir_source_t dt_loc_get_user_cache_dir_source(void)`
- `gboolean dt_loc_user_cache_dir_is_from(const char *value)`
- `gchar *dt_loc_get_default_user_cache_dir(void)`
- `void dt_loc_get_user_local_copy_dir(char *dir, size_t bufsize)`
- enums `dt_loc_cache_dir_check_t` and `dt_loc_cache_dir_source_t`

`src/control/conf.h`
- `gboolean dt_conf_is_overridden(const char *key)` -- whether `--conf` set it
- `gchar *dt_conf_get_stored_string(const char *key)` and
  `void dt_conf_set_stored_string(const char *key, const char *value)` -- the
  stored value, ignoring a `--conf` override

`src/gui/gtk.h`
- `gboolean dt_show_in_file_manager(const char *path)` -- folders only for
  now; Windows `ShellExecuteW`, macOS `dt_osx_open_url`, else GIO

`tools/generate_prefs.xsl` also gains a `dirchooser="yes"` attribute for
string preferences (entry plus folder button plus "open" button), declared in
`data/darktableconfig.dtd`. `cachedir` is its only user.

### Commits

1. the preference itself (this change)
2. `RELEASE_NOTES.md: cache folder preference`, in its own commit as AGENTS.md
   asks

### Tested

Windows (MSYS2 UCRT64, Release): the preferences entry, folder and "open"
buttons, the icons and the message line in every case, the restart prompt, all
four startup dialog choices, a folder chosen in the startup dialog after an
older darktable left `cachedir` in `darktablerc`, the same under `--conf`,
multiple workspaces, a drive that is missing at startup and one removed while
darktable runs (`subst`), creating a local copy while the preference points
elsewhere, thumbnails and kernels landing in the chosen folder, and
`--print-paths` with priority and odd path cases (spaces, quotes, `~`,
non-ASCII, trailing dot, drive-relative, UNC).

Linux (Ubuntu 26.04 container with the CI settings): builds with gcc-16 and
clang-22, no warnings in the touched files, plus the `--print-paths` cases
above and a read-only folder, a folder that cannot be listed, an unreadable
`darktablerc-common`, and a `cachedir` line longer than the config parser's
line buffer.

macOS: the CI job compiles it.

### Not tested

- the GUI on macOS and Linux: I only have Windows. Most likely to differ,
  because that code is only compiled there: the "open" button
  (`dt_osx_open_url` on macOS, GIO elsewhere), and on Linux whether the file
  manager window comes to the front or opens behind the modal preferences
  dialog. Testing on those platforms would be welcome
- a folder that cannot be written to or listed is rejected on macOS and
  Linux; on Windows the check cannot detect it, so an unwritable folder is
  accepted as usable, same as before this patch
- no unit tests: `src/common/file_location.c` has none today

This change was written with AI assistance.

author: meziantou
body:
Review of `Meziantou.Framework.Yaml` and its source generator, focused on C# union support and on removing differences between reflection-based and source-generated serialization. Around 90 bugs are fixed. Every fix has a regression test, and tests run in both modes (`useSourceGeneration` theories) wherever both paths are involved.

The review ran as parallel passes over unions, object contracts, polymorphism/references, collections/scalars, and the reader/writer layer, each driven by a differential harness that compared reflection with a generated context across many types, option sets and cultures, plus round-trip fuzzing of the writer. The harnesses ended with no remaining differences other than the known limitations listed below.

## C# unions

- The most specific case is chosen when writing a derived value (`union U(Animal, int, string, Dog)` used to write a `Dog` through the `Animal` case and drop members), and an interface case is preferred over an `object` case.
- A type is still a union when it declares extra constructors, and the generator now recognizes hand-written `[Union]` types.
- Case matching has two tiers: exact kinds win, and a fallback tier lets a `string` case read a number or boolean, a `char`/enum case read a number, and a case whose type has a custom converter read anything. This makes **nested unions round-trip** (`union Outer(ScalarUnion, List<int>)`), with cycle protection for recursive unions.
- `YamlValue`, `YamlSequence` and `YamlMapping` cases match their own shape instead of everything.
- The structural classifier no longer uses the members of polymorphic cases, honors runtime `UnmappedMemberHandling`, and uses the members of an interface case in both paths.
- Error messages, error positions and write ordering (including generic variance) now match between the two paths.

## Object contracts

- Generated code that did not compile: members named like C# keywords, explicit interface implementations with `[YamlInclude]`, structs with `init` properties, partially implemented lifecycle interfaces, and `Nullable<T>` of a non-scalar struct. Static members and constants are no longer treated as members.
- Reflection lost **every member value** when deserializing a struct; the instance is now kept boxed while members are assigned.
- Member discovery walks the hierarchy from the base down: hidden members are no longer written twice, private base members with `[YamlInclude]` are found, attributes on a base property apply to overrides, and both paths agree on order.
- The generator now honors `[YamlPropertyOrder]`, sorted mapping order and `DuplicateKeyHandling`; merge sequences give precedence to the earlier mapping (`<<: [{A: 1}, {A: 3}]` yields `A = 1`).
- Null into a non-nullable value-type member is rejected consistently instead of silently assigning `default` in reflection, and `[YamlConstructor]` now works on structs.
- Two members mapping to the same YAML name now throw instead of writing the key twice.

## Polymorphism and references

- The consumed discriminator is removed before the selected type reads the node, so it is no longer reported as an unmapped member, captured in extension data, written twice, or resolved a second time by a derived type that is polymorphic itself.
- A type selected by a discriminator ignores its own default derived type.
- Duplicate derived types, discriminators and tags are rejected in both paths, with a new **MFY026** generator diagnostic.
- Boxed structs are not anchored, collection converters track references by runtime type, and `PreserveMinimal` invokes `IYamlOnSerializing`/`IYamlOnSerialized` once per object (converters still run in both passes; the new `YamlWriter.IsCollectingReferences` lets a converter tell the passes apart).
- `YamlPolymorphismOptions.DerivedTypeMappings` is copied and made read-only when assigned, so options already in use cannot change.

## Types and scalars

- `Queue`, `Stack`, `ConcurrentQueue/Stack/Bag`, `FrozenSet`, `FrozenDictionary`, `ArraySegment`, `KeyValuePair`, `BigInteger`, `Version` and `Rune` round-trip instead of being written as their public properties and read back empty. Stacks keep their order.
- `SortedDictionary`, `ConcurrentDictionary`, `SortedList` and `Dictionary<,>` subclasses are written as mappings; the string-keyed dictionary interfaces read like `Dictionary` (merge keys, null keys, case-insensitive names).
- Types that cannot be supported now fail loudly (`NotSupportedException`, or the new **MFY007** diagnostic) instead of losing data silently.
- Scalars that would read back as null, a boolean or a number are quoted, including enum names, `char '~'`, relative `Uri`s and mapping keys of every key type.
- `[YamlEnumMemberName]` applies in collections, nullables and dictionary keys; enum formatting is culture-invariant.
- Generated element/key reads honor `UseSchema`; `[YamlSerializable(typeof(object))]` and `object` dictionary keys work instead of producing broken code.

## Writer, model and API

- Output that could not be parsed back: empty root containers with an anchor or tag, anchors/tags on mapping keys, verbatim and non-specific tags, parser-inserted default tag directives, multi-document streams, and single-quoted scalars ending in a line break.
- `YamlMapping` keeps its key lookup and enumeration order consistent after edits; `Keys` is a read-only view.
- Writing a loaded `YamlNode` no longer changes its meaning (scalar styles and tags are preserved).
- An empty payload no longer throws `NullReferenceException` (it escaped `TryDeserialize`), and invalid UTF-8 is reported as a `YamlException`.
- `YamlSyntaxTree.Parse` with trivia was quadratic: 16k lines went from ~2.5 s to ~155 ms.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **Public API additions** (generated code can only call public API): `YamlReader.BufferCurrentNodeToStringAndRemoveDiscriminator`, `YamlReader.MarkCurrentNodeDerivedTypeResolved`, `YamlReader.IsCurrentNodeDerivedTypeResolved`, `YamlWriter.IsCollectingReferences`, `YamlWriter.ShouldInvokeOnSerializing`, `YamlWriter.WriteDictionaryKey`. `ref/` is regenerated.
- **Behavior changes worth a look**: null into a non-nullable value-type member now throws in reflection; duplicate derived-type registrations and duplicate YAML names now throw; unsupported types now throw instead of writing their properties; a tag or anchor written just before `WritePropertyName` now belongs to the key (observable to third-party converters).
- **Known limitations left as-is**, documented in `readme.md`: the source generator bakes `PropertyNamingPolicy` and the other `[YamlSourceGenerationOptions]` values at compile time; a discriminator coming from a `<<` merge is not read; `StringBuilder`, `Complex` and `ValueTuple` still serialize as their members.

## Validation

- `Meziantou.Framework.Yaml.Tests`: 5017 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (net10.0 and net11.0).
- `Meziantou.Framework.DependencyScanning.Tests` (consumer of the model API): 236 passed.
- Release builds with `/p:IsOfficialBuild=true /p:TreatsWarningsAsErrors=true`: library, source generator, test project, AotSmoke and FeatureSwitchSmoke, all clean.
- `dotnet run ./eng/update-all.cs`: no further changes.

author: fdittgen-png
body:
## What

**S1 of #1310.** `OPERATIONS.md` has documented the dump and the restore since the day it was written, and nothing had ever executed it. A backup procedure that has never been restored is a hope, not a recovery plan.

Every pgTAP file in this repository rolls back, so there was not even a row on disk to dump. `supabase/restore/seed.sql` is the one fixture that persists: two workspaces, a floor plan in each, bookings across two months, and an invoice with the credit ledger row and the match that settle it — the three legs `reconcile_workspace` compares. Two workspaces rather than one, so the copy can be checked for tenancy and not only for row counts.

It deliberately does **not** live under `supabase/tests/`: that directory is swept by `supabase test db`, which ran it as a pgTAP file on the first attempt here — no plan, so that run failed, and since the seed commits it also left its rows behind and the drill's own apply then collided with them. The header says so, so it does not come back.

`scripts/restore_check.sh` seeds it, dumps, restores into a fresh database, and then makes the copy prove itself:

- equal row counts across ten tables;
- `reconcile_workspace()` clean for **both** workspaces — reconciled as each owner, since the function refuses anyone who may not see the finances;
- the two tenants still two, and no member holding another tenant's booking.

And then it proves it can **fail** (#1338): the verified copy, about to be dropped, is damaged on purpose — one reservation deleted, one match moved away from its ledger credit — and both have to be caught. If either goes undetected the drill fails and says which of its own checks proved nothing.

Everything runs through `docker exec` into the stack's own postgres container: the runner's client is older than the server and `pg_dump` refuses a server newer than itself, and dumping from inside also lets the dump carry `auth` — a public-only dump cannot restore, because members reference `auth.users`. The extensions the copy needs are asked of the source rather than guessed.

A **step** in `quality · database`, never a renamed job. It runs last because its seed is the only data left on disk, reports a `Restore drill` row, and the Gate fails on it.

`OPERATIONS.md` now says the procedure is executed on every pull request — and says plainly which part CI still cannot rehearse: storage and the `auth` step, which touch a real project.

Closes the `Restore drill detects a deliberate row loss` item of #1338.

## Tests

- `flutter analyze --fatal-infos lib test tool` — clean.
- `flutter test test/lint` — 167 pass.
- The drill is a CI step, so it is tested by this pull request's own `quality · database` run.

author: hellofrequencylab
body:
Royal Temple's join page rendered **seven stacked cards for four memberships**, because a tier row holds one price and one interval, so every annual plan had to become its own tier. Four rungs, one toggle.

## The change

`space_membership_tiers.annual_price_cents` (null = no yearly option) and `space_memberships.billing_interval` (which cadence the member actually bought — without it a membership cannot say what it is paying). A yearly plan stops being a second tier.

- **Join surface**: one monthly/yearly toggle, cards in a two-column grid, stacking to one column at phone width. A tier with no yearly price says so plainly under the toggle rather than looking identical. The saving is computed from the real numbers, so it never claims "two months free" unless the yearly price actually is ten months.
- **Checkout**: bills the selected cadence with the matching Stripe interval, and **fails closed** on a yearly request for a tier that has no yearly price, rather than silently billing monthly.
- **Editor**: one optional "Yearly price" field per tier. Blank means monthly only.

## Migration ordering

`20270345005000` is **not applied**. Applying ahead of the file landing on `main` is what turned `check:migrations` red for every open PR earlier today (LIVE-351, #2647). Applied at merge, then the ledger stamped with the repo version per `supabase/migrations/README.md`.

The five `check:schema-contract` ALLOWLIST entries are dated and owned and retire together when `lib/database.types.ts` is regenerated after that apply — the same clock the previous twelve ran on, and they retired this morning.

## Provenance

Built in an isolated worktree, then cherry-picked onto current `main` and reconciled here. Two things needed correcting in the process, both worth naming: the allowlist header still claimed the list was empty while carrying five entries, and every entry's `owner` pointed at `LIVE-359`, which had been taken upstream by #2649 in the meantime. ## O que muda

Pedido do usuário: "no app Home, Painel de Gestão, aba Barris, na opção de barril vazio
colocar a opção de colocar a quantidade total, pois não precisa de data de validade".

Antes, no painel de edição da supervisão, cada barril vazio era uma linha própria — 7
cliques em "+ Adicionar" pra lançar 7 vazios, cada um com um select de status e uma coluna
de validade que nunca era usada (vazio não tem validade).

Agora:

- Os vazios saem da lista linha a linha e viram **um campo de quantidade por tipo**
  (🍺 Claro e 🍷 Vinho), com o rótulo "Vazios (sem validade)".
- Os barris não-vazios continuam listados um por um, cada um com o seu status e validade.
- Mudar um item da lista pra "Vazio" pelo select faz ele entrar na contagem sozinho (ele
  some da lista individual e a quantidade sobe).

## Como o save continua funcionando

Sem mudança no `_salvarEdicaoBarrisLoja` nem no schema — o banco continua com uma linha por
barril. Ao mudar a quantidade, a expansão preserva o que já existe:

- **Subir** → mantém os vazios que já têm `id` (viram PATCH/nada) e acrescenta os novos sem
  `id` (POST). Não faz DELETE+POST à toa em barril que já estava lá.
- **Descer** → mantém os primeiros (com `id`) e o excedente simplesmente some da lista, que
  é o que o save já trata como DELETE.
- **Zerar** → remove todos os vazios, sem tocar nos demais.

Entrada inválida (texto, negativo) vira 0 e o campo é normalizado na tela. O handler é
`onchange` e **não** dispara re-render, senão o campo perderia o foco a cada digitação —
mesmo cuidado que o campo de validade já tinha.

body:
## What this is

`CONTRIBUTING.md`'s docs gate documents a last line that raises. One line changes:

```diff
-python .github/scripts/check_api_page.py docs/build/html/api.html
+python .github/scripts/check_api_page.py docs/build/html
```

`check_api_page.py`'s `page_path()` appends `api.html` to whatever it is given, so the documented form builds `docs/build/html/api.html/api.html`. Run as written, in a worktree with the docs built:

```text
NotADirectoryError: [Errno 20] Not a directory:
'docs/build/html/api.html/api.html'
```

The corrected line exits 0. Both halves of that pair were run — the failing one first, as the positive control that makes the passing one mean something — and both were reproduced independently by the reviewer in its own worktree rather than attributed.

## The corrected line is the one CI runs

`docs.yml` passes `post-build-script: .github/scripts/check_api_page.py` with no argument of its own, and `btclib-org/.github`'s `reusable-docs.yml` runs it as `python "$SCRIPT" docs/build/html` — the directory. The two together produce the new line word for word. Read at both files rather than derived.

## The paragraph below the block, which is the issue's second box

It describes what the script checks — every name of `bitcoin_core_rpc.__all__` against the built page, and `docs/source/api.rst`'s one `automodule` per submodule making each findable — and never names the argument's shape. So it is true beside either form and is left unchanged. That is the sentence a repair is most likely to leave quietly false, so it was read whole and quoted rather than skipped, by the author and again by the reviewer.

## Scope

This repository only. `check_api_page.py` exists in no other tree, the four siblings' `CONTRIBUTING.md` mention it nowhere, and `git grep 'check_api_page'` here finds the one wrong invocation and otherwise only generic or correct references — the script's own usage string already says `<build directory>`.

The edit sits at line 468, below `## This repository in particular` at line 227, so section 14's verbatim comparison does not reach it and no `EXPECTED_DRIFT` entry is owed. Verified by line number against `shared()`'s own `MARKER` at `btclib-org/.github`'s `origin/main`.

The script itself is untouched: its interface is what CI depends on, and the documentation is what was wrong.

## Review

Reviewed locally at fresh context against this tree's own `REVIEWING.md`, `CLEARED` in one round. The reviewer reproduced the traceback and the fix itself, re-derived the CI form from the two workflow files, and checked the gate logs' timing against the commit's — they are named for the base sha because the gates were run by hand before committing, which is this file's own documented order.

body:
# Forecast time contract repair — September 15, 2026

PR33 passed all executable exact-head checks and merged into dev as `1ade7a5119aaac39a578af0eefccdfaac11c3562` at 23:44:07 UTC. Its swell/total-sea distinction is retained. Netlify page-change neutral status is not scientific validation. Render rollout is unverified under the existing automatic-review/account-usage browser block.

## Verified defect and repair

`services.surf_conditions.get_surf_conditions` accepted an explicit target datetime but preferred provider current values, queried only today's forecast, and substituted the first hourly row when the target height was unavailable. An offset timestamp was compared to UTC strings without normalization.

The repair normalizes the target to UTC (naive timestamps retain the historical UTC convention), requests the containing hour through start_hour/end_hour, ignores current values for explicit requests, and removes first-row substitution. A default current request still uses current data when available. Missing target height stays unavailable; other fields at that same hour remain independently available. Physics, units and score coefficients are unchanged.

[Open-Meteo's documented hourly interval and UTC contracts](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/marine-weather-api) support the request parameters. These are forecast requests, not a promise of historical archive coverage: an unsupported target may return provider error/no data and must not silently return a different hour.

## Evidence

- `before.log`: 6 new controls fail, previous 12 quantity controls pass.
- `verified.log`: **102 passed** across the time/quantity controls and nearshore, precompute, hub-parity and partition suites.
- Intervention: identical target instant represented in UTC, UTC-6, UTC+9 produces the same request and output despite conflicting current data. Null target heights, short arrays and absent target hours cannot inherit the first frame.
- `after.log` preserves an intermediate edit error: the first patch inserted normalization in the tide function instead of the surf function, causing 15 failures. Fatal lint independently found three undefined names. Corrected placement, reran full affected selection: 102 pass, zero fatal lint findings, whitespace check clean. The error was never committed or pushed.
- Local interpreter still lacks two declared packages. CI/production parity is not claimed.

## Limits and next work

This fixes the direct marine time-selection contract. `get_conditions_for_spot` still drops its optional target_datetime, and full conditions combines current wind/tide. Do not forward only the marine target there and create a mixed-time response; that wrapper requires a coherent multi-variable contract or explicit unavailable response. That work remains open.

Post-composer zero handling, precipitation missing-data display, production-flag oversize inversion and source/cycle cross-surface acceptance remain open. No browser visual validation is claimed for this API-only change. PR27 HOLD, Render OOM attribution and scientific/provenance gates remain. Continue within the existing 71-task/40-objective register.

author: ormeilu
body:
`quality / semver-checks (advisory)` has been red on every PR built from `master`, including ones that never touch `rolter-proxy`:

```
--- failure inherent_method_missing: pub method removed or renamed ---
Forwarder::forward_bearer, previously in file crates/rolter-proxy/src/lib.rs:486
```

#1446 renamed the public `Forwarder::forward_bearer` to `forward_mcp`. `cargo-semver-checks` diffs against the `v0.1.0` tag and cannot tell a rename from a deletion, so the symbol reads as removed. The job is `continue-on-error`, so nothing was blocked — the failure just became permanent background noise, which is how a review signal stops being read at all.

## Change

- `Forwarder::forward_bearer` is back as a `#[deprecated]` shim delegating to `forward_mcp` with `McpUpstreamAuth::Bearer` and `McpTransportOverrides::default()`. The rename stands; the old symbol is simply present again, so the advisory job goes green without reverting #1446. No `since` on the attribute — release-plz picks the version from commit types and the workspace is still `0.1.0`, so naming a release that has not happened would be wrong as often as not.
- A unit test asserts the shim still applies the gateway-owned credential and still strips a client-chosen `Authorization`, so the delegation cannot rot into a credential leak.
- `docs/development/api-stability.md` gains a *Renaming a public item on a guarded crate* section: deprecate-and-delegate, or drop it and say so in the PR description — but never rename quietly. The page previously closed by claiming the job was green on a clean tree, which this failure had falsified.

The in-tree caller (`crates/rolter-gateway/src/mcp_proxy.rs`) already uses `forward_mcp` and is untouched, so nothing in the workspace depends on the deprecated name.

Per ADR-0032 no rolter crate promises a stable Rust API, so the shim is a review-signal hygiene fix rather than a compatibility promise; it can be dropped in a `!` commit whenever that is wanted.

Closes #1473

- Changing a transaction whose current medical/not-medical verdict came from an automatic rule now tells you so: the confirmation reads **"A rule filed this one. Review it?"** with a **Review** button, instead of the usual plain confirmation.
- Covers all three places a decision can be changed: the row's Healthcare / Not healthcare buttons, the row menu's "Mark as Healthcare" item, and the expanded transaction detail's toggle.

Overriding a rule-filed decision to "not healthcare" replaces the usual dismiss confirmation, which normally carries an "Undo" action — that Undo is not available on this specific path. Reviewing/fixing the rule is the more useful next step in that moment, but it's worth knowing this one case doesn't offer a one-click undo the way a plain dismissal does.

**Also found, not fixed:** a manual override does not clear `applied_by_rule_id` on the transaction, so the rules panel's "Applied to N transactions" count can include rows the user has since overridden by hand. body:
Make typed IR, rather than printer inference, the foundation for reliable C# emission. This slice advances #2095 by materializing already-decided named-reference storage; it does not merely redistribute printer code.

**PASS within the stated coverage:** current-head CI and the required fixed-head review are clean. Printer-considered slots fall from 28,552 to 8,412 (20,140 fewer, 70.5%). Full render A/B finds no valid-to-invalid regression. All 1,528 changed methods have source accounting and paired fidelity outcomes; two preexisting malformed-C# cases retain explicit semantic limits. This is a reduction in printer-owned inference, not deleted printer lines or whole-program equivalence.

- Head: `c9bfa406ba9f6a77d80696976cfb0b0b631cdbf5`.
- Effective base: `f9f682eddd59931a952ce1a64089c5bbdee19985`.
- Owner: `docs/design/value-typed-emission.md`, Instance 2 / migration step 5.
- Scope: exact, spellable metadata-known class/interface/delegate storage, including constructed generic reference types.

## Demo

The canonical unchanged-output witness is Microsoft.CodeAnalysis 5.0.0, `lib/net9.0/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.dll`, `ChildSyntaxList.GetHashCode` (method token `0x06001A15`).

```sh
dotnet-inspect member Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.ChildSyntaxList GetHashCode \
  --library /path/to/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.dll \
  -S "Decompiled Source" --all
```

### Before

```csharp
public override int GetHashCode()
{
    SyntaxNode S_256 = _node;
    if (S_256 is null)
    {
        return 0;
    }
    return S_256.GetHashCode();
}
```

### After

```csharp
public override int GetHashCode()
{
    SyntaxNode S_256 = _node;
    if (S_256 is null)
    {
        return 0;
    }
    return S_256.GetHashCode();
}
```

The emitted C# deliberately stays identical; ownership of its type decision changes. The product stage dump shows the materialization step:

```text
==== IR (after slot-materialization) ====  [92/99]
  …
      Block IL_0000
-       StoreStackSlot S_256
+       StoreLocal 0 (SyntaxNode)
          LoadField ChildSyntaxList._node (SyntaxNode)
  …
          LogicalNot
-           LoadStackSlot S_256
+           LoadLocal 0 (SyntaxNode)
          Block IL_0009
  …
          CallVirt object.GetHashCode
-           LoadStackSlot S_256
+           LoadLocal 0 (SyntaxNode)
  // fidelity: Full
```

Before/After independent verdicts: printer exact **not enrolled**; no Applied Taste choices; whole-program correctness **unverified**. Both whole-module compile-back attempts are **RecompileFail**, with the same `CS0075` context diagnostic. They are not passing fidelity evidence. The compiler-produced reference fixtures supply the separate exact compile-back gate.

**Structural review:** attempted with both product-issued annotated documents. Result **Partial**, 18 unsupported/ambiguous nodes, no supported structural changes. This does not establish the IR rewrite. The standalone Before/After documents and generated report are retained.

**PDB Source -> After:** SourceLink resolves Roslyn commit `6c4a46a31302167b425d5e0a31ea83c9a9aa1d09`, `src/Compilers/Core/Portable/Syntax/ChildSyntaxList.cs`. The product reports portable-PDB SHA256 agreement after CR/LF normalization (`8538E57A1851BC1712F53D6F15BFDC7AC9694EC204E57C8001A547A75C9633CE`), with one authored comparison line versus six decompiled comparison lines.

**Neighbor:** the four-argument Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4 `JsonConvert.DeserializeXmlNode` also retains byte-identical C# while its already-typed reference becomes IR-owned storage. Unresolved reference fixtures and bare generic-parameter storage remain on slots.

### Production consumers

Both existing hosts use the shared raising pipeline; there is no new host-specific conversion path or API.

The C# CLI call site remains `MemberCommand.ExecuteAsync`:

```csharp
var writeExitCode = await ApiCommand.WriteTypeOutputAsync(
    apiType, acquisition.FoundIn, acquisition.PackageName, acquisition.PackageVersion,
    acquisition.ApiSource, acquisition.SelectedTfm, effectiveOptions,
    memberCodeSourceAssembly: sourceAssembly);
```

The TypeScript call site remains `inspect-web/src/dotnet-inspect.ts`:

```typescript
const result = await inspectMemberFindingCensus(
  request.packageId,
  request.version,
  request.framework,
  request.assembly,
  request.typeIdentity,
  request.type,
  request.member,
  request.memberSignature,
  request.selectorKey,
  request.metadataToken,
  request.taste);
const document = result.annotatedSource.document;
validateAnnotatedSourceDocument(document);
```

The invocation returns an in-flight Promise; `result` and its document are realized values after `await`. These are adoption call sites, not a claim that a separate Browser/Wasm execution was performed.

## Raise contract

The recognized shell is a synthetic slot web whose every observer agrees on one type and whose every producer already has that exact type. The existing imported type-shape map must identify its named definition as a reference, and the entire type must pass the existing explicit-parameter spelling checks.

Materialization consumes every outer store/load in the admitted web and introduces one fresh typed local. Direct-copy components remain atomic. The existing independent `SlotMaterializationInvariant` checks ordered node identity, slot/local correspondence, and nested-body preservation. No control-flow edge is consumed or changed.

The decline boundaries remain unknown or value-type shapes, bare generic parameters, unspellable/out-of-scope constructions, non-exact producers, disagreeing or missing testimony, structural folds, pending swaps, and incomplete copy components. CoercionDomain, the rewrite algorithm, pipeline ordering, and all printer files are unchanged. The spelling gate is not a universal binding or generic-constraint proof.

The Roslyn nested-storage regression fixture now explicitly preserves both remaining nested slots and references already materialized by their own nested pipeline. Existing nested-name collision gates remain in force.

**Fully raised endpoint:** no residual synthetic storage requires print-time type inference. This PR does not reach that endpoint. EH adoption and #6907 remain a separate workstream.
