| Rewrite/admission gates | Compiler-produced and adversarial fixture family | Passing; existing independent rewrite checker exercised | Evidence coverage |
| Fixture IL fidelity | Nine named-reference methods in one Release-built input | Exact for all nine; coupled generated-lambda gate also passes | Bounded correctness evidence |
| Real witness source | Same pinned Roslyn physical method | Byte-identical Before/After | Same |
| Real witness fidelity | Same pinned Roslyn physical method | RecompileFail on both sides; CS0075 | Unavailable |
| Printer telemetry | Same 14 assemblies / 89,065 methods | 28,552 -> 8,412 distinct considered slots; 0 -> 0 pass bugs | Less printer-owned storage; not a deleted-line count |
| Render A/B | Same pinned input bytes, paths, working directory and caps | 1,527 comparable changed methods; 735 valid->valid, 4 invalid->valid, 0 valid->invalid, 788 invalid->invalid | No validity regression in the compared population |
| Source accounting | All 1,528 changed physical methods, including one raw exclusion | 1,526 comparison-accounted; two preexisting parser/semantic limits with all changed bytes inventoried | Complete accounting, explicitly bounded semantics |
| Paired changed-method fidelity | All 1,528 exact changed identities | All status categories unchanged; one new dead initialization pair accounted by source/IR | No Exact or checkability loss; not whole-body equivalence |
| Required fixed-head review | Exact published head | CLEAN; zero findings | Review clean |

The initial unchanged-product counterfactual predicted 20,112 newly eligible **outer webs** in 4,784 methods. That is a different measureme

author: milad-alizadeh
body:
## What this does

A Session that another process runs live now reads as locked. The Roster draws the lock. The composer is hidden from the moment you select the Session, and not after a Send fails.

For Claude, a Session is live when `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` names a live `claude`, busy or idle. For Codex, a Session is live when the newest Turn mark in the rollout is `task_started` with no later `task_complete` and no later `turn_aborted`, and the rollout was written within 30 minutes. Those rows now read `running` in place of `unknown`.

A Session that this Argo holds never locks this way. An idle external Session keeps its composer.

## Base

The base branch is `main`, merged at `e32b77fb76cb835b5496d69422d0cfc626b45743`. The merge was clean. No path conflicted.

## Docs changed in place

1. `docs/domain/l2-session.md` says what locks a Session.
2. `docs/adr/0040-origin-does-not-gate-a-resume.md` says that any process that runs a Session live locks it.

## Evidence

On the committed tree before the merge, 918 unit tests pass across 177 files. 376 Storybook tests pass in `src/renderer/modules/sessions`, in dark and in light. The packaged Session proof returns `ok: true` over 22 cases.

A read-only check ran against the real machine. 8 of 228 rows read locked: 6 live `claude` Sessions and 2 Codex threads inside a Turn.

The 30-minute bound comes from measurement. Over 89,725 gaps, the longest silence inside a running Codex Turn was 10 minutes. One rollout held a Turn left open for 33 hours. The event names were checked against all 416 rollouts on this machine, on codex-cli 0.147.0.

## Gate

The gate is `bun run quality`, run from the worktree root on the merged tree, with the Node version from `.node-version`. It passed in full.

Before the merge it failed only `quality:i18n`, on `apps/desktop/src/renderer/modules/sessions/feed/content/feed-images.tsx`. This branch does not touch that file. The check diffs against origin/main, and the base of this branch was behind. The merge of origin/main cleared the failure.

## Carried, not fixed

There is no GitHub issue for this work, so this pull request closes nothing.

1. A Send is still refused only on the `held-elsewhere` state of the ownership ledger. A Send made before the next Roster poll can still resume a Session that another `claude` holds.
2. A reused process id can lock a Session that is not live. The existing status join has the same weakness. The `procStart` field in the pid files would close it.
3. A Codex Turn that stays silent for more than 30 minutes unlocks.
4. Nobody drove the real cockpit by hand against a live external `claude`, or against the real Codex app. The evidence is the reader output and Storybook only.
5. The session that dispatched the work reviewed the diff. A fresh-context `/code-review` did not.

author: hobbyiq
body:
## The defect

`rungFoldingFor` may derive a root no file states, so Spectra's fourteen `Dual Patch Autographs <colour>` files land on one card set. Its gates ask whether the siblings **could** be one set — rosters agree, tails differ, signing matches. None of them can ask whether the tail is a **colour**, and that is the question that decides it.

Measured on 2020-21 Panini Mosaic: `Rookie Private Signings Association Version` and `... Icon Version` are two different card sets. They agree on their roster (one card, #12 Tyrese Haliburton), their tails differ, and both are unsigned — so every gate passed and the fold derived `rookie-private-signings`, reading **each set's name as a parallel of it**. Both then collapsed to one subset slug, `subsetsToSeparate` saw a single slug and separated nothing, and the rows landed on the base product where card 12 Gold collided with card 12 Gold. The guard refused the whole 14,186-row file.

This is pre-existing — `origin/main` has the identical mis-fold and escapes the collision only by accident (its Icon rows keep the colour inside the rung name, which is wrong in a different way).

## The rule: a measurement, not a lexicon

`CF-A-COLOUR-RUNG-IS-NEVER-A-CARD-SET-KEY` is explicit that a word list would fold `Gold Standard` and `Black Gold` — real products whose names end in a colour word. So the tell is **what the cell prints as a parallel**:

| cell states | on how many categories |
|---|---:|
| `Gold` | 8 |
| `Platinum` | 2 |
| `Association Version` | **0** |
| `Icon Version` | **0** |

A tail this fold would turn into a parallel must be a parallel the cell actually prints somewhere. When not one of them is, the fold is refused and the siblings keep their own full-name keys — which is what the source states, and what lets each become its own registered insert key.

**This does not cost the Spectra fold.** cardboardconnection ships one file per rung with the colour in the manifest and the parallel column blank, so no cell-stated vocabulary exists to test against; the rule fires only where the cell **has** a vocabulary and the tails are absent from it. The mutation test asserts that fold still folds, and `cbcAcquisitionSubsetKeysAreFixedPoints` (43 Spectra/Prizm keys) stays green.

## Refusals are now reported

`rungFoldingFor` carries a non-enumerable `refusedRoots` map — root, reason, siblings, and the tails the cell never printed — so a section that keeps its own key **says why** instead of looking like no fold was attempted. Non-enumerable so every existing caller that spreads or iterates the Map is unaffected.

## Measured

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| files PASS | 7 of 8 | **8 of 8** |
| writable rows | 63,147 | **77,333** |
| 2020-21 Mosaic | REFUSE (id-collisions=2), 14,184 ids | **PASS, 14,186 ids** |
| Mosaic subset keys | 22 | **24** |

The two extra keys are the Private Signings sets now correctly addressed in their own right.

## Verification

- **12 affected suites, 119 tests green**, including the `#2195` colour-sibling mutation check and the 43-key Spectra fixed-point suite.
- Ingest validator on the 8-file package: 8/8 PASS, **0 unregistered keys**.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

The NLnet grant application lists "Bug Bounty framework" as TBD. This closes that gap honestly (recognition-only, not a fake paid program).

Tooling epic, run before EPIC-11 (D-10): cut the round trips between the developer at the Atari ST and the agent at the Mac. The tools reach the RP only through picotool, the Debug Probe (SWD) and the console UART, never through the firmware's own HTTP server (D-11), so they work with any microfirmware built from this template and on a hung RP.

## Host tools, in `tools/dev/`

- **`console.py`** captures the debug console (921,600 baud) to a timestamped log and shows it live. `since-boot`, `tail`, `grep` and `wait` read that log, so a boot log no longer has to be pasted by hand. It finds the probe by its USB name and reopens it after an unplug.
- **`flash.sh <release|debug>`** builds out of tree and incrementally (35 s cold, 4 s warm; `rp/build` and the submodules untouched), flashes with picotool or the probe, and then checks over SWD that the RP booted the ELF, that its flash matches byte for byte and that it carries the new build ID. About 18 s from command to a confirmed boot.
- **`swd.py`** wraps OpenOCD: `running`, `verify`, `build-id`, `read`, `program`, `resume`, `screen` (the setup menu as a PNG), `text` (the menu as text), `shared` (the shared variables by name), `select`, `key`, `app`, `inject`, `crash` and `postmortem`. Memory is read while the CPU runs, so a hung RP can be inspected too.
- **`smoke.py`, `measure_builds.sh`, `stackdepth.py`** move in from a gitignored folder. The smoke script now stops the countdown, presses SELECT and checks the menu text and the firmware's own state itself; only the cold boot, the `[G]` desktop file copy and switching the ST to `[U]` still need a person.

Nothing hard-codes an address: offsets come from `chandler.h` and the ELF's symbols (C-04).

## Firmware changes

- **Build ID in both build types.** `rp/src/build_id.cmake` regenerates `build_id.h` and `build_id.c` on every build (not at configure time, so an incremental build is never stale) with `<sha7>`, or `<sha7>-dirty.<diff7>` when the tree has uncommitted changes. The same tree gives the same ID and a byte-identical binary. It is reported on the console at boot, in `GET /api/v1/system/health` next to a new `debug` flag, and by `sidecart.py health`.
- **Debug-only mailbox** (`rp/src/include/devhooks.h`, self-contained like `debug.h`): host tools write a request over SWD, `devhooks_poll()` in the main loop runs it. A protocol request goes through the new `chandler_injectProtocol()` as if the ST had sent it, so an injected keystroke takes the firmware's normal path; an app request goes to a handler the app registers (`emul.c`: countdown stop and restart). `release` contains none of it.
- **Crash PC no longer lost.** The once-a-second stall timer wrote `watchdog_hw->scratch[1] = 0` whenever the watchdog had been fed, and that is where the panic and HardFault handlers store the crash PC in the 100 ms before the reboot. Crashes whose reboot window overlapped a tick reported `pc=0x00000000`. The timer now only replaces its own values there. This is an EPIC-09 bug the new tools found.
- SELECT needs no firmware support: `swd.py select` forces the pin's input high through `IO_BANK0 GPIOn_CTRL.INOVER`. A long press needs `--force`, because it erases the global settings.

`release` grew 64 bytes of code and 32 bytes of RAM against `release/v1.1.0`, all of it the build ID and the two new health fields. It exposes no debug-only route or symbol.

## Verified on hardware

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Smoke on `debug` (`--manual`) | 13 passed, 0 failed; console clean: no panic, HardFault, ROM3 overrun or dropped bytes |
| Smoke on `release` (`--manual`) | 12 passed; the one failure was the script using the mailbox a release build lacks, fixed |
| Menu PNG against the ST | Matched before HELLO, after an ST reset (Phystop, Screenmem, countdown line) and after a forced panic (`Recovered: panic @10005194`) |
| Shared variables after HELLO | reloc and memtop `0xF4000`, drive `C`, first file descriptor 64, hook vector `$70` |
| Countdown stop and restart, key injection | Menu bottom line changed as expected; console logged the injected keystroke |
| SELECT short press over SWD | `released after 304 ms`, `Short press detected`, next boot `reset` |
| Post-mortem of a forced hang | Backtrace `health_runPendingTest health.c:415` ← `health_tick` ← `emul_start`, RP resumed |
| Crash report after panic and HardFault | `health.c:404` and `health.c:409`; five panics in a row all kept the PC after the fix |
| Flash and verify | `debug` with picotool, `release` through the probe; a wrong ELF fails `verify` |

## Known limitations

- Halting the RP pauses its timer and watchdog, so a hang halted in its first seconds reboots as `reboot` rather than `hang`; the backtrace is the better evidence.
- Keys and app commands need a `debug` build; on `release` those steps fall back to prompts.
- The tools see only what the RP draws (the setup menu), not the ST's GEM screen, and cannot reset or power-cycle the ST.

body: Authorized by Jamie Yellow. Restores handbook invariant 1 (protocol depends only on `zod`) and upgrades the workspace compiler to TypeScript 7. ## CJK ownership Native `@node-rs/jieba` moves off `@do-soul/alaya-protocol` onto Node-only `@do-soul/alaya-cjk-segmentation`. Core cannot be the sole owner: storage tokenizes FTS and must not import core. A second copy in core+storage is rejected. The helper is the one acyclic owner. Protocol keeps pure policy: interrogative fallback atoms, the CJK-candidate predicate, fail-soft atom-split. Native bind is **once-only** on `node/source-frame`, not the protocol browser root. Protocol does not import jieba. Inspector SPA and Inspector server do not depend on the helper. `retired_import_paths` keeps `apps/inspector/web/src/utils/parse-search-query` and appends `packages/protocol/src/shared/cjk-segmentation`. Handbook invariant 1b, architecture, recall, CHANGELOG Unreleased, and `hygiene:inspector-deps` match live code. Workspace-internal; not a §25 MCP/EventLog/config change. ## TypeScript 7 - Catalog `typescript` is **7.0.2** (native `tsc` for typecheck/build). - Inspector web drops `ignoreDeprecations` / `baseUrl` / `moduleResolution: Node`. - `ci:repository-structure` keeps the Compiler API via `@typescript/typescript6@6.0.2`. - Vitest 5 stays deferred. No compile-time performance claim from the cloud runner. ## Independent review TS7, jieba ownership R2, and CJK drift R2 reported no remaining Blocking/Important on `ab64b7466`. Those reviewers confirmed the Inspector overview refetch does not reopen their scopes. `9a959b286` only updates the S08 policy digest pin. ## CI Quality on `9a959b286` (run 35047388258): Bench content contracts, Quality ubuntu-node24, Quality macos-node24, Quality windows-node24, and CLI install surface smoke all passed. Ready for review. Do not merge without explicit merge authorization.

author: 1duo
body:
Upstream-branch PR opened as `1duo` (same change as #823 fork PR and #834). Supersedes #823 and #834 so full secret-gated CI runs with `1duo` as author.

---

### Description
Fixes spurious mainline failure of `QnnHTPBackendTests.TopK_QDQ_U8_FoldsQDQIntoQuantizedTopK` (added in #775) on HTP arch <= 68 runners.

Root cause: `TestQDQModelAccuracy()` issues `GTEST_SKIP()` from inside a helper (`qnn_test_utils.h:1175`, `CONDITIONAL_SKIP_TEST_ON_LINUX_ARM64`). That marks the test skipped but does NOT return from the caller's `TEST_F` body, so `AssertOpInQnnGraph/AssertNodeNotInQnnGraph` ran on an empty dump dir and failed with `No QNN JSON graph file found in TopK_QDQ_U8_FoldsQDQIntoQuantizedTopK` (`qnn_graph_checker.cc:74,105`).

### Changes
- `onnxruntime/test/providers/qnn/topk_test.cc`: add `if (::testing::Test::IsSkipped()) return;` after `TestQDQModelAccuracy` — same pattern as `conv_test.cc:1154`, `matmul_test.cc:753`, `softmax_test.cc:308`, `resize_test.cc:607`.
- `onnxruntime/test/providers/qnn/qnn_node_group/qnn_graph_checker.cc`: propagate skips at entry of all 4 asserts (`AssertOpInQnnGraph`, `AssertNodeNotInQnnGraph`, `AssertFp32StaticBytesBelow/Above`) as safety net for future dump-and-assert tests. No-op when not skipped.

### Validation
- `clang-format --dry-run --Werror` on both files: pass.
- `git diff --check`: pass.
- No new includes (both files already include `gtest/gtest.h`).
- Audit: 25 other dump+Assert sites now covered by safety net; guard is no-op on supported arch.
- Full HTP/QDC validation requires CI (no local device): please run `/ci` + device suites.

### Motivation and Context
Unblocks mainline red from #775 on `linux-arm64`, `windows-arm64`, `android`, `oe` QDC jobs. Fork-PR device tests are stubbed green, so this class of arch-dependent skip bug needs both the call-site guard and the checker safety net.

author: msradam
body:
## Summary

- Remove the `start` and `finish` chunks `CreateUIMessageStream` added to every composed stream, matching `createUIMessageStream` in the registered `ai@7.0.65` baseline.
- Inject the response message ID into a written `start` chunk that lacks one, reusing the last original message's ID when that message is an assistant message, so `useChat` continues that message instead of opening a second one.
- Run `OnFinish` whether or not `OriginalMessages` is set, and replace the continued message in its `Messages`.
- Document the framing contract on the API and in the two guides that recommend it, and record the new coverage and one known gap in `PARITY.md`.

Closes #180.

## Code Changes

- `stream.go`: `CreateUIMessageStream` now builds a `uiMessageStreamConfig` and takes its response ID from the existing `responseUIMessageID` helper, injects that ID into `start` chunks without one, tracks finish reason and abort state from written chunks, and emits nothing of its own.
- `streamtext.go`: added `buildUIMessageStreamFinishState` next to the other finish-state helpers, and `ToUIMessageStream` now calls it instead of repeating the same assembly inline, so both entry points share one continuation rule.
- `stream.go`: the doc comment states that `Execute` owns writing `start` and `finish`, and every `CreateUIMessageStreamParams` field is now documented, including that `OriginalMessages` supplies prior history and no longer switches on a persistence mode.
- `docs/guides/streaming-http.md` and `docs/concepts/wire-protocol.md`: both recommend this API for merging model output with application chunks, so both now say the caller frames the stream, and the guide carries a worked example of the merge shape.
- `chunk.go`: `StartChunk` documents that an empty message ID lets the stream assign the response ID.

## Tests And Fixtures

- Replaced the two tests that asserted SDK-added framing. `basic execute produces start and finish` becomes `written chunks pass through without added start or finish`, and `persistence mode sets messageId on start` becomes a case that writes a bare `start` chunk and asserts the injected ID.
- Added `keeps existing messageId from start chunk` and `continues the last assistant message`, mirroring the upstream cases in `packages/ai/src/ui-message-stream/create-ui-message-stream.test.ts` at the pinned commit.
- Added `OnFinish runs without original messages`, mirroring upstream's case of the same name, `OnFinish reports abort and finish reason` for the two branches this change adds, and `generates a response messageId without original messages`, which fails with an empty ID if the response-ID resolution regresses.
- No conformance fixture changed. Conformance replays provider stream parts through `StreamText`, which does not exercise `CreateUIMessageStream`.

## Validation

- `go vet .`
- `go test -race -count=1 .`
- `gofmt -l stream.go stream_test.go streamtext.go`
- `mise run test`
- `mise run test-examples`
- `mise run build-examples`
- `mise run vet`
- `mise run build`
- `mise run test-conformance`
- `mise run test-integration` (27 React hook tests, 8 gateway command tests)
- `mise run lint-docs`
- `mise run validate-parity-baseline`
- `mise run parity-check` fails before and after this change on a checkout without the pinned upstream clone at `~/src/ai`, so it was not used as evidence.

Dogfooding evidence, using the upstream Human-in-the-Loop and Multi-Modal examples rebuilt on a Go backend with their React pages, tools and helpers copied unchanged from the pinned upstream commit:

- Before: the approval turn sent an extra leading `start` with a new message ID and an extra trailing `finish`; the browser turned one assistant message into three and React logged five duplicate-key errors.
- After: the chunk sequence matches the upstream route replayed on `ai@7.0.65` with a scripted `MockLanguageModelV4`, and approving in the browser updates one assistant message with no console errors.
- The Multi-Modal example matched upstream before and after, in both its chunk sequence and the provider prompt built from image and PDF parts, which covers the unchanged non-composed path.

## Residual risk

- Callers that wrote only content chunks and relied on the SDK to frame them now emit an unframed stream, as upstream does. No caller in this repository did; the two affected tests were the only users. Such a caller also loses the server-assigned message ID, which is why the doc comment and both guides now name the obligation.
- `OnFinish` now runs for composed streams built without `OriginalMessages`, so a persistence callback in that configuration starts receiving a one-message history with a generated ID where it previously received nothing.
- `OnFinish` on the continuation path reports the continued message rather than a new one: `Messages` keeps its length, `ResponseMessage.ID` is the existing assistant message ID, and `ResponseMessage.Parts` carry the prior parts followed by the new ones. A persistence callback should upsert on `ResponseMessage.ID` and treat `Parts` as the whole message, not a delta.
- Review found four lifecycle and error-handling differences from upstream that predate this change: a nil or panicking `Execute`, chunks merged after `Execute` returns, discarded assembly errors, and `PipeUIMessageStreamToResponse` abandoning its stream on a write error. They are tracked in #181, outside this change; the delayed-merge one is now recorded as a gap in `PARITY.md`.
- Two behaviors were checked directly against `ai@7.0.65` rather than argued: it injects a generated message ID even with no `originalMessages`, and it also produces duplicated parts when a caller-supplied start ID differs from the last assistant message. Go matches both, so neither was changed here.
- `FinishChunk` takes a plain string and converts it into a `provider.UnifiedFinishReason` without validation, so a caller can produce a finish reason outside the known set. That predates this change and is left alone.
- Upstream's default error text ends with a period and the Go default still does not. That difference is untouched here.
